Memories That Never Fade Away

by Peridot_Garcia

https://archiveofourown.org/works/60339511

    Chapter 1

    From Death, Life Chapter Notes See the end of the chapter for notes The kid annoyed her...in a good way.

    His temperament wasn't all that surprising considering the age of his soul was going on four years. That, coupled with teenage hormones, made Billy Maximoff an intriguing, if not irritating, specimen. Actually, the kid was a triple threat when she really thought about it. A young soul with teenage hormones and all the dramatics of a Maximoff. At least he hadn't enslaved a town...yet...

    As of late, Billy Maximoff (but Wanda was not his mother!) was increasingly prone to probing Agatha with all sorts of pesky questions. Most notably with ones regarding her personal life. He would get this wide-eyed look on his face right before asking Agatha one of his many, many, many questions. How he managed to think of so many in the few days she'd hung around him, she'd never know.

    "What was it like growing up without the internet? What kinds of games did you and your friends play? Wait, did you even have friends, or did you think you were too good to play with other witches?"

    She would moan and groan and deflect for a few moments, just enough to torment the boy, before dazzling him with a tale or two. (If she made up a thing or two, well, who was going to fact check her? Rio?) The delight and, often times, annoyance that crossed his face never failed to freeze her in place.

    Moments like these with Billy scratched and ached deep within her icky, black soul. Like a piece of Nicky had nestled into a bit of the teen to chase away the darkness that she herself had conjured. But, for the most part, he was more like her. Hungry for knowledge. Cautious with his newfound powers. Terribly sensitive at times that meant hiding behind a mask of indifference. Yeah...she didn't like the reminder all that much.

    Today, the young witch eyed her hovering form from his desk chair, lips pursed. His brows furrowed as he warred internally with a silent question. Agatha ignored him to the best of her ability as she listened to one of his many records. Blue Oyster Cult's [Don't Fear] The Reaper was playing softly, eliciting a hum from the ghost. Without much thought, she found herself saying, "The number of times I thought about playing this for Rio outnumber the stars in the sky."

    Billy's gaze burned into her shimmering form, clearly intrigued. "Why didn't you?" he finally asked. Whatever question he'd been pondering lay forgotten for another day. Agatha turned her head to look at him, realizing she must have voiced her thoughts. She cleared her throat out of habit as she floated over to his bed to claim it with her chilly presence. Because her smile would have dashed away the hate in my heart, leading me to forgive her and giving up my hunt for a way to bring back my son, Agatha didn't say. (He didn't need to know that, and you didn't hear anything either!) "I never learned how to work a boombox," she stated dramatically, wiggling her fingers in a dismissive gesture. "Damn thing ate up all my cassette tapes in the 80s."

    The curly-haired teen narrowed his eyes. He leaned back, arms crossed. "Did you know that you raise the tone of your voice when you're lying?"

    See? An-noy-ing!

    Agatha shot him a glare. "I beg your finest pardon," she huffed. "I forgot I was talking to my second biggest stalker." Well...maybe my biggest stalker now that Rio's MIA, Agatha noted sourly. She pushed aside the hurt in favor of bickering with the inquisitive child. Billy continued as if she hadn't said a word. "I'm guessing you didn't want her to know you thought of her often. I imagine it wouldn't look good for the Big, Bad Agatha Harkness to have a soft spot for anyone." He smirked as she dropped her mouth open in a silent gasp. "You've got a lot of nerve." The translucent woman rose from the bed as gracefully as she could. "At least I don't cry when my boyfriend shoots me a text with all those insipid hearts!" The teen had the gall to laugh. "Somebody's cranky," he quipped easily, cheekily. The dimples in his cheeks conjured the memory of another cheeky boy she once had the pleasure of knowing.

    Oh! What a troublesome boy Wanda's son was! Agatha drifted out of the room with muttered curses. "He better be glad I don't have a body," she grumbled.

    Now that she had vacated the Kaplan Residence, the witch returned to her empty house. The place was still as wrecked as it had been the day she died. Her little burial garden was flourishing better than ever, though. She figured Rio had enchanted the mound to remain in a constant state of living and decomposition. Agatha chose to ignore the implications of such a memorial, and floated into her old bedroom. Remnants of Agnes still littered the place. She never had a chance to remove them, actually. With the Salem Seven hot on her heels, and Billy sending the haphazardly constructed coven on a journey in a nightmarish version of The Wizard of Oz, Agatha had put 'make Rio clean up her mess' at the bottom of her to-do list. And after dying, the residents of Westview were far too terrified to set foot on her property in fear of triggering another freak storm or hex. (Cowards.)

    Her pale hand hovered over surfaces as she roamed the dusty house. The action tugged a bitter cackle from her chest.

    She was haunting her own home like some sad, old biddy!

    Agatha promptly ran from this painful reminder as she was wont to do.

    "You...are a coward!"

    Curious, the dead witch traveled until she found her target. Smirking, she phased through glass and promptly knocked over a bowl of jade eggs. The heavy polished stones thudded to the ground with a deafening noise. (To others, that is. One of the few blessings afforded to ghosts.) Several patrons jumped in shock as the green balls rolled along the hard-wood floor. The woman of the hour emerged from behind the counter with a scowl.

    "Must have been too close to the edge," Jennifer Kale told her customers, transitioning to a polite smile. "Nothing to worry about."

    Agatha moved over to a 'store closing' sign and tugged it down with a laugh only she could hear. She didn't want to give herself away too soon.

    Jen whipped around with furrowed brows. "Just another reason to avoid cheap tape," she told her wide-eyed companions. The pink clad witch rushed over to fix the sign and immediately stepped on one of the jade eggs. She shrieked as she fell backwards in a way Agatha thought only possible in the cartoons Tommy and Billy had forced her to watch. "Time for some fireworks," Agatha cackled. With raised hands, she focused on disrupting the energy around her. Lights flickered violently, a few bulbs bursting from the power surge. A handful of shoppers abandoned their task and ran from the store. The witch grabbed whatever she had enough energy to pick up and began hurling items at the remaining store occupants. Jennifer covered her head as she scrambled for cover. "Te ipsum revela, aggressorem," she chanted. Her hands began to glow bubblegum pink as she aimed a burst of energy in a random direction.

    Now that she'd run everybody else off, Agatha drifted up behind Jen to tap on her left shoulder. When the woman jumped, the ghost tugged at her right sleeve. Another jump, a ball of magic fired aimlessly. Finally, Agatha took hold of Jen's ankle just for the satisfaction of scaring the witch half to death.

    "Te ipsum revela, aggressorem," Jen screeched.

    "Someone needs to brush up on their spells," Agatha teased. She settled on a ruined display case with a wolfish grin. "Did ya miss me?"

    "Agatha!" Jen eyed her, tears in her eyes. "What happened to you? I...I thought..." Oh yeah... "Whoops! Forgot you weren't invited to the party," the ghost said with pursed lips. "As you can clearly see, I'm a ghost." Agatha wiggled her fingers with a dramatic, warbled, "Ooooh."

    Jen jerked back as if she'd been slapped. She quickly looked around as a new thought occurred. "What about Teen? Is he...?"

    "Billy," Agatha corrected before she could register what she was saying. "He's fine. In fact, he's twice as mouthy now. Guess that's on me for keeping the brat alive as long as I have." She gestured to the glowing woman. "You, on the other hand, are looking much better. Mud really wasn't your best fashion accessory. Those shoes, though..." Agatha tutted with a shake of her head.

    "How," Jen whispered, still very much in shock.

    "How," she repeated, confused. "Oh! Right. The whole ghost thing." Agatha rolled her eyes. "You know the song. 'I hold Death's hand in mine.' It was always a bit more literal for me." That was as much as she was willing to elaborate as she felt the other woman's eyes roaming over her appearance. Pleased, she leaned back with a suggestive look. "Careful, Hot Stuff. Even in death, I'm still too much for you to handle."

    "No kidding," Jen scoffed. She seemed to come to terms with the news relatively quickly now that Billy was okay. "Death wasn't even good enough for you."

    Okay...ouch! The world probably deserved to know that was no fault of Rio's. It was Agatha who had pushed the cosmic being over the edge and made her...well...crippled with grief and longing. Nope...Nope, nope, nope. Not gonna think about that.

    Agatha licked her lips, eyes finding the floor. "Anyway, I thought I'd come bother you since Billy's being a bit of butt-head."

    Jen made a face. "You're just haunting a teenager? That's a new one. Planning on killing him after all, Witch Killer?"

    "And here I thought we'd had a moment the last time we saw each other," Agatha told her, tone dripping with sarcasm.

    The taller witch rolled her eyes. "You mean when you revealed you'd bound me a century ago? Not exactly romantic."

    "Boo," the ghost said, pouting. "Actually, I might have a favor to ask. Well, it depends on if you've finally perfected this patented crap."

    "I wasn't aware ghosts required face masks, though you certain do."

    "What can I say? A lot of my victims could use one."

    "...Alice...," she heard Jen whisper.

    Digging a metaphorical grave as a ghost...not something I'd considered. "So, about your products...?"

    "Don't you have eyes? I'm closing my store and getting the hell out of town." "Right, right. Impending lawsuits. Look, I kinda owe the kid for using all his face wash to prank Dottie. So, you got anything for him or...?"

    "Asking before taking?" Jen laughed to herself. "You've gone soft, Harkness." Agatha shot her a glare. "The face wash, Jen," she growled. "Do you have any, or not?" The witch smiled widely. "I do. Some of my own personal stash that won't have any side effects like those," she said, waving a hand at her failed cosmetic line. "Great! Now, I'll give you Billy's address, and you can drop 'em off." Agatha moved to find a pen and paper.

    "You're gonna make me carry everything?"

    "I'm a fucking ghost, Jen!"

    "Oh yeah..." The witch turned awkwardly before disappearing through a door. "Honestly," Agatha muttered.

    The floating witch buzzed with excitement as Jen's car pulled up to the Kaplan Residence. Upstairs, Billy sat unaware of the present he was about to receive. Agatha recalled the time she had acquired a gift for Nicky the night before his fifth birthday. He had seen a necklace in the market, a beautiful pendant of jade and obsidian in the form of a Waning Moon. "Please, Mama," he'd begged. "I shant be ornery. Promise!"

    She had told him 'no' firmly and ushered them into the woods to rest. As he slept, she crept into the jeweler's home and stolen the token. The few hours between her return to him and dawn had chewed at her nerves mightily. It had been worth it, she decided, as his face lit up and his arms wrapped around her shoulders.

    "Hello," she heard Jen say in greeting. The witch had wrapped up the balms, poultices, and soaps as if it were a prize for some suburban competition. "Does a Billy Kaplan live here?" Man Kaplan, as Agatha had come to name him, smiled warily at her. "It is." Jen smiled impossibly wider. "He entered a drawing at my store and won." She held the basket out. "I've come to deliver it myself to...to thank him for his support. If it weren't for him, and several others, I wouldn't be here."

    "Touching," Agatha whispered into her ear. "You've gone soft, Kale," she teased. The witch fought a glare as she waited for Man Kaplan to fetch his son. Billy stopped in the doorway with wide eyes and an open mouth. "Jen!" He rushed to give her a hug, forgetting his audience. "It's so good to see you. You look great!" The poor witch gasped for air as the gift basket was rammed into her chest. "Nice t'see you too," she told him. Jen sucked in a breath as Billy released her. She cleared her throat, presenting the basket for a second time. "All the good stuff, just for you. Congratulations on winning the, uh, The Road Competition."

    "Play along," Agatha instructed the teen. "Your dad thinks you won some raffle." "I'm just glad I was able to get my name in," Billy said, winking at the witch. Woman Kaplan smiled politely at the pair, silently waiting for the stranger to leave her son alone. Agatha made a note to stalk the woman. She still didn't know her name. "By the way, I've closed my Eastview location. I'm moving to another state," Jen informed carefully. "Here's my new business card. Agatha can tell you more about it." She handed Billy a small pink card with a series of bewitched runes. "I better head out now, but keep in touch, okay?"

    Basket in hand and card pocketed before his parents could see, Billy wished her a safe trip. He made up a quick lie about Jen being a relative of his boyfriend before leaving his parents to take their pick from the basket.

    "How did she know where to find me," he asked his ghostly guide.

    "She's stalking you," Agatha told him with a mischievous twinkle in her eye. "What did she mean when she said you could tell me more about this?" He held up the pink card with a quirked brow. "What is it?"

    Agatha settled on his bean bag, spreading her legs a bit. "It's a summoning card. New form of magic. Witches hand them out to coven members and close friends in case they're needed." She fiddled with her brooch, mind drifting elsewhere for a second. "You activate it with a spark of magic and intent. Think of it like sending a text that says, 'Here boy!' If you're powerful enough, it'll zap 'em here in the blink of an eye."

    "Huh...That's pretty neat," he said, more to himself. "Did you ever have a summoning card?" Agatha wrinkled her nose at the thought. "Ugh, as if! I only ever needed to summon one witch and all I needed was a fresh body for that. Much faster than incantations." Billy stashed the card in his wallet. "You must have missed her all the time then." She would have told him off for his presumptions if she weren't so deep in a memory of her estranged lover. Agatha could almost feel the mist against her cheeks as Death approached from the tree lines to collect another soul. The woods. Always bodies deep in the wooded shrine. An altar for the cosmic being that held her heart as tenderly as the dagger Death was known to caress.

    "Agatha," Billy called. He looked at her with those wide eyes that begged for a story. (Always wondering, begging.)

    "Mama, why do we kill witches?"

    It was a pity she couldn't run from her thoughts the way she used to.

    The ghost leaned forward, carding through her memories for a tale to make another spark of Nicky flicker in the boyish face in front of her.

    "Tell me about how you met Rio," he said as if he managed to read her mind this time. "Not that one," she answered softly. The idea made her phantom heart clench. "Not yet." Someone needed to remember for her when time droned on for too long. Goodess! How did Rio manage? She hadn't even been a ghost for a week and she was already sick of it. "Tell me about your first magical lesson," he suggested instead.

    "You were born evil."

    A bitter laugh escaped her lips. "Wasn't much of a lesson, I'm afraid. No, think of something else. One that doesn't involve my family, preferably."

    "So, no stories about Nicky?"

    The nickname stung worse than the reminder of her mother. He had to be doing it on purpose at this point. "Why don't I tell you about some of the things I remember from being your babysitter? Like the time you cried so much you nearly broke Wanda before I could." Billy sat up straighter, eyes impossibly wider. "What do you mean by that?" "The Hex was already stressing her out, but you and Tommy were really doing a number on her. She-"

    "No," he said, cutting her off. There was an edge to his tone. (His Maximoff rage.) "Why were you trying to break her? How?"

    Oh, right! The kid didn't remember that her and Wanda were enemies. Nor did he know that she was behind the scenes sowing chaos to fracture a fragile woman's mind in search of power to reincarnate her son. If only she had succeeded...

    Instead of elaborating, she sent the boy a wink. "Maybe when you're older, I'll tell you." By the clenching of his jaw and the blush of his cheeks, he'd fallen for her trick. So naive, that one. "Anyway! You and Tommy cried and cried for hours. The whole neighborhood could hear you two. It was very annoying."

    "Why were we crying?" She watched him try to remember the event.

    "Not sure, really. I always chalked it up to your moth-, Wanda wanting to have an interesting story line. But then you two aged yourselves up to about five years old." She hummed at the memory, a smile growing across her face. Agatha recalled drinking and imparting some motherly advice. She understood the struggle of trying to slow down time to keep her child young. To hold them in your arms just a little longer. To put a space between each damning, rattling cough.

    "You're being very wispy today," he told her gently. Billy rubbed his hands together awkwardly. "What else?"

    "Well, there was a day where you forced me to watch Finding Nemo and The Lion King. I must say, Scar and I would have totally dominated the Kingdom, and then I would have killed him." (And with the aquatic film, she'd never felt so much anxiety for another parent before. Had that happened to her Nicky, the world would have been turned to ash. And, no! No, she didn't cry. Those were just allergies from Wanda's stupid, gross laundry soaps.) "What was I like those days? What did I look like?"

    Agatha found no reason to lie. "Cute as a button," she rasped. "You were calmer compared to Tommy. He was a whirlwind of chaos. But you both protected each other, so I can't fault either of you for that."

    "I miss him." Billy lowered his head. "I still can't pinpoint his location." "We'll find him," she assured him. "You just need to hone your skills first. No point on going on a wild goose chase with those fritz-y powers of yours."

    "I know." He shot her a small grin. "You don't look as sad anymore. You must have enjoyed spending time with us."

    "Me? Sad?" Her voice, as noted by Billy, raised an octave. She cursed him silently as he gave her a knowing look. "Look, being dead ain't all it cracked up to be, okay? Enjoy the ability to take a nap while you can."

    Billy walked over to his record player and set a new disk on the round table. "But you make it look so fun," he teased. The Chain by Fleetwood Mac filled the room. "I'm gonna do some studying. No pranks. No shenanigans."

    She stuck her tongue out at him before settling deeper into the beanbag chair. She let her form fully dissipate as the sound of turning pages added to the musical talents of Stevie Nicks. Billy would know she was there. Somehow, he'd learned to sense her presence even when she slipped into the In-Between. She had to be close, but Agatha couldn't think of a reason to not be at the ready should he need help. (Goddess help her! There was a twinge of motherly affection blossoming at a rapid pace now that she didn't have a coven to distract her.)

    Slipping away into the Ether was the closest thing to taking a nap. A way to rebuild her strength after all her chaotic pranks and hauntings. At least she could hear the music and Billy's steady breathing in this inky, dark realm. He was always within arms reach, safe and healthy. And, in a way, so was Nicky. She could sense his soul resting on the Other Side. Her only sons students, flanking her side. Needing her.

    Agatha closed her eyes, and waited.

    Chapter End Notes Have some mother-son bonding with a serving of yearning Agathario in these trying times.

    I love you guys. Please stay safe.

    You Know...Many Hands Chapter Summary Agatha decides to follow Billy for a day.

    Chapter Notes See the end of the chapter for notes In all her years, Agatha Harkness had never once set foot in a school of any sort. Not when women were allowed in their spaces. Not while sniffing out a new set of victims. Not even while hunting Wanda in her hex had she done so. Had she attended school events which were always hosted outside, yes. But the witch avoided schools like the plague. In fact, she'd willingly lick a bubonic pustule if it meant she didn't have to enter one. Agatha had held this sentiment until Billy. Sweet, albeit irritating, Billy. Bored out of her mind, she dared venture where she'd never ventured before.

    Upon entering the shiny halls of linoleum and polished brick, the ghost nearly vomited ectoplasm all over a teacher. She thanked the goddess she was buried in her own backyard, well away from the screeching of pubescent voices. The sound alone would have woken her from the dead if she weren't already a spiteful ghost.

    "Maybe being born during a time without a proper toilet was worth it," she said into the Ether. "There's absolutely no way I would have attended as a child." Agatha sneered as a preppy cheerleader walked through her, bubblegum popping bitchily. (She'd never killed a kid before, but that didn't mean she wasn't willing to try if necessary.) Billy shut his locker, head lowered. His usual fire heavily subdued as his classmates surged around him. The boy made his way over to his first class of the morning, unaware of his second shadow. He dropped into a desk chair, careful to remain in the background. A few students bid him a good morning before doing the same. (Instead of chasing down witches, she should have been burning schools to the ground.)

    "Why so shy?" she wondered aloud. Agatha drifted slightly closer, examining the boy she thought she knew. Nothing seemed out of place to her, so she chalked it up to Billy just being bored. Well, that and the fact that he was still coping with the loss of two brilliant witches a few days ago. Still, she didn't like to see her the kid looking so down in the dumps. She'd cheer him up the second she found a chance.

    An older woman, likely in her fifties based on the gray adorning her head, instructed the class to quiet down. She pulled out a worn copy of a book and slipped some glasses on. "Would anyone like to remind the class where we left off in The Masque of the Red Death?" She looked around the room, waiting.

    Agatha decided she didn't really want to hear Rio's first holiday be retold and returned to the empty halls. The witch peeked in on boring class after boring class. Nothing of interest in each disappointing room. Suddenly, a shimmer caught her eye. Floating leisurely, she found an old man mopping near a water fountain. There would be nothing wrong with stumbling upon a janitor in a school. It's just...well...he was dead. Cleaning was a bit pointless for someone of his nature. Agatha made sure to say as much.

    "You're new," he rasped, eyes drinking her in. "Wasn't aware our drama teacher offed herself?"

    "Oh, you are just a treat," she laughed. "Not a drama teacher, but I am a teacher who loves drama." Agatha pointed a finger at the mop. "How did you manage to take that with you?" "It was my only friend," the man told her. He cracked a smile at her frown. "Fucking with you, toots. But I did spend a lot of time with it, so it was like a personal artifact." "Hm...Interesting. Well, what's your story? I can't think of a single reason for hanging around this place." (Goddess! Is that what she looked like to the living?) She sought her brooch to fend off self-deprecating thoughts.

    The janitor shrugged. "Got no one on the other side to see. At least here, it's like I never left." He sniffed, looking away. "It's homey."

    It certainly didn't look that way...

    Agatha nodded slowly. "Right, that's just..." Utterly pathetic, she wanted to say. And she would have told him if she wasn't literally, actively hiding from her son. "So, mopping? You don't do anything for fun around here?"

    "I scare the brats when they make a mess in the bathrooms, but that's about it." She looked around at all the shiny lockers and poorly designed posters with cheap paint. "But do you really want to be here? I mean, you could always travel. There's a whole world outside of these alabaster walls just waiting for you." Just because she had chosen to suffer a fate worse than death didn't mean someone else had to.

    The old man shrugged. "Can't leave unless I'm moving on. You know how it is." "Sure, but you could probably do a lot better in your next life," she told him. If Rio put in a little more effort, there wouldn't be so many ghosts, she reasoned silently. Agatha reached into a locker and began rearranging a student's belongings in hopes of scaring them later. In fact, she was definitely gonna do the whole hallway now.

    "Next life?"

    Ah, there was that hopeful tone she'd grown accustomed to in her many years of conning witchkind. At least she couldn't kill him. "You heard correctly." Agatha turned back to him. "No telling how long it takes, but crossing over does give you the option. You might not have anyone right now, but you could. All up to you, Big Guy."

    The man pondered her words, hands twisting along the pole of his phantom mop. There was a long, drawn out moment of silence between the two made more deafening by the lack of their own heart beats. Finally, he offered her a smile before pushing his mop bucket down the hall. "Okay...?" Agatha watched him walk away. A soft light began to radiate from his body the farther he got from her. In the blink of an eye, the janitor was no more. "Huh." To be entirely honest, she was expecting to see Rio usher him away. She tucked her disappoint away and decided to find another sad, sorry soul to experiment with.

    The cafeteria, Agatha decided, was her least favorite place within the sprawling prison complex. It was louder and rowdier than the hallways. Too many high-pitched voices grated on non-existent nerves. Still, she roamed the cavernous room in search of a certain curly- haired teen. "You'll make a whole road to torment your fellow coven members but you can't do anything to shut these people up," she groaned. Agatha made a face as she spotted Billy with his boyfriend. They were a cute couple, don't get her wrong, but young love was just gross. All those touchy-feelly emotions and holding hands and laying on beds of grass while soft hands stroke inky tendrils and...and...

    "Wouldst thou like a flower, m'lady?"

    Agatha rolled her eyes at herself. "Pull it together, you simpering fool." She drifted over to the pair as they exited the cafeteria. "Taking food into a library! The youth of today!" The trio entered the drastically quiet room. The couple found a table to sit at. Based on the pleasantries they shared with the librarian, this was a tradition of theirs. It warmed and disgusted Agatha to no end. She nearly tripped them in an attempt to stop the insanity of it all.

    "So...?"

    Billy looked away with a blush as his boyfriend leaned in close, a teasing smile tugging at lush lips. "So?"

    "You gonna tell me what happened when you ran away for a whole day?" Trent, no, Teddy offered a fry as he waited patiently.

    The young witch pressed his side against his boyfriend as he accepted the greasy morsel. "Promise you won't freak out?"

    Agatha sat in the seat across from them, eyes narrowed as a plan formulated. She knew that Teddy knew about Billy's odd past, but did he know about his powers? And if he did know about Billy's powers, what did he think of them?

    Teddy chuckled endearingly. "So long as it doesn't involve anymore meet-ups with strangers in dimly lit places."

    Billy looked away with a blush. "That was a one-time thing, promise." He took a sip from his juice box. "Okay, so not a one-time thing. You remember how we got that information about Westview and those two Avengers?"

    Agatha raised a brow at that. She shouldn't be surprised. Of course, he'd researched Wanda and Westview. Why wouldn't he? It made sense that he would go down a rabbit whole in search of his true identity. And, that rabbit hole would always end in that goddess-forsaken town.

    After a nod from the other teen, Billy continued. "Well, it led me on a journey with some witches. I learned some things, made a friend, that sort of thing."

    Teddy scoffed light-heartedly. "What happened to going out to see a movie with the parents," he teased lightly. "Did you at least find what you were looking for?"

    "Kind of." Billy fidgeted with the sleeve of his jacket. "I've got a brother out there. I'm gonna go look for him once I get some other stuff taken care of."

    "Well, I'm glad you're okay. I was pretty worried about you." Teddy flashed a grin to his boyfriend. "And I can't wait to meet this brother of yours."

    Agatha gagged to herself. Honestly, the amount of heart-eyed looks and fingers brushing against one another was making her sick with heartbreak. She tuned back into the conversation as Teddy disappeared in search of a water fountain for his water bottle. She made herself known, lips pursed as Billy stared at her with wide eyes. "I'm curious," she began. "Why don't you tell him about your true self? About your powers?" "Did you follow me?" he hissed quietly. "Really, Agatha! Are you that bored?" "Do you expect me to stay in your room for the rest of my existence?" She threw her hands up dramatically. "Just answer the damn question."

    Billy glanced around the room before leaning closer. "How would I even explain anything about myself to him? Sure, he knows I'm not Billy Kaplan, but magic? Our coven dying because of me! That I can create alternate realities and make them real?" "Okay, okay, chill," she huffed. Agatha gestured to the cold food on their trays. "He seems nice. You should bring him over more often. Get him used to the idea of magic so I can scare the life outta him." The witch sneered, hoping to get cheer the boy and get a laugh in return. "Go home, Agatha."

    She pouted. "Now, why would I do that? I think you need me here. What if someone tries to pick on you? You're so lanky and scrappy."

    She didn't miss the flash of blue in his eyes as he clenched his jaw. After a steadying breath, Billy held her gaze firmly. "I don't need you here."

    "I could help you cheat on a hard test," she offered. "Or-"

    "Home," he said more forcefully. "And no more spying on Teddy and I. It's weird." "Uh...is that a ghost," a third voice said from a foot away.

    Billy and Agatha whipped their heads in Teddy's direction with similar, shocked expressions. "I can explain," the young witch choked out.

    Agatha beat him to it. She floated up to him, eyeing him up with a hand tucked under her chin. She hummed in approval. "I'm his guardian angel," she announced, flipping her white hair. "You are?"

    "Confused," the mortal responded. "But you can just call me Teddy." He extended a hand before withdrawing it awkwardly.

    Billy palmed his face with a groan. "This is Agatha Harkness, my pet ghost." "Isn't that the witch that guy told us not to get involved with," Teddy squeaked. He shot her a look as he moved to stand between his boyfriend and the apparition. "I won't let you possess him or whatever it is ghosts do."

    "Cute," she laughed. "But possessing and killing him wouldn't do me any good." She waved the boy away. "I just thought I'd see what all the fuss was about. He's always giggling and kicking his feet when you call and text him."

    Billy dropped his head into his hands. "You can go now!"

    Agatha gave Teddy a wink. "Well, looks like you're in good hands Billy. I'll meet up with you when it's time to go home. I'm curious to see what your Drama Department's all about. I can get up to some real hijinks with those cheap props." She waved to the couple before hiding herself once more.

    "So...is that the friend you made?" she heard Teddy ask Billy.

    The next time she found Billy, he was in a classroom surrounded by papers and charcoal sketches. Agatha figured it was some sort of arts and crafts class and settled on a nearby desk. Unlike the first class she attempted to sit in on, the witch made sure to be close enough for Billy to sense her. Maybe if she kept quiet, he wouldn't send her home early. This school thing was starting to grow on her. (Those five would-be thespians, though? They wore fear well.)

    He flicked his eyes towards her direction before he continued to drag his charcoal stick along the large drawing pad settled on a large wooden easel. The forms he sketched were abstract but easily identifiable.

    Their coven on the road as a full moon rose overhead.

    It transported her back to those cool, perpetual nights. The softest of leaves cushioning their heels as they walked. A sense of comradery Agatha hadn't felt since before coming into her powers. The Witches' Road had been rather impressive despite the horrid trials they faced. (And, it had given her a chance to be around Rio without fighting and spitting insults.) Agatha watched in silence, appreciating the teen's concentration. His brows bunched and his lips pursed just so. She wondered if Nicky would have branched into drawing had he been given the chance to live a full life. Already, Agatha could imagine papers and crayons strewn about as he doodled by the hearth of hers and Rio's cabin. (Was it still standing?) You're quiet, Billy sent her telepathically.

    She hummed a laugh. "Just admiring your skill," she told him honestly. "You've got a real knack for that stuff." She wasn't a fan of the blackened fingers, though. Billy fought a laugh. Just a knack? He set his charcoal stick down before grabbing a charcoal lifter.

    "You should do one for me," she playfully suggested. "In all my glory." Agatha floated to rest atop the easel like the weightless being she was.

    Sure. Any specifics I should include?

    She froze, not expecting him to agree. "Uh...surprise me! I'm down for anything, really. Just be sure to capture my good side."

    Billy gave her a grin before returning to his current drawing. It helps if I know more about you, he pressed gently. What was your hair like when you were younger? Ugh! Of course he would find a way to start up his questions again. She tapped her chin in mock thought. "Oh, I don't know...Brown and wavy. It was late 1600's Salem, so we didn't have much in terms of hair fashion. A purple dress, of course, with lacing in the front. No brooch, then. My mother hadn't died yet."

    "Your brooch belonged to your mother?" he asked aloud. Billy's ears turned red as his classmates turned to stare at him. "Sorry, was listening to an audiobook," he lied. His magic created a random headphone to help support the fib. It was enough for the bored students. They turned back to their own projects without a single protest.

    Agatha tapped at her Hecate brooch with a thick swallow. "It did," she managed to say. Thinking about her mother was almost as painful as thinking about Rio and Nicky. "I simply acquired it after her untimely demise."

    Lilia said you killed your old coven. Why?

    "Wouldst thou like a flower, m'lady?" Two witches lying on a green cloak in a field of grass. Legs tangled. Hands clasped.

    "Agatha Harkness!" Her mother had spat the words as she stumbled upon the pair, eyes aflame. "There hath ne'er a disgrace such as thou."

    Agatha considered running away from him. (Always running.) "You heard her at my trial," she rasped.

    Billy raised his head to look up at her. You're not evil, Agatha. You're not great; you're not bad. You're...human.

    She wrinkled her nose despite the phantom tears gathering in her eyes. "Gross," she spat. "Don't give me that sappy crap, kid. I killed for power and for fun. I'm as evil as they come." He rolled his eyes at her. Sure, Jan. Whatever you gotta tell yourself to get through the day. The teen pulled out a can of setting spray and spritzed his sketch. School will be done in about an hour. My next class is AP Calculus. You should join me so you can learn to count past ten.

    "You..." She moved to swat his head, but let it phase harmlessly through him. "Just for that, no story about my coven."

    As if you were actually gonna tell me, he mentally scoffed. Billy moved to put his things away as the bell rang. If you don't want to come, go wait in the car.

    Agatha considered flipping him off, but flew away instead.

    After some practice, Agatha managed to tether herself to the fabric of Billy's passenger seat before school let out. (Already, she could hear the thunderous pounding that heralded the freedom of subdued horrors. She shivered.) Now, the witch would be able to have her first car ride since running into the young Maximoff and dying. Even though the risk of dying was non-existent, she still hated the horrid contraptions. (It didn't help that Wanda had lobbed an entire vehicle at her once. Maximoff's and vehicles...They were not a good mix.) At least Billy appeared to be a safe driver. On his way to school, an older man with the thickest pair of spectacles passed him.

    Finally, though it had only been minutes, her wayward pupil entered the car. Billy huffed and ignored the grin she offered as he slid into his seat. He tossed his bag into the passenger seat and into Agatha's transparent form. "Rude," she grumbled. "What if I don't want your homework inside my abdomen? I already know how to multiply."

    He shot her a look. "You can sit in the back if you'd like."

    Agatha resisted the urge to flip him off. "I miss you being a floppy-eared puppy. Remember that?" The witch made a face and clasped her hands together. "What's a coven-stead?" she told him in the same mocking tone she'd used on the road.

    Billy turned on the AC, waiting for the hot car too cool down. (Not that Agatha had noticed. She was always cold, like her beloved's heart.) "Why can't I just have a relaxing drive home?" he argued. He flipped his visor down to fix a few errant curls. "You don't have to bring that up all the time, either."

    "Rawr! Someone's grouchy." She patted his shoulder, pouting. "Do we need a snack and a nap?"

    Billy dropped his head against the steering wheel. "Why did you have to follow me to school? Seriously?"

    She shrugged. "Never been to one. I was curious."

    Dark eyes searched her face.

    "But know this: I don't trust you!"

    Agatha quieted as she waited for the Maximoff to pass judgement. She was shocked when he turned the key in the ignition and pulled out of the parking lot. Honestly, she was expecting another argument. The witch contemplated leaving him to his temper tantrum, but figured it was better to clear the air now. Nothing worse than being dead for and guilt-tripped by the son of the Scarlet Witch. There was still a possibility that he'd get fed up and try to banish her again. Banishment, as the ghost had decided, was a pretty good threat to hang over her head. So, to placate the moody teen, Agatha kept her thoughts to herself and focused on not accidentally untethering herself.

    The car slowed as red and blue lights flashed up ahead. Police cruisers, an ambulance, and a fire truck blocked their road home. When no slipped curse or irritated sigh filled the air, Agatha looked over to find Billy gripping the steering wheel tightly. His face had paled drastically as a sheen of sweat leaked from his adolescent pores. She could hear his breathing quicken the longer he stared at the scene ahead of them.

    "You okay?" she asked, though she dare not reach out. Not yet, at least. Witches and emotions weren't a very good combo.

    The teen struggled to suck in a breath as his eyes welled with tears. "Fine," he choked out. Agatha did the only thing that felt right and rested her translucent hand over his, materializing it to provide some comfort. "Why don't you pull over and take a minute?" She nearly didn't recognize her own voice. It hadn't been that soft since...since Nicky went to sleep and never woke up.

    Billy nodded, a tear shaking free. He pulled off the road and threw on his hazards. His breathing grew quick and shaky, but his hands continued to grip at the steering wheel. "You're okay. You're alive," she assured him. Agatha felt confident in her approach until a dark green shape took form near the more badly wrecked vehicle. A part of her wanted to rush to her lover's side, but the other part kept her firmly tethered to Billy. There would be other instances to see Death. Right now, the kid needed her more.

    "Are they...?" He gestured to the roll over with a shaky hand.

    Agatha settled for a mostly truthful answer. "Already ferried away. It was quick. And knowing Rio, she's far more gentle with those who had a violent passing. If they were innocent, that is."

    Billy jerked his head in a pained attempt to nod. "I hope William was...There was so much blood..." He gasped for air before stumbling out of the vehicle.

    Agatha winced as she heard him spit up his lunch. She floated to his side to pat his back. "I could...ask her...maybe?" She cast a glance over at the wreckage. Rio was still attending to business. The soul didn't seem please to know they'd passed. The cloaked figure of her estranged wife stood still. After eons of ushering souls into the next phase, she was likely desensitized to the begging. Did Nicky beg?

    Billy waved her off as he moved away to pace. "I just need a minute to myself," he rasped. "Go...go do whatever it is you two do to greet each other."

    The witch wasted no time in sneaking up on her wife. Already, she had a whole plan concocted to surprise the immortal entity. Hands over the eyes, lips to the shell of an ear. It would be glorious! It would hot! At least the thought was until she heard Death's true voice. It halted her, feet away, from the only being other than Nicky that she'd loved with her whole being. How would she react to seeing her as a ghost? How would she feel about seeing her at all? Refusing to let her do her job twice? That had to have stung. (As if telling Death to leave her along for all eternity hadn't wounded the unkillable, godlike servant.) Suddenly, leaving Billy alone seemed like a very idiotic thing to do.

    Agatha quietly floated backwards towards the car. Her attempts were futile as the hooded being twitched her head to the side, listening to her flee. (Who was she to think Death wouldn't sense her of all people! She should have just bullied Jen instead of stalking Billy.) Agatha opened her mouth to give an excuse, but booked it back to the car. She didn't bother to look behind her to see if Rio had fully turned to watch her.

    "Hey, you gonna be ready to go anytime soon?" She found the young witch rinsing his mouth out with a bottle of water. He shot her a look before spitting into the grass. "Turns out my son isn't the only one I can't face," she said with a self-deprecating laugh. "Come on. Vamanos!" Billy rolled his eyes before weakly pulling himself back into the car. The pair did their best not to look at the wreck. Agatha, unfortunately, still saw Rio watching them as they drove by. Her eyes, the most beautiful shade of hazel in the sunlight, met hers for the briefest of seconds. Guess we'll be having that meeting sooner than later, she noted apprehensively. As if she hadn't sought her lover ought earlier. As if she didn't miss her terribly. Nervously, she began to hum the only tune that brought her peace.

    "Walk, walk, walk the road. I walk the wind-y road..."

    Chapter End Notes stares blankly at a wall

    That's Not Why I Came Here (But It Is Why I Stay)

    Chapter Summary Agatha gets scolded by the unlikeliest of people.

    Chapter Notes Sleep is for the weak. Agathario is for the strong!

    See the end of the chapter for more notes "Are we just not gonna talk about it?"

    Agatha continued to sulk and knocked another figurine to the floor. If she truly cared, she'd be disheartened to see she'd run out of objects to abuse. At least Toto and his owner were reunited, even if it was on the dusty carpet Billy refused to vacuum. (He actually did, but wasn't going to clean her mess up. Just another battle of wills between the two.) The goth teen tossed a pencil at her. It passed harmless through her, just as his pair of used socks had. When she ignored him, again, he threw himself down on his bed. "If you won't, I will. You're being a baby. The biggest baby, actually. All you do is whine and mope. You should have talked to her and-"

    "Did you know that Wanda could perform multiple spells at once?" Agatha interrupted as if he hadn't said a word to her. (Billy was not about to try and be her therapist. Not if she had a say.) "There were so many spells layered over one another, I could sense her from three states away. Even I am incapable of such a feat. Not that I didn't try."

    Billy scowled, but didn't ask her to stop. He was probably glad she was finally talking again. She supposed it would weird anyone out if their companion suddenly went quiet for three days straight.

    "Naturally, my mind is protected from hostile take overs, so I went to investigate." The ghost picked Toto up from the floor, playing with him in the air as she spoke. "One mind is hard to control, consciously. Two minds, a feat. But nearly a thousand souls bent to her will without much thought?" She spat out a laugh. "That's a whole level of power all witches can only dream of. It could have been all mine if I had just kept my mouth shut. I just never pegged her for a quick study."

    "You were going to steal her magic, weren't you?"

    "I did, for the briefest of seconds, have it all." Agatha could still feel the surge of chaos magick thrumming under her skin. It was a high not even the Darkhold could compete with. "But I got cocky. So, let that be a lesson to you, kid." Finally, she turned to stare him down. The folds of her dress shifted lazily around her ankles. "Don't think that, just because you've gone unchecked all your life, you can just take what you want from anybody. That you can order whoever you want around."

    He scowled at her. "If you're going to be so miserable, go back to your house. I've had it with whatever this is," Billy told her as he gestured to her.

    Agatha felt relief annoyed by his irritation at her. She chased the familiar hit, the sting, for another. "It's still a mess because someone threw Rio through the window. You're paying for that, by the way."

    "Forgive me for trying to save your back-stabbing butt," he hissed. "I should have left you to fight your own battles."

    "I gave you all the time I could, Agatha!"

    Being dead sucked. Sucked, sucked, sucked. She'd trade eternity for the ability to shut her own head up.

    She leaned in with a sneer. "Is that what you were doing? Pardon me. I must have dozed off during your light show. Any witch worth their salt would have been able to hold their own for much longer."

    Billy pursed his lips together, eyes reddening. He pointed to the door as he sucked in a shaky breath. "I don't want you here if you're going to be like this. Maybe it worked on Rio, but I'm not going to stoop to your level. Get out."

    Agatha blinked.

    "Go!"

    She flew through the roof before he could banish her for real. The witch hovered above his roof as the wheels in her non-existent head struggled to make sense of what just happened. Of course, she knew what happened. Agatha had just never been challenged from that angle before. She didn't know how to proceed with her anger. Didn't know who could hurt her just right for her to feel something again.

    "He's smart. I'll give him that," a familiar voice said. That voice that once soothed, once inspired, once cut so deep. "I never learned when to walk away when you were lashing out." Agatha whipped around to find the last person she needed to see. She shrunk back from the figure sitting on the roof. (What was with Death and roofs?) The witch would run, but she knew Death would only give chase. "You've been avoiding me," she rasped out. Maybe the Green Witch was here to collect her.

    Rio gave a half-shrug, feigning indifference. "You're the one who told me to stay away. I was just honoring our deal."

    The ghost chuckled dryly. "The deal I didn't hold up? Figured that would have told you you didn't have to." Because I never meant it, she didn't add. Rio knew this, though. Had always known. She was just hurt too deeply from hearing the words aloud to call Agatha on her bluff.

    "Then why have you been avoiding me?" Dull hazel eyes regarded her. Searched her. Agatha looked away, grateful that she couldn't blush or cry. "Because I didn't think I deserved to see you." Her soul ached, reached, for her other half. 'I missed you' was kept tucked away. (How soon is too soon? There's not exactly a handbook for the dead to use. If there was one, it probably didn't have breakup tips for those whole fooled around with Death.) The pair let a beat of silence keep them company before Rio grew a small flower in her palm. With the blooming of the seedling, Death's gaze began soften. "He misses you. He won't wait forever, Agatha."

    The floating witch flinched at the statement. "Not yet," she whispered. "I'm not ready. I might never be."

    "Then when, Agatha?"

    Agatha turned away from the harsh reminder. This time, she did run. The ghost slipped into the In-Between. Into the closest thing to Rio's warm embrace. Billy was too close. Nicky was too far. Rio...Rio was everywhere, always. There was no escaping the entity. The constant flow of life and death.

    Of course, Death didn't have to move from her perch. She existed in all realms simultaneously. The only thing that changed was the roof to a felled tree trunk. Thick roots twisted and grew in all directions.

    "In the end, all roads lead to me."

    The silence is broken by a simple, "Why?"

    Rio didn't have to elaborate. Agatha knew exactly what Death was inquiring about. "Because I couldn't do anything for Nicky. Because you had to do your job when it came to him. But Billy was different. I had a choice for once."

    Death kept her distance, but moved closer. The shadows curled towards her in greeting. "I tried," Rio began, voice breaking. "You don't know what it meant to give you that time. What it cost me."

    Her dead heart clenched painfully in her chest. She turned back to the hooded figure, lip trembling. "I forgive you," Agatha told her firmly. She held Rio's gaze. "I had always forgiven you. I just didn't understand. I didn't...I didn't want to."

    Rio looked small as she asked, "But now?" So many emotions were held in those beautiful eyes of hers. Fear, hurt, anger, anguish, and hope. So much hope.

    How many seconds did Death have to count since meeting her? (If the change in her appearance was anything to go by, too many.) How terrible was she to have broken Death herself? Could anyone else claim such a feat? Of course, Rio had admitted to her on the Road that no one else had been given special treatment. No one else got the chance to hold her except Agatha. With that special treatment, Death had bestowed a gift on the witch despite the risk. And when that gift proved disastrous, Death provided another. Both times, Agatha had foolishly, blindly, taken them for granted. How could she be expected to even begin to make up for such grievances? Only fools would think a single kiss, a single confession, would fix the damage she'd caused.

    Agatha drifted closer, daring to risk being reaped. (Not like she didn't deserve it. Not like she didn't deserve it.) She reached out to drift a hand along her beloved's face. Her palms tingled at the sensation. Like being tickled by flower petals in the spring. "I am disillusioned, my love, and I beg your forgiveness. I have hurt you far more than you have ever hurt me." Rio leaned into the touch with a warmth Agatha hadn't felt since kissing those deadly lips. Skeletal features melted away to reveal a face that was beautiful and heartbreaking. "Do you truly mean this?" she whispered. A tear threatened to spill over the gentle swell of her eyelid. Agatha nodded as she thumbed away the tear. She wished she could easily wipe away the hurt that lay firmly embedded in her beloved's soul. "Maybe I should have led with, 'I miss you.' But I've never been one to follow the rules," she told her other half. Agatha smoothed Death's hair with her free hand as if they had all the time in the world. "But I won't blame you if you want nothing to do with me."

    "I was going to leave you two to tear each other apart," Rio admitted, a smile curling upwards. "Make you two suffer for leaving me alone. Especially since you ran from me the other day."

    Agatha swallowed habitually. "But?"

    Rio pulled her in close, a hand gripping at her hip. "But then you started picking on the boy the way you used to with me. I didn't want someone else to carry that scar, too." "Ah..." She felt the need to run again. (Coward. Coward. Coward.) "Can you blame a girl? He likes to poke and poke at me. I didn't know ghosts could get migraines, but-" "Agatha," Rio told her firmly. "I let that boy live because you asked me to. I'm not going to let that sacrifice be in vain. Find someone or something else to take your aggression out on, but not a child. Not if he's your current version of Nicky."

    Now, she did try to jerk out of Death's grasp. "He's nothing like Nicky," she spat. "He's just like Nicky," Rio argued. "I may have kept myself hidden, but I still watched. If you really mean to make amends, don't waste your time lying to me. We both know exactly how you feel about him."

    Agatha settled as she warred with her options. Blood for blood, she reasoned. If Rio can show me her scars, I can too. "I'm not good, Rio. Not for you. Not for Billy." The cosmic being threw her head back with a laugh. "Oh, Aggie," she breathed. "Maybe you don't see me as your enemy anymore, but you clearly still see yourself as one. I wonder what it's gonna take for you to pull those blinders off. I want you to see what I see when I look at you."

    The witch felt like a child as Death forced her to face one of her many demons. At least her tormenter was Rio and not her mother. "We've already had that discussion plenty of times," she reminded sourly. "I don't really want to have it again."

    "Another one of your 'not yet's," Death noted. She raised her chin, eyes staring out into the Great Beyond. Agatha knew that look. She'd seen it constantly when the two had been more intimate. Truly, she didn't envy Rio's job. The hooded entity looked back at Agatha with a ghost of smile. "I think you owe someone an apology. Do that, and I'll know you mean the things you've said."

    Agatha scoffed. "Was admitting fault not apology enough for you?"

    Rio rolled her eyes, a chuckle slipping out. "Not to me. The Boy."

    "Billy?" The ghost pursed her lips. "He'll be fine. I bet he's already gotten over everything. He's surprisingly good at bouncing back from the horrors of his existence." "The Boy..."

    "...Billy..."

    "...is just as dependent on you as you are him. Apologize," Rio ordered. "Or, I'll accept your nullification of our deal and take him. Your choice."

    Agatha pouted. "But he's the one who started it!"

    "Agatha."

    "Fine," she groaned. "I'll make sure I didn't hurt his dumb feelings." Rio brushed a stray lock of white back, tucking it behind an ear. "You know, I think I like you like this."

    "What? Vulnerable?"

    "Free."

    Agatha felt her mouth fall open. She promptly snapped it shut, clearing her throat. "So...am I forgiven?"

    Death laughed softly. "You should get The Boy a familiar." She pulled back, skeletal features returning. "Te veo."

    The ghost instinctively reached out for one last touch. (Please, Goddess! Just a little more time!) She swallowed back a sob as Rio flickered away like a flame dying in a gust of wind. Agatha let herself feel her disappointment for a second before steeling herself to greet Billy. It wasn't until she exited the In-Between that she realized what Rio had told her before leaving.

    Time in the Ether was different from that of the Living's. What had felt like an hour long meeting with Rio ended up being a few days away from 'The Boy'. (He was collecting nicknames the way Wanda collected dead relatives.) Agatha made a quick trip to her grand tomb (her house) and collected a certain critter that decided to not go down with the ship. Unsurprisingly, it was a difficult trip from Westview to Eastview with a living thing in her arms, but she did it. (Take that, Mom! Bet you can't do that, either.) Now, all she had to do was sneak Señor Scratchy into the Kaplan Residence without anyone noticing. No biggie! The upstairs window was her best option, it seemed. Man and Woman Kaplan had family over, so Billy would be distracted. Agatha unlatched and eased a pane open, her strength beginning to wane. Finally, Señor Scratchy was safely deposited on the floor of the ungrateful Maximoff's bedroom. That's an oxymoron, she noted with an inward giggle. "Did someone switch sides during Wanda's Hex," Agatha cooed to her beloved rabbit. "He reminds you of Nicky too, huh?"

    He moved to nibble at one of Billy's house slippers.

    "Careful, or you and I are gonna be ethereal besties." She hummed to herself. "Speaking of dying, why aren't you? I just know I didn't leave you anything to munch on while the rest of us popped off." Agatha winced as she failed to solidify her hand. Billy was well off. He could afford another pair.

    The door to the bedroom swung open, revealing the Maximoff of the hour. Billy stopped in his tracks as he stared down at the rabbit demolishing a slipper. Shreds of fabric littered the floor as beady eyes trained themselves on the would-be witch. He let out a long sigh, shoulders dropping. "Where did you come from?" Billy crouched down to cradle the bunny to his chest. "You must be hungry."

    Agatha cleared her throat with another wince. She was in the process of learning what happens when you expend too much energy for long periods of time. The ache in her soul was unfamiliar and unwanted. "Surprise," she whisper cheered. Problem was, she was actually trying to shout at the boy. A trip to the Ether was needed asap! "Why do you have a flower in your hair?"

    That was not the reaction she was expecting. Agatha reached up with both hands, brows bunching together in confusion. Her right hand found a small, pink flower tucked behind her ear. The stem had been woven around a strand of hair. "When did she...? Never mind." Finally, Billy caught on to her pain. "Is something wrong? Are you finally moving on?" Agatha scoffed. "Hell no!" She waved his silliness off. "But you better take good care of Señor Scratchy as if I were. Every witch needs a familiar."

    He pet the bunny, brows creased. "Have you given him to me before?"

    "Look, I'd love to have a heart to heart and talk about you coming over all the time, but I don't have much time right now. Mama needs a nap bad." She flipped her hair, but was careful with Rio's gift. "I just wanted to say I'm sorry." Agatha gave him a curt nod before she let herself begin to fade.

    "That's it?"

    Exasperated, she rematerialized. "I'm just following orders, okay?"

    Billy shot her a dark look.

    "Good, extremely wise, orders," Agatha argued. "But I feel like I'm being torn to shreds right now, so take the spark's note version."

    The teen rolled his eyes. "Well, you go do whatever you gotta do. I'm gonna figure out how to explain Scratchy to my parents."

    Agatha nodded quickly. "Yes, yes." She resumed her dematerialization process, sinking gloriously into the darkness.

    Upon her return, she found her pupil and former familiar curled up in bed with a thick spell book. Billy didn't bother to look up at her as he flipped a page. "Stole it from your house," he informed monotonously. Of course, he had.

    "Atta boy," she cheered. "We'll make a witch outta you yet." Agatha tethered herself to the carpet so she didn't have to focus on not floating off. She clapped her hands together, the action soundless. "So...I'm...sorry," she struggled to get out. (She'd rather be forced to watch Bubble Guppies with Tommy than apologize.)

    Billy lifted his head, a brow quirked. "Did Agatha Harkness just apologize? Someone's in the doghouse."

    Gotta make it up to him to make it up, sorta, to Rio, she reminded herself. Agatha composed her irritation. Calmly, she continued. "I have a nasty habit of attacking others in hopes of being attacked back. You were, for whatever reason, trying to cheer me up. I will try to do...better." (Goddess! She missed being able to drink.)

    The Maximoff looked stunned. Agatha did her best to not be offended. "I probably shouldn't have been so pushy," he settled on. "I don't like when Wanda's brought up. I bet me asking about Nicky and Rio doesn't help your mood."

    "Not usually, no." Her hands reached up to touch her brooch and flower. "I can't promise it won't happen again, Billy, but I'm going to try."

    He looked at her the way Nicky used to after his innocent heart forgave her for an outburst. She wanted to scream into the Ether.

    "Mom and Dad said I could keep Señor Scratchy," Billy announced. "I was wondering..." Agatha smiled, unbidden. "You and Tommy used to visit in the little bit of time Wanda allowed. Time was different in the Hex." She pointed to her beloved familiar. "This adorable traitor must have sensed your potential, and slotted you as my replacement. He always favored your calmness over Tommy's overexcitability. You would always go straight to him when you could come over."

    Billy stroked soft fur in thought. "I think...I think I can remember that." The ghost shivered at the thought. (The dog was still buried in Wanda's lot.) "Right...Well, I hope he's been behaving himself. He's got a knack for trouble."

    The Maximoff laughed. "Tell me about it. No one's shoes are safe." He pressed a kiss to the bunny's head. "But Dad doesn't mind. He said he always wanted to have a bunny since he was a kid. My parents love him!"

    "Man Kaplan has good taste," she noted with a hum.

    "Jeff," Billy reminded.

    "Yeah, whatever." She ghosted a hand over her former familiar with a sad smile. "You take good care of each other," she instructed. "His magic is just awful," she groaned good- naturedly.

    "Could we," Billy shrugged. "Could we have a lesson?"

    "Use your purple," a gentle voice whispered.

    Agatha sniffled. "Allergies," she mumbled. "What exactly did you have in mind?" The curly-haired boy sat up straight, energy buzzing off of him. (If she stole a bit of it to endure her current plane of existence, who was going to notice?) "I found this old spell used to transmutate organic matter. I thought I'd start by working with plants before moving up to more difficult things."

    Pleased, the older witch gestured him from the bed. "Your room is nice and all, but magic is best practiced in the wild. You don't want to accidentally turn those parents of yours into pumpkins. That would be a bit difficult to explain to the police."

    Billy sat in Agatha's ruined garden, feet away from his mentor's grave, and focused on a blade of grass. Agatha had tasked him with turning the blade of green into a leaf. So far, he'd succeeded into setting the piece on fire. He stared at his palm harder, eyes wide and trained as he willed the plant to do his bidding.

    "He's going to give himself an aneurysm," a voice whispered into Agatha's ear. The warm presence behind her embraced her before being physically touched.

    The ghost bit back a moan as hands lightly touched her hair. (Goddess, it's me, Agatha. Thank you for this second chance!) She lolled her head to the side to meet Death's gaze. "Come to watch the show?"

    Rio rested her chin on Agatha's shoulder with a lazy grin. Her dark makeup was slightly subdued today. Smokey, but not heavy like a forest fire. "He'll never get it if he doesn't make a connection."

    "I know," she told her companion. "But, he needs to learn that for himself." The Green Witch scoffed. "At the expense of my precious babies? I don't think so." She slipped past Agatha with ease. "Boy," she ground out. "You're doing it wrong." Billy whipped around with wide eyes. "Agatha!"

    Part of her relished in him seeking her out for help, but the deepest part of her that she thought she had buried a long time ago panicked at the urgency in his voice. She materialized, rushing to Rio's side. "You've offended Rio's sensibilities," she explained quickly to the frightened teen. "So, now she wants to take control of my lesson." Rio drifted her gaze back towards the white-haired ghost, a smile stretching across her face. "Do you get deja vu-oo," Death sang.

    Agatha's brain short-circuited as Billy dusted himself off. Just what in the hell are we doing? "It only makes sense The Green Witch would want to show me how to do it right. Clearly, Agatha's not much help," he grumbled. Billy side-eyed the living(?) witch. "I thought you hated me."

    Death flashed the Maximoff a manic grin. "I do." She thumbed the hilt of her dagger, salivating at the thought of reaping the Body Snatcher. "But Agatha and I have an agreement, so you live to see another day. That, and your disrupting even more of the natural order by messing up such a simple spell."

    Meanwhile, Agatha was still trying to figure out if Rio was toying with her, or if she was genuinely flirting with her again. She recalled the flower, Rio's traditional farewell phrase, and now the touching. (Goddess! The Touching!) The witch drifted aimless along the grass as if representing her train of thoughts.

    Rio reached out and tugged her back to her side. "Running?"

    Agatha jerked back as if she'd been burned. She caught the flash of panic slide across Death's face. "To a cold shower," she joked, hoping that was the right answer. The cosmic entity relaxed, her hand still bunched in the fabric of the ghost's dress. "Boy, tell me what your trying to do."

    "Billy," Agatha corrected.

    The teen scoffed. "You guys really are two halves of a whole." He shook his head, curls bouncing lightly. "Agatha was teaching me to transmutate a blade of grass into a leaf." Rio turned her head dramatically, eyes comically wide, to look at Agatha. "An animal, maybe. But Aggie here can't perform green magic to save her life. Oops!" Oh! We're bantering, the dead witch realized. She nearly slapped herself for being so dense. Agatha feigned a gasp, hand pressed delicately over her heart. "Well, I never!" She heard Billy and Rio share a laugh, the sound a balm to old wounds. The witch settled her hands on her hips. "Go on then, Ms. Green Witch. Show Beauford how it's done."

    Rio rolled her eyes before reluctantly releasing her grip. "You walked the Road. It may not have been real, but bits and pieces of it were true. Green magic is about becoming one with, and understanding, nature." She pointed to her own bare feet, toes wiggling gently. "Get those horrid things off."

    Agatha was content to watch from the background. It was one thing to receive lessons from Death herself. It was something entirely more meaningful to see the entity branching out to train her frenemy's frenemy's kid. It was also extremely comedic. Unfortunately, she was weak-willed and wanting. Her blue eyes tended to drift to Rio's musculature and flowing silhouette. It was enough to have Agatha reliving their last kiss. Life and Death, Love and Sorrow, Hope and Despair. (Maiden. Mother. Crone.)

    "I did it," Billy cheered. His excitement snapped the ghost from her daze. "Look, Agatha!" He tilted his palm until the baby leaf was revealed. His beaming grin warmed her soul like an ember.

    Rio smirked from her place at his side, her hazel eyes drifting over Agatha. "That's one point for me," she announced smugly.

    "I wasn't aware it was a competition," she challenged with a matching smirk. "I've already taught him loads of things." She waved her hands about, shaking her head for dramatics. "Body snatching doesn't count," Death informed, a bit more seriously.

    Agatha pursed her lips. "Had to make sure he survived so the Road didn't collapse on me," she said.

    Rio hummed. Her back straightened, eyes flashing green. She looked back at Agatha with a smoldering gaze. "Te veo."

    Before she could bid Death 'adieu,' she was gone. Agatha let out a small sigh. She turned back to Billy, smile returning. "So, your first lesson with Rio? That's gotta be pretty special, even for you."

    He grinned widely. "She called you a bunch of things, but you weren't paying attention." "A mutiny," she tutted. Agatha ruffled his curls. "I'll give her a piece of my mind later. For now, I want you working on that spell every chance you get. Once you can do it without speaking the incantation aloud, we'll move up to whole plants."

    "Why didn't you tell me about the incantation?"

    Agatha pursed her lips "We really oughta get home, kid. It's getting late." Billy stared at her for several minutes. He visibly noted the way she avoided looking at him. The boy began to laugh, tears gathering in his eyes as he clutched his sides. He sucked in a breath before telling her, "you totally missed her."

    The ghost turned her back on him, arms crossed. "I don't know what you're talking about." "Agatha and Rio, kissing in a tree," the teen began to chant.

    She covered her ears. "Sorry. Can't hear you. Bad connection," Agatha told him as she began to dematerialize her form.

    "K-I-S-S-I-N-G,' the boy belted, face red.

    The witch entered the In-Between with a smirk. "First comes love. Then, comes marriage," she finished quietly. It filled her with a new sense of purpose. Yes, she'd help Billy find Tommy. But, trust, she was going to win her wife back. Then, she was going to torment the Maximoff's. Oh yes, it was all coming together. Agatha tilted her head back and cackled. Chapter End Notes Worry not, Reader. I know one conversation doesn't fix such a damaged relationship. We just gotta lay the foundation.

    Primal Night Chapter Summary Billy sleeps. Agatha stands guard. Nothing could possibly go wrong.

    Chapter Notes Agatha watching over Billy in episode 4 altered my brain chemistry. We're gonna explore that with some tasty angst.

    See the end of the chapter for more notes The Road Agatha feels a familiar fear grip her heart as Teen collapses. It's sudden and sharp. Digs its talons into the muscle beating rapidly in her chest. Her heart weeps internally as Teen bleeds externally. Even if, and that's a strong if, this is Wanda's son, the thought of losing him hits too close to home. She doesn't even stop to question what would happen if he dies in his own hex. Agatha can only focus on getting him out of the trial room and onto the road. There's absolutely no excuse for the way she feels about the boy. For the way her eyes begin to water and her mind goes blank with worry. She didn't birth him. Hell, she didn't even get a chance to really know Billy! (And, honestly, her remembering his name is sign enough that she had a soft spot for the silent twin.) When the time came to enact the final phase of her hunt, she didn't physically harm the twins. They were never in any real danger because they were never real. At least, that's what she thought. Looking back, she would have just left Wanda and her sad reality alone.

    Unfortunately, she isn't a time traveler. She fucked up and played with fire twice! Now that the youngest Maximoff had dropped himself in her lap, he'd managed to worm his way through the hallowed soil that guarded her cold, dead heart. She had hoped, prayed even, that she was wrong. That Nicky had made his way back to her. That no one else could make her maternal instinct reawaken but her only son.

    She'd laugh if there wasn't such a deep, taunting gash in the unconscious teen's side. Fate was a cruel woman. Fate had a score to settle for twisting her best soldier into a dark, obsessive thing. Agatha would congratulate the Ancient Ones in kind when the time came. She'd be sure to use the powers of both Maximoff's as a big ol' 'fuck you.'

    But for right now, she really needed Jen to figure out what the fuck to do before Rio took another step. She barked orders as she cradled Billy's head in her shaky hands. The witch pleaded with Death without a second thought. (As if that worked out so well for her last time.) She didn't miss the way Rio, Death, jerked back with shock and hurt in her eyes. Once his wound had healed, the coven carried him a ways from the trial exit. Agatha assigned tasks to her fellow witches to get them the hell away from Billy. The boy needed rest, so they would camp for the night. That's what she told them, and they believed her easily. Alone, she constructed a shelter for the teen. Agatha ignored how easily she recalled building such a structure for a boy much younger and much sicker. No cough would pierce her heart tonight, though. All the while, Rio watched her curiously from the other side of the path.

    "Don't you have anything better to do," she hissed at the Green Witch. "Go...go pick your next target. I'm sure Alice would make a tasty meal."

    Rio huffed out a laugh. "You really want me to hang around a bunch of other women? Women who have the hots for me?" She nodded, eyes falling back on the sleeping boy. "So you can play-"

    "Go!" Agatha instinctively moved to summon magic to her curled hands. All it did was earn her a harsh laugh. She watched Rio closely as she skipped away, the rest of her insult settling in the empty space between them.

    Ignoring her deranged wife, the witch shrugged off her coat. She couldn't help herself. He's still young, she told herself. That's the only reason I'm helping him. it didn't matter that her line of defense fell flat as she stroked curls away from his brow.

    He was so much like Wanda. So much like the woman that trapped her in one hell whole just for her son to trap her in another. Agatha decided that was what it meant to be a Maximoff. Inconveniencing everyone when they, themselves, were inconvenienced. Annoying trait, really.

    The longer he slept, still as a corpse, the longer Agatha worried he might not wake up. The thought brought up painful reminders of a similar night. A night two pairs of eyes closed, but only one opened with the sun. Here, there would be no sun to wake her if she closed them. There were no critters that would rouse her if she nodded off. So, she just wouldn't sleep. I'll use it to break Wanda if we ever meet again, she reasoned. That ought to teach her not to create souls without bodies. It would crush the other woman to know she'd been replaced by the magic-stealing Witch Killer. She could hear Wanda already, pleading in her fading Sokovian accent.

    Agatha sat on a stump, telling herself lies in hopes she'd believe them. In hopes Rio would believe them. Because, at the end of the day, Death did not appreciate being cheated. Especially not by little boys who ran around in stolen bodies. No. Rio would take him, too. She couldn't bear the thought. Not after Nicky.

    With the moon as her companion, Agatha stood guard. Magic or no magic, no one would be taking the boy unless it was on her terms. Rio's rules be damned!

    Kaplan Residence Another night, another boring routine. Agatha moved Man and Woman Kaplan's car keys and wallets around as she waited for Billy to get out of the shower. There was only so much she could do to entertain herself. She stole a glance at the kitchen clock with a frown. Nearly midnight and the teen was still up. She clicked her tongue in annoyance. Once he was finished minimizing his pores, Billy finally left the steamy bathroom for his bedroom. The teen wore soft, cotton pajamas with fuzzy socks as he shuffled into the room. Sensing that the water was off, Agatha entered with hands on her hips. "You were supposed to have been in bed three hours ago," she reminded him. "Children's brains can be severely altered by lack of sleep and poor diets. Do you want to lose your potential to poor life decisions?"

    Billy pressed a kiss to Señor Scratchy's head before putting him away for the night. He turned to face her, head tilted with a face of annoyance. "Sleeping wasn't your priority on the Road." "Well, duh," she laughed. "We were being chased by the Salem Seven and the hell of your own making. Now, you need to get lots of rest. Witches-"

    "Can lose control of their magic when tired and emotional," he finished. "I know, Agatha. You don't have to worry about me."

    She blew a raspberry. "Worry," she chuckled, though it sounded more strangled. "The only thing I worry about is that Chemistry grade. I'll be sure to have Jen tutor you on the weekends now."

    Billy made a face as if he wanted to say something particularly acidic. He stopped himself, though, and climbed into bed. "Goodnight, Agatha."

    She knew that tone. That was his 'this conversation is over' tone. (One he'd inherited from Wanda, no doubt.) Agatha wasn't sure what exactly she'd said or done to upset him, but she'd figure it out later. The ghost moved to sit at the edge of his bed, dematerializing to give him a sense of peace. She relaxed as his breathing evened out.

    The Witches' Road had picked at an old wound, effectively turning the villainous witch into a worry wort. After his panic attack, Agatha had hovered around the boy a bit more than usual. If he ever needed her, she'd be right there to smooth any wrinkled brows away. Of course, now that her and Rio were on speaking terms again, she didn't need to worry about Death coming in like a thief in the night.

    Then again, that could be a ploy. Death could be toying with her loneliness. Billy was still a body snatcher, still an abomination to the Sacred Order. But surely Rio wouldn't...She'd been so nice last time they saw each other. If it was all a rouse, Agatha would likely die a second time. Nicky would never see his mother again if Rio tricked her. She'd be reduced to ashes and her own broken heart.

    Billy twitched. A gentle whimper escaped him as his hands twitched and gripped at his sheets. He dug his face into his pillow with a whine. A soft blue crackled and sizzled as it tried to form into whatever it felt he needed.
