    This was precisely why witches needed to keep themselves healthy and well-rested. Agatha shifted closer to run a knuckle softly down his cheek. She didn't dare to do more than that. There was no telling how he'd react if she woke him up. If he sent her away......Despite her worries, the teen settled and his magic faded.

    Briefly, she considered haunting his dreams. If she knew what was bothering him as of late, she could help him. But if he was anything like his mother, she would easily wind up trapped for a third time. So, Agatha kept her telekinetic hands to herself and let her presence comfort him. She hoped Rio wasn't spying on her. This would lead to one hell of an awkward conversation.

    As the hours crawled by, she moved away from the bed to snoop. After deciding to be his guide, she'd explored every knook and cranny in his tiny room. (Tiny compared to her expansive one in Westview.) There wasn't much left to discover outside of his many, many, many hyperfixations of the witchy kind. The kid was decidedly boring and a major fanboy. (She made it a point to ignore all of the notes he'd written about her. Billy promptly hid the papers once she moved in.) With nothing to do, she began to tidy up his room according to her standards.

    She had just moved to his closet when Billy began to thrash around. Agatha flew over, hands moving to still his flailing limbs. "Shh," she soothed. "It's just a bad dream. You're safe." The boy opened his eyes briefly, tears spilling. There were unfocused as they settled on the ghost in front of him. "You have to help her. You did it. You fix it," he sobbed. "Save her!" Agatha swallowed her guilt and cupped his face. "Billy, we're not on the Road anymore. There's nothing I can do."

    He moved to grasp her wrists, but his hands passed through them. It sent his addled brain into a more severe panic. Billy scrambled to sit up, breaths coming in harsh pants. "No, no, no! There has to be a way. Please!"

    "It's a bad dream, Billy," she reminded firmly. "You're in your bed in Eastview. No more trials. No more death." She drifted through the bed to keep contact with his face. The ghost thumbed away tears, shushing his cries. "I'm here, Billy. I'm not going anywhere." "I want Tommy," he rasped. "Where's my brother? What did you do to him?" "We haven't found Tommy," she told him, gently and calmly. Agatha continued to stroke his face, his hair, anything her hands could apply pressure to. "We're still working on a way to find him."

    The Maximoff's brain worked overtime to overcome the cruel dream. After a few shaky breaths, he gave her a nod. "I know that. He's out there."

    She nodded along with him, offering him a reassuring smile. "See? Much better." Agatha pressed a kiss to his temple. "Mama's got you." She froze, horror marring her ghostly features. "I-, I mean..."

    Thankfully, blessedly, Billy's eyes had already drifted shut. His body flopped back down as he gave in to the exhaustion his nightmare gave him. If he heard her slip up, she wouldn't know until he woke up. Maybe he would think it was part of his dream. Maybe he'd convince himself it was Wanda or the Woman Kaplan.

    Agatha put a large distance between herself and her pupil. Her hand sought out her brooch, gripping it for dear afterlife.

    The ghost didn't say much as Billy rushed to get ready. She ignored the radiant sunlight peeking through his blinds. She ignored the music the boy used to energize himself before school. She ignored the way he talked at length as if she hadn't betrayed the memory of her son to comfort another. Not that Billy was her son, that is. (Shut up. Shut up. Shut up!) Agatha's mental wellbeing dangled precariously above a pit of despair. The string holding her up was fraying quickly. Each time she looked at Billy, she would be faced with the still form of her late son. Agatha wanted so badly to be a mother, once upon a time. But now, with all her experience, she wondered if she even deserved her second chance. She forced Nicky to suffer for her own selfish needs. Now, she was selfishly seeking to fill the hole her actions had left. Selfishly hanging around a boy that probably wanted nothing to do with her. He already had two mothers. Why should she try to stake a claim after nearly handing him over to Death?

    Her actions had scarred Billy. Just as she had scarred Rio. Just as she had wounded Nicky by demanding, "more." (Goddess! She was a glutton for punishment.) Agatha considered taking the plunge. To remain in the Ether and just rot away like she deserved to. There, she couldn't hurt anyone else. Couldn't steal sons. Wouldn't be able to feel the pain radiating in her chest. "Agatha, did you hear me?"

    She looked at him, eyes wide. When had he gotten out of bed? "Huh?"

    Billy rolled his eyes, a grin firmly residing on his face. "I was asking if you wanted to come to school today. They're making us watch a school production of Wicked. Figured you might want to prank the cast and crew to spice things up."

    She pursed her lips before giving a curt nod. "Sure. You call the shots, kid." (She could always wallow in despair later. That's what eternity was for, right?)

    The teen grinned widely. "I thought you might like that idea." He checked his wardrobe pick in the mirror before turning to her. "Any notes?"

    Agatha let out a chuckle. "You're wearing something other than blue and black for once. What's the occasion?"

    "I dunno. It was in my closet when I woke up." He turned back to the mirror to fluff his curls. "During our first trial, Alice told me she liked my hair. I guess I'm just feeling sentimental." The ghost looked away, wringing her hands. "Well, best be off, huh? You need to eat before school."

    Billy grabbed his backpack from off the floor. He tilted his head to the side as he stopped at the door. "Do you...miss eating?"

    At that, Agatha laughed loudly. "Y'know, I don't. Less hassle as a ghost." She followed him out of the room to find Man and Woman Kaplan munching away happily. (She'd try harder next time she hid their silverware.)

    Her kid pupil ate a healthy serving of pumpkin spice oatmeal before pressing a kiss to the cheeks of his parents. Woman Kaplan looked pleased with the boy as she bid him a good day. (If only she knew her son was long gone.)

    By the time the play rolled around, Agatha was back to sulking. Today, the noise of the children didn't annoy her. All those young, curious voices tortured her. She wished she had Rio to run to as kindergarteners ran through her. They crashed into waiting arms before being led towards the auditorium.

    "Mama, Mama! I made some friends today!"

    Agatha bristled as parents sat with their children. All happy faces and breathing, living spawn looking at them with undeserved adoration. She longed for her power. She longed to raze the place to the ground. Agatha deserved to have more time with her child. What made these magicless mortals special? What did they have that she didn't? She wanted their breathing to stop. (Her energy surged a nearby outlet, the plastic charring slightly.) Billy entered, Teddy's arm looped in his, and sat in a row not far from the stage. He reached out to her telepathically, urging her to join them. The Maximoff sent a wink in her general direction. Can you get a good look at the cast behind the curtain?

    She moved to the stage, eyes boring into the crowd. Reluctantly, Agatha turned to pass through the heavy curtain. Students and teachers moved around in a mad dash for last minute adjustments. Now what?

    When the play starts, you should trip the guy in the green wig. He's been loudly spouting hate against same-sex couples, Billy told her. He managed to project an image of the target into her mind. She noticed that the kid was handing the young witch a note with a not-so nice word on it.

    Agatha seethed. (No one picked on her emo son but her! Wait...no! Not her son. Definitely not her son! Fuuuucccckkkkk!)

    The auditorium lights dimmed and a hush fell over the crowd. The stage lights focused their beams as the curtains were drawn back. The cast danced to their first mark in their ridiculous get up. A poorly constructed dragon on a grandfather clocked let out a roar. (The budget must have been tight. They totally used a recording from Jurassic Park.)

    Agatha sneered at the bully as he approached her. She'd trip him all right. Trip him off the stage and into a hospital bed! The witch moved to deliver her vengeance when the group began to sing. The first few lines stunned her effectively. The combined lyrics were her final straw.

    "No one mourns the wicked! No one cries, 'They won't return!' No one lays a lily on their grave."

    The sudden release of her anger burst the bulbs to the stage lights behind her, sparks raining down. The actors screamed and ran for the wings. The smoke triggered the fire alarm, which sent the younger students into a blind panic. Parents rushed the exits. Teachers tried to scream above the chaos. In short, Bedlam had erupted. Agatha didn't care. She gathered herself up and teleported as afar as she could get from the mocking of the Universe.

    "What the hell was that?" Billy burst into his room, ready to condemn the ghost for her actions. "That's not what I meant when I-!" Unfortunately for him, his guide was not hiding in the Kaplan Residence. "Agatha?"

    He rushed down the stairs, grabbing his keys from the door-side rack. "Forgot my phone at the store," he shouted to his parents. He didn't wait to hear what they had to say. What's her problem this time? The witch had been off all morning. She didn't react at all to him just saying nothing but a string of 'Rio' and 'Nicky'. She didn't turn her nose up at his idea regarding school. She didn't even follow him during his classes. But she had looked away at the mention of Alice before he left for school. That gave him a little to work with, but didn't explain her reaction to the play. Unless...Had Rio and Agatha gotten into a fight while he was asleep? Had Rio tried to reap her at the play and that was what created all the chaos? He pressed his foot more firmly on the gas pedal.

    Billy was grateful that Westview was as close to Eastview as it was. It meant he could reach Agatha's house in record time. (By now, the residents were used to him visiting the home of their late hero. They figured he was some relative of hers.) He pulled into the driveway and quickly exited his car.

    "I wouldn't go in there," Rio warned from the porch. She fiddled with her knife, eyes dark. "Why not?"

    "She gets this way sometimes. Usually when Nicky is involved." Death pushed off from the wall she had been resting against to eye him warily. "Did you do something? Say something?"

    He wanted to laugh at how protective the two were of each other, even when separated. "If I knew, I wouldn't be here." Billy made a move to enter the house, but the Green Witch blocked his path.

    "Come back tomorrow." She cast a glance through the ruined front door. "She can be...cruel when she's upset."

    The boy wondered, not for the first time, just how toxic a relationship had to be for Death to walk on eggshells. "She needs someone to talk to."

    Rio scoffed as she sheathed her dagger. "She needs space." She pressed into his personal space, staring him down. "Or do you have some magical balm to heal her broken heart? Can you help her forget the pain of losing her child?"

    He faltered. "No..."

    "Because you've never lost a piece of you before," she snarled. "It burns. Forever. And any little reminder is like salt being rubbed into the wound. It eats at every single cell of your being. Turns you rotten from the inside out until your nothing but a bitter person." Billy swallowed thickly. He remembered watching Agatha react to her own hallucination in the first trial. The sob that tore from her throat still echoed in his head when the sadness crept into her eyes. However Nicky had died, it was still as fresh as it had been that day. He would never doubt how heavily it weighed on the ghost. How it seemed to only get heavier now that she was dead.

    "Being alone makes it worse," he argued weakly. "Besides, I'm tough. I can handle whatever she has to say."

    Death laughed harshly. She moved aside as she bared her teeth at the boy. "I think I know what happened now," she hissed. "Go on then, hero. See if you can save her when Death could not."

    The teen pushed past her, steeling himself for whatever condition he might find Agatha in. He was acutely aware of the chilly presence following him as he pushed deeper into the house. The lights were off, which didn't do much given the time of day, but it made the place feel especially eerie. He climbed the stairs, hoping she'd be haunting her old room. Billy found the spare bedroom empty, so he moved on towards the master bedroom. Inside, the place was filled to the brim with props Agnes had made to match her reality. The most damning evidence of her internal suffering came in the form of drawings done by the woman to emulate her dead son.

    "Agatha was cruel, but never this cruel," Rio whispered from nowhere and everywhere. Billy didn't miss the hurt that gave Death an edge to her tone. "Did Wanda know about Nicky?"

    The being didn't respond.

    Sighing, he returned downstairs. He already knew not to check the kitchen. Agatha didn't seem like much of a cook, nor would it hold enough sentiment for her to haunt. The teen looked around the living room and noted all the greenery depicted on the walls. Subtlety was never her strong suit, he thought with a sniff. Billy moved to the basement and immediately felt a drastic chill in the air. It wasn't the kind that came with being in a dark room. No, this was the chill one felt in the dead of winter. The kind that made your breath mist in front of your face and numbed your nose.

    "Agatha," he shouted into the darkness. "What's wrong?"

    "Why didn't I think about that," Rio told him sarcastically. She materialized to his side in normal streetwear. It looked extremely odd after seeing her in more witchy outfits. "The Boy came to speak to you, so come on out."

    The house rumbled as if suffering the aftershocks of an earthquake. Billy looked around with wide eyes, his magic sparking to life at his hands.

    "Put that away," Death ordered. "You don't even know what you're doing." "What if she's being attacked by something?"

    Rio laughed, her teeth flashing in the dim light. "Not likely. No, she's just wailing loud enough it can be felt in your plane."

    "Wailing?"

    "Crying," she hissed. "That thing you do when you're upset."

    Billy looked away, effectively embarrassed. "Is that what she's been doing this whole time? I can't hear anything."

    Rio frowned. "I don't know how long she's been audibly crying. Her soul has been screaming since last night." She shifted, hand gripping her dagger's hilt. "I was busy with a mining accident. I couldn't come see what was wrong."

    The house shook again. This time, the teen swore he could hear a guttural scream faintly bouncing off the stone walls. "Agatha!" He hoped she could hear him. Billy used his telepathy to reach out to her. What he found was a jumble of words and noise. It sounded like Rio, a boy, and a few other voices were all screaming over each other. He pushed forward with his mind, trying to reach the core of his mentor's mind.

    A hand tugged him to the ground as objects flew from the shelves around them. "Whatever you did, don't do it again," Rio shouted over the noise.

    Above them, a screeching Agatha appeared. The white glow to her form had darkened, and her face was frozen in anguish.

    "What's wrong with her? Why does she look...wrong?"

    "She's on the verge of turning into a vengeful spirit," the Green Witch told him. "Her grief is starting to overcome her."

    "So, what do we do? Do we...Do we have to help her pass on?" He looked between the two, heart racing. Billy didn't want to lose his mentor if he didn't have to. He'd finally come to accept her presence in his life. Enjoyed the banter and the care she'd gifted him. But if she needed to cross over, he'd help her.

    Rio, on the other hand, looked as if she'd been mortally wounded. "She's not ready. Making her cross over would only make things worse. She'd come back as pure grief and anger. There'd be no helping her at that point."

    There has to be something we can do, he wanted to yell at Rio. She's just stuck in her own thoughts. Maybe if I... Billy flexed his fingers, magic pulsing through the air. A blue haze stopped the flying objects above them and held Agatha in place. He moved on instinct, and stood. A ball of blue grew in his palm before he tossed it at the transparent witch. Rio lunged for Agatha. The two were hit with an echoing, "No!"

    The room went dark.

    Chapter End Notes Agatha would definitely throw a tantrum after realizing she's adopted a Maximoff lol. The author proceeds to weave her trauma with Chemistry in to her fics. (Please, no more Chemistry!)

    Giveth Sight Chapter Summary Billy did a no-no.

    Chapter Notes Fair warning, the author doesn't know the rules of Old English and the like. Enjoy! See the end of the chapter for more notes The world spun for an eternity as Billy tried to right himself. Colors, sounds, scents. They all blended in with one another until he found himself standing in a field. It took several seconds before he found his balance, the world righting gradually. The teen looked around, confused. "Where am I?" And where is Agatha and Rio?

    Mountains of ice stood in the distance as elk grazed. Green grass swayed in a gentle breeze, a few flowers dotting the land. Lush trees grew sparsely, their branches waving to the boy. A bird cawed overhead, the only foreign sound in the immediate area. As far as he could tell, there weren't any nearby towns to help him identify his location. When he inhaled, Billy swore the air tasted younger. Then, he felt a tugging sensation from deep within. It tickled a bit. Like when you sit on the edge of a blanket and someone pulls at it anyway. Suddenly, his feet began to move on their own accord. Where he was going, he wasn't entirely sure. What he did know was that he had no control over his body, only his eyes. Still, he moved towards the tree line as if on a mission. Surrounded by the greenery, he drifted along an invisible path until he reached a cave. Short shrubs and stones dotted the ground around the entrance. Inside, a group of nomadic people wearing furs knelt around a body. Jewelry and fragrant petals were bestowed upon the fallen traveler. Somewhere, a small fire crackled with life. The group sang softly in a language Billy didn't recognize. The words, however, felt like a farewell.

    Billy was forced to bend down and touch the cold body. He tried to jerk his hand way as unfocused eyes stared up at him. To his surprise, the figure moved. He felt his hand raise, waving the person towards the entrance of the cave. Billy shivered as the opening shifted to a portal of green and black shadows. To his right, the person followed as he led the way to the swirling void of green.

    "Hey! Wait, wait! I'm not dead," he tried to shout at the person. "Rio! Agatha!" The portal swallowed them up.

    Billy shivered and twitched, eyes tightly squeezed shut, as he waited for his soul to be reaped. When nothing came, he opened his eyes. Standing before him, a young woman with auburn hair looked down at a man. Her dress was torn, her hair was wild, she bore a busted lip, and a bruise on her left cheek. There was a familiar fire in her eyes and blood on her hands. The woman raised her chin as a figure joined her.

    "Agatha?" Billy wondered aloud. Why was he seeing his mentor? What happened to her? The woman didn't answer him. Instead, she turned to face her companion. "We must remove the body or more will come. The coven..." The possible Agatha grabbed her stomach with a cry.

    In doing so, Billy finally noticed the blood trickling down her legs. He wondered what kind of wound she had suffered.

    "Worry not, sister. Thou art hurt gravely," the other woman said. "See to thine injuries." She helped the bleeding woman step away from the body. "Thine enemy is slain. Thy sisters shall attend to the rest."

    Billy looked down at the man before repeating the gesture from the cave. The person jerked awake, cursing. "Foul woman! Thou art a witch!"

    For the first time, Billy heard a familiar voice. This time, it came from his lips. "And a witch hath slain thee, hunter," Death laughed. "What good did thee hope to accomplish from such a heinous act? Thou art but a beast driven by lust. Thou hast lost thy good name and cast aside the light evermore."

    "Hateful creature," the man spat at Billy who finally realized he was in Rio's body. "Thou art beneath me. Submit as womankind ought do and repent."

    Rio cackled, her true voice bleeding through. "Such malice shall be rewarded, hunter. Thou hast chosen the patch of damnation. Thy soul, mine to take." A skeletal hand gripped the witch hunter, a scream filling the air. He thrashed and swung at Death, but no hits ever connected with her form. Death's dagger was produced and sunk into the blackened soul with a sickening squelch. The man turned to dust, eyes still wide with terror. Billy, as Rio, sheathed the dagger with a gentle laugh.

    The world spun in a haze of green before Billy found himself in yet another field. He could taste a tang on his tongue. Like smelling rain before a storm made itself known. He moved forward and found himself in front of a hut. Somewhere, a baby cried shrilly. The teen never felt a tug as Death entered silently. They moved like a shadow, sliding across the floor, until they were standing at the foot of a bed. The woman from earlier, the one that looked a bit like Agatha, held a bundle in her arms.

    "Is that Nicky?" Billy tried to ask Rio.

    Death did not respond.

    "Thou art born from wickedness," the woman hissed to the crying bundle. "I care not for thee, child. If not for a harsh winter, thy life, the Green Witch taketh. May the Divine Mother deliver thee swiftly unto Her."

    Billy felt a stir of emotion, foreign and fiery.

    "Sister Evanora," a woman said from the doorway. "What news of the babe?" The teen stared hard at the bundle as it sought contact from its mother. Evanora never let their skin meet. The baby was no 'it,' he realized. The baby was none other than his mentor, hours old and already promised to Death. Another cry stirred an anger deep within Billy. "Come forth, sister. The babe hath much life. She will prove herself yet." Evanora held the newborn out for her visitor to take.

    The other witch brushed past Death, tightening her shawl around her shoulders with a shiver. "What calleth thy babe, sister?"

    "Agatha," Evanora responded blandly. "In hopes she might honor the Divine Mother." Billy was forced to turn away from the scene, likely due to Evanora's change of heart. He could still hear the harsh, "I ought to have slain you the moment you left my body," that she would later tell her daughter. Rio had already known the truth of those words before they were even uttered.

    Another shift, a new location. Carts laden with barrels and bundles of hay passed Billy as if he weren't even there. Technically, he wasn't. Across the path, an elderly woman took her final breaths in a nearby cottage. Strangely, Billy didn't find himself moving towards the tug. Instead, his eyes were trained on a young maiden. Her curly hair lay across her shoulders, a crown of flowers adorning her head. The young girl, about fifteen years in age according to Death/Billy's guess, laughed with a fellow witchling. Rosy cheeks and blue eyes called to the entity. Beckoned Death sweetly to her side.

    The old lady was still breathing, so the tug was ignored. Billy felt a tingle across his cheeks before his body moved to gaze down into a barrel of water. The reflection that met him was none other than that of Rio's. Round-faced and innocent. Nothing like the dark-eyed entity that was in the basement however long ago.

    Pleased with her new look, Rio moved towards the teen with confident steps. Before the two had the pleasure of meeting, the tug in her chest burned white hot. Death was unceremoniously ripped away from the street. The old woman had finally keeled over. Death glowered from the room as a sob filled the air. <>A bell was rung from the window, alerting the coven to the demise of an elder. Billy felt a frown form as the young maiden slipped away. His eyes tracked the girl as long as they could, but eventually, she disappeared. He wondered who she was to have caught Rio's attention.

    "I'm feeling much better," the woman said from the bed. "Have you any water for drinking?" "At the River," Rio replied dryly. "I'll take you there."

    Billy anticipated the shift before it even happened. The world fell away, rotated, then solidified once more. Not far from him, a group could be seen advancing on someone. The maiden from the village stumbled away from the men. Her face was red as if she'd been crying. The men didn't seem to care as they cornered her. Death moved closer, the air charged with energy. There was something, some scent, that Billy could practically taste. Death seemed to know what it was. Seemed to want more of it as she sniffed it out. "Please, kind sirs, you mistake me. I am but a humble girl seeking herbs for her ailing mother," the maiden informed. She raised her basket to show them the greens and whites of her harvest. "I know not of this witchcraft."

    "She sounds really familiar, doesn't she?" Billy said, more to himself. Still, he hoped Rio might have heard him.

    No response from Death as they watched the scene unfold.

    A bearded man moved forward, a torch held aloft. "Pray tell, child. What ailment does your mother suffer that requires the Devil's poisons?"

    The maiden looked between the four men advancing on her. She dropped her basket and ran for the woods.

    "Witch," one of them shouted. The taller of the group notched an arrow and let it loose on the girl.

    After the missed shot, the group chased after her. Death flowed through the trees, hoping for a body or two. Billy urged the girl to run faster. "Find your coven," he tried desperately to tell her. The girl made no sign that she heard him. Together, they all moved through the forest until huts came into view. He quickly realized her mistake. "They'll kill everyone if you go that way," Billy shouted. "Fight back!"

    "Mother! Mother," the girl cried.

    A graying woman appeared near a row of white stones, her face full of thunder. "Stupid girl," she hissed. The older woman produced a bell. "Hunters to the south!" The clang of the bell echoed through the air as the torches got closer.

    Witches ran to the woman's side. Their magic pulsed as they attacked the witch hunters head on. Billy finally put a name to the tang on his tongue. "Magic. I'm tasting magic," he said aloud. But the specific scent Rio was following had moved away. Death moved to a low hanging branch to watch the battle unfold. Her eyes scanned, her nose sniffed, in hopes of finding the source.

    She grew a flower, massaging petals between her fingertips. She found something amusing, a laugh filling the air. From her perch, the group looked like little playthings. Toy soldiers on a carpet acting out a silly fantasy.

    "Where are you going," Rio wondered aloud. She slipped back to the ground as the maiden scrambled away from one of the men.

    Blue eyes searched the crowd for help as her back met a tree. The shouting from the coven and other hunters filled the air. Magic and arrows whizzed wildly into the night as the battle continued.

    Suddenly, Billy was looking at Rio, the young maiden nowhere to be seen. The green figure tilted her head to the side, watching him. It sent a shiver down his spine. Death looked hungry.

    "You and yours will burn this night," a man snarled from the thicket. He must have lost his torch during the chase. The hunter charged at her with a knife, hate filling his blackened eyes. Billy began to panic and raised his hands in defense. The magic that leapt form his fingertips were no longer blue, but purple. But not just any purple. No, Billy knew this purple. He watched it arch through the air and strike the man in his chest. The hunter fell to the ground with a strangled cry, hands clawing at his throat. Before the person he was possessing could celebrate, the figure in green moved closer. It looked like Rio was a ghost as she drifted through the darkness towards him. A siren calling a sailor out to sea. "Who are you," the maiden asked. There was terror, Billy noted, and another feeling. Something close to curiosity, but not quite. It felt a bit like that indescribable emotion he felt when he first saw Teddy. Not quite love, but definitely not indifference. It was magnetic. It was exciting.

    "I have no name," Rio answered. She looked shocked at her new voice, and pressed her fingertips to her lips. Death pressed onwards. She held out the flower to Billy. "Who are you, my lady?"

    Billy felt his mouth open, words on the tip of his tongue.

    "Agatha Harkness," a woman snarled. The tone sparked a fear in the teen. Something that made his stomach drop and his blood run cold. He wanted to hide. Wanted to run. Rio vanished in the blink of an eye, flower forgotten. Billy could still feel eyes on him, though. It was the same feeling he got when Agatha was watching him from the Ether. Death had not abandoned Agatha.

    Evanora rounded on Agatha, and Billy, her hand striking a cheek solidly. The pair fell to the ground in a daze, the sting searing their nerves. "Will you never disappoint me, child? Must I always pay for your wrongdoings? Four hunters. Four! And you bring them to our home!" "Mother, I-"

    "What insolence! You've no right to speak." The gray-haired woman looked down at them in disgust.

    Billy sucked in a breath as a foot connected with his gut. Tears pricked at his eyes as he struggled to regain his breathing. He covered his head as he was pulled upwards to stand. Heavy hands rained heavy blows to his body until he was freely crying. "Please," he begged. "Please stop!"

    The pain vanished almost as quickly as it came, leaving Billy extremely disoriented. Rio was back, her hazel eyes staring deep into his soul. He found himself reaching for her, a tug in his chest that wasn't the pull of a dying soul. This tug felt like a want, a need, that could only be satisfied through Death's touch.

    Rio smiled and took the offered hand in hers. "There's nothing wrong with you, Agatha. Your powers make you special."

    "Mother doesn't think so."

    "Your mother's wrong." The young Death pressed a kiss to her knuckles. "She can't hold that accident against you forever."

    "You're the only one who doesn't," Agatha admitted. She returned the gesture, her heart stuttering in her chest.

    Billy suddenly felt like he was intruding on something very special. Whatever spell he cast, he was ready to undo it and find his mentor. The way young Agatha spoke, it hurt him. And if it hurt him, he could only imagine how Rio felt. To watch someone you care about grow into a powerful witch, and then into a stranger with a sharp tongue.

    Soft hands tugged Agatha along, away from the rows of cottages. "Come," Rio whispered. She smiled sweetly. "I'll teach you a spell for whenever you miss me." "It had better be a good one," the young witch giggled. (Who knew Agatha giggled! Weird.) "Not a day goes by that I don't yearn for your presence, my dear."

    The pair found themselves deep in the woods, bare feet planted on the soil. Rio knelt, a finger sliding along the dirt to create a rune. "The incantation is simple enough. It can be used to summon me for the briefest of seconds."

    Billy felt disappointment settle in his heart. "Where do you go, my friend? Why can I not join you on your travels?"

    Rio tucked a strand of hair away. "You cannot follow. Not yet. If I were to tell you, you would not want to join me any longer. I don't think I could bear to part with you, Agatha." Agatha's irritation flooded his senses. "You don't want me, do you? You want only my attention. Do not toy with me."

    "I want you more than you could ever imagine," Rio hissed. She gripped Agatha's hand in hers. Her eyes burned with emotion. "For you, I would burn the world." "Then tell me who you are!"

    "Another time." The Green Witch pressed a kiss to her knuckles. "I must go. Te veo." The boy felt a tear wet his cheek as a growl tore from his throat.

    Billy blinked, and the world was dark once more. He was still trapped in his spell, whatever it was. It looked like he was in Agatha's room on a simple bed. Just looking at the lumpy mattress made him thank whatever god could hear him. He'd never complain about his own mattress ever again if he ever got to see it again. The flame to a candle flickered before Death made herself known. She stayed on the other side of the room as Agatha combed her hair with her fingers. (If she ever came back to life, he was going to recommend her a different type of conditioner than whatever was used in this godforsaken time.)

    "You're hurt," Rio noted with a slight hiss.

    Her tone stirred a sense of relief in Billy. The teen felt a burning in his back as he turned to stare at the woman in a green dress. (He was definitely going to poke fun at Rio for her fashion sense.) "Mother doesn't appreciate my intention to improve my abilities." Rio scowled, dark and menacing. "I will see to her in due time. For now, let me tend to you, my love." She moved forward, her skirts swishing delicately against one another. Billy felt his breath hitch as warm fingers settled on his skin. Agatha, it seemed, was extremely sensitive to touch. No, that wasn't right. She was touch-starved. Her skin wasn't used to gentle touches.

    The realization made him feel sick to his stomach. No wonder Agatha had fallen for Death. No one else had shown her kindness. Not if her mother could help it. And because of her vulnerability and need for connection, she'd drawn the immortal in. "Okay, I really need to get out of here before Agatha kills me," he groaned. "Or Rio. Actually, she's definitely gonna kill me now."

    Agatha jumped with a slight whimper as hands slipped under her nightshirt to expose her back. Billy shut his eyes, not wanting to see anything he didn't need to see. "I'll kill her," Rio seethed, just as she had when the ghost of Evanora had appeared on the Road. "Why do you let her do this to you?"

    "She's my mother," Agatha protested weakly. "I want her to see I can be good. Good daughters obey their mothers."

    "This turned depressing really quickly," Billy told whoever could hear him. "I get it. She had a hard life. That's great. Not really, but I get the picture. Can I go home now?" He remained firmly planted in Agatha's body as Death healed the blemishes marring his/her back with gentle touches.

    "Why didn't you wait for me by the lake today?" Rio asked cautiously.

    Billy's heart began to race as Agatha gave her response. "I saw you today." His head turned, but he kept his eyes shut. "I saw you."

    "And now you don't want me," Death lamented.

    Panic gave way to a fondness that was strong and heady. "I don't want. I need." "Time to move to the next chapter, please," he begged his magic. "Agathaaaaaa!" His prayers were answered. In fact, his magic had thrown him back into Rio's body. He thanked the gods, the Divine Mother, and even Rio for good measure. Billy found himself in a clearing as hooded figures formed a circle around what looked like a stake. "Oh great, another trial," he grumbled. "Who're we burning, ladies?"

    Rio's chest tightened as a young woman was brought forth. The pair recognized the captive's voice immediately.

    "Agatha?! They're burning Agatha?" he asked Rio. Billy tried to move. Tried to stop them as his mentor was secured on the pedestal. What unfolded was pure insanity. Never in his life had the teen ever heard of someone being punished for being intelligent. For being hungry for knowledge. (He would need to brush up on his history when he got home. The Witch Trials were literally because women were smarter than those around them.)

    Rio seethed, eyes trained on Evanora Harkness as she passed judgement. Billy watched in horror as the coven attacked Agatha. "She's telling you she can't control it," Death howled into the Ether. "Fools!" It wasn't long before their attack backfired. Death tipped her head back and cackled as purple overcame the magic assaulting her love.

    "No wonder you hate her mother," Billy breathed. "She's the worst!" He watched as Agatha walked over to her mother's corpse and plucked the brooch from her dress. Rio clapped loudly before stalking towards the tear-stained woman. "Congratulations, my love," she soothed. Her hands cradled Agatha's face. "You survived."

    "But...it happened again," Agatha rasped. "I tried to tell them. I swear! They wouldn't listen." "Shh," Rio began, patient and understanding. "You have nothing to feel sorry for. You protected yourself, as so many have in the past. Your power is a gift from the Divine Mother, Agatha. You're free now."

    The witch slipped into her arms, holding her close. "I killed my own mother," she hiccupped. "And it felt good."

    Death rocked the witch until the tug of souls could no longer be ignored. "Go, rest. It's my turn." She shushed Agatha before the woman could protest. "Let me do this for you, mi amor."

    Billy was grateful that Agatha didn't kiss Rio. He didn't feel like adding that to his list of mental scars. As his mentor slipped away, power sparking at her fingertips, Rio rounded on the seven corpses. She stopped before Evanora, and removed her enchantments. "Get up," she spat.

    The figure stirred before rising from her spot on the ground. "The Green Witch," Evanora greeted, unaware of her companion's other identity. "Does my daughter still draw breath?" "What do you think?"

    "Get her ass," Billy cheered. "Oh, and she's not your daughter anymore." Evanora's form flickered before turning opaque. "Then I cannot go with you." Rio laughed harshly. "I wasn't going to take you, anyway. You don't deserve peace. Not after the way you've treated Agatha."

    The older woman scowled at her. "Only one has spoken to me in such a way." Evanora spat at the ground. "Not only is my daughter wicked, but a whore. To lie with Death like man and woman," the ghost sneered.

    "And to think I once carried out justice on your behalf," Death scoffed. "If you ever try to go near her, I will make your eternity one of suffering. Of that, I can promise you." Billy cheered internally. "Okay, but why is this so romantic? I actually hate how cute this is."

    The field flickered and faded as a new scene tried to form. Agatha's face flickered briefly before a voice pierced his ears.

    "Get. OUT!"

    Billy flew backwards, his back colliding with the hard ground. He slid until a wall stopped him. "Oh, thank god, I'm back," he cried. "That was a my bad, you guys. I promise, it was a total accident."

    Rio glared down at him as Agatha gripped her head.

    He laughed weakly. "I see that you've stopped...uh...grieving."

    "If you ever enter our minds like that again, I'll reap your soul," Rio growled. "What did you see?" Agatha asked. She floated up to him with a panicked expression. "Billy, what did you see?"

    "A bunch of stuff," he admitted quickly. "I think I saw a few random souls be taken, your mom. Total bitch, by the way. Sorry we almost left you with her. Uh, maybe your dad? That was a bit murky if I'm being entirely honest. I was just trying to figure out where I'd even ended up."

    Rio unsheathed her dagger. "Stop talking."

    "You know who my father is?" Agatha asked her.

    "I meet everyone," Death reminded. "Not all are worth remembering, but I would have met him at some point."

    "You totally turned that dude to ash. It was lowkey badass," he told her. Rio shot him a look. "Not. Helping."

    Agatha rubbed her temples, her form flickering. "I can't do this right now. Everything hurts." "You can thank Boy Blunder for that. You're lucky he didn't accidentally split your soul into a million pieces. He's lucky none of my magic killed him." Rio rounded on him. "Are you an idiot? Do you want to take Agatha's spot? Of all the stupid things you could go and do, you did the most dangerous one of them all."

    "I'm sorry?" He scrambled to stand up. "I didn't mean to. It just...happened." Billy looked between the two and felt his ears redden. "Eugh, you guys have been at it for a while, haven't you? Centuries of flirting and you still can't have an honest conversation." Death hissed. "Go home, Boy. You did your job and brought her out of her vengeful state. Leave the rest to the professionals."

    Billy made a face. "That's code for 'I'm gonna make out with her now,' isn't it?" Rio lunged for him only to be held back by Agatha. "You little..."

    "Now, now. Let the boy have his fun," the ghost sighed tiredly. "If anything, he get's his cheekiness from you." She patted Rio's head as if she were a cat.

    The two looked at her in confusion, but Agatha continued to flicker between the two worlds. "Behave for your mother," she mumbled to Billy. Her eyes began to droop as if she were about to fall asleep.

    Rio turned in Agatha's grasp. "No, don't you dare. Stay with me." She shook the translucent shoulders. "Why do you have to be so stubborn? Just stay!"

    "Agatha," Billy called out. "Agatha, don't leave me!"

    The ghost's eyes snapped open. "You two are so dramatic," she huffed. "I'm just resting my eyes."

    "Ghosts don't rest," Rio growled. "You were about to slip into the Realm of Lost Souls." She looked away. "I can't see you there."

    Agatha shook violently. "It hurts."

    "Of course, it does. Your ghost body got invaded by a living one." Death wrapped her arms around her wife. "Take a walk," she ordered Billy.

    He didn't need to be told a third time.

    Agatha let herself sink into Rio's warm embrace. "Am I dying?"

    "You're already dead," the Green Witch reminded, a smile tugging at her lips. "Oh..." She closed her eyes and focused on the bit of touch she could still feel. "You've been confusing the two, haven't you?"

    "Don't," she hissed. "Please, don't."

    "The more you ignore it, the worse this will get for you. You're convincing yourself of things that aren't true."

    "I'm betraying him," Agatha whimpered. "He's going to hate me."

    "Nicky won't hate you for that. If anything, he'll love the idea of a brother." Rio combed her fingers through Agatha's hair. "After all, your both their mothers."

    The ghost turned her head to look into hazel eyes. "What?"

    "Wanda didn't tell you?"

    Agatha began to shake, and with her, the house. "Tell me what?"

    Death pressed a kiss between her brows. "Witches don't need men to make children. They just need a bit of magic from another witch. We shared magic, so Nicky came to be. I don't know how, but Wanda took a bit of yours, and the twins came to be. Actually, her hex probably did it for her, and she never knew." Rio brushed her thumb along Agatha's cheek. "A part of you lies within those boys, Agatha."

    "You never said," she whispered, mind racing. "All this time, you knew?" Rio merely nodded, hands stilling.

    Agatha ripped herself from Death's grasp, housing shaking once more. "You. Knew!" "If I had told you while on the Road, you would have gone insane. You were already having a hard time because of Wanda's spell." She stood to face the ghost. "It was already hard enough being around you while you openly hated me. I couldn't add that to the list of things you held against me," Rio argued.

    Agatha clawed at her chest as a scream tore from her throat. She dropped to her knees and rested her forehead to the ground.

    "I don't need you," he had told her. "I don't trust you." Billy Maximoff, son of the Scarlet Witch and the Witch Killer. "Why won't you just leave," he'd screamed at her. The son that never wanted her. Not even after all she'd done for him to keep him safe. "Agatha," Rio pleaded. "Don't push me away again. I did it for you. I always do it for you!" Rio never lied to her. Omitted, but never lied. She'd told her, early on while on the Road, that Billy wasn't Nicky. She'd given clues to Agatha to solve trials. Hell, she even healed her shoulders after being attacked by Alice's demon. If she felt the truth would have done more damage then than now, it had to have been true. Rio was always doing for her. What had Agatha ever done in return?

    "Does he know," she choked out.

    "No."

    She raised her head to meet Death's gaze. "Don't tell him. Not ever," Agatha ordered. "Do this, and I will stay."

    Rio looked at her, burned and healed anew. Nothing was easy between the two, but Death would take her wins with her losses. "I promise."

    The ghost reached out for her, always needing to feel her lover. "Don't leave me," she begged. "Not yet."

    Death cradled her once more, shushing the woman. "Just a little more time." Agatha held her tightly and dared to break her own heart one more time. "Rio...is Wanda dead?"

    Chapter End Notes Me, starting this fic: I'm not gonna write an origin story.

    Also me: My other fic watching me work on this one daily: 🫠 Three of Pentacles Chapter Summary Bombshells aside, the house is still in shambles. They should really do something about that.

    Chapter Notes See the end of the chapter for notes Agatha refused to return to the Kaplan Residence after Rio left, so Billy was forced to go home without her. Not without a fight, of course. He apologized. He begged. Finally, he left with a slammed door. She didn't miss the hurt in his eyes, but she wasn't about to make matters worse by divulging yet another hard-truth on the boy. There was no love lost between him and Wanda. Agatha refused to be added to that list. So, she stayed in her house and tried to wrap her head around the situation. The whole mess could have been avoided if she had just left the red head alone.

    It made sense, in an odd sort of way, that Billy and Tommy were hers. Of course, she found it odd when Wanda appeared pregnant the next morning in her 70's attire. But she didn't really focus on the twins too much. Now, she's a bit mad she didn't notice things sooner. After Tommy revealed his speed abilities, it shouldn't have shocked her that Billy would have been more like his mother. (They had the same naivety and tempers, after all.) And while Billy didn't have succubus powers, his magic was far more tame that Wanda's. Agatha had quickly forgotten them as her battle with the Scarlet Witch ensued. It was probably a good thing the two hadn't clashed. That didn't matter, though. The signs of his true lineage were practically put up on a billboard in flashing, neon lights. She hadn't forgotten the way he had quickly manipulated Jen into joining her coven hours. Billy knew how to work an angle, and he excelled at it. They had worked so well together in that moment. (He definitely got that from her and not from Wanda. Sweet Wanda who was always too blinded by her own small needs.) Then, there was Tommy. She had thought she was overreacting when she first saw the older twin with long hair. The two had looked so similar she nearly kidnapped Tommy. It wasn't until he tried to shave Señor Scratchy with a razor that she'd shut those feelings down real quick.

    Lastly, there was Wanda. Innocent, irritating kinda cute Wanda. The Scarlet Witch. The bane of her existence. Stealing her magic to make kids wasn't enough. No! She had to go and rip it away from her entirely! What kind of monster does that? Like, really! Trust, that woman was going to be paying her child support.

    Yes, Agatha had done the same. Yes, it was the perfect punishment. That didn't mean she had to like it. And she didn't. Not a single second trapped in that hell was worth any ounce of chaos magic. Even if it was some of the most delicious magic she'd ever siphoned, it still wasn't worth it. No crime was worth punishment by Maximoff. None! (She made her kiss a man! That's vile! That's illegal! She was going to tell Rio to take that guy, actually. He had bad breath.)

    "You're still here," Rio said from the shadows, pulling her from her thoughts. Death's eyes twinkled like two nebulae burning in the heart of space. Her wife was such a darling little thing. "I would have thought you were sick of this place."

    Agatha chuckled dryly. "I'm a sentimental witch," she told Death. The ghost opened her arms, waiting.

    Rio slid forward, slotting herself against Agatha with a sigh. She was always a good girl for Agatha. Especially if it meant she could hold her wife once more. "You stay here too long, and you'll get stuck."

    "At least you'll know where to find me," Agatha whispered against dark lips. She closed her eyes as Rio closed the millimeter-wide gap. Death whimpered into her mouth, hands clutching her in a vice-like grip.

    Kissing as a ghost was...interesting. It tingled and tickled with just enough pressure to know something was there. Unfortunately, it didn't fire off the nerves needed to feel. So, it was a bittersweet torture for the witch. There, but not. Lukewarm at best. She definitely missed being able to fully sense her wife. Missed feeling teeth nip at her. The delicious heat from her body. That wasn't to say their new arrangement was without its complications. Rio could touch her freely, despite the muted sensations. Agatha, however, had to make a more conscious effort. All focus would be directed to hands and lips when her live was around. It meant she could back the Green Witch up against a column and nip at her neck and shoulders.

    It was for the best, Agatha decided. It meant the two couldn't get caught up in each other the way they used to. Couldn't lose themselves to the all-consuming passion of teeth and nails. And, as she'd come to realize, it allowed her to focus on Rio's needs. Her wife was a neglected, needy little thing. It was high-time she made up for all the jagged words she'd sunk into her lover's skin. Even before meeting her, Death was just as touch-starved as she was. No one had ever shown her a kindness for doing her job. (Agatha was guilty of this. One might argue she did the most damage to the cosmic entity's psyche.) But Agatha had taken the time to learn what her wife needed. Knew where to push, to pull, to squeeze to make the immortal shudder and beg. Oh! How Agatha used to take her time drawing out every little sound in the early days of their relationship. The hours sequestered away in their cabin, hair and skin sticking to one another. Moments seared into Agatha's senses for days like today when she wished she could kiss her wife properly.

    And Rio now? Rio took it all. Hungrily and desperately. She would paw at Agatha, desperate to return the favor, only to be swatted away.

    "My turn to chase," she had told Rio. She wanted Death to know her intentions before leaving her with all her knew information. Needed Rio to know she was really trying this time. (If she could fix her relationship with Rio, she could maybe, maybe, entertain the thought of moving on to see Nicky.)

    Today, as the pair defiled the basement, cars pulled into the driveway overhead. The sound alerted Rio, who pulled away from Agatha. "Did you order dinner for me?" she teased. "You shouldn't have."

    The ghost was not amused. (Her poor Death was probably starving now that she couldn't keep her well-fed.) "Ugh...How many times do I have to throw him out? He's like a damn puppy."

    Rio made a face. "You find out you have another son and your response is to avoid him?" She hissed through her teeth, eyes flashing with emotion. "Not beating those coward allegations, I see?"

    "I'm processing," she argued. Agatha turned away, steadying herself as she remembered the last time that word came into play. (Don't cry, don't cry, don't cry.) "Nicky was a shock. Twins are double the trouble. Show me a woman who can handle all this crap, and then we'll see who's a coward."

    Rio moved towards the stairs, laugh on her lips. "I think I'll go toy with The Boy since you don't want him anymore. Should be fun watching him squirm and cry for his mommy." Eugh! Agatha stomped her foot, a moot gesture given her current form. "You guys are the worst," she grumbled. Begrudgingly, the witch floated upwards to greet her unwanted son guest.

    She joined Rio in the living room as Billy and Teddy stood outside. A second car had parked behind theirs, but the driver had yet to exit. The couple waited on the porch, hands clasped and heads tilted towards each other.

    "What are we doing here?" the taller teen asked. "This place looks like it's about to cave in on itself."

    Billy waved to the car with a grin. He turned back to Teddy as the mysterious person opened their car door. "My pet ghost is being temperamental right now. I figured a new face would cheer her up. That, and I've been meaning to share some stuff with you." He scuffed a toe against the cement. "I want you to know all of me, and Agatha being there for that means a lot to me. She's...I don't know...familiar."

    Rio shot Agatha a smirk. "You mean a lot to him," she teased. "How touching." The ghost pursed her lips. "He's just saying that." She turned away from the gaping hole that was once her window. "His boyfriend makes him say gushy stuff all the time. Doesn't make it true."

    "You know that's not the case. That's why you're hiding," Rio pressed. The Green Witch turned back to the gaping hole and laughed. "Well, I wasn't expecting to see her so soon." Agatha floated back over to her lover and balked. "Eugh! Jen? Seriously? Who all did this kid invite?"

    "He's worried about Mommy Dearest," Rio whispered in her ear. "Ooo, you've got that look on your face. Did I strike a nerve? If you just let me-"

    "You irritate me enough to begin with. I'm not going to add 'sexually frustrated' to the mix." Still, she pressed a quick kiss to those enticing lips. (Leave her alone! She just really likes her wife, okay!)

    "Agatha," Billy shouted as he entered the house. Adorably, he looked around for her. "Literally right here," she grumbled. (No, you didn't see her smile fondly and lovingly. That was just a trick of the light.) "Is there a reason why you brought so many people to my house?"

    Jen raised a brow. "This place looks worse than the last time I was here." "Forgive me for living on a known battleground," Agatha told the witch. "Some of us didn't skip town when shit got real."

    "Who's the other lady," Teddy whispered to Billy.

    Rio leaned forward, flashing a manic grin. "Your bestest friend to the very end!" Teddy looked to Billy for help.

    "Play nice," Agatha warned. "Him, I can tolerate. It's Billy you should bully." "You're still mad at me?" he grumbled. "I said I was sorry. I even reinstalled your front door." Agatha waved to the rest of the house. "Because that was the most pressing matter." Jen waved her off. "Teen..."

    "...Billy," Agatha and Billy corrected in unison.

    "...said that you needed help, so I risked getting arrested to come see you." The pink witch crossed her arms. "So, what did you do this time?"

    Agatha scoffed. "I haven't done shit. He's the one who went into my memories uninvited!" She pointed at the teen with a scowl.

    "Well...that's why I'm asking them to help me rebuild your house. Jen's going to move in. Then, she can help me with potions and my Chemistry."

    Agatha, Rio, and Jen were quick to hit him with a, "What?"

    The curly-haired teen looked around the group with a nervous laugh. "We need someone to move in and keep vandals away. I'm not gonna fix the place up just for someone to come and smash it to pieces again."

    "I'm, like, really confused, but I do know how to hold a hammer," Teddy informed brightly. He patted a bicep proudly.

    Agatha let out a long-suffering groan. "Fine! Jen can move in, but the master bedroom stays mine. In fact, Rio, move my stuff for me."

    The Green Witch laughed richly. "Well, would you look at the time! It was great seeing you again, Boy and his boyfriend." She turned to grin widely at Jen as she snaked an arm around Agatha. "Mine," she informed saccharine sweet. Death preened as the pink witch took a step back, hands raised in defense.

    "Don't leave me alone with them," the ghost pouted. "You're the cause of half the damage. My fucking sink is still in the backyard!"

    Rio pressed a kiss to her cheek. "I was owed some damage after years of someone hiding behind a certain, dark book." She moved to leave, hood raising.

    The ghost waited a few beats before giving in. "You haven't said the thing," Agatha reminded quickly. She raised her chin, shaking her hair back in the process. (Okay, fine. She had fallen into old habits faster than when she died. That didn't make her weak. No, sir. Not Agatha Harkness.)

    Death glanced back at her, a twinkle in her eye. "Te veo."

    With Rio gone,much to the ghosts chagrin, Agatha ordered Billy to move her personal items out of the guest bedroom. It would be a long process for the group. She had a bunch of junk stashed away from her Agnes Days. Jen, however, had driven into town for cleaning supplies because, "this place is not to my standards!"

    Teddy followed his boyfriend, righting items and dusting what didn't need to be fixed. He was content with listening to the ghost and other teen banter back and forth about his eyeliner. A few times, he'd throw a word in just to keep the conversation going. Agatha liked that about him.

    Once they really got elbows-deep into the clutter, Agatha was quick to let them know what exactly was trash to her. "Toss all those drawings," she told the teens. "I don't want a single one left." They're not his, she had to remind herself. She knew if she kept them, she'd let herself believe they were. Agatha was not about to spiral down that rabbit hole again. "These are cute," Teddy cooed. He turned to face the mentor/mentee duo. "Did a kid live here at some point?"

    Billy grimaced. "Not exactly." He shot the ghost an apologetic look. "So...it's probably time I told you about me and Agatha. See, my mother used to be Wanda Maximoff. Agatha, here, is a witch who went up against her. We sorta went into an alternate reality of my own with a bunch of random witches. One of which is Jen."

    Agatha resisted the urge to comfort the boy and merely observed. If he needed her, wanted her, he'd let her know. (If only they knew how to work and talk at the same time.) She settled on the twin bed, lips pursed as Billy broke down their journey. The witch was thoroughly impressed with how well the other boy took the information in stride. Rather than bombard his boyfriend with questions regarding the Scarlet Witch, he pestered Billy about his abilities. All that, she could ignore. Unfortunately, the conversation soon turned to her. It was to be expected, but it didn't make it any less uncomfortable for her.

    "So, are you like an ancestor that's here to tutor him, or did you choose him?" Agatha laughed. "Something like that. Or maybe I'm just a manifestation of his consciousness?" Billy deserved some teasing for the many stunts he'd pulled since meeting her. "I'm afraid his fashion sense is beyond help, though. All those shopping sessions with Wanda, wasted!" She struck a dramatic pose if faux despair. The back of her hand resting against her forward like a damsel's when distressed.

    "You picked out clothes for me?" the young witch asked her. "That sounds so wrong. I can't even remember you."

    "Well, it was nice regardless. I never got to go shopping for Nicky," she lamented quietly. Would Wanda have helped her pick something for him if given the chance? Something told her she would have. They could have been pretty good friends if it weren't for the unfortunate need to steal magic to survive. The twins were just an added bonus setback on her path to coven-less survival.

    "Who's Nicky?" Teddy whispered to Billy. "Did I miss him earlier?"

    Agatha's ire was swift and true. She rounded on the boys, floating to make them crane their necks to see her. "How dare you!"

    Billy moved Teddy behind him, a hand held up to keep her at bay. His face softened with guilt and a touch of understanding. "He didn't know," he reminded her gently. "It's not his fault."

    A worked up Agatha was always hard to wind down. And when Nicky was involved, she tended to let the insults fly. Today was no different. "You're fine with telling him everything else! Why not add my son to the list? It's not like you didn't get all the answers you've been pestering me for," she growled. "I bet you were just dying to take a peek into my mind! Poor little Nicky with his bloodthirsty mother. Why did nobody save him?"

    There was the sound of footsteps on the staircase before Jen ran through the doorway. Already, her hands were pink with magic. "What's going on on here?"

    "It's just a misunderstanding," Billy explained. He held his ground with the ghost. "I didn't tell him about Nicky because I still don't know about Nicky. I didn't get that far in either of your memories." He shuffled a bit now that he had a larger audience. "The last thing I saw was your witch trial. Pretty sure that was before him when you were still all young looking." Agatha shrank back, her hand flying to her brooch. She looked away, recalling the damp soil of Salem. The stench of rotting corpses at her feet. Her bittersweet victory over her mother and years of abuse. Rio...

    "You mean you actually went into their memories?" Jen all but shouted at Billy. "Do you have a death wish or something!"

    "It was an accident! Agatha was about to turn into a vengeful spirit. I thought if I could reach her, I could calm her down," he reasoned. "But then I was in Rio's body, living out her life, and-"

    "You inhabited Death!"

    "That other woman was Death?"

    "Enough!" Agatha caused the lights to flicker with her surge of energy. "Nicky is still off- limits." She pointed to the group. "And don't go around telling people you know Death. I'm not above sending anyone to an early grave for her." The ghost flipped her hair back over her shoulder. She pursed her lips, treading carefully. Rio was always on her case about the misinformation regarding her son. If anyone needed to know the truth, it would be Billy and, by extension, Jen. Agatha lifted her chin, eyes firmly planted on the trio. "Now, just this once, you may ask about Nicky."

    "Did you trade him for the Darkhold?" Jen rushed to say. (Because of course she would.) "What really happened to him?" Billy asked. (Also not surprising.)

    Teddy held up his hands. "I'm good with their questions." (The boy earned his right to live.) Agatha composed her anger as she lowered herself to sit. "I did not trade my son for the Darkhold," she told Jen pointedly. She looked away as she moved on. Her hand moved back to her brooch, fingers stroking the silhouette of the Triple Goddess. "He was sick, and I..." Her voice cracked with emotion. She cleared her throat. "I couldn't save him." Agatha shut her eyes, trying desperately to push away the images of her son's gaunt face. The way the circles around his eyes darkened with each passing day.

    Jen had the decency to mumble an apology as she looked down at her feet. Billy looked surprised. As if he had truly expected the worst of her. Agatha was powerless against the hurt she felt. She would never be someone worth trusting in his eyes, would she? "Why didn't Rio heal him?" he asked her.

    Agatha stared hard at him. Her anger boiled over. "You asked your one," she snapped. Her own voice shook her. She hadn't yelled like that since the Road. When she truly began to panic, fearing they were stuck forever. The witch took a steadying breath. "Now, get those drawings out of my house." Agatha sped away to the In-Between. Anything to escape the pitying glances of her audience.

    Billy cleared his throat as his mentor blinked out of existence. "Well...Guess we better get back to work." (Teddy would probably break up with him after today.)

    "What all did you see? What did it feel like being Death?"

    The teen looked at Jen, thinking carefully. "It felt lonely and numb until Agatha." He sensed around the house for his mentor before continuing. "By the way, her mom was a real piece of work. Rio had the right idea when we met her ghost. Yikes!"

    "I don't imagine Agatha was an easy child," Jen scoffed. She nudged a box with her foot. "Maybe that's just how they see things."

    "I'm still on the whole 'your ghost mentor's girlfriend is Death' thing...," Teddy said with a squint. "Starting to think you might have gotten in way over your head." Billy laughed. "Oh, yeah, that's a thing. We just sorta moved on from that." He shuffled over to a stack of drawings and dumped them in a trash bag. "But Agatha's mother was, quite literally, the worst. She had some bony hands, too. I seriously thought I was gonna find bruises when I got home."

    "What's that supposed to mean?" Jen gave him a look, waiting for him to elaborate. Billy grimaced. Maybe sharing with them wasn't a good idea, but it did change the way he saw her. More people needed to see the real her too. "I was in a few of Agatha's memories, too. I think Rio did her best to keep me out, but I slipped into one anyway. There were witch hunters, and Evanora was mad she'd led them to the coven stead." He swallowed thickly as he recalled the memory. The way Agatha had begged her to stop. "Agatha's not a good person, but I get it now. Why she never formed another coven. It'd be kind of hard when all of them wanted you dead from the get-go."

    Teddy rubbed his back and offered a tissue with his free hand. "Don't want you to ruin your eyeliner," he whispered gently.

    Billy touched his cheek in shock. "Thanks," he laughed shakily. "Didn't even realize I was crying."

    Jen moved to comfort him as well. "It's going to be okay. You're out of there now." "I'm not the one who needs this, you guys. Agatha's the one who lived it. It was seconds for me. That was her whole life." Billy felt his heart break a little. "That's why her and Rio protect each other so much. No one else knows how to be there for them." Teddy pressed a kiss to his cheek. "Well, if anyone can cheer her up, it's gonna be the sweetest guy I know."

    Billy blushed as Jen sent him a wink. "Let's get the place fixed up for her. Then, I'll give her a few more days."

    "Let's see what your magic can do," Jen told him. Her hands were already glowing and lifting objects. "Blessings and burdens, alike," she reminded.

    Billy returned home, Agatha having remained hidden. She was well and truly upset about Nicky, as well as Billy's mental violation. He hoped she'd appreciate how they'd fixed the house back up for her, but figured it wouldn't. The only thing that would make Agatha happy was her son. If Billy knew how, he'd bring him back for her. He just wish he knew why Agatha being sad made him sad. It wasn't like she cared about him to the same degree. She was always acting like being around him was the last thing she wanted to do. But she's sacrificed herself for him, even if she denied it, so she had to care to some degree. Who knows? Maybe she does, he wondered.

    The teen finished his nightly routine, taking longer just in case Agatha was home and wanted to tease him, and climbed into bed. The lack of Grumpy Ghost in Corner made the room feel smaller and colder. Billy had never quite realized just how much of a difference Agatha had made in his life. What if she never came back? The teen chose to ignore the thought. He turned off his bedside lamp and let sleep pull him under.

    Billy jerked awake as a shiver shook his body. All his senses were screaming for him to sit up. He scrambled upwards and around towards his desk. The boy turned his lamp back on to find Rio sitting cross-legged at the foot of his bed. She was in her Death outfit, crowned and solemn. He began to breath heavily as her eyes remained trained on him. "Hey," he told her weakly. "Is...How are you?"

    Rio narrowed her eyes at him. She let the silence play tricks with his mind. Let it settle under his skin so that he squirmed in place. "Are you good?"

    He blinked in confusion. "What do you mean?"

    She tilted her head to the side, looking around. "You're not, I dunno, dying or anything?" "I don't think so..." Billy scratched the back of his head. What the hell is going on? "Do you feel that tug thingy with me? Am I dying?"

    Rio laughed. "No. I haven't felt that since Agatha died for you." She sneered at him, clearly still unhappy with that day's events. "That was some spell you cast. I didn't know it let you feel things, too."

    "I couldn't hear your thoughts, it that helps." He remembered his conversation with Agatha and added, "And I didn't see anything about Nicky."

    She nodded slowly. "I know. I stopped you before you could." Death watched him closely, never blinking.

    Billy threw caution to the wind. "Who was that person in the cave? The first one I saw you take."

    Rio tapped her chin in thought. "You entered both our minds at the same time, so your magic sought out memories that were related. Must have been one of Agatha's ancestors. You'd have to show me for me to know for sure."

    Billy nodded. For a few seconds, the two just stared at one another. "Did you need something?" he finally asked her.

    "Agatha's hiding," she sighed, shoulders slumping. "I'm bored, so I figured someone should keep an eye on you. She'd kill me if something happened while she was away." The teen felt very special, very quickly. Death, herself, was watching over him as he slept. That was definitely not lost on him. "Thanks," he told her, a grin growing. "I'm sure Agatha will be happy to hear that. I know you don't care for me 'cause of Tommy." Rio shrugged. "What's done, is done. I'll take care of things when the time comes." Billy shivered. "If it makes you feel any better, I didn't really want to do that to him. He's out there, alone and unloved."

    Death grinned. "That was a good trial," she admitted. "They all were. I've never seen anyone make Agatha squirm like that before. I owe you one for that."

    "Were you on the Road the whole time!"

    "I'm Death, Billy. I'm everywhere. You just didn't need me yet." She gave a half-shrug. "Once Blondie was gone, you pulled me in for a bit of fun. Well, as much fun as I could get until you also pulled that woman into Agatha's trial." Her distaste was as evident as the crown on her head.

    "Yeah...she was too much." A thought occurred. "Why don't you reap ghosts?" "I can't force them to go. I'm just a guide. But I leave Evanora Harkness alone to make her suffer. If I had reaped her, she'd be given another chance to be reborn. No one wants that." Rio pulled out her knife to stab at his bed.

    Billy moved to stop her but gave in at the first tear. He let out a sigh and pulled his feet in closer. "Could I ask you about Nicky?"

    "You could," Rio mocked. "Doesn't mean you should." She let her scowl fall away as she drug her blade across the comforter. "But Aggie won't talk about him, not with me." "She said he was sick, but she didn't say why you didn't heal him."

    Rio sneered. "I can see why she doesn't let you ask questions now." The Green Witch huffed. "No one would have been able to heal him. He was dead on arrival."

    Billy suddenly felt very stupid for asking. "Well...thanks. I'm just gonna..." He lay back down, hoping to avoid angering the cosmic being further. As he closed his eyes and ignored Death personified, he felt a hand settle on his head. His eyes snapped open but he didn't dare move. "What are you doing?"

    "What? You never get mad when Agatha does it." Rio didn't sound offended, but she did sound amused. As if the thought of Agatha petting his head while he slept were some joke. "I..." He chose his next words carefully. He'd talk to Agatha about that later. "She, uh...she..." "Rio?"

    Oh, thank fuck, he told whoever was controlling the universe. "Agatha!" Billy sat up to find the ghost standing in the middle of his room.

    "You're back," Death said, bouncing over to the ghost. All gloom and doom vanished in an instant. "You made me have to talk to The Boy. He's so boring."

    "I know," Agatha sighed. Her face softened as Death stopped in front of her. "I was looking for you."

    Billy watched the couple. "I wonder how many people can say they've had late-night conversations like me," he mumbled. The two were too wrapped up in each other to tease him. A yawn pulled at his jaw, his lips smacking. " G'night, Rio. Night, Agatha." This time, he didn't bother to stop Rio as she dropped her hand back down on his head. He gave a small laugh as it remained planted on his face. Jen is never gonna believe this! "He lets me do this, too," he heard Rio whisper to Agatha. "That's another point for me." "You and your damn points," his mentor hissed quietly. "I'm his guide! You'll never have enough points."

    Billy let sleep steal him away, two powerful entities, though bickering like children, standing guard at his side.

    Chapter End Notes Y'all, I miss Lilia. I'd make her a ghost, but that feels disrespectful to the masterpiece that is her character arc. RIP Diva. You are missed everyday along with Agatha's coat. Hope you're partying with Alice and Sharon.

    If it wasn't obvious, I'm gonna follow the little bit of comic lore that makes Agatha and Wanda the parents of Billy and Tommy without the Mephisto bit. For all intents and purposes, Wanda's chaos magic stole a bit from Agatha and boom bebes!

    It should also be said that I know very little comic book canon. It would just make for interesting TV/fics if this was used for (potentially) season 2.

    It's Not Loyalty (It's Analysis)

    Chapter Summary The coven has a totally normal get together where nothing goes wrong.

    Chapter Notes See the end of the chapter for notes "Billy, come on!" Agatha hovered by the car as she waited for the teen to lock up. Sure, she could just fly to their destination, but she wanted to ride in the car. (She missed feeling alive, okay. Fuck off!) "I told Jen you'd be there thirty minutes ago. What's taking you so damn long?"

    Billy turned away from the front door and jogged over to his Subaru. "Give me a second," he grumbled. "I couldn't find my journal."

    "Real magic is practiced enough times until it's etched into your brain," she told the boy. "Let's just hope we never run into another one of those horrid trials ever again. You still owe me a new coat." Agatha tethered herself to the car as Billy shot her a look. (That coat, man. She had really loved the damn thing. R.I.P.) She stared at him as he turned the key in the ignition. "Billy, I miss my coat," she whined.

    The teen banged his head against the steering wheel.

    The duo drove to the other side of town, picked up Teddy, then made their way to Westview. "How's school going for you, Teddy? Anyone died or done anything interesting yet?" The teen laughed. "I'm afraid not, Ms. Harkness."

    The ghost visibly shuddered. "Don't call me that ever again," she instructed quickly. "Do that with his mother. I'm actually worth talking to."

    "That's still my mother," Billy reminded. "Sorry, not all of us won the 'mom' lottery." (If he only knew...)

    She shot a look at the teen. "Apparently, seeing my life through Rio's eyes has made your boyfriend an expert," Agatha told Teddy. "I suggest a tin foil hat for your next date. Wouldn't want him to snoop, accidentally or not."

    "Mrs. Kaplan is very sweet," the other boy said in defense of Billy. "I bet the two of you would get along nicely. She loves all of Billy's witchy movies and decorations." "Oh yes, totally," she drawled. "I could show her all the different ways to ensnare a feeble mind, and she can teach me how to use one of those horrid kitchen contraptions. That's just what a ghost needs. Food."

    "Since you were around during covered wagon times," Teddy began. "I was actually wondering if you could help me with some history reports."

    "First, covered wagons were after I was born. You're thinking about those yahoos that expanded west with the railroads. No steam power in my time, baby. Second, it depends on the version of history they're asking for. Do they want the truth; or the whitewashed version?" Billy tried to hide a laugh, catching Agatha's attention.

    "Oh, that's funny to you?"

    "No, no. You just reminded me of Rio's ugly dress she used to wear. Her new fit is lit AF." He giggled to himself. "She looked like a special edition Barbie doll."

    The ghost looked at him as if he'd found his way into another sigil. "What the hell did you just say to me?"

    Teddy attempted to tap her shoulder with a whispered, "We'll, talk more at the house. I want to hear more about Rio."

    Billy looked over at his mentor for a second before returning his eyes to the road. "What? It was hideous. The lacing was beautiful, don't get me wrong, but I just know her cloak and hem were always gross from the mud. I mean, think about it. All those bodies with their blood and guts. There's no way she kept any of it clean. Also, the eyeliner makes her look way more menacing. Without it, she's like any other person dressing up for a Renaissance Fair."

    Agatha narrowed her eyes at him. Did he just insult my wife? In front of me??? "I dare you to tell her. Seriously."

    The teen sent her several looks, waiting for her to say it was a joke. He gave up with a huff. "Fine. I will!"

    "Fine!"

    The trio entered Agatha's house with a few laughs between them. The ghost moved to spook Jen, but Billy and Teddy had already tripped her wards. She glowered in the living room as the living trio moved into the dining room. Reluctantly, she joined them. Not like there was much to do without a body. She eyed the cauldron and vials resting on the table. "No poisoned wine this time," she told Billy.

    "As if you wouldn't break the bottle first," he quipped.

    "Why are you blaming Teen for the trial?" Jen said in his defense. "You're the one who cheated and wasted our time."

    Oh yeah...she still thinks the Road was its own thing. Yikes! "I just like to give him a hard time," Agatha told the other woman. "Keeps him humble." She flicked a curl on her...son's...head with a teasing grin. (She was still getting used to the idea.) Billy shot her a grateful look before pulling his journal out. "So, what's the lesson for today?" Agatha moved away from the pair to sit across from Teddy. "Now, you said something about a history report?"

    The rosy-faced teen nodded sweetly. (He was quickly growing on her. So much more well- behaved than the Maximoff.) "Fall's coming up, so we're discussing the Salem Witch Trials.
