We've been reading The Crucible in class, but they want us to do our own research." Billy dropped the wooden spoon Jen had just handed him, head turned towards them. He mumbled an apology and tried to ignore their conversation.

    Agatha pursed her lips. She appreciated his concern. Truly, she did. But he had nothing to worry about. The witch had moved on by now. (She had not.) "I see." She tapped her brooch in thought. "Which one, exactly? There were hundreds of trials with varying degrees of punishment. It also depends on the Witch Finder General in the area. I saw a few during my time, so this shouldn't be too hard to spin you a tale or two."

    "God, you're ancient," Jen remarked from the other end of the table. By now, her and Billy had given up on their lesson to listen to Agatha.

    "The powerful usually are." Agatha propped her chin up on her hand. "So, you got answers to any of my questions?"

    Teddy slid over the rubric with a tight grin. "It's more of a generalized report about how witches and the wrongly accused suffered. Is that something doable?"

    "It is, but it's a lot to cram into a five-page paper. It also wants you to have a variety of sources, but there aren't many my age that are still alive to tell the tale. Billy can whip out his ouija board, and we can get a few more sides of the story that way."

    "And risk your mother possessing someone again? No thanks," the pink witch told her. "We don't have Alice or Lilia to help us out."

    Agatha glowered at the woman. "At least Alice stepped up. You wanted to run away." "Guys," Billy groaned. "Let's not do this right now. We've got a lot of homework to get through."

    "We'll come back to this at a later date," Jen promised. She pointed at the ghost with the wooden spoon.

    The other teen cleared his throat. "By sources, they want us to use books written on the subject," Teddy explained. "You know, reading old written accounts and forming an unbiased narrative."

    "Ah! I see. I can't help you there." Agatha flipped her hair with a sour grin. "I don't tend to read books about my old friends being burned at the stake. Although, they had the kinder deaths. Goody Patterson was boiled alive. She deserved it, of course. That's why you don't go around telling people you're a witch that curses children, but that's just me." Teddy grimaced. "I don't think I wanna know about that."

    "Wait a minute. How did you survive the Witch Trials?" Billy asked.

    Agatha tapped her brooch, frowning. "I stayed out of Massachusetts," she told him carefully. "After my trial, there was no point in hanging around." She laughed to herself, proud of her gallow's humor. (Boy, she was on a roll.)

    Billy fidgeted.

    Jen sighed. "I'll just ask since he won't. What did you do to piss your coven off?" Where to begin? There was her birth, for whatever reason. (She really needed to talk to Rio about that.) Then, it was when the coven realized she had magic that didn't look like theirs. That fear and disgust was heightened once her first accident occurred. That amount was multiplied tenfold when her mother caught her with Rio... (Agatha was starting to think her environment was not a healthy one.)

    "You don't have to tell us," Teddy told her. "I get it if it's too painful." Agatha laughed. "Pfft! Nah, those guys just always had a bone to pick with me. I was trying to pinpoint the main reason." She slapped the table with another forced laugh. "If I had to say, I'd say it was when kissed a girl and sucked the life right out of her!" (Itwasanaccidentitwasanaccidentitwasanaccident)

    The room fell silent save for Agatha's manic cackling.

    Jen sent her a glare. "Still lacking a sense of humanity, I see." She turned towards the teens. "I don't blame them for wanting to kill a witch killer."

    "Get used to it, toots. They don't hand that title out for nothing." She sneered at the group, old habits wrapping her up like a trusty security blanket. "Her lips were chapped that day, so I'm not too cut up about it."

    "You were born evil. I should have killed you the moment you left my body." Teddy pulled a book out of his bag. "I'll just...use the textbook and Google. Thanks anyway," he said with a nervous laugh.

    Billy, however, slammed his journal down and stormed out of the room. The back door slammed shut, causing the group to jump. Jen shot her a new glare that clearly screamed, "Look what you did!"

    Agatha sighed. "I'll be back..." She drifted off towards the backyard, steeling herself for the oncoming tantrum. The witch felt the prickling sting of discomfort as she found the boy stewing in his rage.

    Billy kept his back turned to her as he stood in from of her burial mound. (The flowers were stunning, as always. Rio had added some blue perennials to accent the purple azaleas over the weekend.) He didn't bother to acknowledge her as she floated closer. He merely took long, deep breaths in an attempt to curb his anger with his mentor.

    Agatha gave in and broke the silence with, "What's the matter now?"

    He turned to her with red eyes. "Why? Why can't you just be normal for once?" Oh, there were a number of reasons, but none that would satisfy him. So, Agatha lay on her own grave with a sigh. The flowers smelled of Rio, which calmed her. "When you've lived through some bad things, sometimes, all you can do is laugh. If that means making a joke at someone else's expense, so be it. Besides, what does it even mean to be normal? You're acting like being different is a bad thing."

    He glared down at her, arms crossing like a child's. His stance was reminiscent of Wanda trying desperately to cling to the high-ground. "You're always switching between trying to do good and wanting them to think you're evil. I don't understand why you can't make a decision and just stick with it. Do you like being the bad guy in everybody's story? Is that it?" She sat up, eyes narrowed. "Why are you angry on my behalf? You, yourself, said I was nothing more than a covenless witch. You don't see me bent out of shape because of that. If I cried over ever little lie the world believed about me, I would have dried up and died a long time ago. What does my reputation have to do with you?"

    Billy stomped a foot petulantly. "Because I actually want to believe you're worth believing in!" The force of his anger sent a wave of blue towards her. His magic knocked over the trellis, a few potted plants, and sent Agatha flying. "How can I trust you if I don't even know you?" he continued, his anger blinding him from his actions. "Why can't you just pick a side?"

    The ghost struggled to move against the wave of blue until it ebbed away. She cleared her throat, trying to think of something to say that wouldn't piss him off more. "I don't need you to believe in me," she said carefully, softly. "I am literally known for killing my own kind. It would be like asking you to believe a shark can grow wings and fly. It's not worth it. I'm not worth it, and that's okay."

    Billy's eyes flashed blue, hands balling at his sides. "Stop! Stop saying that." Agatha shook her head. "I'm not gonna sugar coat it for you, Billy. I do bad things, so I deserve to have bad things said about me. I'm evil and-"

    He screamed at her, wordless yet impactful. His magic hit her square in the chest, briefly turning her fully solid as she tore through the fence.

    Had it not been for Rio catching her, there was no telling how far, and through how much, she would have traveled. Agatha stumbled along the ground on shaky legs before her form de-materialized. "Did he just...?"

    "Later," Rio hissed. "Why's The Boy upset this time?"

    "I was just making a joke," she grumbled. "He had to go and get his feelings hurt." Rio helped her stand, her hand brushing along her dress. "You're hurt." She had that tone, the one that meant someone was going to pay. Any other time, it would have warranted a heavy make-out session. Now was not that time.

    The ghost looked down to find an odd blood-like slime staining her front. She pressed her fingers to the tender area. "Huh...That's new."

    Rio narrowed her eyes. "Maybe..."

    "Maybe what?"

    "Nothing. It's impossible." She tugged her wife along. "Let's just get The Boy under control before he goes too far. I'm already busy as it is."

    They found Billy pacing, tears streaming down his cheeks. (Just your average four year old with a case of the terrible two's.)

    Agatha didn't hesitate to rush to his side, hands outstretched to hold him. He pulled back from her, mouth set in a firm line. "No," he told her. "You don't get to come back and act like you care. You only care about yourself. About how the world perceives you."

    She let her hands drop to her sides. "I'm not acting. I wouldn't..." Agatha wanted to scream. She wanted to shake him and let him know the truth. She wouldn't, though. He still didn't trust her. He probably never would. "The world is more than black and white, Billy. Your mother had the same problem. I'd really like to not do this whole song and dance with you, too."

    Rio shot her a warning look. "What Agatha means to say is, she doesn't want people to know how deeply their words cut her. How sensitive she actually is."

    "Hey!" Agatha quieted. It's not like Rio hadn't been honest when she said she watched and saw her. That didn't mean the truth didn't sting like a bitch. In fact, she'd like for Billy to send her through another fence if it meant she could leave the conversation. Her wife continued, unbothered. "She went through life with the worst always being expected of her." Rio shrugged. "So, she wore the mask they gave her. The mask you gave her. You don't get to demand her vulnerability when this is how you act."

    "But she doesn't have to pretend anymore," the boy grumbled. "She hasn't had to for a long time! No one judges her but herself. If she would just be honest, she'd feel better." "Ha! Here we go again!" She'd had just about enough of that from him. "Pot meet kettle," she sneered. "You see a few snippets of my life and you think that gives you the right to tell me how to feel. You wanna be the hero of my story so bad." Agatha barked out a laugh. "I'm an evil, rotten thing, Billy. There are so many bodies piled at my feet, your climb will never end. So, go on, say it. Call me the villain." Agatha moved towards him with a snarl, dress and hair flared out around her. "Say it!"

    Rio grabbed her wrist and forcibly put her in the In-Between. "That's a party foul, and you know it." She eyed the ghost, face softening. "Stay put until I get you. You need to heal." With that, Agatha was left to stew in silence.

    Death returned to The Boy with a frown. She didn't care about his feelings. She cared about Agatha's. Right now, The Boy was making Agatha upset. Rio didn't like that. Didn't like to hear her wife's soul cry regularly. Hated the way he tripped her wife up emotionally. Even now, Agatha had retreated into her self-deprecating charade to hide her fear. Fear of how Billy made her feel about herself. Rio wanted that to stop. So, if she had to play parent to her naturally sworn enemy, she would. For Agatha.

    Rio looked down at her flowers with a sniff. "They didn't deserve to be flattened by a child's tantrum," she ground out. The Green Witch crouched to wave a hand over her precious garden. Did he have respect for anything sacred? "Sit," she instructed firmly. He pouted. "I don't have-"

    "SSSIIITTT"

    The Boy dropped to the ground without another sound.

    She nudged a mushroom back to life, encouraging it to stand tall once more. "You should know that Agatha and I have had that argument more times than you could ever know. Trying to change her mind is practically impossible." Rio finally looked up to face The Boy. He waited for her to continue, tears still wet on his cheeks. She had no intentions of wiping them away. Only one boy was worth caring about. This boy was not him. "Agatha doesn't like to be known in any capacity. To be seen for who she truly is. When you challenge her coping mechanisms, you back her into a corner. Cornered Agatha is more dangerous than any wild animal."

    The Boy sniffled. "She's annoying."

    "Funny. She says the same thing about you. But as annoying as you are to her, she doesn't try to change you."

    The Boy looked away. "She has these moments where it's like she's an entirely different person. She's...I don't know. Nice!" He hugged himself, clearly torn. "Agatha's been really nice lately. But then she goes and tries to convince people she's evil and I...it just makes me so angry! I don't know what to believe. How do I know when she's being honest with me?" Death had made a promise, so she wouldn't let slip that 'nice' Agatha was just her being motherly. The safety of their fragile relationship, and Rio's mission, hinged on Agatha's connection to The Boy. It irritated her to no end. "Do you think Agatha is evil?" she asked point blank. (If he said 'yes,' Agatha would return to a fresh grave next to hers.) The Boy pulled back with a shaking head. "No...?"

    "How convincing," Rio spat. "Dig deep. Really do something with that brain of yours since William didn't get a chance."

    That got The Boy to react. "I don't know, okay! She confuses me. I saw what her life was like. How she never had a chance. I felt sorry for her. But then she goes and says stuff about happily killing people, and I wonder why I ever cared about her in the first place." Sometimes, living forever meant having to entertain yourself with people watching. Of all the mortals to cross her path, Agatha had been the most captivating. It wasn't just because she was one of the few infants promised to her. No, Agatha had a lust for life and power. So, when she could, Death followed the witch like a loyal shadow. It didn't take long to learn the woman's tells. Death knew when the witch was hiding behind her defense mechanisms, and when she was openly being vulnerable. As of late, the ghost had been a bleeding heart. It was...endearing. Clearly, she was trying to make amends after years of letting dark magic twist her into someone entirely different. For cursing their union and pushing her away for so long. For failing to appreciate the time she had with her son.

    And all of that was fine for Death because no one else would live long enough to truly understand Agatha Harkness. No one would appreciate the effort and desire it would take for Agatha to want something as hallowed as forgiveness.

    When The Boy sequestered her wife away on the make-believe Witches' Road, she didn't think much of it. Just a soul trying to prolong their miserable existence. Death knew the story well. But then Agatha had gotten attached to The Boy. Had reignited a spark of authentic Agatha with his proximity. Death was in awe. She nearly praised The Boy. And just as quickly as he'd impressed her, he'd insulted her a second time. Death watched as her wife protected The Boy. Was burned by the image of Agatha begging, for the second time in her tear-stained life, for Death to spare another of her children. Even before Rio scanned his soul, there was no denying the claim her wife had lain on The Boy. And he threw it all away because of one accident. He was no different from the witches of old.

    Death saw, and Death did not appreciate the wound he'd left.

    "You aren't meant to know," she told him firmly. "That's why they're defense mechanisms, Boy."

    He looked at her, some small, banal, emotion flitting across his face. He didn't understand. Not yet. Mortals could be so tiresome.

    Rio leaned forward and spoke to him as if he were Nicky. As if she were trying to explain the cycle of life and death to a newborn. "Agatha has never been cared for by another mortal other than her son. She was alone, so she built herself armor out of sharp smiles and cruel jokes. I ask again, do you think Agatha Harkness is evil?"

    The Boy set his jaw, gaze never wavering. "No."

    "Why?"

    "Because she helped me find Tommy even though she'd be left alone and powerless in the final trial. She didn't have to do that, but she did. Just like she gave herself up in exchange for me."

    Rio didn't need to be reminded of that evening. Agatha's dying gasp was seared into her memory. "If you know the truth, then why do you have to argue it with her? That's something that needs to be argued with her enemies."

    The Boy lowered his chin, a shaky breath leaving his fragile body. "I know. I just want Agatha to see herself the way I see her."

    Rio cocked her head, time slowing around them. "Which is?

    "A friend."

    Death laughed. So close. "Yes... a friend. That makes total sense given your age gap." She levitated herself to stand easily. "I'm going to bring her back now that you've calmed down. Think long and hard about what you're going to say."

    The Boy nodded before moving to get up.

    Agatha turned towards the sound of ripping fabric. The sound triggered the memory of the Road. Wounded hazel eyes. The lack of a farewell. No, come back. I didn't mean it, echoing in her head. The witch surged towards Rio, hands seeking her true form. She needed to know for certain that this wasn't all in her head. That she hadn't fallen into another hex where her love was dangled in front of her cruelly.

    Death held her tenderly, fingers pressing through the funerary robes adorning her wife. "I'm here," she soothed.

    Agatha gripped Rio's face. Clung to fleshy cheeks like a life line. "I need to see you," she gasped. (If she still had a heart, it would be racing right now.) "Rio, please!" The cosmic being complied, false features melting away to cool ivory. She sucked in a breath as wispy tendrils, Agatha's fingers, curled into her rib cage. The intrusion stung in a good way. Her lover used to hold her just like this after a particularly bad experience. She would always console Agatha in any way the witch deemed fit. Right now was no exception. The ghost pressed herself close until she could feel the hum of the Universe in her very molecules. Time unraveled, twisted, then snapped back together as their hearts connected. Agatha tilted her head back to place a lip to Death's eternal grin. (Somewhere in time, Lilia placed The Lover's card with a hum.)

    "Careful," Rio warned. "Too much of a good thing." But she didn't untangle herself from Agatha's grip. Why would she? This was their love in it's purest form. Adoration, worship, and understanding chaining them, binding them, as one.

    Agatha released her with a shudder, eyes squeezed shut as they were split back in two. When she opened her eyes, the blue of her soul was like an expansive ocean. The witch pressed a hand to her chest. "That hurt a bit. It doesn't usually."

    Rio caressed the spot, gaze softening. "It will need more time, but you should be safe to visit the Living." She pressed a kiss to the small wound and watched it start to stitch itself back together. "I've spoken to The Boy for you."

    "Billy," Agatha reminded, but her usual fire was watered down. "If you're going to play 'Good Cop,' you might as well use his name."

    "He hasn't earned that right," Rio huffed. "He keeps hurting you." Her hands sound white strands, stroking them delicately.

    "I hurt you plenty," Agatha told her, looking away. "You don't call me 'The Fool,' or anything like that."

    Death tucked a new flower into her lover's hand. "I don't fault you for your grief, Agatha. I see you as I have always seen you."

    The ghost risked a new argument as she asked, "And how's that?"

    The crowned entity bowed her head in reverence. "Human."

    The couple returned to the Realm of the Living, arm in arm. Billy had taken Rio's words into consideration and ran to meet Agatha. She rushed to create enough energy to keep him from running through her. The witch narrowed her eyes as she felt fabric slide across her palms. She even caught a whiff of his body spray. She dare not tell Rio. The Green Witch was still upset with Billy for hurting her ghostly form. This would only make her distrust him more. Instead, she kept the attention on her witchling. "Are you alright?"

    He nodded into her shoulder. "I'm sorry, Agatha. I know you're doing your best. I didn't..." He hiccuped. "I didn't mean to act like I knew better than you."

    She shushed him, silently thanking Rio for lending her energy. She cradled him to her, freely allowing herself to console him. "We're both doing are best, Billy. I know I don't have the healthiest of coping methods."

    He didn't say a word, just let her hold him. Gradually, his crying subsided. Rather than drag the whole, touchy-feelly session out, Agatha ushered Billy back inside to finish his potion's lesson. Jen looked confused as Rio entered with the mentor/mentee duo. Teddy, at least, looked excited to see Death.

    "We were wondering if you guys were ever gonna come back in," the teen laughed. "Group hug?"

    "Ew," Agatha immediately replied. She shrunk away with a wrinkled nose. "Thank the Goddess I'm a ghost."

    "We hugged outside, though," Billy told her with his wide, pout-y eyes. "Thanks to me," Rio explained. She dropped into the chair in front of the magic-less mortal. "Heard you had a history paper due. I can tell you which authors to use." She's in a good mood, Agatha noted. Since her spot had been stolen, she moved to watch Jen and Billy. She kept her thoughts to herself as the older witch taught her son to mix ingredients in the stereotypical black cauldron.

    As if sensing her thoughts, Jen told her, "It's for training purposes only." (Lilia would have loved that.)

    "If you hold the spoon like this," she said, helping Billy, "then you won't get a cramp while stirring."

    The rest of the evening passed amicably. Agatha helped with definitions when Jen was at a loss for words. She also split her time between the two teens and joined Rio in helping Teddy. They were able tk make an outline for him to use so he could detail the Witch Trials in a way the teacher would accept while also imparting the true horrors of the 1600s. The living decided to take a break for lunch and began to clear the table. "There's a small lock box under my bed," Agatha announced. "There should be plenty of money for you to order whatever you guys want to eat."

    "Is it boobie-trapped?" Jen was quick to ask.

    Agatha smirked as Rio licked the inside of her cheek. Hazel eyes bore into her from across the room. "Not my forte," she drawled. "I did lose the key to it, though. Have fun taking whacks at it. I'm sure that century's worth of rage ought to do it."

    The pink clad witch rolled her eyes. "A century, Agatha. A century!" She disappeared upstairs in a huff.

    Billy cleared his throat. "Could I just speak to you in the kitchen real quick?" Agatha shrugged. "Don't see why not." She followed after him, a tingle of anxiety firing within her nonexistent stomach. "I'm all yours."

    "Does Jen know I made the Road?"

    Well, that was an easy question. "Nope! Didn't think she needed to know that bit. Why? Wanna tell her?"

    Billy quickly shook his head. "She'd flip! I...I don't want her or anyone else to know. I still feel guilty about the others."

    She nodded in understanding. And I feel guilty about taking you from Wanda, she wanted to say. Agatha offered him a smile. "It's our secret. No one has to know. Except Rio. Rio knew all along."

    "Of course, she did," he sighed. "Thanks for keeping my secret! It means a lot to me." "Well, why wouldn't i? I'm your m-mentor," she was quick to correct. "Your mistakes are mine."

    Billy hugged her for a second time, his curls tickling her cheek.

    That's definitely not right... She let him go with a tight smile. "Go get some food with the others. Rio and I will hold down the fort."

    Billy wrinkled his nose. "Something tells me neither of you will be on high-alert." "And you'd be correct!" She shooed him away with a laugh. "Oh, Rio~!"

    "Teddy, get in the car," Billy yelped as he sped-walked from the room. She watched him leave, glad to see him in better spirits. Hands snaked around her waist, Death holding her from behind. "You," Agatha began, turning in Rio's grasp, "were nice to Billy today. I knew you didn't hate him."

    Rio chuckled darkly. "I talked him down. I wasn't nice about anything to anyone but you, Sweetheart." She flashed her teeth at the witch, daring her to argue.

    Agatha preened the cosmic entity, testing out her new ability to feel things. She hummed as Rio's eyes fluttered at her touch. "You helped Teddy, too," she cooed. "So, that was a lie." "Him? I don't mind Teddy. It's The Boy that's the abomination."

    The ghost tutted, fingers trailing down to cup her lover's chin. "Behave. If you still thought of him as an abomination, you wouldn't take turns watching over him."

    "Maybe I'm just using him to get to you," Rio teased, eyes flashing.

    Agatha froze. She pushed away her insecurities, her hand tightening slightly around Death's neck. "Maybe I'm using him to get to you? You want sink your dagger in him so bad, you look silly."

    Rio moaned into the hold. "Mm, you always know just what to say."

    "Well, you do deserve a little treat for fixing my grave," she purred. "What do you say, pretty girl? Want me to take you back to my place?"

    "Can you at least put a blanket down this time? I'm not a fan of your crappy basement floor," Rio argued playfully.

    Agatha crooked her finger at Death. "I was actually referring to my bedroom. But if you want to go back to the basement, I won't stop you." She slid away with a gentle laugh. Hopefully, Billy and the others would take their time getting a pizza or whatever. She had a feeling Rio was going to take every millisecond she could get. Not that you'd find her complaining. Agatha loved having Rio at her mercy for as long as the Universe allowed. She grinned as Rio bolted up the stairs. Bless! The grass was about to get a little greener outside. Chapter End Notes The fact that I stop around 4,000 words on my first draft and somehow manage to add 1,000 more before posting is mind boggling. But hey, keeps me busy at work hehe. Hope y'all are enjoying so far!

    You Walk This Road Alone, Do You?

    Chapter Summary In which the Ballad is discussed.

    Chapter Notes See the end of the chapter for notes Giggling filled the vast forest like a gentle melody. The sound bounced off the ancient bark, warming the chilling heart resting in Death's chest.

    Nicholas Scratch, her beloved son, was playing with his living mother. Death kept her distance, not daring to make herself known. Her last proper visit when Nicky was less than a year old had panicked Agatha to the point of spells being hurled in her direction.

    Nicholas dashed through the trees, his spindly legs carrying him quickly away from his mother. He laughed despite the weakness of his lungs and the unsteady beating of his heart. Agatha moved as fast as she could through the trees, weaving left and right as they played. The young witch was unaware that her time with their son was running out. But Death could see it written plainly on his face. His body wouldn't be able to hold out for much longer. Already, his soul was screaming for her to take him away.

    She was torn.

    Did she ease the suffering of her child and inflict unimaginable pain on her wife, or did she inflict unimaginable pain on her son to ease the suffering of her wife? It was an impossible conundrum. Death was quickly growing to regret granting Agatha any time with their child. Not because she felt she didn't deserve it, but because his death was going to tear the woman apart. No matter what happened, Agatha was going to turn from her. Was going to curse her until her dying days. It wouldn't even matter that Death would continue to love her with her entire being. The love of her life would never forgive. Death would never forgive herself.

    She waited until the sun had sunk below the horizon before sneaking over to the small camp. She thanked the Triple Goddess that Agatha was such a heavy sleeper. It meant she could move right up to the edge of her wards without waking the woman. Not that she needed to get any closer anyway. What she wanted could easily come to her.

    "Mother?" Her son rubbed at an eye as he slipped out of his mama's hold. "I missed you," he whispered. His feet crunched the soft leaves and grass. Everything about him was gentle. A soul too perfect and pure.

    Rio smiled gently, heart aching at his innocence. "I missed you, too, querido." She took his hand as he passed through Agatha's wards. His hand was so small compared to hers. It was a challenge to keep herself from crying at how frail he was. If she could take his place, she would. She'd give him the infinite powers of the universe just to return the smiles to his and his mama's faces. In fact, Death had already tried. In the end, the Ancient Ones only allowed her to offer time to Agatha Harkness. Death was never supposed to be a mother, just like Agatha was never meant to be one. Doomed from the start.

    "Mama says I'll be seven years in a week," Nicky informed proudly. He puffed out his chest with his tiny jacket. Her son made quite the image of a fine young man. "She's going to let me start singing in the taverns with her so we can make money." He continued to tell her about the towns they were going to visit.

    The Green Witch led him down to the nearby stream as she grappled with the weight of reality. (It was the one thing Agatha always stayed close to during her travels.) Nicky had, at most, two more months in him before his own body betrayed him. If he could endure, she would let him travel more. She wanted him to sing. The world didn't deserve to hear his voice, but they needed to hear it at least once. (Death just wanted the world to find her boy as special as she did.) She waited until her throat was no longer thick with emotion to give him a response. "You've finished your song then? Let me hear it." She sat on a decaying log, always a willing audience for her boy.

    Nicky fixed his hair in a way that was entirely Agatha. He slipped into a performer's stance, hands gripping his lapels. His small foot began to tap a rhythm for him to follow. "Down, down, down the road. I walk the witches' road..."

    Death mourned the life he could have lived had she not condemned him at conception.

    Agatha sat on Billy's bed as the boy worked on drawing a circle on his floor. She waited until he had finished before speaking. "A little shoddy, but it'll do. Now, you've made your incantation circle. What's next?"

    Billy automatically reached for his spell book only to huff.

    "It wouldn't be a test if you could cheat," she reminded. Agatha held the book up with a chuckle. "Come on. You've got this. You've cleansed your space, drawn your circle, so you need to...?"

    He snapped his fingers. "Light the candles!"

    "Atta boy! Knew you'd get there eventually." Agatha followed him with her eyes as he set up twelve candles. "Now?"

    "The incantation," Billy told her. He sat as she had shown him numerous times and closed his eyes.

    "Ah ah," she chastised, wagging her finger. "One more thing. Very important for safe spell casting."

    "Right, right." He pulled out his chalk and added a few runes around him. "I think that's it, right?"

    "Is it?"

    He made a face, nose scrunching in thought. "I can't remember," Billy admitted, deflating visibly.

    Agatha hummed and set the book aside. "Do you wanna take a rain check? If you're not in the right mental space, you know how it affects your magic."

    "No, I...It's just..." The teen played with a shoelace. "What if I never learn to control my powers? What if I end up like Wanda and ruin everyone's lives by coming in contact with them?"

    "Woof, those are some strong 'if's," she told him. Agatha drifted into his spell circle to join him on the floor. "Wanda, for the most part, never intended to hurt anyone. She made mistakes." The ghost wiggled her fingers over his hands. "Your magic isn't like hers. It's unique. We'll never know if we don't at least try to understand it."

    Billy nodded, a small smile forming. "That feels weird."

    She drew her hands back. "Had to do something to pull you out of that big head of yours. I think we should try the teleportation spell again tomorrow. You need a good wind down session."

    The teen waved a hand over the floor, his mess clearing instantly. "At least we know that works," he joked. "I'm gonna go grab a snack."

    Agatha jerked her head towards the door, shooing him away silently. She moved from her spot to his record player. Absentmindedly, she picked a record and set it to play. That sweet 70's flute began to play a gentle tune. The singers, two women and a man, entered with a flowing melody.

    She had been a fan of the late 20th century. There had been so many movements and new forms of media that entertained her outside of her main hustle. Witches had been harder to find, but she never found a dull moment. The world was always moving. Always flowing. And, like all things, it always led to one person. The very person lurking in the shadows of the room she was in right now.

    Agatha turned, beckoning her guest from the far corner. "Come to join me?" she asked, a grin growing lazily.

    Rio stepped forward, her Green Witch attire a lovely shade of sage. "I was enjoying the show," she drawled. Her hazel eyes raked over the ghost's form.

    "Easy there, tiger. We both know how that'll end." Agatha invaded Death's space, hands moving to cup that adorably endearing face. It still hurt to see her in this form after losing Nicky, but she was learning to accept it. The similarities were neither of their faults. That was just the way his genetics had been shuffled. She gave her wife a watery smile before pressing her lips to Rio's.

    Since her little misunderstanding with Billy, her sense of touch had heightened. It hadn't returned entirely, but Agatha could definitely feel the slide of skin on skin. She shivered in Death's hold, hands sinking into her hair.

    Rio pressed forward, fingers curling into Agatha's hips possessively. She tried desperately to devour the ghost whole, soft moans escaping into the quiet room.

    Agatha growled at her inability to engage in more intimate acts. If she could, the pair would be back in her house in Westview. She wanted nothing more than to have Death laid out before her, wanting and willing. Oh, how she craved her wife's touch and vice versa! The bedroom door opened, but Rio had no intention of breaking away from her lover. It wasn't until Agatha pulled away, eyes conveying her embarrassment in a way no blush could ever do justice, that Death relented.

    Billy stood in front of the door awkwardly, a bottle of water and a plate of ham, cheese, and crackers in his hands. "You know, I was really hoping it was a joke that you two still made out," he told them. He nudged his door shut as he entered his room. "Welcome home, Rio." Agatha moved to tease Death but choked on her words as a new song began to play. She turned to Billy. "Turn that off," she told him as gently as she could. He gave her a look as he switched the turntable off. Lorna's words faded as the record slowly spun to a stop. "I thought..." He looked at Rio for a second, gauging her reaction. "I thought you liked the song. Is it because of Alice or...?"

    Agatha winced as Rio made a noise in the back of her throat. (She was about to be in a lot of trouble based on that alone.) "Sure. We'll go with that." She prepared to flee for her own sake, but Billy had the bit between his teeth now.

    "So...was it really an accident? You taking her all of her powers and killing her?" (Billy Maximoff really had a way with questions and empathy.) Agatha put some distance between her and her jury. "It was," she reaffirmed. "My magic, like all witches', acts on instinct. I couldn't stop myself. Not until you yelled his name." She couldn't bare to conjure up his memory when discussing her proclivity for killing witches. He wouldn't have appreciated that. Not after what she did.

    Rio made herself comfortable. "She didn't hold it against you," she informed gently. Always gently when Agatha did care about the victim. And there was no denying just how much the young witch's death affected her.

    The ghost nodded quietly. She didn't really want to talk about the girl. The first witch to try and defend her selflessly, and she had died at Agatha's own hands. Even if her mother had forced it on her, Agatha was the one who couldn't control her magic. Another accident under her belt that proved her mother right.

    "Well, I'm glad she was able to pass on peacefully," Billy said once the silence had stretched on too long. "She's with her mother, now. No more curses to haunt them or keep them apart." Rio, who hadn't stop watching her wife, added, "Lilia went along willingly, too. But her spirit lives on. You know that."

    Agatha tried to smile, but her guilt-ridden mind turned it into a grimace. "That's great, dear." She hoped that the two would drop the conversation now. (No dice.)

    Billy looked over at Lorna's record as he finished chewing his mouthful. "So, where did the Ballad come from? I never did find the source when I was researching you." Agatha felt like time slowed to a stop as Rio fixed her with a pointed look. "It's such an old song," she began, a nervous laugh nipping at the heels of her words.

    "Nicky wrote it," Rio ground out. For the first time in a long time, Death looked angry with her. (Angrier and more hurt than when they last fought.)

    Billy turned to face Agatha. "But you said-?"

    "I say a lot of things," she quickly reasoned. There was no way she was going to let him dig her a deeper hole. "Nicky wrote the original version."

    Death tilted her head, fingers digging into Billy's headboard to the point of chipping the wood. "That's all you have to say?"

    Agatha entered a staring contest with her wife. "He doesn't need to know anything else," she told Death firmly. "That's between us."

    Rio huffed out a disbelieving laugh. "The whole world believes in his song because of you. The whole world fears it because of you, too."

    Billy looked between the two. "Don't fight," he told them, voice small. "Pretend I didn't ask. I'll just..."

    "NNNOOO." Death turned to him, fleshy face gone. "I wwwaaannnttt you to know." Agatha reached for magic she no longer had access to. "Stop," she pleaded. "Don't tell him." "Not that," Rio spat. (Oh, Agatha had definitely fucked up.) "That little tune your coven sang before walking towards their death. That was created by Nicky."

    The ghost growled. "That's enough!"

    Death pressed on. "He wrote it for him and his mother to share on their travels. But when he died, it became a siren call."

    "They deserved it," she snarled. The depth of her wound, uncovered. "Every last witch that sang the ballad deserved to die. I never heard you complain when you collected your bodies." "You guys-"

    Rio laughed. "Why would I complain, sweetheart? You never wanted to see me. You never once thought about how I might have felt."

    "You stole him from me! Like a thief in the night," Agatha spat. She slipped away into the Ether, but she knew that was futile. Rio was already there, waiting to carry on their argument. Death marched up to her, eyes angry and red. "I did what was best for him! I thought you finally understood that."

    Of course, she did. Agatha heard the coughing. Spotted the blood on his handkerchief. Soothed every ache and fever that came their way. Agatha understood all too well. "You didn't let me say goodbye," she sobbed, her anger giving way to hurt. "I woke up to his cold body. I had to bury him alone. Where were you when I needed you most?" Rio looked shocked. (And she had every right to be. Agatha had never brought this point up before.) "I knew you would hate me if I went to you," she answered honestly. "I thought if I gave you space..."

    Agatha threw herself at Death, wound gushing with sorrow. "You took him and left me alone." She buried her face in Rio's shoulder. "I know. I know! But it still fucking hurts." Death held her. "It hurts for me, too."

    The ghost raised her head to look into hazel eyes. She pressed her forehead to Rio's. "You had an impossible choice," she acknowledged aloud. "I hate it, but you were the one who was dealt the worst hand in the end." She pressed her palm against the spot over Death's heart. "I have punished you long enough. Let me bear the weight now."

    Rio gripped at Agatha's arms, her breathing growing heavier by the second. She shook. With rage. With grief. With relief. "I never wanted to," she whispered. "I never wanted to hurt either of you. He was hurting."

    Agatha let them sink to the cold ground of the Ether. Black soil stuck to the two as Death allowed herself to grieve. Agatha wrapped Rio up in her arms, her heart aching for her love. "I've got you," she promised. "He wouldn't want us to fight anymore. He..." Her voice cracked. "He always chose peace."

    Death shuddered as the first sob ripped from her chest. Her fingers dug into Agatha as a shout soon followed. The sound echoed endlessly in the dark world between realms. Rippled through time and space.

    It settled in Agatha's chest, telling her the things Rio could never say. Burned her the only way aged grief bottled up for centuries could burn. It drowned her in sorrow, but she held firm. She had promised to be there for her wife, and she meant it. They had skirted around the issue long enough. Rio had always been patient with her, so it was time she returned the favor. Agatha let Death pound her chest with heart-wrenching sobs just like Agatha had done when she had fallen apart in Death's arms.

    They were two damaged souls reuniting in the face of their shared grief. After an eternity of sniffling back and forth, the couple moved to leave the gloomy In- Between. Unsurprisingly, Billy was still in his room, a spell book in his hands. Agatha cleared her throat even though she knew he knew they were back. "Anyway, where were we?" she said, fluttering her fingers as she waved to the boy.

    Billy swiveled in his chair, a serious look on his face. He looked a bit like Wanda right before she locked Agatha away in her own mind. The teen tossed the spell book aside, sizing the pair up. "You guys...you're getting a lot better about talking to each other." Agatha couldn't help but laugh, the tension in the room defusing. She shared a look with Rio, her heart stuttering at the look of adoration on the other woman's face. "And all it took was me dying." The ghost moved to claim his bed with her shimmery form. "I'm in a good mood now, so you may pester away. I know you want to."

    Rio sat at the foot of the bed, her eyes glued to Agatha. She looked like she wanted to say something, but kept it to herself. Instead, the Green Witch turned her attention to Billy. "I wouldn't waste the chance, Boy. She might never be this open ever again." The Maximoff buzzed with energy. "Okay, great! I've got so many questions." He jerked his thumb in the direction of his silenced record player. "Did you ever make Lorna pay you for the rights to the Ballad?"

    The lounging witch smirked. "Nah. Not that I didn't think about it." She looked to Rio. "It didn't feel right."

    Billy mumbled to himself as Agatha heard a pencil scratching along the surface of a piece of paper. "How did the Ballad even get popular?"

    Agatha sat up, eyeing her would-be interviewer with an amused grin. She turned to Rio and gave her wife a 'this guy' head nod. "Wanna tell him?"

    "Sweetheart, you know how much I love it when you spin a good yarn," Death teased. For the briefest of seconds, Agatha could pretend they were telling a teenage Nicky about their crazy, early days. But as quick as the thought entered her head, it passed. She would never have that with Nicky because she had been too afraid to let his mother be around him. She would be sure to avoid that mistake with Billy. Agatha cleared her throat, her fingers tapping her brooch. "It started off as a tavern piece Nicky would sing. At some point, witches began to get it in their head that the Road was real." She silently thanked Rio for the arm that wrapped around her waist. "After his death, like right after, a witch stumbled on me. I was having a moment, but that didn't seem to matter to her. She wanted to go down the Road for whatever reason, and I needed magic."

    Death leaned forward, her hazel eyes lit up. "So, she went on a killing spree! Oh, you should have seen her." She bit her lip, eyeing Agatha like a piece of meat.

    "Okay, okay," she told the Green Witch. "Let's keep it 'PG' for the boy." Billy stopped writing. "Oh! So, that's what you meant when you said you planned on killing everyone day one!" A menacing grin grew. "But you sent me upstairs."

    Rio gave Agatha the same look. "Hm....?"

    The ghost pursed her lips and raised her chin. "I didn't know if you had any magic to steal," she lied. "I was going to make you my errand boy. You were terribly efficient at it when it came to acquiring witches."

    Billy laughed, shaking his head. "I see what you mean now," he told Death. "Has a soft spot for warlocks," Billy mumbled as he made a note.

    "Cheeky," she grumbled, but there was no malice to it. Now, she had to worry about two people peeking through her defenses. (Oh, Goddess! Were they going to include Jen? That woman would make her afterlife unbearable!)

    "What does the song even mean? Like, some of it makes sense. I get where it makes references to witchcraft of old, but there are some pieces that I don't get." Agatha swallowed thickly. "You'd have to give me examples, kid. Some bits, I made. Some bits, Nicky made."

    "Well, like, going down the road for starters. What road were you guys actually referring to?" That was simple enough for the witch. "The Road of Life, mainly. But originally it was sung because we walked around Massachusetts so much. We could never stay in one place too long. I was a wanted woman, and he..."

    "I was following them," Rio said for her. Her tone softened to a near whisper. "I just wanted to watch him grow up."

    Agatha leaned over to ran a hand down the side of Death's head, soothing her to the best of her ability. "I was a coward," she whispered to her wife.

    Billy looked away to give them a moment. Once the ghost and Death had settled, he pressed on. "There's that bit about 'blood and tears and bone'..."

    "...Maiden, Mother, Crone," Rio sang softly to Agatha, mostly out of habit. "...Does that have to do with a ritual?"

    The witch realized they were one wrong interpretation from having to have sacrifice a person in Billy's eyes. She laughed at the mental image of serving Mrs. Hart up to Rio on a silver platter. "No, 'fraid not. I'll keep that in mind for next time, though." She sat straighter, resting her back against his bedroom wall. "That was a 'me' bit. Nicky was of my blood, my tears, and my bone." The witch risked a joke. "Thankfully, he got his good looks from Rio." Billy scrunched his nose up in confusion. "So, wait...If you're both girls..." The couple fell into a fit of laughter. Meanwhile, the poor boy tried to work the solution out in his head.

    Agatha let out a long sigh, her face adorned with a grin. "Billy, dear, we're witches." She looked over at Rio, her heart nearly bursting out of her ghostly chest. "Where there's love and magic, there will always be a way."

    The teen gagged. "You guys are making me sick," he groaned. "Moving on!" The two pecked lips just to make him squirm.

    "Lastly," he hissed, "is it actually 'coven two,' or 'coven true'?"

    "Two," Agatha was quick to say, just as she had on the Road. "Nicky and I were our own coven. Some whack-a-doo questioned his brilliance and changed the lyrics." "Huh...that's..."

    "Depressing?" Rio said. "Tell me about it. I love Nicky's version, but Lorna's captured the emotion better, don't you think?"

    Agatha fell silent.

    The reds, blues, and greens of the dance floor lights pulsed with upbeat music of the 1970s. Couples, throuples, and groupies swayed in time in their bell-bottom jeans and starched arrow collars. Agatha sat at the bar, a drink in hand and a woman in her sights. The magic the witch held was palpable from across the sea of people. Protection Magic. Advanced and ancient. The woman, a singer from the looks of things, had long, silky black hair that reached down to the backs of her knees. Agatha wondered what it would feel like to run her fingers through it. Maybe she'd have a little fun tonight and then steal her magic. It would be a nice send off. Better than how all those other gullible fools were sent to Rio. Speaking of, she hadn't seen her scorned lover in a while. Probably for the best. Their anniversary was coming up.

    Agatha's thoughts halted as the singer and her band announced their newest hit: 'The Ballad of the Witches' Road.' She nearly shattered the glass in her hand as memories of people and things she did not care to think about flooded her mind. Who was this woman! How dare she take their song and twist it into...into...

    "If I can't hold you/Remember what I told you!"

    She forgot about her target and left the venue. Agatha stopped outside, gasping and gulping for air as hot tears streamed down her face. After composing herself, the witch snuck into the dressing rooms to find this Lorna Wu and make her pay with her life. The Ballad belonged to her and Nicky, and them alone. She threw open the door, curses ready to fly and... Curious eyes looked up at her, blinking slowly. She sat in her mother's, presumably, vanity chair with a Dancerella doll cradled in her arms. The child was probably around the age of ten given her height. She waved to Agatha, a toothy smile reaffirming her innocence in the whole situation. "Hi, I'm Alice!"

    Agatha lowered her hands. "Sorry, wrong room," she told the girl sweetly. She backed out of the doorway and stumbled away.

    The next time the song came on, she listened to it in its entirety. Agatha decided she would leave Lorna Wu be. It was clear to her that it was, as it had always been, a song between mother and child. If there was anything Agatha could respect, it was leaving something for your child to remember your love by. She'd sung the Ballad as she laid Nicky to rest in the cold, hard ground. Lorna sang it in hopes her daughter would always know what she meant to her. From then on, Agatha eased up on her Witches' Road scam. She would find other ways to source her magic.

    The ghost blinked to find Rio's face directly in front of hers.

    "You zoned out there," Death teased. "Wanna share with the class?"

    Agatha shoved Rio to the floor, wincing at the resulting thud. Billy's sound-proofing spell only worked on their voices, unfortunately. Thankfully, the teen proactively shouted a 'sorry' to his parents. She rolled her eyes at her wife before helping her back up. "Don't do that," she huffed. "Just for that, you don't get to know."

    "Do I get to know?" Billy looked at her with a mock pout.

    She wrinkled her nose. "What is going on with you two ganging up on me? That doesn't seem fair!" Agatha drifted through Billy to make him shiver. She pointed to his spell book. "I want you to have that spell ready for tomorrow, Beauford. And another thing-" She stopped as she spied an name on a piece of paper that most certainly did not belong to her son. "Who the hell is Eddie?" She gasped dramatically, a hand pressed to her chest. "I do not condone cheating unless you're me, which you're not."

    Billy laughed. "Calm down, Agatha. Eddie is Teddy's real name. I got his name mixed up in class one day, and it stuck." He looked away with a blush. "I was going over his history report for him."

    Agatha shot a look at Rio. "Thought I was raising a degenerate for a second." "Aren't you?" Death teased. She grinned widely, face glowing in the sunlight. (Just the way Agatha liked her.)

    "Whatever. Just get to work on that spell. We'll discuss your bubbly boyfriend later." The teen retrieved his spell book, rolling his eyes. "Yes, mom," he playfully groaned. The ghost nearly fainted. Rio, as always, noticed and took her hand. "You mind if I steal your mommy for a second?"

    Billy waved them away. "Go do your gross ghost stuff in someone else's room. I'll be here studying, like a good kid."

    "You are a good kid," Agatha couldn't help but say. She looked away when he glanced up at her.

    Billy, with his infinitely irritating sweetness, told her, "Well, if things had been different, you would have been a great mom. I'm sure Nicky would agree."

    Rio drug her away before she could turn into a sobbing mess.

    Chapter End Notes Fuuuuuuuuuckkkkkkkkk! I really am just as bad as Agatha when it comes to names. Y'all really let me write 7 chapters calling Billy's bf 'Teddy' and it's actually Eddie. 😭 "No loyalty! No loyalty! Not even from you! Where is Nicky!" (Sorry, had to finish the audio hehe)

    Sorry, buddy. That was a my bad. I was lost in the Agathario sauce and never stopped to check 😂 Anywhosits! Hope y'all enjoyed this chapter! I almost cried lol You Are the Magician...

    Chapter Summary So...Y'all remember how Agatha's got some weird ghost thing going on? There's a reason for that.

    Chapter Notes Thank FriendofthePhoenix1234 for the chaos that is about to ensue!

    The way I could have gaslit everyone into thinking Eddie's name was Teddy all along is comical, endearing, and concerning. I fear we all would have fallen for Agatha's scams in a heartbeat (as if I wouldn't have done so knowingly and willingly) 😂 Love y'all so much for that, tho. Let's me know I'm not alone in this brainrot. See the end of the chapter for more notes Somehow, the coven (because that's what they were now) began to meet regularly during the week. Every Tuesday, Thursday, and Saturday found Jen, Billy, Teddy, Agatha, and sometimes Rio, hanging out in Agatha's house. With some help from Billy, they'd drafted a fake will for Agatha that left all her possessions in his name. Since he was still a minor, Jen was given guardianship for the time being. The witch had spruced the place up within days of taking pseudo-ownership. She promised not to paint the house, but did leave her own touch here and there. (Pink curtains in the kitchen. Blegh!)

    Today, a Saturday, meant the group would take a break from magic lessons and school. The living took up the living room (hehe) while Agatha floated about aimlessly. She just...bounced around everywhere like the old DVD logo. (Honestly, the woman was bored out of her mind without Rio or her magic.) With the sun setting, Agatha considered going down the street and haunting the living shit out of some random family. Maybe she'd find one with children and stand menacingly in their bedroom. Anything to make her feel alive again. Unfortunately, Billy had other ideas.

    "So, now that it's spooky season, I was thinking we could watch a movie or two tonight." The teen pulled out a stack of DVDs and a couple of VHS tapes. "I wanted it to be a bit of a mystery, so I removed the labels."

    "I'm down," Teddy told his boyfriend.

    "I don't have a problem with that. Agatha?" Jen looked over at the ghost who was currently holding a match to one of her jackets. "Agatha!"

    She pouted in response. "I was giving it some personality," Agatha informed. She tossed the lit match behind her. "What are we doing now?"

    Jen ran over to stomp out the small patch of singed hardwood flooring. "Now, you don't get a say. We're going to watch a movie, no arguing."

    "No! No more Frozen," she told Billy. The ghost dropped to her knees, hands clasped together tightly. "Anything but Ms. Cold Shoulders! Please! There's no way to kill myself this time."

    He made a face. "What...? I don't want to know." Billy held up a VHS tape. "I brought witch- themed movies."

    "Thank the Divine Mother," she praised. "That, I can do. If I ever meet the people that constructed that curse of a song..." Agatha drifted over to settle on the back of the couch. The back door opened and closed. It wasn't long before Rio appeared from the darkened kitchen. She wore a deep emerald green turtleneck and black leggings with green and purple plant imagery. Her makeup had been reduced to a minimal amount of eye shadow and wing- tipped eyeliner. (If she had told them she just got back from working an office job, the coven would have believed her. That thought alone had Agatha biting her lip.) "Sweetheart, I'm home," Death announced confidently. She raised her hands, waiting for her lover.

    Agatha was quick to meet her for a kiss. "You're just in time. Billy's torturing us with, what are the kids saying these days? Spoopy? Whatever! We're watching a movie." Rio quirked a brow. "I hope it's a slasher," she said as Agatha pulled her along. Billy, Jen, and Teddy sat on the full couch, bowls of popcorn in their laps. A large blanket draped across the trio to keep the chill away. Meanwhile, Rio made herself comfortable on the black and white recliner from Agatha's Agnes days. Death patted her knee with a mischievous grin.

    The ghost rolled her eyes before settling in Rio's lap. "No funny business," she warned. Rio held her hands up in surrender. "Go on, Boy. We're ready."

    Billy didn't even bother to correct her. He hit 'play' on the remote and sat back. "This one's for you and Agatha. Thought we should get a peek into your lives a bit."

    The Disney logo appeared and the ghost nearly sobbed. ("Let it goooo! Let it gooooo!") She whimpered as the old theme quieted and fingers tangled in her hair. Rio ran her fingers though the tendrils until Agatha was practically a shimmering, translucent puddle in her lap. If she weren't so distracted, she might have noticed the date '1693' on the spell book in the opening credits. It wasn't until Bette Midler was on screen that the witch howled with rage. "Of all the crappy things to put on, you chose Hocus Pocus!" Agatha flew into the air in a ghostly attempt to pace. "They took all my notes and threw them out the window in this one! Really fumbled what could have been a masterpiece of art."

    "Let the children have their fun," Rio teased. She patted the armrest with a sideways nod. "Think about how mad it would make Lilia."

    Agatha pursed her lips and flipped her hair. "That would have been funny to see," she stated calmly. The ghost lowered back down to her wife. "But I am not happy with this choice. We never even wore such gaudy makeup. People barely made it past the age of twelve!" "Is Winifred based on you?" Billy asked her, tone teasing. (The little shit.) Jen and Teddy snickered despite their confusion.

    "That's right. Laugh it up." Agatha simmered and stewed as the trio finished making fun of her. "Iconic as she is, I'm still the original Bad Girl."

    "What about me?" Rio asked innocently. She caught Teddy whisper something to Billy. Death quirked a brow. "What was that?"

    Billy laughed. "He said your Agatha's babygirl baby."

    Agatha hummed at the information. She turned and stroked Rio's face, making sure the others could see and hear her. "Are you my babygirl, Hot Stuff?"

    "Get a room," Jen groaned. "Or wait until the movie's over!"

    The ghost shot Rio a wink before turning back to the television. "Oh, great. A hanging. Jesus- fucking-christ, this movie!"

    Once the Sanderson Sisters were vanquished, the movie turned into the sort of cheesy film all 80's and 90's media were known for. The immortal couple tried to ignore the sweetness of Dani's innocence that reminded them of another child. (Shut up! No, they didn't hold hands the entire movie! You just happened to look over every time they did.) They grumbled to themselves as the foolish boy (like someone they knew) lit the black candle. Rio grinned at Agatha as the Sanderson Sisters celebrated their return. The minutes ticked by, Agatha beginning to grow bored once more.

    "He just wants to get back to his sister," Billy mumbled once Thackery Binx revealed his backstory. Teddy hugged him tightly.

    "Did you give them the idea for the evil book?" Jen asked Agatha pointedly. "No," she growled. "That was a coincidence. Besides, that looks nothing like the Darkhold. It's literally a dark book forged from the fires of Hell. Their book is made from human skin." "I'm just saying..." Jen raised her hands in defense. "You're one of the few witches to have dabbled in dark magic and survived."

    Agatha rolled her eyes and sulked.

    The movie continued until they reached the musical portion. At this point, Rio was just as interested in the movie as the others. She shimmied and bobbed her head in time with the lyrics. "Reminds me of the Dancing Plague," she sighed longingly. "So many bodies." "Let me possess a pilot, and I'll give you an early anniversary gift," she suggested, a smirk playing on her lips.

    Death grinned widely. "I'll let you know if things run slow."

    "So, is that how the Ballad of the Witches' Road would have worked?" Billy asked Agatha. "Kid, we're gonna work on how you differentiate spells and hexes. You're making me look bad right now."

    "You mean for Lorna?" Jen asked Billy. "Or for us?"

    "Lorna," Agatha was quick to answer. "We've been arguing about why she could never open the Road."

    "Oh..." The other woman turned back to the screen.

    Thanks, Billy sent her telepathically.

    Teddy cleared his throat. "So, since you lived through the Salem Witch Trials, did you learn how to use technology like them, or...?" He shifted as Agatha sent him a disbelieving look. "I didn't vanish for centuries at a time," she told the trio. "A good witch adapts. A better witch bends the world to her whims. I learned just like everyone else, and more." Rio smirked. "Did you ever figure out how to work a dishwasher?"

    "Whose side are you on?" She moved to smack Death on the shoulder, but let it pass through her wife's form. Agatha would give her something to smirk about later. "What I don't understand is how they keep letting these kids get away. Like, I'm entirely against sucking the souls from children, but come on now," the pink witch groaned. "This is just embarrassing."

    "See! It's ridiculous," Agatha said, nodding in agreement. "I tried to tell them, but noooo!" "Did you want the bad guys to win?" Teddy asked with a laugh.

    "Yes," Rio and Agatha said at the same time.

    The Green Witch tilted her head to the side with a menacing grin. "There's nothing more thrilling than watching powerful women do what they do best."

    Billy rolled his eyes. "Not being those simp allegations," he mumbled to his boyfriend. "I think he's calling you 'simpering,' dear," Agatha said with faux offense. She pretended to clutch at her pearls.

    "Oh no, my feelings," Death mocked in a whiny voice.

    "He means you're weak-willed when it comes to Agatha," Teddy explained. He scrunched his nose in thought. "Like when people say they'll do anything for their partner and always tell people how much they love them."

    A crazed grin grew along Agatha's cheeks. "Is that so?" She side-eyed her wife. "I have two new terms for you, babygirl."

    Billy gagged.

    "Stop. It's cute," Teddy told the witchling. "Don't be like that." He looked over at the couple. "You guys are the cutest."

    "You're just saying that because you've labelled everyone," Billy laughed. "Labelled us how?" Rio asked.

    Teddy blushed. "Well, you and Agatha are like the group moms. Jen is the cool aunt. And I'm the strikingly handsome boyfriend to your adorably nerdy son."

    "Huh, I've never been called a 'cool aunt' before," Jen told the teen. "I like it." Agatha looked away before Billy could see her panic. "Yeah, yeah. When is this movie going to be over? We've been here for ages."

    The group quieted as the final chapter of the story unfolded. Everyone agreed Max was annoying and needed to get over himself. Agatha silently cheered Dani on, admiring her courage. But the witches...?

    "If Winifred was smart, she would have chosen a better spell," the ghost grumbled. "What idiot makes such an oddly specific, timed spell and doesn't plan accordingly before having to use it! Besides, teens have far more potent souls to devour," she added just to get a rise out of Jen and Billy. Agatha succeeded as the pair shot her a dark look. She heard Rio chuckle in amusement, hands ghosting (hehe) along her side.

    "Thackery Binx, what took thee so long?"

    Oh, Agatha was a thousand-percent crying as the children passed on. She clutched at her brooch as she fought to hold in a sob. "Stupid cat," she growled, voice cracking. "That's not even what the Afterlife looks like."

    "Aw, Agatha, it's-"

    "Finish that sentence and I'll set the house on fire while you sleep," the ghost threatened the woman. "Just change the damn movie already."

    The other woman spammed the 'eject' button, eyes focusing on anything but the translucent woman.

    "Can I ask a question...about dying?" Teddy said, raising a hand cautiously. "No, I don't know when you'll die," Rio told him. "No, I can't tell you how you'll die. I don't know any specifics. I just guide souls."

    "And you're the best at it," Agatha told her, a hand stroking Death's cheek. "I was just going to ask what it looks like on the Other Side," the teen asked carefully. "Is it bright and cheerful, or does it depend on who you were as a person?"

    "How would you put it, Agatha?" Rio asked her, passing the question along. "You know it looks different to me."

    The witch nodded. "Definitely not bright and cheerful. It's just...how to put it? ...Otherworldly, I guess."

    "It's sort of like walking into a room with a fog machine, but the fog is black and the walls and lights are green," Billy told Teddy. He wiggled his fingers. "It's not cold or hot, just a perpetually misty kind of vibe."

    "How do you know?" Agatha narrowed her eyes at her son.

    "I saw the Other Side when I was in Rio's memories," he reminded.

    The ghost pursed her lips as Death shifted underneath her. "Well...let's just keep our telepathic hands to ourselves and not do that again. What if you had seen something like a badly mangled body?"

    Rio stiffened and let out a long exhale. "Gotta go," she whispered to Agatha. Death pressed a kiss to her wife's cheek. "Te veo, mi amor."

    Agatha bounced on the couch as she was un-tethered from Rio's lap. She picked herself up before anyone could question her lack of ghostness. "Well, when duty calls..." The ghost flicked a light on. "We should probably get going, too."

    "What? No! Just one more movie. Please, Agatha," Billy pleaded. He even tilted head as he pouted.

    "Could we not stay with the witches and survive with them?"

    Goddess, but she was being such a sentimental mess thanks to that horrid movie. "Pick one without witches," she instructed firmly.

    As Teddy picked one out, Billy cleared his throat. "Since Halloween's coming up, can we turn the house into one of those haunted houses for trick-or-treaters?"

    "Great thinking, Billy. We can put Agatha to work so she's not mooching off of us," Jen laughed.

    "I'm gonna set you on fire while you sleep after all," Agatha shot back. "Whatever," the other woman said. "What did you have in mind?"

    Death slipped through the thin veil between realms, but kept herself hidden away from the Living. She stalked over to stand next to her wife, hands moving to grab at enticing hips. "What are we doing outside?" she whispered to the ghost. The ghost that was losing her opacity with each passing day. The soul that felt a bit more solid each time they touched. "Billy's throwing a haunted house thingy tonight. Guess what I'm doing?" Rio hummed, a smile curling upwards. "Let me guess...You're the bouncer!" Agatha barked out a laugh. "If only! No. They intend to use me like a prop. It's degrading." Death looked at her wife with darkened eyes. "We could always sneak off," she suggested, a finger tracing lazy patterns against the would-be skin of Agatha's neck. "I'll be sure you're put to good use. You can even degrade me if you want."

    The witch bit back a groan. "I think you like to get me riled up because you know I can't do anything about it," she growled. "And then I have to take that frustration out on you." Rio gave her a wink. "No, my love. I wish we could dance like old times, too. Maybe..." She kept the rest of her thoughts to herself. It would be a cruelty to fill the woman's eyes with hope. Just because her form was more solid didn't mean she had a body. It did, however, mean that someone (The Boy, most likely) had tampered with Agatha's soul. She needed to figure out what exactly before bringing it up.

    "Maybe?"

    Death danced away, hazel eyes twinkling with mischief. "Maybe we should have some fun tonight."

    Agatha chased after her, the pair weaving around the living with a laugh. It was almost like old times. Almost.

    The Green Witch longed for the days of vast fields and forests. For the days when humans didn't find new ways to kill one another. When all life co-existed in harmony. But those days didn't have Agatha. They were dull and repetitive. Death longed to be held in those strong arms that had felled many a witch and mortal. She wanted those teeth to sink into her throat, to give her a taste of pain again. Needed those warm hands to claw at her hips and shoulders. To have that glorious woman above her like the sun nourishing the earth. Rio stopped as The Boy spotted her, which was not right. She was hidden to mortal sight right now. Death narrowed her eyes at him. "CCCOOOMMMEEE HHHEEERRREEE." The Boy startled at the sound of her voice.

    Good.

    He was one of the few she wanted to fear her. Stealing second lives and tampering with her wife's. Oh, how she wanted to stake him to the ground and leave him to rot! But there would be time for that later. Right now, she needed The Boy to tell her why he could see her. "Do you have to be so loud? You make my head feel like it's gonna split," The Boy whined. He pulled at a few curls that had shifted under his blue headband. (The audacity to wear that horrid outfit when it was the same he'd used to convince Agatha to give herself up.) Rio entered his plane, if only to hear his heart try to escape her proximity, and fixed him with a glare. "You could see me before. Why?"

    The Boy shrugged. "I've been able to since that mind trip incident. What's the big deal?" She wanted to wring his neck. Who did he think he was, speaking to her so casually? He was lucky her love for Agatha trumped her distaste for him. In due time, he'd regret his aloofness. "You can see into the Ether," she reiterated slowly. (Always so slowly for him and his fellow mortals. Thick skulls, the lot of them.) "That's not a skill reserved for you. It's like you've copied some of my powers and made them your own."

    The realization hit her with its full weight. If The Boy could tamper with souls and alter reality, he could rewrite the rules of Life, Death, and Magic. He was dangerous. Maybe more dangerous than the Scarlet Witch. She reached for her dagger.

    "There you two are," Agatha shouted. She drifted across the lawn with a wide grin. "I'm ready to cause some chaos and finally meet your parents."

    The Boy turned away from Death, stoking her ire. "Just remember, if anyone asks, you're a new holographic AI feature. Rio, can you-?"

    "No."

    The pair looked at her. Worry filled those misty blue eyes, so Death relented. "What, Boy?"

    He grinned. "Can you help Jen finish decorating the yard? Teddy and I are gonna finish up inside." The Boy looked down at a plastic skeleton. "I wish it looked a bit more realistic, but it'll do. It's just for one night, anyway."

    Death smacked her lips as magic pulsed through the air. She looked around, waiting for something to happen. Rio narrowed her eyes. "I hope an oil rig explodes. This place sucks." "That's the spirit!" Agatha beamed at her. "I promise to make it up to you later." Death groaned inwardly. Perhaps she was a 'simp' after all.

    Man and Woman Kaplan found Billy talking to Agatha. The ghost turned to them, pleased to be seen for once. They were good to her son, so she would return the favor just this once. "Mom, Dad, this is Agatha. She's a holographic AI interface. Say 'hi,' Agatha." The witch resisted the urge to roll her eyes and struck a pose. "Howdy, friends," she said, slipping into her Agnes character. "My, those costumes are just a treat!" Tone it down, Billy sent her. He laughed, hugging his mother. "Isn't it so cool? Jen is letting Teddy and I borrow her for the haunted house."

    "Yeah...So, when did this thing come out?" Man Kaplan asked his son. He eyed Agatha warily. "I've never seen one before."

    She jumped into action, laughing in character. "Oh my! I came out in the 1600s," Agatha told them with a wink.

    Woman Kaplan clapped, chuckling. "I get it. 'Cause she's dressed up as a witch. Very clever." What?...Oh! They meant...Got it, got it. The ghost wished her wife were there to save her from this conversation.

    "AI answers questions, right?" Billy's father scratched his head. "Hey, Agatha, what's the secret to a long life?"

    "Not dying," she told him. No wonder they have to go to school for eight hours a day, she scoffed inwardly.

    "Ha! That's...that's not wrong." Man Kaplan looked perplexed as he grappled with the weight of his mortality.

    "Did you know that married men are more likely to be killed by their spouses than single men?" Agatha grinned widely, mentally patting herself on the back. Tonight, she would haunt Westview to the full extent of her abilities.

    "Billy, I think your fancy robot might be broken," his father told him. He pulled Woman Kaplan away from Agatha.

    "What? That was a good call-back! Wanda would have laughed," she said without much thought.

    Billy shot her a look. "I think her frequencies are scrambled. You can return to your charging station, Agatha."

    Rude! Agatha tilted her head violently, eyes boring into the teen. "If that's what you want, Billy." Ah, what the hell! Let's really give 'em something to worry about. "Remember, I'm always watching in case you need me. Best friends until the end." She made her ghost form glitch out of existence.

    The Kaplan's grabbed Billy as she vanished from their sight. "That's enough of that," Woman Kaplan said, eyes wide. "Let's see what the rest of the place looks like." Agatha shuddered as she entered the In-Between. She groaned as the edges of the Ether stung at her relentlessly. It was starting to get harder to do so, but she didn't want to tell Rio. If something was wrong, if she was going to fade away forever, she couldn't let Death know. Rio would rip the realms apart to try and save her. And if Billy's magic was the cause...She needed to figure out what the hell was happening to her, and quick.

    Death, as it happened, walked freely amongst the incoming trick-or-treaters. She let them see her true form, hoping to spawn herself some new iconography. (Her old robe and scythe form really needed to be updated in their databases.) Decorations finished, she sniffed around for the strange magic that she sensed earlier. Unlike normal witchcraft, this type seemed to have a mind of its own. Death figured it belonged to The Boy. Irritating and unreasonable. The marks of a Maximoff through and through.

    She hoped it had been nothing but a bio pulse. A wave of magic expelled every so often to avoid pent up surges. If it wasn't, there was cause for concern. His magic, thanks to Agatha's spiritual and biological influences, was more stable than Wanda's. His hex hadn't fallen apart while he was stressed. It adapted. It bent the rules of magic to his whim. (For that, she did blame Agatha.) There was no telling what all he was capable of. And now, Agatha's soul was doing something outside of the ordinary. Death was at a loss and concerned for her wife's well-being. The Boy had meddled with so much, and right now was no different. Clearly, his magic was doing something or the smell would have faded already.

    Rio tilted her head as one of the decorations twitched. She watched it closely, waiting to see if it would move again. The earth tingled, the scent of magic and mud filling her senses. (Was nothing sacred to The Boy?)

    Death turned on her heel and ran for Agatha.

    She wouldn't have stopped if the twenty-foot skeleton had just squished the children. But no, it had to sense her and demand a heart to heart. It ignored the gathering crowd in favor of a real meal.

    Rio sneered. "Wanna see how that ends?" She pulled her dagger from her sheath, more than ready for a fight. (Without her beloved Aggie, her knife was rather sad and underutilized.) Death stood her ground as it stepped towards her.

    "Whoa, cool," some random child exclaimed. "How is it doing that?"

    That seemed to catch The Boy's attention. He sprinted over, blue springing to his fingertips. "What happened?"

    Of course, he didn't know. That would be asking for too much, wouldn't it? Death glared at him. "I hate you," she informed point blank.

    "I love you too, Rio." He blasted the skeletal hand that reached for them. She seethed.

    Amused screams transformed into horrified shrieks as people ran from the house and yard. Jen and Teddy escaped the horrors with wide eyes. Bats flew out of the open doors and windows. Spiders as big as dogs crawled out after the flying creatures of the night. People ran for the hills, the street emptying out in record time.

    "Let me guess. The decorations came to life?" Rio didn't need to wait for an answer as a mummy burst through the front door. She turned to look at The Boy, pointing with a shaking fist. "Somebody put gloves on that damn boy!" (By the Divine Goddess she was sick of him!) Her eyes widened at the lack of retort. "Where's Agatha?"

    Panic gripped at her heart, strong and sure. She could still sense her, but it felt wrong. Their connection felt...slick. Slimey, even. Like Agatha was...

    Death slipped into the Ether. "Agatha! Agatha, where are you?" She had to find her before time ran out. They wouldn't have to worry about her becoming a vengeful, lost, or trapped soul if she didn't get to her soon.

    Living souls that wound up in the Ether were doomed to melt away in a horrific manner. "AGATHA!"

    The realms quaked and rumbled. She spread her consciousness out, feeling around for her wife. She felt a ping and zapped over, tears to the veil be damned. There, writing on the ground, Agatha struggled to breathe. It confirmed her suspicions. Filled Death with dread. Agatha Harkness was between life and death with no body to house her soul, trapped in the Ether.

    ...F U C K...

    Chapter End Notes Continuing the tradition of having the younger characters teach the older characters about the word 'simp.'
