This time, we've added babygirl to the mix because Agatha and Rio are both babygirl in my heart. Author is Rio, Rio is me. Author is also Agatha, but Author has yet to go on a killing spree. (Don't worry, there's still time for that.) (Any fellow sapphic West Texans 🤠 ? Let's form our own coven.)

    There I was, Happy As A Clam Chapter Summary Agatha needs a break. She doesn't get one here.

    Chapter Notes See the end of the chapter for notes "I know you can hear me."

    Agatha wasn't aware that was something the kid could do. No one other than Rio had ever managed to connect with her telepathically. It was, as she was starting to expect, very Maximoff of Billy. Her steps faltered of their on volition, damn traitorous things. She did her best to ignore his prodding.

    "Is this how Nicky died?"

    Was this how Nicky died? Was this how her only son died? She wanted to pelt the insolent teen with his own magic. Wanted to watch the life leave his eyes for saying something so controversial to her, telepathic or otherwise.

    "Mama, why do you kill witches?"

    Agatha remembered that day. The petulant and self-righteous rage that grew at such a question. How her fury nearly turned her on her own child! But then she looked at him, and it stilled. She must have been doing a good job keeping her thumb on the other witches if he knew nothing of their cruelties. That, alone, kept her from ranting like a mad woman. Instead, she gave him an honest answer, even if she did keep it vague. He didn't need to know that she had to constantly replenish her magic without a coven. And because she could never bridge that gap with her own kind, because she would never be strong enough, Nicholas Scratch was always doomed to die young.

    The witch reached for her brooch, needing to touch the part of him she always carried with him. Her heart stuttered as her fingertips met cloth. She had lost the only part of him she had left. With the last trial fresh in her mind, Agatha turned and reached for the only other source of comfort. If she could not have a piece of Nicky, then she would give herself unto Death. She could not fight their connection any longer. Could not bear to push the love of her life away.

    Agatha kissed Rio, kissed Death, and bit the magic bullet.

    I couldn't save Nicky, but I can save Billy. So, she gave herself willingly to the Green Witch. If she knew Rio, and she was fairly certain she did, the woman would not reap her. Would not force her to see Nicky until she was ready.

    Agatha had kissed Rio many times. Had kissed fleshy lips and those pearly incisors. She had never kissed to take Death's power, though. Where other magics had given her a heady rush, Rio's magic wrapped around her delicately. Held her the way Rio had all those nights ago. It was as much a part of Death as Agatha was and it welcomed her warmly.

    It was not long before that warmth hit her heart like a bullet. Her body began to lift, pain stretching throughout her nerves like lightning ripping through the bark of a tree. Her chest seized, no sound escaping her as Death, true Death, finally caught up to her. Agatha held on as long as she could, holding Rio's face, wiping away tears and feeling those lush lips. She had regrets, so many regrets. As her soul slipped out of her body, suspended in the air, Agatha regretted the wound she inflicted upon Rio. As Death wept for her, so, too, did her obsidian black heart with its sickly sweet blood.

    But why was she reliving this moment?

    She had turned into a ghost, followed Billy home, and eventually became his mentor. Why, then, was she back in her backyard dying again and again?

    Why wouldn't her beloved Death look at her?

    "...AAAGGGAAATTTHHHAAA..."

    The witch clutched at her chest. Something was moving. She felt it. What the hell was that! What was happening to her?

    She was helpless as the scene reset itself. Billy, staring at her. The last of his trust in her crumbling to nothingness. Rio, dagger in her hand. Poor thing believing their little ruse had worked and she'd get to kill the boy. Agatha fought against the onslaught of voices in her her. All the while, her chest was throbbing. She felt like she was dying, but Rio was nowhere to be found.

    Death had abandoned her.

    Hands gripped her from some unknown source. They pulled at her, her world screeching in agony. Agatha figured it was Mephisto come to claim her tar-black soul. She cried out, lungs burning. It felt like she was being torn apart. Felt like she was burning up from the inside out. And then it stopped.

    Something wet dropped onto her cheek, rousing the witch. Agatha blinked, then gasped for air. Her eyes widened as her pain began anew. She couldn't breath. She couldn't breathe. Shecouldntbreathshecouldntbreatheshecouldntbreatheshecouldnt....

    "What's wrong with her?" she heard Billy shout. The ghost couldn't make his form out, the world a blur.

    "Agatha, listen to me carefully."

    Oh! It was Rio that was holding her. Rio was...crying? The burning in her chest stole her train of thought.

    Thankfully, the Green Witch shook her, bringing her back. "Agatha!" Hands pressed to her face, turning her head forcefully. "The Boy did something to you. You're soul is meant to be in a body. I need you to possess one of the animated decorations until we can get you one." Agatha did her best to glare in Rio's direction. I'd rather die, she telepathically argued. "This isn't a joke," Death growled, but her voice shook with emotion. "If you don't do this, I'll leave and never come back. No second chances."

    Now, that was a fate worse than death. Agatha pushed past the pain and let her soul seek out the closest, meatiest chunk of Billy's magic. She gasped as her pain stopped. Her breathing stopped, too.

    "Where'd she go? Where's Agatha?"

    "Aw, were you worried about me?" she asked the Maximoff. Agatha flexed her toes and heard a clacking. She flexed her fingers and heard the same noise. The witch narrowed her eyes. "Someone get me a mirror. And if I don't like what I see, I'm going to stab you all with those shitty decoration stakes."

    It was Teddy who brought her a mirror and held it up to her. "You're sort of a...skeleton, but you're killing it!"

    "WILLIAM MAXIMOFF!" She tore the mirror from Teddy's grasp and threw it at her wayward pupil. (Sadly, it did not hit him.) "Of all the things to do on All Hallows' Eve, you force me to be an abomination of a corpse and raise hell in this podunk town!" She stormed over to the bane of her existence (move over Wanda) and poked him in the chest. "What happened this time?!"

    Around them, there were scattered bits of decorations. Streamers, Styrofoam, plastic, and candy littered her yard. Jen, for whatever reason, was battling the giant yard skeleton. Why she was having trouble was anyone's guess. The Kaplan's looked confused. And Rio... Rio looked ready to devour her. Death circled her, a grin deeply etched into her face. "I don't know Agatha, I kinda like this new you."

    "Oh, please! Nothing beats the original," she huffed. "Do I at least have my magic back?" The skeletal witch flexed her fingers, swirling them into an old conjuring spell. A tiny ball of purple formed and sizzled out. "Well, that's disappointing. I can't have a damn thing with you Maximoff's around."

    "I'm sorry. What the hell is going on?" Man Kaplan forced his way between the group to stand in front of Billy. "Why are you yelling at my son?"

    Agatha waved him off, turning back to Rio. "So...how long am I stuck like this?" She shrugged, sheathing her knife. "Until we find you a body. At least you're alive again." "Alive," Agatha scoffed. "You turned my body to mulch. My soul was fine a week ago. What the hell did he do to me?" (At least she stayed calm...not!)

    Death cupped her chin, eyes impossibly soft given the current situation. "We will figure this out, amor. But we should get you inside before someone tries to smash you. Flower Guy was swinging a hammer a few minutes ago."

    Well, when Rio was being the voice of reason, Agatha knew the situation had gotten out of control. She nodded. "You wouldn't happen to have a cloak I can use in the meantime, would you? Not that I feel naked or anything, I'm just used to having something flow-y to play with."

    Death laughed, eyes twinkling. "Purple, just for you."

    "Wait, you can't go inside. We need your help out here," Billy argued. He waved his hand at the destruction.

    Ugh! Right... Him. She turned to face the teen, disappointed she didn't have a face to broadcast her annoyance. Agatha steadied herself, her porcelain-fragile limbs swaying with the breeze. "Are there any more monsters to fight?"

    "No."

    "Do you have magic?"

    "Yes."

    Agatha stomped a foot, pointing to her yard. "Then, clean up this mess!" "Who do you-?" Woman Kaplan froze as Agatha rounded on her.

    "I'm your worst nightmare, lady! I'm a cranky Salemite who just wanted to have a bit of fun this Hallows' Eve. I'm someone who, up until ten minutes ago, was a ghost just trying to make sense of things. So, yes! Yes, I'm gonna yell at your kid. He keeps..." Agatha snapped her jaw shut and pressed her fingertips to her nonexistent temples. She tried to take deep breaths, but she had no fucking lungs! "I just need a minute, Billy. I'm a skeleton." Agatha made her tone as soft as she could. "Do you want me to invite your parents and boyfriend inside to explain this to them, or do you want to go home and do it?"

    He looked between the two, clearly torn. "I...I..."

    Mad as she was, she wouldn't torture the boy. "Go home, Billy. Sort your end out while I get my affairs in order. Let's meet up tomorrow or something." Agatha turned away to leave. "Agatha, I'm sorry," he told her, his voice thick with emotion. She could practically hear the tears gathering in his eyes. "I didn't mean to. I swear."

    "Mother, it was an accident. Please, Mother! Please! I can be good."

    Agatha reached for her brooch and froze. It had fused to her sternum. She would have to get used to that. The witch turned her gaze towards him. "It's okay, Billy. It was an accident. They happen. Go home. Get some rest."

    He was openly crying now, the little boy he truly was bleeding through his fleshy facade. Teddy moved to comfort him but Agatha beat him to it. She pulled him in for an awkward hug. She spied his parents staring at her and wished, again, that she could have her facial features back. A glare would force them to give her some space. He was more her son than theirs.

    Rio tapped her shoulder. "The neighbors are coming back," she warned. "You need to get inside."

    Agatha nodded. She ruffled Billy's hair, hoping it conveyed some positive emotion she held for him. He didn't call for her again as Rio ushered her inside. The second the door closed, Agatha collapsed in a heap of bones.

    Death helped her wife to stand, holding her hand tenderly. There was something about seeing the witch in a form similar to hers that sent her obsidian heart into overtime. She'd flirt with her wife, but now clearly wasn't the time. It wasn't long before Jen joined them. "The big one's gone and Billy took Teddy home." She gestured to her wife's newest form. "Are you keeping that one as a pet?"

    Rio blinked before laughing. "This is Agatha."

    The former ghost crossed her arms. "Everyone's dying. That's it. I've made my mind up. I'm going to kill everyone!"

    Death moved to comfort her only for several tugs to hit her at once. "Some bodies just emptied out. Do you want to try and hop into one?"

    Agatha was quiet for a moment. "...I'm stuck."

    Rio felt her mouth fall open. "Stuck? How can you be stuck? This isn't even a real body." Her wife clawed at her rib cage. "I don't know, Rio! I just know I can't get out of this damn thing."

    Agatha was well and truly panicking. Rio reached for her, hands settling on the witch's shoulders. "I'll figure this out. I promise."

    Jen cleared her throat. "So....I missed something big."

    Agatha screamed, and stepped away to tear the house apart.

    "Agatha," she groaned. A throw pillow was thrown in her direction. "I need you to focus. The Boy's magic is the reason for this mess. We need to find out what he was intending when he hit you with his magic."

    "I'm allowed to be upset," her wife growled. "I. Am. A. Skeleton!"

    "And you're beautiful, sweetheart. Now, get it together."

    Rio shared a look with Jen. "I would love to stay, but I have to go handle a building fire. I'll be back as fast as I can. Don't let her jump from anything."

    Agatha rushed over to her, her phalanges curling around her arms. "Wait, don't leave! How am I supposed to calm down when I can't even breathe?"

    She pressed a kiss to the witch's frontal lobe. "If I could stay longer, you know I would." Death summoned up the cloak she promised Agatha. She pulled it around her beautiful, skeletonized wife, letting the purple surround her ivory bones. "Te veo." She slipped away into the Ether to more easily transport herself to the scene of a major tragedy. When would mortals learn to blow a candle out before going to bed?

    Agatha lay on her bed, Jen sitting at the foot. She hugged Rio's cloak around her, trying and failing to keep from crying. At least there were no visible tears.

    "Billy said he told his parents," the pink witch informed gently. "They'll be here tomorrow to discuss everything." She looked over at her, brows crinkled in worry. "Did you always know who he was?"

    The skeletal witch moved to sigh and felt panic grip her at the lack of exhale. She tried to shut her eyes to block out the feeling, but that was just as impossible without eyelids. Agatha pressed her palms to her orbitals with a sob. "I'm gonna go crazy. Where the hell is Rio!" "Harkness!" Jen shuffled until she was kneeling at her feet. "Pull it together. You've been through worse."

    "If you've got a way to get me out of this damn thing, I'm all ears. Eugh!" Agatha kicked her feet feebly. Before she could throw another tantrum (because that's exactly what she was doing), pink magic shook her like a rag doll.

    "Get up," Jen ordered.

    "Wha-?" Agatha was pulled to her feet.

    "You and I are gonna have that talk now if you need a distraction from your second chance at life so bad."

    Oof. I've really worked us both up, haven't I? Agatha moved to flip her hair and nearly dissolved into another meltdown.

    Jen grasped the sides of her skull. "Billy. Did you know who he was the whole time?" "More or less," she grumbled. "I spent enough time with him and Wanda to see the signs before we got on the Road."

    "Why didn't you say anything?"

    Why hadn't she said something? Agatha reasoned it was due to curiosity. But now...Maybe a part of her had sensed his true lineage. Maybe that was why, for that little bit, she believed he could have been Nicky reincarnated. "I wasn't sure if he was or wasn't Wanda's son." Jen released her from her hold. "So, you didn't have any intention of taking his power?" Agatha habitually rolled her non-existent eyes. "I tried that once with the Scarlet Witch. It left me powerless and bewitched. No, I was never going to steal his life." She gripped at Rio's cloak and looked down at her toes. "I think I should have gone with Billy. He's alone right now, and his parents are only going to make things worse for him."

    Jen quirked a brow. "Well, what are you going to do about that?"

    The witch pressed a finger to her teeth. "We're gonna kidnap him."

    Death eased her last soul into their designated afterlife realm before warping back to Westview. The yard was clean and righted as if nothing had occurred, she sensed the air, four hours prior. Rio entered Agatha's house to find it quiet and empty. Her alarm bells began to ring in the back of her mind, but she could still feel her connection with Agatha. Wherever her wayward witch had gone, she was still safe. Rio reached out and let herself be pulled towards her wife.

    A part of her shouldn't be surprised to find Jen and a skeleton on the roof of The Boy's Eastview home, but she was a bit. Either something had happened, or Agatha was that worried about The Boy. She slipped into the teen's room before the others could. Instead of sleeping peacefully as he had been known to do in the past, The Boy had his nose buried deep into a spell book.

    "Planning on running away?" she asked him. A part of her itched to pull her dagger and end him before he could mess anything else up. She spared him only for the sake of getting Agatha a new body.

    The Boy lifted his head, eyes bright red. "I have to get back to her. She's probably freaking out because of me."

    Oh, the two were so much alike it pained her. "I wouldn't worry about that." She snapped her fingers, opening the window with a gust of wind. Vines hoisted the two scrambling witches before shoving them into the room. "Your mentor beat you to it."

    "Billy," Agatha breathed. She rushed to hold The Boy as if her life depended on it. Maybe it did.

    Rio waited patiently for her wife to notice her, which wasn't long. Agatha tugged Death over to give them both a hug. Now that she was close enough to touch the skeletal witch, she could hear just how confused and panicked the woman still was. Her soul buzzed around violently, her thoughts a swirling mass.

    "Why didn't you wait for me at home?" she asked her cloaked love. "What if you had been seen?" What if you had been hurt?

    Agatha turned to look at her, skull a blank canvas but her irritation palpable. "Someone needed to check on Billy."

    "Jen would have been completely capable on her own."

    "Jen isn't his mo-mentor," Agatha hissed. She released The Boy, putting distance between herself and him.

    Death clenched her jaw. Why don't you just tell him, she sent her wife. This charade has gone on long enough. She reached for Agatha, hands itching to pet and soothe. He's not ready.

    Are you worried about him, or yourself?

    "Are you two fighting again?" The Boy asked. He reached out and took Rio's hand, shocking the couple. "Help me help her. Please, Rio. What do I do?"

    She wanted to shake his grip off of her. She wanted to cut the offending appnding off. She wanted to throw him through more glass to watch his scarlet blood stain the ground below. "I need to know what exactly you were feeling and thinking when you entered our minds." Jen pushed Rio away from The Boy. "Why do you have so much stuff from the Road in your room?"

    Death seethed. Why were all of these mortals so disrespectful? She grabbed Jen and forced her to sit on the bed. "Later." Then, she guided Agatha to sit next to the pink-clad witch. "Behave," she told her wife.

    Agatha sunk in on herself, worrying the cosmic entity.

    "Now, focus, Boy."

    He glared at her. "Can you just use my name? Or go back to 'Teen'. Anything but 'Boy'." She sneered. "My wife is stuck in this body, TTTEEEEEENNN. And if you don't tell me what emotionally charged your magic, she could be stuck like that forever." This was serious. Deathly so.

    The Boy looked at her, eyes wide. (Maybe he finally understood the stakes.) "You guys are married?"

    Rio felt her patience snap like the smallest, saddest, driest, most brittle twig in a dead forest. "That's it!" She flicked her wrist, The Boy tensing.

    "Rio, don't," Agatha said. She lurched forward to stop the Green Witch. Death had her love and Jen wrapped up nice and tight in a bundle of vines. "This is to save you," she told Agatha. She pressed a kiss to the witch's maxillary arch. "I'll be gentle-ish." "No," her wife whimpered. "Let me go with you."

    Rio brought her palms together and pushed them out towards The Boy. With a gust of her green magic, she entered The Boy's mind. His body slumped to the ground, his head hitting a pillow Jen had managed to kick to the floor. Death threw The Boy into one of her memories, anything to keep him occupied while she did what needed to be done.

    Agatha squirmed against her bindings. "Damnit," she hissed.

    "What's she doing?" Jen wiggled until she could nudge Billy's left arm. "Come on. Wake up." "Stop!" The witch head-butted the other witch to get her attention. "You can't mess with him while she's in his head. It could hurt him."

    "So, we just leave him?"

    "We don't have much of a choice. All we can do is make sure his body stays safe until she's done, or her kicks her out." She looked down at her son, worry resting heavily on her shoulders.

    Billy cursed Rio's name as he fell into a memory. He stopped as he came face to face with Agatha. His mentor looked gaunt, her eyes sunken in. His body was compelled to crouch and extend a hand towards the witch. Agatha smacked it away with a growl. Even with her sickly appearance, the fire in her eyes had yet to go out. The part of him that was Rio was relieved to see some emotion behind those eyes.

    "I hate you," Agatha growled. Her body shook as a chilly breeze pushed at her. "I hate you!" "I had to do my job, Agatha." Billy felt a burning over his heart. Like he'd been cut by a jagged blade in the center of his chest.

    His mentor lashed out, purple throwing him into a wall. He stood, unfazed and uninjured. Agatha didn't let up. More and more balls of her magic was sent in his direction. He blocked what he could, the thrumming of Rio's magic calm in his palm. It felt nothing like the vibrating magic he wielded. This made him feel invincible. It was likely why Rio didn't seem too fazed with Agatha's outburst.

    "I'll never forgive you. Not for as long as I live," the witch vowed, spit flying. She stumbled, her body too weak to keep up with her onslaught. Agatha panted, sweat dripping from her face.

    Billy walked forward, offering only kindness to the distraught woman. It was all Rio had left to offer her. "If you don't eat something, you will die," Rio warned. She gestured towards a tree, fruit growing and dropping around her tired wife. "Unless that's what you're hoping for." Agatha spit at her, the glob of saliva hitting Death on the cheek. "As if I'd ever go with you." She struggled to stand but didn't let it stop her. Agatha jabbed a finger in Billy's chest. "You will never have me. Never."

    "Then you should really eat," Rio reminded, her emotions threatening to swallow her. Billy could feel tears on his face, but found none when he touched his cheek. Must be crying in real life, he reasoned.

    Agatha kicked an apple away from her. "If I eat, it will be by my own hands. Not yours. I want nothing to do with you, do you understand me? Nothing!"

    Rio shrunk back, tears gathering in her eyes. "Agatha..."

    "Leave!"

    It was the only time Death fled, and she made sure to fly as far as she could from the pure hatred in her former lover's eyes.

    Billy focused on trying to reach Agatha on the outside. Instead, he succeeded in moving into a different memory. The teen looked around to find Agatha lounging on a chaise lounge. The witch looked up at him, the same look in her eyes. When he gazed into the mirror behind Agatha, he found Death in shambles. Gone was the baby-faced Green Witch. Now, Death stood sharp and poised. She cloaked herself in deep shades of greens and browns, not yet in her modern black attire. She was close, though. Billy could feel the guilt and self-hatred gnawing at her mind, at her body. Rio was self-destructing slowly. Agatha, on the other hand, was spiraling head first into dark magic.

    "I didn't take you for a cruise kind of gal," the witch joked, but her tone held an edge Billy had grown accustomed to while on the Road.

    Rio categorized it as a sign that Agatha was pleasantly surprised to see her. "There are quite a number of witches on this ship," Death noted. "But drowning your victims isn't your usual forte." She moved to sit on a chaise to the right of her ex. Billy caught a glimpse of her form shifting to match that of a woman in the early 1910s. He started to recognize the decor James Cameron had worked so diligently to recreate with his film.

    "No, sweet thing," Agatha hummed. Her eyes raked over Billy in a way that felt very much not-romantic. She was sizing him up for a battle. Rio was on edge. "Tomorrow's our anniversary. Thought I'd give you a vacation. Work and play, hm?"

    There was a sickly sweet twist in Billy's gut. Like hope and disappointment all rolled into one. He wasn't surprised when Rio lay back, a smile playing on her lips. "You remembered?" "How could I forget?" His mentor's face softened as a small piece of young Agatha poked through. He found himself chasing after that crumb and felt disgusted with himself. It was clearly Rio wanting things to return to normal. But she, as he had felt, didn't believe she deserved to see that side of her anymore. Billy focused hard again, thinking of a time Agatha's face had been bright and cheery. If he was going to be stuck here, he might as well look at the few positive memories she had of people.

    Billy felt the world shift violently, jerking and jostling him as he found himself in a memory that looked too good to be true. There, on a crate, a small boy was singing the Ballad of the Witches' Road. He had no doubt in his mind who he'd stumbled upon. Nicholas Scratch, Billy realized, looked so much like Rio.

    He felt a blinding tug as Nicky coughed into a white handkerchief. From his spot in the crowd, he could see flecks of blood. Billy swallowed thickly as his stomach dropped. "He was sick...I couldn't save him," he recalled Agatha saying.

    Billy shook his head. "No, no. I don't want to see this." He didn't want to see a child die. Not if he could help it.

    The tavern glitched into a new one, Nicky only slightly older. The tugging in Rio's chest was becoming unbearable for Billy. He curled in on himself, a groan spilling from his lips. "Don't make me," he whimpered. "I don't want to..."

    "Nicky," Rio said, time freezing briefly once his performance had ended. "I need you to come home. I..." She clutched at her chest with a gasp.

    Billy mirrored her actions, his heart beating wildly with the pain.

    Nicky stared at them in horror. He bobbed his head quickly. "I'll come home, Mother. Just tell me when."

    Rio convulsed, unable to answer him as time continued. Billy screamed as too many emotions ripped through him, fueling the pain Nicky's extended time had inflicted. He barely heard the child tell Agatha he was needed home before the boy slipped away. Death clawed at a nearby wall as she forced herself to stand. She needed to hold out until Agatha was asleep. She couldn't, wouldn't, make his passing a frightening experience. Not if she had any say. Billy was jerked into the forest, the memory pulling him along. His knees buckled, but Rio continued to walk towards a bridge bathed in green. He recognized it from the Ether Portal and felt Rio's anguish pull him under. Death did not fold to her emotions, though. She woke her son from afar, not trusting Agatha to remain asleep tonight. Not after the scare at the tavern.

    Nicky tried to rush towards her, free from his pain. His body remaining in Agatha's arm. So pure, so innocent. So cold.

    Billy felt Rio chastise him for his impatience. She pointed at Agatha, a smile playing on her lips. He gulped for air as Nicky pressed two kisses to Agatha's cheeks. He felt betrayed for his mentor, felt guilty for Rio, felt happy for Nicky. It was tearing him apart. He gripped his head, screaming.

    Chapter End Notes Why don't you want me? :( Absolutely obsessed with the new bts footage Marvel released. I miss our girlies (Joe included).

    Heartbreak, Grief, Sorrow Chapter Summary Rio goes searching for a way to save her wife.

    Chapter Notes See the end of the chapter for notes Rio slipped into The Boy's memories with a sniff. His mind was a never ending room of white with two paths branching off from where she stood. The path to her prize lay on either the red road or the blue road. Death turned towards the path that crackled with trauma. Blue magic that was clearly The Boy's, not William's, enticed her forward. She waved the unnecessary memories away and pushed forward. Unlike The Boy, she did not enter his perceptive state. Death would not have to feel whatever he felt in the moment. (She already felt enough as it was, thank you very much!)

    The first memory she poked her head into was the day Not-William was cleared to leave the hospital. Rio pulled back and moved further down the gallery-like room before repeating the gesture. She found The Boy sketching his sigil over and over and over again. (Why that never raised any flags with his parents, she couldn't tell you.) Unsatisfied, Rio removed herself and strolled for much longer. She picked another one at random and found an interesting moment for The Boy. Death fully entered the scene, the path vanishing.

    The coven, the old one when she had yet to claim half of them, stood, facing Agatha. She wore a painfully bland house-wife outfit that, unfortunately for Rio, looked rather good on her. Death lamented not getting to harass her wife in the first trial, but moved on to what was actually taking place. Her wife looked like she was being chastised for something, which wasn't new.

    "You can't cheat, Agatha!"

    Ah, so she had known The Boy wasn't Nicky from the get-go. That was interesting. The surprise didn't end there. Billy ordered her to drink. It had her wife looking at him in confused silence. A dark look overtook him as he stepped forward. He announced he would drink if she wouldn't. Agatha was quick to react, her hand moving to stop the others from passing the wine glass. Rio sped the memory along, much like fast forwarding a movie to a specific frame. She stopped once she saw Agatha's eyes widen in silent horror. Death followed The Boy's line of sight as her wife moved to an empty space on the floor and crouched. The poison, she realized, had reached the hallucinations portion. She was intrigued to see how her wife would react, and to what.

    Agatha shrank back, a sound of pure pain echoing in the kitchen. Whatever she was imagining upset her enough to have her scrambling away to safety.

    Rio rushed forward on instinct. She tried to console her wife, tell her it wasn't real, but this was just a memory. Death's hands could not hold her. Could not wipe away the tears tat threatened to fall. Her brave witch, her beloved, stood and quickly composed herself. The Boy questioned what she saw, but Agatha brushed him and the coven's stares aside. Rio saw the interest that flickered across the teen's face despite Agatha's closed off response. The Boy had always seemed curious of her wife, but this was the moment he was ensnared by the mystery. Agatha had been placed at the forefront of his mind now. His eyes tracking her closely. Much like his mother, he was an observant little thing. Unfortunately, it did not help Death figure out what he had done to Agatha. Rio waved her hand and sped up the journey.

    She stopped his memories as The Boy and Agatha shared a small conversation on the Road. It was rather telling despite how short it was.

    "Agatha...What really happened to your son?"

    "So nosy," Death tutted. Rio watched as the first genuine smile her wife had worn slipped away at the question. (No wonder Agatha had been in a foul mood when she'd joined her at the campfire.) Just as she'd expected, Agatha abandoned The Boy in search of solitude. The teen watched her leave, always curious. He was chomping at the bit more aggressively now. Agatha was trying to put distance between them, physically and figuratively, but he was whittling her down. Rio could see it in the way she hesitated to condemn The Boy's actions. She knew his identity, but she never once faulted him for it. Interesting... The Boy, on the other hand, clearly looked up to her. It would be hard not to. Agatha was such a flashy, confident woman that charmed the few who didn't know those were bright warning signs. Rio knew that was subject to change with his upcoming memories, but it was still a spectacle to witness. The adoration and reverence he held despite his irritation with her. It reminded Death of Agatha. Truly, this was one of her offspring. Rio would adore him if he didn't put his filthy fingers all over her Sacred Balance and Natural Order. She moved the scene along.

    Death stopped, as she was always going to, in The Boy's memory of Agatha's Trial. His reaction to Alice's death chaffed her. Made her condemn him as swiftly as he condemned Agatha. She wanted to know why he had reacted so strongly. Why did he believe her to be a villain now?

    Alice was dead, lying on the floor. Agatha stood frozen in place, her peace shattered as she took in her actions. From The Boy's perspective, Agatha looked exactly the same. Tears gathered in the witch's eyes, her mouth opening and closing in apparent shock. There was nothing different that would have suggested he saw something Rio hadn't. No secret smile that would have made anyone think she did it purposefully. For the Ancient Ones' sake, did he not pay attention to how awful Agatha's mother was? Clearly, it was a premeditated move. Evanora had used Agatha's one weakness to turn the others on her own daughter and The Boy had fallen for it hook, line, and sinker. It made Death seethe anew.

    Now that her work couldn't interfere, she followed The Boy as he chased after Agatha. He yapped at her heels, blind to the distress clear on her face. The tears that rimmed her eyes. The way she cowered as he approached. Her wife was hurt, and he didn't care. He accused, harsh and unbending. Rio shook as he forced Agatha to put a wall between the two. Pushed her back into the box her mother had fashioned for her. Death laughed when her wife mocked The Boy, the woman's patience gone in an instant.

    "You're so much like your mother," Agatha had told him, malice barely contained. Death preened. She knew she loved her wife for a reason. Her celebration was short lived as The Boy, now a confirmed Maximoff, forced the remaining coven members off the Road. She reached for Agatha, watching helplessly as she sank into the mud. Rio would kill him. She knew Agatha would emerge, so she followed The Boy as he stormed off to sit and think. "I know I like to give her grief, but it always comes from a place of love," she told Memory Boy. "I'll be sure to send lots of dangerous people your way in the future. Just a little payback for your little stunt back there." She took practice swings at his head with her dagger, lamenting the lack of impact.

    The Boy remained silent as he finished blowing off steam. Angstily, he crushed his sigil to pieces. (At least he had been listening to Agatha's mini-lesson.) Rio wasn't very amused. She didn't even care. She just wanted to see how the two had managed to move forward without killing each other. She couldn't help but wonder why Agatha still let The Boy draw breath. Anyone else would have been halfway into the afterlife by now.

    Her wife reappeared, muddied and frustrated. She was quick to mock the Maximoff, all walls and masks deployed to hide the betrayal she felt. It wasn't until she admitted to missing The Boy that Rio tuned back in. Those tears from earlier were in Agatha's eyes again. But, this time, they were due to fondness, not a lack of forgiveness. Death wanted to brush them away, press kisses to those tired eyelids. If only she hadn't been busy with Alice. The Boy was constantly hurting the witch now. Their relationship strained and stretched to a single thread. "But know this: I don't trust you!"

    Rio considered manipulating time to drop a tree on him. It wouldn't kill him, but it would hurt like hell. Just a little something so he could get a taste of his own medicine. His words had clearly cut through Agatha's armor. Now, the battered witch wrapped herself up even more tightly. There was a tightness to her movements. A caution reserved for her more capable enemies. The Boy didn't consider her a threat. Didn't even stop to consider all the things that had led up to Agatha's fall from grace. (In his eyes, at least.) The Boy threw insult after insult at Agatha, unrelenting and unforgiving. He wasn't mourning Alice anymore, he was mourning the version of his would-be mentor he had created prior to their journey. He felt betrayed, so he lashed out. Very Harkness of the Maximoff.

    Death didn't care to see Lilia again. The woman had done nothing but point at her and cry through the various points of her wispy life.

    She didn't stop speeding through until the final trial. Agatha was acting out a bit, which was odd. Death narrowed her eyes. She knew, more or less, what all Agatha had gotten up to when she wasn't nearby. Death didn't know the specifics of her conversations, only that she had them. So, now that her wife was in the midst of a performance, Rio realized Agatha's bleeding heart journey had started the moment Billy appeared in her house. It had snowballed to the point that Agatha had grown to care for all her coven members, not just The Boy. He had to have noticed, if only on a subconscious level, that Agatha was not being her true self in serious moments. That all her grand talk of being wicked were spurious. (His outburst had been about her coping mechanisms, after all.) But this wasn't Agatha masking pain. This was Agatha being kind while keeping her cards close to her chest.

    Agatha successfully tricked Jen and The Boy into believing she had bound Jen. She had taken a risk, as she would momentarily with Death, and executed a flawless deception. Jen was quickly unbound and vanished. Now, it was just the Body Snatcher and her wife. Death waited for the inevitable betrayal, but no pain stabbed her heart. Agatha was doing what she did best: fighting to save her child. As the Maximoff secured another body with her help, he popped away to his bedroom in Eastview.

    Death could tell he was disoriented as he rushed to help Agatha battle her. It didn't make sense their first go around, but Rio could see that her sacrifice had triggered the restrengthening of their familial bond (even if it was surrogate on his end). She had saved the others with the possibility of not making it out herself. It was the thought of her dying alone that seemed to spur The Boy into action. His magic sensed his needs, and blasted him into the sky. Death followed silently. Once The Boy neared Agatha's backyard, however, Death entered his perspective. She needed to understand why Agatha felt like dying for The Boy. (Sure, she could ask the witch, but Agatha rarely gave straight answers. In fact, Rio doubted Agatha understood herself.)

    The first emotion to hit her was a tight, gripping panic. The Boy was worried for Agatha as she was dragged and choked against the trellis. Next, a wave of anger filled him. His magic reacted accordingly, helping him to throw Death away from the bound witch. Relief quickly joined the swirling mass of emotions now that Agatha had enough time to breathe. Then, Rio got to experience Agatha's succubus powers first hand.

    The kiss, when it had taken place, had been all Death could focus on. She didn't feel her power leaving her until Agatha's soul became a white hot brand in her chest. Death had tried, and failed, to heal Agatha before her power could kill her. Had practically pushed their souls together in hopes the witch would remain standing when they broke apart. A chill had replaced the burning once her wife ceased to draw breath. Once her heart stilled in her chest. Once Rio's magic had poisoned her life force.

    This was not the same.

    Rio felt The Boy's magic rip and tear away from his cells as it was sucked towards Agatha. She bent at the waist as the warlock's remaining strength gave way to the all-consuming blackhole. Death finally understood the sensation of dying. It didn't tickle like pain. It crushed you. Pushed you towards Death's waiting arms like a gust of wind catching in a sail. She found herself pulling away from the sensation, as all mortals did. It perplexed and intrigued her. All the while, her wife was regenerating in all her majesty. Her cuts healed. (Something Rio had looked forward to doing with a million tiny kisses.) The Boy dropped to a knee as he reached his end. By this point, Rio would have been compelled to reap him, but Agatha cut the connection.

    She turned to find herself stalking towards herself. (Death made a note to wear her shroud as a shawl more often. She liked the way it accented her shoulders and crown like a fur scarf of old.) The quip could have been better as she listened to herself offer up her ultimatum. The Boy felt a surge of anger, but was too weak to do anything about it. Death didn't really care. She was enjoying watching herself and her wife flirt. Their plan to get The Boy to give himself up not yet derailed.

    The Maximoff was flung, Rio experiencing her own magic for the first time. The Boy took a moment to right his world before his worry began to overwhelm him. At least he was aware that no one could ever beat Death, not even Agatha. It wasn't until Rio had send a particularly harmful blast into Agatha's abdomen that pure rage blinded the teen's senses. Any ill will he'd held for Agatha vanished momentarily as he attacked Rio, throwing her through the back porch doors. She moved with him as he crouched to tend to Agatha, all familial piety and concern.

    "It should be me," Agatha reasoned, authentic and sincere. It floored Rio that she was being honest. The moment was made worse when Agatha tilted his chin upwards, urging him silently to 'be a big boy' and accept the situation. Emotion tugged at Agatha's face as she declared, "You're not bad." Rio knew there was a 'like me' that was missing from that sentence. Betrayed and beaten down by The Boy's harshness, but Agatha still cared for him. Still loved him like a son.

    His grief consumed him as he told her she wasn't bad either. He fought the urge to pull her into a hug. To protect her from Death as if she were some fragile old woman. Death relented. The Boy had his moments of endearment.

    "You're the only one who thinks so."

    Agatha may have been speaking to The Boy, but it was clear a part of her, the pain addled part, was speaking to Nicky, too. Rio vowed to never attack her wife in such a way again. She didn't want to ever hear or see such a thing ever again. Didn't want Agatha to feel that way anymore. Death realized that this was how The Boy was feeling too. Regardless of who exactly she was speaking to, it was the push the Maximoff needed to convince himself he deserved to die. They went through the motions of him giving himself up, heart on his sleeve just like both of his mothers. He bravely stared Death down as she approached them. And then betrayal overtook him as Agatha agreed with his sentiment. She felt The Boy's heart break into a million pieces. Whatever pedestal he'd placed her own tumbled down a near infinite amount of steps until his respect for her was reduced to dust. Rio nearly pitied him. Nearly. She let his shock wash over her, reveled in the haze his mind had to sift through as he processed her betrayal. As the memory of herself stared him down hungrily, dagger mocking him, The Boy swallowed back a sob. (Again, the shroud looked amazing as a shawl.)

    But Rio, as the Maximoff, noted the tear in the corner of Agatha's eye as she left his side. Abandoned him to face Death alone. The decision was not made lightly. The hurt was felt on both sides. Only Rio had the benefit of enjoying the emotional distress because she had yet to realize the depth of their bond. Watching the scene unfold now, she realized Agatha was never going to be able to give The Boy up. Her attachment had grown too strong. But then The Boy went and invoked the name of Nicholas Scratch and she was back to cursing his existence.

    Like a coward, he'd done it telepathically. He must have known Rio would have skinned him alive for posing such a question. Agatha must have too, but her distress was what propelled herself towards Death. All the while, The Boy watched in confusion, then concern, then dread. He had foolishly believed Agatha would fight to save him, not that she would hand her life over for the sake of his. Guilt hung heavy over his head as he watched his mentor kill herself. Rio was forced to watch her own face suspended in grief and disbelief as Agatha fell to the ground with a soundless cry. (Death had heard it, though. Was haunted by the gasp of her wife's soul.)

    The Boy picked up Agatha's brooch while Memory Rio had been distracted. Why he felt sentimental now, Rio didn't quite understand. He flip-flopped between his emotions just as quickly as Agatha did. (Much as she loved her wife, the woman shouldn't have any more kids.) He left when Memory Her sent him away, his eyes drifting back to Agatha's burial. The grief he felt stayed with him as he returned home. Burned hotter and hotter as he made up some ridiculous lie to his body's parents.

    She sped through his 'crying in the shower' sequence only to find her ghostly wife there to spook The Boy. For someone who had just died, she was in good spirits. She even resolved him of his guilt. (Death would be sure to tease Agatha endlessly for her soft spot now. She didn't even let The Boy reflect on his wrong-doings. Very sappy of her.) The Maximoff spiraled, not for the first time, from guilt to outrage. Rio was surprised to find him returning to Agatha's house hours after murdering her. (Because that's exactly what he did.) Her shock gave way to her own outrage as he began an attempt to banish Agatha. (She really ought to stop being surprised by The Boy. Every single decision he made so far always ended up hurting her wife.) He grew frustrated as she refused to disappear. Felt irritated that Agatha continued to seek him out because of a silly brooch. (She couldn't wait for The Boy to die. Seriously.)

    She already knew how the rest played out once the banishment failed. Agatha's flickering soul had alerted Death from halfway across the globe. Rio had followed them as they returned to Eastview with their new alliance. Death decided not to snoop unnecessarily any more. Her wife was still trapped in an animated Halloween decoration. If his magic decided to no longer feed into the plastic skeleton, Agatha would die again. There was no telling what would happen if she did. Her soul was no longer that of a mortal's.

    Rio skipped to the day Agatha had nearly turned into a vengeful spirit. It started off exceedingly quiet. It wasn't due to her wife being pensive, but afraid. Small and tucked away in the corner of the room. Her avoidance triggered concern in The Boy and Rio. He then tried many things to get her attention, one of which was to repeatedly say Rio's name. Death had to agree with The Boy. Agatha wasn't in a good place, and leaving her alone was out of the question.

    At the school, a place of absolute misery, Agatha disappeared into the crowd. What The Boy hadn't noticed was the way her eyes followed the shorter, younger mortals. The way she reached for them like they were the ghosts haunting her life. Unfortunately, Rio had no way of knowing what had triggered her depression. Dreams and small moments of awareness did not hold the way meaningful moments did. Something had occurred in the night to beat her beloved witch down.

    Death ignored the bubbling affection The Boy felt when Teddy appeared. She simply sped things along. The Boy suggested Agatha prank a bully, something that was bound to cheer her up. Then, she heard what The Boy had not.

    The lyrics to the musical had poked the exposed, sensitive nerve the night's events had uncovered. It forced her wife to snap, scaring the Maximoff and his boyfriend as lights exploded. Agatha vanished with a wail only Death could hear. With her new lead, Rio chased down the memory she needed. She ignored the pity The Boy sent her way. Ignored how he sized her up as nothing more than a sad, overly protective lover. (She'd show him what all she could do once she saved her wife.)

    Finally, they were in the basement. Agatha towering over him. The Boy's heart ached for her. Like a child who didn't want to see their mother cry, The Boy only wanted to help. (In that, he had been honest and true.) His main intention, the need to reach through her grief to console her, propelled his magic to awaken. His desire to hold her, truly hold her, freed his magic. Unfortunately, he was too focused on the memories he was hearing, so his magic adapted. It sent him tumbling into their minds and began the process of reversing Agatha's death.

    Rio waved her hand, returning to the road of The Boy's memories. She didn't feel like having to sit there and re-watch her early days.

    She sniffed around for his magic and entered a shimmering pool that looked promising. Death hummed in approval as she found Agatha mocking the offense that had blacklisted her in her own coven. She slipped back into the teen's perspective to find a raging sea of frustration and a clawing sadness. His irritation had magic swirling around him like a whirlpool. (Had Agatha not followed him, she might have been safe.) The Boy moved to stand before Agatha's burial mound, guilt clouding his rage-addled mind. It spun and burned around him, cloaked him like a shroud of smoke. All Death could feel was regret, regret, regret.

    His own mind seemed to be playing tricks on him. Agatha's corpse was still lying in the flowers. Her flesh slowly turning gray and rotting to a horrid paste Death's bouquet happily fed on. The corpse cackled at him as his mentor appeared behind him. His magic cooled in her presence. Rio felt herself be turned to face the ghost, but the nightmarish corpse had taken her place. He did his best to push the image away as he questioned Agatha. Death groaned, shaking her head as Agatha lay in the same place as the hallucination. He continued to ignore the corpse as he addressed the witch. The regret rose and shrunk like a wave, never sure when exactly it should crest and crash against the banks of his sanity. They began to argue back and forth, Agatha just as agitated with his responses. With each defensive answer he received, the more the corpse turned into a younger and younger Agatha. The memories he had seen come to life. A woman Agatha tried desperately to kill with a reputation as dark as the night. But The Boy had seen it, and he desperately wanted her to be that person again. The one who tried to show others she wasn't a heartless monster. The one that had simply wanted to be a mother. The pieces began to slide into place. "What does my reputation have to do with you?"

    Agatha had posed a question the teen didn't want to face. He was just as avoidant as his mother. He was just as cruel as his mother, too. The Boy lashed out in response, a basic power surge pushing her away from him. He didn't want her to look at him with those wounded eyes. Those concerned pools of blue. The look a mother should reserve for her child when she wants to comfort them. Rio felt it. The Boy didn't believe he deserved such a kindness from Agatha. He was well aware he'd hurt her with his words. Like Agatha, it had made him feel better if the other person pulled away from his sharp words. But Agatha was giving as good as she got.

    "I'm not gonna sugar coat it for you, Billy. I do bad things, so I deserve to have bad things said about me. I'm evil and-"

    Death doubled over as The Boy's anger finally reached its boiling point. He wanted her to stop saying that. He wanted her to forgive herself the way he'd forgiven her. He wanted to shake her. He wanted to her to hold him. He wanted...He wanted...

    Rio felt his scream tear from her throat as his magic reacted to his powerful wish. It burned white hot through her veins as it gathered and leapt from her fingers towards Agatha. She tore herself from his mind, the world spinning violently as she landed in a heap on his bedroom floor.

    Agatha kicked Rio's vines before moving to free Jen. Billy twitched and whimpered on the floor, his brow furrowing. Whatever Rio was doing was hurting him, and she was going to give Death a piece of her mind in return. Once freed, Jen crouched next to him. She pressed a hand to his forehead with a hiss.

    "He's burning up. Are you sure we can't do anything?"

    "All you do is ask me questions," Agatha growled. "Can't you think for yourself every now and then?"

    The witch shot her a look. "I didn't ask to get tied up in yours and Rio's crazy antics. All you two do is leave collateral damage in your wake."

    "Oh. Very good," the skeletal witch spat. "You're finally biting back. About fricken time." She crossed her arms with a clack. "We still have to wait for one of them to-" She was cut off as Billy began to tremble more violently. Agatha dropped to her knees, hands moving to brush curls from his face. He thrashed, trying to move away from their touch. "Please," he whimpered. "Please. I don't want to see this." Tears leaked out of his eyes as his breathing began to pick up.

    "Dammit, Rio. What are you doing?" Agatha did her best to soothe her son. If she had more magic, she'd slip in and pull Rio out. Unfortunately, she didn't have enough, and she wouldn't risk hurting him further.

    The teen began to shout in earnest, his voice turning hoarse. He looked like fish flopping for air as he gasped and screamed.

    Jen and Agatha panicked, trying to hold him still to avoid waking his parents. They failed terribly as his feet kicked the floor.

    "Billy? Billy!" The door handle jiggled before pounding ensued. Man Kaplan was just as concerned as they were, it seemed. "Billy, open the door!"

    "What do we do?" Jen wiped at tears on her own face. (Billy's cries were really tugging at everyone's heart strings.)

    Before she could answer, three things happened in rapid succession.

    The Kaplan's broke the door down.

    Rio was ejected in a very ungraceful manner. She landed at Woman Kaplan's feet with wide eyes.

    Billy sat up, clutching his head. He repeatedly shouted, "I didn't want to. I didn't want to. Please, Agatha! I'm sorry. I'm sorry."

    The entire group, save for the traumatized boy, stared at one another in shock. "Surprise," Agatha told Billy's parents weakly. "If you could just give me a second." She moved over to Rio and grabbed her shoulders. Agatha shook her wife, hoping to convey all the emotions she was feeling. "What the hell did you do to Billy!?"

    Death shrugged. "I dunno. I gave him a memory to play with, but he didn't stay put. Whatever he saw is on him." She easily slipped out of her wife's grasp, eyeing the boy writhing on the ground. She tutted. "Might wanna knock that one out. He went a little too deep from the looks of things."

    "That's all you have to say," Agatha growled. "You broke him!"

    Rio leaned in close, deathly serious. "I did what I had to do. If I hadn't, I wouldn't have found a way to save you. Or did you want to stay in that sad excuse of a body?" Agatha shrunk back. "You like it," she reasoned weakly. It was a pale imitation of her usual quips.

    Death laughed. "See, it's all making sense now. I'll be back. I need to gather a few things before we can finish the spell he put on you."

    "What spell is that?" she dared to ask. Oh...I'm totally going to die. Rio stroked the side of her skull, eyes softening. "The spell that brings you back to me, body and soul."

    "So...my soul is trapped in a faulty spell." She nodded her head, trying not to cry. "I'm gonna die."

    "No, amor. He gave you a second chance at life. He just didn't think to give you a body." She rolled her eyes. "Your lessons need work shopping. If you'd trained him right, we could be in bed right now."

    "I don't understand," Agatha told her. She leaned in close, staring up into Rio's eyes. "How did he give me a second chance? I thought only you could do that."

    Death looked around the room before tapping the side of her head. "Later. Te veo." The witch shook her head as Rio left her to clean up her mess. Perhaps Rio knew something she didn't, but she highly doubted it. "Alrighty then! Jen, get downstairs and brew me an antidote for a near-death experience. Billy's gonna need all the help he can get to recover. Woman Kaplan, Man Kaplan, I'd love to chat, but I need to get the kid back in good shape first. From the looks of things, he's stuck in a nasty nightmare. We'll treat it like the flu, and keep you living blobs away."

    "That's my son," Woman Kaplan argued. "I'm not going to leave him with a total stranger!" "Lady, I've been free-loading in your house since the day I died. I know this place like the back of my hand. Now, go downstairs and help Jen find the sous vide."

    Woman Kaplan took hold of her wrist, only slightly flinching at the feeling. "I'm not leaving Billy."

    Agatha tried to fix her with a glare, but remembered her lack of skin and muscles and eyes. "Then you can put him on the bed. He's heavy. Tell your husband to cook something like a hearty soup."

    "I'm right here," he scoffed.

    "I don't care. You didn't laugh at my jokes." She waved Jen and Man Kaplan away. "Shoo. Scram! He's literally on the precipice of death."

    Jen tugged the man away, apologizing to him silently.

    "I don't trust you," Woman Kaplan told her. She tucked Billy into bed, a hand brushing his curls aside. "And I don't care what he says. He's still my son."

    Agatha nodded. "He's a good kid, Rebecca. I won't let anything happen to him." "Haven't you, though?" The older woman turned her back on the witch. "Mama's here," she soothed. "Mama's got you."

    The skeletal witch stepped away, hugging her cloak to her.

    Chapter End Notes Ooo, what's gonna happen???

    We're Cool, Baby Chapter Summary In which the author continues to torture Agatha...for fun. :D Chapter Notes See the end of the chapter for notes Agatha tapped her index finger to her chin with a clink, clink, clink. It was the only way to keep herself calm with her lack of breathing. Especially as she watched over Billy, her unblinking gaze trained on the feverish boy. Rio's trip into his mind had been a rough one. So rough that Agatha worried it would kill him. (She was sick and tired of having to see her sons in such a state.) Already, a full day had passed, but he had yet to wake up. This was nothing like his wound on the Road. There were no spells or incantations that could be used. He wasn't poisoned by a plant. He didn't have an illness known to man. Billy had simply had Death in his head far longer than he should have. Sure Rio had been in Agatha's head plenty of times, but she'd been gentle and cautious with her presence. A few times, it had left Agatha's body sore, but it had healed with time. With Billy, Death had forced her way in and dug around ruthlessly. His magic had no time to protect him. There were no runes placed to ensure safe travels for either party. In fact, Agatha suspected Rio had been wounded to some aspect as well. Death had yet to return and explain what the hell was going on with her.

    Agatha stewed in her confusion, clink, clink, clinking the seconds away. She just wanted Billy to open his eyes and ask her one of his pesky questions again. She'd tell him whatever he wanted to know, he just needed to wake up.

    Rebecca peeked her head in, a firm scowl on her face. "We're still waiting for you," she reminded the witch.

    The Kaplan's had decided not to trust Agatha. They seemed to trust Jen just fine, but not the woman that literally died for their would-be child. It was less irritating and more insulting to Agatha. She had thought they could have bonded on a mother-to-mother level, but she had been wrong. Rebecca had even ordered her to keep her hands to herself. No one was to touch Billy without her or her husband in the room. Agatha only obeyed her orders to avoid being thrown out of the house. Once she had enough magic saved up, however... "Someone needs to keep an eye on him," she told the woman. "If he wakes up..." "He can find us downstairs," Rebecca said. "If you value your shins, you'll do as I say." Agatha flipped the woman off before pushing past her.

    Downstairs, the coven, plus Man Kaplan, sat waiting. A hush fell over the room as Agatha made herself known. Their eyes seeking her out like the scope of a sniper's gun. It reminded her of another coven many centuries ago. One that eventually turned on her. Agatha finally found an upside to her lack of facial features, though. Now she had a mask no one else could see through. With friends like these, being a skeleton was the least awful thing in her life. "Jen, here, was telling us that you're stuck in that...body?" Man Kaplan began. He gestured for her to sit. "And that Billy is the reason for it, somehow."

    Agatha remained standing. "Thank you, Jen," she told the woman sarcastically. "Aren't you just the biggest help on the block!" The skeletal witch ignored the look she was given by the other witch. "What does it matter? I was a ghost a few days ago, and that wasn't a problem for anyone."

    Teddy tapped a rib. "I got this for you," he said, holding out a plush squid. "So, you can help us know how you're feeling. You can turn it inside out." The teen showed her the two faces; one happy, one mad. He offered her a friendly smile.

    She accepted the gift with a flutter of maternal affection. "Thank you, Teddy. You're staying in the will," she joked, a bit of her irritation easing. At least somebody was taking her into consideration. Other than Rio, that is. Agatha turned the squid into its angry version. "That's how I feel, but it's not aimed at you, hun."

    "Aw, thanks!" He snapped a quick photo of her holding it, promising to show Billy when he woke up. (If he woke up.)

    "How did you come in contact with our son?" Rebecca questioned. At least the woman had a brain and was using it. Agatha couldn't fault her for being protective of her child, even if it stung to be accused of anything but caring for the boy.

    "He broke into my house," Agatha told her, doing her best to keep her tone even. "He was trying to break me out of the Scarlet Witch's spell."

    "But how did he know to find you?"

    "I don't know! I was under a spell," she stressed. "Don't you people listen?" "We're just trying to make sense of things," Man Kaplan explained. "Our son comes home beat up. Then, he's always gone to some random woman's house. Now, he's saying he died and knows Death who happens to be your girlfriend?"

    Jen made a face at the comment but decided it wasn't worth arguing about. She looked more content with watching Agatha be grilled by a unified pair for once. Traitor. Agatha face palmed. "I'm going to tear into that boy," she groaned. "He knows better than to tell people that." She turned her attention to his parents. "I'm not discussing Billy unless he's awake and here to speak for himself. You wanna talk about me being in this body? Fine. I was no longer a ghost because, somehow, he made me be alive again. Just no body, which is very on brand for him."

    "I tried to tell them," Teddy whispered. "I figured you and Rio would want to talk to them about everything." He gestured vaguely with a frown. Poor kid was the only one considering all sides of the story while worrying about his boyfriend. Agatha decided she was going to make sure he knew how much she appreciated his support.

    She patted his shoulder. "Remind me that I owe you one for your birthday, kid. Whatever you want, you name it, I'll get it for you. If I can't make it happen, I'm sure Rio can." "Agatha," Jen breathed. She squeezed her hands together. "When is Billy going to wake up? That's all we wanna know."

    Oh, now she cares she noted internally. (No, that wasn't a pang of betrayal. Agatha didn't care for Jen.) "I don't know. I-"

    "What did you even do to him? Is there anything you can tell us?" Rebecca looked ready to take a meat tenderizer to the skeleton.

    "Three centuries later, same kind of witch trial," she mumbled. "Billy has magic. His magic did something to me. My wife, the other woman, went inside his head to try and find out what. She found it, but she took off. Billy wasn't ready, so it gave him a bit of an injury." "He should be at the doctors," Man Kaplan urged. He moved to stand, but Agatha wagged her finger at him. The man sat back down with a puzzled expression.

    "And what are you gonna tell them? 'Hey, everybody! My son got his mind invaded by an ancient witch. Got any Ibuprofen?' " She waved her hands about shaking her head in disbelief. (Morons, the lot of them!) "I mean, even if you told another witch that, there's nothing you can do. Your concern is Hallmark movie worthy, but a tad unhelpful. Now, if that's all, I'd like to get back to monitoring my so-uh, student! My student," Agatha was quick to say. She waited for someone to catch her slip, but no one brought it up. Rebecca blocked her path. "I don't know if I want you around my child." "Toots, you can mean-mug me all you want. You're not keeping me from Billy." She wished she had a face again, just to prove she wasn't scared of the other woman. "In the end, I know what's best for him."

    "I'll call the cops on you."

    Agatha laughed. "Oh boy! They'll have you in a padded cell in a heartbeat." She wagged her fingers in the other woman's face. "You'd have a better chance calling the Avengers. Good luck with that, though. I hear Wanda killed a good chunk of them."

    "I'll go watch him for you," Jen offered.

    "No," she growled. "None of you are capable enough to take care of him. None of you have ever had to watch your child grow sick and die!"

    The room fell silent as her words faded.

    Man Kaplan stood to be next to his wife. "With all due respect, Billy isn't your son." Agatha glared at the couple. "And with all the disrespect in my heart, he isn't your son either. The flesh may have come from you, but not what's inside. Not what matters." "Whoa, there," a familiar voice laughed from next to Teddy. Rio threw an arm over the teen, dark eyes settled on the three arguing parents. "Lots of angry words firing away." Death grinned, face flickering. "You've got less than three seconds to step away from my wife," she warned sweetly.

    "I would do what she says," Jen told the couple. "Seriously."

    "Atta girl, Jenny," Death sneered. "Coming to your senses now that I'm around. And here I thought covens were supposed to back each other up. Only one I see doing that is Teddykins here." Rio hugged the teen warmly. "That's why you're my favorite of the group." The teen nodded with a tight smile. "Can I go sit with Billy?"

    "Sure, go right on ahead." Rio pushed him forward, mouthing a 'sorry' as he stumbled to find his footing. "Now, where were we? Oh, yes. You were badgering my wife. Never a wise decision. Not because I'd kill you or anything," Death laughed. "Agatha wouldn't hesitate to rip your throat out and make you watch each other bleed out, but she's playing nice for The Boy." She made a face. "Sorry, Teen."

    Agatha fixed her with a look. "You're not out of the doghouse either, love. You left me with these people."

    "I'll make it up to you after we get you a body." Rio sprung from the couch to pull Agatha in for a kiss. "Is Mommy having a rough time?"

    Rio," she hissed. "You promised."

    "No," Death drawled. "You made me promise not to tell Teen. You didn't say anything about William's parents."

    Agatha threw her hands in the air. "Just one day! Just one day where I don't have to worry." "If you tell them, you won't have to." Rio pressed another kiss to Agatha's skull. "If you stopped being good, they wouldn't be here at all."

    "I'm not going to kill them," she told her wife. "So, get that thought out of your head. If you need bodies, help me find Dottie's house."

    "You won't kill them because you can't," Rio laughed. She danced away, moving to sit next to Jen. "You can thank Teen for that, by the way. He wanted you to be that person he saw in your moments of weakness so bad, he practically rewrote your soul. You get to be alive and you can't fight those maternal instincts, sweetheart. Best of both worlds, am I right?" Agatha pressed her hand to her sternum, feeling for her engraved brooch. "He did what!" "Ooo, are you angry about that?" Death turned to face Jen. "I think she's angry that the Body Snatcher is making her regress emotionally."

    The skeletal witch looked up towards Billy's room. "He wouldn't have. He doesn't even know..."

    "What was it you told him? 'You don't need to know a person's name to know who they are inside'? Pretty sure that works in all contexts, dear."

    "Why are you doing this?" Agatha looked away from the ceiling. "What did I do to you?" "Nothing. I just thought we could have some fun, but he really did a number on you." Death was at her side in an instant. "Say, you should let me reap the other one. Just for fun." "What! I can't do that. Billy..."

    "He stole another life, Agatha. Someone's gonna have to come with me, and I refuse to take you a second time."

    "You don't get to make that decision for me," she argued. Agatha pointed a finger at Death. "You're supposed to be in control of the Natural Order, so get to rearranging." Rio chuckled, eyes dark with lust. "Mm, I wish I could, Agatha. The Body Snatcher beat me to the punch. They're both dead boys in living bodies. You're a living soul in a fake body. Natural Order's kinda out the window at the moment, sweetheart. But I'm willing to make another kind of trade."

    "I'm back to being confused," Man Kaplan groaned. He looked between the couple, hairline visibly receeding.

    Death covered Agatha's mouth with. "That boy isn't yours, meat bag."

    "We're taking this outside," the skeletal witch announced. "Somebody make sure Billy's got a fresh, wet cloth on his head." She didn't wait to see if they'd followed her instructions. Rio seemed to be in an excitable mood which always led to a heated argument or a wild fuck fest. (It was a terrible shame she didn't have a body right now. The second option was definitely needed right now.)

    The couple stood out in the back so Agatha could still look up at Billy's window. Her conversation with the Kaplan's had gone awry quickly, but she had avoided being kicked out of the house. Rio, on the other hand, was growing handsier by the minute. Death was practically gnawing on her mandible as she tried to work out her frustration. Much like Agatha, the experience was very enjoyable without some nerves to excite. "Will you cut that out," she growled, swatting away a hand. "What the hell was all that!" Rio grew serious, settling her hands on Agatha's hips. "I cannot complete his spell without taking the other boy. I need you to convince to let him go."

    The dread from yesterday returned. If his spell really was faulty... "Billy isn't going to do that, and neither am I. You don't get to..." Agatha stopped herself before she could dive into old habits.

    "His spell is annoying, isn't it? You never used to hesitate with mean words. Now, you can't seem to find enough anger to finish a sentence." Rio pulled her in for a hug. Death seemed just as affected as she was. "I'm sorry that he did this to you."

    "I thought I was going crazy," Agatha admitted. If only she could feel the warmth coming off of her wife, things would feel a bit better. There was no denying the truth now. "I thought I was just replacing Nicky, but it was all him. But I still can't...I can't do that to him." "Then the only other option is Wanda," Rio told her softly. "And I have a feeling she won't be happy to see you."

    Agatha clung to Death at the news. "If I have to, I guess that's what I'll do. They're still her kids."

    "I don't like Teen," Rio reminded. "But I'll help you because I miss kissing your lips, as well as other things." Her hands settled against Agatha's ribcage suggestively. Hazel eyes twinkled in the sunlight.

    "How romantic," Agatha laughed. She pressed her incisors to Rio's cheek. "I prefer you as the skeleton. You make a lovely corpse. All beautiful and pearly just for me." Death moaned. "Let's go find Wanda," she practically whined. "I need you." "I know you do, hun, but I need Billy to wake up first."

    Rio groaned. "You're really gonna make me do it?"

    "You want me to have skin and blood again, or what?"

    Death grumbled to herself before lifting them to Billy's window. "You know I can't take away whatever he saw, right?"

    "I know. I just need him to wake up so he can get his parents off my back." "They're not his parents," Rio ground out. "Their son died a long time ago. He should be calling you 'Mama' and doing his best to make you proud."

    "I'm Nicky's mama," Agatha whispered, heart breaking. "And he made me very proud. I don't need Billy for that. I just want him to get his brother back. I owe him for giving him a brutal death."

    "You didn't know they were real," Rio reasoned, but she helped Agatha crawl into the room anyway.

    Teddy merely laughed to himself. "Had a feeling you'd be sneaking back in here at some point," he told Agatha. "Still not up yet."

    "Don't worry. Rio's gonna help with that." She helped the teen roll Billy onto his back before brushing his curls away. Teddy shared a look with her, and she knew he knew. For once, the truth didn't scare her. Agatha was just glad someone other than Rio saw it as a good thing. Death rolled her eyes before growing a flower. She placed it against Billy's forehead, then sprinkled some dirt around the plant. Green magic poured from her fingertips, the flower wilting in the process. By the time the petals had finished decaying, Billy was blinking himself back into existence.

    Rio removed the flower before gently dusting the dirt from his face. "There. No more traces of me left in that pretty, little head of his. You're welcome, m'lady." She offered the dead plant to her wife.

    Agatha gave her wife a peck. "I appreciate it," she purred. The witch lightly poked Billy. "Time to wake up, Sleeping Beauty. There's an evil dragon downstairs, and she's not my biggest fan."

    The drowsy teen sat up carefully, rubbing at his eyes. "What happened?" "What didn't happen?" Rio grumbled.

    Agatha elbowed her. "Billy, Rio and I are going to be gone for a few days. Stay home with Teddy and get lots of rest."

    His eyes widened in panic. "No, you can't leave. What if something happens to you?" "I'll be fine. I'll probably find a witch to suck dry. Or think of it as a vacation for me. The gods know I need it," she grumbled.

    Billy gripped at his sheets. "Please, don't go," he whimpered. "I can't...I can't get it out of my head. It hurts."

    Rio quirked a brow. "The hell did you get into? You were supposed to see a lovely honeymoon on the Titanic. Get emotionally scared by the sounds..." She fell quiet as he began to cry anew.

    He looked up at her with red eyes. "He was hurting so much. I could feel it." Billy began to hyperventilate. "I could feel all of it."

    Agatha looked between the two. "What's he talking about? Feel what?"

    "He's delusional. Leave him be," Rio said, tugging her along. She kept sneaking glances back at Billy as they moved away from the bed.

    The boy's face turned red as he began to cry in earnest. "Agatha, I didn't want to. I swear! He was hurting. He was hurting! Tell her. You have to tell her, Rio!"

    His yelling had his parents barging into the room, angry faces turned to the couple. "What did you do?" the man asked. (He really thought he was an imposing figure, didn't he?) "We healed him. Get your panties out your ass and say, 'thank you' like normal people," Agatha growled. "Billy, it's okay. No one's hurting. Well, except maybe you." She shot a look at Rio. "Help," she whispered.

    He pulled at his hair. "I'm sorry. I'm sorry!"

    Rio snapped, putting him back into a deep sleep. She made a face at the Kaplan's. "Nobody wakes him up until we get back. If you do, the same thing's going to happen. It would behoove you to not stress him out further."

    "Why would we-?" Jen began.

    "Just do it!" Death glared at her audience before wrapping her arms around Agatha. "We need to go and get back."

    Agatha nodded.

    The couple had returned to the backyard. Rio held an ancient mortar and pestle in her left hand. A murky brown paste sat waiting as a finger dipped occasionally into its depths. The group had chosen to lock them out, but Teddy pointed at himself as if to say, "I'll take care of him for you."

    "Where the hell is Wanda anyway?" Agatha asked her as she looked around the small yard. Death finished painting runes on the lovely bones that made up her wife with a hum. "Europe."

    The witch put her hands on her hips. "Just 'Europe'?"

    "You know, if I wasn't so worried you'd turn to dust, I'd keep you just. Like. This," she told Agatha, accenting the last half of her sentence by pressing her lips to any enticing part she could reach. "I won't, though. Can't live in a world where your soul doesn't get to haunt me endlessly."

    Agatha caressed her cheek with the cool ivory of her palm. "Magic me some lungs and I'm yours," she laughed softly. "But, like you, I much prefer something more to work with." She lightly clawed at Rio's face with a gentle laugh. Agatha loved the way Rio shivered in her palm.

    Death hummed, resting in her wife's hold. "I know. You can't feel things the way I do while in that form. It's no fun if I can't make you scream."

    That made the witch cackle. "Oh, honey! All you do is make me scream. Too bad it's usually because you pissed me off."

    "You like it when I get you all hot and bothered," Rio purred. She would be on her knees and proving her statement true if there was something between Agatha's legs. Since there wasn't, and wouldn't be for the next few hours, Death merely kissed the back of her wife's hand. "Now, how do we get to Europe?"

    "You'll fly, of course."

    "Rio, I love you, but I'm literally a talking skeleton," Agatha groaned. "How the hell do you expect me to get on an airplane without the whole planet going on lockdown?" Death circled her, hands sliding along dips and bumps of the many, many bones that made up her wife. "You're a witch, sweetheart. Why else would I put these pretty little symbols on you? Not that I don't worship and adore you."

    Agatha re-examined a rune on her wrist. "An old-fashioned glamour spell. Haven't had to use one in ages." She flapped her cloak. "What about this?"

    "Should look like you're wearing a purple business suit if I did it right. If not, your plane might just end up in the ocean." Death handed her a card. "Slipped it from Jen's wallet earlier."

    Agatha took it with a dark chuckle. "Well, who am I to resist a vacation at Jenny Kale's expense? Tell me, what's the most expensive way to fly?"

    Agatha waved Rio off before passing through the gate for her flight. She wished she were still a ghost to make the whole process easier, but she couldn't resist racking up some debt for her traitorous covenmate.
