There was something about being hitting the witch in the financial gut that put a bit of pep in her step.

    Flying in a plane felt so much more dangerous than riding a broom. Plus, she didn't have Rio at her side. Rio, unfortunately, detested being in tight spaces. (Yes, yes. Death was claustrophobic. Just don't laugh at her, or you'll be stuffed in a box.) Agatha dropped into her seat and waited for the flight to kick off. Maybe someone would choke and die on board, so her wife had to make an appearance. (Unfortunately for Agatha, Rio always waited for the body to reach land before guiding the soul away.) The plane jostled intermittently, never letting Agatha fully settle into her seat. Once she had her body back, she was going to raze Westview to the ground for having enticed her in the first place.

    The plane touched down hours later, bouncing down the runway. Agatha hoped Rio's runes worked on the sound of her bones clicking against one another. If not, things were about to get very interesting for everyone on board. The witch bounced her leg impatiently as they waited to release the first-class passengers. (What was the point of paying all that money if she didn't get to be the first one out?) Finally, finally, a stewardess appeared to usher her off the plane. Agatha hoped the glamour spell allowed her to wink at the young thing. Maybe Rio would allow another witch to join them once they fleshed out their relationship. (She'd be sure to use that same joke with her wife.)

    Agatha felt her heart stutter in her hollow ribcage as she caught sight of her wife. Rio wore a beautiful, flowing summer green Jíbaro dress with blue and purple flowers stitched around the collar. Her hair was flowing with beach waves that framed her face just so. She held a vibrant, lilac flor de maga in her hands. The witch took long, confident strides over to her love. She eyed Death appreciatively before accepting the offering.

    "How was your flight, amor?"

    Agatha hooked Rio's arm in hers, guiding Rio to the airport's exit. "Bumpy, but not too bad. I haven't had to fly in one since the 80's. They've improved in some areas." Death shrugged. "They all fall the same regardless." She pressed a kiss to Agatha's illusioned cheek. "Think you can handle a little chill?"

    The skeletal witch laughed. "Not like I have any tits to freeze off."

    "Which is a shame," Rio lamented. Her eyes shot down to where she would have found them under different circumstances. "All the more reason to make the journey." The couple left the bustling airport in search of a garden. Rio hid them in a patch of bushes, sweeping her shroud around Agatha's shoulders.

    "This might feel weird, but it's perfectly safe...I think."

    Agatha didn't have much time to protest as the ground gave way, swallowing them up. The witch decided very, very quickly that she did not enjoy the sensation of dirt filling up her hollowed bits. Her bones would need to be hosed down nicely before throwing any flesh around them. She dare not open her mouth. Tongue or no tongue, she wasn't risking anything. The couple burst from the ground, white billowing around them. Rio blew gently in Agatha's direction, dirt flying off her wife and onto the snowy patch behind her. "Why didn't we do that to begin with? I could have had a body sooner!" Death's eyes twinkled. "It would have taken longer. Trust me." She waved her wife along. "Now that we're finally alone. What couldn't you tell me the other day?" Agatha hugged her cloak tightly around her lest it fly away with the gusts of wind.

    Rio twirled her wrist, the wind moving around them so her wife wouldn't be knocked over. "Your soul...I don't think I can reap it anymore. It's been changed so drastically by Teen's magic."

    "But how did he manage that? Only you can control Life and Death, give or take." Death sighed heavily. "As the son of the Scarlet Witch, he was destined to become the Demiurge of this reality."

    Agatha stopped abruptly. "The Demiurge...As in, absolute control of reality? That Demiurge?" (Oh, she was starting to feel that rising panic that a lack of lungs brought her.) "The very same. He wasn't very powerful until he went inside my head." Rio bobbed her head from side to side with a sniff. "Teen may or may not have adopted some of my abilities. One of which is the ability to blur the lines between Life and Death." She blew a raspberry. "The Boy adores you, unsurprisingly. But in your last fight, the one where he hit you with a juicy bundle of magic, he reformed your soul."

    The skeletal witch clacked her fingertips together, trying to ignore her inability to breathe as her stress levels rose. "Okay...Reformed it how, exactly? Am I going to just...poof one day?" Why did she bother to ask? She already knew what a faulty spell meant. If she could just get a little more time...

    Rio had a dark look pass along her face. "I don't know. Not entirely. I've got an idea of what could happen, but we'd need a body first. You might even have some new abilities, my love." "That doesn't sound too bad." Agatha shrugged. "Maybe Billy was a blessing in disguise. I mean, we get way more time together now, don't we?" She hoped Rio would have a definite answer. The witch needed to plan accordingly. She had so much to do now. "Maybe. I don't want to get my hopes up," Death admitted. "Not after everything. But, there's more, Agatha. Teen was still angry when he attacked you. It confused his spell. That's why you were redesignated as 'living,' but you never got a body back. He...There's a very good possibility he already knows you're his mother."

    Agatha laughed, harsh and in that self-deprecating tone that always grated on Rio's nerves. "Yeah, right! And he'll want to move in when we get back, too." She shook her head, mocking the teen as if he were telling her something. "Let's just stick to reality, hm?" Rio looked away, shoulders slumping. "You're lucky he's just as scared of the truth as you are."

    "I'm not scared of the truth," Agatha argued. "I just know how impossible it sounds to non- witches. And if Wanda finds out? Woof!"

    Rio sent her a look. She was likely imagining the red head and her together. Bless! "Don't give me that," the witch groaned playfully. "It was only a light amount of flirting. She wouldn't even flirt back. It was very disheartening."

    "You were too handsy."

    "Was not!"

    Death rolled her eyes. "You even called her 'Hot Stuff' as if I wouldn't hear you." "I was under the spell by that point," Agatha reminded her. She crossed her arms. "Where are we even going? There's not a damn thing out here but rocks, snow, and more snow." "Not rocks. Rubble," Rio corrected. She pointed to a clear spot with a frown. "And that's where our missing witch was supposed to be....Great!" The Green Witch huffed, flipping off the area.

    Agatha screamed internally but was quick to make use of the situation. "Good news, though!" "What?" Rio sighed.

    "She's still missing," Agatha stated cheerfully. "Which means I don't get blasted into dust or have a house dropped on me."

    Death looked over at her wife with a groan. "And I was so looking forward to celebrating. I bought one of those human toys you like to wear so much." Her eyes dropped down to her wife's pelvis with a whine.

    Agatha shook her head with a laugh. "With Wanda included, right?" she asked, tone lilting upwards to mess with Death.

    Rio stormed off with a growl.

    Chapter End Notes I've been harassing my blorbos enough. They needed a moment of good news (kinda) and a chance to breathe.

    Where're Mah Children Chapter Summary So...Wanda's free...That's good, right? Right?

    (Rio, put the knife down!)

    Chapter Notes Rio as Peter in that "I just wanna talk to him" scene from Family Guy, my beloved hehe.

    Sets chapter down and runs away.

    See the end of the chapter for more notes Agatha tapped her sternum impatiently as Rio released Billy from her sleep spell. The rest of the room held their breath as he stirred. Slowly, painfully slowly, the teen stretched with a groan. The witch had to restrain herself from tossing Rebecca and Man Kaplan aside so she could hold her son. Billy rubbed at his eyes, smacking his lips the way he usually did when he'd overslept before school. His curls were nearly ruined from how long he had lain in bed, tossing and turning. Agatha wanted to tell him it was time to get dressed and usher him around as if he were a small child.

    "Mom?"

    For just a singular second, Agatha nearly responded. She had enough self-control to keep from spilling the metaphorical beans in a roomful of people who didn't need to know that information. Instead, she let Rebecca console him. Rio took her hand, gripping it tightly in silent support. She was still wearing her dress from their brief trip to Europe. (It was one of the few things keeping her sane.) The witch leaned into her wife, fingers pressed to her engraved brooch.

    "Agatha?" Billy looked around his parents. His wandering eyes eventually settled on her. They lit up, a smile forming. "You're back!"

    She did her best to walk over calmly, but the excitement in his voice, when there had hardly been any for the Kaplan's, put a skip in her step. The witch flourished her cape before sitting at his side. She patted his hand, keeping the touching to a minimum with his parents around. "I'm here, kid. Had a nasty go with Rio's mind magic, didn't you?"

    He nodded slowly, brows furrowing. "You're...still a skeleton."

    "How very astute of you," she teased. Agatha clasped her hands together, settling them in her lap. "Yes, we've hit a minor snag. I'll be like this for a little longer, so please don't do anything stupid to lose your magic. I don't feel like not existing."

    Billy smiled at her. His eyes looked so tired despite sleeping for a full seventy-two hours. "Pretty sure I wouldn't let that happen to you. I don't feel like finding a new mentor." He waved to Rio, a genuine grin stretching his cheeks. "I forgive you for the headache, by the way. I know you were just doing what you needed to do. Did you figure out how to fix Agatha?"

    Rio took a step closer, eyes searching him. "By 'fix' do you mean getting her a body?" The teen laughed softly, a hand rubbing at his left eye again. "Maybe. What's wrong with the spell? Did I do an incantation wrong?"

    "Not wrong. You just didn't complete it." Agatha swallowed thickly. How to tell him without giving everything away? "Our memories messed with your head, Billy. You wanted me alive again, but...different."

    "You wanted her to be who she was before Nicky left us," Death explained quietly. "When she was nice."

    "I wasn't nice. Don't say that," she warned her wife. "But it has changed me. I'm not complaining a whole lot. Would just be nice to not hesitate when I want to kill someone. Your parents, for example. And Jen."

    "I didn't know...Just tell me what I need to do, and I'll fix it."

    Agatha looked back at her wife. "See? He's a good kid." She turned back to the teen. "We'll worry about that later. Are you feeling better? No more horrible memories making you scream weird things?"

    "I was screaming?"

    "A lot," Man Kaplan informed. He rubbed his wife's shoulders, throwing a look in Agatha's direction. "We've got a lot to discuss."

    "Like the fact that Agatha and Rio stole my wallet to make a trip to Europe," Jen grumbled. "What the hell did you buy? I've got a $6,000 bill!"

    "Sorry, not sorry," Agatha said with a shrug. "They were getting ready to throw me to a pack of dogs, kid. I did what I had to do to survive. You get it, right?"

    "Please don't," he told his parents, a smile twitching to life. "I need her to help me control my magic. And I need her to help me find my brother. I doubt she could do that as some dog's chew toy."

    Agatha would have grimaced if she could. "About that...."

    Billy looked at her, grief-stricken. "No...Is he...?"

    "Body Snatcher Number Two is still alive and well," Rio told him quickly, tone bored. (She couldn't fool Agatha, though. The skeletal witch saw the flicker of amusement in her eyes.) "It's Mommy Maximoff that's got us in a real bind. She's on her way to collect her baby chicks."

    "He isn't a Maximoff," Rebecca hissed. "You're all just confusing him." (At least Agatha wasn't the only mother spiraling hopelessly towards a bitter end.)

    "Mom, it's true," Billy urged. "I know it's crazy. I...I thought I was for a long time, but I am connected to Wanda Maximoff."

    "Spiritually," Agatha explained. "The body isn't...Isn't his, exactly. That's why things are such a mess and Rio got into a bit of a fuss."

    Man Kaplan stepped forward, his face thunderous. "I refuse to believe my son is dead," he told her lowly. "He's sitting right here talking to us."

    "Dad," Billy breathed. He held his head in his hands with a groan.

    "Back up," the skeletal witch instructed. "Your thoughts are too loud for him. You're making things worse."

    "What?"

    Agatha pushed him back lightly with the little amount of magic she had. "Head noisy. Be quiet." She wanted to stroke those curls and soothe his worries, but things were far too tense to start that kind of fight. "Billy, take deep breaths. Remember the meditation technique we worked on for noisy environments. If it'll help, I could always have Rio give them a long walk off a short pier."

    He gripped her hand silently and followed her instructions. Billy closed his eyes, chest visibly moving as he focused on blocking the world out.

    "Firstly, I'm a skeleton and still alive. So, if that can be true, Billy being a Maximoff is possible. Secondly, if we could all just hold off on the witch hunt, I'd appreciate it. He's barely woken up and you lot are not helping." She turned to Jen and pointed to her favorite of the group (other than Rio...and Billy). "Maybe take Teddy home. Oh, and go check on my house. Wanda might have set it on fire while we were out. If she did..." Agatha shook her head. "Well, it doesn't really matter. My favorite coat's already gone. R.I.P." Her covenmate leaned forward with a quirked brow. She looked at Agatha as if she'd turned neon. (With Billy's magic, that was a real possibility.) "Why would I go towards the Scarlet Witch? I don't have a death wish."

    "Jen the Reluctant, that's Billy's old mother. If she goes to kill you, just tell her where to find me. She might give you a reward or something. I don't know. Just check the damn thing, will you?"

    The teen reached forward and gripped her arm. "She'll kill you!"

    Agatha gently pushed him back against his pillows. "Dying's not so bad. I'll keep dying if it means keeping you safe."

    She heard Rio shift with a strangled noise.

    "But I don't want you to die," he argued. "I still need you. Who's gonna teach me how to teleport?"

    "As if I'd leave you to your own devices, Beauford. Can't have people hearing that the Great Agatha Harkness' pupil accidentally gave produce sentience or anything embarrassing like that." She patted his hand. "I'll be fine."

    "You don't have magic," he whined. "You'll get turned into paste. Cheap paste." "Yikes! You don't have much faith in me, do you?" She laughed, hamming it up for the boy. Agatha shook her head, lamenting her inability to comfort him. She turned away to face the room. "Seriously, though, Jen. Go check on my house and get Teddy to safety. Once Wanda realizes where Billy is, she'll stop at nothing until she gets him back." Rebecca was the next person to grab her. Rio growled lowly from the corner of the room. "No one's taking my son."

    "Yeah, you try telling that to Wanda." Agatha shook her hand off. "My wife doesn't appreciate the attitude, either. Might want to keep your hands to yourself. She can get pretty jealous."

    "She's just scared," Billy told Rio. "Please, don't be mad at her. You know how mothers can get when their children are about to be taken away."

    Agatha and Rio both jerked back. They shared a similar look, Rio swallowing thickly. To the skeletal witch's shock, Death nodded and visibly relaxed. That was new. Certainly made things easier moving forward.

    "Everyone just needs to chill out," she told the group. "And Jen, if I have to tell you a third time, I'm going use your business funds to buy all sorts of lewd and sexually deviant items. Your reputation will never recover. Now, go!"

    The pink-clad witch finally led Teddy away.

    Rio moved forward now that there was more room by the bed. She dropped her hand onto Billy's head. "Your magic is very annoying," she told the teen. Rio slid her hand down, teasing him despite her next words. "But you're going to need to be ready to fight Wanda just in case she comes in blasting."

    Agatha placed a hand under her chin, thinking. "No, you should take him and his parents away if that happens. I'll handle Wanda on my own."

    Billy shook his head. "I'm not leaving you to face her alone," he argued. "Maybe if I give you a bit of my magic..."

    "That's sweet, Billy, but you're still recovering." He's right, though. Even if I have Rio, she can't do much of the fighting thanks to her shitty rules. No...No. We've got no choice in the matter now. She turned to address Rebecca and Man Kaplan. "I suggest packing a bag. Wanda can be a bit...much." Agatha looked back over at her son, swallowing back the emotion that threatened to swallow her whole. "Pack one for Billy, too." "Agatha!" Billy sat up, brows furrowing deeply. "I said-"

    "Billy, I can't promise you'll be safe," she finally told him, voice raising an octave in the process. "She loves you so much! Wanda will stop at nothing to get you and Tommy back. If you're with your parents, I'll be able to talk to her without anyone else getting hurt. But if you stay here, a lot of people could die. Can you live with that on your conscience?" "She's right," Rebecca told him gently. "We'll stay in Hoboken until this all clears up. After that, we can come home and sort things out."

    He scowled, petulant and resistant. "Agatha needs me. She's powerless right now, and it's all my fault."

    "Hey now," she hissed. "All I need is my brilliant mind and charm. I'll have Wanda in the palm of my hand once it's all said and done." Agatha hoped he believed her lie. She didn't want him to remember her angry or upset.

    Rio gave her a look, eyes downcast. Maybe she finally remembered what Agatha never had the benefit of forgetting.

    Agatha steeled herself. She had to do this. There wasn't another option. Not anymore. "Billy, you're a great kid, but you don't have to worry about me. I'm a grown woman, and I have Rio at my side. Go with your parents. Take Teddy if you need to. Just...don't stay here with some silly idea of being the hero."

    He took her hand, his eyes brimming with unshed tears. "She will kill you," Billy all but sobbed. "Please, don't fight my mother alone."

    She squeezed his hand, heart shattering anew. "She's not your mother...and neither am I. Go with your real parents and live a long, happy life."

    His face fell, throat bobbing with words that failed to come forth.

    Agatha stood, flourishing her cape. She made her voice as firm as it could be. "Pack the boy's bags and be gone. Billy can send Jen and Teddy a text to meet you in Hoboken. Jen should be able to protect you if things go south."

    Death stepped over to her side, taking her hand to keep it from trembling. "Agatha, tell him," she hissed louder than Agatha would have liked.

    "I've said all I need to say," she ground out. Agatha pulled her wife along, not daring to look back at her son. "Now, be a good Green Witch and keep an eye out for the Scarlet Witch for me. I've got a phone call to make."

    Rio paced in the Kaplan's garden as clouds drifted lazily overhead. The witch had her jaw clenched tightly. She kept her eyes on Agatha as the witch sat in the center of the backyard. Death froze as car doors closed and an engine started. She gripped the hilt of her dagger as irritation won out. "Why didn't you tell him?"

    Agatha turned to face her, her skull a bright white in the mid-day sunlight. "Why drop that bombshell on him when I'm about to die?"

    "Who said you were dying today?" Death glared at the skeletal witch. Even without a proper face, she could tell she'd hit an exposed nerve. How easy it was to settle into old habits. "Who said you could just love another kid just to run away again?"

    Her wife laughed. "How is this running away, Rio? I'm preparing to subdue the Scarlet Witch's rage so he might have a chance. I accept the challenge, just as I always have." Agatha gripped at the purple fabric hanging limply around her shoulders. "Why the change of heart? Why now? Yesterday, you were ready to bleed him dry for a fresh coat of nail polish." Death walked over to sit next to her. It took everything in her to keep from shaking her wife. She encouraged the grass to soften in her presence, dandelions blooming around them. "He lived it, Agatha. My taking of Nicky." She refused to look over, but she knew Agatha was staring at her. "That was the memory he accidentally stepped into. He was me in the moment, and it's stuck with him."

    "How can you be sure?" her wife asked quietly. As if she were afraid of the answer. As if the truth hadn't been shouted at her each time the teen had woken up.

    "Because Billy looks like he's lost his innocence," Death informed, head bowing. "He will never look at people the same. Will never take for granted the small moments in his life. Won't take time with his coven for granted." She met Agatha's orbitals with her own. "Won't take time with you for granted."

    Agatha was silent for a long moment. Finally, she cupped Rio's cheek with an audible grin. "You finally called him 'Billy'," she whispered softly.

    Rio nodded, tears streaming down her cheeks. Ivory fingertips brushed them away. "He..." Her eyes widened, her wards firing off around them. "Wanda," she growled. "Stay behind me."

    "I know you're all powerful, but if you have to fight Wanda...?" Agatha shrugged her shoulders questioningly.

    "Still can't die, but she could make things very uncomfortable for me." Death unsheathed her dagger, a grin spreading lazily. "Nothing I can't handle."

    Overhead, a scarlet ball of magic heralded the arrival of the chaos witch. Wanda appeared, crowned and visibly pissed. She fired a warning at the couple. "What have you done with my son?" the woman asked with glowing eyes.

    Rio cocked her head to the side. "Why don't you come down here and find out?" she teased. "I've got a bone to pick with you, myself."

    The redhead lowered to the ground, her magic sending wave after wave of energy out from her body. Her soul was coated in it like a powdered donut, the scarlet sugar dusting around the woman.

    Death inhaled, the taste of the chaotic magic coating her senses like a drug. She licked her lips. "What? Didn't like hanging out with your brother and parents? It was hard wrangling them together for you."

    "I didn't come for you, Lady Death," the Sokovian witch drawled. "I'm here for her." Wanda pointed at the skeleton standing defiantly next to Rio. "Where is my son, Agatha? I know you've had him."

    Agatha stepped forward, cape flourishing dramatically. Her solemn attitude shifted subtlety. "So, funny story, your son isn't actually here right now." The witch shrugged as if she were innocent of the whole ordeal. "I'm not sure what took you so long, but he took off a little over an hour ago. The outfit's cute, though. Much better than sweats and a hoodie." Rio gave her wife a look. What game is she playing? "Might as well tell her where he went if you're going to be so forthcoming." She shifted her gaze back to the witch. "I'll make you a deal. You give Agatha a body, I'll tell you where your son is."

    Wanda laughed. "Why would I do that? She's the one who's hellbent on ruining my life." "No, that was you," the skeleton argued. "I just wanted your power so I could bring my dead son back to life. Nothing personal."

    Death turned fully to stare at her wife. "That's why you went through that whole mess with the Darkhold and her!" She rolled her eyes. "Whatever. We'll talk later." "You don't have any children," Wanda told Agatha. (Always taking the high ground, that one.) "No mother would do what you did." She took a step towards the couple. "No mother would rip children from another mother's arms."

    "Hey, I totally hear you," the skeletal witch reasoned. "I was a bit crazy from the Darkhold, but I do have kids." Agatha tilted her head, a small laugh bubbling up from wherever her voice came from. "Did you...I mean, if you did, it's fine, but...Did you use my magic to sire your twins? Again, fine if you did! I just wanna get the story straight." Rio put her dagger away. "Agatha..."

    Wanda pushed her away with her magic, eyes glowing a brighter scarlet. "How dare you!" Clearly, Agatha was up to something. Maybe she believed this demure mother-to-mother ploy would placate the witch. She didn't really want to play along, but if Agatha thought it would work... "Sweetheart, if I said they're half your kids, they're half your kids. You don't need to ask her," Rio grumbled. She waved a hand, entangling the Scarlet Witch in thick roots. "I'm going to need you to calm down. If I have to deal with another Maximoff tantrum, I'm ending your bloodline personally."

    Her wife pressed a hand to her clavicles, mouth falling open. "Wha..? I was just asking, okay! She's the one who went around making magic babies without consent." Agatha crossed her arms. ".......But, like, did you?"

    Wanda looked between the two, brows furrowed in a way that reminded them of Billy. (Welp, that was her done for. She ran a good game, but the kid beat her into submission.) "What are you talking about? Why won't you just give me back my son? That's all I want." Rio shared a look with Agatha. "Well, go ahead, darling. Don't act all shy now." She threw her hands in the air at the skeletal witch's silence. Nope. I can't do this. There's literally so many bodies piling up right. "Not like I was looking forward to a challenge or anything," Rio told her wife. What was the point of Agatha's dramatic farewell if this was how she was going to handle The Scarlet Witch?

    "Oh, settle down. It could still happen." Agatha moved closer to the tied-up witch. "Now, this feels familiar," she hummed. Rio could practically hear her grinning, the cad. "You've got some 'splaining to do, little lady. We'll start with Westview." Agatha rubbed her fingers together with an incantation only for her magic to fizzle out. "This is so annoying!" She shook her hands out of frustration. "Rio, help me out here."

    Death dropped to the ground with a groan. "I'm gonna let her out, actually. This is too boring!" She waved her hand, freeing Wanda. "Hey, enslave another town. Those souls were fun to ferry away. All of them hated you so much."

    "Rio! Stop that," Agatha growled. "We were prepared for an all-out battle," she admitted to the Scarlet Witch. "She gets like this when she doesn't get to cause some damage. Just...Just ignore her. She'll leave in a minute."

    Wanda rubbed her wrists, eyes flicking back and forth. "I'm thoroughly confused. What's even happening here?"

    Agatha threw an arm over the Scarlet Witch's shoulders. "So, after you trapped me in that horrid little town, a boy came to break me out. Seems you used a bit of my magic and soul to make those irritating twins of yours. Said boy turned out to be Billy, who I've sent away just in case you start blasting away with that crazy magic of yours."

    "Why is he with you? Why...Why didn't he stay to see me?"

    Rio watched the woman grapple with her new reality, a flicker of sympathy sparking to life. "He stole a second life when you released your spell. His soul entered a random teen's body after said teen died in a car accident. His soul fused with the other boy's, and it messed with his memories. Agatha's been trying to mentor him, but he got a mixture of Harkness- Maximoff temperament. So, there's that."

    "He doesn't...remember you," Agatha added carefully. "He doesn't remember me, either, by the way. I just happened to have the answers he needed since you were a bit," the witch made a throat slashing gesture. "A lot happened, actually. But we'll deal with that later. He didn't want to see you because I sent him away...for his safety."

    "Aggie doesn't want him to know she's his mother too," Rio explained. "But, if you give her a body, we'll get him over here in a jiffy."

    "I fail to see why I should help her. She'll just try to steal my magic again," Wanda argued. "I learned my lesson. Promise," Agatha said, hands held up in defense. "I would just like to be able to emote properly. Full disclosure: Being a skeleton fucking sucks." Wanda eyed Agatha, then turned to Rio. "Is she lying? I can't...She doesn't have a face." "My point exactly," Agatha shouted.

    Death narrowed her eyes at the living woman. "She not, but I can tell you won't help." She moved to stand, dusting herself off. "Sorry, Agatha, but if she won't give you one, I'm taking the other boy as collateral."

    Her wife froze. "Rio, let's be reasonable now. She hasn't said 'no' yet. I can still convince her to-"

    She shook her head. "I've wasted enough time here. If she doesn't give you a body in the next minute and a half, I go after the boy." Death waited for her words to sink in, the next phase of her plan setting into motion. It wouldn't be hard to find Tommy, after all. She could hold him hostage until Wanda gave in.

    Wanda was the first to react, her hands raising. "I won't let you harm my children." "Then you should have thought about that before creating them," she growled. Rio shifted into her true form, scowl melting away to her grinning mandible. She turned to face Agatha. "Te veo."

    The witch reached for her, but Death had already slipped away into the Ether. She watched as Agatha and Wanda turned to face each other. If this didn't compel the Scarlet Witch into helping her wife, nothing would work. Unfortunately, it looked like Wanda was still being uncooperative. Death sighed. The things she did for love. Hopefully, Billy wouldn't hold it against her for too long.

    Agatha stared Wanda down, silence pressing in on them from all sides. She crossed her arms. "Look, I don't want her to take Tommy either, but I can't do much to hold her off in this state. If I had a body, I'd keep her busy long enough for you to hide him."

    The Sokovian soldier glared at her. "This is all your fault! You took everything from me. I was finally happy."

    "You created a fake reality because you couldn't bear to face the truth," Agatha growled. "Vision would have realized the truth at some point, and you probably would have had to have fought him. I saved you the heartbreak and pain that comes with getting too attached." It was the hardest lesson she'd ever learned, but she'd still let her heart get in the way of things when it came to Billy.

    Red swirled around the woman's hands, enticing Agatha. "Maybe so, but that doesn't take away what you did."

    "I'm all for you being pissed, hun, but I still need a body to help save Tommy." Agatha took a risk. "He's my son, too." A spell was lobbed at her, hitting her in her chest. Agatha absorbed it greedily. (So, she had lied. Sue her.)

    "He's my son!"

    Agatha laughed. "What? You thought a robotic figment of your imagination could knock you up! Please," the witch cackled. "Another witch was always going to be your solution. Brings a tear to my eye that you chose me, though. I knew you couldn't resist me for too long." She wiped at her dry skull with a finger. "The make-up sex with Rio is going to be legendary, I assure you."

    Wanda shook with fury. Her face was scrunched up into a mess of emotions. "I...I can't do this! You look ridiculous." She dispelled her magic, a hand pinching the bridge of her nose. "I agree. So, give me a body." Agatha flapped her hands towards herself. "Just...give me one. Doesn't have to be exactly perfect. I'll take anything at this point. I just need a little something long enough to..." She swallowed back her panic. Was she doomed to always want more time? The skeletal witch decided to give one last good effort. Maybe the Universe would take pity on her. Maybe not. All she knew was that she had to try. She had to. The Scarlet Witch circled her as her eyes took in Agatha's new form. She sniffled, wiping away a stray tear. "If I make you a temporary body, will you help me save Tommy?" Agatha latched onto the offer with a hunger she hadn't felt in ages. "Not only will I help you save him, I'll see what I can do to help them remember you." She tapped her fingers together. "There is a bit of an issue, though. I'm not sure how willing Billy will be to see you. He can get in a mood, sometimes."

    "How do I know you're not lying to me again?"

    "You're just gonna have to trust me, dear." She leaned forward, curling and uncurling her fingers. "Come on. What mother wouldn't give up the world to be with her kids again?" Wanda swallowed thickly. "Tell me about your child first. Prove you're worth trusting." Agatha shook her head, irritation growing. "Boy, you and Billy! One in the same." She waved the woman off. Why did everyone want to know about Nicky so bad? Could she not have this one, perfect thing to herself? "Forget I ever said anything. I'll go get Tommy myself." "What mother wouldn't give up the world to be with her kids again?" Wanda parroted. (Mocked, more like.)

    The skeletal witch turned and marched over to the living woman. "You have no idea what I've been through. The twins are alive while their older brother was put in the ground centuries ago! I have killed so many for the chance to hold him again, and you just get everything you want! And what you can't get, you make."

    Wanda met her blow for blow. "I tore realities apart for my sons. I killed heroes for a chance to see them again. You and I are not the same. I have lost so many. I only want my children." "Oh, boo-fucking-hoo!" Agatha turned away from Wanda. "You and your fancy magic can go hide under a rock for all I care. I forgot how pitiful you really are." A blast of red light the grass next to her, throwing Agatha several feet away. She tried to rise but her bones had been scattered throughout the yard. Wanda stormed after her, magic swirling menacingly.

    "Yeah, go on. Blast me to bits. Any chance you would have had with Billy will go with me." Agatha glared at her bleached bones. They refused to snap back together. "You've got to be kidding me." The witch wanted to sob.

    Agatha had run out of time.

    "You probably brainwashed my son. You made him think you care for him just so you could use him against me."

    "Says the woman who mind-controlled an entire town," she spat. "You're exactly like me. Always imposing our will, consequences be damned. You'd make a fine witch killer." "I'm nothing like you! I love my children. I would do anything for them. I have done everything for them. You're just a coward who doesn't feel anything."

    "You think it doesn't kill me to know I sentenced the twins to a painful death? I thought they were fake. That they were just another piece of your sad, sad mental state." Agatha managed to roll her skull over to face Wanda. "I could have used Billy to fight you. I could have used him to buy me time, but I didn't. I sent him away so he wouldn't have to see me die because I..." She bit back the end of her sentence. Agatha would miss her irritating son. She really would. "Just finish me off already, Wanda. Anything's better than watching everyone else get to be his mother."

    The other woman stopped to stare at her. "Why are you so sure you're going to die, Agatha?" The skull laughed. (Sobbed, more like.) "Don't you remember what I told you? Once a spell is cast, it can't be adjusted. Even if you gave me a body, I'll still be a cheap, plastic skeleton." She thanked the Goddess she couldn't cry. It was hard enough to talk as it was. "I just needed to buy time so Rio would get bored and leave. I thought she'd remembered that rule, but I was wrong. I didn't want her here for this. If she knew what I was planning, she'd go insane." Wanda stopped to stand just a few steps away from her skull. "Can't she save you? She's Death."

    Agatha pawed at the earth with her disembodied hand. "Billy tampered with my soul. I'm outside of her control now. The only options I have are to die or fade away once Billy's magic runs out. I'd like it to be on my own terms." Her fingers sank into the soil, letting her feel closer to her wife who was likely busy by now. She should have sent Rio off with a kiss. Wanda's hands began to glow once more. "Will you tell me where Billy is?" Agatha stared out into the distance, not daring to look the other witch in the eyes. "No. He should go to you when he's ready."

    "If you won't tell me, I'll leave nothing for Lady Death to collect," Wanda growled. "It will be like you never existed."

    "So be it."

    The earth shook as Wanda raised stones and other heavy items the Kaplan's kept around their house. Agatha gripped the patch of grass tightly, her gaze landing on the field of dandelions. She heard the witch grunt as the projectiles aimed for the bones lying scattered about. There was a sickening crack as her ribs and limbs were smashed to pieces. At least she couldn't cry. At least she'd spared Rio and Billy the worst of it. Maybe...maybe she'd see Nicky this time. Agatha liked that thought.

    CRACK!

    Rio found her next soul, an elderly man in a nursing home. He eyed her warily. She groaned inwardly. Stubborn ones always required so much effort she shouldn't have to give. "It's time," she told the man.

    He waved her off. "Tomorrow," he told her.

    "I'm not coming back tomorrow, Jerry. Let's go."

    Jerry shot her a look. "I refuse."

    "Not an option." She waited patiently for him to rise from the bed. "There's nothing else you can do in this state."

    He flipped her off.

    Death took a step towards him before her heart seized in her chest. She collapsed in a heap, hands clawing at her chest. "AGATHA," she howled. Death turned until she was pointing in her wife's direction. "What did you do?"

    Ignoring Jerry's soul, as well as all others, Rio raced back to Eastview. The beating of her heart had stopped indefinitely, which only meant one horrible, terrible thing for Death. By the time she stepped into Eastview, dark, swirling green clouds had gathered over most of the state. Any bodies of water in the area violently surged and ebbed. Wild animals began to panic, running for cover in a cacophony of noise. Nature was in an upheaveal as Death walked over to flecks of white adorning the ground. An amalgamation of stones and household items atop the shattered limbs.

    She stared at what should have been her wife in a new body. There should be a smirk on her face, a twinkle in her eyes. Rio could almost see her crook a finger at her with a teasing whisper.

    But that wasn't what she found.

    Agatha had been smashed to bits by that damned woman. She didn't need to turn anything over to confirm her suspicions. Death would find no skull for Agatha's head had been crushed by a large rock. She surveyed the carnage, looking for any signs that her wife might just be playing a trick on her. The only thing she found were sections of her right phalanges deeply embedded in the soil.

    Rio fell to her knees with a wail.

    Lightning flashed overhead, the wind picking up. Death could not sense her wife's soul. Had nothing to guide. Had no one to send off to Nicky. Agatha was gone, plain and simple. Death glared at no one and nothing. If Wanda wanted to play that game, she'd play. Death would claim what was hers from the very beginning.

    Death would reap Wanda Maximoff's twins.

    Billy craned his neck to see the sky from the dingy car window. The last time he had seen weather this crazy, Agatha and Rio were fighting. Billy worried his bottom lip, wondering for the millionth time if he should have stayed. The note burning in his pocket told him 'no'. If he stayed, they would miss Tommy.

    The radio began to glitch.

    "...illy...Billy?...oming to get....Bil..."

    Rebecca turned the radio off. "A silent drive is best," she hummed, paling. Billy shared a look with Jen. "That was what happened when the hex was breaking down," he explained quietly. "I can remember that bit now thanks to Agatha." Agatha? he sent his mentor. The connection felt off, though. Like there was a solid, touchable wall between them. Billy frowned, a churning, sour feeling in his gut.

    "What's wrong?" Teddy asked, a hand resting on his arm.

    "I...I can't reach Agatha," he told his boyfriend. "And I think Rio's upset." Billy felt his heart began to beat faster. "We should turn around. I need to make sure Agatha's okay." "We're not going towards the danger," his father scoffed. "Your friend-" "Agatha," Billy corrected. "Her name. Is. Agatha."

    "Agatha," Jeff said carefully, "told us to take you away from Eastview for a reason. Clearly, she knew you would be in more danger with her than away."

Armed men watched the immediate area carefully. The group was quickly realizing Tommy wasn't at just any government facility. He was in a maximum security prison.

    "How do we get in there?" Teddy hissed. "That place is crawling with-" He yelped as everyone slid to the right.

    Rebecca pulled off before they got too close to the facility. She parked the car behind a row of trees and took a deep breath. The car radio began to blare, making everybody jump. The group scrambled out of the car to find a red glare clashing against the green sky. Two figures floated above the ground, flanking the vehicle.

    The teen scanned the area, his stomach churning aggressively. "Rio, where's Agatha?" Billy asked the black clad woman. He hadn't seen her wear this much black in a long time. He really hoped she was just trying to intimidate Wanda.

    "Billy, is that you?" the red haired woman asked. She moved to see him, but Jen stepped between them.

    Death looked down at him, her makeup ruined and staining the ivory of her skull. She looked haggard. "sSshHheEe'sSs gGgoOonNneEe."

    The teen felt the world turn on its side as his legs gave out on him. "No," he hoarsely said. "No!" Billy held his head, reaching out to his mentor. "Agatha," he sobbed. Death's face lit up with a brief flash of lightning. Her hazel eyes were pained and broken by the weight of the truth. She made no move to comfort him.

    "She knew she was going to die," Wanda told the group. "I just sped up the process at her own behest."

    "You killed her?!" Billy glared at the witch, angry tears blurring his vision. "How could you? She was my friend!"

    "I had to protect you from her." Wanda's face softened. "She was going to take you and Tommy from me. I couldn't let her do that."

    Billy scrambled to stand back up, his clothes changing to that of his caped outfit. "She was protecting me from you! You're evil!"

    "No, no," Wanda laughed. "Agatha was evil. She tricked you into believing something that just isn't true. I'm your mother."

    Death growled, sky flashing. "Agatha is his mother." She looked around with a manic cackle. Thunder shook the air around them. "There! I said it, Agatha. I said it, so get over here and..." The cosmic being choked back a sob.

    Billy blinked. "She's what?"

    Death threw her head back with another laugh. She was spiraling, tears a constant stream now. The cosmic being clawed at her chest, eyes locking with his. "You stupid boy. Agatha has been your mother since day one. Half of your soul is made from hers." She pointed at him, eyes flashing green. "You are the son of Agatha Harkness."

    The teen looked down at his hands. His brain struggled to make sense of everything. Not only was Agatha dead, but his mother as well? How could that be? Why hadn't she told him? How did Wanda know? What did it all mean in the end? Why him?

    He was vaguely aware that Wanda and Rio were arguing above. Vaguely aware of the hands that grabbed and pulled at him as he collapsed back towards the ground. Vaguely aware of the tears staining his face or the wails spilling from his lips. He had just gained a mother, and she was already dead.

    Billy closed his eyes and shut the world out.

    Agatha had practically spelled it out for him. All those looks. All those moments where she'd soothed his nightmares away. The way she had been so adamant about his safety on and off the Road. Always watching over him. The fact that she never left him for long when they argued. Always leaving until she'd calmed down enough before returning to help him with his own issues.

    God! She'd done so much for him. She...

    "Wanda's not your mother...And neither am I."

    She had known she wouldn't be seeing him again. She had known, and she wanted to cut their bond before she inevitably hurt him with the loss. She didn't want a repeat of Nicky. She didn't want him to see her die. Didn't want their true familial bond to make things harder for him.

    Agatha had pretended to be fine the moment he tampered with her soul so he would never feel guilty. She had, as she always had, turned his mistakes into her own. The Harkness would never have to atone for his own sins because that was how much she loved him. And now she was gone forever.

    "...What?"

    Billy looked around in confusion. "Wait, what's happening?"

    Teddy grabbed his arm, pulling him towards the fence. "Rio's going to reap you and Tommy. We have to get to him first."

    With Agatha gone, Rio's gone insane, he told himself. Billy looked behind him. Death was throwing everything she had at Wanda, fury fueling her magic. He wanted to hold her. "Stand back." Billy blasted the gate, an alarm blaring. Search lights swiveled around to focus on him and Teddy. Billy held his ground, blue swirling around him and his boyfriend.     Death blinked as she found herself standing in what she would have believed to be the Salem of old. The taste of magic on her tongue, however, told her she was in a hex. She looked over at where Wanda had been, but she was no longer glaring her down. Death growled, turning around until she saw a cabin resting where the prison had just been. She drifted over, dagger poised for any surprises. "Nothing's ever easy with you Maximoff's."

    The cosmic being entered the cabin to find herself looking at Billy. He turned to face her, his face just as broken as hers.

    "Rio...Is she...Is she really gone?" he choked out.

    Death clenched her jaw, her grip on her dagger's hilt tightening. "Yes," she hissed out. The Green Witch aimed her blade as she advanced on the teen.

    He didn't try to move away from her. "Lilia said that death isn't always the end of something."

    She faltered. "What?"

    Billy held his ground. "She left a note for me. She must have seen it before we ever met, but that's what she said to tell you. I'm choosing to believe she knows something we don't." He extended a hand.

    Death snarled at him, slapping his hand away. "I don't care what Lilia said. Her soul is gone! She's never coming back, Billy. Never." She swung her dagger at him.

    The Universe groaned in protest. It must have forgotten how far she was willing to go for Agatha. Still, it burned her hands as she proceeded to chase the boy through the cabin. The Universe sided with the young Maximoff and rearranged the cabin.

    "Rio," Billy shouted over his shoulder. "I get you're upset, but-" He ducked as she threw a vase at him. "Killing Tommy and I won't bring her back."

    Death lunged for him, sinking the blade of her dagger into a wall in the process. "If you had left her alone, none of this would've happened. She'd be alive. She'd be safe." Death swiped at him with her razor sharp nails. "This is all your fault, Billy!"

    The boy nodded, tears in his eyes. "I know. I'm sorry, Rio. I'd take it back if I could." He swallowed thickly. "But what if she can come back? Do you really want to risk hurting her again by reaping Tommy and I?"

    The cosmic entity removed her knife with a growl. "Your mind tricks won't work on me. Can't guilt me the way you guilted your own mother," she told him lowly. Death smirked, a small laugh taunting the teen. "Yeah, Billy, think about it," she said as his face fell. "You used the memory of your dead brother to push her towards me. You're a coward. Just. Like. Her." He yelled at her, charging with fists of blue magic. Their bodies collided with a crack. Their magic pulsed and sparked as they struggled to take control of her dagger. Death sneered in his face, weeks worth of pent up aggression tumbling out of her like lava from an erupted volcano. "Don't act all high and mighty now, Witch Killer. I lived that day from your point of view. You knew what invoking my dead son would do to her. You knew, and you did it anyway." She threw him into a wall with a laugh. "You forced me to kill my own wife. I killed the woman I love more than anything in this wretched world. But to her, she died for love of you."

    Billy hit her with a stream of unstable magic. She let herself be thrown backwards. Fed off the pain that radiated through her body. This was what she deserved, after all. If she hadn't left Agatha's side, had considered Wanda to be more ruthless than she seemed, her wife would would still be alive. She had failed the witch again, but this time there would be no chance at redemption. Agatha wouldn't appear out of the blue to save her from herself. And since all reason for existing was truly gone, Death would burn the world to the ground. The whole damn universe would be Agatha's funeral pyre. The whole universe would be Death's grave.

    Pink streams of magic added to the mix before Jen snuck away with Billy. The cabin rearranged itself for a second time. The groan of Billy's hex magic filled the air. Death found no issue with it. She would look for Tommy first. She'd torture him until he handed himself over, then she'd do the same with Billy. Death would deliver their heads to Wanda. The grief would push her over, and she would return to the afterlife. Then, and only then, would Death use her Green Magic to enact the end times. The world didn't deserve to exist without Agatha in it. She'd be cursed with eternity, but at least the Maximoff's wouldn't be there to rub their unholy faces in hers.

    "What have you done with my son?" Wanda questioned from the end of the hall. The witch must have appeared while she was seething. Wanda caught a glimpse of a photo and stopped. Death followed her line of sight as she healed a gash in her shoulder. In the frame, Agatha and Rio stood together with matching grins. Their hands rested on Agatha's swollen belly. The cosmic entity swallowed thickly. Billy's magic had pulled from her memories to create the place. How irritating.

    "Agatha told me the spell was faulty," Wanda said carefully. "She asked me to kill her." Death rounded on her, eyes burning with angry tears. "Like hell she would!" "My hex was faulty. She said, once cast, spells couldn't be altered. Agatha said a body wouldn't work because of whatever Billy did to her." The Scarlet Witch eyed the dagger in the immortal's hand. "I helped her...And I did what was necessary to protect my children from her, harmless as she was."

    "They were her children too," Death hissed. "She took care of your brat the moment he darkened her doorstep. Healed him back to health and refused to hand him to me." She waved a finger in Wanda's face. "Agatha sent him away to protect him from you. You who used the Darkhold to massacre hundreds in different realities because you didn't think to get therapy." "How is Agatha any different?"

    Death scoffed, a manic grin stretching across her cheeks. "I never said she wasn't. That was you, little Miss Perfect." She punched the woman through a door. With a swirling hand, wind twirled the witch around in a miniature tornado. "If you want to compare yourself to anyone, compare yourself to me. I have all the time in the world, baby."     Rio whirled around, face fleshing out, before facing the small child who couldn't really be there. She took in a shaky breath, a hand reaching out towards the phantom. He had no soul. He was just another one of Billy's tricks. That didn't mean she didn't miss her son. Rio dropped to a knee, waving him over. "Nicky? Nicky, have you seen your Mama?" The little boy tilted his head to the side. "Why are you crying, Mother? Did you miss me? We saw each other not too long ago."

    The cosmic entity pressed her clasped hands to her chest with an unsteady laugh. "I always miss you, querido. Always."

    Nicky walked forward, his little hands reaching for her face. It was an endearing gesture he'd picked up from his mama. "I miss you, too, Mother." He kissed her forehead, solid and cruel. "Can we go play?"

    Death shook her head. "No, cariño." She stood, waving her hand over him. "Te veo, querido. Te quiero mucho." His form dissipated as she disrupted the magic that made the figment. Wanda sniffled behind her. "I'm sorry. Maybe together we can-"

    Death tackled her to the ground, swinging her blade down with a shout. A hand stopped hers, but she sensed no soul. Another figment of Billy's imagination had come to disrupt her plans. This time, the person was just as cruel as the last.

    "Now, that's not very nice," a young Agatha laughed. She tugged Death away from her victim, a smile playing on her lips. "You're gone for weeks, and you don't even bother to greet your wife with a kiss." The witch leaned forward, placing her lips to Death's. The immortal was more willing to let this imposter distract her if only to see her wife's face one more time. She stumbled along, her eyes drinking in the gentle features of a woman long gone. "Agatha...Kiss me again," she pleaded. "Just one more time. Tell me you love me. Anything. I'll take anything."

    Wanda used the opportunity to slip away and resume her search for her sons. Death didn't care. She was perfectly fine with playing out this fantasy for a few more minutes. Especially now that those blue eyes were showering her with pure, unbridled love. Her wife, so beautiful, so gentle. Warm hands cupping her ivory cheeks as if their world wasn't ending around them. As if she weren't gone.

    Agatha kissed her nose with butterfly kisses. Quick but full of so much adoration it brought Death to her knees. The hallucination only smiled and held her close. Her fingers eased back her widow's shroud to card fingers through her hair. Death closed her eyes and leaned into the touch.

    Billy stumbled along with Jen, eyes scanning the rooms wildly. He could hear the sound of fighting and figured Rio had found Wanda, or vice versa. He didn't really care. The teen followed his covenmate around a corner and skidded to a halt.

    The Kaplan's were talking to Alice.

    "Billy, Jen," the witch greeted. "How've you guys been? I haven't seen you in ages. You're looking good, kid."

    The Maximoff approached her cautiously, but Jen launched herself at the other woman. "How are you here? You..."

    "Alice," Jen sobbed. "Alice, I'm so sorry. I should have done more to..." She shook her head, hugging the younger witch more tightly. "I'm just glad you're back."

    Billy looked to his parents. "Where's Teddy?"

    "He stepped into that room," his mother told him. "He's talking to an older lady. She was a bit all over the place."

    The teen entered the room, his parents following behind him. He gasped as the woman looked up with a smile.

    "Hey, Teen. It's been a while." She patted the seat next to her. "Let's have a quick chat before we all have to go back, shall we?"

    Billy sat before briefly poking her. He shook his head as his eyes widened. "I don't understand. You and Alice...you guys are dead."

    "Yeah, we are," Lilia confirmed. "But, I think you pulled our consciousness out of our bodies. Who the hell knows? You've got a knack for giving us grief, kiddo." She smiled at him, winking. "Got yourself in quite the pickle, haven't you?"

    Billy nodded. "Agatha's my mom. My other mom, Wanda, is here to take me away from my family. This is my other, other mom," he said, pointing to Rebecca Kaplan. "And my dad. Oh, and Rio's trying to kill me again."

    Lilia nodded. "That's usually how it goes when you're a witch. The Road is wild and wicked, my friend." She took his hand in hers. "Teen, you've just got to stay strong." Lilia sipped from a cup of tea. "I need you to know that I don't blame you for what happened to me. I'm sure Alice doesn't either, but I won't speak for her."

    "But you should," he told her hoarsely. "If I hadn't gone looking for answers, you would all still be alive. Agatha would be..." He dropped his face into his hands. "I've screwed everything up. Rio's right."

    "Don't listen to that bone head," Lilia told him. "Agatha Harkness has always known the risks and consequences of every action she has ever taken. She knew what she was getting into when she took you under her wing. Rio's just hurting. I can't imagine Death taking the loss of her wife well in any capacity."

    "She's not," he laughed. "I'm starting to think Agatha was her only reason for living." The older woman sighed, a smile sent in his direction. "Rio loves you, too. She just loved Agatha more. But, if you want to stop her reign of terror, you're gonna have to talk to her." A little boy entered the room before crawling into Lilia's lap. "My mother didn't want to play with me, so I sent fake Mama to talk to her."

    "Nicky!"

    Jen and Alice popped their head in, eyes wide. "That's who that is?" Alice said, mouth falling open.

    The child smiled brightly. "Wow! Mama must have talked about me a lot." He looked up at Lilia. "I can't wait to see her."

    Billy swallowed thickly, the vestiges of Rio's pain still fresh in his mind. "Nicky, where is your Mama? Is she here?" He started to look around for his mentor.

    Nicky shook his head. "I haven't seen Mama sent I went with Mother to go home. She must still be killing witches to survive."

    "Uh...." Jen made a face, eyes narrowing. "Are we just gonna ignore what he said, or...?" Billy dropped down to his knees, taking his brother's hand. "Nicky...Nicky, your Mama loves you so, so much! She thinks about you all the time. She never stopped." The child grinned impossibly wider. "Thanks, Billy! Mama loves you a lot, too." The teen blinked. "How...?"

    "Mother tells me about you sometimes. When she gets a chance, she talks about how much you and Mama like to play fight. How Mama misses me, so she does her best to take care of you so you won't miss her when she comes home. I think it's cool I have two more brothers! We could play so many games," Nicky said, his eyes alight.

    Billy hugged him, tears falling onto the child's back. "I think it's cool to have another brother, too." He squeezed his eyes shut. This moment should have been Agatha's. He let his brother go, smiling at him warmly. "Say, do you know where our other brother is? I need to find him before your mother does. We're playing a game right now."

    Nicky nodded. "Grandma 'Lia, can we go see Tommy now? I wanna have a group hug." "Sure thing, kid." She looked at the group. "Isn't he the sweetest? No idea how this came outta Agatha, but I'll take it."

    Billy gave her a tight grin before waving his family along. "Let's go get Tommy." Chapter End Notes Me, pursing my lips like Agatha: I do have a tendency to...kill my blorbos Any of my seasoned readers: 🥲 please stop My Blood, My Tears, My Bone Chapter Summary The fight for Tommy continues.

    Chapter Notes Mmm, all of your tears and pain were very delicious. Thank you for the rejuvination. 😈 See the end of the chapter for more notes Death pressed kisses to Fake Agatha's neck, desperate for one last taste of her wife. Her fingers raked along the illusions back, drawing out a breathy moan. Fake Agatha clung to her, pressing her form against Death's. The imposter certainly responded and tasted the same way her wife did. There just wasn't that beautiful soul humming in contentment that Death was so used to. She found she missed that more than Agatha's face.

    The cosmic entity knew she ought to move on from this sad fantasy if she wanted to avenge her wife. But if she left this Agatha, it would truly be the last time seeing her beloved witch. Death figured a few more minutes would be fine. Even if the others found Tommy, they'd never be able to outrun her. That much, she was certain of. For now, she'd abuse Billy's magic to find the closure she needed. Well, as close as one could find. Not that she was going to walk away from the hallucination. No, no. Death was going to get Agatha out of her system one way or another.

    Death backed the woman against a wall, hands grasping soft flesh. Agatha laughed lightly, breathily. Her warm hands settled on Death's shoulders.

    "What's the occasion, my love? Did you miss me that bad?"

    Rio looked up at her, locking her hazel eyes with blue eyes. "Don't you know that I always miss you, Agatha." She stroked a cheek. "Every day I'm with you is a special occasion." She pressed her lips to the other woman's, her dead heart clenching in pain. "Don't leave me," Death pleaded. "Let's just stay here."

    Agatha tilted Rio's chin, her eyes twinkling. "I've never left you," she reminded. "You're the one who's always leaving me alone. If I could go with you, you know I would." Death licked her lips. "Come with me?" she asked. (The first time she'd ever said those three words aloud and it wasn't even to the real deal. How pathetic was she?) Her hazel eyes searched the made-up woman's face, still expecting an answer.

    "Rio," Agatha breathed. "You'll have to let me go at some point. You've still got work to do." The witch laughed softly, but no air hit Death's face. "Are you really going to run and hide? That's something I'd do. That's not you, Rio."

    "I can't live without you," she whispered. "Don't make me leave." Death pressed her forehead to Agatha's. "Even if you're just a piece of Billy, I'd still listen to you. Tell me to stop. Tell me to turn around and never come back. I'd do it for you. Always for you." Agatha stroked her hair, a gentle hum in the back of her throat. "You weren't there for her after Nicky died," the figment said, breaking the illusion. "But you can be there for Billy. He'll need guidance now that she's gone."

    Death gripped at the other woman as Agatha's form started to fade. "Will I ever see you again?"

    "This me? Heavens no!" The illusion laughed. "I'm not real. Never was. But you knew that." "Aggie, please!" She clawed at the vision of her wife. "Don't leave me. Don't leave me!" "Death isn't always the end of something," Agatha said before disappearing entirely. Death roared her anguish into the world around her. Her dead heart, a lump of obsidian, refused to beat. The Maximoff's would pay.

    Billy stopped as a wail echoed through the building. It shook the walls and rattled the glass. "We better hurry up. I think Rio's even more pissed."

    "What's 'pissed' mean?" Nicky asked him.

    "Uh...forget I said that, okay? Your mother and mama would kill me." Billy scooped the child into his arms. "Right or left, Nicky?"

    "Right," the boy informed. "Is Mother losing the game?"

    "Not sure," he told the child. "But if we don't win, nobody will." Billy found a door and pushed it open. It looked like a sitting room with plush couches and many hung photographs. Billy skidded to a halt with a grimace. "Oh...hey Mom," he said with a nervous laugh. The teen quickly pushed his anxiety away in favor of anger. After all, she was the one who kick- started Rio's rampage. She was the one who had stolen his mentor's mother's life. Wanda pressed a hand to her mouth. Tears began to well in her eyes. She took a step towards him only for Jen and Teddy to block her from him. The witch jerked back, shaking her head. "Billy, I would never hurt you," she told him. "I love you."

    "You killed Agatha," he spat, shaking. "How could you? She was harmless." The Scarlet Witch wrung her hands, tilting her head imploringly. When he made no effort to have Jen and Teddy move, she sniffled. Wanda tilted her head back with a small laugh. "I know you don't remember me, so you probably don't remember Agatha very well, either. But she kidnapped you and your brother and tried to kill me. She..." Wanda laughed again, shaking her head. "She even killed your dog. Your dog, Billy! What about her sounds safe?" Billy didn't know what to do about the dog bit, so he focused on the more important aspect of their conversation. "You're the one who let her babysit us. She was always around us from what she's told me. How was that safe?"

    "I didn't know she wasn't under my spell," Wanda huffed. "Billy, please! Just give me a chance to prove that I do love you. I haven't stopped. Not even when everyone else told me you were never real."

    "Then why didn't you come get me the second the hex was gone? I grew up not knowing who I was or why I was different for three years," he argued. "You abandoned me." Wanda wiped at her face as more tears fell. "I never knew you survived! I lost myself to the Darkhold and tore through the Universe looking for you and your brother. The darkness that consumed me was so bad that the other versions of you and Tommy were petrified. That's why I..." She looked away, hands clasped tightly. "That's why I destroyed all the copies and myself. I followed Death to the afterlife in hopes of seeing you and your brother again. But then I heard you in the Realm of the Living. I came back as soon as I could. I promise." Nicky hugged himself to Billy tightly. "I don't like that book. Mother says it's a bad book that makes people do bad things. Mama had it, and it made Mother very sad." The teen shuffled in place. It didn't seem like Wanda had any intent on hurting anybody. The 'fit of rage' Jen had been talking about must have been her attempt to find him and Tommy. Maybe there wasn't any cause for concern after all. Except there was. Agatha was still dead, and Wanda was still the person who killed her. Then there was the matter of... "Oh, Billy~," Rio sang from the doorway. She drug her knife along the wood of the cabin, her true form present once more. Wind filled the room, whipping her shroud around her in a violent frenzy. The calm hazel eyes of yesterday, the unwavering gaze used for Agatha, were lost to the madness and grief the immortal had fallen prey to. Her outfit, always so put together, was now in tatters from their previous fight. Death scanned the room with a calm, chilling laugh. "I see you've decided to play a new type of make-believe. Really improved on your mother's methods." The Green Witch tilted her head downwards to glare at him. "You decided to make puppets of my family and your coven. It's sick!" She threw a gust of wind in his direction with a laugh.

    Billy tucked and rolled, a hand cradling Nicky's head. "I've got you," he told his brother. The others were knocked over and pushed away from him. His parents scrambled for cover behind couch. Teddy lobbed a lamp at Rio with a quick, "Sorry!" The woman didn't take too kindly and turned the couch over.

    "Great! Only two of us have magic, and we just happen to be up against two of the most powerful witches in existence," Jen groaned. She threw a spell at Wanda before urging the group to find a corner. She threw up a shield before moving to press her back to Billy's. The Green Witch scoffed. "Don't worry, Jenny. The whole world's gonna be in flames. I'm just gonna see to you guys first," Rio growled.

    "Rio," Lilia began, "you have to calm down. You're scaring Nicky."

    Death rounded on her, a smirk darkening her features. "Don't bring my son into this, you kook. I'll run you through a second time." She pointed at Billy and Nicky. "I'll start with you first for using the memory of my child as a shield."

    "Mother," Nicky whimpered. "What happened to your face? Did you get hurt?" He wriggled around in Billy's arm, his hands reaching out for his mother.

    "Rio, it's really your son," Billy rushed to explain. "Just...just put that face away. I'll go with you. Leave everybody else alone, and I'll go with you. You...you can torture me for everything. Just don't scare Nicky."

    Death cackled before licking her blade. "That boy doesn't have a soul. None of them do." Blood dripped to the floor, black and stagnant. "They're not real, you stupid boy. You made them to torment me!"

    Billy looked at the others for help. "Mom, take Nicky." He handed his brother over to Rebecca. "Jen, protect Teddy and the others." The teen summoned up his magic. At least Agatha had taught him the basics for defensive blows and blocks. "I know you're mad, and you have every right to be. I hurt Agatha, and I've hurt you. But you can't do this. You can't destroy the world just because it hurts."

    "Watch me," Rio hissed, a green glow emanating from her.

    Wanda lowered to stand behind Billy. "You can't have him," she argued. "Not him. Not Tommy. Not ever again."

    "I'll deal with you later, Wife Stealer. I've been dying to sink my dagger into the kid long enough." Rio charged at them, but the Scarlet Witch used a spell to throw her up into the air. Death turned herself with a breeze before diving down towards them.

    Billy formed a shield, barely managing to keep the blade from stabbing his mother. He was starting to regret not entertaining Agatha's idea of making Rio his sparring partner. He could feel a headache forming. "We don't have to fight," he groaned as he focused on keeping the spell active. "I miss her too. I'm always going to miss her."

    "Mother, stop," Nicky shouted. Rebecca held him tightly in her arms, shushing him gently. He kicked at the woman. "Don't be mean to my brother. I'm gonna tell Mama!" Rio sneered at Billy. "Where do you get off? It wasn't enough living our memories, you had to recreate them, too. Had to rub my dead son in my face!" She shattered his shield by headbutting the blue wall. Her dagger nicked his right arm, causing him to hiss. Rio pulled back for another attack. Wanda caught her hand with a spell, holding the arm back as Death leaned in closer. "You're cruel, William Maximoff. You took after Agatha in the worst way. Nothing is sacred with you. Nothing!"

    Billy tried to get away from her as her hot tears dripped onto his face. "He's real," he told her, voice shaking. "I swear, they all are. I keep trying to tell you. If you would just listen." Wanda groaned as Rio exerted more force to grab him. "Run, Billy. I'll hold her off." "I'd listen to your mommy, Billy." Death turned, flinging Wanda into a table. Rio faced him again, blood and tears staining her ivory face in a nightmarish combo. "Never mind. We can play now." She grabbed his legs and threw him out into the hallway.

    "Mother-!"

    "QQQUUUIIIEEETTT!" Death twisted a wrist, sealing the group inside of the room. Billy ran down the hall, leading her further away from the others. The blood in his ears drowned out the sound of his footsteps. His magic twisted and turned the cabin into a giant labyrinth. He knew he didn't stand much of a chance against her on his own, but at least the others wouldn't get hurt in the process. (No wonder Agatha had sent him away. Being the hero was so much more stressful with an audience.) Billy turned into a room and nearly wept with joy. It was a bedroom with minimal furniture and a singular window. A prison cell if he had ever seen one. A lone figure sat on the bed facing the sunlight.

    "Tommy?"

    "Billy?"

    The brothers ran to each other, sharing a hug. They looked at each other, surprised at how similar they looked. Tommy, at least, still had straight blonde hair. Billy wanted to ask him so many questions. Wanted to tell him all the craziness of his life. Wanted to warn him they were about to face another witch in the middle of a mental breakdown. He wasn't given the chance as Rio appeared in the doorway.

    "Isn't that sweet?" Death snarked. "Now I can crush two little Maximoff's with one stone." She blocked the doorway with her body. The three stared at one another, waiting to see who would move first. Ultimately, it was Rio. She snarled as threw her knife at the brothers. Dark, shadowy tendrils of her death magic appearing like smoke from a fire.

    Time seemed to slow for the teen. His mind raced, thoughts buzzing for a solution. His eyes widened as he recalled how Agatha had blocked Rio's dagger during her fight with Death. He quickly formed a small shield of magic between his palms and held it like a tray. He nearly wept with joy as the black blade bounced away and skidded to a stop. Then, he remembered that Agatha had to make a mad dash to grab it before Death did. "Tommy, the dagger!" His brother sped over and back. "Now what?"

    "I don't need that to kill you," Death laughed. She took a step towards them with a predatory look. "I'm going to- ugh!"

    Red magic blasted the door into Rio's back, sending her to the floor with a growl. Wanda waved them over to her. She kept her foot firmly planted on the door to keep the Green Witch down. "Come on, boys. We need to get you out of here."

    "I'm confused," Tommy whispered.

    "No time. We've gotta go." Billy pushed him towards Wanda. He grabbed her arm and pulled the woman along with him. "I don't know if I trust you, but at least you're not trying to kill me."

    "I'll take it," Wanda breathed. She turned to backwards, guarding the twins' backs. "I don't know if I can beat her, Billy, but I'll try."

    He shook his head. "No one can beat her. Agatha didn't even bother to try. Not really. If she couldn't get Death to stop, no one can. Maybe if you try to talk to-"

    Billy yelped as he was yanked into a room. His legs were swept out from under him, his back colliding with the ground. He swallowed thickly as Rio stood over him. She pressed her foot down on his chest as she leaned down to taunt him. The teen squirmed under the uncomfortable amount of pressure that kept his lungs from expanding properly. "That's not true, William. Agatha did stop me. She just had to die first." Death freed him just to pick him up and throw him into a cabinet. "That was all you, Billy. Always you." She threw him over into a kitchen area.

    Billy ducked behind the center island with a pant. "I never wanted her to die," he explained. "I just wanted her to convince you not to kill me." The teen risked his neck to sneak a peek at her. "You know she wouldn't want this." He yelped as a cookbook was flung at his head. Death glowered from the other side of the island. She ripped the counter out of the floor and tossed it aside as if it were nothing. "The funny thing is, I would have loved you like my own if you had just stopped running your damn mouth. But no! William Maximoff likes to play Judge and Jury." Rio began to pelt him with kitchen objects her magic found. (For whatever reason, she didn't use anything sharp and heavy. So, that was a plus...) "I watched you, Billy. Every step of the way, you had to be cruel to her like her mother had been. I was just waiting for you to tie her to a stake and set her ablaze."

    He held his head as he scrambled to safety. Billy imagined the room as empty and unfurnished. The objects disappeared, disappointing Death in the process. He stood to face her, glowing fists raised. "I'm sorry, Rio. I don't know what else to say. I don't know why my magic did that to her. It was all an accident. The memories. Everything!" She pounced on top of him, hands wrapping around his throat. "You thought I'd forget everything you did just because you experienced me having to take my son? Or that I'd forgive you for making my wife cry because you started leaning into her maternal gestures? Was that it, Billy?" More tears splashed on the teen's face as he struggled to get her off of him. Death laughed; head thrown back. "Funny thing is, I did. Yeah, I did. I forgave you against my better judgement. For her." Her hands loosened before she removed them entirely. She slid away, collapsing on the floor with a sob. "You're too much like her, Billy. You're just...too much." Rio curled in on herself, her cries muffled by her hands. The teen lay there for a moment, eyes staring straight up at the ceiling as he sucked in lungful after lungful of air. Once his heart had settled, he rolled over to face Rio. She had quieted, but her shoulders still shook with intermittent hiccups. Billy didn't need to enter her memories to know just how grief-stricken the immortal was feeling. He missed Agatha, he did, but he knew he would never understand the level of love and understanding the two had shared. If he wasn't so battered, he'd crawl over to comfort her. The pounding in his head and the ache of his back won out, unfortunately, so he tried something different.

    "It was because of you that I gave her another chance," Billy told her. "You were willing to, so I figured I should try. I mean, she was awful to you. And you were awful to her. Your way of saying 'hi' consisted of trying to slit her throat. But if you two could forgive each other, why couldn't I?" He shifted and hissed when glass sliced bruised skin. "That's why I started to get defensive on her behalf. She's better than she thinks she is, and you were the only other person who was willing to see that. I guess I wanted that back for you, and for myself." Billy huffed out a laugh. "I guess...I guess a part of me always knew she was my mother. But I would have never helped her if you hadn't taken that first step. You reached out when she was too scared to face you herself. You were always patient even though you had every right to be mad." He turned to look at her, offering her a small smile. "I admire you for that." Death looked at him, eyes bright red. "Billy, I'm-"

    Footsteps crunched along broken glass and splintered wood. Both of them stilled, their eyes widening. Did Wanda have a change of heart?

    "What the hell happened over here?"

    The witch and warlock sat up. They scrambled to stand as they took the stranger in. Whoever she was, she was practically glowing. Billy didn't know who she was, or why she had suddenly appeared in his hex. He shared a look with Death.

    "Rio," a woman suspiciously similar to Agatha hissed. "What the fuck did you do this time? You've got the Ancient Ones breathing down my neck because of you." The woman walked over, her brown hair bouncing slightly. The silver streak caught the light as she passed a faux window. The woman stopped a few feet away from the bloodied pair. Her dress was a sore thumb in the chaos of the room. The young maiden furrowed her brows, the gesture unsettlingly familiar. "Billy, are you okay? You've got a nasty bump on your head. " He stared up at her, mouth opening and closing. "...Who...are you?"
