    The woman gasped dramatically, a hand pressed to her purple-clad chest. "Geez, I know I've been gone for a hot minute, but not that long." She looked over at Rio. "What? Cat got your tongue, Hot Stuff? You look like shit."

    Death threw herself at the stranger, lips pressing against the maiden's in a heated kiss. "You were gone," she whimpered. "You left me."

    The auburn woman thumbed away fresh tears with a sad smile. "I know, my love, but I didn't want you to see me get smashed up. Not exactly a flattering way to go." Realization hit the teen like a sack of bricks. "Agatha!?" Billy was quick to shove Rio to the side to squeeze his mother. "But...but..."

    "Oh, brother! Spit it out already, kid," the witch grumbled. Her steel-grey eyes twinkled in the light. She seemed to have almost entirely new features. Then again, she had a body after being a Halloween decoration. He much preferred her alive with flesh and blood than a heap of trash.

    "You died! Everyone said you were gone," he rushed to say. Billy gripped her hands, squeezing them to prove she was real.

    "And they were right. I did die, and I wasn't supposed to come back. But, I met with some of my old flings and now I'm here." Agatha posed for the two. "What're we thinking? Too showy? I can age myself up a bit if I need to. The silver streak doesn't go away. Trust me, I've tried. I spent ten minutes in the bathroom down the hall just trying to get rid of it. Damn thing's more stubborn than Rio. I'll get used to it, though. Makes me distinguished." Agatha sent Rio a wink.

    Billy scratched his head, brows furrowed. "I need a minute."

    "Billy! Billy, where are you?" Rebecca yelled from the hallway.

    Rio hissed through her teeth. "Oof. This is gonna be awkward."

    The witch sighed heavily, hands gesticulating her frustration. "Why Rio? Why is it gonna be awkward?" Agatha slumped her shoulders. The trio caught the glare Rebecca sent in Death's direction. Agatha turned back to Rio with crossed arms. "What did you do?" Death scoffed and sheathed her dagger. "It was a little bit of everybody, to be honest. It wasn't just me this time. Wanda started it, though." She clung to Agatha's side, fingers digging into the folds of the violet dress.

    Agatha fixed her with a look as the rest of the group filed into the kitchen. She turned to face the wide-eyed faces filing in. "Hey guys," she greeted with a wave. "They're not being very helpful, so tell me what you think? Too young? Too old? Just right?"

    "Who's this?" Rebecca asked Billy.

    "I think...this is Agatha," he told everyone slowly.

    The witch rolled her eyes. "You think? Gah! You're gone for a day or two and they all act like they've never seen you before." Agatha turned to make a face before doing a double-take. "Nicholas?"

    Billy winced. "It's, uh, really him," he told her. "I sorta pulled their spirits here. I'm not too sure how I did it."

    "You never do," she mumbled loud enough for him to hear.

    Rio hissed before scuffing a toe against the glass on the floor. She put her hands behind her back, head lowered in shame. "Whoops..."

    The teen threw himself back on the ground with a huff.

    Agatha slowly approached her son, a tight grin twitching her lips upwards. (Less than an hour and her body was already sweating profusely and not in the fun way.) She took him in, breath catching in her throat. He looked so very much like he did the last time she saw him, but with much more defined features. She swallowed thickly as she stopped in front of him. "Nicky, darling, is that you?"

    The young boy nodded carefully. "You look funny, Mama. I like your dress, though." "I know," she laughed. She carefully extracted him from Rebecca's arm. "You look..." Agatha cleared her throat, her new eyes misting over. "You look as beautiful as ever." He giggled with a blush. "I've been waiting a long time to see you. Mother said you were busy. Were you killing more witches?"

    "I was," she told him gently. "Busy, that is." Agatha would talk about her side hustle at a later time. "Mama made a lot of mistakes over the years. Could you ever forgive me?" Nicky pressed his face into her neck, hugging her tightly. " 'Course, Mama." He pulled back to look at her, those hauntingly dark circles no longer around his eyes. "Are you and Mother still fighting?"

    Agatha laughed, brushing his hair out of his face. "Not anymore, Nicky. Your mother and I are just bad at talking. I'm sorry you didn't get to spend more time with the both of us." She pressed a kiss to his face. "I've missed you so much. I'm sorry I never went to see you. I just...I couldn't."

    "Billy told me you missed me. And Mother said you were too sad to come say 'hi'. She said if you did, you'd never want to leave. How come?"

    Agatha snuck a glance at her wife. Rio seemed to be frozen in place, her eyes gaunt with obvious tear tracks. "The truth is, I was too scared to see you. I wasted our time together on silly things like killing witches. I should have focused more on spending time with you and letting you sing to people as much as you wanted. I thought you wouldn't want to see me after I...after I went too far."

    Nicky repeated her gesture and fixed her hair. "I want to see you all the time, but Mother said I had to wait. You could only visit when it was 'your time' or whatever that means. But now you have to stay. You've gotta take good care of my brothers." He waved to Billy and Tommy. "Now that I got to see you, I'm gonna see if Mother will let me go on my next adventure. I was gonna wait for you so we could go together, but I'm a big boy. I'll go by myself."

    Agatha sniffed loudly, tears streaming down her face. He wanted to reincarnate without her? Why? "You...Are you sure? Maybe Billy and Wanda can-?"

    A small hand covered her mouth. "Mama, I made you real sad all the time. Mother said it wasn't my fault, but I know it was. If I go on the Big Adventure, I can make you happy. I'll be happy for the both of us, and maybe you'll start to feel happy too." He hugged her again, his curls tickling her nose. "I love you, Mama, but you have to let me go." Agatha held him tightly as she openly wept. "I don't know if I can, Nicky. I love you too much."

    His fingers brushed away her tears. "It's okay, Mama. Don't cry."

    Billy stepped forward, clearing his throat. "You know, if you let me and Wanda work a little bit of our magic, we can play all the games we want." He gestured for the Scarlet Witch to join them. "You don't have to go anywhere to make your mama and mother happy. You can stay."

    Wanda wiped tears from her face with a quiet 'sorry'. "I'm not sure how we would..." "All you need to do is make him a body. Billy can reattach Nicky's soul to it. His magic will bend the rules, and I won't have to take him." Rio shuffled over, eyes downcast. "I don't even need to take his or Tommy's because of his magic, so it should work."

    "You chased us and threw them all over the place for nothing," Jen growled. "We were scared for our lives, you asshole!"

    "I can still take your soul if you'd like," Rio growled.

    "Settle down," Agatha told them. "So, what do you think, Nicky? Wanna give it another try?" She held her breath as her son thought long and hard. Smart boy. He'd listened to his Mama well over the years. Her new heart really started to pump as the seconds ticked by. Nicky slowly turned his head from Rio to her, a smile lazily growing. "Okay! But can we please stop killing witches?" he asked his mother. "Oh, and can we stop sleeping outside? It gets cold a lot."

    Agatha laughed. She broke out into a wide grin. "Love, I've got a bed with your name on it. As for the witches bit...." She shrugged with a grimace. "No promises. Mama made a deal with some people to come back here. There's no telling what they'll put me up to." Rio gave her a look. "Well, let's just get him in a body before the hex collapses. I know how inconvenient your magic likes to be," she told Billy.

    "I love you, too, Rio," the teen sighed. "Thanks for not killing me."

    "Don't push your luck," she warned. Still, Rio flicked a curl with a smirk. At least she didn't look five seconds from keeling over.

    Agatha looked back at her other covenmates. She pointed to Lilia and Alice. "Do you guys wanna get in on the action or...?"

    Lilia waved the offer off. "I'd love to, but I've seen enough of your wife to last several lifetimes. You just take good care of those boys. If not, I'll haunt you." She rolled her eyes at the woman, but didn't bother hiding the smile on her face. "Alice?" The young woman shuffled around, eyes flitting over to the black-clad witch. "If it's okay with Rio..."

    Death shot her wife a look. "Sure, let's just open the floodgates and give bodies to everyone, why don't we! Not like I don't have a Sacred Balance or Natural Order to uphold." Agatha turned back to Alice. "That's the best 'go for it' you're gonna get kid. Go get in line." Rio walked over to her as Wanda took Nicky from Agatha's arms. She went back to clinging to her wife's arm. "What happened to you? Why didn't I sense your soul until the moment you walked through that door just now?"

    Agatha didn't miss the way Nicky skirted around Rio with wide eyes. She pulled her wife into the hallway, safe from prying eyes and eavesdropping ears. "We're gonna have a long chat about whatever that was. Now, you couldn't sense me because I really was gone. Like, gone gone," she told Rio honestly. "After Wanda dropped a house on me, it was just total darkness..."

    Chapter End Notes Help! I wanted to do the joke like Fietro (Fake Pietro in WandaVision), but Fake Agatha would be Fagatha 😭😂 Now, I brought Alice and Nicky back because they have a lot they can bring plot wise for Agatha, Rio, and Billy's growth. I've done some more analysis, and there's a lot that occured in the series I didn't think to touch on that I do. So, this fic will be going on for a little bit longer.

    Lilia, as I've said before, had a perfect arc. I will not be touching her development because it just feels wrong. Anywho! Hope you guys have enjoyed the emotional rollercoaster 🤠 If You Want Straight Answers...

    Chapter Summary Agatha takes charge. Rio likes that about her. Everyone else does not. Chapter Notes I didn't know that the Ancient One was an actual Marvel character when I wrote this chapter. So....enjoy what my brain cooked up before I learned this information 😂 See the end of the chapter for more notes Agatha floated in a sea of perpetual, inky darkness. It wasn't cold. It wasn't warm. She couldn't move, couldn't speak, couldn't even hear herself think. She just was. It was terribly boring.

    The witch was unsure how long she'd existed like that. She completely lost track of time after realizing she was far too lazy to count past ten. (Shut up, Billy!) Agatha was dead and stuck. It just .............................. .....................................................stretched on ........................................................................................................Forever.................................

    And then it didn't.

    As if she had blinked, the woman found herself standing in what could only be described as the Parthenon but not all busted up and in space. The Universe sprawled out like a dazzling garden of nebulae and stars outside of the columns. The temple stood immaculate as four cloaked women sat behind a desk. Agatha pursed her lips, looking around in confusion. She was expecting fire and brimstone, not...this. Not that she was complaining! No, no. Heavens no! She was just very, very, very disoriented and perplexed.

    "Agatha Harkness," the first Ancient One began. She had a thick, country accent that dripped with disdain. (Agatha was surprised a steel guitar didn't strum in the distance.) "I'd hoped to never see your face again, you vile thing." The woman removed her hood, a displeased look greeting the witch.

    "Dolly," Agatha laughed. She leaned forward, her eyes raking across the legend. "Long time, no see, indeed. You're looking good, girl. Still using press on nails, I see." "Not now you two," the second Ancient One groaned. This time, Agatha heard a raspy, smokey voice call on her. "You've got a nasty habit of playing with Death, don't you, Agatha?"

    "Eartha, baby," she greeted. The witch spread her arms with a grin. "You never called me back, hun. I didn't know you were on the payroll."

    Eartha shook her head but her smirk said the opposite. "It wouldn't have mattered anyway," she laughed.

    "Not with our Agatha," the third Ancient One said, her voice heavy with a thick accent. "Frida," Agatha groaned. "Now, there's a face I haven't seen in a while. How's it goin', darling? I'm still waiting to paint the fruits of your vine."

    The fourth Ancient One sighed heavily. "Are we going to get down to business or what? Some of us have other things to do than flirt?"

    "Oh, come on Betty. You're not still mad about Carol, are you? I swear, I never saw the invite. You know I would have gone on and put on quite the performance if I had," Agatha reasoned. "Say, where's Stevie?"

    "Concert," Dolly huffed.

    "Don't be like that, Doll. It was a harmless prank. You know I'm not into men." "We both know you were planning on sucking something else out of him," the woman growled.

    Agatha flipped her hair with a sniff. "He was being too showy with his magic. I couldn't let him threaten our safety, and I'm still not going to apologize for it." She put her hands on her hips. "So, what're we doing? I know Betty and you are in a foul mood, but I'm always down to party with my three lovely ladies." Agatha shot a wink at the center of the panel. "Well, since you can't seem to stay way from Lady Death, and her, you, we've decided to dole out a more appropriate punishment," Betty told her. She fluffed her curls in a mirror. "Right now, Lady Death is on a rampage because you're so dead even she can't reap you," Eartha began. "The Universe is on the brink of destruction."

    "So, to help persuade her to keep her dagger to herself, we're going to offer a proposition," Frida added. She grinned widely, her own eyes undressing Agatha. The Ancient One bit her lip with a groan.

    Dolly rolled her eyes. "We are willing to give you your life back, but you'll have to work for us permanently."

    "Like what? You want me to get you guys a coffee and massage your backs?" Agatha scoffed. "Not sure if my eternal existence is worth a life of servitude. I mean, have you seen how overworked Rio is? My wife needs a break, you guys!"

    "And we can arrange that if necessary." The curly-haired Ancient One rubbed her temples. "Agatha, we'd be willing to give you a station equal to Lady Death. You would, essentially, become the Triple Goddess to Death's Horned God," Betty sighed as if she wasn't entirely on board with the decision. She probably wasn't, but the Universe was literally in danger of burning to the ground. "We would have you oversee all witches in all capacities until the end of time, yada yada yada."

    The witch blinked, lips pursed. "You want to make mea cosmic being?" She couldn't help the grin that grew out of the wicked thoughts that blossomed.

    "Correct," Eartha told her. Her eyes twinkled mischievously. "Complete mastery of the craft, perfect for training the Demiurge and his mother. And you and Lady Death get to be together, or whatever."

    "Forgot about Billy, if I'm being honest." She hummed in thought, eyes narrowed. Agatha tapped her chin and was quick to ask, "Do I still have to be that shitty Party City skeleton?" "No," Dolly growled. "Just tell us your damn answer, woman. Some us have a signing at four and a gig at six."

    "Rawr," Agatha sent her, nose wrinkled. "Yeah, sure. Whatever. I'll do anything to get back to the kid and keep Rio from gutting the poor boy. I'm pretty sure she's trying her best to do that right now."

    Outside of the temple, a star exploded. It sent ripples through the fabric of time and space. Agatha found it beautiful, but she was pretty sure that wasn't supposed to happen based on the concerned looks settled on the Ancient Ones. The group returned to business with nervous laughs.

    "Come here, lovely," Frida purred. She crooked a finger at the witch, eyes dark. "Oh, lovely, is it?" The witch sauntered over with a charming grin. "Anything for you, sweetheart."

    Frida painted a gold rune over Agatha's heart. "Now, you will carry out your sacred duty according to our rules." She pressed a kiss to Agatha's lips with a moan. The woman pulled back with a hum. "You'll find Lady Death in Springfield, New Jersey."

    Agatha grinned like the cat that got the cream until she received her destination. Her good mood took a hit. "Ugh. They couldn't pick a better place to start the apocalypse." She blew a kiss to the panel. "Tell Stevie I said 'hi'. She still owes me a jacket, and I know just what I want." (Goddess, she missed her coat!)

    "Oh, tell her yourself," Betty grumbled. "Come on. Let's go see if I Love Lucy is on. Dolly, love, we'll see you for dinner."

    Agatha was dropped unceremoniously from the temple. She would have screamed, but honestly, she was just too tired to at this point. All she knew was Rio and Billy needed her, and Wanda was still hot on their trail. She'd have time to grapple with her new existence later.

    Rio glowered. "...You sold your soul to your exes to become the immortal ruler of magic?" Agatha pursed her lips. She twirled a strand of her hair, batting her eyelashes. "Were you not trying to kill my kids?"

    Death rolled her eyes. "I'm sorry," she huffed. "I was in the throes of grief, my love. Forgive me for not thinking clearly. Why don't you have your heart stop, and have your wife vanish on you for all eternity!" Rio blinked away angry tears and crossed her arms. The reformed witch cupped her wife's face before pressing a kiss to her nose. "I understand, Rio." She smiled, all teeth as she tightened her hold. "But if you ever try that shit again, I'll hog tie you and leave you in my basement."

    Death groaned at the thought, her anger quickly switching to lust. She pressed against her goddess with a soft whine. "Let's get out of here. I need you now!"

    "Ah, ah," Agatha tutted. "Consider the wait your punishment. What the hell happened with Nicky?"

    The Green Witch looked away, shrinking in on herself. She just had to ruin the moment. Rio snuck a glance at Agatha before lowering her gaze. "I scared him," she mumbled. Perhaps 'scared' wasn't the right word. Rio had terrified her son to the point of crying and worrying for her safety.

    "How?" Agatha pressed. She took Rio's hand to give it a squeeze. "Rio...how?" Death sniffled and blinked back tears. (By Agatha, would she ever stop crying?) She snuck a glance at the goddess and was met with look that held so much spite. (It didn't take much for her wife to regress, it seemed.) Rio scowled, ignoring the tears running down her face. "I thought he was fake, okay! He didn't have a soul, so I sent him away." Agatha pulled her wife into a hug, cradling the back of Rio's head.

    Death sunk into the embrace. She inhaled deeply and shakily. Her wife was starting to give her emotional whiplash. She gave it a week before things would start to go south. Rio ignored the sinking feeling in her gut and continued. "I went after Billy in my true form. Nicky happened to be with him. They..." She hiccupped, her breathing turning uneven. "They tried to warn me. Nicky was so scared and yelling at me. It was too much. You were both gone, so I...I yelled at him."

    "Oh, Rio," Agatha sighed. She squeezed her tightly. "It was an accident. He's not scared of you. He was scared of what you were doing. We'll explain it to him, together." She ran her fingers through Rio's hair, kisses pressed to the crown of Death's head. "It's gonna be okay. I'm here now."

    Rio risked her wife's ire for a second time. "I told Billy."

    The witch froze, taking the information in. "Okay...Okay...Well...We'll deal with that later." "Are you mad?" Rio already knew she wasn't. Agatha was scared. The boy had such a hold over her emotionally. Death wondered what would happen if Billy ever turned on her. How would Agatha Harkness react to having her love rejected? The Ancient Ones didn't really think things through, did they?

    "No, my love." Agatha thumbed away tears. She carefully cleaned her wife's dark, ruined make-up around those wounded hazel eyes. "Did he ask for specifics or...?" Rio laughed softly. "No. I told him so you would come back to beat my ass. But then you didn't."

    Agatha swallowed thickly. "I probably should have told you from the beginning. Faulty spells...they can't be fixed, remember? I was living on borrowed time. Worst kind of time, if you ask me." Her wife looked away, a dark thought shifting across her face like a shadow. She moved to pull away, to hide the hurt still present. It didn't matter that Nicky was back. Death clung to her, holding her in place. "Wanda reminded me, but I was too far gone by that point..."

    Agatha shrugged. "I had hoped Wanda would buy me some time, but I lost my patience with her."

    "It's my fault, too. I shouldn't have left you." Death practically climbed into her wife's arms. She was still so terrified the new immortal would slip away into nothingness. "Nah, don't worry about that. I finally tricked you good," the new immortal laughed. She tugged her sad, little cosmic entity towards the kitchen.

    The Green Witch kept herself firmly planted in the hallway. "I don't know if I want to go see everybody," Rio mumbled. "They're going to be very pissed with me."

    Agatha tilted her chin up. "That's a first for you." She ran a thumb along Rio's bottom lip with a teasing smirk. "They'll have to get through me. I'll take any excuse to try my new magic." She used her free hand to spark purple around them, delighting at the sensation. "I've really missed that."

    Rio looked at Agatha as if she'd fashioned the Universe in that very moment. With those hands that never failed to tell you more about Agatha than the witch could ever do with words. Death loved it. Loved her. The words, "I missed you," tumbled out of her mouth before she could decrease the level of intimacy in them. Before she could make sure she didn't overwhelm her wife. She wasn't prepared for the response she got. "I missed you, too," Agatha whispered. She leaned in for a kiss, reveling in the sensation of her wife's lips after so long.

    The kiss quickly grew heated, hands running over every inch of one another. The goddess backed the cosmic entity against the nearest wall, her hands sliding down Rio's shoulders to her breasts. Death broke away with a moan that had Agatha biting her lip. Someone cleared their throat, ruining the moment.

    "Billy, I swear if that's you," Agatha growled. She turned and smirked. "Oh...Hello again, Wanda."

    Rio bit her shoulder, shooting the redhead a glare in the process. Damn Maximoff's... Agatha ignored the pain, her smirk widening. "Come to join us, hun?"

    Wanda's eyes widened, mouth opening and closing. She pointed towards the kitchen. "Your son and friend are...uh...They're...alive again." She looked away with a blush as Rio licked up the side of Agatha's neck. "Thought I'd tell you," Wanda said before running away. "You're being very naughty," Agatha laughed.

    "So punish me," Rio drawled with a rasp. "I'll even let you call me 'babygirl'." "I was going to call you that regardless." She stepped back and threw an impish grin on. The witch was back to her masks, it seemed. (Typical Agatha.) "Now, let's go see about kidnapping Tommy so we can get the hell out of here. I'm not keen on staying in a fourth hex, thank you very much!"

    The couple re-entered the room to find Nicky chatting away with his brothers. They shared a look, hearts clenching in sync. Agatha pulled Rio along until they were standing with the rest of the adults. The Green Witch crouched; a flower offered to the young boy. She'd grown his favorite: a buttercup variant that used to grow around the river he and Agatha had lived by. He took it but kept his distance from his mother. There was a look in his eyes that was so very much Agatha, Death nearly panicked at the sight. Years of neglect and barbed words pricking at her skin. She pushed past it. There would be time to cry later. "I didn't mean to scare you, Nicky," Rio began softly. "I couldn't find your Mama, so I lashed out. I never should have yelled at you. I'm sorry." She felt her face fall as her son pressed himself against Billy's side.

    Agatha bent down to wrap an arm around her wife's shoulders. "It was an accident, love. Your Mother's been through a lot since you last saw her. She tends to get very cranky now. Bit like you used to when you weren't feeling well."

    "You try working my job," Rio grumbled quietly.

    "I think I can have that arranged," Agatha mumbled in thought. "I'll talk to Frida later. Anyway, Nicky, we're both very sorry for everything. Your mothers need a stern talking to. Why don't you give us one?"

    Their son crossed his arms, face scrunching up in thought. He stepped away from Billy, his hands tugging at the lapels of his new jacket. (Much like Agatha, he found a mask to wear for this conversation.) "I think you two need to think about what you've done," he said, parroting an old lecture. "Naughty witches seldom survive. From now on, you have to talk to each other and...and you have to make me soup whenever I want!"

    "Very good," Agatha praised. He'd managed to work an angle into the equation. She was so proud! "Your mother and I will certainly do just that. How about we go home now? I'm actually very tired, and everyone looks terrible. Not you, though. You're still my darling little imp."

    The child preened. "I'm ready, Mama. I wanna feel a real bed."

    She laughed, scooping him up. "Give your mother a kiss. She feels very bad for scaring you." Nicky slipped into Rio's arms and pressed a kiss to her eyes. "It was an accident. Mama says we all make them sometimes." He rested his head on her shoulder, a yawn pulling at his face. "Okay, grab Tommy. Let's get the fuck outta here," Agatha told the group. "Head to my house. I'll meet you all there shortly."

    "The car kinda got thrown into the trees," Jen informed her.

    "Wanda can fix it," Agatha told her, waving the group off. "Start heading out. I'm not saving your asses if he drops the hex and you're still in here."

    "My spell," Billy said. "How do I stop it?"

    Agatha waved him over. She brushed his curls back with a gentle smile. "Hexes are the same as sigils. You destroy them when they're no longer needed. Now, if I were you, I'd wait until we're outside and away from the guards with guns before you shatter it. Unless you want to go home looking like Swiss cheese."

    Billy and Tommy shared a laugh. "Will you help me?" He looked at her expectantly. His dark eyes soft and gentle with all the trust in the world.

    Agatha gave him a tight grin. "Duh! You might be like Wanda and widen it if we're not careful."

    "You're already on thin ice," the woman reminded.

    "Good luck with that threat, hun. I'm immortal now," she said with a cackle. "Play nice and I won't seal you under a mountain."

    The group exited the cabin. Teddy talked at length with Tommy, telling him all the things Billy and him liked to do on the weekends. Jen and Alice copied the two, their heads bent towards each other as Jen filled the younger witch in on everything. The Kaplans and Wanda seemed to be on much better terms compared to their relationship with Agatha. Said witch walked with her son in her arms, not yet ready to put him back down.

    "Mama, where were we?" Nicky asked her.

    She huffed out a laugh. "Your mother and I had a cabin just like this, love. Billy remade it, didn't you?"

    The curly-haired teen grinned anxiously. "I just needed something to slow Rio down." "It's a very good replica, but let's not do that again. Nicky may be back, but the pain's still there." He had better be glad she didn't set the damn place on fire once she realized what he'd done.

    The curly-haired teen mumbled a 'sorry' with a small grin. "But he's back back," Billy told her. He shared a look with Rio who merely nodded in silence. "You get a second chance. Are you excited?"

    Agatha grinned widely. "I'm excited to have a second chance with everybody. But yes. I'm most excited to give him the childhood he deserves."

    "We're ready," Jen told the family unit. "We'll see you guys back in Westview." She glanced over at Rio as if waiting for her to say anything.

    Death hissed at her, hands forming claws.

    Jen booked it to the car.

    "I'd tell you to stop, but she did a terrible job at protecting Billy," Agatha laughed. "If you need to go get caught up, that's fine with me."

    "I do. I'll probably get summoned to the principal's office, too." Rio pulled her in for a kiss, brief but full of passion. A hand snuck out to ruffle Nicky's floppy hair. Death pulled back and snapped finger guns at Billy before slipping through the veil between realms. With Agatha's guidance, Billy slowly collapsed the hex in on itself. They watched as guards and the facility gradually reappeared. An alarm that had been going off for who knows how long filled the air. The incessant beeping was paired with a message that a prisoner had escaped. That was a cue if they ever needed one. The pair took to the skies, cloaked in a spell of Agatha's weaving. Nicky yawned a few more times, his little body exhausted from the day's events. He fell asleep within minutes. Agatha cradled him close to her. "You're improving," she praised, a proud grin sent in her other son's direction. "No deaths this time."

    "I've got a pretty good mentor," he told her. A blush adorned his cheeks as he looked away. "...When did you know?"

    Agatha instinctually felt the need to touch her brooch. With her hands full, she was forced to remember that she'd lost the piece of her mother when Wanda killed her. She pushed away the icky feeling she would get any time the item was missing. Nicky was alive and well. She didn't need it anymore. "I had a feeling when we first met. I never remembered your mother and I mixing magic, so I figured I was reading into things. Didn't stop me from caring, though. I enjoyed spending time with you and Tommy during Wanda's hex." She pursed her lips, letting him take in the information. "When did you know?"

    He turned to face her fully, expression so much like an amused Nicky, it nearly brought her to her knees. She had to remind herself, again, that Nicky was back. This wasn't tragic anymore. Billy touched his curls, fluffing them. "You were always strangely protective of me, but it was the night Rio said you would stroke my hair while I slept that..." He looked up, trying to find the right words. "It just made sense, I guess. It didn't fully click until she told everyone." Agatha winced. "Yeah...I was gonna try and tell you long after finding Tommy. Probably after you moved out of your parent's house to avoid the whole mess we're about to walk into." They landed in her backyard. Unlike Billy's home in Eastview, the yard was still immaculate. One of the many good things she'd returned to. Agatha cleared her throat as the two gave each other a look.

    Billy stepped closer to hug her tightly. He made sure to be careful with the sleeping child in her arms. "You left all of us, Agatha, but you hurt Rio the most."

    "I know. I just didn't expect her to react so...well, you know..."

    "She was pretty fucked up over you," he told her with a laugh. "But it gave Wanda a change of heart."

    "Yeah, I'm really, really not looking forward to the conversations we adults are going to have in a moment. We'll get it figured out, though. You just spend time with your brothers and Teddy."

    Billy nodded. "Let's go inside before they realize we've been standing here the whole time."

    Rio stood at the back door to Agatha's house, a full bouquet prepared for her wife. She hadn't felt this nervous since Agatha told her she was pregnant. Death changed out of her work clothes and into a simple sage green shirt with black shorts before entering the house. The smell of Agatha's magic hit her senses before the eerie silence did. The group had obviously waited for her to arrive before their little heart-to-heart. How unfortunate. She had been looking forward to fucking her wife into a coma right about now.

    Still, she greeted Agatha as she had in the past. A, "Honey, I'm home," entering the living room before she did. A genuine grin grew as her steel grey-eyed goddess bounded over to her to press a kiss to her lips. (By Agatha, she'd missed this!) Her wife wore a simple shirt and pants, looking very much like her Detective Agnes personality. She leaned into her wife, coaxing a moan from the woman at the thought of those heated looks they'd shared. (Oh yeah, they were definitely going to defile Agatha's home tonight.)

    "About time," Wanda huffed. She'd changed into regular street clothes. The woman looked nothing like the witch she'd tried to kill earlier.

    "Some of us have a job to do," she quipped, teeth flashing at the woman. Agatha pulled her along with a warning look. "Now, let's do this the correct way." The goddess sat and patted her lap with a sultry grin. "You didn't think I was going to sit in yours, did you?" She laughed lowly, stirring the fire already blazing in Death's soul. "Sit." Rio straddled Agatha's waist if only to make everyone else uncomfortable. "Whatever you say, amor." She turned her bouquet into a flower crown and placed it on her wife's head. "God, you two make me sick," Jen groaned. "It was bad enough when she was a ghost, but now!"

    "The other way," Agatha ordered.

    Death complied, making herself comfortable. She shot Wanda a look as she threw an arm over her wife's shoulder. "So...what're we doing?"

    It was Bearded Man who spoke up, visibly and deeply unsettled by the level of their affection. "We need to discuss everything that's happened. And we need to figure out what to do about Billy and Tommy."

    "Well, that's obvious," Wanda laughed. "My kids are coming with me."

    "I gave birth to Billy," Stock Image Woman told the Scarlet Witch. "He's staying with us." Rio grinned, enjoying the chaos. Mortals never learned to share, but she supposed she was just as bad when it came to Agatha. The Ancient Ones were going to regret flirting with her wife. She had a whole slew of pranks lined up for the three infamous womanizers. Death also had a plan to get back at Agatha, but that depended on how long the woman was going to make her wait before they went to her bedroom. She'd already scarred Nicky once. She didn't feel like doing it a second time.

    Agatha cleared her throat as she ran her fingers through Death's hair. (Rio wondered what her wife would do if she started moaning.) "I think all of you are being brats." She shifted so that she sat straighter. "None of you have even considered Billy and Tommy's feelings in the matter."

    The brothers looked to Agatha. Rio could see their souls shaking with apprehension. Her amusement gave way to irritation. "Not brats," she corrected. "Fools." She curled around her wife as angry eyes settled on the goddess. Rio slipped her hand under the collar of Agatha's V-neck to place it against a bare shoulder.

    Agatha hummed in agreement, ignoring the sensation in favor of chastising the adults. "You four, go upstairs and do something. The adults aren't mature enough to have you around, it seems. I'll call you back down when we're ready for you."

    "Who says you get to call the shots?" the IT Technician asked. He looked around the room for support.

    "I love you guys, but I'm going to listen to Agatha," Billy told the room. "She's the only one who's taken me into consideration." He sent the couple a nod. "Come on, Nicky. We can put on more Bluey," he told his little big brother.

    The Green Witch waved the teens and Nicky off, offering them a quick smile. The second they disappeared upstairs, though, Rio let a scowl settle over her features. She might have caused most of the trauma, but they were the ones who had pushed her and Agatha to that point. If they had just learned to listen to her wife, they could all be in bed right now. "Clearly, we've got a situation on our hands," Agatha told Wanda and the Kaplan's. "Billy can't be in three places at once. And even if he could, that doesn't mean he should." "He shouldn't go with you," Wanda told Agatha. "You're a serial killer." "And he always gets hurt when you're around him," the Female Kaplan added. Rio sneered at them. "Oh, 'cause you two are so much better," she mocked. "One of you is unable to control her emotions, and the other is annoying."

    Rebecca glared at her. "Better to be annoying than someone who tried to kill children." "My wife was dDdeEeaAadDd!" Rio jumped away from Agatha to snarl at the woman. "I can still burn the Universe down if I wanted to. Agatha is the only reason anyone gets to draw another breath. Do you understand me? You live because of her!"

    "That's very romantic, dear, but no one's burning anything down. You do that and the lovely ladies upstairs will revoke my immortality," Agatha reminded her. Her eyes had taken on that commanding look she reserved for play time. "My lap is cold."

    Death kept her eyes locked on Billy's would-be mother as she walked backwards to Agatha. She sat on her wife's knee, but kept her hand on her dagger this time. It was extremely effective.

    "Now, I'm no fool," Agatha continued. "Billy won't be staying with me because his body belongs to Rebecca and the Man. That, and I'll have my hands full with Nicky and Rio. He needs to be with someone boring to keep him humble."

    "Seriously?" Mr. Receding Hairline sighed.

    Rio bit back a laugh. She wasn't going to risk annoying her wife and lose kissy privileges. Not when she was this close to having the other woman sit on her face. No, Death kept quiet and waited until she was needed.

    "You're giving him up?" Wanda asked, an incredulous look on her face.

    "I'm not giving him up," Agatha laughed harshly. "He can live with the Kaplan's, but he'll come stay with us from time to time. See, I've got this new job now. It's gross, I know. But if I'm going to be a mentor to the masses, I'm going to need to create an academy of sorts. I mean, if Mundane Mind Guy gets to have one, I can too." She returned to running a hand through Rio's hair. "Wanda and Tommy will stay with me. I know she needs just as much help as Billy does. Tommy, the poor thing, doesn't need to be shuffled around. He's already had to deal with enough."

    "What about Crafty Kale and Alice?" Rio asked for fun.

    Jen shot her a look but Alice smiled brightly. (At least the protection witch hadn't fought her fate and used her time wisely. Rio supposed she had earned a second chance unlike Billy, Tommy, and Wanda.....Okay, and Agatha, too.)

    "She can come too, granted she doesn't turn on me again."

    "I didn't turn on you," the witch argued. "I just wasn't going to get involved on your behalf. I'll go wherever Billy goes."

    "Then you can come live in my mansion."

    "You have a mansion?" Alice asked. Poor thing was in a constant state of confusion now. "No, but I will with Wanda's help," Agatha laughed. "Does that sound reasonable with everybody?"

    Death listened to the mumbles but knew her wife's logic had won out. It was amazing what a bit of confidence and a beautiful face could accomplish with such a smooth-brained crowd. She turned to face her wife, ready to worship at her altar. "You're so hot when you get all commanding," she told her, breath coming in a pant.

    Agatha leaned forward, brushing her nose against Death's. She smiled against her lips before gifting Rio a kiss. Nothing that would get a crazy rise out of their audience, but enough to let the Green Witch know she was just as impatient. "Almost done," Agatha told her. "Behave." "I am," she growled out quietly. Rio had to fight so many inner demons to keep from stealing another kiss. Get through this and we can kiss her as much as she want, wherever we want, she reminded herself. Thankfully, the group had concurred with her incredibly smart goddess. Death preened.

    "Is there anything else we need to discuss before bringing the boys back down?" Agatha asked.

    "I have several," Wanda began. "How did Billy break my spell? How did you die? Why were you a ghost? How did you end up as a skeleton? How did you come back?" She raised her hands in confusion, head shaking. "I'm just...I'm still so confused. Also, if Lady Death didn't need to reap Billy and Tommy, why did she even try to begin with?"

    Rio was quick to defend herself. "If I couldn't have my wife, you weren't going to have your kids," she explained easily. "Speaking of, I may or may not have created several tears between the Afterlife and the Realm of the Living. The Ancient Ones are probably going to pin that on you, amor."

    Agatha waved the notion off with a chuckle. "If I bat my eyes and do a strip tease, I'll get ya off the hook, babygirl."

    Death should not have enjoyed the term as much as she did, but she couldn't help blushing at the thought. "I'm gonna fuck you right here if you don't hurry up," she warned. Blue eyes darkened quickly. Agatha cleared her throat. "You'll have to wait for a one-on-one, Wanda. My wife's very impatient right now, and I finally have a body." She sent the woman a wink. "Any and all women are welcome to join."

    "No they're not," Rio growled.

    "I think I actually hate it here," Man Kaplan told his wife. "Did we die in the car accident?" Death fumed. She turned to the Kaplan's with her true face. "That's a terrible thing to say. Your son is actually dead. Pull something like that again and I'll leave you two to rot when your time comes."

    "Wait...You're actually the embodiment of Death and that's your wife?" Rebecca asked. Rio laughed. "The skull didn't give it away for you?" Honestly! Why were mortals so thick at times? "Go get the boys," she ordered the woman. She delighted in the way William's mother scurried away. Maybe now she'd think twice about giving Agatha attitude. It wasn't long before Teddy, Billy, Tommy, and Nicky reappeared. Her son ran to her, jumping into her arms as Agatha announced the agreement she'd come up with. Death pressed kisses to her son's face, relishing in the fact that he was truly home now. He pressed his fingers to her face in quiet curiosity. "It doesn't hurt, querido." "It looked like you were hurt," Nicky told her. He pressed a kiss to her nose. "No. I was just sad and missing Mama," she told him. Rio fleshed her face back out, giving him a smile. "I'm much better now."

    Her son grinned, not a sign of pain or illness marring his soul. "Love you!" "Te quiero mucho, querido mio." She hugged him tightly, sneaking a glance in Agatha's direction. The goddess had a similar, misty-eyed look.

    Nicky pulled away to point at Billy. "Is that a bunny?" He ran over, excitement buzzing through his little body. "What's his name?"

    Rio watched as Billy crouched to be at the same level as Nicky. "This is Señor Scratch. He's actually your mama's familiar, but I was taking care of him while she was...away." Agatha tugged at her wife's chin, drawing her attention away. "You think I can convince Billy and Teddy to babysit for a few hours?"

    Death grinned, eyes dark with lust. "Only hours?" she teased. She walked her fingers up Agatha's arm. "I was thinking at least a day. Legs tangled, my face between your thighs. And now that you're an immortal, we can really go all out." Rio leaned in to whisper, "I brought you a leash."

    Agatha moaned, eyes sliding shut. "Everybody get the fuck out of my house," she instructed loudly and firmly.

    Billy laughed. "Wha-?"

    "I'm being so serious," the goddess told the room. "Get. Out. I've been patient long enough." Rio stepped behind her wife to wrap her arms around her middle. She brushed aside auburn locks to suck at Agatha's neck. It was the push everyone needed to rush for the front door. "Anything happens to my kids, and I'll steal your lungs," Agatha yelled after them. As the door slammed shut, she turned in Rio's arms. "Get on your knees," she breathed out, her hands pushing Death down to kneel.

    Chapter End Notes So...if I made an AAA discord server, would anyone want to join and just vibe? 👀 If so, I'll create a comment with the link.

    Work & Play Chapter Summary A fluff piece to prepare you for the horrors to come hehe Chapter Notes See the end of the chapter for notes The forest breathed with a gentle breeze, branches ruffling their leaves with a sigh. Insects of all kinds lazily milled about in the mid-spring afternoon. Their wings caught the thin, wispy rays of sunlight like glittering gems. Cool hands worked tirelessly at the damp soil as their owner rooted out fresh carrots. The witch was rewarded with a hearty bounty. Agatha sent a silent thanks to the Divine Mother for such a gift before setting them in her basket. She would have a cauldron of stew this evening.

    Agatha returned to her camp with a hum, swishing her skirts with a proud grin. There was nothing like a little manual labor to put her in a good mood. Nothing like being one with nature. Alone and unbothered by witchfolk and the like. She produced a sharp knife before chopping her washed carrots, potatoes, rabbit meat, and onion. They were dumped into the blackened pot filled with spiced broth. The fire cracked and popped as she stirred the ingredients together. All was right with the world.

    The witch slowed as the atmosphere became blanketed with a thick aura. The scent of fresh rain and damp soil washing over her. Agatha turned to face the source with a quirked brow. "Smells delicious," her visitor greeted. The green-clad witch stayed just outside Agatha's wards with a flower in her hands. She smiled sweetly, head tilting in amusement. This wasn't the first time the woman had appeared. And just like all the other times, the figure didn't seem to look any different. It was, however, the first time the beautiful maiden had commented on her cooking. Agatha eyed her warily. "Now, you come to visit?" "I was busy," Lady Death said with a laugh. "Someone killed a string of witches not far from here. You should be careful, being all by yourself. There are dangerous witches out there." She finally crossed over the threshold, feeble wards shattering in her presence. The entity stopped feet from her, flower twirling between her nimble fingers. "Did you miss me?" Agatha broke into a grin. "Why else would I have made a convenient path of bodies for you to follow?" She left the fire's side to take the flower from her lover's hands. "What kind is this? It's beautiful."

    "Aconitum napellus," the cosmic entity told her. "It's poisonous."

    "My favorite," Agatha purred. She sniffed it, taunting Death as it neared her lips. "Have you missed me, my love?"

    The other woman reached for her, a smile playing on her lips. They clasped hands as Death nuzzled her nose against a cheek. "Oh, my dear, I want nothing more than to see your face daily." She pulled away, batting her eyelashes at the witch. Death bent at the waist, her deadly lips pressing against Agatha's knuckles. "Especially when you're flushed from strenuous labor." Her hazel eyes darkened as they met with a patch of exposed flesh along the collar of Agatha's dress.

    Agatha laughed, eyes twinkling. "Such a foul mind for such a great being. What you know of such things?" She tugged Death to her. Their lips connected, a tingle sent through both participants. "How long do we have?"

    "If the mortals can keep their hands to themselves, all night," the Green Witch told her. Her hands settled on Agatha's hips gently. Poor thing was always so worried about hurting her delicate flower.

    "Well, this mortal doesn't know the meaning of the word 'restraint'," Agatha drawled. She roughly pulled Death closer to her with a bit lip. "You don't have to be careful with me, my love. Many have tried, but none can break me."

    The other woman tucked a strand behind her flower's ear. Her hazel eyes were impossibly soft. "My survivor. My dandelion."

    Agatha preened. Where others saw a monster, Death saw something beautiful. It never ceased to make her heart flutter. "Kiss me," she ordered breathily. Her eyes slid shut as Death complied willingly. She ignored the bubbling of her cauldron. Ignored the in's and out's of the shifting forest. Ignored the sound of her heart beating in her own chest in favor of the soft sighs Death gave only to her. Agatha Harkness felt more powerful than any other person. Felt smaller than anything in existence. She felt...felt loved.

    Love.

    It was a funny word with many different types and uses.

    Agatha loved power. Agatha loved her freedom. Loved overcoming those who would subdue her. But Agatha loved Death more. Loved the way the woman loomed at a safe distance. Loved to be loved by the witch. Loved to be held and told the things she needed to hear. It kept the spot of evil in her hidden behind the curtain of warmth the two had put up in their own little world. Death's love kept her sane. Kept her free. Agatha loved. "Do you like living out here?" her lover asked suddenly. Warm fingers tangled in her auburn locks. "You mortals are exceedingly frail and susceptible to the elements." Agatha laughed, licking her lips. "Are you asking to 'bed' me, my lady?" Death grinned. "And if I were?"

    That was new. The witch wasn't aware powerful entities like Death would be interested in carnal desires. Then again, why wouldn't she be? Here she was, in a forest, kissing a mortal who would eventually die. Agatha would leave her one day, but Death risked the pain the more she visited. If that wasn't romance, Agatha didn't know what would be. She stroked a cheek, eyes searching Death's face before answering. "I wouldn't be opposed to a soft bed rather than a lump of dirt."

    "Then I shall build you a house," the Green Witch promised, "so that you may only know comfort." Death waved a hand, fingers wiggling and weaving a spell in the air. "A place for just the two of us. Safe from those who would do you harm."

    Agatha leaned forward to kiss her once more. Her stomach fluttered as the hand on her hip tightened possessively. "Just us," she breathed. "Only us."

    "You look tired," Rio laughed. Her chest rose and fell as she lay next to Agatha. "Maybe you should take a break."

    The goddess rolled her eyes. "I'm not tired. Goddesses don't get tired." (Why did she have to be so stubborn?)

    Death rolled onto her side to eye the woman. She traced runes over Agatha's heart with the point of a nail. "You're not a natural goddess, sweetheart. I'm pretty sure you can still get tired."

    "Is that why you're not tired?" Agatha huffed. "That's a bunch of bullshit." Rio laughed, eyes drinking in the sight of her limp-limbed wife. "You should have negotiated that in your contract. Not like you were in a rush to get away from your exes." "You can't be upset about that forever," the other woman argued. She rolled her eyes. "They were one time flings."

    "You slept with Frida eight different times," Rio reminded, her nail pressing into soft skin. "And you spent a whole week with Eartha."

    "Two weeks," Agatha corrected.

    The nail began to draw blood as it was run down the top of the goddess' sternum. "Don't even get me started." Rio leaned over to lick the wound even if she felt her wife deserved an ounce of her pain. She rested her head on the chest, ear pressed to the woman's heart. She worried her lip for a moment, eyes flicking up to her wife's face. "Are you sure you want this? To be immortal?"

    Agatha looked down at her, a Big Emotion on full display. "Why wouldn't I? Now, we get more time.....Isn't that what you wanted?"

    Rio swallowed thickly. "Always, but I didn't think you did. You've been..." Pissed? Angry? Upset? Hurt? Drunk with dark magic? There was so much between them that they'd yet to discuss. Of course, she didn't know what Agatha truly wanted. Even now, magic and time at her disposal, and the witch was still hiding behind wall after wall after wall. Motivations were easy to figure out. Attachments and why, just as simple. But Agatha hardly knew what she wanted, so Rio had to guess just as much as she did. She'd have a migraine if she were capable of one.

    Her wife stroked her cheek, nails tickling Rio's skin. There was an affectionate smile on her face. One that was gradually becoming more common. It gave Death hope that things could be fixed. (As if there weren't a whole slew of examples that showcased Agatha's love for her.) The goddess softened, more of her mask dropping away. "I was upset with you for a long time, but I made peace with your job, remember? I haven't blamed you since we last discussed Nicky. Not one bit." Agatha thumbed away a tear that had escaped the Green Witch's eye. "I don't hate you, Rio."

    Death didn't know how badly she needed the reaffirmation until now. Losing her had terrified her. Had made her think Agatha didn't want her anymore. Didn't want her again. Her fingers curled around a bare shoulder. "I can't live without you," Rio confessed. "You can't leave me. Not again."

    "I promise to stay with you even after all the stars have burned out," Agatha promised, her eyes twinkling with mischief and devotion. "You'll never be able to get rid of me now." She tried to say it like a threat, but Rio knew what she really meant.

    Rio pressed a kiss over her wife's heart, eyes sliding shut. "You need to get some rest," she breathed. "The kids-"

    The pair felt the bed disappear beneath them before they were dropped onto the floor of a certain cosmic temple. Agatha clutched at her in her confusion. Death covered her until she realized just where exactly they'd been summoned. She glared as at the white columns and white, robed figures. They never got their timing right.

    "Pay up, Betty," Eartha laughed. "Told you they wouldn't last twelve hours without going at it like rabbits."

    Death stood, not bothering to cover herself. Maybe Agatha would get jealous and take her in front of the Ancient Ones. That would be quite the cautionary tale to tell Wanda. "Jealous?" she sneered.

    "Don't get yourself in a tizzy," Betty chastised. "You forced our hand in the matter." "You're the ones who dropped the Demiurge on my wife," she argued. "A lot could have been avoided if you'd sent him to someone else."

    "We'd still be fighting if they had," Agatha reminded. Much like Death, she stood in the nude. She even dared to wink at the panel right in front of her.

    Rio fumed. "What are you staring at?" she practically barked at the four Ancient Ones. "You're the ones putting a show on for us," Frida laughed. She eyed Agatha and bit at a nail. Death threw a sheet over her wife. "We were in the middle of something important," she told the group. It was hard enough having a conversation with Agatha now that there was a group of mortals in the way. Why couldn't they let her finish having a serious conversation with her wife? They could have finally talked about Nicky and Billy. They could have talked about that she-devil, Wanda...

    "We wanted to make sure the two of you weren't starting any fires," Dolly told the couple. "We know how Agatha gets when the power goes to her head."

    "Only fire we started was the one between each other's legs," Agatha told the Ancient One with a suggestive look. She turned to eye Rio, a hand reaching for her wife. "Should we show them how hot it can get?"

    "Only if the audience is allowed to participate," Frida was quick to say. She looked ready to tackle the goddess to the ground.

    Rio wrapped Agatha up like a mummy. "I don't like that one."

    "You and me both," Dolly groaned. "I'm surprised you're not tearing the place up." "Who?" Death asked. "I don't have a reason to be upset about her new position." Or did she? What weren't they telling her this time?

    The senior Ancient One smirked. "No, not you. Agatha........Or has she not realized yet?" That piqued their interest.

    "Realized what?" Agatha ground out. "What did you do to me?"

    "You'll see." Dolly laughed to herself, clearly pleased.

    "Don't be that way," Frida told the other woman. She leaned forward to address the goddess. "She's talking about your magic, flor."

    "Mine," Death growled to the Ancient One. "She's not your flower." (What did she need to do to get them away from her wife????)

    "Settle down," Agatha told her. "What about my magic?"

    "You're not hot shit, babes," Betty finally told them. "Dolly's capped your magic." Rio turned her glare from Frida to Dolly. "WWWHHHAAATTT?"

    "Capped is a strong word," Eartha said, shaking her head. "She still has her magic, she just didn't gain the others."

    "How the hell am I supposed to teach Wanda and Billy then?" Agatha growled. "I need chaos magic for that. What's the point of having mastery of all magic!"

    "No, you just need the knowledge of how it works." Dolly sent a small spell book in the goddess' direction. "If you were to wield that kind of power, you'd decimate the world on a whim."

    "I'm definitely thinking about it now," Agatha huffed. She thumbed through the book with a litany of grumbled curses. It must have been filled with tons of new spells. The goddess was quickly engrossed, her nose shoved deep into the pages.

    "And you," Betty began, pointing to Rio, "will need to stop that child from resurrecting anymore souls. Next time, we won't be so forgiving."

    Death glowered. There was nothing she could say to such a command. Arguing rarely worked in her favor. Last time she'd been summoned for a tongue-lashing, they'd doled out a punishment that lasted centuries. Rio glanced at Agatha before bowing her head. "I will speak to the boy. It won't happen again."

    "Good," Frida purred. "We don't want any more misunderstandings. Nor do we want you to think this...promotion is a reward for your bad behavior."

    Agatha lifted her head at the comment. "So, I killed a few witches," she huffed. "Let's not be so dramatic."

    No one bothered to correct the preoccupied woman. Looks were shared. Warnings. Rio knew what was at stake if she didn't comply with their laws. She wrapped herself in clothing, her crown and shroud hiding her face. "Will that be all?"

    "You may go, Lady Death...Divine Mother," Frida purred. She blew a kiss to Agatha before dropping them back to earth.

    The couple bounced on the bed as they landed back in Agatha's house. Rio wrestled with her shroud as it tangled around her neck and blocked her sight. A final 'fuck you' from the Ancient Ones for her foul behavior.

    "Hold up," Agatha laughed. She tugged at the thick fabric. "Those four are so dramatic when Stevie's away," she grumbled. "There we go!"

    Rio flopped backwards with a huff. "Just do what they want you to do," she instructed carefully. If her wife knew how far they were willing to go to stay in control, Agatha really would decimate the world. Rules be damned.

    Agatha set her new spell book on the bedside table along with Rio's shroud and crown. She quickly grabbed the green headpiece, a twinkle in her eyes. "You know..." Death grinned. Of course her wife's mind was still very much preoccupied. She licked the inside of her mouth as she eyed the goddess. "Mhmm....?"

    The still-very-naked witch nestled the crown back on Rio's head, cheeks flushed. "I've never had you wear it while we-"

    Rio laughed loudly. "I didn't want your ego to get any bigger," she told Agatha. "You'll still need to earn that right, my love." Death pressed her down against the sheets, a hand wrapping around Agatha's throat. "Because when I wear this, no one is my better. No one." Agatha bit her lip with a moan. "So put me in my place," she groaned. "Show me Lady Death in all her glory."

    "Won't that shatter your pretty, little illusion?" Death questioned as she straddled a thigh. She ground down, letting the pressure in her build slowly.

    "What illusion?" Agatha breathed. She watched the cosmic entity ride her leg with dark eyes. Those pants making her core throb and ache with need.

    "The one where you think you hold my leash. That you control me." Rio threw her head back with a keen as Agatha pulled her down to press more firmly against her taut muscles. "Oh please," the goddess laughed. "We both know that's a cheap party mask I wear. I can't control you anymore than you can control me. But pretending is just as fun, don't you think?" She removed a hand from her wife's hip to squeeze at the wrist near her throat, urging Death to tighten her grip. Rio gazed into steel-grey eyes, searching for any signs of a trick. For some ulterior motive.

    Very rarely did Agatha relinquish control in the bedroom. She'd fought and clawed and struggled to have that nugget of notion when the two were intimate. To hand it over... Flesh gave way to pearly incisors and cream-colored bones. Death squeezed the once-fragile column with a bruising grip. She used her free hand to pin her wife's hands above her head. "Who do you belong to?"

    Agatha grinned. "You, my love. Only you," she managed to say. Her steel-grey eyes held firm as Death gazed down at her in all her majesty. She gave a strangled cry as a knee pressed against her.

    Death held her head high, chest heaving. Her hair cascading down in murky waves. Landslides of beauty in the wake of those unwavering rings of hazel.

    It was like their wedding night all over again.

    The Green Witch freed Agatha from her grasp to take. To mark. To claim. Her fingers twisting and rubbing at a feverish pace until her wife was shouting praises unto her. Until those glorious breasts raised with an arched back. Until Agatha had nothing else to give her. Death felt her heart stutter in time with the Triple Goddess'. Shuddered with the force. Basked in the afterglow as the organ restarted. Sucked in a breath, air heavy with their combined scent.

    Death blinked as a snore reached her ears.

    Rio shrugged with an amused grin. Even the Divine Mother needed to rest. She carefully repositioned her wife on a plump pillow before cleaning up their mess. Kisses soothed the worst of the bruising to Agatha's neck. She didn't want to have to explain that to any of the teens even if it would make Wanda squirm. Rio slipped away in search of Agatha's shower. Chapter End Notes A much shorter chapter compared to the others, but only because this was a last-minute, squeezed in entry. If the smut was bad, tell me. I'm still iffy on if it was cringe or not hehe (sobs)

    Blessings & Burdens Alike Chapter Summary Maybe bringing Alice and Nicky back was a bad idea...

    Chapter Notes See the end of the chapter for notes Billy looked over at Wanda, his fork stabbing absentmindedly at his plate. He knew they could read each other's minds, but he was doing his best to avoid that. Now that Agatha and Rio had kicked everyone out to fuck talk, they had nothing but time to reconnect. He envied his brother who didn't have to wait years to figure out who he was. Tommy could easily accept Wanda as his mother. He didn't have to have two pairs of eyes hovering over his shoulder to find out why he was so different. Tommy didn't have to try and ignore the voices questioning his every move for years on end.

    "Is everything okay, Teen?" Alice leaned over, concern etched into her features. "You're really doing a number on that carrot."

    Billy set his fork down. "Just...tired," he lied. "Are you doing okay? I mean...you were..." She smiled at him. "I got to see my mom again. We had a really good talk, but we both felt I didn't get to make the most of my time." Alice shrugged. "I wasn't exactly expecting to come back if I'm being honest."

    He returned her smile with his own. "I didn't know I could do that, if that helps any. Rio thinks it's because I wanted Agatha back and I guess I kinda did."

    "It's actually super crazy that Wanda and Agatha are your mothers," she admitted, eyes flitting over to the Scarlet Witch. "Did you know?"

    Billy shook his head. "Agatha didn't either. Rio's the one who sort of came in with her bag of secrets and handed them out like birthday presents." The pair shared a laugh at the image. His face dropped. "I just realized...that makes Rio my stepmom." They shared a look. "My mother's wife is Death, and I'm Death's stepson."

    "Kid, when you turn twenty-one, we're gonna go out and have a drink," Alice laughed. "Thanks, Alice. I didn't realize how badly I needed a good laugh." He bumped shoulders with her. "Thanks for being the cool older sister of the coven. You and Teddy are gonna get along."

    "Your boyfriend is very cute. I'm happy for you," she told him.

    "How, uh...how long do you think they're gonna go at it? I'm trying to avoid the mental image, but I doubt Agatha would be okay with us taking Nicky all the way to Eastview." Alice nearly choked on her drink. "No," she groaned. "Don't put that image in my head." She wiped at a corner of her mouth with a blush. "Look, Agatha's a freak. I give it at least four hours."

    He dropped his shoulders with a huff, hand gripping his fork. "It'll be bedtime soon." "Does she have a phone you can message? What about Rio?"

    Billy laughed to himself as he recalled Agatha's 'summoning card' comment. "Only way to get ahold of them is if we kill a person."

    Alice made a face. "I don't volunteer this time. No offense."

    "Oh...geez. I'm so sorry, Alice," he quickly told her. "I didn't mean to bring that up for you." She gave him a tight grin. "It's okay. I probably just need a good therapist." "I'm just...I'm really sorry about everything. If I had known I was in control, I would have gotten us all off before the first trial."

    Alice tilted her head with furrowed brows. "What do you...Billy, what are you saying? Did you have something to do with the Witches' Road?"

    The teen dropped his fork with a clatter. "I...It..." Where's Agatha? I need her, he realized quietly. Things were easier to ignore when she was around. There was no one to buffer emotions for him. No one to help with the tightness in his chest. He shifted before nodding. "My magic made the Road. Turns out the whole thing was a scam Agatha made up." Nicky leaned over, bursting their little bubble. "You've heard my song!" He grinned madly. "I didn't know Mama sang it for everybody else. I'm glad she had it while I lived with Mother." Billy looked at his brother, his stomach churning violently. The walls seemed to close in on him. His lungs clenched, throat closing up on him. The teen scrambled from his seat and booked it to the bathroom. He burst into the first stall he found and emptied his stomach. It was one thing to know Agatha had sirened witches to their death. It was another to have it forced in his face with Nicky's innocence. To see the betrayal on Alice's face. How was he supposed to cope with this knowledge? How did he face these people after doing terrible things with a child's lullaby underscoring his actions?

    "If you want to be a witch, get used to this feeling."

    How often did Agatha have to tell herself that? At what point did she finally accept the bad she did? Had she accepted she was capable of evil? Billy wasn't sure anymore. Didn't want to have to think about it anymore than he already had.

    The bathroom door opened as someone entered quietly. A hand rubbed his back, a napkin held out to him. "Is everything okay?" Teddy asked softly. He dabbed at Billy's face when he failed to answer. "Wanda said you left the table in a hurry."

    "How can you love me?" Billy asked. "How can you love a monster?"

    "You're not a monster," his boyfriend soothed. "Why are you thinking like this? Did Wanda tell you something?"

    The young witch shook his head. "My mind killed Alice, Teddy. And it happened because I used Nicky's song to make a fucked up pocket universe that Jigsaw could have been filmed in."

    The other teen remained silent for a long moment. "I think you should talk to them about it before jumping to conclusions. I mean, what did Agatha say? Has she told you anything?" Billy let out a weak laugh. "To get used to the feeling."

    Teddy made a face. "Okay...don't take her advice. Maybe talk to Rio. She knows what it's like to deal with death all the time. She might have some helpful words."

    "She's a bit busy at the moment," he reminded his boyfriend.

    "Well, you're only other option is Wanda. She's got experience in that department, too." Billy nodded. He took the napkin and finished cleaning himself up. "Thanks. You've been the best through all of this." He hugged the taller teen, cheeks warming.

    Returning to the table was easy. In fact, it was a little too easy. The teen plastered a smile on, just the way he had with his parents in the very beginning, and continued to eat. Worried glances melted away as he laughed at a silly joke. This is good, he told himself. No one has to know. No one needs to know. Billy reached down to grip at his left knee while entertaining Tommy with a story. The only one who gave him a look was Wanda. Her eyes told him everything he needed to know.

    Nicky insisted on visiting a park before going home. "Mama and I liked to stay near the trees," he told them. He held Wanda and Rebecca's hands in his, swinging them with a wide grin. "Mama said it was because witches have to stay connected to nature, but Mother says it was because they missed each other."

    Billy stuffed his hands into his sweater, eyes scanning the field of playing children. He couldn't shake the feeling that he was being watched. Like eyes were always on him. No one will hurt you, Wanda's voice said, filling his head gently.

    The teen schooled his face before responding. Stay out of my head.

    I'll get Agatha if that's what you want. I'm fine with that so long as you feel better. Was that a hand resting on his shoulder?

    Who said I wasn't feeling well? He wanted to leave the park for the safety of his room. (Where Agatha would have been so he could vent.) Maybe he did need his other mother in this moment, but she would probably laugh at him. She'd killed so many witches and barely let the hurt show. He may not be a conscious serial killer, but there was something about crying after doing a Bad Thing when you should have been more careful to begin with. Having the victims of your poor decisions walking around certainly didn't make things easier. Perhaps that was why Agatha had remained alone for so long after Nicky's death. She didn't want to see what she'd done either.

    A mother just knows, Wanda told him. She shot him a sympathetic look that did little to ease his annoyance and discomfort. I'll send for her right now.

    Billy figured he should have told her not to, but the spacious outdoors felt more smothering than any trial location ever had. In fact, this felt more dangerous than the Road. He found a tree to sit under and was grateful when Teddy joined him. They sat together in silence, hand in hand. Billy rested his head on his boyfriend's shoulder with a yawn. "Take a nap," the other teen whispered. "I'll wake you up when it's time to go." The young witch nodded, eyes drifting shut.

    "Billy...You ready?" Rio asked, appearing from nowhere. She stood in the center of their giant, odd family. Death wore a sweatsuit in a mint green color. Her hair was pulled up into a messy bun. The oddest thing he found was her lack of makeup. She looked...at peace. Nicky ran to her, hugging her waist with a giggle.

    "Where's Agatha?" Wanda asked, her eyes flitting over in Billy's direction. The teen pursed his lips lightly in a poor attempt to keep a straight face. Rio turned her gaze to him, a smile quirking her lips.

    "Turns out she still needs to sleep," the Green Witch informed. "It should be fine for everyone to come back now."

    Billy pulled himself up before helping Teddy to stand. "Tell her I'll see her tomorrow." Rio scoffed. She took a step towards him, pulling Nicky with her in the process. "Everyone's staying in Westview for tonight. Agatha's orders."

    "She doesn't order me around," he told her a tad petulantly.

    It was one thing to have your mother reach out to your other mother because you were on the verge of a mental breakdown. It was an entirely different matter to have your step(?)-mother show up on your murderous mother's behalf. It was like crying for your parents after your first sleepover. It made him feel silly and small. Billy Maximoff-Harkness-Vidal-Kaplan was done feeling small and hopeless and scared. The blood of powerful women coursed through his veins! (He missed Agatha.)

    Hazel eyes practically held him in place. "If you thought my little tantrum was a big deal, you don't want to see Agatha in a fit of rage." Rio tilted her head just so as if to say, "Leave, I dare you" to the teen.

    Billy relented if only to protect the world from his mother's rage. (Great! Three of four could tear the Universe into pieces if upset.) He walked over and kept his gaze downturned. "I'm ready," he bit out.

    "The others can take the car. Agatha wanted me to see you home personally," Rio told him. She crouched to kiss Nicky's cheek before pushing him towards Wanda. The two women shared a look before the Scarlet Witch led the young boy away.

    The pair watched the reluctant group pile into his non-magical mother's car. The vehicle pulled away before speeding down the road towards Agatha's house.

    Rio awkwardly and lightly punched Billy's shoulder. "So, what's got you all glum? Must be pretty serious if you had Wanda looking for Agatha and risk seeing something. I nearly killed her for peeking."

    The teen wrinkled his nose at the mental image that tried to form. "I don't...I don't want to know about that." He shook his head. "It's nothing. I'm sorry she did that. Everything's fine." Death scoffed. "You got your magic from Wanda. Your body from the Kaplan's. But your whole...," Rio gestured to all of him, "emotional constipation comes from Agatha." She threw an arm over his shoulder and walked him over to the sidewalk.

    Billy looked down, lost in his thoughts, and noticed that the Green Witch was barefoot. It was enough to bring him back to reality. He looked up and found Rio watching him carefully. The teen looked away, brows furrowed. He took a few steadying breaths before letting out a long sigh. "I've been thinking...I mean, it's nothing, but...it's my fault Alice died. Ghost or no ghost, that was my mind. I orchestrated all of that. And now...she's back. I just..." "You feel guilty," Rio finished for him. Unlike Agatha, she didn't belittle him. Didn't crack a joke or try to shift the blame from him or to him. She simply listened. The witch nodded slowly, suddenly much older than she appeared. "And you wanted to talk to Agatha because of her experience."

    He jerked his head in a pained nod. "Last time I felt like this, she told me to 'get use to this feeling'," he told her. (It suddenly occurred to him that he was walking with literal Death at his side, and Death was the one comforting him. What a crazy world he lived in...) Billy gave a half shrug. "I told you it was nothing."

    Rio let out a soft sigh. "I wouldn't call that nothing, Billy. You shouldn't want to ignore your remorse. It's not valiant. It's not healthy. There's a reason why Agatha's hated by the world, and it's not because of what she did."

    He turned his head to look at her, blinking. "But Agatha...?"

    Death pulled a long-suffering face. "Agatha runs away. Away from others. Away from her feelings. Away from everything she can't control. She'll never take responsibility for anything she's ever done." Rio grew a flower to play with, a distant look stealing her gaze away from him. "I blamed you for the Road and her killing herself the first time. A part of me is still upset for everything, but your clever death traps forced her to take a look at her own actions for once. It scared the hell out of her, but it was for the best."

    Billy hummed in thought. "So...what should I do?"

    "Talk to Alice," Rio told him simply. "Not much else you can do."

    "...Are you okay? I mean, Agatha and Nicky are back, but even I feel like things are different."

    She scoffed down at him, but he found no malice in the gesture. Death was simply amused by him. "Don't worry about me. Worry about that fragile, little heart of yours." She poked his chest, careful with her nails. "In fact, don't even worry about Agatha. I'll handle her." Billy gave her a look. "Is there something wrong with Agatha?" Was that why she hadn't left the house to see them? Maybe that was why she wanted them all back at her house. His heart began to beat a little faster as his mind raced.

    "Cut it out," Rio told him. "There's nothing wrong with her. She's perfectly fine. I just know how she can be, is all." Death tapped her flower to her nose with a chuckle. "It's cute, though. How much you worry about her."

    "Why wouldn't I?"

    "Because, before you, Agatha was pretty good at pushing people like you away." She let her flower blow away with a gust of controlled wind. "Don't hide yourself like she did, Billy. You'll never know peace if you do."

    Billy dared to bump his shoulder against hers, offering her a smile. "I'll try, but only if you hang out at home more. I like getting to talk to you."

    Rio reached up and put her hand on his head to shake it lightly. "No more soul transfers," she told him. "I'm in the negative now, which means overtime for me. Unlike you mortals, I don't get paid for the fruits of my labor."

    He laughed, a bit of his worry and guilt ebbing away. "I'll be sure to get on Agatha's nerve. It's not much, but it'll be a start to make it up to you."

    Death grinned. "I've got just the thing to kickstart your revenge tour."

    The world lay at Her feet, small and precious like a glittering gem. The dazzling blue and green of Earth greeted Her in the rays of the Sun. She reached for it, Her hand yearning to stroke the side of Her delicate, beautiful wife. The Moon could practically hear the trees call to Her. They yearned for Her nightly caress. Yearned for Her gentle gaze. Her wife was too far, and the Moon did not appreciate that. She moved closer until...

    ....Until a pillow smacked her in the face.

    Agatha sat up with a gasp. "Rio, what the fuck!" She lobbed a small spell at the Green Witch. "Don't ever do that shit again."

    Her wife smirked before climbing onto the bed to straddle the goddess' waist. "Having a good dream, amor?"

    Agatha sucked in a breath, hey eyes fluttering, as a hand ghosted along her bare shoulder. "I, uh, it was weird. I think I was the moon."

    Rio peppered her face with kisses but stopped at the information. She laughed. "Are you not the Triple Goddess?"
