    "Yeah, but I didn't think I'd literally be the fucking moon," she huffed. "That's going to get annoying very quickly."

    Death rolled her eyes before slipping her hand lower. Her fingers stroked at Agatha, pulling a gasp from her lips. "I happen to love the Moon very much," she breathed. Agatha rolled her head back as she ground down on the hand with a pant. "Mmm...The Moon loves...loves you very much, too," she huffed. The witch pulled Rio in for a kiss as those talented fingers continued to work her into a frenzy.

    Rio groaned into her mouth as she shifted onto a knee. She used her free hand to steady herself, knuckles turning white as she gripped the headboard.

    The goddess stared at Death, heart hammering in her chest. She had missed the easy moments between them like this. Those pre-Nicky days where they hadn't a care in the world. Lazy mornings and domestic evenings. It enticed the witch to the cosmic entity. She gripped at Rio's sweat top and magicked it away. Her mouth moved to attack Death's neck, all teeth and tongue. She smirked at the hiss she'd won.

    "We...we have guests," the Green Witch informed as she struggled to think. "So keep it down," Agatha rasped. She flipped them over, pressing her weight onto the immortal.

    "You're the one who likes to wake the dead," Rio huffed. Her eyes were dark with lust as she licked her lips.

    Agatha leaned down and pressed a soft kiss to those lush lips. The simplicity of it all left her reeling. So many years of keeping her guard up around this woman made it nearly impossible to enjoy the moment. She pushed it away in favor of pawing at her wife's chest. If there was one thing about Death, it was that she was a receptive little thing. All pants and keens if you knew where to touch her. And Agatha? Agatha knew every bump and dip of her wife's body. Had mapped it with all five senses and then some. She knew her wife so well. Agatha planned to reconquer every inch.

    The goddess threw a robe on before grabbing a towel. "What was that all about?" she asked the reclining spirit guide.

    "I thought you were asking me to fuck the moon," Rio responded cheekily. She hopped off the bed and wrapped her arms around Agatha's middle. "Billy wants to talk to you." "Is that where you ran off to?" Agatha pulled away, ignoring the soreness in her muscles. "What does he want?"

    Death eyed her warily. "He needs motherly advice. The real kind, Agatha. Not the crap you tell yourself when you're too scared to look in the mirror."

    She spun around to face her wife with a stern look. "What's that supposed to mean?" "You know exactly what I mean."

    Agatha scoffed. "I don't have time for this. I need to shower."

    Rio hummed. They both knew Death had won the argument. "Te veo."

    The goddess bolted from the room in a huff. She didn't need Rio to give her crap so early in the...night? "Fuck," she hissed to herself. Maybe having a raunchy sex session and napping before dinner had been a bad idea. At least she felt rejuvenated. That was probably thanks to the moon in the sky, fucking symbolism.

    Wait...Is there going to be a whole power clause with this whole moon goddess thing? I should've asked follow up questions. She wanted to slap herself for getting so distracted by all those new spells.

    Agatha entered the bathroom and fiddled with the shower knobs. She had just found the right temperature when Wanda slipped in. Well, it wasn't entirely Wanda. The Scarlet Witch was astral projecting. Infuriatingly, she seemed to be doing it while awake. The goddess considered sucking the chaos magic from her body for a third time.

    "Neat trick," she told the woman dryly. "What do you want? Can't you see I'm about to hop in the shower?" Agatha's face lit up. "Or was that what you were hoping for, sugar tits?" Wanda glared at her. "I came to talk about Billy."

    "Eugh! You always gotta kill the mood, Wands. What's his problem this time?" She dropped her robe and slipped into her shower. Agatha kept the door cracked so she could still hear her guest.

    "He was upset earlier. Eddie was worried about him."

    "Teddy told you this?" She knew he hadn't. The boy was as loyal as they came. "No. I gleaned it from his mind. Whatever it was, they both were hoping you'd show up to fix things."

    Agatha removed her head from the stream of water. "Rule one of staying with us: No mind reading. Billy and I don't do it, so you aren't allowed to either. Rule two: Limit magic usage until you've got a better grasp of it."

    Wanda laughed. Actually laughed at her. "You're a few years behind," the woman taunted. "I used the Darkhold just like you did. I'd say I've improved quite a bit since we last saw each other."

    The goddess lathered shampoo into her hair, nose wrinkling at Jen's perfume-y soaps. "Ooo," Agatha mocked. "Look out for the Big, Bad Wanda Maximoff. She'll make you act out a sitcom." She cackled loudly, her voice bouncing off the walls. "Don't give me that bullshit, Wanda. We both know the Darkhold has a way of tricking us into thinking we gained control of ourselves. I might have been under your spell, but some of your actions still bled through." "Whatever," Wanda huffed. "We're talking about Billy, not me." She hovered closer until she was phasing through the shower door. "Billy was upset to the point that Lady Death walked him home."

    Now that was something Rio had left out. Agatha eyed the other witch. "How long were they gone for?"

    "They walked from the other side of town to here."

    "Interesting..." She waved Wanda off. "I'll talk to him. You and I can have our chat after the kids have gone to bed."

    "Is that why you're keeping Rebecca and Jeff here?"

    "Is that his name?" Agatha laughed to herself. "He definitely looks like a 'Jeff.' No, I don't know what you're talking about."

    "Sounds like you and Lady Death aren't on the same page. Take it from me, hat's usually where all the drama starts." Wanda disappeared before Agatha could argue. The goddess stewed in her thoughts and the steamy air. Rio seemed to be playing a new game with her. One that left little room for her to be alone with her thoughts. That was going to be a problem. Death knew how much Agatha coveted her solitude. If Rio was going to shove her in a box of domesticity, she had another thing coming! Agatha finished her shower with a game plan forming.

    Billy sat with everyone downstairs as a he queued up the movie Rio had suggested. He watched the doorway to the rest of the house with growing excitement. There was no telling how Agatha would react, but he knew exactly how Nicky would. It tickled him to no end. Agatha would probably throw another dramatic whining fit and everyone would laugh. "You sure this is a good idea?" His father asked him. "She doesn't seem like the kind of person who would enjoy this movie. We don't want her to tell that wife of hers anything. Pretty sure she doesn't like me. Neither of them."

    "Oh, she's not," he told the older man with a smirk. "But that's why I'm putting it on. It's her punishment."

    Jeff gave him a tight smile. "Punishment? Isn't she one of your mothers?" "Well, yeah. But that doesn't mean I can't make her squirm a bit," he reasoned. Somehow, Billy felt as if he were digging a hole for himself. What kind of hole, he wasn't sure. There was just a hint of trepidation in his father's eyes that made him pause. "Are you scared of Agatha? She won't do anything to hurt you. Not if I tell her not to."

    "I know, more or less, what to expect from that woman. That's not why I'm worried," Jeff told him carefully.

    He's not scared of Agatha...He's...He's scared of me, the young witch realized. "Dad, you know I would never purposely hurt anyone, right?"

    The graying man shook his head. "No, I know. You're a gentle giant. Always have been. Or...maybe not always..."

    Billy swallowed thickly. "I'm going to play the movie now," he announced. Running. He was running from the situation. If Rio had never brought up Agatha doing it, he would have never realized how much he did it. But how in the hell was he supposed to talk to his sort-of father while wearing the body of a dead boy? What could he say to ease the pain and confusion his parents must be feeling? How did he explain the full scope of his magic, his lineage, everything to people that just wanted to have a normal life with a normal son but got stuck with him?

    "William!" Agatha stormed down the stairs as the Ice Chant began. "Do you want to lose television privileges in this house?" The witch stood in the middle of the living room with soaking wet hair and a baggy shirt thrown haphazardly on. He thanked the Ancient Ones that she had enough mind to throw shorts on before coming down.

    "Mama, please," Nicky whined. "I wanna see Elsa and the trolls."

    "Who cares about that prissy crybaby and those dumb rocks?" Agatha dripped all over the floor as she nosed around for the remote to the DVD player. "What's to like about a witch who can't control her powers and is ostracized by her own parents? It's not even believable." Billy blinked. "Uh..."

    "Sounds just like you," Jen was quick to snark. "Right down to the dead parents and self- isolation."

    The teen swallowed thickly as the two women eyed each other hotly. "Guys, I'll just..." He spammed the buttons on the remote, but his magic made the t.v. increase in volume. "You wanna be bound a second time?" Agatha asked the pink witch with a tone dripping with malice. "You won't even be able to remember a single element when I'm done with you." "Agatha," Billy warned. "It's just a movie." (Why wouldn't the damn movie shut up!) She turned to look at him and spied the remote in his hand. "Is it, though?" she asked him, that venomous hiss from the Road making a second appearance.

    The teen sunk into the cushions, eyes widening.

    Agatha took a deep breath, rubbing her temples. "Turn the movie off."

    He felt a flare of rebellion that usually appeared during their arguments. "Nicky wants to watch it," he challenged. "I think it's the least you can do after-"

    "Careful how you finish that sentence," his mother growled.

    The young Harkness appeared between them with a sour look. "I don't want to watch a movie if you're gonna be mean, Mama."

    Billy shut the t.v. off at Agatha's stricken face. The cheery atmosphere effectively ruined by the teen's antics. "We'll watch Wall-E instead," he told his brother. "It looks way better than Frozen anyway."

    Nicky shuffled over to sit with him. "Are there witches?"

    "Nope. None," he told the child. "But there's space and robots. Two things Tommy and I are gonna teach you about."

    Agatha and him shared a look.

    Don't pull that shit ever again, the goddess told him. And don't ever use your brother as a shield.

    It was just a harmless prank, he argued. Why are you being like this?

    Like what, Billy? Like someone who's sick and tired of that crap? You know how I feel about that movie! She crossed her arms with a huff.

    Billy scowled. You can't get upset over every little thing. What if Nicky wants to do something different than you?

    Something strange happened. Something new. Billy blinked, the living room disappearing momentarily.

    Nicky looked up at Agatha, presumably. "Could we not stay with the witches and survive with them?"

    Agatha was quick to respond with a, "No."

    The area shifted until Nicky reappeared. He stood near a river, rocks plunging into the flowing stream. The boy sighed before telling her they'd kill more witches later. The world distorted until Nicky lay next to Agatha, face still and pale.

    The memory passed in the blink of an eye, but he'd seen it. Nicky had gone against her before, even if it was by doing something as simple as questioning her, and then she'd lost him. She'd lost control of him, and she'd associated that with the trauma of losing her son. It made sense. Agatha loved to be in control. Killed for it. But this wasn't an instance or a time where that would be acceptable.

    Billy waited for her to berate him for sneaking a glance into her psyche, but it never came. He figured she might throw something at him, but that, too, never happened. Billy furrowed his brows. It quickly dawned on him that he'd done a new thing entirely on accident...and completely unnoticed. Agatha couldn't find out. Not yet.

    He closed his mind off to her as Jen switched out the discs.

    "Mama, come sit with us. I won't be able to see the movie," Nicky whined. He looked at her with child-like irritation.

    Agatha eyed them both before moving to sit next to her sons. "Add a 'please' next time," she chastised gently. The goddess gave Billy another look before falling completely silent. The teen clenched his jaw and pressed 'play'.

    Chapter End Notes It begins.... (insert evil OwO emoji here)

    The Respect of Your Peers Chapter Summary Rio spends more time with the rest of the coven.

    Chapter Notes Not nearly as painful an Tuesday's chapter is going to be hehe. Enjoy! Rather than have a chat with Agatha as planned, Billy sought the Scarlet Witch out. He really hoped she had an idea on what to do with her former best friend. It wasn't like the two hadn't butt heads before. It was, however, the first time he saw her trauma affect her decisions in real time. He wondered, not for the first time, just how little control his mother had had in her life. How awful had Agatha's mother been daily?

    Wanda stood outside in the backyard, eyes trained on the ever-present bed of flowers. The petals swished lazily with every breeze that passed them by. The fungi stood proudly, the silent sentinels of the garden. The first rays of the morning sun made the purples, blues, and creams of the plant life more vibrant. The rays also made his third mother's hair look fiery and wild.

    "Good morning, Billy," she greeted softly. It was like she was afraid to startle a wild animal. Was he a wild animal? Was that why his father looked scared of him last night? Was that why Agatha lashed out at him over a movie? Was that why Death was the only one who could have a civil conversation with him?

    "Morning," he mumbled. Billy stopped at her side, his gaze dropping to the cheery botanicals of Rio's garden. "This is where Agatha died," he found himself saying. (What a way to start a conversation off...)

    "So she said." Wanda clasped her hands tightly as she looked over at him. "Were you able to talk to her as well?"

    He shook his head. "We're both a bit too hot-headed for that. I was wondering if you could tell me a little bit more about her. She said she was your best friend." The Scarlet Witch laughed as if he'd just told her a joke. (That didn't bode well.) "I guess that's one way of looking at things. In the early days of my hex, yes. She was a big help during moments of trouble. Looking back, I realize those were just situations she orchestrated.....I don't get why I fell for her tricks, though."

    Billy swallowed past a lump. "She has a way of twisting the truth. It's her best superpower." He dropped to his knees to sit on his heels. He reached out, stroking a petal the way he'd seen Rio do in the past. "She can be so frustrating sometimes. Caring one minute, and belligerent the next."

    "Has she hurt you?" Wanda was quick to ask, her maternal instincts kicking in. (Billy felt four mothers to be exceedingly suffocating.) "If she has-"

    "No, she hasn't hurt me. In fact, I've hurt her more than anyone else has. Well...except for Rio, but she didn't do that willingly." Billy looked up at Wanda with a tired sigh. "Do you feel bad about the things you've done with your magic?"

    The red-head joined him on the grass with a sad smile. "When I first started out as an Avenger, I accidentally killed some people while trying to stop an explosion. I was devastated. I haven't stopped thinking about that day since."

    "So...you don't, I don't know, ignore it?" He winced at his own words. What was he even saying?

    "Is that why you haven't said much to your friend?"

    Billy shrank in on himself. "...Maybe...."

    Wanda cautiously set a hand on his shoulder. He found he didn't hate the contact. "Agatha said that people had been hurt on the Road, but she never said anything about you being at fault."

    Before he could consciously control his actions, he'd tucked himself under her arm with a sniffle. "My stupid magic made the stupid Road and created horrible death traps that killed her and two other really cool women."

    "I don't know how to make things better for you, Billy. Our magic is so different compared to everyone else's. But as annoying as it is, our magic is a part of us. Don't hate it; embrace it. Running from it will only make things harder." She hugged him tightly, gently rocking him. "Alice seems like a reasonable person. I'm sure if you talked to her, she'd understand. I could...I could join you if you needed me to."

    Billy considered her offer. Normally, he'd ask for Agatha to be there, but this was a delicate matter. He wasn't sharing something like, 'Hey, here's my ghost mentor' with Alice. He was going to explain why she died. That required a more gentle touch than what Agatha could offer. "I'd like that," he told her. "I think I'll talk to her before I go back to Eastview."

    Rio entered Agatha's house with a sniff.

    Someone was cooking breakfast.

    She slipped into the kitchen to find Alice, Billy, and Wanda moving around like a well-oiled machine. She sensed around and found the other souls in the house were still fast asleep. It made sense. The mortals had navigated a rough forty-eight hours of adrenaline and fear. Food was the second most necessary item on the recuperation to-do list. Death stood in the corner just observing the trio. This time, she made sure to tightly wrap herself in shadows to avoid Billy noticing her.

    The teen was saying something about the Road. "...when I realized I had the same leaves in my bedroom. I started to really panic. Then, Agatha popped up, and we had a small chat. That's when she told me I made the Road."

    Ah...So he was finally coming clean to the protection witch. That was good. At least someone had taken her advice for once. Agatha would likely dance around this conversation for as long as possible. Billy was willing to take the necessary steps at making amends. Not that Agatha didn't make an effort. She had recently, but that was with her. There was no telling what one of her victims would push her to do. The guilt was bound to eat at her sanity. Rio wondered if she should warn the household, or just let it run its course. "That's like...crazy," Alice laughed. "You made that whole pocket reality on your own without even meaning to! You've got to be crazy powerful."

    Rio laughed at the way Billy blushed. He was just a kid, after all. Not some hardened killer like her wife. His skills did deserve praise. When she'd been summoned to that non-glitchy reality, she could stop looking at all the details he'd managed to create. Agatha would have been delighted if she hadn't been pulled onto the Road. That much, she was certain. "It's not that cool," he deflected. "My mom created a whole fake town." Wanda laughed nervously. "Also unintentional," she told the other woman. "By the way, Billy. I probably won't be able to visit you in Eastview for a while. I need to make sure the Avengers aren't looking for me. They're probably still upset with me." "What would they do to you?" the teen asked.

    From Rio's experience, nothing nice to the young witch. They were likely to bind and burn the woman for the atrocities she'd carried out against the multiverse. Wanda dying would upset the boys, which would upset Agatha, which would upset her. This time, Death would agree with her for lying low.

    "I'd probably go to prison for a very long time...or I'd be put on retainer for them. Either way, I wouldn't be able to see or take care of you and your brother." She looked away with a grimace. "You and Tommy should be careful about revealing your powers, too. There are recruiters on all sides, not just good."

    "And then there's just a bunch of stalkers and weirdos," Alice added. She dished scrambled eggs into a bowl and lightly covered them.

    "But Agatha's making an academy. Won't that draw attention to us?"

    The kid was starting to use his brain. Rio could see the cobwebs falling off the pink muscle in real time.

    "What Agatha does is her business," Wanda told her son. "If the Avengers come knocking, we'll only help if she asks."

    Rio sensed the weather, making sure snow wasn't on the way. Two Maximoff's were using sound logic for once! It was a miracle that no one would have believed if she hadn't witnessed it. She waited a few more seconds to see if there was anything else she needed to know.

    "Are you staying, Alice? To help with her academy like Jen?" Billy said to the protection witch.

    Alice smiled. "Yeah, of course. You guys are my coven."

    Agatha was going to have a heart attack.

    Death moved over to the living room before making herself known. "Smells good," she lied as she re-entered the kitchen. She magicked her clothes into her sweatsuit from earlier, deciding she enjoyed the comfort it brought. That, and it still smelled of her wife. To her surprise, Billy skipped over to give her a hug. "You were totally right," he began. "I feel so much better for talking to Alice about everything."

    Alice waved to her with her own bright smile. "Please help me convince him how impressive that is," she said with a laugh. "That kind of magic is just..." The young woman imitated an explosion bursting forth from her cranium.

    Rio patted Billy on the back in hopes he'd let her go. He did not. She gave a light-hearted groan. "It's too early for affection, Billy. But, yes, Agatha and I were impressed." "Agatha, too!"

    His face lit up too much like Nicky's. It threw her off kilter. "She didn't try to steal your power the second you summoned it, so she was definitely impressed." Rio pried him off of her before she could get even more attached to the mortal. "You already know I enjoyed your little traps."

    "So, you knew the whole time, too?" Alice asked her. "And you never said?" "I was in the process of trying to re-woo my wife, but she was being very stubborn." Stubborn, and hot, and sad, and a little bit pathetic at times...All in all, it had been a fun vacation up until the whole 'I don't wanna see your face' bit. Rio could have done without that.

    "When isn't she," Billy muttered. His mood instantly soured, pinging Rio's alarms. "What happened?" she asked without a second thought. Yup...She was definitely a guardian of sorts now. Damn mortal emotions and her stupid, beating heart.

    Billy remained quiet which did little to ease her irritation with her wife. "There was a small disagreement last night," Wanda began. Even she looked upset by whatever had happened.

    "Jen and her got into an argument, which led to her and Billy, uh...getting involved." Rio nodded slowly, eyes shifting to look up at the ceiling. "I see..." "Rio, don't," Billy pleaded. "She's just stressed."

    Death scoffed. "She doesn't have anything to be stressed about. She's got a body and Nicky back." That itch of anger was returning. It demanded she go settle old scores with Agatha. To remind her of the pain she'd felt when their son was gone so she might act more like an adult. Didn't she understand her time with them was still limited? That they could be ripped from her at any moment!

    "It's my fault. Dad didn't think playing Frozen was a good idea, but I did it anyway. She didn't like the parallels between her and the main character."

    Rio kept her cool as she eyed the boy. "This is on her, not you. If she can't take a joke, she doesn't need to have Nicky with her." Their son had learned to stick up more for himself, and Agatha was bound to notice. The goddess was going to spiral once she realized how little control she actually had. It left a sour taste in Rio's mouth. "I'll talk to her." Billy latched himself to her side. "No. Please don't. I don't want to have a fight so early in the morning. It's not worth it. Really."

    She flicked a curl. "I was just gonna wake up Nicky. Why don't you do it instead? I'll stay right here." And plot how to get back at her for upsetting you and Nicky, she didn't add. Death hoped he hadn't read her thoughts as Billy slipped out of the kitchen. She turned to face the women. "Things are going to get a bit rocky around here. If they get into another argument, separate them. Billy's magic is still too unstable, and Agatha has a bag full of terrible things to say. It will devastate him."

    "How can you love her?" Wanda asked, truly confused and concerned. "She just...takes the life from everything around her."

    "She wasn't always that way," Rio admitted softly. "And she is trying, but Rome wasn't built in a day. It might be centuries before she unlearns the bad." Death looked away with a slight frown. There was an eternity laying in front of them, but could she live with the constant back and forth? Could she live with watching her wife fight off the sliver of good in her just so she would never have to face her past?

    "Mother!" Nicky launched himself at her, his tiny arms wrapping around her neck. She steadied herself with a gentle breeze against her back. "Buenos dias, querido. How did we sleep?"

    "Muy bien," he told her with a grin. "See? I remembered!"

    Her heart burst with pride. "You did!" She pressed a kiss to his cheek. "They've made breakfast for you. Why don't you give them all a hug and a 'thank you' for being so nice?" Nicky stepped away to do as his mother suggested with his rosy cheeks. He politely asked Wanda if he could have a plate to eat, hands clasped behind his back like a small gentleman. The child caught his mother staring and sent her a toothy grin. "Are you gonna eat with me, Mother?"

    "I'm not, querido. I don't need to eat." She pulled out a chair for him to sit at and pushed his seat in once he was ready.

    "How old is he?" Alice asked carefully. "He's adorable."

    Rio smiled, a hand fixing her son's messy bed-head. "Seven," she told the trio. "He'll be eight next fall."

    Nicky looked at her as he shoved a forkful of eggs into his mouth. She wrinkled her nose at him, grinning ear to ear.

    Billy served himself and sat to Nicky's left. "How does it work? Our bringing him back?" "He'll age normally. Live a witch's lifespan, and then come back home with me." She pushed away the fear that came with having a living child in favor of facing Alice. "The same is to be said for you. No one but Wanda, and potentially Billy, will live forever. You still have a mortal's soul. You will do well to take care of it."

    "What's a soul look like, Mother?"

    "It's diamond-shaped and matches the person's personality. You might hear mortals talk about auras and spiritual colors. I see those, sometimes. But I can hear souls, too." She gave up trying to fix his hair and moved her hands to her lap.

    "That's cool," Alice told her. She moved to sit next to Billy, her own plate in hand. "Do you have a soul?" Her eyes widened. "Not that you're soulless! I just meant, y'know, does Death technically have a soul?"

    Rio put the poor woman out of her suffering. "I do, but it's nothing like any of yours. I will always exist, whether I like it or not. There will always be souls of some sort to ferry over." By Agatha, she was tired. But Death kept going.

    "...And Agatha?" Billy chanced. His eyes flicked up to meet her gaze.

    "Modified by the Ancient Ones. She won't die as long as they'll have her." Rio scoffed. "And they'll have her for some time."

    "How come Mama's different looking?"

    Death grinned. "That would be her own doing, querido. She doesn't understand how beautiful she is, so she tries to look how she thinks she should. Mama's still a bit shy around other witches."

    "I know," Nicky sighed. "She wouldn't sing me to sleep last night. I liked my bed, though!" So pure. So innocent. So susceptible to Agatha's mood swings now.

    "Your mama will sing to you tonight." Or else! Rio stood. "I'll go pick out some clothes for you to wear, mijo. You need a bath."

    He pouted. "They don't have any rivers here, though. I don't want to have to walk all over the place to find one."

    "Querido, the world has moved past that. I'll show you once you've finished eating." Nicky's eyes lit up. "Is the water warm now, Mother?"

    She grinned. "Steaming."

    Her son gasped, his whole face a mask of pure joy. "I love it here! I love nature, Mother, but I hated the river. It was always so cold."

    Rio decided she would never tell him the water only felt that way because of his poor circulation. His feeble heart couldn't withstand the temperature. His lungs, terribly battered with illness and decay. "No cold water unless you want to go swimming in the summer." She hummed to herself. "We should probably have a healing witch looking over you...just in case."

    "In case what?" He looked at her, his green eyes pure.

    "All children get checked to make sure they're not dirty and stinky and covered in germs," she told him. Rio pinched his nose with a grin. It was enough of an answer to satisfy him. She dropped a kiss to the top of his head. "Behave for Wanda and the others. Finish your food, too."

    "Okay," he told her, another forkful raised to his lips.

    Rio patted Billy's shoulder before slipping out of the room.

    She kept her word to the young Maximoff and left Agatha alone. They'd talk about whatever the hell had happened when no one else was around. For now, she shifted through boxes in the room Nicky had claimed. Rio could have sworn Agatha had bought a bunch of clothes while under Wanda's spell. Sure enough, clothes for a young boy were neatly folded and tucked away. Rio picked out jean overalls, a simple enough t-shirt, and socks. She briefly wondered how much agony Agatha must have been in while under the mind spell. Just looking at all the toys and clothes that had been bought and stashed made Rio feel queasy. "Excuse me," Rebecca Kaplan said from the doorway. The woman did her best not to shake in front of Death.

    "Did you need something?" she asked evenly. Rio knew the mortal posed no real threat. She tucked the clothes under her arm and stepped closer to the Kaplan.

    "Do you know how long Agatha wants us to stay? Jeff and I need to get back and check on Greg."

    Oh right... "Just until lunch. She wanted the boys to have a little bit more time together before Billy left." Rio gestured to the hallway, hoping to get by.

    Rebecca gave a small laugh as she stepped back. "I know we got off on the wrong foot when we first met. You understand, I'm sure. I just wanted to make sure my son was safe." Rio weighed her options. Rebecca was just an ordinary, magicless woman who had been dragged into hers and Agatha's mess. The mortal was just a mother, like so many before her, who wanted the same thing. There had been strong words and looks, but that was all they had been. So, if she could be cordial, Death could be, too. There was no reason not to be, not anymore. Agatha was alive and had the power to take her son back if need be. "I do," she told Rebecca. "Wanda, Alice, and Billy made breakfast. You should get you something to eat."

    She wasn't offended by the shock on the other woman's face. No, Rio was glad for that specific reaction. It meant the mortal understood that an olive branch had been extended her way. The Kaplan left her in the hallway, a small smile on her lips. They weren't friends, far from it, but it was a good first step. Now, she just needed Agatha to make the same effort. Rio prepared the tub with warm water and a few bath toys. She cut a small hole through the fabric of the Universe to grab soaps from Agatha's old cabin. They smelt of home. Of simpler days. When Agatha would laugh and smile unhindered. When the dream of starting a family hadn't soured and rotted by the demands of the Ancient Ones. Death sat with the gnawing feeling in her gut before leaving to gather her son.

    The Green Witch re-entered the kitchen to find most of coven had woken up. Tommy dashed around her with a whirl, voice distorted as he spoke nearly at the speed of light. She reached out to stop him with a stern look. "You'll trip," she told him firmly. Wanda heard her and turned around. She gave the speeding teen a look. "Not inside the house, Tommy. And definitely not around people."

    "I got excited," he told the women. "Not much space to run around in my cell." "How did you end up in there?" Rio asked, curiosity getting the best of her. The long-haired boy scratched at the back of his head with a laugh. "I sorta...vaporized a school during a track meet. Then I ran from the cops and they had some lame guy with a stupid looking hairline lock me up. I think he called himself a doctor, too, which didn't make any sense." Tommy rolled his eyes at the memory.

    Death chuckled darkly. "That was you?" She grinned widely. "Oh, you'll fit in nicely. With the four of you, I'll never have a lull in the year."

    "I don't think you should be proud of that," Wanda told her. "That must have been horrifying!"

    Tommy shrugged. "As if I'd cry over those assholes. Kinda wish they were slowly burned to a crisp instead."

    Oh, he was Agatha's son alright! No remorse for those who had hurt him. Rio nodded, grin still in place. "You kept me pretty busy," she told him. "I was impressed. It was nice not to see carnage for once. We'll be in touch."

    Wanda made a face. "Well, still, let's not encourage that kind of behavior." She pulled Tommy off to the side. "Why don't we think of a way to convince Agatha to let me build an indoor track for you?"

    "Why not do it regardless?" Rio heard Tommy tell her.

    Agatha was going to have her hands full with Nicky and Tommy. That much, Death could tell. She looked around until she found Nicky sitting on a counter. He was hidden by Agatha's imposing form. They spoke softly with one another. Rio walked over and stopped at her wife's side. "You're up late," she told the goddess with a lilt in her tone. It had meant to be gentle teasing, but she'd underestimated her wife's crankiness.

    The other immortal fixed her with a look. "Don't start."

    "I'm not," she lied. Rio raised her hands in defense.

    The witch pulled out a mug for coffee with a groan. "I don't want to talk about it right now." "I know. I don't want to either. I can't guarantee I won't slit your throat," Rio huffed. She smiled sweetly to Nicky. "Ready for your bath, querido?"

    He nodded. "Is the water warm?"

    "Of course," she told him. Death picked him up, holding him against her side. "Soon, you'll be too big."

    Nicky preened. "I hope to be big and tall like my brothers!"

    "Eat all your vegetables then," she told him. Rio threw Agatha a look. "Later."

    Nicholas bobbed a toy boat, his mouth imitating a whistle, while Rio lathered his hair with soap. He giggled to himself as a rubber duck floated by. She gently probed his soul, checking for any illnesses or residual symptoms of having been dead for centuries. It was almost like Billy had completely reincarnated her son, but kept the memories. It was no small feat. Such a skill was reserved for the Ancient Ones. If he honed his skills, he would probably get elevated to their status in the Universe. Or, if he followed Agatha's lead, be put on a leash to keep him in check.

    "Ready for me to rinse?" She asked him.

    The boy nodded. He closed his eyes and held his breath.

    Rio poured a cupful of water onto his head, careful not to drown him. She grinned as he shook his head. "Was that too much?"

    "No," he laughed. "I just wanted to shake my head like a wolf."

    "No wolves here," Agatha said from the doorway. She held her mug of coffee in both hands, watching the two over the rim. "Which means you can stay outside longer. I'll have a fire pit put in for old time's sake."

    Rio looked over her shoulder and pushed her irritation away for the moment. "I need a wash cloth," she told her wife calmly.

    Agatha set her mug down and pulled one out of the linen closet. She passed the small towel over to Death, a smile twitching her lips upward. "That one has ducks on it," she stated a bit awkwardly.

    "I like ducks," Nicky exclaimed with wide eyes. "I can wash myself, Mother. Mama showed me how."

    Rio turned away from her son to give him privacy. She moved to sit on the lid of the toilet, eyes taking in half-dressed witch. "Did you eat something?"

    "I stole some bacon from Jen and a piece of toast from Billy."

    Death hummed to herself. It would be so easy to point out that those happened to be her victims from last night's outburst, but she kept her mouth shut. Nicky didn't need to see them fight. "The Kaplans are leaving after lunch," she informed. "So if you need to talk to anyone, do it before then."

    "I don't need to," Agatha told her. "They know where to find me."

    Rio fought the urge to sigh loudly and dramatically. "If that's what you want," she told her wife instead.

    "All done," Nicky announced. He took the cup from his mother and rinsed himself off. "Can I get a towel now?"

    The Green Witch turned around and helped him step out of the tub to wrap him up. "What did you think of your first real bath, mijo?"

    The boy beamed. "Much better than a river," he told her. Nicky hugged the towel around himself as Agatha squeezed in to help him dress.

    "Wait until you're big enough to shower on your own," Agatha told him. "It's like standing in the summer rain."

    "I missed the rain," he admitted. "Mama, when will it rain again?"

    "I'm not sure. You're mother might now."

    Rio closed her eyes, putting on a show as she sensed the weather pattern. "In two days time...around...lunch time," she told the pair. Rio opened her eyes to find them both looking at her with matching grins.

    "I'm gonna tell Billy and Tommy," Nicky cheered. He dashed out of the bathroom in his overalls and bare feet.

    "Nicky, your socks," Agatha yelled after him. She groaned out a sigh. "His feet are going to be so dirty now."

    "Let him have his fun." Rio unplugged the drain before facing her wife. "Have you talked to Billy?"

    The goddess pursed her lips. "No..."

    "What happened last night?"

    Agatha hugged herself, a hand propped under her chin. "It was nothing. Just a little misunderstanding."

    Billy and Agatha, one in the same. Rio exhaled through her nose, hands gripping her knees. "Agatha..." How to put her next words delicately? "You need to apologize to him...and the rest of your coven."

    The woman glared daggers at her. "I'm not apologizing to them! They're the ones who put that abomination of a movie on."

    "Agatha," Rio bit out. "I told Billy to put Frozen on. If you're going to throw a fit over something as little and menial as a children's movie, Nicky doesn't need to stay with you." The goddess rose to full height, panic in those steel-grey eyes. "You are not taking him from me again!"

    "That's not what I meant," she told her wife, keeping her tone even. "But you need to get yourself under control. You have three boys who look up to you and a coven of witches that admire you to varying degrees. They're scared. They don't know what to make of their world. Now isn't the time to try and put walls back up. They don't need that. They need a mother and a mentor." Rio stood slowly. Agatha was gaining that wounded look faster than she had the last time they spoke like this. She took her wife's hands in hers, squeezing them. "You don't have to be scared. This is your last chance to make things right with everyone. Don't push them away."

    Agatha looked away, her jaw visibly clenching and unclenching.

    She'd pushed too hard again. Now, Agatha was going to shut down. Rio looked down at their hands with a sigh. "Think about what I said." She released shaking hands and stepped towards the doorway. "Te veo," she muttered.

    Agatha sucked in a shaky breath, a tear sliding down her cheek.

    And A Fulfilling Home Life Chapter Summary Billy has a new shadow.

    Chapter Notes Me holding a pewpew to my brain: Write some fucking fluff, dammit!

    But in other news! Expect some earlier chapters this week.

    Wednesday, or Thursday (not too sure just yet), might be exceedingly long. (But again, might be Thursday.) I'll post the super long one and then give myself a couple of days to get caught up in future chapters before posting the next one. I promise that it will not leave it on a cliff-hanger, hence its longness. I will be making you cry, though. So happy holidays or whatevs! :P See the end of the chapter for more notes Billy jolted awake, his wards making his skin tingle. He sat up and came face to face with none other than Rio. She was dressed more casually than the last time she'd made an unexpected night-time visit. Death wore a black sweat top with black joggers. "What time is it?" he rasped. Billy turned his phone over. "Oh..." It was five minutes before his alarm was set to go off. "Good morning, I guess."

    Rio threw a sprig of lavender at him. "Good morning."

    He took the plant and sniffed it. "Thanks! Is there a way I can preserve it or...?" "Agatha hasn't taught you that yet?"

    "We sort of got side-tracked by the whole 'stuck in a decoration' bit," he reminded. The teen tucked it into his pillow. "That's fine. It can help me sleep."

    Rio remained planted at the foot of his bed as Billy riffled through his drawers for something to wear. "How's school?"

    She must be bored... "It's good. Teddy and I are thinking about joining Mathletes. Our Calculus teacher thinks we could actually win in this year."

    Death narrowed her eyes. "Do you talk to Agatha about this stuff?"

    Billy thought back on his time with his mentor. "Yeah. I guess I bored her with it, didn't I?" He laughed to himself, suddenly feeling childish.

    "If she never left, she enjoyed it," Rio informed. "What're you wearing for school? Don't you have any natural colors to wear?"

    The teen filed the information away for another time. He'd wasted too many precious minutes standing in the middle of his room. "What? Black is a natural color," he argued with a quirked lip. "What would you have me wear?"

    Death stalked over to his closet and laughed. "How much junk do you have in here? Is that Lilia's house in there?"

    Billy laughed nervously. "I didn't want someone to take her stuff now that she's gone. She sacrificed herself for us. It was the least I could do."

    Rio shrugged and stepped into the pocket reality to dig through his clothes. She grabbed a baby-blue polo and a pair of cream slacks. "There you go. Repressed nerd." The teen fell into a fit of laughter. "I am not wearing that combo. I'll get bullied." "You don't have anything purple, red, navy, or green," she told him. "Hard to give you something good to wear."

    "Why those colors specifically?"

    Death looked at him almost as if she were stunned. "So, you have some of your family with you."

    He blinked. "I can change the color of my clothes," he reminded. The teen took the light blue polo and focused on changing the dye until it was a rich violet. "How's that?" "A bit too bright."

    Billy chuckled and focused once more. When he opened his eyes, he found he'd changed the color to a lilac. The embroidered logo had also changed to that of a red rose motif. "Now, what do you think?"

    "Much better." Rio held up the pants. "Let's see what else you can do." It took Billy an extra fifteen minutes to get ready. The pair eventually agreed a nice pair of blue jeans worked with the shirt. Not too nerdy for him, not too drab for Rio. She followed him downstairs and greeted the Kaplan's. Billy worried they would argue about her being there but was pleasantly surprised when his mother greeted the cosmic entity warmly. "Oh...Where did you get that shirt?" His mother cooed. She cradled his face to pepper it with kisses. "You look so handsome!"

    "I made it," he told his parents proudly. "So, I always have my family with me." Rio nodded, a smile gracing her lips.

    "That's sweet," his father told him. "But you might want to dine and dash. You've got five minutes before the bell, buddy."

    Billy threw a sandwich together and was out the door in two. He threw his car in reverse only to startle as Rio jumped in. "What...What are you doing?"

    "Making sure you get to school on time."

    The teen snapped his mouth shut as he felt time distort. He pressed his foot down on the gas and weaved through the stand-still traffic. Had it not been for his stepmom, Billy would have been ten minutes late. He jumped out of his car and raced towards the front doors. The teen startled a second time when Rio appeared out of nowhere to open the door for him. "Have a good day at school," she told him.

    "Thanks," he breathed. Billy risked his life and gave her a hug. "If Agatha doesn't trap you in Westview, you should join us for dinner."

    Rio smiled. "We'll see. Now, go. Go be a nerd and save those exponents." Billy entered the school with a laugh.

    The final bell rang, freeing the teen from his daily confines. He left his last class to find Teddy. His boyfriend was exactly where he'd find him. The jock shut his locker to fix him with a look. "Who told you you could look that cute today?"

    Billy blushed. "Rio thought I should shake things up for once."

    "Not that I don't like your goth aesthetic, but this is nice. You look...distinguished." Teddy stepped away from the shiny red rectangles to walk the Kaplan-Maximoff-Harkness-Vidal to his car. "Did you understand our Physics assignment? I'm still a bit confused." "I think it's just a modern take on how to read a sundial," Billy told him. Once they were in the parking lot, he took his boyfriend's hand. "I mean, why else would we need to know how to calculate the time of day using a flagpole? I guess Mr. Dahl thinks society's going to collapse within the next ten years or something."

    Teddy laughed. "Yeah, no that makes sense. He gives doomsday prepper vibes." The two jumped as a blur approached them.

    "Bro, what's up!" Tommy tackled his brother for a noogie.

    Billy laughed, pulling away. "Tommy? What are you doing over here?"

    His twin grinned widely, a bit like Rio if Billy was being honest. "Mom's cool and all, but I couldn't just stand around all day in that house. Oh, Nick says 'hi', by the way." "Did you leave without telling anyone?" Teddy asked carefully.

    Tommy shrugged. "I'll be back before they notice. Right now, they think I'm taking a nap." The teen blew a raspberry. "So...what're we doing?"

    "Uh...Uh, we were just headed home." Billy shook his head lightly. "We can go somewhere for a bite before you have to head back." He considered asking about how the others were, but honestly, he needed the break.

    "Snacks with the bro and his boyf!" Tommy threw his arms over their shoulders. "I'm starvin', man."

    Teddy laughed. "You're crazy. Let's go see if White Mana's open. I could use a bite, too." The twins got into Billy's Subaru. Billy and Teddy waved before pulling out of the parking lot.

    "It's a bit weird, you being in a different house," Tommy confessed. He shifted until he was manspreading the way a certain witch had.

    "Yeah, it is. I guess things feel strange now that you're in a new place entirely." "Did you see what they did to Mom's house?"

    Billy nodded. "I mean, I don't remember it, but that's gotta suck for her. Do you...remember it?"

    "It's kinda fuzzy. I remember Agnes, though. She was always nice to us." "Huh..." He'd never stopped think about his life with 'Agnes'. Sure, she had been tricking Wanda, but she actually spent time with them. It was weird now, knowing what he knew. "Like whole memories, or just flashes?"

    "A few whole memories. Dude, she totally kidnapped us," Tommy said with a grin. "We were living a superhero movie and everything."

    "I don't remember," Billy admitted. "I can't remember anything before the hex fell apart." He wished he could. Had practically begged his powers to give him a glimpse or two. Night after night, nothing ever came. Perhaps it was for the best.

    Teddy greeted the brothers as they slid into the booth. He put his menu aside and leaned in. "Did you know that Michael and Jennifer hooked up?"

    Billy gasped; a hand pressed to his chest. "Bitch, you're joking!"

    "Who're they?" Tommy asked. "Are they also witches?"

    "Pfft, they wish they were!" Billy pulled out his phone. "They're these two kids in our class that have been talking shit about each other for years! Jennifer called him a 'shrimp-dicked mama's boy,' and Michael fucking lost it."

    Teddy snickered. "Turns out it was all just foreplay. She wanted that cookie so damn bad!" Tommy scrolled through the pictures of his brother's classmates. "Hey, you've got a good- looking class." He zoomed in on a few random students. "Maybe I should pop by one of these days."

    "You won't like them. I took the sweetest guy around," Billy told his brother. He smiled over at Teddy with a light blush.

    "Guess I'll take a look at the girl's 'til another one goes by." He slid the phone over to the witch. Tommy stole the menu and scanned the glossy book for something to eat. The trio ate and laughed without a care. Teddy and Tommy began to discuss lifting weights and other jock related things that Billy wasn't as interested in. He sipped at his tea, just letting the calmness wash over him. Billy wondered if this how things would have played out had Wanda actually given birth to him and his twin. Would he have met Teddy at a school function? Would Tommy have made friends with Teddy first and introduced them? He would never know the answer, but Billy knew that he liked how simple everything was for him in that very moment.

    "Ah, shit! I gotta get back before one of them realizes I snuck out." Tommy hopped over the side of the booth and ruffled his younger brother's hair. "I'll see ya 'round, bro." He bumped fists with Teddy. "Bet you can't hit 350 before we meet up next time." "You're on," Teddy told him with a laugh.

    The speedster twin left the restaurant in a blur, napkins floating into the air. "I bet Agatha's gonna get onto him for sneaking out," Teddy laughed. He popped a fry into his mouth.

    "She might encourage it. Agatha likes it when someone does the bad thing." Billy placed a tip on the table. "I better get going. I need to tell my parents I invited Rio over for dinner." The other teen's brows raised. "Really? I thought they didn't get along?" Billy shrugged. "I guess they worked something out. She showed up this morning and talked to them for a bit while I packed my lunch."

    "What is your life?" Teddy said with a laugh. "Let me know if I need to whisk you away at any point."

    "I should be fine. Rio's not like that. She's really chill and easy to talk to." He stood and cleared his mess. "I bet you could ask her all sorts of questions about famous people that have died."

    "Thursday," his boyfriend told him. "I wanna pick Agatha's brain, too. When those two get together, it's like watching The Addams Family."

    Billy laughed as they left the building. "They could totally swap roles if they wanted to," he told the other teen. "I'll force them to watch it later." Billy made a face. "Well, I'll suggest it. I don't want a repeat of the other night."

    "Did you guys talk about it?"

    "No...But I'm not going to worry about it. She usually waits a few days and then we have a little chat." Billy unlocked his car. "She should be fine by Thursday." "Well, I hope you have a great dinner tonight. Let me know how it goes." Teddy pressed a kiss to his cheek. "See ya."

    Billy blushed before getting in his car.

    "Billy, can you get the door?" His mother shouted from the kitchen.

    The teen ran down the stairs and pulled the door open. He felt his mouth drop open, eyes wide. "You're...You look...Whoa," Billy told his fourth mother. He shook his head. "Sorry, come on in."

    Rio drifted in, eyeing the place as if she hadn't been in his house multiple times. Death had pulled her hair up and wore a sensible suit. Her blazer, paired with a purple button-up shirt, flapped lightly as she turned towards the kitchen. Billy had been in so much awe of her outfit that he never even realized she had a bottle of wine in her hands. Rio passed it off to Rebecca with a warm grin. "I hope you're fans of dry red."

    Jeff snuck a glance at the bottle, his eyes nearly popping out of his skull. "Is that a real bottle of Chateau Lafon-Rochet!"

    Billy looked at his mother with a quirked brow. "It's just wine, Dad." "Billy, this is a $600 bottle of wine," his father exclaimed.

    "I made sure to have a casket undergo the mevushal process under the supervision, and accordance with, Rabbi Katz of Paris. He owed me a favor," Rio explained as if the gesture was no big deal.

    The teen found himself staring at the bottle just as much as his father was. "You just...You just have contacts for kosher wine?" Billy asked Death.

    "Oh, come on you two," Rebecca told the males. "Thank..."

    "...Rio," Death told the woman.

    "Thank Rio for the gift. Don't be rude." She gave Rio a hug before moving away to chill the bottle.

    Billy watched his father eye the wine until it was out of sight. "Hungry?" he asked the cosmic entity.

    Rio laughed. "I almost starved to Death on my way here."

    The teen grinned. "You're terrible." He led her over to the dining room. "How was work?" "Long," Death drawled. She made herself comfortable in a seat across from him. "You?" "Teddy and I are gonna save Math's butt," he told her. "That, and we're looking forward to Coven Night. Tommy may or may not have snuck out to see us."

    "Crazy tyke," Rio said sarcastically. Her eyes followed Jeff and Rebecca as they served the table. "Salmon...sauteed mushrooms...roasted carrots." She hummed in appreciation. "Much better than the dishes of old."

    "Do you eat?" Billy asked her, brows furrowed. He really hoped she did or inviting her to dinner was going to seem rather silly on his part.

    "I don't need to, but I can partake in this mortal custom." She picked up a fork, eyeing it curiously. "The last time I had a meal, the Bubonic Plague was ravaging Europe. There was a group of infected Flagellants who sat down for a meal, unaware they had single handedly spread the bacteria all over the continent. I arrived, minutes before they were to expire, and was invited to sit and break bread. None of them continued their route after that evening." Billy cleared his throat. "I'm surprised you can remember everything." "Billy," Rebecca huffed. "Don't be rude."

    "I'm not," he told her with a chuckle. "The entirety of human history is in her head. That's why Teddy and I go to her for help with our homework."

    Rio smiled, quiet and a tad pensive.

    "I'm scared to ask...but what made Agatha special?" Jeff questioned.

    The teen recalled Rio's first memory of his mother. He bowed his head, stabbing at a mushroom.

    "We just have a unique relationship," Death answered. She speared a morsel of salmon with her fork. "When you get to be as old as I am, you tend to have favorites." "Jeff and I met at a mutual friend's wedding. He was the Best Man." Rebecca grinned at her husband. "He loved to dance and wouldn't stop bugging me until I gave him a turn." Red and blues interchanged as a silent party spun and swayed with one another. A young man flashed a dashing grin. A hand was extended and taken.

    Billy blinked, his mother's memory disappearing as quickly as it had come. He laughed to himself, catching the attention of the adults. "Who told you to wear a bright yellow tie?" His parents shared a look.

    "What was that?" his father asked him. Jeff squinted. "I don't think I wore a yellow tie. Did I?"

    "It's been so long," Rebecca said with a nervous laugh. "You must have seen the wrong picture."

    Billy mentally kicked himself. He'd forgotten his parents didn't know the full extent of his magic, much less the fact that he could read minds. "Oh...yeah. I keep getting that one and the picture of Uncle Andrew mixed up." He shook his head with a chuckle before stuffing his mouth.

    The tension ebbed away as his parents breathed a sigh of relief.

    Rio eyed him discreetly, but he noticed. "How long have you two been married?" she asked the couple, moving the conversation from the teen.

    "Eighteen years," Jeff supplied easily. "And we've loved every minute of it." "That's a good amount of time," Rio told them. "Agatha and I were married around the turn of the century...18th century, that is. Nothing in a church, of course. Just a simple exchanging of vows under a starlit sky."

    Billy braced himself as another memory hit him.

    "I take thee, Lady Death, in this life and the next."

    The memory was much shorter. Almost like it had been cut off.......Billy risked a glance in Death's direction. She met his gaze, chewing her food slowly and carefully. He gave a small nod. At least she didn't look mad at him.

    "Speaking of weddings and days gone by," Billy began, "but what was with your dresses?" Rio laughed softly. "To which are you referring to? I've had many throughout the centuries." "What's this about a dress?" Rebecca asked with a laugh.

    "I can appear in a number of forms and outfits. When I go to collect a soul, the person will see me in a way that is most comforting to them. But Billy seems to be questioning my sense of fashion when I began courting Agatha. Is that right?"

    Billy nodded, swallowing his mouthful. "Victorian lace and all that mud," he said with a shiver. "And probably barefoot the entire time."

    "And you'd be right," she told him with a grin. "Mud is good for the soul. Rejuvenates you. Gives lives and continues the flow of nature." Rio took a sip from her wine glass. "The first dress I ever wore was for Agatha. I'm not sure if you were able to see it, but it was a simple one for the time period. Green, of course, with brown laces."

    "An old lady had just died," he said, smiling at the memory.

    "An old biddy with a lot of nerve," Death hissed. "She complained the whole journey. I nearly left her to fend for herself."

    "Why didn't you?"

    "She was Agatha's nursemaid when that woman refused to take care of her." Hazel eyes hardened as teeth were bared.

    Billy toasted the Green Witch right as his father said, "You sound like a stalker." It amused Death. Tickled the ire right out of her features. She grinned salaciously. "Only for Agatha."

    The teen was quick to tease her, eyes twinkling with the same mischief as his goddess mother. "Simp."

    Dinner done, dishes washed, and parents showering for bed, Billy sought solace in his bedroom. He jumped for the third time that day.

    "Can you wear a bell or something? You're going to give me a heart attack." "I couldn't get that lucky," Rio laughed. She stole his desk chair, perching delicately on the small seat. "Did you hear it, or did you go into my head for a second?" Billy flopped onto his bed with a groan. "It's a new, secret third thing." He rolled over to face her. "I can see the memory, but I'm not in it. Does that make sense?"

    Death nodded. "When did this start?"

    "After we got back to Westview. It doesn't happen often. Just with intense emotions." He sighed heavily. "It's annoying."

    "That's what it means to be a Maximoff," she teased. Rio produced her knife, playing with the blade as if it weren't the most dangerous object to man. "Are you okay?" He pursed his lips in thought, nose scrunching lightly. "I think so. It's nothing like living the memory. None of that was fun, by the way. I don't know how you do your job every day." "Someone had to. All those lost souls in the beginning...I couldn't leave them there." Her face softened as she thought back on her drawn-out existence. This time, no memory snuck past Billy's defenses.

    "Thanks for coming to dinner," he told her with a yawn. "It means a lot to me." Rio smiled. "Whenever you need me," she laughed. "Maybe Jeff will let you have some of that wine."

    Billy laughed. He rolled onto his back to look at his ceiling. "He's going to sleep with that bottle. I can't believe you bought that just for a small dinner."

    "I needed to wow them to ease the tension. You're all still mortal. I'm the Big Bad in every one of your stories."

    He turned his gaze towards her. "We mortals are a bit daft. None of us know how to appreciate a good thing 'til it's gone."

    Death hummed in thought. "You should get some sleep. That brain of yours needs it." She used a small gust of wind to roll him off the bed.

    He pulled himself up with a huffed laugh. "Concussions are good sleep aid methods," he teased. Billy stretched, a yawn tugging at his lips. "I gotta change. Get out." "I'll be in the closet...snooping." Rio closed the door behind her. She probably wanted to see what all he'd collected from the victims of the Road.

    Billy washed his face and changed into his night clothes. He returned to his room, ready to throw himself down for another round of weird dreams, but once again, he was startled by Death. The teen chucked his laundry at her.

    She let it hit her in the chest, an amused laugh filling the air. "I figured you would learn to sense me by now, but I can see that's going to take some time."

    Billy kicked his clothes away and climbed into his bed. "Is there something I should be feeling when you're around?"

    Rio regarded him for a moment, head tilted. "You're a weird kid, Billy Maximoff." She plopped down next to him, legs crossing. "You don't feel anything?"

    He shook his head. "I don't know you're there until I see you. The only time I sense you is while I'm asleep." Billy made himself comfortable, another yawn escaping. "Agatha would make the room feel cold whenever she was nearby. But that's the only time I've sensed someone hovering."

    The Green Witch hummed in thought. "Well, we'll try to figure that bit out later. You stay up any later and you'll be late." She stood to tuck him in as if he were a small child. Billy supposed he was. Perhaps that was why he felt warm and safe and comfortable. His eyes began to droop as Rio switched his lamp off. The room was blanketed in darkness, but he knew Death was still there, sitting at his side. He struggled to open his yes to see if she was looking at him or not. Ultimately, he failed. Billy summoned the last of his willpower to deliver a sincere, "Goodnight, Mom...."

    Rio froze at his parting words as Billy fell asleep. She smiled to herself, basking in the warmth of that three-letter word. Death rose and worked her magic, humming Nicky's Ballad. She wouldn't be able to stay the whole night, but her little helper would be sure to let her know when her...her son was awake. The Green Witch set her present aside in a spot it would appreciate before checking over the boy once more. Pleased, she slipped away into the Ether. So many souls, so much time.

    Billy stirred, a scent tickling his nose. He stretched, blinking awake. Resting on his windowsill was a bushy bonsai tree. The teen grinned widely, leaning in closely to inspect his new friend. Verdant, tiny leaves sprouted so cutely and proudly. Billy vowed to take the best care of the plant or die trying. (Well, maybe not die...He would just as Rio for help.) "What do you think?"

    He turned to find Rio standing in the doorway, leaning against the frame. "I love it! I'm gonna see if the library has any books on how to care for one. Oh! I need a name for him." "Him?"

    "Yeah, you don't name your plants?" Billy went back to cooing over the tree. "Bobby," he said confidently. "Bobby the Bonsai!" Billy pet the gravel protecting the soil. "Bobby, you let me know if this is too much sunlight for you, okay?"

    Rio chuckled behind him. "He said he would." She cleared her throat. "I can't make things out of thin air like your mother, so I brought you a mister. They need moisture in the air to help them grow."

    Billy beamed. "You're the best!" He tackled her in a bear hug. "Come take a picture with Bobby. I'll send it to Teddy and Tommy. They're gonna be so jealous." The teen vibrated with energy.

    Rio obliged if only to get away from the infectious, bounding excitement rolling off the teen. "You're going to be late," she warned.

    The Maximoff nearly dropped his phone. "Oh shit!" He rushed over to his closet. "This would be so much easier if we just had a uniform at school," Billy told her. "I miss the days of top hats and arrow collars," Death lamented. "It made burying people easier too."

    Billy hopped out as he pulled a boot on. "Why's that?"

    "Their wedding outfits usually became their burial clothes," Rio informed. She watched him before laughing. "Do you ever get up on time?"

    "Uh....no." He rushed past her to fix his hair and wash his face. "I mean, I used to. But then Agatha moved in and would annoy me, so I started taking my time in the mornings to stress her out. Now, it's a bit of a bad habit."

    Death rolled her eyes. "You two...I wonder what would happen if you two were left to your own devices."

    "Oh, before you two got back together, we messed with each other a lot!" Billy made for the stairs. He struggled to slip his arms through his backpack straps without tumbling down the steps. At least Death would already be there to collect him. "One time, Agatha told me I wouldn't be able to get ready in fifteen minutes. I stayed in bed until I had only fifteen minutes to get dressed and get to school. I was late, obviously, but she threw a fit the entire time."

    Rio followed behind him with slow, calculated steps. "That doesn't surprise me. She probably cussed you out, didn't she?"

    "She called me, and I quote, a 'fribble gallinipper without an ounce of wit or sense of fashion.' So, you know, that was a fun morning."

    Death grinned widely as they entered the kitchen. "She called you a dumb, blood-sucking bug. That's so Agatha," Rio said, all but sighing dreamily.

    Billy rolled his eyes as he packed himself a lunch. "You guys will find anything cute for each other. Don't think I didn't see you two flirting during her trial."

    Rio smirked. "That was fun. Until her mother showed up. Then it was less fun." He stuffed his lunch bag into his backpack. "Well, I'll do my best not to summon the Ghost of Christmas Past the next time a ouija board is pulled out."

    "Pfft. That movie was good until they made Ebenezer a good guy. Some people don't need to be redeemed." Death sifted through their mail. "You've got about thirteen minutes now." Billy found his parents to give them a hug and kiss. Then, he rounded on the Green Witch. "Rio~"

    She glared at him. "No."

    "Come on~. You don't want me to be late, do you?" He opened his arms to the woman. "Bring it in."

    "No."

    Billy waited. If he was late, he was late, but he wasn't leaving until Rio initiated the hug. His grin widened as the witch visibly struggled to keep herself in place.

    Finally, she stormed over and gave him a hug. "There. Happy?"

    "My kiss?" he asked, batting his eyelashes.

    "I hate you," she growled. Still, Death pressed a kiss to his temple. "Go. Don't die or whatever."

    Billy waved before running out of the house. (Okay, he totally cared about not being late!) He got in his car and found his parents, all three, sharing a laugh. He grinned, and threw the car in reverse.

    Chapter End Notes This is the bottle of wine Rio gifted the Kaplans.

    Also, that Physics assignment is a real thing I had to do in class once. That's all I remember from high school Physics.

    Sweetheart...You Okay?

    Chapter Summary I think the title says it all......

    Chapter Notes Happy crying! (I didn't have fun. I cried a lot.)

    See the end of the chapter for more notes Agatha sulked..........for two days.

    She simply refused to leave her bedroom. The others in her house wondered what she could possibly be doing in that tiny room. Well, truth be told, the goddess had turned towards her spell book for comfort. She had to give it to Dolly. The damn thing was filled to the brim with spells, hexes, potions, incantations...A lot. There was a lot in the book. On the third day of ignoring the knocking at her door, Wanda phased into the room, hands on her hips. "Agatha, what are you doing?"

    "Studying," she replied, flipping a page. "I'd like some privacy, if you don't mind." Chaos magic slipped the book from her hands and into a void. "Nicky is asking for you," she told the goddess. "Or had you forgotten about him?"

    Of course, Agatha hadn't. That was why she was hiding. Watching Rio parent him before being chastised like a child herself had left Agatha feeling like absolute shit. It made her think of a certain Harkness. One that turned a coven against her.

    "He's in good hands," Agatha grumbled.

    Wanda shifted deeper into the room, her eyes scanning the scattered clothes and rumpled sheets. "Clearly, this isn't working for you. Get in the shower and-"

    "You don't order me around," she spat.

    "I'm not ordering you," Wanda argued. She made a face before composing herself. "Look, I have to believe you've made some effort to change for Billy to be so attached to you." The Scarlet Witch dared to inch closer. "So...," she wrung her hands, "so I'm willing to make amends."

    "You made me flirt with a man," Agatha growled. "A man!"

    "All I did was turn you into the character you created," Wanda reminded. "Time to grow up and get your head back in the game."

    The witch glowered. "No!"

    "Must you be so difficult." Wanda grabbed her arm and hauled her off the bed. "You're going to spend time with your family, and you're going to like it."

    Agatha dug her heels into the floor with a grunt. "No, you can't make me," she argued. The goddess broke free from the grasp to hide in her closet. "Just...go away, Wanda. You wouldn't understand."

    "What? How you're clearly hiding because you don't want to look Alice in the face?" Agatha pursed her lips and hugged herself.

    "Billy talked to her. That's all you need to do too." Wanda slipped into the small space and sat across from the woman. "What do you have to be scared about? Alice is a sweet girl. She'll understand."

    Would Alice understand? Could she forgive Agatha for killing her? For dragging Sharon along on the Road when she had no business being there? For leaving Lilia to handle her enemies? Why would Alice forgive her for any of those things?

    And then there was Nicky? Her sweet, pure, little Nicky...If he ever found out what she'd done to his lullaby...

    Agatha pressed a hand to her mouth as a sob threatened to tumble from her lips. She squeezed her eyes shut and shook her head. She couldn't, wouldn't, leave the safety of her room until she had a game plan. There was no way she was going to face those demons. She should have stayed a ghost. Should have declined the Ancient Ones' offer. Cool, mist-like hands settled on her shoulders. "You can't hide forever," Wanda told her. "It's good medicine," she parroted.

    Agatha felt a laugh bubble to the surface. "I hate you," she told the witch. Agatha wiped at her face with a groan. "I'm only going out so I can get something to eat." Wanda gasped. "Have you not been eating!"

    "I thought I didn't need that, too," Agatha informed glumly. She patted her stomach with a wince.

    The red head made a face. "How is it that you survived as long as you did? Come on, Aggie." "Don't...That's Rio's name for me," she told the witch. "You don't want to piss her off any more than you already have."

    "She doesn't scare me," Wanda said with a smile. "Now, if you come downstairs, I'll make you those fluffy waffles you liked so much."

    Agatha pursed her lips. "With powdered sugar?"

    "With powdered sugar."

    The goddess groaned. "You drive a hard bargain, Maximoff." She opened the door to the closet. "Let me shower and I'll be down."

    "Don't take too long or I'll let them go cold," Wanda told her before blinking out of existence.

    The resurrected witch quietly descended the stairs and turned into the living room. Tommy and Alice played some trivial game on the television as Jen cheered the two on. She snuck past the trio and stopped in the kitchen. Nicky held a whisk in his hands, trying and failing to stir the thick mixture. She felt a smile grow at the sight. And then it disappeared. Was everyone a better mother than she was?

    Agatha turned to run back to her room.

    "Mama! Mama, look!"

    She cursed herself and turned back towards her son. "Oh! Look at you," she told him through clenched teeth. "Are you helping Wanda bake?"

    Nicky nodded. "We're making waffles!"

    "Mmm. Delicious!" I would love to be under another spell, or stuck in another hex, Agatha groaned inwardly. She walked over to her son and pressed a kiss to his temple. "Don't make too much of a mess."

    "Messes are okay," Wanda told her. "We all make them."

    "Some more than others," she mumbled.

    Wanda gave her a look, but it wasn't one Agatha could identify. "Messes are just accidents with a funny story," the witch told her gently. "Everything's okay so long as we clean it up afterwards."

    Agatha looked away. "And what happens when it stains, huh? You toss it out," she said a bit more forcefully than she meant to.

    "Stains are okay, too." The red-head rested a hand on her shoulder, green eyes meeting steel- grey. "Sometimes, stains make things better. People stain wood, and we find it beautiful, don't we?"

    "What is this?" Agatha huffed. "You gonna give me stuffy and tell me to cry my heart out?" Wanda laughed softly. "We're just talking about messes," she told the goddess. "Nothing more, nothing less."

    She hovered between uncertain and annoyed. "Chef, stir faster. I'm wasting away here." Nicky giggled. "I'm a witch, Mama, not a chef." He got a look on his face that reminded her of Billy. (Funny how quickly things had changed for the witch.) "Can you use your purple to help me?"

    Agatha felt excitement bubble inside her. No one other than Rio had ever been interested in her magic. She felt her face break into a grin. Agatha wiggled her fingers, warming her magic up. "Do you mean this?" she asked, her magic levitating the bowl and whisk. Nicky nodded enthusiastically, his mouth falling open in awe. "Mix it faster!" She was too caught up in entertaining her child to notice the audience forming behind her. Agatha poured the batter into the waffle iron with a wave of her hand. Her body hummed in delight as her magic flowed unhindered. She breathed a sigh of relief at the sensation, eyes sliding shut.

    "Can I do that?" Tommy asked, appearing next to her suddenly.

    If Agatha were an amateur, which she wasn't, the bowl would have dropped out of the air. As it happened, the witch was unfazed by the interruption in her train of thought. She turned to the teen, probing at him with her magic. " 'Fraid not," she told him as gently as she could. "There's not a crumb of magic in your body, kid. Doesn't mean you're not special." Tommy shrugged. "If I shake myself fast enough, I can go through walls," he told her. "That's badass enough for me."

    Agatha grinned widely. "Well, look at you," she praised. "At least one of you doesn't hate their gift. Billy spends so much time moping about his power to the point that I'll wish I'd drained him dry."

    Wanda gave her a look. This one, Agatha could read.

    "Don't worry. Me taking either of your magic is like trying to fill up a shot glass by dumping a five-gallon drum into it." She decided to be a bit showier now that there were people who would appreciate her talents. Agatha had a plate, fork, knife, the syrup, and powdered sugar leave their resting spots to set themselves up on the kitchen table. She gestured towards the waffle iron and flipped the cake.

    "Show off," Alice teased.

    The batter exploded on everyone.

    Agatha gasped as the gooey mixture landed mostly on her. (When had she moved to take the brunt of the impact?) She wiped the batter from her eyes with a sigh. "Guess that was a given. Too much of a good thing."

    "What happened, Mama?"

    "I was having too much fun." It wasn't a total lie. She was having fun. So much so that the reminder of Alice surged her magic. Agatha waved and whipped her hand around quickly. The batter sloughed off the surfaces and regathered in the bowl. "Anyone up for some special seasoned waffles?"

    "Gross," Tommy laughed. "I want one."

    Agatha moved the bowl over to him. "Have at it, kiddo. I need another shower." Her skin was going to be so dry after today.

    Second shower completed; she returned to the kitchen to eat her one good waffle. It was fluffy, if a tad burnt, but good, nonetheless. Agatha munched away with a moan. Her stomach gave her a stern, loud lecture. "Shut up," she told her body. "I'm feeding you now. Get over it."

    Wanda stayed with her in the kitchen, the pair leaning back against the counter. "What...What do you want to do today?"

    Agatha knew that wasn't what the woman was going to ask originally, but didn't push for details. "Well, since you're holding my spell book hostage, why don't we do whatever you want? Not like you're going to let me go back to my room."

    "Nope!" The shorter witch smiled at her. "Have you always been this...I don't know...timid?" Agatha glared at her. "I am not timid," she growled. "Get that silly thought out of your pretty, little head."

    "See...I thought this whole act was your confidence, but it's not." Wanda grinned wider. "All you do is pretend, don't you? You pretend you're untouchable so it can never hurt." The goddess set her plate down roughly. "You've got a lot of nerve," she hissed, but her eyes gave her away. Agatha rubbed the traitorous tear away. "That doesn't mean anything." Wanda quirked a brow. "Are you sure about that?" She cocked her head to the side, that calculating look trained on the older woman. There was a reason the multiverse trembled in fear at the title 'Scarlet Witch'. "What if we went down memory lane, Agatha? Would that make you feel better?"

    The witch could already smell the damp earth of Salem.

    It was enough to have her bolting from the house, the back door slamming open. She sucked in lungful of air after lungful of air. She didn't even know where she was going. She just had to get away from Wanda. Away from those eyes that were peeling back too much too quickly. Agatha tripped with a yelp, barely managing to catch herself on a tree trunk. She dug her nails into the bark, grounding herself with the pain. Hot tears stung at her cheeks. The witch pressed her forehead to the rough, cracked wood and called for the only thing that could ease the hurt.
