    Rio's ears perked as she heard her name be called. She looked at the soul she was ferrying and sighed. Once she was on the boat, it was nearly impossible to leave. Agatha would have to wait until she made it back to shore.

    The goddess clawed at the tree as the last of her sobs shook her shoulders. Damn Wanda Maximoff! Damn that woman! Why did she think she could waltz into her home and just attack her like that? Who gave her the right? Who? Who? Who? When Death didn't appear, Agatha roared into the open air. To hell with Rio! I don't need her, she told herself. But she knew that was a lie. She always needed her wife. Even if they were keeping each other at arm's length, Agatha wanted her by her side. But the entity hadn't appeared, so Agatha would tell herself whatever she needed to hear to feel better about her grief. Just like she did with all her victims.

    The witch resumed her journey away from the house, not caring that she was in her robe and her hair was crazy. In fact, she probably looked like she was in the midst of an episode. (Hardy har har. Go fuck yourself!) Agatha didn't stop until she found herself all the way by the Westview sign. Her neighbor, Herb or whatever, was in his car trying to entice her to get in. She waved her hand and whisked him back to his driveway.

    Agatha froze.

    Alice waved to her in a simple pair of shorts and tank top. "Is everything...okay?" The young witch looked at her, clearly aware things were not.

    The goddess fidgeted, her head shifting as she tried to think of a lie. "How curious! You're jogging! Me too!" It wasn't her best fib. (Fuck, she was really falling apart!) Agatha cleared her throat, flipping her hair in the process.

    Alice, the former cop, nodded slowly. "Well...Since you're jogging," she began, "we should finish out my route together. It looks like it's going to rain soon."

    Nononononononono... "Great," she squeaked out. "Perfect! Yeah, totally!" Agatha wanted to step into oncoming traffic as Alice approached her. "So...let's go. Rio said the rain would be here around lunch time, and time's a-wasting!"

    The goth witch eyed her warily. "I need to tie my shoe first."

    So much lying, but neither knew where to begin telling truths.

    Agatha nodded, waving her arms as nervous energy began to make her fingers and toes tingle. "Y'know...I can just...I can head back on my own. I know the way," she rambled. "Don't even...Just don't even worry about me. You do you, girl. You do it...You do it so well!" That seemed to be the final nail in the coffin for the goddess. Alice jumped up and grabbed Agatha's arm. "Uh...I'm going to worry about you. You're clearly freaking out." Agatha blew a raspberry and fought with her messy hair. "No, no. I'm fine. I'm so, so, so fine."

    Alice fixed her with a look. "What's wrong, Agatha?"

    A small child sitting with a doll in her arms. Lorna Wu singing in the distance. "...I can't do this," Agatha said, turning away. "You can have the house. I'm running away." The protection witch began to panic. "But Nicky!"

    That pushed the goddess to walk faster.

    "Agatha," Alice shouted. "I don't blame you for what happened to me."

    Now, why didn't they just throw a car at her like Wanda had? She would rather be squished like a bug than have to have these hard conversations. Agatha much preferred violence to words. That was how her mother raised her, after all.

    She slowed to a stop, taking a deep breath. If she didn't do this, her mother would have the last laugh again. Agatha turned around and marched back over to the child (because Alice would always be that sweet child). She fixed the witch with a confounded look. "Why not?" Alice shrugged. "Your mother forced you to kill me. Rio said you couldn't control it in that moment. It was too much of a shock after not having magic."

    Agatha reached for her brooch only to claw at her bare neck. "I...I never meant to kill you while on the Road." She grappled with her actions. Stared herself in the mirror, as Rio liked to put it. "But I was going to after the chant."

    The goth nodded slowly, taking the information in. "That makes sense. Billy said the Road was a scam. For what it's worth, I'm glad I got to die for a good reason. And if it weren't for you forcing me to face my family's curse, I wouldn't have ever broken free of it." She took a step forward, face impossibly soft. "Agatha...I think you can be good, too." Agatha blinked back tears as a sword was sunk into her heart. "Don't..." "You can be good," Alice repeated more firmly. "It's possible. I wouldn't have come back if I didn't believe that. I saw the way you were with Billy. There's goodness inside you." She tried to run again, but her legs were frozen in place. "You're just saying that," she tried to growl, but it came out a whimper.

    Alice wrapped her up in a hug. "I'm sorry your mother didn't see that for herself." Agatha choked back a sob. "I'm evil," she told the other woman. "I'm evil." "If you were, you wouldn't have to tell people that."

    The goddess felt another sword sink into her fragile organ. Anymore and she'd die on the spot.

    "Let's go home," Alice told her.

    Agatha let herself be led away as she tried and failed to compose herself. Damn Billy Maximoff for forcing her to be a skeleton! How was she supposed to appear aloof and superior when she forgot how to school her face? Agatha sniffled, her head hanging as she followed the composed witch. She cleared her throat. "Do you even remember me? Really remember me?"

    Alice glanced at her over her shoulder. "What do you mean?"

    Maybe this was the push the child would need to keep Agatha at arm's length. Agatha desperately needed it. Space to breathe. Space to hide. "We met before Billy and I went after you. Your mother had just debuted her version of the Ballad. I was going to kill her for taking my song, but I found you instead."

    Alice was quiet for a long moment. "...You said you had the wrong room." "If it weren't for you, your mother would have died that night." She hoped she said it menacingly enough.

    She hadn't.

    "So, you've always had a soft spot for kids? That's pretty good of you." Agatha glowered. "That wasn't supposed to be your takeaway."

    Alice shrugged, slowing so they could walk side by side. "Why not? You had a line, and you didn't cross it. That's admirable."

    "All of you younger witches are annoying," she huffed. "What happened to holding grudges? Or...Or blood debts?"

    "That kinda died out with your generation," Alice laughed. She grinned up at the older witch. "Maybe that's why you're having a hard time believing you deserve to be forgiven." Agatha fell silent.

    The goth continued, tone light. "Don't worry. You'll believe it one day. Doesn't have to be today. But I know you'll wake up some day, and you won't hate that about yourself." The younger witches were annoying, but in that touching, sentimental kind of way. At least this one gave her enough slack. Gave her the notion that she could forgive herself in the future. It wasn't a ham-fisted demand or instruction. The choice to want to forgive herself was simply hers. Agatha let out a shaky breath. "Thank you."

    By the time they reached her house, Agatha was well and truly drained. Her legs burned from the exercise. Her head pounded from all the crying. She managed to walk in and avoid answering any questions. Agatha didn't even entertain the possibility of crawling up her stairs. Her legs would detach from her and run away. Instead, she shuffled into the living room and flopped down onto the sofa.

    "Are you good?" she heard Tommy ask.

    Agatha waved him away, not bothering to lift her head from the cushion that smelt of chips and...was that maple syrup? Ugh, her couches were so ruined! She magicked a blanket over and buried herself in the cushions.

    "Are we taking a nap?" Wanda asked her. Her breath tickled the shell of Agatha's ear. "Can I take a nap with you, Mama?"

    Agatha lifted an arm, inviting the child into her cocoon. Nicky shimmied until he was tucked under her arm. He pressed a kiss to her cheek before making himself comfortable. Agatha listened to him breathe in...and breathe out. She found herself copying him, matching the intervals until her body grew weightless.

    Agatha swept the floor of her cottage, head lowered as her mother entered their home. She dare not bring attention to herself. Dare not glance in the direction of the others. The maiden simply slipped away to hide until their guests had all gone upstairs. Their stern faces blending one into the other.

    She listened carefully as her mother's heeled boots clacked along the wooden beams of the second story. The creaking of the wood settled, signaling to the young witch that the adults had sat down. Agatha set her broom aside and slipped out of the house. If she was quick, she could pay Neva a visit. Her darling, fellow witchling with the dazzling eyes of green. Agatha knocked at the servant's door, waiting for her summer fling to appear. "Agatha," the maiden exclaimed, face a lovely shade of pink. "Thou hast appeared like a beacon of hope!"

    The witchling sauntered over, a smirk playing on her lips. "Wouldst thou accompany yours truly to the river's edge? Thy mother shan't know."

    "Thou art a vixen," Neva giggled. She whispered an order to a scullery maid before following Agatha towards the woods.

    They found a patch of bluegrass to rest on. Neva kissed Agatha's calloused fingertips. The witchling batted her lashes at the smiling creature. Her sweet thing was so cute, so full of life. Agatha dreamed of running away with her. They could live in a cottage somewhere along the coast. Bury their toes in the sand of freedom from the rancid, ruinous coven system. Neva gave her a chaste kiss. Her green eyes bright with joy. "What ails thee, Agatha? Thou art equanimous with a somber face."

    She pulled the other maiden closure. "I long for freedom, Nev. I know not the path my mother hath lain for me but that of an early death."

    Her friend turned her chin to face the misty-eyed witchling. "Thine mother is a doddering fool. Thou art a gift." She pressed another kiss to Agatha's lips.

    "Come with me," Agatha pleaded. "Let us be rid of this place." She clutched at Neva, her magic rumbling deep within.

    "Mine own mother needs me, Agatha. One more full moon, then we shall flee Salem." Neva sparked her magic with a poor incantation. Poor thing tried her best, but she could never get the words in the right order.

    Agatha reached up to adjust Neva's hand position. Her magic leapt towards the other maiden's. She gasped as her chest warmed. If she had bothered to open her eyes, to listen, Agatha would have noticed that her Neva was shriveling into a husk of a child. It wasn't until the scullery maid screamed in horror that Agatha realized what she'd done...again. Her mother was summoned by the sound, her gaze damning. There would be no arguing in her defense with this instance. No way to make her mother understand it was an accident. She hadn't meant to kill her best friend. Didn't know how she'd done it, or why. Not that Evanora Harkness cared.

    She'd been waiting for a reason to try her own daughter. And now, she had one. The woman was practically celebrating as Neva's mother wailed and beat Agatha with a stone in her hand and the firm toe of her shoe.

    Agatha covered her head, pleading. Begging. Trying and failing to tell them, "it was an accident!" She twisted and turned away from the blows, but they wouldn't stop. They wouldn't stop. They wouldn't stop. Wouldntstopwouldntstopwouldntstop....

    The goddess yelped as her back hit the hard floor of her living room. Her legs were tangled up in the blanket as her roommates(?) stared down at her in confusion and worry. Agatha struggled to catch her breath, her chest heaving. Sweat coated her body from head to toe. A third shower would be needed.

    "Mama-?"

    "Not now, Nicky. Mama's not feeling well," she breathed out before the questions could pour in. She placed a shaky hand over her eyes. "It was just a dream," she told herself, ignoring her audience. "Just a dream..."

    "Honey, I'm- What's wrong?"

    As if puppeteered by Wanda, Billy entered with a, "Who's ready for Coven Night!" The house fell silent as everyone exchanged looks. Billy and Teddy shut the front door behind them.

    Agatha scrambled to stand only to trip. She growled as she tugged the blanket away from her feet. "I'm fine," she insisted. "Just...give...Gah!"

    Rio was at her side in an instant, knife slicing through the cloth. "What happened? What's wrong?"

    "Nothing. Nothing's wrong. I'm okay." Agatha slapped hands away as she tried to get the situation under control. "I need a minute, and then we'll start our lesson." Rio gave her a look before grumbling. "Who the hell died this time?" She threw her hands in the air before turning her attention back to Agatha. "Sweetheart..."

    "Go. I'm fine," she repeated. "Maybe it's someone funny or lame. I don't care." Death pressed a kiss to her lips. "I'll be right back. Fifteen minutes, tops." "I'll be here," Agatha mumbled. She wasn't going to fall apart in front of so many people. Not after having a moment with Alice. That would be humiliating! No, Agatha was going to teach a lesson and be above all these annoying emotions.

    Billy walked over to Wanda. "What's wrong with Agatha?"

    She pulled him away from the Divine Mother's ears. "I don't know," she sighed. Her eyes kept flicking over to the woman. "Alice said she was having a breakdown. Agatha took a nap and...I think she was having a nightmare. We're trying to figure out what to do." The teen eyed his other, other, other mother with a frown. "Well, she's gonna want to do a lesson regardless. Why don't you check on her and I'll talk to Teddy and the others. Maybe we can think of something."

    "Good idea." Wanda walked away, an air of determination of aggressive kindness. Billy gathered his brothers and boyfriend over into the dining room. "Okay, Agatha's having a bit of a day. She's going to want to do a lesson, but I'm thinking of doing something a bit crazy."

    "I don't know...," Teddy began. "After the movie debacle, I doubt she's going to trust anything you do."

    "Yeah, but that was because it was a movie. This is something that might actually help her." He glanced over the groups' heads to look at his mothers, Jen, and Alice. "They've all been having some issues. I had my own problems with Agatha, but that changed when I saw her memories. What if....," Billy worked his spell book out of his pocket. "What if I sent them into her memories so they could all see she means well?"

    "Didn't that scar the hell out of you?" Teddy hissed quietly. "You had nightmares for days." "That was because Rio didn't give me time to prepare myself. I've got the spell right here. I cast it. We sent them all into the spell. They see a few things. They come out closer than ever!" He glanced over again, Agatha and Jen bickering. "Come on guys! This might be the only chance we get to make them get along."

    "I don't know, Billy."

    Tommy grabbed his hand with a grin. "Do it." He lightly punched Teddy's arm. "Let's fucking go, bro! They'll have to bond."

    Billy nodded, feeding off his brother's energy. "Yeah. Yeah!" He flipped to the page. "I just need one of Agatha's hairs and a door."

    "I'll get the hair; you pick the door," Tommy told him. The twin was gone in a flash. "Teddy, can you watch Nicky while I do the spell?"

    "Are you sure you know what you're doing?"

    "Totally! The book's been good so far." He ushered his younger older brother over to his boyfriend. "Maybe distract Agatha and them until I'm ready." Once the two were gone, Billy practiced the spells in his head. Finally, Tommy returned with a long strand. He passed it over to his witchy twin with a grin. Billy took the hair and focused on chanting the spell. "Repete um memoria"

    The hair turned blue.

    Billy sent it towards the pantry door. The hair touched the wood and transformed it into a hut. "Uh, guys," he said with his best worried tone. "There's something wrong with the pantry." It helped that Teddy and Nicky were confused. The women came over, staring into the room. "What in the...?" Agatha stepped forward. "Did you use a spell?"

    "I was trying to clean your laundry up," he lied. "It was all over the place." "What kind of spell? It's like you time-traveled a hut into my house!" She stepped into the room and vanished.

    The other three women rushed after her with panicked shouts.

    Billy let out a pleased puff of air as the door closed behind the group. "There we go! Let's go take a break."

    Rio stepped into the house and immediately felt a shift in the atmosphere. A wall of something thick and heady made walking around feel like she was wadding through water. She narrowed her eyes, tasting the air.

    Magic!

    Old magic at that. From the Darkhold...

    "Nicky!" Death hurried over to the living room. She breathed a sigh of relief as she caught sight of his beautiful face. The witch could still taste magic in the air, though. "Who did what?"

    The teens turned to face her.

    Rio had a bad feeling. The house was still too quiet for her liking. And where was Agatha? "Where are the other? You're supposed to be having a lesson."

    Billy smiled widely. "Don't worry! I tried a spell, and I think it worked pretty great." He nodded his head as his excitement began to overtake him. "Agatha and the others are gonna be back and be a true coven."

    Death walked around the couch, her stomach sinking. "What. Did. You. Do." "Just a simple memory spell," he told her with a shrug.

    Rio narrowed her eyes at him as her worry began to grow. "What memory spell? How do you even know a memory spell from the Darkhold!"

    The teen shook his head. "No, I used one from my spell book." He held up his pocketbook. "All you need is a hair from the witch and a door. I said the incantation and sent them through."

    Death felt her eye twitch. ".......You did WHAT!"

    "It's harmless. It's not like how you entered my memories." He smiled proudly as if he'd done some noble thing. To him, he probably had.

    Rio scanned the room. "Which door did you use?"

    Billy got off the couch, the others following suit, and walked over to the kitchen pantry. "This one," he told her. "I can't believe they fell for it either. I totally got this and the laundry room mixed up."

    The door was as normal as any of the of the others. It was also bare. Rio felt like she was going to hyperventilate, and she didn't even need to breathe. "Where are the runes, Billy?" "....The what?"

    "The runes, Billy! The runes! Where the fuck are the runes!?"

    His grin vanished. "The page didn't say anything about runes..." He began to flip through his spell book.

    The Green Witch felt as if she'd been kicked in the stomach. "That's because you're supposed to go in there with them. If not, you need runes for safe passage in and out. Or had you forgotten how you nearly died," she hissed.

    Billy looked at the door in horror. "Well...well you can just go in and-" "You sent Agatha inside her own memories! How am I supposed to enter her mind if her body isn't here? It's not even a realm I can cut into." Rio screamed into her hands. She straightened her back to compose herself. "Kid, I love you, but what the fuck!" He looked at her, going full Harkness. "Aw, you love me..."

    "Focus, Billy!"

    Teddy cleared his throat. "So...How do we get them out?"

    Rio took a steadying breath, eyes transfixed on the regular, totally-not-a-bad-sign door. "We can't. All we can do is hope one of them finds a way out. There's no door. No runes. And Billy's out here, so he can't interrupt his own spell from the outside. If you do, you might make things worse or break her body into a million pieces." Death paced, thinking and thinking and thinking. She turned to them with a calm look on her face despite her inner turmoil. Bad news was always supposed to be delivered gently, right? "...She might actually be stuck this time."

    The teens began to panic.

    Chapter End Notes Fun little fact: Neva is a Spanish colonial name. Agatha has a type, which is Spanish/Latin women with charismatic eyes. (Maybe Wanda's green eyes remind her of Neva, too.)

    You Were Born Evil P.1 Chapter Summary Girls' Trip!!!!

    [•••••••] separates memory events from the coven's scenes. Hopefully that helps keep things from getting too confusing.

    Chapter Notes Long chapters incoming!!! (No seriously) Who's ready for more hijinks?! TW: Child abuse mention (lots of it in the 1st half. Nothing super graphic. Mostly mean words and vague descriptions); blood/menstruation (very brief in 1st half. Agatha gives you a heads up); Evanora Harkness (booo, most of this chapter) See the end of the chapter for more notes Agatha's hands raised as the wails of a baby reached her ears. Much as she loved her sons, the sound did little to rouse her maternal instincts. The goddess looked around as Jen, Alice, and Wanda entered the room after her. She turned her back on the source to face her rag-tag coven. "What happened to the door?"

    "The what?" Wanda asked, shouting over the noise. She squinted as if that would help her hear better.

    The Divine Mother rolled her eyes. Had the Maximoff always been this dense? "The door!" Agatha had a sinking suspicion it changed for a reason.

    The group turned to stare at what had been the pantry door. Now, however, it was a drab piece of wood. Alice turned back to her with wide eyes. "Uh...I don't think we're in Kansas anymore, Dorothy."

    "Ya think!" She wanted to kick herself for falling for such a lame trick. Laundry in the kitchen pantry. Honestly! "Get us out of here, Wanda."

    The damn baby wouldn't stop fucking screaming. The cries were like that of a banshee. Somebody was gonna die alright, but it wasn't gonna be her! Agatha was about to torch the damn thing and be done with the whole mess. Why was there even a crying baby to begin with?

    The Scarlet Witch looked at her. "Me? I didn't do anything!"

    "You're the only one who knows the spell. You're the only one who could have cast it. And to use Billy!" Agatha formed a fist as she rounded on the woman.

    "I swear, I didn't! I'm just as confused as you are," she argued. Wanda squared her shoulder, not backing down. "I don't even know where we are, or what happened."

    "Uh...My memories, you dolt!" Agatha waved her hand at the sad, sad room. She didn't exactly recognize it, but it reeked of Salem. The damp soil called to her. Salt, brine, death, and decay. Her first home.

    "Wait...we're in your memories," Alice exclaimed. Her eyes bulged in her head. "How?" Agatha rubbed a temple. "Billy....I'm gonna kill that kid."

    The baby continued to scream its head off. What the hell was their problem? Surely they had cried themself out by now!

    The witch whirled around to face the source. "Oh, will you shut the f-!" Her mouth fell open as her hands dropped to her sides. Finally, the baby's cries softened. Agatha thanked Herself. She was certain she was going to lose her hearing.

    "It's like it's on loop," Jen told her. She shuffled closer to the goddess. "Whoa! Is that you?" Agatha waved her away as she circled around the bed. She had never seen her mother when the woman was still young. Had never even given it much thought. The resemblance was striking. Was damning. She bolted for the door and tugged at the rope handle. "Get me the hell out of here! I can't...I can't!" The immortal slapped a hand against the wood with a growl. Wanda appeared at her side, but the goddess knew the look on her face. She had half a mind to slap it away. "It's good-"

    "Finish that sentence and I'm going to bind your magic for all eternity," she growled. Agatha pressed her back to the door, eyes landing on her mother. The scene continued to loop, her own cries driving her insane once more. "What does it want?"

    The chaos witch looked from mother to child. "Aren't you supposed to go inside yourself or something?" Wanda asked her. "That's what you did with me." (Agatha would have made a lewd joke if she wasn't panicking.)

    "This is different," she told the group. "The spell I used didn't have a copy of you to look at. It was just you!" The goddess tugged at the handle one last time, throwing a bit of magic into the mix. It didn't budge. "Dammit, Billy!" Agatha scanned the room for another exit. She didn't want to see any of her past. None of it. And whatever Billy had done, it wasn't a simple memory spell. Memory spells show you what you remember or vaguely remember. But this? This was showing her the very day she was born from an outside perspective. It was wrong. It was...It was...

    "I think you have to want it to begin. You have to face it," Alice told her. She had the decency to look apologetic even though it wasn'ther fault. "Like when I faced my family's curse on the Road."

    Why would she do that? She'd rather stand there for the rest of eternity than learn what her past had entailed. There was nothing worth remembering. Nothing worth reliving. No one worth hearing besides Rio and Nicky.

    Ugh, this is the fucking worst Billy. I hope you're happy kid, 'cause I'm so murdering you. Agatha tossed her hair back, eyes scanning the coven. There was no choice but to bare her soul to them. Not if she wanted to find a way out. "If I start the spell, we'll see my whole life. All of it. The good, the bad...Sex with Rio..."

    The group wrinkled their noses in disgust. If only they knew how bad it had gotten most of the time. The way their hate sex had left them bloody and battered. She didn't want them to see that. She didn't want to relive it. She didn't even want to think about it. "We'll have to get over it," Jen told her. " 'Cause I'd rather see whatever freaky shit you guys did than hear that baby scream anymore."

    Agatha decided not to tell them that it was her causing all the racket. They'd find out soon enough. She took a deep breath, steeling herself. "Okay...Okay, show me." Billy's spell responded. An invisible wave pulsed in what showed a small box. Agatha grit her teeth. They wouldn'teven be able to move around all that much either. Not at all like the Darkhold's memory spell.

    "So, is that Nicky in your arms? You're both so adorable," Jen cooed. She walked over to get a better look.

    Agatha had been adorable, hadn't she? The goddess was given five blissful seconds before the weight of her reality came crashing down.

    Her mother looked down at her, face shifting into a heavy scowl. "Thou art born from wickedness. I care not for thee, child. If not for a harsh winter, thy life the Green Witch taketh. May the Divine Mother deliver thee swiftly unto Her."

    "Less adorable," Jen said. She backed away, hands raised. "Why would you say that about your own child?"

    Agatha was too busy reeling from the words her mother had spoken to correct the woman. There was a rage stirring in her. White hot and fiery.

    Those had been the first words to enter her tiny mind. They never left her psyche. No love had ever been lost between the two.

    Deep down, she had known her mother didn't want her. But to hear her offer her up to Death, to her future wife, cut her deeply. This meant Rio had known, but had protected her from the truth. Promised as a babe... She had been delivered swiftly, indeed.

    A figure entered, calling to her mother. Agatha barely recognized the witch. One of the fated seven to betray her whilst still in her prime.

    The women exchanged pleasantries as if her mother hadn't just cursed her. Meanwhile, her infant self lay forgotten. Small rosy lips rutted for a teat. Had she ever mattered to the woman?

    Tears slipped down Agatha's face, heart breaking in her chest.

    "What calleth thy babe, sister?"

    This was it. The moment her coven would know her path. No turning back. No hiding. The Road was wild and wicked, indeed. It had forged a killer out of her. They would see that path unfold, and they would run, too.

    "Agatha. In hopes she might honor the Divine Mother," her mother declared. Evanora held her daughter out as if it were a rotted, tainted thing. "Take her. She will need a wetnurse. I dare not touch her lips to my bosom for fear of coddling her so."

    The baby was handed off, the room moving along with her younger self as if they were projections in time. Ghosts of the future forced to endure the past. She hated it. Hated her mother. Hated Salem. Hated how she still loved the woman before her!

    "...Agatha," Jen began.

    "Don't," she ground out. "I don't need your pity."

    The group clearly wanted to comfort her, but Agatha was too raw from the confession. Too hurt.

    It was one thing to be called 'evil' after having caused numerous deaths. It was another to have been branded 'evil' at birth. To have it vocalized before she'd ever lifted a finger. She glared as the coven member handed her off to Old Hildy. The woman had been kind, for the most part, but was a doddering old fool.

    "Is Evanora well?" Hildy asked the younger covenmate. The elderly woman rocked in her chair, a quilt on her lap. Her blonde hair was fading to white. Supple skin now gave way to deep wrinkles.

    "She will recover in time, sister." The witch nodded her head to the baby in her arms. "Sister Evanora hath requested a wetnurse. Thou art able, correct?"

    The older woman nodded. "Hand the babe to me. I shall honor our sister as the Divine Mother sees fit."

    Agatha chuckled darkly. "I do not see fit, Hildy, but at least you never whipped me." "So...We're gonna be here a while, aren't we?" Alice asked her.

    "I lived nearly four-hundred years......Yes, we'll be here a while. Get comfy. Pull out some popcorn for all I care. Just don't fucking touch me."

    Months passed the group.

    Baby Agatha was ignored almost entirely by Evanora. Meanwhile, adult Agatha seethed. She glared at the woman each time she got too close. Swiped at her with her hands, never landing any blows.

    As an infant, she learned, Evanora visited her three times a week. The witch never stayed long. She would ask how Agatha was fairing, then leave. Agatha's anger festered.

    "Come child," Old Hildy told her one day. "Let us find some yarrow. Mine joints doth protest this wintry chill." She scooped up the one-year-old and exited her cottage. "M-ma," her infant self-managed to say. It did little to lessen the sting of rejection. "Oh, dearie no," Hildy laughed. "Thine mother is a beautiful maiden. A strong witch who leads our favored coven. Thou art a descendant of powerful witches, dear Agatha."

    "Why didn't she just take you in?" Jen asked adult Agatha. "It's not like your mother was worried about you."

    "How the hell should I know?" she growled in response. "I was a baby."

    Hildy set her down so she could gather the herbs she desired. It was sunny for a fall day. Leaves rustled, but Agatha couldn't recall the warmth. She felt her heart stop as her younger self stuffed random leaves into her mouth to chew on.

    "You're not even watching me, you old bat!" She tried to stop herself, but it was only a memory. It had already happened. Agatha felt powerless as she watched the child, watched herself, grow pale.

    The infant began to vomit bright yellow and foam. Choked cries filled the air as she spat the leaves out. Hildy grabbed her and hobbled as quickly as she could to the closest witch. Her younger self continued to wail, drool and sick mixing on her nurse's top. "I need a healer," Hildy told a group of women. "The babe...She hast poisoned herself." Evanora appeared from around a corner, eyes falling to the infant. She was incredibly calm given the situation. "Do you know what she ate?"

    Hildy shook her head.

    "Then it is in the Divine Mother's hands. Her will be done." Evanora tightened her shawl around her shoulders. The ghost of a smile appeared on her face.

    "Okay, fuck this bitch," Wanda growled. "That's her child. That's...That's you!" Agatha ignored her. She had seen what plants she'd eaten. Yarrow and hemlock leaves. It was a death sentence if she ever saw one. "So how did I...?"

    "Put the babe in her crib. We shall wait and see." Evanora didn't bat an eye as the ailing baby was carried away. She moved to sit by the fire and continued speaking with her fellow witches.

    The group watched and waited as Agatha's younger self continued to grow weaker and weaker. Hildy had stayed by her side for a majority of the time but left as soon as Agatha's cries turned to huffs and soft whines. She was losing the battle for her life, and quickly.

    A spot of green appeared from across the room. It blossomed and bloomed until a figure took shape. A green candle was held in a skeletal hand as a cape swept the floor quietly. Even without her fleshy face, even without light, Agatha recognized her wife. The quiet she brought when collecting. Rio stepped up to the crib. "Thou art fighting still, Agatha. Thou hast much to do. Grow strong, and I will give unto thee the very world." Her infant self began to fuss anew, limbs thrashing.

    "Thou art a fine babe. I carry thee not with me this day. We will meet again, child." Rio brushed her fingers against the infant's stomach. There was a pop of purple and the wailing grew in intensity. Death laughed before leaving.

    "She...she healed you," Jen breathed. "Can she do that?"

    Agatha looked down at herself. Her face was covered in drool. Her cheeks were red and angry, but she still drew breath. "No. No, she didn't heal me. I stole some of her power to heal myself." Not even two-year's-old, and she was using Death to heal her injuries. Agatha had to hand it to herself, she knew how to adapt quickly.

    When Evanora discovered her baby alive and well, she did little to hide her disappointment. "The child will stay with me. There are many chores to be done. I will need the help." "Thy babe is still young and recovering," Hildy argued. "Permit me, sister, to care for her still."

    "No," Evanora told the witch. "Thou hath done enough. My child is mine own concern now."

    Agatha was still reeling from watching herself almost die. She had little time to process her mother stealing her back. Hildy had loved her. Why couldn't she have stayed with the woman? Old as she was, at least she cared. Evanora could have abandoned her entirely, but she still held on. Why?

    Many moons later, the group watched tiredly as three-year-old Agatha swept the floor with an oversized broom. The floor, which wasn't dusty at all, creaked under her feet. Evanora sat by the fireplace, a spell book in hand.

    "Mama, look!"

    Evanora gasped as Agatha began to levitate. Purple glowed around her as she hovered over the floor. The woman rushed over to snatch her from the air. "Never in my days! Thou art a willful child, Agatha Harkness." The woman slapped Agatha's hand with a sharp smack! "No magic. Thou hath no need for it. Thou art an abomination! Do not disgrace the Divine Mother with thine unholy gift."

    The child pulled back, tears in her eyes. "Mama-"

    "If thou must call on me, thou ought calleth me 'mother.' Cease thy babbling and begone, child." She waved a hand, knocking Agatha to the floor.

    "Mother-"

    "Away!"

    The child ran for her room as fast as her little legs could carry her.

    Agatha curled her hands into fists. She didn't remember any of this happening, but she didn't need to. She knew what she had wanted to say in that moment. All she wanted to do was apologize. That was what good children do, did they not?

    Now, she had the displeasure of watching herself cry to sleep. Never mind the fact that she hadn't eaten yet. Agatha could hear the rumble of her stomach. Could taste the tears on her tongue. Shivered the way she once shivered under the sad, tattered blanket cast in her direction. She was three-year's-old and so alone.

    "I'm sorry," Jen told her. "I'm sorry I ever thought you were just a terrible child. It's clear that wasn't the case."

    "I don't need your pity," she reminded the witch. Agatha scrubbed the tears stinging her face. "I survived. I always survive."

    "You shouldn't have had to," Wanda told her. "Your mother..." She fell silent as Agatha turned her gaze on the woman. "You're not an abomination."

    "No," Agatha told her. "Not yet."

    The abuse continued. The yelling. The hitting. The starving.

    It was a wonder she had managed to survive in any sense of the word. At least, now, Agatha was old enough to forage on her own. It was her second favorite thing to do outside of reading.

    She had always loved to learn. As a child, she absorbed books far quicker than any other in the coven. It hadn't been hard to teach herself to read. She put words and sounds together in the market and practiced at home with recipe cards. After all, Agatha was expected to cook at a young age.

    That was how she happened to stumble across a garden patch in the woods. Thick, juicy tomatoes shone brightly just for her. Round, robust carrots and potatoes beckoned her close. Their leaves were verdant and waving. Agatha admired the plants. Gently touched their stems.

    "Do you like them?" a hooded figure asked.

    The six-year-old straightened her back. "I do! They're really very pretty, ma'am!" She pointed to a beet. "That one's just right."

    Rio crooked a finger but never revealed her face. "Tell me, child. When was your last meal?" Agatha scrunched her face up, making her adult version laugh. She looked just like Nicky and Billy in that moment. Her genetics, thank Herself, had won out in the end. "I think I had some stew last night," the child confessed. "Mother says good witches receive breakfast, but I woke up late."

    The Green Witch tutted. "Tardiness can be bad, but not for children. Sit. Eat a carrot. My garden is open to you should you ever need it."

    "Okay!" Little Agatha wasted no time in tugging another taproot from the ground. She didn't even care to tell the witch 'thank you'.

    "Why is Rio stalking you?" Alice asked. "You're not even dying this time." "You can die slowly for days when hungry," Agatha told her with a rasp. She cleared her throat. "Hunger takes fourteen days for a healthy adult." She watched as the child tore into a tomato, juices smearing across her chin. "That explains why my gardens have always been better than all the others."

    Jen nodded with a hum. "But why is she stalking you?"

    "Don't you keep up with your pets?" she asked the witch in return.

    "Hurry child," Evanora hissed. "We have not the time for dawdling. Make haste!" Agatha hurried down the stairs, her hair braided down her back. "My apologies, Mother. I could not find my shoe."

    "Pitiful creature," her mother mocked. "Should we nail them to your feet to avoid a similar occurrence?"

    "No, Mother," Agatha responded quickly. "I will do better. I swear it." "All you do is swear. When will you take action for your shortcomings, girl?" She dragged her daughter along, face a firm scowl.

    "I'll be good," the girl promised. "I will."

    Agatha looked away. She remembered this day well.

    If her memory served her correctly, and it seemed to be, a storm was brewing. The clouds had hung heavy with rain as thunder shook the land below. They were off to see their coven deeper in the woods. A brotherhood of wiccan priests, though more aligned with the Old World, had come for a most festive day.

    Even now, Agatha could feel the magical charge of those Salem woods.

    "Stay inside with the children," Evanora ordered. "Keep the doors locked tight. We will return at sunup."

    She nodded obediently, not daring to speak out of turn. Agatha watched as the women pulled their hoods over their heads and disappeared into the forest. The rain would not reach the sacrificial altar. Too many protection charms and runes had been put into place by witch and warlock folk. How did Agatha know....?

    Well, she was a willful child, after all.

    "Where are you going?" Wanda asked her. "What's out there?"

    Agatha chuckled darkly. "You'll see."

    A great fire lit up a clearing deep, deep in the woods. By a slab of wood, a goat and dog stood tethered. Old magic was in progress. Ancient and crackling like lightning in a bottle. Soon, the chaos would begin. But not yet. The sacrifices had yet to be bled. Young Agatha, all of ten years now, watched from inside a bush. Adult Agatha stood immediately behind her, her pulse thrumming in time with the drums.

    The priests carried out the bloody ritual. Guts and innards tossed into the fire. The women danced and leapt around the great flame, their voices echoing off the trees. The virgins presented the salt cakes, and the luperci were anointed. Now the chaos could begin. The men of all ages and virility chased after the naked women. Young Agatha watched the debauchery unfold; eyes wide.

    "What the hell is going on?" Wanda asked her. "Don't look at them! They're naked!" Agatha couldn't tear her eyes from the scene. It was like she was in the bush again, learning the ways of man and woman. The witch heard herself respond, "It's Lupercalia, hun. You're supposed to look."

    Jen made a noise in the back of her throat. "No wonder you're so fucked in the head, girl. You watched your mother sleep with strangers in the woods."

    Agatha laughed. "Must have blocked that part out."

    "No," Alice told her. "Looks like you had your eyes on the goods." She pointed across the clearing as two women embraced, hands roaming unhindered.

    The goddess licked her lips. "Not from my coven, unfortunately. My first teachers, and they never even knew."

    "Somehow, it makes sense your Sex Ed was a bunch of neglectful adults having sex in the woods," Alice muttered. "I don't know what I was expecting."

    Agatha shrugged, eyes still drinking in the two women as they moaned their passion into the night sky. "Oh, honey, we've not even gotten to the best parts of my life yet." Or the worst, she didn't say. It was the least they could do, be shocked and horrified along with her younger self.

    Her naked mother leapt past her, all the 'goods' in full display.

    "And the good feeling's gone," she groaned. "Christ, Billy. You're buying me a therapist."

    "Agatha?"

    "What, Kale?"

    "You're really old."

    "And you're really annoying."

    Agatha was growing numb to how often her mother called her something vile. The group, like her, had burned out emotionally after Agatha was taught to slaughter. Evanora had taken pride in making twelve-year-old Agatha cry. But that was on her for naming and getting attached to the hen. Only familiars deserved names, or so she'd been told. The goddess sighed heavily as her thirteen-year-old self milled about in the forest. The teen doubled over, a hand pressed to her abdomen. For once, Agatha felt the need to warn the other women about the impending humiliation and abuse.

    "Full disclosure: I just got my first period."

    There was a collection of winces and pained groans.

    "How did you guys do it in ye olden days?" Jen asked her. The potions witch backed up as young Agatha put a hand under her skirts. "Girl! Your hands are covered in dirt and germs! Stop!"

    "I had other things to worry about," Agatha snapped. "I thought I was dying...again!"

    The teen dropped her basket and ran for the covenstead. "Mother! Mother," she cried. It all sounded so dramatic and pitiful to her now. Tears over a little bit of spilt blood...how trifle. "Mother, come quick!"

    Evanora appeared with an unamused look. She had a shawl wrapped around her shoulders and her hair was down. Deep lines had marred her once beautiful face. (At least the outside finally matched the inside.) "What now, Agatha? Why must you cry as if the Devil, himself, is at your heels?"

    The teen held out her bloodied hand. "I fear I'm dying, Mother. There's...There's so much!" The older woman laughed harshly. "You are not dying, you pitiful thing. Your first cycle has begun. How inauspicious, too, that it should be on a blood moon. I don't think I ought to worry about you, girl. The Divine Mother has made it clear. You shall be as barren as the sandy beaches that ferried me here."

    The teen made a face at the news.

    Agatha was heartbroken.

    All the women of the village and their coven had declared motherhood the greatest gift of all. Why, then, had she been passed over? Had she not earned the right? "Why?" she asked. "I bleed for the Divine Mother. Why should I not be rewarded?"

    Her confusion amused her mother. "Why, indeed? Yes, you bleed, but you are certain to have difficulties. A babe would be a death sentence. By all means, child, tempt Fate. She has a funny sense of humor; I'll give Her that. She might entertain you for some time."

    Agatha put her hands on her hips. "This all feels a tad cruel, don't you think?" She wasn't talking to anyone in particular. Technically, she was talking to Herself. The goddess portion of her that had mocked her relentlessly. "Who was Me before I was Me? Who's ass do I beat?"

    "Uh...You doin' good?" Alice asked her.

    "No...I'm confused," she admitted.

    All of her older, darker memories were starting to wear her down. It wouldn't be long before the carnage began. All the camaraderie was soon to dissipate. She didn't want to keep going, but there was quite a bit of irony and dark humor to her suffering. What would her mother think if she found out her daughter grew up to be The Divine Mother? She'd probably die a second time. (She'd go in search of the ghost later.)

    "Oh fuck," she groaned. She'd forgotten the next part.

    Evanora, heated and unamused by something she'd said, was now tearing her dress off. "Willful as the day you were born. Go, then. Go be a harlot. Show the village your shame, girl. You think yourself so clever and bountiful. Find a man to bed you." Agatha tried to cover herself, tears running down her face. "No, Mother. I'll be good. I'll be good. I swear it!"

    "Can you, child? You shout as if you want the attention of others. Go on. You want a babe in your belly, do you not?"

    Agatha, even now, burned with shame. She hadn't meant to irritate her mother to the point of being harassed this bad. She just wanted to know where children came from. And her mother wondered why she never touched a man.

    Her maiden self ran for the house to find another dress. Her mother was quick to spell the drawers shut. "Mother, please," she wailed. "I don't want a child. I'll be good!" Evanora watched her cower in the corner with a steely gaze. "Dress and clean your mess. Do not stain my floors with your filth." She left her there, sobbing.

    She ended up having to scrape her blood off the floors with a knife. (So much for stains providing beauty.)

    "When do you start learning magic?" Alice dared to ask. Everyone had been so quiet after Agatha's memory of her first period. If they were traumatized from seeing it, they would never truly understand how she'd felt that day.

    "With a teacher, you mean? Not until much later. I'm mostly self-taught," she answered easily enough. Her voice was raw from silently crying through her memories. She missed seeing Rio, but was sure her wife had been around, just unseen.

    It was several weeks of Agatha accidentally causing magical mishaps. The first had been when she set fire to a corner of her room. She'd stubbed her toe and cursed the dresser to ashes. Another time, she'd traced runes absentmindedly and turned the kitchen table to stone. That had been the last straw for the older witch. She had been beaten rather harshly before locked in her room.

    It was 'days' like these that Agatha missed Old Hildy. Watching herself grow up had never been more depressing. Her magic was begging to be used, but none would teach her. Her own mother forbade it. Agatha watched as her younger self turned to experimentation. Some dangerous, some more comical. And some...some were spells of the flesh. It came in the form of Neva. The Spanish witch had migrated from the Old World to escape the trials being held there. Her family, full of life and charm, welcomed Agatha into their home. Neva, a novice, would sneak away with Agatha to play in the meadows. They got along well very quickly. Both longed for a life free from coven constraints. On one particular 'day,' the pair walked arm in arm down a path from a neighboring village. The townsfolk milled about, ignoring the two. Agatha couldn't stop sneaking glances and smiling at her companion. The light caught her hair just so. Her eyes like emeralds.

    "You seem in good spirits, dearest Agatha. What has brought this upon thee?" Neva leaned her head on Agatha's shoulder to look up into her blue eyes.

    The teen rambled off some excuse. Something about finding a patch of pumpkins for Samhain. The girl believed her, eyelashes batting innocently.

    "You're really sweet on her," Alice cooed. "This is the longest you've been friends with anyone."

    Agatha hummed. "She was sweet, but a fool. The others had stayed away, and for good reason." She watched her younger self sway, hand in hand, with Neva. So much would change soon. Her wife would reappear any day now. That was the first bad omen. She wasn't ready for that rollercoaster of emotions. Not yet.

    "Did you love her?" Wanda asked cautiously. At some point on their trip down memory lane she'd planted herself right next to the goddess. A few times, she'd hooked pinkies with her when Evanora was being a total bitch. (Later, Agatha would deny the exchanges ever happened.)

    "No..." She looked away from her memory, ignored her misty eyes, and faced the trio. "But she was enough for me then. You saw the other girls I chased. Stupid strumpets galivanting and flaunting their feeble magical prowess."

    "Damn, girl. Tell us how you really feel," Jen teased lightly. She threw an arm over Alice. "You were quite the womanizer."

    Agatha twitched her lips into a smile. "I still am." She pursed her lips as her memory self groaned.

    "I've forgotten my mother's henbane and poppy seeds," the teen told her friend. "Go on ahead. My mother will tan my hide if I return without any."

    Neva giggled. "Such a forgetful thing, Agatha Harkness. I shall see you at midnight, turtledove." She skipped away, her skirts slapping the tall grass.

    "Oooo," the group laughed.

    "I think she likes you back," Wanda told her, nudging her with an elbow. Agatha didn't laugh. She didn't even crack a smile. Today was the day things changed for her. Today, her countdown to self-destruction began.

    Back in town, the cocky maiden strutted towards a vendor. An old woman with a blind eye turned to her. The two never hit it off even when Agatha had been a child, and things certainly hadn't improved with time.

    "Goody Mason, I come for some poppy and hensbane," Agatha declared.

    Loud, she had been too loud. Her words had been overheard by a godly woman. The hands of Fate shifted forward.

    "Beastly child," the woman rasped. "Have you no manners? Do penance and I might spare a single seed for thee."

    Agatha shifted her weight with a huff. All brazen foolishness. "I have nothing to apologize for. I'm a paying customer. Your seeds, Goody Mason, and then I shall bid you a 'good day'." She held out a hand, two glittering coppers in her palm.

    The woman slapped her hand. "You reek of destruction, girl. You and yours are not welcome."

    Agatha watched herself shove the old woman aside before grabbing what she needed. She hugged herself as Goody Mason cried for help. She branded Agatha a thief...and a witch. The town would soon be after her. If only she had taken the beating instead of unknowingly stoking the fires of the Trials to come. (So many bodies...)

    Her younger self had walked away calmly, but her pace picked up as more people began to shout, "Witch!" Danger loomed. The air was heavy with malice and hate. Her magic sparked hungrily. Agatha began to run.

    Four men had taken on the task of capturing her. Four men for one little girl. Not that she was little and incapable. No, far from it. But she was untrained. Her magic was itching to lash out. She ran for their safety just as much as she ran for hers.

    "How would you like to see a battle?" she asked her covenmates. "One with real witches and hunters?"

    "Going off the tone of your voice and the fact you've chewed a nail off, I don't think I want to," Jen told her. She shared a look with Alice and Wanda. "What's gonna happen, Agatha?" The goddess watched herself be cornered; eyes trained on the path that would take her towards her wife. "Death returns to Salem."

    The basket of goods was dropped as Agatha failed to prove her innocence. Her skirts threatened to tangle her legs as she ran for the covenstead. The protection wards were in place, but these were no ordinary hunters. They were mutants with thick skin and sharp, pointy weapons.

    "Stupid girl," her mother snarled. Magic gathered at her hands to ring the alarms. "Hunters to the south," she told the coven.

    Agatha ducked as an arrow was fired at her. "Mother-!"

    "Get away! You have blood on your hands, girl." The woman brushed past her to handle a hunter.

    Her younger self ran back for the trees as a burly man targeted her. His heavy footsteps were like the thundering of hooves. She could practically feel his hot breath on her neck. Agatha ran until her lungs burned and her vision blurred. She was too far for another witch to aid her. It was perfect.

    The young witch smirked as the man approached her. Purple swallowed her hands as she extinguished his torch. She ripped the wood from his hands and tossed it aside with her magic. It had felt good, in the moment, to see what she could do. That was until she spotted a figure out of the corner of her eye. A green-clad woman watching her intently. Her heart beat wildly in her chest as she backed away. The woman looked hungry. Looked starved. And she was staring at Agatha like she was on the menu. She'd forgotten all about the hunter until he spoke.

    "You and yours will burn this night," the hunter snarled. He produced a knife and lunged at her.

    Agatha had little time to think, so she let her magic do it for her. The stream of purple collided with the body and began to pull at something. It was unlike anything she'd ever felt before. Her hair tingled at the roots. Her toes curled. Her mouth fell open. It felt...exhilarating!

    Whatever spell she'd cast left her feeling weightless and re-energized. She could probably run for several more miles if she wanted to. A world of endless possibilities had opened up to her. And so had a world of pain.

    The cloaked figure now stood next to the body, eyes unblinking. They were hazel, shades of brown and green mixing. Agatha wanted to stare into them forever. "Who are you?" she breathed. There was a charge to the air as the woman smiled. And oh! Agatha had felt her insides twist at the gesture.

    "I have no name," her future wife informed. Rio looked adorable as she touched her own lips. Her voice had changed since Agatha last saw her at the ripe age of six. She had chosen a mortal sounding voice. No echoes to hinder her clarity. Death extended a stem of bitter nightshade. "Who are you? she asked as if she didn't already have the answer. Agatha had opened her mouth to tell her. To see if she could coax another smile from that beautiful face, but her mother had beaten her to it, literally and figuratively. Rio vanished in an instant as the first blow landed.

    The slap had years of malice behind it. Years of disappointment justified. She had led hunters to their doors, after all. Endangered the lives of many when it could have just been her.

    The goddess looked down at herself, pleading and crying, and laughed. "One can always rely on the kindness of witches," she told the figment with a bitter tone.

    "How come you never fought back?" Jen asked. There were tears in her voice, but Agatha didn't turn to console anyone. Why should she? No one ever thought to console her until Rio. "Because I loved my mother," she told the witch. "Good witches take their beatings and still love their parents." Her voice was hollow by this point. The lie was getting harder to believe.

    Evanora left her in the field. Left her with the body of her first victim in hopes they might bury two in the morning. Agatha wept.

    "Greatness is often forged in the harshest environments," Death told her, silently reappearing. She extended the flower once more.

    Agatha looked up at her, face dirtied and bloodied. "What? Want me to eat it?" Death laughed. It was a pretty sound. One the witch couldn't ignore. "If it pleases you, you could."

    Agatha wiped her face, looking away. "Where are you from? You could have helped me with the hunters."

    "You had it under control. He was no more a threat than a babe is." The woman glanced down at the corpse, her tongue licking the inside of her cheek. "Such potential squandered with the likes of these."

    Slowly, younger Agatha reached for the flower. Her heart beat madly in her chest. Her body knew what her mind did not, but it didn't scare her. Not when the figure felt so comforting. "Do you really not have a name?"

    "Not one anyone would say fondly," Death admitted. Her eyes dropped to Agatha's lips. "No mouth to call for me when needed."

    "You two are still so fucking gross," Jen groaned.

    "I think it's cute," Alice said. "She's comforting Agatha."

    "Shh," Wanda hissed. "I can't hear them. Agatha, speak up."

    The goddess rolled her eyes.

    "I will find you a name," her younger self vowed. "And I will call for you." Death stepped closer; face titled towards Agatha. "You're not afraid, child?" The young witch smirked, eyes roaming the fleshy face of a cosmic being. "What is fear if not excitement for the unknown?"

    Death laughed softly. "Permit me, Agatha Harkness, to teach you a spell or two. I promise to make it worth your while."

    The hunger for knowledge. The desire to learn. Agatha could never have refused. "I permit you, fair maiden. What shall I give you in return?"

    Death inched closer, breath softly hitting Agatha's face. "A kiss, my dear, for I have so long waited for you."

    The goddess swallowed thickly. She'd been chased and loved by Death all her life, and the first thing Death wanted to do once revealing herself was shower Agatha with gifts in exchange for a kiss. Agatha would be sure to find her wife and return the gestures tenfold. She just needed to find a way out of her own memories. They would need to find somewhere secluded. She wasn't going to stop at just kissing.

    The bewitched maiden closed the distance of her own volition, just as Death had always wanted her. Her magic surged around them, purple turning the grass to ash. Both Agathas trembled, the older pressing a hand to her lips with a moan. Kissing Death shouldn't have been so sweet and addicting, but it was. She'd chased the taste of Death, her tongue licking inside that warm mouth that no one else dared touch. Agatha wondered if she tasted rotten to her wife. If that was why she wanted her so bad. It made more sense to her than being a baby promised. Surely there were others that had been condemned at birth.

    "A part of me wants to be really happy for you, but the other is actually terrified to find out what happens next," Alice squeaked. She hid behind Jen with a small laugh. "No offense." "None taken. Things do get a bit....hectic from here on out," she told the group. "Call this my true sexual awakening, if you will."

    And awaken, Agatha did.

    The group were quick to groan and turn away as the younger Agatha sought out Neva for a frisking.

    "She was the first woman I deflowered," Agatha told her audience. "This might be fun after all. My mother starts to get a bit bolder, but I finally had an outlet for all that pent up energy." Wanda turned away with a bright blush. "I wish we could control the volume. She's so loud." Agatha smirked, smug and proud. "Jealous, hun? I bet you've never been bent over like that, have you?"

    Neva gasped loudly as young Agatha pressed her fingers into her.

    "I want to be impressed. I really do, but this is weird," Alice said loudly. She pressed her hands over her ears in a weak attempt to block the sounds out. "There's no way nobody heard you two going at it."

    Agatha shrugged. "If they did, they never stopped by. They must have thought a boy was becoming a man." She examined her nails, ears red.

    The 'days' began to rapidly pass the group by. Agatha, the younger version, ran off with Neva more often for tryst or two in the woods. But at night? At night, the witch sought out Death for her arcane knowledge.

    "What if wolves found you?" Alice said, concerned in that endearing way. "Or what if you had gotten hurt and couldn't find your way home? It's so dark out here." "Dark?" Agatha laughed. "Are we not seeing the same thing? Look at it!"

    The forests of Salem were vibrant under the brilliance of the moon. A glow to every leaf and blade of grass that had the pleasure of seeing the celestial body's face. Foxes crept through the underbrush, watching as the young witch sauntered through the wooded land. She always met Death in the same place. Along the river where smoothed and mossy stones lay. Fireflies weaved through the air with magic of their own. Agatha knew where exactly to look once she stepped down towards the edge. There, on a large boulder, Death waited with a new flower in her hand.

    "You have taught me much," Agatha began, "but I seek more. What great magics might I try tonight?"

    "What a voracious appetite you have, mi flor. Those will be reserved for later." Death, still a stranger to the witch, moved from her perch to circle Agatha. Her fingers ghosted along set shoulders. "Tell me...have your witchkin taught you the power of flight?" "No," she hissed, but not out of anger.

    No, Agatha wanted those fingers to burn themself into her skin. Even without knowing her name or seeing her magic, the girl knew the woman was no simple creature. Her teacher would not stoop so low as to bed a novice. Agatha would just have to get better if she wanted the chance. She would do whatever it took to earn the mystery woman's favor. Death chuckled, stopping in front of her protege. "First, we require a sturdy branch." She waved her hand out towards the forest. "You pick on for me; and I, you. Decorate it however you deem fit. Just be sure to think of me as you do."

    That wasn't hard for the teen. She dreamed of those hazel eyes. The way they always seemed to hunger for her. Those lush lips that were soft as rose petals. Those gentle yet firm touches on her arms. Agatha all but floated away. She wanted to be a good pet for the woman, after all. Wanted to be picked for once. So, she made sure to find a branch worthy of the woman.

    "Oh, hey! Hexenbessens training," Alice cheered. "I remember when my mother taught me." She bounded over to Agatha with a grin. "What did you think of your first time?" The goddess gave her a tight grin. (Were all of her happiest moments doomed to end poorly? How was she supposed to enjoy anything?) "It was great," she told the younger witch. "Yeah, yeah. Great."

    "Doesn't sound like it was," Wanda told her. She looked out at young Agatha as she picked a branch and hauled it over to a stump. "Which doesn't make sense because you look happy here."

    Agatha didn't even bother to slip her mask back on. What was the point? They'd seen so much of her life now, hardly anything was a mystery. She let out a long sigh, her own eyes drifting over to herself.

    "Back in my days, a novice witch was meant to be trained in a specific area, and only that area. To stray from the path was to disgrace your coven. But no one wanted to teach me." She shoved her hands into her pajama bottoms. "Rio taking me on, fun as it was, meant I'd been entirely ostracized. I'm happy because I'm finally wanted, but...we got cocky. My mother caught us, and my training was sabotaged."

    "Did you ever find out why your mother was so against having you?" Jen asked. Even her voice had softened over the course of their journey. "There had to be a reason." "Rio knows," she told the group. "But she hasn't told me. I haven't bothered to ask, either. It makes little difference to me."

    They quieted as the young witch carried her broom over to Death, a blush in her cheeks. The broom was, as it would later be, covered in moss and leafy vines. Greenery blended with natural shades of brown.

    Death held it as if it were the most precious gift in the world. She passed off the broom she made for Agatha. It was decorated with leaves, spindly roots, and smoothed in a spot for her to sit. Agatha knew green magic had been used for such a feat. Care had been put into it. Thought and....No... The stranger did not love her, and she did not love the stranger. Not yet, at least.

    "Pro te delecta aperio via," the two chanted, circling one another. The moonlight bathed them in a wash of blue.

    Their magic surged into the wood with a quiet hum. They officially handed each other their brooms, completing the ritual. Death straddled her broom with a grin before taking to the skies. Agatha eyed her hungrily before pursuing her. Her take off was shaky, but she had always been a quick study. She managed to dodge a few branches as her feet lifted off the ground.

    The cool wind whipped at her hair as they soared up and over the treetops. All of Salem lay quiet below, small fires twinkling like fireflies. The young witch laughed as she took in the stars and giant moon overhead. She had loved it. Loved the freedom it provided. Loved the weightlessness. She exhaled all her troubles and...

    "Agatha Harkness!"

    She was pulled from her broom, the ground rushing to meet her. Agatha closed her eyes, bracing for her untimely demise...and was caught by her flying instructor. "She sounds mad," Death told her with a manic grin. She'd kiss it off the woman's face if her mother weren't watching. What their audience didn't know was that the young witch had noticed a lack of heart beat in the other woman's chest. There was no pulse where her hand lay.

    "You should have let me fall," Agatha lamented. "She will send you away now." The pair landed before the coven leader, but she didn't cower as she had in the past. A perfectly good evening had been ruined, and for what! Because someone dared take a chance on her? If her mother wanted a willful daughter, she'd show her willful.

    "How dare you?" her mother growled. "Running off to cheat your lessons with this...this..." Death grinned, waving. "Hello again, Evanora."

    Originally, Agatha had assumed they'd met in the past in some other coven. But now Agatha knew the truth. Death was taunting her mother. Instilling fear after watching the woman treat her daughter so terribly. It warmed her heart to know Rio had always been on her side. Promised or not, Death had earned her devotion and then some.

    "Who are you?" the graying witch asked. She eyed Death with a heavy scowl. "What coven are you from?"

    The cosmic entity laughed, shaking her head lightly. "I wouldn't worry about that. There's no one for you to call on."

    "Step away from that woman, Agatha."

    "Don't pretend to care now," Death snarked. "I know what lies in your heart, Evanora Harkness. It is not love."

    "What would you know of love? A covenless witch cast out for bewitching young girls to follow in your wickedness. Away!"

    Death preened. "If it means I'm able to meet beautiful maidens such as she, then it must be so. But know you cannot take what is mine from me. You, yourself, gave her freely." The younger Harkness was thoroughly confused, but deeply enamored. Never in her life had someone defended her. Never had someone stood up to her mother. She was going to marry this woman.

    Evanora pulled Agatha away. "Begone, demon. You are not welcome here." "She is welcomed by me," Agatha argued. "I would have her." She stepped forward, chin raised.

    "There is a sickness to your mind, child. You have no wants or needs that are your own." Evanora moved to strike her daughter only for her hand to be caught. "Unhand me!" Death whispered something in her ear just to pull away with a laugh. Whatever she said left the older woman shaking.

    "Come back to town with us," Agatha told her. Stay with me, the girl wanted to say. She wanted more lessons and more kinship with the woman. She wanted that feeling of safety to return.

    The woman beckoned her forward, eyes twinkling in the light. Death tightened the cord to her cloak. "Go now, Agatha. Your mother will find you a teacher."

    But I want you, had never left her mouth. Young Agatha reached for Death to kiss her. To tell her the things only her lips could say when caressing Death's plump ones. The woman disappeared with a cackle before the maiden ever reached her.

    Agatha was given a teacher by her sixteenth birthday.

    The woman was pathetic. Truly, that was the best word Agatha could use to describe her. She flubbed all her spells. Got runes mixed up. Accidentally killed her own familiar on one occasion.

    Overall, her mother was still trying to keep her from learning and reaching her full potential. That didn't matter, though. Agatha still met up with Death every night. Instead of spells, to avoid being executed per the coven's updated rules, her mentor taught her telepathy and telekinesis. In these moments, Agatha's memories did not convey their silent conversations. It was for the best. Most of it was highly suggestive in nature to the point the Divine Mother was blushing.

    "I wonder how long we've been gone," Jen groaned. "I'm starving."

    "I've got a protein bar," Alice offered. She pulled the treat from her pocket and handed it over. "How much longer Agatha?"

    She glared at them. "I'm sixteen! You've still got a long, long, long, long, long way to go. Take a nap or something." Agatha turned back to the memory and balked. "Take a nap." Unfortunately, that drew the trio's attention. Agatha was with Neva again.

    "Thou art a vixen," the witchling giggled. She had slipped back into the Old Tongue to tease Agatha. "Sarah, I must pick rosemary with Agatha. I'll be back."

    The goddess paced. She knew what came next. She didn't want it. It had been an accident! She may not have loved Neva, but she cared for the girl. One of the few who didn't shrink away at the sight of her strange magic. One of the few her mother hadn't poisoned against her. Neva had been sweet and innocent. Neva had been pure.

    They were in the fields too quickly. Time speeding up the more Agatha tried to ignore her memories. They were laying in the grass now, tangled within one another. Those batting eyes. Those gentle touches. The calm before the storm.

    Neva had noticed her sour mood and tried to lighten her spirits. "Thine mother is a doddering fool. Thou art a gift." She kissed younger Agatha. Love unbidden. Love given freely.

    The goddess shook. "I am no gift, Neva!"

    "Hey," Wanda soothed. "It's okay. She obviously loves you. That's alright. It's okay to be scared."

    "I don't want to see," Agatha told her. "It was an accident!" It didn't matter if she closed her eyes. She knew the next part by heart. Had regretted it bitterly.

    Neva's choked gasps filled her ears as her younger self drained the witch. She hadn't meant to. She only wanted to help her with her hand position. Her magic! Her damn magic killed her! How was that a gift? How?

    The scream pierced their ears just as it had Agatha's. Now, the young witch was scrambling away from the body with a sob. Her hand pressed to her mouth as she tried to make sense of things. They would burn her for this. Agatha knew.

    Neva's mother beat her while the coven watched. Agatha swore on her life it had been an accident. Both versions of herself screamed it until their throats were raw.

    Wanda and Alice wrapped themselves around the Divine Mother, whispering softly to her. Wanda stroked her hair. "It was an accident. It wasn't your fault."

    As Agatha was led away, she saw, for the first time, Death. No flesh to hide her face as she bent down to examine Neva. The young woman knew in that moment. She knew she'd fallen for Death.

    "No spell was cast," Neva's mother told the coven. She turned her gaze to the shackled Agatha. "We have no proof. Not yet."

    "You are forbidden from using your magic henceforth," Evanora told her. "If you are caught, you will be bound and executed. That includes the study of magic beyond a babe's." Agatha lowered her head, accepting her fate. "Relegate me to the woods," she pleaded. "Where I will not be near you or yours." Anything but the loss of my magic, she had wanted to say.

    "You cannot be trusted on your own," Evanora told her. "You will remain where you can be seen."

    For the following months, Agatha was locked away in her bedroom. She knew she could summon Death to her. Had been given the incantation many moons ago before her mother discovered them the first time. Now, she wasn't so sure if she should continue her dalliance with Death. What did that say about her? Did she enjoy killing? Was she as wicked as the coven claimed her to be?

    Both times had been accidents. Once in self-defense, and one purely outside her own accord. The room began to make her go mad. The seed of hate had been planted. Her coven would never accept her. But maybe...maybe her mother had a crumb of compassion. She'd been good since her arrest, had she not? Agatha waited for her next visit.

    It was a week later that her mother finally poked her head in.

    Agatha bowed her head to the woman, prostrate with remorse. "Mother, I beseech you. Permit me to learn to control myself. I swear it! I can be good!"

    "Why must you always swear it, Agatha? Why can you not simply be? Your disappointment is like a stone around my neck." Evanora glared down at her before her eyes shifted beyond her child. "There will be no more chances." She reached past her daughter for the book she'd foolishly forgotten to hide. It was a spell book. Strictly against the rules. Her mother smiled for the first time. "You will weigh me down no longer."

    "Mother, I was only reading," she pleaded. "No one will teach me. Mother! Mother, please!" The teen pounded on the door as it was sealed behind the older woman. She beat at it with all her might, but it wouldn't budge. Agatha screamed, rage burning through her. Her furniture was reduced to rubble. The walls deeply scuffed. Let them remember her by the damage she caused. Let her anger permeate every pore and grain. May they feel it any time they set foot in the house. Agatha Harkness would not go quietly.

    "What's going on?" Wanda asked her. "I don't..."

    Agatha reached out to herself with a heavy sigh. "My only crime was wanting to stop another accident from happening," she said, voice thick. "I have already been tried. I broke their rules." The goddess pulled her hand back. "I have been condemned."

    "For reading!" Jen grabbed the somber woman, turning her to face her. "You read a book, Agatha! Why would they execute you for that?"

    "It's not because I read," Agatha laughed tiredly. "It was just an excuse. That's all my mother ever wanted. An excuse to kill the evil she brought into the world." She pointed to the door. "Here they come now, my darling escorts."

    Two hooded women grabbed her and bound her. Her younger self twisted and turned, fighting the whole way. It was futile. That was Agatha was learning to see. Her whole life had just been futile.

    Poor Alice. The girl rushed forward as if she could help the figment escape. Jen tried to calm her down, but the youngest witch was very upset. Wanda stepped away to help console the goth, but even she was beginning to grow antsy.

    "Do you remember it, Wanda?" Agatha asked, a crumb of her old self surfacing. "When you pushed into my memories. When you stood where I stood. Did you know the pain you were inflicting?"

    The Scarlet Witch refused to glare at her. "You were terrified then, and you're terrified now. But you don't have to be. We're here now."

    The younger version was bound to the stake. Evanora passed judgement.

    "It's wrong," Alice sobbed. "You're a child!"

    Agatha turned away from her execution and pulled the witch into her arms. "I survived," she reminded her. She stroked a cheek gently, softly. "Watch."

    The combined streams of magic burst forth, hitting Agatha from all sides. She threw her head back as their magic burned her from the inside. Unfortunately for her original coven, she was hungry for magic. She always would be. And if they were going to foolishly throw it at her, her magic figured it might as well have a snack. Agatha couldn't control it, but she didn't try to stop it either. The old biddies could shrivel up for all she cared. They would make lovely presents for her love.

    "Your mother," Alice breathed. "She didn't die."

    The goddess chuckled. "Not yet."

    "Please...I can be good," her younger self reasoned.

    "No, you cannot."

    The trio shouted, not to warn the memory of her mother, but in outrage. Agatha found herself watching them more than she was watching herself. The tears that streamed down Jen and Alice's faces. The fury on Wanda's as she tried to blast the woman. The way they all clearly wanted to step between the teen version of herself and her mother.

    Why hadn't her first coven done that? Why had they seen what the trio saw, but stood by? It perplexed Agatha. It ate at her. The knowledge that she felt closer to these younger women than she ever had in the covenstead she was born into. What did they know of her birth that she didn't? She would have to ask Rio. That was her only option.

    "Calm down," she told them. "She's been dead for nearly four-hundred-years. You're a bit late for the theatrics."

    "It doesn't bother you that she was going to kill you?" Jen asked, eyes wide. "I killed her," she reminded. "Of course, it bothered me." Agatha felt that old anger swell. "Sixteen years of my life were wasted because of that woman. I carry that knowledge with me every fucking day! She never loved me. Never!"

    "Okay," Wanda soothed, taking a deep breath. She rubbed Agatha's shoulders like the goddess had calmed her in the hex. "Let's all just calm down. We've got a long way to go, and nobody wants to die in here."

    The group settled.

    "Agatha?"

    "Yes, Jennifer?"

    "You're mom's a bitch."

    Agatha sighed. "I know, Jen."

    Chapter End Notes Wowee! I know we had some repeat scenes from Billy's time in her memories, but I wanted Agatha to really put her life in retrospect.

    Chapter Notes Just a friendly reminder that Part 3 will be up a little bit later/early hours of Thursday morning...hopefully. Tbh, I have yet to start writing it....
