    Eh, it'll be fine. You've got like 20,000ish words to tide you over til then anyway. Love you all!!!! ❤ Rio and Agatha were building a cabin. Partly for Agatha's comfort, partly for Rio's ability to sleep with her wife. They were nothing if not determined to reach their goals. (Mainly the goal of binding their souls for all eternity and then some.) As the Green Witch cut the lumber, Agatha hefted the wood before sealing it in place with her magic. Currently, they planned for a one-bedroom home. Nothing big. Nothing fancy. Something Agatha could easily defend if anyone from Salem found her.

    "Damn, girl, look at those muscles," Alice laughed. Her eyes were no longer puffy as she watched a free Agatha roam the forests of Massachusetts. "I can't believe you're going to marry Death, herself!"

    Agatha preened. "Told you guys I was exceptional." She sighed as she took in the easy smiles her and Rio had shared. The touching of hands. The way their magic mixed and melded together. This was her life for fifty-seven years. Laughing in the forest with her soon-to-be wife. A drop in an ocean of her time on earth. She would get those smiles back. She vowed it. "This is cute," Wanda finally admitted. She leaned against the true Agatha and gave her a smile. "You both look so happy. And Rio...She looks so young."

    The goddess looked down. "We were very happy," she stated. Happy until I wished for a child. The group watched silently as the house was built over the course of several weeks. Rio would stop by often. She would shower Agatha with gifts. Books, flowers, and the likes. It had been perfect. She had known peace and love.

    "I bet you're glad you can wear pants and a tank-top now," Wanda teased. "Those dresses looked uncomfortable."

    Agatha hummed. "Truth be told, I don't care for dresses."

    The group looked at her in shock.

    "But...you wore a dress all the time."

    "When?" she laughed. "If you recall, I wore pants on the Road. Dresses are for frilly girls. I'm not a frilly girl." Can I sit? My feet are killing me! The goddess risked altering the spell and sat. "We can sit now," she cheered. "Thank Me!"

    "What? Why thank you? Shouldn't we thank the Agatha?" Jen blinked. "Sorry. I was trying to say the Agatha."

    Wanda shared a look with Agatha. "Are you making her do that?"

    "No, but it's funny."

    Rio laughed behind them. "My love, you should pose like that more often." The younger, toned Agatha was leaning against a tree as she took a break. If her dress had had pockets, her calloused hands would have been shoved deep within them. Agatha laughed, a smirk playing on her lips. "If it pleases you."

    "It does...immensely," Death admitted. She took slow, calculated steps towards the mortal. "Are you excited, my darling? Once the door is set, our home will be complete." She stopped in front of the witch, hands reaching to cup Agatha's face.

    Agatha kissed her love, fingers tangling in Rio's hair. "If you want me, you'll help me finish the door before sunset."

    Death chuckled. "Sweetheart, I always want you," she purred. "But it was you who said no magic. I'm merely following your wishes."

    "True...Disregard my silliness. I wish to be wed tonight." She flourished her skirts as she marched over to the final slats of wood that would become the door. Agatha stopped and turned back to her, lips pursed."Can Death wed?"

    "Now, you think to ask?"

    "I was a bit preoccupied, my love. Your hands tend to roam." Agatha looked down at the stack of timber. "Well?"

    "I am not permitted, technically. However, I'm always willing to break whatever rule necessary to be with you." Death waved and twisted her hand over the boards. The wood fused together as if it had been one piece all along. "I would burn the world for you. I would break time for you." She pulled Agatha to her, their hips meeting. "I would even die for you if you so wished it, Agatha."

    "Let us pray to the Divine Mother it never comes to that," the witch breathed. She leaned in to close the gap, moans filling the air.

    "That! I was trying to say that," Jen screeched.

    "The D-word," Alice clarified. "Not the...moans...Anyway! Every time we try to say the D-M thing, it comes out different."

    Wanda waved them off. "You guys are just being silly. Watch." The Scarlet Witch took a breath. "Agatha Harkness." She made a face. "Thank Agatha Harkness." The red head scowled. "Stop it."

    "I'm not doing anything," Agatha laughed. "But I must say, it's stroking my ego in all the right ways." She bit her lip as the coven stewed in delicious confusion. "D...Div...Agatha," Alice tried. She furrowed her brows. "Why can't we say the D-M words?" Agatha hummed. "Well, that is me," the goddess reminded. "So, I imagine that has something to do with it. That's the least of your worries, though. The show's about to start."

    Night had fallen over Massachusetts. A plainly dressed Agatha took Rio's hands in hers. They stood before her campfire, eyes trained on one another. All was quiet as a blanket of stars witnessed their devotion.

    "You must be careful not to take my power lest you die," Rio warned. She gripped tightly at her witch. "Are you certain this is what you want?"

    Agatha stood next to her younger self; face flushed. "Always," they said in tandem. "But when I marry you, I wish to marry you as yourself."

    Rio looked down, uncertain.

    The Agathas chuckled. "Do not be shy. I already love you."

    Death raised her head, her skull illuminated by the flames. "Why do you not fear me, Agatha?"

    "Because you have never feared me. We are two wretched souls cast aside. Let Fate bind us together for all eternity so we might not be alone any longer." Agatha clasped her right hand with Death's. She waved her left-hand's fingers, letting her magic seep out like smoke. It twisted and twirled around their hands.

    Hazel eyes drunk in the electric violet. The shadows of her skull danced with the flickering light. "Just be careful," Death reminded. She followed suit, a murky green of combined death and green magic drifting down to mix with Agatha's succubus magic.

    Agatha grinned widely. "You would never hurt me," she breathed. The witch cleared her throat and held her head high as their magic formed chains to bind them. The weight settled on their clasped hands and began to wrap tightly around the flesh. Not even Death, true Death, could break the bond. "I take thee, Lady Death, to be mine in this life and the next." "And I take thee, Agatha Harkness, to be mine for as long as I shall exist." The would-be Divine Mother gasped as the chains seeped into their skin. It burned down, down, down until her blood carried the enchantment to her heart.

    Rio lurched forward, her free hand pressing to her chest. "What is that?" She looked panicked as she pressed at her sternum. "It's...something's moving!"

    Agatha ignored her pain and pressed her palm over the spot. She smiled, a small laugh escaping her. "You have a heart, my love."

    Death blinked. "A heart?"

    "And it beats only for me," the goddess said aloud. She wiped at a stray tear as Rio and her kissed. "I forgot how adorable she is when she's enamored with me."

    "Uh..."

    "I wouldn't even bother, Alice," Wanda told the young witch. "Let them have their moment." The couple entered the cabin and headed straight for the bed. Agatha bit her lip, a moan rattling in the back of her throat. "This was a fun night." She whirled around. "You might...You might want to turn around. Cover your ears. Just...y'know, don't look or anything. I'm totally about to have sex with Death and none of you want to see that." Jen and Alice pressed themselves together with a whimper.

    "Unless you guys wanna watch," she teased. "Wanda~"

    The woman blushed. "I'm good. No, thank you." She held up her hands, looking away. "Come on," Agatha purred. "You guys can be some of the first people, other than myself, to see Death naked. I promise to keep my jealousy in check."

    "She's just bones," Jen told her. She snuck a glance before whipping her face away. "Ah, but she's flesh where it counts. And trust me, she makes it count." Agatha bit back another moan as her younger self lay the cosmic entity back.

    "You're sick," Jen sobbed.

    "Agatha, I'm started to get bored of this whole...domestic thing," Wanda told her. "All you two do is stay in, cuddle, maybe have sex, eat, and cuddle some more." She turned to the goddess. "How did you two end up...?"

    "Broken beyond repair? Shells of our former selves? Bitter?" Agatha tapped her chin. "What day is it? No...What year is it? Based on my hair, those daisies, that dress...Hm....Give it a week. You'll get the answers you're looking for."

    "That sounds..." Alice grimaced. The goth shook her head. "I like the cottage core vibes. You two are cute." She walked over to where the couple were snuggled up by the fireplace. Rio was reading in Spanish to her witch, a book in one hand and her wife tucked under the other. Young Agatha had her eyes closed, drifting in and out of sleep.

    Agatha moved closer so she could hear her wife. "We spent so much time together. Loved each other so deeply...And I ruined it." If only she could jump into the fire to atone for her shortcomings. Alas, her memories wouldn't allow her. Pity.

    "How do you know that?" Wanda asked. "Did she say that?" She sounded offended on Agatha's behalf, which was comical. Rio would never tell her anything outside of calling her a coward.

    "I can't honestly remember. We'll find out if she did." She shifted, resting her chin on her knee. Practice makes perfect, right? "I'm sorry, Rio...I'm sorry I asked."

    The dozing Agatha nuzzled deeper under Death's chin. She cracked an eye, a smile twitching to life. "Can Death have children?"

    The reading stopped.

    "I'll take that as a 'no.' Forget I asked." Agatha tried to hide her face. "...I don't know, Agatha. I've never tried." Death tilted her wife's chin upwards. "Would you like children?"

    Agatha gazed up at the cosmic entity as if she were the Universe. "I would like one, maybe two. But it doesn't have to be now. I was just curious."

    "Say 'none' you idiot. You're going to hurt her," Agatha growled at herself.

    "I wouldn't mind," Rio told her, a soft grin blooming. "A little girl to look just like you." "It could be a boy," the figment laughed. "The world doesn't have to be all girls, superior as they are."

    Agatha swiped at herself. "Just shut up!" If only she could land a single blow. If only she could teach herself a lesson.

    "Hey," Jen told her. The witch pulled her back. "It's already happened. Just like at your trial execution thingy. Keep it down so we can hear. You two are always whispering." "We never did the spell," she groaned. "I put it in her head, so she made it a reality. She carved a piece of her soul and gave it to me." Agatha felt like her throat was closing on her. The goddess tried to pull her wife away from her younger self. She met only air. Only ever air. "....I want Rio..."

    Her coven took her in their arms and held her.

    Death had grown fidgety, but her wife had yet to notice. Agatha had become engrossed in trying new types of food and fighting off nausea. It never occurred to her that she could be pregnant. Never occurred that Rio would gift her such a priceless piece of herself. Yet here they were, living two different lives. Death watched her wife move about, hand on her dagger with unblinking eyes.

    "You guys have been really quiet the past few days," Alice said. "Did she already...y'know?" "Yes, but don't ask me when. This place obviously doesn't show what happened while I slept. It could have been that night. It could have been a week ago. All I know is that she clearly had concerns from the very beginning."

    The silence carried on for several more days.

    "Why haven't you said anything?" Jen asked. "Were you mad at each other?" Agatha shook her head. "We're communicating telepathically. We used to do this a lot. Mostly when I was too tired to open my mouth......Or if I had a sore jaw." "I knew you were going to say something nasty," Wanda grumbled. "I'm going to look for a door again."

    "Wasting your time, hun. I've checked with my magic at each decade. I'm in here. Billy's out there. We're not going anywhere unless he finds a way in." She hugged herself as she analyzed her wife more closely. "She hasn't brought me a flower in days." "I'm going to take another nap," Jen said with a yawn. "Wake me up when something interesting happens."

    "I'm sorry my happiest years are so boring," Agatha told her. "I'm about to have the roughest decade of my life. But sure, take a nap." She rolled her eyes and went back to studying Rio. "Why hasn't she brought me anything?"

    "Maybe she's scared," Alice suggested. "She looks it."

    "She does, doesn't she?" Agatha narrowed her eyes. Had she known from the very beginning? Why hadn't she said anything?

    "Do you remember what the two of you would have been saying here?" Wanda asked. She had Jen's head in her lap.

    "No..." If she could remember, this wouldn't be so confusing.

    "I cannot give you a child," Rio said suddenly.

    Her younger self turned to face Death. "Are you sure?"

    Rio nodded slowly. "I'm sorry, Agatha."

    The goddess lowered her head. Rio had known and tried to tell her as gently as possible. And what had Agatha done? She'd blindly carried on. Hell, Agatha had gone so far as to find books on how to do it herself. She had been so adamant about having a child. There was no stopping her now that she'd crossed Rio out of the equation. They were barreling towards a brick wall at breakneck speed. The coven could do nothing but watch as the young woman found another source of misery. No mother to love her. And, soon, no son to love.

    Rio picked her head up from the swollen belly, a tight grin on her face. "It's a boy." The rounded Agatha beamed. "The Divine Mother has blessed us," she told her wife. Death rose to full height. "Aggie...Agatha, I will be gone for some time." "How long?"

    Her wife couldn't seem to get the words out. She looked away. "A few months, at least. Will you be fine on your own?"

    Agatha waved her off. "Don't worry about me, my love. I have toiled and survived much since I was a child. I used to forage for vegetables on my own in the cold winter."

    The goddess laughed. "She knows, you fool."

    "Be nice to yourself. How could you have remembered? You were in a stressful environment," Wanda chastised.

    "Yeah...You're not a divination witch. You couldn't have known," Jen told her. This time, Alice was napping. She leaned on the potions witch with a soft snore.

    Agatha was growing tired of watching her life. The happy parts were about to end, and then there would be only anger. Agatha didn't look forward to seeing the person she was once she wrapped herself up in all that dark magic. The person who pushed Rio away. The person who killed to justify her grief.

    Agatha jerked awake in time with her double. The memory version of her had gone into labor, but she could feel it.

    "Oooh, it's happening," Jen squealed with Alice.

    The goddess held her stomach, as her heart thudded in her chest. "No." She waved her hand, trying to stop the memory.

    It played on. The pregnant woman stumbled out of the cabin, a satchel in hand. She gasped and groaned in pain as she rushed for the river. Rio would want to be there for their son's birth.

    "Where's your midwife?" Jen asked.

    "Jen, did you see another soul since the cabin was built?" Wanda hissed behind Agatha's back. "There is no midwife."

    Agatha blocked them out as she began to rock herself. "Get to the river," she told herself. "Just get to the river." The phantom pain of contractions rippled through her abdomen. She cried out in time with her memory. It was too deeply embedded to ever forget a single thing about that day.

    The damp soil. Salem. The river.

    Everything was there plain as day. She could feel the stickiness of blood between her legs. The excruciating clench of her muscles as it tried to force her son out. But she knew what her past self did not. Nicky wasn't breathing. Probably hadn't had a beating heart for the past few days. It was all wrong. All so very wrong.

    "...breathe," Wanda told her, a hand on her back. "Just breathe."

    The goddess felt a scream tear from her throat as the figment began to push. She gasped for air between the contractions. Was beginning to lose track of what was memory and what was real. Her vision began to blur as tears welled. "Rio," she sobbed. Her wife would not come to help her. They were stuck. They were stuck because Billy had to be the hero. Agatha clawed at her empty womb.

    "...He was a stillborn," she heard Jen say. The information hit the others like a wave. Wanda brushed back Agatha's hair, trying to get her to breathe along with her. It did little to ease the pain. Only Death could help her at this point.

    Rio appeared along the water's edge. She held a particular flower, one not known to man. (Later on, she explained it was a Death Flower. A special flower reserved for precious souls.) Agatha hadn't known the meaning of the flower, but she knew the meaning of the cloak. Saw the remorse in the lines of Rio's frown.

    "It cannot be," the doubles cried, pain wracking their bodies.

    Death approached her solemnly. "It must be."

    "You do this, and I will hate you forever," the pregnant version spat.

    Meanwhile, True Agatha pressed a hand to her mouth to stop the words. She would not disgrace her wife a second time. Agatha forgave her. Would continue to forgive her. She trembled and cried, but she would never utter those words again.

    "Please let him live. Please, my love!" The pain began anew as her body proceeded to reject her child.

    Rio closed her eyes, the Universe bending to her might. "I can offer only time."

    Agatha wanted to thank her, but her younger self had been too addled with pain and the potential loss. Rio was gone. But why, Agatha had never known? She had pressed, once, for the information. It had led to a century's long silent treatment which was odd, even for them. Maybe now she was ready for their next heart-to-heart.

    "She gave him life and aged him up!" Jen looked ready to faint. "All that on your own. No healers, no midwives, not even a potion to aid in recovery." She grabbed Agatha before hugging her tightly. "You both could have died."

    The goddess exhaled as the pain in her body subsided. The worst of this particular memory, over. She sank into the witch's embrace. It was what she had needed once Nicky was born, but she had been alone. She would take what she could get now.

    While the memory of her gathered a bag to flee, the goddess pushed Jen away. "You'll want nothing more to do with me now." All the sympathy that her early life had gained her would now be spent and then some. Covenless once more, the other Agatha would need power. Power to fight Death. Power to heal her son. Power to survive.

    "What do you mean?" the potions witch asked. "You just went through something traumatic. You need your coven."

    "Maybe you've forgotten what I'm remembered for. It's not for being the moon, or for being a hero," she growled.

    "We know you now," Alice argued. "You can't push us away."

    "Wanna bet your life on it?"

    "Agatha," Wanda said with a strained laugh. "You've..."

    The goddess sneered, lips twitching. "Don't give me that bullshit, Maximoff. There's a reason I was alone for so long. I'll outlive every single one of you, and my name will still be synonymous with Death." She waved them away. "Stick to that side. It's for your own good."

    Nicky cried..............and cried..............and cried.

    Frustrated, the new mother wandered into town in search of a witch. If there was someone who could help her, she'd be in their debt. It wasn't something she liked, but she'd get over it if it meant helping her son. Rain drizzled down on them as she scanned the doors and signs for anything witch related. Finally, she found a symbol of the Old World. Agatha knocked at the door, Nicholas screeching his lungs out.

    "Oh, the poor child," a young girl cried. "Come in, come in."

    Agatha entered the town home. "Blessed be, sister. I have a sickly child." She held Nicky out. "Please. I don't know what to do."

    "Just a moment. I will fetch my coven's healer." The maiden rushed off. Agatha eyed the room. It was stately for a witch's home. Salem had certainly moved up in terms of homemaking. The chairs were finally made of sturdier stuff. She sat, rocking Nicky. Eventually, she tried to breastfeed him, but that failed as well. Her head was beginning to pound from all the noise. Another moment longer and she was bound to lose her temper. The door to the townhome opened to reveal a woman slightly younger than herself. The air became charged.

    The mother rose, arms tightening protectively around her child. "I mean you no harm. I simply-" Agatha ducked as a spell was aimed at her. "Please!"

    "Stop her," the witch ordered.

    The young maiden ran to bind Agatha with her magic. It wasn't her fault. No one must have told her not to attack Agatha Harkness. She was drained in seconds.

    "It wasn't your fault," Alice was quick to tell her.

    The goddess ignored her. She watched the scene unfold. The door to her freedom, to a simple life, slamming shut. The stories that would spin from this night would brand her forevermore.

    "Wait, wait, no!" Agatha held out a hand to keep the witch at bay. "I cannot control it!" "You will atone for your wrongdoings," the woman hissed. She turned into a snake, lunging at her heels.

    The mother and son fled into the stormy night.

    Salem was no longer her home.

    "Why hasn't Rio made you any plants to eat?" Wanda asked. She hugged her knees as she looked over at the silent immortal.

    Agatha refused to answer any more questions. It was only a matter of time before they started hurling insults at her. She needed to prepare for the heart break. Not that she cared what they thought or anything. She was a god now. Cold and unfeeling.

    Her younger self wandered in a daze as hunger began to set in. Rio would start circling soon if she didn't find food. The witch stumbled over rocks and twigs until she heard singing in the distance. She would need to be cautious about being seen. There was no telling who was associated with the Salem Survivors.

    She closed her eyes as the coven fell prey to her magic.

    "They were kind to you," Wanda said softly. "Why?"

    Agatha had an inkling that her magic imbued her breast milk. A charge up for her meant her son would benefit from the energy. But why tell them that? Would it make a difference? She didn't care what they thought of her.

    Cold and unfeeling. Cold and unfeeling.

    The speed of her memories began to pick up and blur. Soon, Nicky was learning to walk, but a cough came with it. The coven, aside from her, cheered for him at every milestone. They cried when he said his first words. They laughed when he would find himself in quite the predicament. They gagged when he would make himself sick from all the spinning he would do.

    When night would fall, and Agatha held him in her arms, the coven fell silent. Like their voices might stir the sleeping pair. Like they might anger the crying specter. Her son was sickly. Agatha had known from the moment he was born. Now, she had to worry about his health. About Death finding them. About never being strong enough.

    "Don't get attached," she warned the witches. "This is where he stops breastfeeding. His strength will fail quickly." Agatha wasn't telling them to be nice. No. She simply didn't want anyone to be surprised by the outcome.

    Now that Nicky had grown enough to understand her, Agatha turned to a new form of survival. Conning.

    "Now, remember, you go up to the fine ladies and you snatch the prettiest thing you see. Run as fast as you can to me, and I'll take care of the rest," her young-faced self said. She pushed back her son's hair, dropped a kiss to his brow.

    " 'Kay, Mama."

    "Agatha....," Wanda began. She grimaced as the child left the stables. "Please tell me you didn't."

    The goddess averted her gaze. She knew what she had done was shameful. Agatha hadn't been promised a lifetime, but she squandered time away as if she had. She should have found a coven far from Massachusetts to raise her boy in. Should have let him play with the other kids. Should have let him meet his mother. "...I did."

    "But..." The pink-clad witch fell silent.

    "That's it, Jen? No clever words? Nothing to joke about?" Agatha hunched in on herself with a scowl. She kept her back to the group. "I know what I did was wrong. I know..." "You loved him. That's all that matters," Alice told her.

    "Oh, spare me! I know what you're really thinking. I'm evil for turning him into a thief before teaching him to read."

    "I mean, I'm not saying you're doing a great job," the goth argued. "I'm just saying that you loved him despite having a horrible mother. It's better he's a thief than someone's punching bag."

    Agatha fell silent. She wasn't a great mother, but she had never struck her child. She had never purposely had him skip a meal. Any cons they executed benefited him the most. He got a toy and a meal while she got her power. She wasn't great, but she wasn't her mother. Agatha found she could live with that idea. She would ask for no praises, of course, but she would think about that the next time she began to lose her patience with someone. "Sorry, Kale."

    "I forgive you," Jen responded. "But only because I imagine the late 1700s sucked." Agatha laughed, her eyes falling to her returning son. "They were awful, but at least I had Nicky."

    The surviving Salemites were hot on her trail again. Their hoots and hisses and howls followed her and her son as they ran through the trees. Seven against one was hardly fair, but that was a fear for feeble-magicked witches. And Agatha could fight them off, but she wasn't sure if Nicky would be okay. At the risk of Rio finding them, she would have to send him off for his safety. She just needed to buy enough time to slow them down. Then, they could set up a new camp well-hidden and warm. Winter was approaching.

    Agatha knelt before her son. "Listen to me, love. Go into the forest and find a hollow tree to hide in. Take some sticks with you to play with. Mama will come find you once she finishes her game, okay?"

    He nodded. "Have fun, Mama!"

    She grinned maliciously. "Oh, I will. Off you go!"

    The boy ran off into the thicket with a giggle. She should have told him to keep quiet. Agatha wiggled her fingers, summoning her magic. If Rio had given her anything worthwhile, it was knowledge.

    "So...question..."

    "What is it this time, Jen?"

    "Where's Rio in all of this? Why haven't we seen her?"

    Agatha looked away from her rather impressive battle display to eye the other witch. "I ran away from her. She was going to take Nicky. She still is. I was buying myself time." "Surely-"

    "Jen, I know. I've already talked to my wife about keeping her out of our son's life. Trust me when I say I'm very aware that I fucked up a lot after asking for more time. I keep doing it, but I'm trying." She wished she had her coat to wrap around herself. Billy was definitely going to make her a new one now.

    Wanda rolled over with a yawn. "We're still in the woods? How much time did you spend out here?"

    "I'd say three hundred of the four hundred, give or take a couple of decades. Technology had yet to be introduced outside of buggies and coffins." She laid on her side but refused to sleep. Agatha missed seeing her son in his element. Now that he was back in her younger self's arms, she breathed a little easier.

    The Scarlet Witch tugged her into a hug.

    "What are you doing?" Not that she was opposed to snuggles with the red head, Agatha was just a bit confused. So much was happening emotionally in the vast amount of time they'd been in her memories.

    "You looked sad. Hugs make me feel better when I'm sad." Wanda spooned her, propping her head up on her right arm so she could see over Agatha. "I miss the kids." "I miss them too."

    Agatha fought sleep as Nicky walked alongside her. Señor Scratchy, a goat for the time being, walked on the other side of the boy. (The familiar had been given strict instructions to always serve as Nicky's protector first, and Agatha's familiar second.) She sat up quickly as those fateful words left her son's lips.

    "Mama, why do you kill witches?"

    "To survive," both Agathas answered. One was cautious, one was full of remorse.

    "Oof," Alice said, wincing. "This is gonna be awkward."

    "Yes, thank you!" The goddess rolled her eyes. The end was nigh.

    "Could we not stay with the witches and survive with them?"

    Instead of watching Nicky, all eyes were on the immortal. She gave them a look. "No," she said in tandem with her memory.

    "Why?" the coven said in unison with Nicky.

    Agatha would laugh if it weren't so heartbreaking. "Because they will try to kill us," the doubles explained. "Because no one wants me alive," the goddess added, as she should have said from the beginning.

    Nicky was alone in asking, "Why?" a second time.

    "If you want to survive, get used to this feeling," her memory said, also alone.

    Wanda crossed her arms, facing her. "You told Billy the same thing. You upset him." "It was the best lie I could come up with. How else do you tell a child that you can't be a witch and die with clean hands? Not unless you die young like Nicky, that is." Agatha looked over at the pair as they walked in silence for a bit. This bit, she would love to see again. "Don't talk."

    Nicky had begun to sing. "Walk, walk, walk the road..."

    Tears welled in her eyes. She might have told Billy it meant nothing, but it meant everything. It was theirs, mother and son, to use when one had grown icy towards the other. An olive branch. Love without being directly stated. Not that Agatha hadn't told Nicky she loved him all the time. But his Ballad was sacred to her. Nicky's Ballad was the song that played with every beat of her heart. Her son, the lyrical genius. His song, tarnished. "Oh! You walk this road alone, do you?" Agatha said in time with herself. She smiled through the tears as he grinned up at her.

    "He's got a great voice," Jen said, tears in her eyes. In fact, the who group was openly crying. The child had captured their hearts. Good. He deserved it.

    "If you had had a coven, do you think you could have bought him more time?" Alice asked. She picked at the hem of her shirt, raising her eyes only. The young witch was afraid to pick at her wound. Agatha appreciated the gentle approach.

    "Maybe...but it would have been the same result," she told the goth. In front of them, Agatha began to teach Nicky the basic hand movements for spell casting. The hands of Fate had begun to tick down again. Soon, there would be no light left in her soul. She worried her lip as Nicky coughed. The sound went straight through her just like it had those days.

    Ignoring the gaunt look to his face, the way his limbs dragged after waking, the rattle in his chest with each cough, the pair continued their life. There was enough cause for concern that Agatha, the memory one, had pulled back on their cons simply to play in the fields with him. His strength was waning, even if she didn't want to see it. Nicky began to collect sticks, teaching himself to weave. His mother held him tighter each night until... "Mama, can I sing my song in the tavern today? It worked really good with the last town."

    The goddess curled into a ball. This was it. The day she lost her ball of sunlight. The evening fall of her life dissipating into a cold, winter's night. Agatha wasn't ready to face this moment. Even though her Nicky was alive and well in Westview, the pain of losing him was deeply engrained into her soul. If Agatha had been Rio's scar, Nicky was hers. "He's gotten so good at putting on a performance," Wanda said, nudging the immortal. "He certainly got that from you. You two could have formed your own traveling show with costume designs and everything."

    "If you have any self-preservation skills, you won't touch me for the next few 'days'." Agatha curled up tighter, shaking.

    They were in the tavern now. Nicky was preparing to take a stand and sing his song. Everyone would be clapping and cheering soon, but the goddess was scanning her memory to see where Rio could have been hiding. She knew Death had been there. There was no other way for Nicky to know his time was coming to an end unless she had said something. But then Agatha thought back to what Billy and Rio had said. That he was hurting, and they could feel it. Her shoulders began to shake as a sob worked its way up. She had used her sick child for a few coppers and silvers. He was dying before her very eyes, but she had focused on the coins until it was too late.

    The coven, excluding Agatha, clapped along with the boy as he sang. He bobbed his head and tapped his foot, but his eyes had settled on the corner behind Agatha. He saw what she could not. Death was calling him Home.

    "I thank you, but no," he said softly, a scratch to his voice. Then, Nicky turned and faced both Agatha's with a firm look. "My mother needs me home."

    "Wait...Since when does he call you 'mother'?" Alice asked. She looked over at Agatha for a response, but the older woman was biting her hand to keep from crying. "Today's the day, isn't it?"

    Agatha nodded, eyes sliding shut as the first few tears fell.

    Nicky ran off to the forest as his mother was left reeling. She knew just as well as the coven did. Death would be with them soon.

    "Where'd he go?" Jen said, panicking with Memory Agatha. "How did he disappear so fast?" "I...I don't know," Wanda said. "Agatha, where did he go?"

    The immortal was crying too hard to answer. Unlike reliving his birth with physical pain, she was wracked with emotional pain. Precious hours were giving way to Fate. Agatha wasn't ready. Would never be ready. And the worst part? She'd convinced him to come back just for him to die all over again one day. The goddess sobbed harder.

    "Mama," Nicky began. He rubbed at his eyes, his strength running on fumes. The boy was now between realms. He was never going to make it to morning. "We can kill more witches tomorrow. I promise," he told her. Her perfect son, always thinking of her. How had he come from her? How could he be so good when she was icky like tar?

    Jen sniffled. "I know this is a serious moment, but why does he say it like it's your shared hobby? Nicky, you don't kill witches for fun," the woman cried. "My dress is filthy now. You owe me, Agatha."

    Agatha flipped her off with her free hand. Her right, unfortunately, had begun to bleed from how hard she was biting it. There was still an hour before they laid down to sleep, but the immortal was still begging for more time. "Just a little bit more," she whimpered before biting her hand once more.

    Her younger self sang with him, adding new lyrics to his Ballad before laying him down. She covered him with her cloak, wrapping him up tightly. Her precious son. Keeper of her joy. The child of Death and the Divine Mother would be closing his eyes for the last time. "My blood, my tears, my bone," she sang to him. She fixed his hair, making sure he was comfortable.

    "Oh...," Alice said before she burst into tears.

    "Maiden, Mother, Crone," Nicky finished, voice soft. He tapped at her brooch with a small, weak smile. His breathing had gone shallow, but his mother had yet to worry. She simply believed today was one of his bad days. He was tired, so he was falling asleep faster. Both Agathas were expecting to stay up longer. To hold that image with them, but she had fallen asleep. Now, the goddess had to face the whiplash that came with the night being skipped. From bittersweet embrace straight into a nightmare.

    Nicky was cold.

    Both versions of herself pressed to the ground with a wail. Only one begged for more time. Only one thanked Rio for her gift.

    The coven huddled together only because Agatha initiated it. She pulled them tight to her and held them. Much as she would deny it later, she was the oldest. She was their leader and their mentor. She knew the pain they must be feeling.

    Even before getting trapped in Billy's sick and twisted memory spell, they were attached to her son. To experience her loss as their own had to be just as gut-wrenching. They mourned together as a coven should. As a family should.

    "His was the only grave I ever dug," Agatha told the group, still tangled up in their arms. "And I vowed to never dig another because I would never love someone that much again." "I'm sorry I talked all that shit about you trading your son," Jen told her. "I can't imagine how that made you feel."

    "I deserved it. Death gave me a gift, and I spat on it. I deserved every single thing I got from that moment on."

    Wanda squeezed her tightly. "No one deserves to lose their child, Agatha. No matter what they've done."

    Now solitary, a mourning Agatha laid a bundle of lavenders on her son's grave and sat back. "I have always known... This Road is cruel and wild... I bury my own heart... Here with you, my child.......... If one be gone, we carry on..... But every mile I go.... With every bend.... Beyond the end.... Your mother loves you so," she sang. She sniffled as she put a lock of Nicky's hair in her locket. The woman was distraught, deeply so, as she closed her brooch.

    Alice hiccupped. "It was coven two!"

    Agatha huffed out a laugh, pain paused for just a moment.

    "So you must know the way then?" a strange woman asked.

    "Who the fuck do you think you are?" Jen growled as the memory of Agatha barked a, "How dare you?"

    "You haven't even finished mourning," Alice grumbled. "Did witches not have manners back then, or what? She worse than the paparazzi."

    Agatha chuckled brokenly. "Don't worry. She's about to be dished up."

    "Aggie, what did you do?" Wanda asked, sighing.

    "She deserved it," the witch argued.

    "No, no. She's got a point," Jen told Wanda. "This woman really watched us bury a child and didn't think, 'Hm, I should come back later. She seems busy.'?"

    Alice tapped Agatha's hand. "....Where's Rio?"

    "I wouldn't hold my breath. She doesn't show up again for a few months," Agatha sighed. "It was a point of contention for me, actually. We've also worked through that a bit." "Well, I, for one, am glad," Wanda told her. "You two are perfect for each other. We'd all be very sad if the two of you were to split, or fight, or just go silent for days at a time." Jen and Alice mumbled in agreement.

    "Don't worry. I'm probably going to take her upstairs as soon as we get back, if we get back." Agatha sniffed as a sacrificial coven was gathered. "Just an 'FYI', but a lot of people are going to die now. Like....a lot more."

    "Can I ask why?"

    "You could, but I think my memories speak for themselves," Agatha told Wanda. Younger Agatha became belligerent once the 'incantation' failed to summon the Road. Jen and Alice shared a knowing laugh.

    "So, Nicky, our son," Jen began, "created a song so catchy that it became a legend of its own?"

    Agatha rolled her eyes. "I'm only sharing him because you've all done the hard part with me. But, yes, Nicholas's Ballad was the true song. I'm glad it stayed alive, but......I know I abused it. That's what makes things difficult now that he's back. One day, he's going to grow up and learn what I did to it. He'll be angry."

    "Agatha, you literally turned killing witches into a bonding exercise. He might be upset that you weaponized it, but he won't be surprised or anything. All you need to do is prove you won't use it that way ever again. In fact, have you even used it before you met us?" The goddess shook her head. "The last time I used it was the 90's. It was hard finding anyone who believed the legend. It was like pulling teeth with you guys. And I only asked you to form a coven with me because the Salem Seven were after me. Wanda took my magic, and Billy sparked the idea."

    Wanda huffed. "We're going to have to curb his impulse control. He gets that from you, y'know!"

    Agatha laughed. "Oh, honey, he gets a lot of his flair from me. I'm still waiting to see what he got from you outside of theatrics and magic."

    "I'm putting Frozen on when we get home," Wanda told her firmly.

    The goddess hissed. "Oh, I hate you!"

    You Were Born Evil P.3 Chapter Summary Winding down on the last leg of Agatha's Memory Lane.

    [•••••••] separates memory events from the coven's scenes.

    Chapter Notes TW: Toxic Relationship (not very detailed or graphic. I hardly touch it because I don't have the experience or delicacy to fully explore that.)

    Apologies for the delay! I don't have the time to do a proper edit, so here's what I've got. I will def go through and rework it some time this weekend. Enjoy!

    See the end of the chapter for more notes Rio was back.

    Agatha let out a shaky exhale as her younger self stiffened.

    Death looked down at her, the broken version, as she hugged a wall. The goddess couldn't remember where exactly she'd wound up after killing the first coven. She just remembered her grief bending time as she waited for her wife to appear. Looking at herself, Agatha was surprised she hadn't been killed on the street like a rabid dog. Hungry, cold, and alone, she faced Death.

    "I'm here, amor," Rio told her softly as she crouched. A hand was extended only for it to be slapped away.

    "I hate you," the stranger growled.

    "I had to do my job, Agatha," Death reminded.

    Wanda hugged Agatha's arm. "For what it's worth, I don't think there was anything either of you could have done to make amends," she mumbled. "You were both too hurt. You were both blameless."

    The immortal sighed. "She never once blamed me for my reaction. Not until things got out of hand. If I had just cried it all out here, we could have survived the coming years." "You must've made up at some point," Jen told her. "Even though you both were getting under each other's skin, we could all tell you both cared about each other on the Road." "Actually, her appearance on the Road was the second time I'd seen her in...I dunno...a century?" Agatha shifted to cradle the potions witch better. "Thing's went south real quick." Flashes of purple lit their faces up as younger Agatha forced Death away. "Do you think she could have said anything to make you feel better here?" Alice asked. "Like, I think about the last time I saw my mom, and I can't think of anything that would have eased the hurt but time."

    Agatha combed a hand through the young witch's hair. "No. I was too far gone to listen to anyone. She could have crawled on her hands and knees for the rest of her life, and it wouldn't have been enough.

    The Ballad was sung over...and over...and over...and over...and...

    "You actually did kill a lot of witches," Wanda huffed. "I thought Jen was kidding." Agatha laughed dryly. "Not my most shining moments. Although, I do still believe most of them deserved to die."

    "Don't take this the wrong way, but I would have been surprised if you didn't go around killing everybody," Alice told her. "That's sorta always been your vibe. Even in your early days."

    She hummed in thought. "Do you guys...and this is just a silly question...But did you see anything I might have missed? Y'know, evil wise?" Agatha fidgeted as she waited for them to share their thoughts. She already knew her mother's opinion. But what did the coven think of her so far? (No, for the millionth time, she doesn't care what they think. She's just curious. Curious is fine!)

    "Honestly, I think you were just a normal girl," the youngest answered. Alice shifted to get a good look at her. "You saw you had different magic, but you didn't immediately start killing people. The first two were accidents. They used that to brand you. If any of them had cared, you probably would have been taught to control it at some point."

    Jen covered her mouth as a yawn pulled at her face. "Look, killing is wrong, but some of these are self-defense. I mean...look at this group right now. You called them some names and that warranted attacking you?" She blew a raspberry. "They lost their cool too quickly. Now, me, I was gonna kick your ass old style."

    "Like it rough, do ya?" Agatha asked her, winking. "Careful now, Wanda might get jealous." The red head elbowed her. "I'm not jealous," she grumbled. "Stop telling people things like that or Rio's going to reap me."

    "I wish she were here to 'reap' me," Agatha sighed. "I know things are about to get dicey for my other self, power of foresight and all, so I was hoping...youcouldsparesomeadvice" The group looked at her with matching furrowed brows. "What was that?" Alice asked. "Don't make me say it again, guys," Agatha groaned.

    Jen smirked. "Consider it payback for all your snarky comments on the Road." The goddess huffed. "Fine!" She crossed her arms, shaking her hair out of her face. "I, Agatha Harkness, am requesting advice. I want to do more for Rio. I want...to be a better wife."

    The trio squealed, hugging her tightly.

    "Your heart," Alice said, grinning ear to ear.

    "What about it?" Agatha asked, eyes widening. She pressed a hand to her chest. "You have one," she laughed. The goth hugged her again, tucking her head under the goddess' chin.

    The immortal felt her breath hitch at the gesture. "I will deny this as soon as we're out of here, so enjoy it."

    "Okay, now I'm jealous," the Scarlet Witch told her. "How come Alice gets a real hug and we don't?"

    Agatha smirked. "Because Alice is the only one who didn't try to kill me out of this group."

    Jen winced. "I take it this is about to be bad," she mumbled.

    Agatha nodded silently

    Death had appeared to collect the fifth coven Agatha had slaughtered. Her vibrant green cloak had darkened significantly. The shade was closest to that of evergreen pine needles. The immortal woman faced her estranged lover, a flower twirled between her fingertips. "It's been a while..."

    Agatha, in a Victorian dress and hat, glared at her wife. "That was quick. I figured you would have taken your time."

    "You're the one who stayed behind an extra fifteen minutes."

    "Oh! So you are following me," the woman snarked. "Always around when you're not wanted. Gone when you're needed." The prim mortal jutted her chin out, her steely eyes unwavering.

    "What you're doing is wrong, Agatha. This isn't what Nicky wanted for-" Purple was fired off like a shotgun blast. "Don't you dare!" Agatha barred her teeth. "Nicky was my son. Mine! You took him!"

    Rio growled. "Listen to me!" She raised roots in hopes of holding the woman in place. "If I hadn't done my job, he would have suffered more. Do you think I wanted to hurt you like this?"

    Agatha tore the greenery to shreds as she advanced on Death. "You must have!" She sent the immortal flying. "You said you would burn the world for me!"

    The Green Witch rose, her magic swirling around her. "You're not the only one hurting," she ground out. "He was my son, too."

    The witch flew into a rage, her body soaring to collide with her wife's. They fell to the ground as Agatha wrapped her hands around the immortal's neck. "You took him!" They rolled around, struggling as Rio forced her onto her back. "It was my job!" Death pinned her down. "Agatha, why won't you listen to me?"

    "I don't want anything to do with you," the woman hissed. "You took him. You took my Nicky." Tears were streaming down her face, lip trembling. "I hate you." "You don't mean that," Rio told her, her face softening. "If you did, you wouldn't have stayed to see me."

    The goddess pursed her lips. "I hate it when she does that."

    "What? Calls you on your bullshit?" Jen laughed. "She knows you like the back of her...uh...carpals." The witch elbowed her before groaning.

    "Are you guys really making out right now?" Wanda said, her nose wrinkling. "I don't know if that's a good idea. You're both pretty...messed up."

    Agatha laughed. "I missed my wife. Can you blame a girl for finding an opportunity and taking it?" She winced as her memory self grew rougher with Death. Rio had told her she was the one who usually took. It was a lot harder to ignore that fact now. Any sane person would have run for the hills after the rough fucking Agatha dished out, but Rio, her wounded Rio, just kept coming back for more.

    She may not have been her mother when it came to Nicky, but she'd learned to be her mother when it came to her wife. Agatha looked down at her injured hand with a sigh. The next one- hundred-and-fifty years were going to hurt.

    "Do you want me to heal that?" Wanda asked her, her green eyes falling to the bloodied hand. "No," she told her. Agatha hid the wound away under her pajama shirt. "I've cheated through my pain enough."

    A hand shook the goddess awake. She rubbed at an eye, looking around. Based on the location, Agatha had slept through the latter half of the 1800s. There wasn't much she'd missed there. Just some time galivanting around in Eastern Europe in search of the Darkhold. No biggie. "What's wrong?" she asked, voice thick with sleep. "Did you find a way out?" Wanda shook her head. "We've got questions."

    "Of course you do," she huffed. "That's where Billy gets it from. Go on, Maximoff. Fire away."

    The red head mouthed 'sorry' before continuing. "I know you've been studying magic on your own up until this point, but I still don't get why you went after the Darkhold." "For starters, that's not a question. Secondly, I was looking into advanced necromancy." Agatha rolled her shoulders. "Oh...hey...It's my anniversary."

    "So that is the Titanic," Alice said, nodded exaggeratedly. "I thought it looked familiar." "Wait...If you're on the Titanic....How did you bind me?" Jen asked her. "Ah..." Agatha had forgotten about that fib. "I didn't. Bind you, that is. I did bind women once I got back to Boston, but not you."

    The witch stared at her in abject confusion. "But you said..."

    The goddess juggled her hands as if the truth were a set of rice sacks. "I needed to find a way to get you off the Road. I figured if Billy believed it, the Road would unbind you. So....So, I y'know..."

    "But if you didn't...And you..." The woman looked back over at younger Agatha. "I don't understand."

    The immortal pulled her closer, an arm over Jen's shoulder. "See, I don't know who bound you. It could have been a number of witches. But I, personally, didn't get roped into that mess until after I sunk the Titanic."

    Alice whipped her head in Agatha's direction at the words 'I sunk'.

    "If I didn't pretend I had, you would have been stuck in that trial with me. Things were already complicated. Billy's mind was controlling the Road, so I tricked him and you. One thing led to another, and, boom, your powers are back."

    Jen blinked slowly for several long moments.

    By now, Agatha was lounging as Death appeared. She sat across from the mortal, face firm. Now, her cloak was shifting to a brown with little green to accent her wardrobe. "Tomorrow's our anniversary," the witch said carefully. "Thought I'd give you a vacation. Work and play, hm?"

    Rio lurched forward, eyes torn between hope and disgust. Agatha had done that to her. Had made her wary of mortals. "You remembered?"

    She stood from the chaise-lounge to straddle her estranged lover's hips. "How could I forget?" she breathed. Agatha fisted Rio's hair and pulled her in for a kiss. Her free hand clawed at a shoulder, drawing blood.

    Why couldn't she had just been honest with herself? That she still loved Death as much as she loved Nicky. Why did she have to go and twist something so special to alleviate her own pain?

    Rio was bound and gagged. Was choked and clawed at as Agatha took. As Agatha inflicted pain she thought her wife deserved just for Rio to turn around and press soft kisses to her face. To rock her before Agatha was to flee from her emotions and her pain. Just this once, however, the two indulged in the fantasy that nothing was wrong between them. "You're not running?" Death asked, voice steely. She pulled at her bindings but thought better of it. The Green Witch relaxed back against the chaise with a wary look. Agatha stroked her cheeks, brushing hair back as if she didn't have the Ruler of Life and Death at her mercy. (Well, Rio could break free whenever. But that was another part of the fantasy Rio played into.) "You have the most beautiful eyes, my love,' she whispered. "I would give anything to see these every morning."

    "You could," Rio told her. "But you choose not to. If you would just-" Agatha pressed a finger to lush lips. "I don't want to fight. Can't we just...pretend? Just for today."

    Death swallowed her words before nodding. "Okay, Agatha," she said softly. "Just for today." She unbound the witch and pulled her into a hug. Agatha sighed into it, pressed her nose into Rio's neck. "Happy 217th anniversary, my love."

    Rio gripped her tighter. "Happy anniversary, amor."

    "Why not longer?" Alice asked. "I mean, it's clear as day you love her. Why couldn't you two just talk it out?"

    Agatha swallowed thickly. "I always was too smart for my own good. I knew if I asked her not to bring it up, she wouldn't. Rio always thinks of me...does for me." She laughed, bitter and pained. "But I thought I could have it all, no strings attached. I thought I could ignore my emotions."

    The coven did their best to comfort her.

    "Well, that's one of the things you can consider working on," Wanda told her. "What?"

    "Giving back. I'm not saying throw yourself at her feet and beg forgiveness. But you could start by complimenting her more."

    "I do compliment her," Agatha argued. "I just don't say it out loud because then all of you would give us shit."

    Wanda rolled her eyes. "No, don't flirt. Compliment. Tell her something like...Like how you love her eyes! You two go straight for the kill. Chase her a little bit." "Oh! Go on a date, but let her pick everything," Alice suggested.

    Agatha laughed, more to herself than the others. "I don't know if you've noticed, but Rio isn't exactly the type to do all of that."

    Jen fixed her with a look. "After looking at all of this," she said, gesturing to the sad, sad looks the couple were giving one another in the memory, "I can safely say she was having a blast on the Road. Rio wants to be wanted. That's the whole reason why you two got married in the first place."

    Alice nodded. "Girl, we all saw those looks at the campfire. You both love each other so much! But you, Agatha, get in your own head too much."

    "You were doing so good once you two got back together," Jen said. "What happened? Why did you pull away from her again?"

    Agatha looked from them to her memories. She knew exactly what they meant. The longing in her own eyes was just as intense as the longing in her wife's. When was the last time she treated Rio with a compliment or tried to make her feel special? "Okay...I hear you guys. I'll," she sucked in a breath. "I'll take her on a date. Hopefully enough people can avoid dying so it's longer than thirty minutes."

    "Right...But the pulling away bit?"

    She rubbed a temple. "I may have been a bit jealous."

    "Of Rio?" Alice gave her a look.

    Agatha pursed her lips. Sharing her feelings, especially those tied to recent issues, still felt odd. "Yes...and no." She grappled with her tired mind in search of the right words. "I didn't want to face Nicky when I died. Then, he came back. Now I see the way she's so...so maternal and I just..." She waved her hands around, blinking back tears. "I'm not my mother, but I'm not much better."

    Jen took her hand. "That's what you've got us for, Harkness. We'll keep you on the straight and narrow. Besides, we all know it'll take a village to raise him and Billy...and probably Tommy."

    She laughed, squeezing the hand back. "You guys still get on my nerves, though." "I'd be worried if we didn't," Alice told her. "Now, why did you sink the Titanic?" Agatha sniffled. "It was an anniversary gift to Rio."

    "Girl!" Jen dropped her head into her hands. "You created one of the most infamous disasters as a gift! Definitely don't give any more of those to her."

    "What! She loved it," the goddess argued. "Look!"

    The deadly couple were resting near the bow of the ship when a younger, happier looking couple appeared. They shared a look of annoyance as the young man helped the woman stand at the bow of the ship.

    "I'm the King of the World," the man shouted, arms spread open wide. His plaything followed suit until the two were whooping and shouting like yahoos.

    "Sometimes, I think mortals should stop breeding," Rio told her wife.

    Agatha grinned maliciously. "I was going to wait until morning, but I think I'll go ahead and speed things along. Is that a problem with you?"

    Death grew a smirk. "By all mean, mi flor. You won't find me protesting." The young woman sauntered away in search of the captain. She found the older man sitting in his cabin. He was a tired old thing, but just what she needed. Agatha knocked at the frame, posing suggestively. "Say, I've always wanted to steer a ship, mister." He quirked a brow. "I beg your pardon!"

    The witch leaned forward, pouting. "You wouldn't deny a woman the experience, would you? All that power in your hands. It's such a big ship! How do you do it, sir?" The captain stepped over to her, ready to throw her out, when she blew some of her magic into his face. She waved her hand around his face, eyes shimmering in the dim cabin light. "Filium imperio anime." Agatha pulled up as if tightening a cord. She grinned as the captain straightened. "Now, then, let's get this show on the road."

    Once inside the wheelhouse, Rio reappeared. She licked the inside of her mouth as Agatha commanded the man to stand at the helm. "Mm...What do you have planned?" Death purred. She sucked in a breath as her wife walked over to her.

    "You'll see," the witch told her. She pressed Rio up against the door, her lips attaching to the long column of neck calling to her.

    "I didn't know mass murder could be a form of foreplay," Jen laughed. "You guys really will fuck over anything, won't you?"

    "She could have gotten laid on the Road if she had just waited a few more minutes," Agatha grumbled. She stretched as her younger self slipped a hand between her wife's legs. "Oh~! You guys are gonna watch this time?" A spark of jealously flared at the thought. Alice shrugged. "You guys are constantly having sex. I'm not even shocked by it anymore." "Yeah! Like, you're married to her, but I feel like I'm married to the both you now, too." Jen rested her head on her palm. "Plus, my curiosity got the better of me. Oh...wait...you're going to literally bone?" The witch's eyes nearly popped out of her skull (hehe). "See, this is why I'm not worried about anyone stealing her from me," Agatha sighed, content. "No one else is willing to love her in all forms like I am."

    "She's bones Agatha!" The potions witch threw herself back with a huff. She pressed her hands to her face with a muffled scream.

    Wanda opened her mouth.

    "Yes, you can ask questions," the goddess told her. "Let's just skip the preface and find out what's eating you...even though it could be me."

    The red head glared at her, a blush creeping up her neck. "Stop that!" Wanda cleared her throat. "But now I'm curious. Can she feel anything? You couldn't......could you?" "Rio as a skeleton? Yes. Me as a skeleton? No. If I could have, you would have heard us rattling away all the time," she said with a laugh. "Me, I miss my wife!"

    "I want you inside me," young Agatha growled.

    "Oh my god, Agatha!" Wanda's eyebrows practically shot off towards the heavens. "Funny...That's what Rio said too."

    The goddess paced. "Okay, I'm starting to go stir crazy. I really need Billy to figure something out, or I'm going to risk tearing the Universe to get out of here." Jen leaned back, rolling her head to pop her neck. "Okay...What traumatizing thing is coming up?"

    Agatha hugged herself, glancing at the club her memory self was about to enter. "Not traumatizing for me..."

    "Mom!"

    "There it is. Yup..." She put her hands on her hips. If only she could take a sip of that brandy right about now. "Mama Wu, everybody!"

    Alice made a face. "You're kinda...staring at her intensely."

    Agatha pursed her lips. "I was just admiring the color scheme and the new age sound of the late 60s, early 70s. But looking back-"

    "Agatha, did you fuck my mom?"

    "No!" The goddess hugged herself. "Unfortunately for your mother and I, she had to go play a mean song."

    "Ohhhhhh," Jen said, drawing the word out like she was unraveling a spool of thread. "I was wondering how you must have felt about this version."

    "Nicky's will always be my favorite......But Lorna would have made him proud." Agatha eyed the woman on the stage. She turned away to avoid seeing herself break down. No point in reliving that trauma.

    "That must have been painful," Wanda said. She combed her fingers through her hair. Scarlet locks, once vibrant, were greasy tendrils hanging limply around her face."It looks like you hadn't had a reminder of him in a very long time."

    "Very long," she mumbled. Agatha turned back around to find Alice. The girl would need her support. Agatha may not have cared for her own mother, but the young woman had had a real mother-daughter relationship. This was bound to sting. "Come here," she said, waving the goth over.

    Alice slid into her hold, resting her teary-eyed face on her shoulder. "Thanks for not killing my mom."

    "She was a good woman. She deserved all the time in the world."

    "You look great in that jacket," Wanda said with a yawn. "You should wear leather more often."

    "I would, but Stevie stole it. Haven't been able to find a better one since." Agatha glared at the floor. She'd make the Ancient One return it, or else.

    "Why are you forming a coven? You haven't needed to con one in some time," Alice said. "Oh, yeah. You were asleep for the last 'year'. I'm about to get the Darkhold. These young things are about to get a one-way ticket to the Afterlife."

    "Agatha," Wanda reminded.

    The goddess rolled her eyes. "Their sacrifices weren't in vain, at least." "Still murder," the Scarlet Witch told her.

    "Yeah, yeah. I've got a list in my head now. I'll visit their graves and remove the graffiti I left."

    The coven gave her a look.

    "That's a joke, you guys! I'm a killer, not a monster." She turned back to her memories. "Oh boy..."

    "Well, well, well," Death began, stepping from the shadows. "Just can't help yourself, can you?"

    "Don't harsh my vibe, man," Goth Agatha warned. "I was never even here." She turned to leave.

    Rio appeared in front of her, a hand gripping her throat. "I know where you're going," she growled. "And I won't let you have it."

    Agatha licked her lips, eyes dark. "As if you could stop me." She headbutted the Green Witch. She laughed as her ex fell to the ground. "Been fun, but I've a library to check out." The mortal took to the skies. She never expected Rio to chase after her. "Agatha!" Death pulled a gust of wind towards her, dragging Agatha along in the process. "You're not running from me this time."

    Purple blasted the immortal back towards the ground. "Somebody's panicking," she said, mocking the cosmic entity. "It's almost like you care." Agatha pulled a nasty trick from her hat, staking Rio to the ground with hexed steel. "Stay," she ordered. "And think about what you've done."

    "Agatha, don't! I won't..." Death's face grew pained as she pulled at the dark magic binding her to the land. "Don't leave me!"

    "You left me first," Agatha spat. "I'm simply returning the favor." She turned away, leaving her now former wife to scream after her.

    "Why is the Darkhold conveniently in Salem?"

    "Because the Universe has a sick sense of humor," Agatha told Jen. She lay fully on the floor, her body starting to ache. Billy's spell was finally taking a toll on her. There was a reason memory spells were dangerous, after all. "I'm taking a nap." She rolled over and closed her eyes.

    "Uh...the memory stopped," Alice told her.

    Agatha opened her eyes. "And?"

    "And now it's back," Jen said.

    "Does it do that every time I sleep?"

    "...No. That's new."

    Agatha sat up and turned to find her memory self. "What the hell, Billy? What's so important about reliving all of this?"

    "Did you talk about the Darkhold around him?" Wanda asked, eyes widening. Jen audibly wince. "That was a my bad. I brought it up on the Road."

    Agatha shrugged. "When? I was with him the whole time."

    "It was during my trial. We went to find the corkscrew." The witch looked away. "I might have put it in his head that you traded Nicky for the Darkhold."

    "Well, that's just lovely, Jen!" She crossed her arms in a huff.

    "He didn't believe it, if it makes you feel any better."

    "It doesn't. No wonder he poked and prodded so much! Do you know how many hours of pleading and begging I had to endure because of you?" Agatha got up to pace. She didn't last more than a few steps before she dropped back down in a huff. "I don't want to worry anybody, but if I don't get out of here soon, we might have an emergency on our hands." "What do you mean?" Wanda was at her side, hands running over her. "You feel cold." "That's the whole 'Moon Goddess' thing. I wouldn't worry about that," Agatha told her. She raised her left hand and tried to spark her magic. It puffed out pathetically. "Yeah, that'll do it."

    "Are you dying?" the red head asked.

    Alice and Jen were suddenly checking over her like a team of doctors. The goddess slapped their hands away.

    "The spell is eating up my magic to keep it going. Problem is running out might kill all of you."

    "Crossing over isn't...isn't that bad," Alice said, gulping.

    "That would be the case, but Rio can't come over here to get you guys. You're inside my head, and I'm inside my head, too." She waved her hands around. "So, you'd likely disappear forever."

    Jen furrowed her brows, brain working overtime. "How do we stop you from running out of magic?"

    Agatha pursed her lips, looking at Wanda. "Mama needs a boost, Wands. Care to do the honors?"

    The red head shifted. "Our magic doesn't work in here, remember?"

    The goddess smirked. "Darling, there are plenty of ways to skin a cat." The Scarlet Witch gulped. "I don't like what you're insinuating."

    Agatha rolled her shoulders and fluttered her lashes. "I'm a succubus, Wanda. I can syphon magic through intimate acts."

    "We are not having sex!"

    Agatha laughed. Her memories flickered. "It's just a kiss, hun. I'm not asking you to marry me or anything. I'd ask Jen, but I know I'll kill her. She doesn't have enough juice." Wanda glared at her. "Was this all just a rouse so you could smack your lips to mine?" "I have better ways of flirting. Trust me. There's nothing romantic about watching a sad, old woman have her heart broken by the world." Agatha waved the witch over. "Come on. I'll make it quick."

    "No tongue," Wanda demanded. "Just...just a peck."

    "Gonna need more than a peck to keep us all alive, hot stuff."

    The red head groaned. "You're the worst!"

    "Yeah, my memories established that for us. Kinda don't have all day, Wanda." The witch stormed over and pulled the goddess in for a kiss. Agatha pulled at the chaos magic humming under the woman's skin. She curled her fingers along Wanda's arms as energy and life rushed back into her. Agatha closed her eyes, feeding and feeding until her magic stopped pulling. She stepped away with a gasp, eyes opening.

    Wanda looked tired, but alive. She wiped her mouth with the back of her hand before sliding down to the floor of Agatha's mind. "You have morning breath," the woman remarked. "When you find me a sink and toothbrush, I'll happily wash up for you." Agatha wiggled her fingers, a light purple glowing. "Back to full. Thank you for your sacrifice. I'm sure it was life changing."

    "Don't talk to me."

    Agatha rolled her eyes. "I wouldn't have asked if there was another way, Wanda. If we wanna get back to Billy, we have to survive."

    "I don't know how much longer we can go like this," Alice told her. "I'm starving." The goddess sighed. "I know. I'm sorry. Not much we can do in here."

    Jen hugged the younger witch. "Isn't your life almost over? Won't we just pop out once we catch up to Billy sending us through?"

    Agatha looked away. She had been hoping they'd be rescued before anyone used their brain and noticed the real issue. Now, she didn't have much choice but let the others know. "...Maybe."

    Jen scowled. She rose to her feet. "Maybe? What do you mean, 'maybe'? How long are we stuck in here for, Agatha!"

    "I don't know!" Agatha ran a hand down her face. "In the original spell, the caster goes in with the enchanted. You sift through what you want and then get the hell out. Billy Big Shot didn't do that!" She took a steadying breath. If she panicked, they'd panic. It was her job to keep everyone calm. "There are two possibilities. One, we enter a mind-altering loop where we watch ourselves in the mindscape; or, two, we just start all over." Alice dropped her face into her hands with a sniffle.

    "Can you at least make us some food?" Jen asked. "We're not immortal like you and Wanda." "....I can't," she said, feeling the familiar sting of incompetence. "At least, not anything substantial. I might be able to make an apple or two."

    "Make a leaf, for all I care. Just give us something to eat," the witch told her. Agatha sighed. "Give me your shirt."

    "My shirt?"

    "Yes, your shirt, Jen. I need something to make an apple out of. I'm not wearing anything underneath this." She tugged at the hem of her pajama shirt.

    The witch handed over her pink top. "Glad I wore a tank top today," she grumbled. Agatha infused her magic into the shirt, mixing transfiguration and transmutation spells in hopes of creating something edible. She let out a sigh of relief as two small apples appeared. "Sorry, Wanda. We'll have to sit this one out."

    The Scarlet Witch waved her off. "They need it more."

    The goddess turned back to her memories with a sigh. "Come on, Billy. Get your head out of your ass."

    Jen sat up straight as she saw herself. "Hey, this is where you came and wrecked my shop!" Alice gave her a look. "You guys had met before?"

    Agatha shrugged. "I was making a list and checking it twice. Sue me." She pursed her lips as her slightly mad self descended on the midwife.

    "What is your name?" a floating Agatha asked. The ink from the Darkhold had yet to reach her the tops of her fingers. They would, in time, but not yet. She hadn't played with enough dark spells for that.

    "Jennifer Kale," the potions witch responded. She kept her back to a sturdy wall and held her ground. "What do you want?"

    "And what do you do?" Agatha looked around at the plant and herbs. "Make candles?" "I help women in need," Jen had answered. "Those are the tools of my trade. Midwifery and healing."

    The briefest flicker of a younger Agatha danced across the souped-up woman. She drug her eyes over the pink-clad witch with a sniff. "This place is a mess. You should clean it." And then she was leaving as if she had never run into the woman before.

    "You didn't kill me...because I was a midwife," Jen said slowly.

    "Like I told you before. The work you were doing was important. I wasn't going to put another woman through that pain."

    "Well, you better keep your thoughts to yourself, Harkness, because I'm going to hug the fuck out of you."

    The immortal groaned as arms wrapped around her. "This is getting ridiculous, you guys. Enough with the touching!" (Agatha Harkness found she liked group hugs.)

    Agatha paced as the others slept. Currently, her memories of running around with the Darkhold were playing back. She actually hadn't done much those days. Agatha had hidden from Death, but that was her only real goal. There was nothing for her to live for. No family. No friends. She had Señor Scratchy, but he needed little in the grand scheme of things. Her life was just...sad.

    The goddess was missing her wife and kids terribly. She missed the sun. She missed her house.

    Agatha wanted to go home.

    She was beyond tired of being in her own head. Beyond upset with watching her coven grow weak. Agatha could only keep them alive for so long before things went south. And what about Rio? Was she panicking? Did she kill Billy for trapping them in a new, inescapable trial? Was Nicky crying? Was Tommy losing his mind? Was Teddy going crazy trying to keep everyone calm? Was Billy blaming himself?

    She hoped the boy felt a healthy amount of regret and remorse. His spells were gradually growing in strength and horror. That was probably why the Ancient Ones put her in charge of his education. Anyone else would have run for the hills by now....or died. Her memory self found a covenless witch, one with a reputation as dark as hers, and drained her with a cackle.

    Agatha might have killed a lot of witches in her time, but at least she tried to remove the ones who posed threats to children. It was just unfortunate that there were so many willing to maim the innocent. Every corner she turned, a new woman set up shop. They would peddle Death and Destruction to all the unfortunate souls. They all looked for the easiest of targets in groups already struggling. (Just like she had in the beginning. Talk about self-loathing.) I preyed on the weak for a quick buck and some power, too, she reminded herself. I killed mothers and daughters. All were loved by someone. Only I had no home. Agatha sat with that knowledge. Stared at where her hand had been injured in her grief. She couldn't even heal properly.

    "Is that me?" Wanda asked, smacking her lips. She pointed to a person in black and white. "Would you look at that," Agatha said, pushing her pensive thoughts aside. "We're almost to the good bits."

    Jen and Alice stirred. "Huh? What's happening?" they asked at different intervals. "This is where I meet Wanda," Agatha explained. "Your little hex had been a treat in the beginning."

    "That's you!" Alice pointed to the two monochromatic women. "You guys looks...different." Agatha hummed. "Wanda was having her 'I Love Lucy' moment."

    The Scarlet Witch had fallen eerily silent, her eyes trained on the glimpses of her husband. The goddess swallowed the last of her irritation with the woman and pulled her into a hug. "It'll go by quick," she told Wanda. "I didn't watch him much."

    True to her word, Agatha had mostly wandered the town in search of runes the first few 'episodes'. She hadn't found any and had to keep doubling back to the Maximoff Residence. It had annoyed her, then. The inability to crack the magical code. Now, the goddess finally understood just how tragic the whole thing was. Much like her, Wanda had escaped and hidden behind her magic.

    "Girl, you are a stalker," Jen told her. "And why do we still not have color?" "We haven't gotten to the next stage of grief yet," Agatha told her. "Have some patience, will you? I'm not entirely keen on seeing the fritzy three years I was trapped under a mind-altering spell."

    "I still can't believe you messed with my talent show act. That was very mean of you," the red head huffed. She did, however, laugh at Señor Scratchy as he hopped across the stage. "It was funny. Don't be that way, Wands. The hubby was having a good time," she reasoned. "And look, now we're getting color."

    "Wait, why are you suddenly pregnant?" Alice asked. "Agatha, why didn't you go in there and ask her why her stomach just grew like that?"

    "Ah...I must have been standing too close and your magic noticed mine," the immortal said with a hum. "That, or chaos magic is just that powerful."

    "I swear, I didn't knowingly take your essence to make kids," Wanda told her. "It's extremely unethical."

    "Said the former terrorist."

    "Hey!"

    "Sorry, Wands. Old habits."

    "The babies are here," Alice cooed. She laughed as Agatha, in her 80s wear, moved to offer her help to the Maximoff's. "Oh...Oh, I don't like you doing the mind-fuckery thing. That's just...a whole lotta nope!"

    "It was very mean of Agatha," Wanda said in agreement.

    "It's too bad that it worked in pushing you closer to the edge. I mean, I feel a little bad now, but Vision's face was priceless!" She snorted, slapping her thigh.

    "And to think you almost gave our sons alcohol," the red head sighed.

    "So the Road wasn't the first time," Jen said with a laugh. "You're not allowed to serve drinks to minors, Agatha."

    "They were being annoying." Agatha rubbed her temples.

    Time was progressing faster in the memories as Wanda's hex began to fall apart. Sparky had just run into her yard, yapping at her heels. Agatha had Ralp make quick work of the animal, eyes rolling.

    "No! Sparky," Alice shouted. "How could you?"

    It was a dramatic, entirely unserious comment, but Agatha flinched anyway. She pulled away from the group to hug her knees. "It wasn't real."

    "Billy and Tommy aren't either, but you haven't killed them," Jen told her. Agatha hunched her shoulders. "You guys are too loud. You're giving me a migraine. No more talking."

    Fietro moved in, poking at Wanda's older wounds. The other Agatha sat around watching and listening to everything her puppet overheard and saw. With Wanda preoccupied, she got into her car and drove off.

    The immortal stood to pace.

    "Am I dead?" she had asked.

    Vision furrowed his brows at her. "What makes you think that?"

    "Because you are."

    Agatha felt a sharp sting on her cheek. The sound of the slap was heard loud and clear in Vision's silent confusion.

    "How could you!?"

    She turned her head back to face Wanda, not bothering to touch the mark. Another would hit her soon.

    "Dead...Dead...Dead!"

    The goddess held firm as Wanda raised her hand. She was prepared for a slap, however, not a punch. The blow caught her right on the nose, throwing her back.

    Alice and Jen sprang into action to separate the two. The goth knelt to help Agatha up, but she refused. "You were taking too long with Fietro," she explained. Her case wasn't helped as her memory self cackled madly in the car. "I had to speed things up a bit." She wiped the blood off her upper lip.
