    "You had no right to tell him," Wanda growled. Tears streamed down her face. "You...you..." "Say it," she told the woman.

    "You monster!"

    Agatha took the pain in stride. "There...Don't you feel better?" she asked, tone even. She let out a shaky exhale as Wanda collapsed in Jen's arms.

    The night skipped to Agatha waking up. Things were once again rolling downhill. Wanda's hex would fall, and so would Agatha.

    Alice kept glancing over at Wanda, so Agatha gave her a small push. She would survive the red head's cold shoulder.

    "Just...go with Agnes," the memory version of Wanda laughed. She ushered her boys over to the witch, eyes wild.

    Agatha blocked out the sound of her covenmates sobbing and trained her eyes on the twins. If she had known they were her kids too, she would have put them in a dungeon room with a bed. The closet they were stuffed in had been tiny and cramped. Guess Billy was familiar with that feeling by now.

    "I like it here," Billy told her memory self. He smiled up at her, still innocent. Agatha wiped at a stray tear as she watched herself lean in with a, "Is it because Señor Scratch is such a good listener?" They reminded her too much of Nicky that day. But she had still locked them away.

    "Agatha..."

    The goddess turned to Wanda. "I'm fine. Takes more than a punch to knock this kitty down." "But I-"

    "Wouldn't worry about it. Water under the noose or whatever that saying is." She waved the woman's worries away. "I deserved it. Consider my taking your anger an apology." "What if that wasn't enough for me?" Wanda challenged.

    Agatha shrugged. "I can't promise to hold still next time. We both know who will come out on top."

    "Where are the kids?" Memory Wanda asked.

    "Oh...I think they're playing in the basement," was Agatha's response.

    Alice made a face. "Since when do kids play in basements?"

    "They don't," Wanda and Agatha said in unison.

    "It was a trap," the Scarlet Witch added.

    "Wasn't even a good one," the goddess muttered.

    The wicked witch shook out her hair and picked up her familiar. "Show time," she whispered. The pair descended into the basement after the soon-to-be Scarlet Witch.

    "You look a bit creepier in these memories. Like...Like someone entirely different," Alice dared to say.

    Agatha looked over at the goth, suddenly feeling very old. "The Darkhold has a way of twisting you. Whispers in your ear."

    "It can make you hear and see what you want to hear, too," Wanda added. "What was it telling you, Agatha?"

    The immortal pursed her lips. Would it hurt to tell them? Surely not. "I would hear Nicky calling for me from the Other Side. I thought...If I had enough magic, I thought I could bring him back."

    "I heard the twins," Wanda admitted. "...Guess I was wrong."

    "It's not your fault," Agatha began.

    "No. I meant I was wrong about us. I'm not all that different from you after all." Agatha ran a hand through her hair. "Welcome to the club, then."

    "Aggie, I'm sorry for punching you."

    The goddess laughed. "What about the slap? Not sorry for that one, are you?" Wanda shook her head, a smile finally splitting her face. "That one, you deserved." The coven regrouped for the big reveal. Although, only Wanda and Agatha knew what to expect.

    "What are you doing with her hair?" Jen asked.

    "You see how the door disappears?" Agatha told the witches, irritation slipping into her tone. "It can do that, but I'm inside the memories with her." She pointed to Wanda as she shifted into a child. "And that should have happened with me, but Billy fucked the spell up. Hence, trapped for all eternity."

    "Wow...He's grounded," Jen huffed.

    "I'm going to filet him," Agatha grumbled. "Really hoping they show up soon. Things are about to get real embarrassing." She crossed her arms, scowling.

    "How? Those are my traumatic memories!"

    "No, after this," Agatha explained. "Everyone's going to cry for you the way they cried for me." She wiggled her fingers at the happy family. "Look at all those bright smiles. If you had had a coven, they could have-"

    The coven jumped as a bright light filled Agatha's memory.

    "Wha....What just happened!" Alice reached forward as rubble appeared. "What....?" Agatha tugged the group back to her. She hugged the younger witches tightly, instinctually dropping kisses to the tops of their heads. "War happened."

    Vision was in pieces. It was as visceral as it had been the first time Agatha had seen the memory. The way they had no regard for the grieving woman. She didn't know the S.W.O.R.D. man. Couldn't care to keep up with his name as he manipulated Wanda in hopes of stealing a nugget of her power. Unfortunately for Agatha, she found herself tossing her name into the 'Villain' pile alongside his. The witch had been just as callous in her quest for power.

    The coven held Wanda through her pain. Billy would get an earful for putting everyone through their traumas a second and, in Wanda's case, a third time. She stroked a hand through red hair as they finally exited Wanda's memories and returned to Westview. Now, Agatha was in all her dark magic glory.

    "Those fingers look real gross," Alice told her. "I'm glad you don't have that gunk on your hands anymore."

    Agatha scowled. "I didn't ask for icky fingers. They happen to be non-negotiable." "Oh shit! Car!" Jen tried to duck as the car Wanda tossed went through them. "What the hell, Wanda!"

    "She was choking my children!"

    "They were fine!"

    "Shut up, I can't hear," Jen growled.

    The rest of the coven looked at her.

    "What? I'm invested, okay? I want to see a little Karma come through." Agatha pursed her lips. "You guys will enjoy this, then."

    "Runes." Her memory self looked worried. And for good reason.

    " 'In a given space, only the witch who cast them can use her magic,' " Wanda repeated.

    The real Wanda smiled. "You really are a great teacher, y'know. I never forgot what you said, and studied up after I left Westview."

    Meanwhile, Memory Agatha was having her power removed in its entirety. The sentiment overpowered by the pain of such a loss.

    "Forgive me for not jumping for joy at the news. I've just been dropped like a sack of shit and had my powers stripped," Agatha told the witch. She hugged herself as The Scarlet Witch approached her beaten form.

    "You're totally killing it in that outfit," Alice whispered to Wanda.

    The goddess felt her chest tighten as Wanda passed her judgement and executed her punishment. Her dress, a symbol of her power and control, were phased away to a dressy blouse and slacks.

    "Hiya, hun!"

    Agatha clawed at herself. Her voice sounded wrong. She had been screaming in her own mind. Begging to be released, but Wanda ignored her pleas. She closed her eyes, breathing deeply through her nose. To this day, it was still the perfect punishment. She would never trifle with the woman in such a way ever again.

    "Agatha," Wanda began.

    She held up a hand, silencing her. "I need a minute."

    "Did I leave the oven on, or is that just you, hot stuff?" her enchanted self asked.

    "You really don't let up on the flirting, do you?" Alice asked.

    The immortal buried her head deeper in her arms. There was nowhere to run off to. Nowhere to hide. She would have to relive her cursed days. All those damn potlucks! The men! "Wait. You really just left her trapped in her own mind?" Jen asked Wanda. Shutupshutupshutupshutupshutup "I didn't kill her," the woman argued. "I gave her a comfortable life." "Comfortable?" Agatha laughed, a bit of her sanity slipping. "I had no control of my actions. I was forced to eat things I didn't want to eat. Forced to watch things I didn't want to watch." She smiled with gritted teeth. "I couldn't even scream."

    Wanda had the decency to look stricken. "You weren't supposed to be aware." "Well, I was!" She stood to pace, hands balled into fists as her memory self was led away by a medic. A male medic she flirted with. "I knew until you died. I knew and no one could hear me. No one could see me."

    "I didn't know," Wanda argued.

    "Yes, you did," she growled. "Vision told you. I was only lucky that I never had your nightmares." Agatha grew a ball of magic and lobbed it at herself. "Because you couldn't leave well enough alone!" She fired several more until her strength began to wane. Her memories were wearing her down again. Making her cranky and bitter and scorned. She took a deep, deep breath........and exhaled. "I'm taking a nap."

    "What if it stops your memories again and we really get stuck?" Jen said, reminding the goddess of their most pressing issue.

    Agatha wanted to scream. "Fine. But I'm not going to be in a very good mood." "I think we can forgive you for that," Alice told her.

    She sat back down and crossed her arms tightly. "I'm mad, but not at you you, Wanda. You should be proud to have stopped me and my reign of terror. I just need a minute." "I understand," she responded, voice thick with emotion.

    The coven quickly realized why the immortal had hated her cursed life so much. Everything was so mundane as the powerless witch went to work at the school only to return home and sit in silence. Occasionally, she would visit her neighbors. Stick her nose into their business, share a piece of gossip, and then return home for the same silence that greeted her every morning. The days, weeks, months blurred worse than any other time in Agatha's memories. "Okay....Okay, this is suffocating," Wanda finally said. "We have to get out of here. I can't do this anymore. How long has it been?"

    "How did you know what I was thinking?" Agatha said bitterly. Wanda whipped her head around with an open mouth, confused and shocked. "Kidding. I was thinking most of that, but you can't hear it here."

    Her cursed self picked up a newspaper from the doorstep. Agatha leapt up from her spot. "Billy!"

    "What? He's here!" Jen rushed over. "Where?"

    "No...Not that. The car accident...This is an update on his condition." Agatha tried to pry the paper from the figment's hands. "There's still so many days to go." Hot tears welled in her eyes. "I don't want to do this anymore." They weren't even half a year into her hell. She still had to wear those terrible outfits and watch children go by everyday with their smiling parents. Still had to come back and stare into nothing as her own mind screamed and screamed and screamed.

    "I'm sure the others are working hard to get us out," Alice soothed. "We just have to hold onto hope."

    "Hope is fickle thing," Agatha sneered. "I'd rather die a third time than stay here any longer." "Stop that," Jen told her. She wrapped her arms around the witch and held her tight. "We'll get out of here. Rio wouldn't let you be stuck in here forever."

    Agatha felt what little sanity she had left snap at the word 'forever.' The goddess pulled at the arms around her and stomped her foot with a guttural scream.

    The immortal lay on her side, staring blankly forward. She was vaguely aware of fingers in her hair but ignored the sensation. Agatha had long since lost track of where they were in her life. She just wanted to go home, drink a shot of something, and curl up with her wife in her bed. Oh, and maybe set Billy on fire. Just a little something for payback. "Whoa! What the hell's going on with your house?" Alice said.

    The movement in her hair stopped, clueing the goddess in on who's hands had been in her hair. She blinked herself back to reality and breathed a sigh of relief. Her wife would be home soon. "Wanda just died."

    "I did?"

    "It fucked with your spell. Sent me down a spiral with you as the murder victim." Agatha sat up, head spinning from the movement. She reached out and steadied herself with Jen's shoulder. She let out a soft groan. The pounding in her head was returning. She shouldn't have wasted so much magic in her temper tantrum.

    "Girl, what are you doing? Why are you breaking into the police station?" "Will you just watch, Jen!" Agatha held her head in her hands, taking steadying breaths. If they didn't get out soon, she was going to cannibalize the women.

    'Agnes' began to color pictures in the style of a child. Agatha wanted to gag. "This is..."

    "...Depressing," Jen finished for Alice.

    "It's sick," Agatha choked out. "But it's almost over."

    "Here I am," a familiar voice said from the doorway to a room that didn't technically exist.

    "Rio," Agatha sighed. She reached forward, wanting to turn that face towards her to kiss. Her hands phased through the woman.

    "Eat my ass, Chief," the detective spat.

    "There's the Agatha we know and love," Jen cheered. "It only took your wife showing up." Agatha laughed. "She tends to draw me out." She moved to stand by herself so she could stare into her wife's eyes. Rio looked...irritated. Like she wanted to scream that the world Agatha was seeing was a dream. Instead, she chose to play along and gently work out the knots of Wanda's bindings. It was likely she'd had to fight to even get through the spell to manifest a form Agatha could see.

    "I don't want you here," 'Agnes' told the 'federal agent'.

    "Te veo."

    "She said the thing!" Jen and Alice high-fived.

    Wanda shook her head with a laugh. "Seriously, you two?"

    "It's cute," Alice reasoned, grinning widely. "Look. Agatha's blushing." The goddess gasped. "Hey! I'm allowed to be excited. I haven't seen her in so long," she grumbled.

    The coven whooped and ooh'ed and ah'ed when Rio appeared at her door with a box of pizza. "Get it," Jen cheered. "Pizza and beer date!"

    Agatha smirked to herself as she was playfully shoved around by the women. "Prepare to be disappointed. I'm too preoccupied by my job."

    "That's not why I came over," Rio said, eyes boring into 'Agnes'.

    "Yeah, fuck the case," Alice shouted but the pair had already moved on. "Boo," Wanda said. "Throw the pizza and get your wife."

    Rio leaned forward. "Can I ask you something?"

    "Yeah."

    "Oh, you were quick to answer," Jen teased.

    "Shut up," she said, shoving the witch lightly.

    "Do you remember why you hate me?" her wife had asked.

    The roughhousing slowed.

    "No..."

    "Oof," Alice said, wincing. "Did she have to ruin the mood?"

    "She's trying to break me out."

    "But why?"

    There was a thud upstairs, interrupting the conversation.

    "Billy's home. There goes another shining moment," Agatha huffed.

    The group laughed through most of the interrogation and kidnapping. Cheered for Agatha as she began to break the spell. Laughed some more as she nakedly ran for answers. "This is so much crazier than I could have ever imagined," Jen told Agatha. "No wonder you were all over the place."

    "Well, about that..."

    Rio burst her door down and flung her younger self into a wall.

    "Goddamn," Alice breathed. "She is not happy."

    "I did leave her staked to the ground for who knows how long," Agatha reminded. "And all those years of neglect and abuse and blaming..."

    "Yeah. Better to stop there. We got the picture," Wanda told her.

    Agatha winced as she slammed her wife's head against the wall.

    "To think you two were practically fucking right in front of Billy," Alice laughed. "You guys are freaks!"

    Rio licked her hand, stopping any protest Agatha was about to make. She pursed her lips instead.

    Agatha's mood was lifting as her and Billy found their first victim. Lilia had done a number on her emotions with little more than a few details. She had been an amazing divination witch. Agatha wished she had come back if only to spend more time with Nicky and the coven. Next was Jen. Alice and Wanda laughed as Billy and Agatha teamed up on her. Finally, there was Alice. She blushed as Billy gushed over her and her mother. "He can be such a sweet kid."

    "Until he puts you on a fake Road and makes you see all sorts of horrors," Agatha told the goth.

    The coven watched the coven meet up to discuss they're lack of green witch in their coven that was needed to go down the Road...as a coven. (The coven was not covening, as Billy had put it one day.) Agatha pursed her lips as she slipped away in her perfect, wonderful, world- ending coat to fetch Sharon Davis.

    "I still can't believe you invited her," Jen told her. "How were we supposed to keep her alive?"

    "Considering you were all going to die because the Road wasn't real, you weren't going to have to worry about her safety. Then, I was just gonna zap her little brain and wipe the memory," Agatha explained. "But Billy!"

    Agatha returned to the house with her neighbor in tow. The goddess worried her lip as the sun lowered more and more outside.

    "Lilia was really feeling herself," Jen said with a laugh. "She killed those high notes." "Is that why you called her tone 'pitchy'?" Alice asked, laughing.

    "I couldn't give her a compliment just yet. She was rude first."

    "Poor Lilia," Jen sighed as Agatha comforted the hallucinating woman. "And see, Agatha, you never lost your compassion."

    Agatha kept quiet. Her own hallucination would appear soon. She didn't really want to see it again.

    "I love my son, but he's really being a bit of a child about all of this. I mean..." Wanda sighed heavily. "If his mind is doing all of this, why did he think it would be fun?" "Because no one's died yet," Agatha told her. "Once he realizes it can be dangerous, he feeds that into the Road. The Road turns deadlier and the cycle repeats. That's the problem with chaos magic. It's highly unstable and extremely temperamental."

    A baby began to cry.

    Agatha flinched at the sight of the crib. Even though she knew what she would find, her heart still beat wildly. She felt the others jump around her as the Darkhold was revealed. The immortal's hand flew to where her brooch had been, desperately seeking a connection to her son.

    "That was horrific," Wanda breathed. "Why did you see that?"

    "Because Jen told Billy I had traded my own son. He believed it, so the Road showed it to me." The goddess took a steadying breath. "We really dropped the ball on this trial. Sharon dead. Billy losing his innocence. Almost drowning because I didn't trust the wine, and for good reason." She shrugged, filing away the pain for later. "If we walked it again, we at least know what to look for."

    "I'm not walking that ever again," Jen said, shaking her head. "Screw that."

    "The fact that you really thought you could summon another green witch while The Green Witch was around just proves Billy gets his impulsiveness from you," Jen told the immortal. "I didn't think she could enter the Road," Agatha reasoned. She watched the vein in her forehead pop as she reached up to smack her wife. "She did provide some comfort, though." "I bet she did," Wanda teased cheekily.

    Agatha smirked. "Oh, it's like that now, is it? I think you've been in here too long, Wands. You're turning into a menace."

    Alice shifted. "Man, I hated doing this, but I'm glad I got to understand my mom better." Agatha tucked her under arm. "Hey, at least we get to watch you kick that demon's ass! That was fun, wasn't it?"

    "It's Rio...Oh dear Agatha! Tell me you two aren't about to fuck in the booth," Jen groaned. "You were there! We didn't do anything," Agatha growled.

    Wanda blushed. "You might as well have. You two are practically salivating over each other." "It had been a while," the goddess reasoned. "We were never going to be able to keep our hands to ourselves. At least Billy stopped us before we scarred him."

    The coven sat through the revelation and the 'jam session' with apprehension. Agatha grabbed Wanda as Billy collapsed. It was a good thing she had. The red head had tried to catch him and likely would have landed on her face. It would have been funny, but they'd hurt each other enough over the years.

    "He'll be fine," she reminded the witch. "He's still at home, making messes." "Then why are you crying?" Wanda asked.

    "She always cared for him," Alice said for the goddess. "She couldn't ignore it here." "Yeah, girl. You were straight up panicking," Jen added. "I think that was the first time I realized you might have a heart after all."

    Agatha shot her a look. "Thanks," she bit out.

    "You're welcome," Jen said with a laugh.

    Agatha felt like they were watching a movie as they rushed to outrun the Salem Seven. Her memory was a powerful thing. It felt like they were being left behind as their past counterparts took to the sky. She returned to biting her hand as the coven ran into the cabin. Her mother would be back now. Alice would die. Billy would hate her. Rio would lose her patience with her and start working towards her real goal for once.

    "Oh, it's very 80s," Wanda said with an appreciative hum. "You all look so good here!" "You gonna be okay, Agatha?" Jen asked.

    She nodded silently, eyes flicking around the room. Had her mother been there the whole time? Was she supposed to have spoken to her mother at all? If so, why had Nicky reached through the veil? Had Nicky seen her kill Alice?

    "Breathe," Jen told her. "We're all right here. She can't hurt you."

    Agatha's chest continued to tighten as the ouija board was set out for the coven. She bit down harder only for Wanda to remove it and hold it tightly in her hands. Agatha eyed the room, waiting.

    No one laughed at her Sharon impression. They were too on edge as the ghost of Evanora Harkness began to make her presence known.

    "So...Why did the ouija board spell out 'death'?" Alice asked.

    "My mother was trying to out Rio to the rest of you. She wanted you to abandon the both of us."

    "Damn, she just never lets up, does she?" Jen groaned. "I really do hate that woman." "That makes two of us," Wanda grumbled. "She's not even a mother in my opinion." "Sorry I led the witch hunt against you," Jen told Agatha. "I just thought it would help us get out faster."

    "I can't fault you for that. Not really. I would've done the same if it meant getting the hell outta there," the goddess chuckled.

    She squeezed at the hands in hers as her mother hopped into her body. Agatha could easily recall the way her body quickly returned to a puppet on strings. The way her mother's cold fingers made her dance like a marionette. How she attacked Billy, then Jen in hopes someone would blast her. That was all her mother wanted the entire time. Was to out her as a monster to the coven she had begun to truly care for. And she had achieved it. "It was an accident," Agatha blurted as Alice's magic began to get sucked in. She shook as she tried to will her memories to stop. Shut her eyes, hoping the room would go blank. It did not.

    "Don't touch her!" Billy rounded on her, disgust and hate chiseled into his crying face. "She was protecting you...But you didn't deserve it."

    It was saying something, how loud her son's voice was in that moment. How the rest of the room lacked greater details, but she noticed every strand of hair on the teen's head. It was like her mother promising her to Rio all over again. Condemned. She would always be condemned...

    "I don't regret it," Alice told her. "I wasn't expecting to die, but I died for a good reason. Don't beat yourself up." She hugged Agatha. "I've already forgiven you."

    She held the girl tightly, recalling the small child waving to her. The goddess vowed to protect Lorna's daughter henceforth. She was a precious soul. One she wouldn't want to part with for some time. "Thank you," she whispered.

    Anddddd Billy threw them off the Road.

    "You provoked him," Wanda reasoned.

    "He was being a brat," Agatha growled. "And I was tired."

    "At least you didn't have to walk through a shitty tunnel with the Seven behind you," Jen told her. "Lilia and I were scrambling to find you two."

    "I'm just glad I get to see what you guys were getting up to while Rio rowed me across the River."

    Agatha and Billy finally met back up for his angsty little tantrum. A Maximoff, tried and true. "You both are being brats," Wanda huffed. "How did you two survive?"

    "We almost didn't," the immortal mumbled. She shifted to lay down, closing her eyes briefly. "Oh, great! Swords," Alice exclaimed. "What the hell did Billy grow up watching?" "I don't know, but I'm gonna have a word with Rebecca and Jeff," Wanda told her.

    Rio and Agatha now faced off, words flying. Blame and anger and grief. (One might say Heartbreatk, Sorrow, and Grief.) The bitter witches glared one another down until Rio convinced her to sit and rest. Why couldn't the two just say how they really felt? Oh, right! Because Agatha refused to acknowledge her own pain, so she forced it onto everyone else.

    "...I don't wanna see your face."

    The immortal dropped her face into her hands. "Just stab her, Agatha. It'll hurt less," she told herself.

    "That was probably the most painful thing I've ever heard," Jen sighed. "Meanwhile, Billy and I are just walking in silence. Glad I wasn't here for this. I probably would have held you down so Rio could beat your ass."

    "You've got my permission for next time," Agatha said, face still buried away from the hurt look on Rio's face.

    "I'm perfectly aware Agatha Harkness can never be anything more than a covenless witch," Billy said, up ahead on the Road.

    "What the hell! Where is all of this coming from?" Alice asked. She raised her hands as if waiting for an answer to fall into them.

    "You died. We were all trying to cope. And then Lilia..."

    Alice patted Jen's back. "You remember what she said. She was proud of the life she lived."

    "If you don't know, then keep quiet!"

    "Oh shit...Please don't ever yell like that again," Alice told the immortal. She frowned. "Agatha?"

    The older witch had her eyes closed and was rubbing her temples. She couldn't tell if the throbbing came from nearing the end of her memories, or her body shutting down for a second time. Regardless, she knew they needed to get out, and soon.

    "Oh crap! It's dark now," the goth yelped. "What the hell is going on!" "Final trial," Agatha hissed. Nope, definitely not an ordinary migraine. "Billy...hurry the hell up!"

    The goddess ignored the conversation around her as Jen was unbound. Wanda was saying something about Billy. She hoped it was something damning. The boy was doing a number on her mental health. If they survived this new Road, she was going to cap his magic until he was ready. Agatha was not going to do this again. She hissed through her teeth as she felt a pressure building behind her eyes.

    "Agatha...Am I killing this boy so my brother will live! AHHHHHH!"

    His words bounced around in her skull and around the coven. Wanda was sobbing. Jen was sobbing. Alice was sobbing. Agatha was holding her head together to keep them all alive. It was becoming too much too soon.

    "No, Billy. Sometimes....boys die," she heard herself say.

    "Oh...that's a mood killer," a voice said behind the coven. "Glad I didn't stick around for that bit."

    Agatha whipped her head in the direction of the teen. "Get us out of here," she growled. "I feel like I'm dying and it's all your fault!"

    "Right! Sorry...Just gotta..." He rushed over to her and plucked a hair. "Any idea how to undo it?"

    The goddess fought off a litany of hexes and curses. "It won't work like the spell book says. Time to grab ahold of that chaos magic and tell it to behave for once." She took his hand, helping to stabilize his magic. "Just tell it to pull us back out of my mind." Billy nodded and focused.

    Jen, Alice, and Wanda disappeared with a pop. Agatha looked at the teen. "Wait, why are we-?"

    The pair dropped to the floor of the Ancient Ones' temple. The goddess sucked in a breath, the pain in her head disappearing almost immediately. "Thank Me, I'm out of there!" She pressed the heels of her hands to her eyes. The goddess nearly wept with joy. "Agatha!"

    She sat up quickly. "Rio!" The goddess scrambled to launch herself at her wife. She pulled her in for a kiss, tears streaming down her face. "I'm an idiot. I'm stupid," she told Death. "We're going on so many dates." Agatha kissed all over Rio's face, hands digging into her ribs.

    "Ahem!"

    "Oh, just beam us down, Scotty! You can yell at me later," she spat at the panel. Rio threw her head back with a laugh as they fell down to Earth.

    We Carry On Chapter Summary The coven reunites.

    Chapter Notes If the chapter feels a bit rough, it's because my brain was reduced to a raisin Thursday. It's taking me a bit to get back into the swing of things hehe. Just gonna drop this lil chapter off and start working on the really, really fluffy pieces!

    See the end of the chapter for more notes The trio landed in the living room before being slowed to a stop by Rio. Billy stumbled forward and caught himself on the edge of the couch. Agatha had yet to untangle herself from her beloved wife. She pulled Death with her, lips firmly locked. There was the sound of pattering steps on the hardwood floor.

    "Mama!"

    The witch finally broke away, her face breaking into a grin. "Nicky!" She crouched down and threw her arms open to receive the boy. Agatha braced herself as he collided with her. They swayed backwards as Agatha curled around his small body.

    "You were gone for so long," he cried. "We were so worried you'd left us forever." The child clung to her. His tears quickly wet her pajama shirt as he emptied out his bottled-up emotions.

    Agatha rocked him, shushing him gently. "I'm okay. Jen, Wanda, and Alice are okay, too. Everyone's okay, my love."

    Rio looked at her wife, hair crazy. "You look a mess."

    The twins stopped hugging the other coven members to smother Agatha. She hugged them back just as tightly and pressed kisses to their temples. They pulled back, all smiles until the immortal put her hands on her hips.

    "Now, who's bright idea was it to invade my privacy and send three unwilling participants into my memories?" Agatha fixed the two boys with a firm glare. "Do you know how dangerous that was?"

    Billy shuffled and hunched his shoulders. "It was my idea, Agatha. I thought if everyone got to see a few pieces of your life, they'd-"

    The goddess raised a hand, silencing him. "Billy, there are a number of things I would like to say to you, but I'm still too emotionally raw to do so. I'm not mad, but I'm not exactly thrilled, either." She settled Nicky on her hip with a long exhale.

    "Oh, that's not even the best part," Jen bit out. "Who wants to tell her how long we were gone?" She crossed her arms, fixing the boys with a glare.

    Tommy gave the puffy-eyed immortal a tight grin. "I guess I'll do it since I encouraged my lil bro." He rubbed the back of his head. "You've sorta been gone a week, give or take a day. It's a bit of a blur, to be honest. My bad, fam."

    Rio sniffed, face set with a slight frown. "Witches around the world had trouble using their magic," she added. "And the moon didn't shine as brightly. The world went a little mad in the process."

    Agatha's frown deepened. "Billy, Billy, Billy..." She shook her head. "We will be having a chat, mister. I don't really care what happened to other witches, but your little stunt put your coven at risk."

    "You put your mother through a world of hurt," Wanda told the boy. "And you violated every single thing about her for days."

    Billy lowered his head. "I just thought...on the Road...It made us a coven. We grew to care for one another." He glanced up at the women through his lashes. "And you guys do seem closer."

    Jen stepped forward, a look of shock on her face. "Billy, we're real, living people you're talking about. You can't just shove us into dangerous situations to make us bond. We grew closer in spite of your little spell. Wanda nearly killed Agatha because of you." "I did not," the woman hissed. "Don't exaggerate things."

    "We almost starved to death," Alice told him gently. "None of that was fun. Sure, we got closer, but that should have happened naturally. This was just cruel." Wanda lowered her gaze before addressing him. "You were cruel to your coven, Billy, but you were cruelest to Agatha even after knowing she had a traumatizing past." She raised her chin to meet his eyes. "We will be discussing this incident amongst ourselves to find an appropriate punishment. This can't happen again."

    Billy swallowed thickly. "I didn't mean to get you guys stuck. That was an accident." "But forcing us to relive my memories was not," Agatha began. She forced herself to keep her tone even to avoid making things worse. "You wanted that, clearly. But there are some things none of the coven should have seen. They saw everything, Billy." She hugged Nicky tighter to her, clenching her eyes shut. "I saw everything."

    Rio shifted, an arm wrapping around Agatha's shoulder. "I would love to continue this conversation, but the four of you need to eat and rest. You're on the precipice of Life and Death right now." Her free hand instinctively settled on her dagger hilt. "You're not looking too hot yourself," Agatha told her. "What have you been up to?" Death grinned. "All sorts of things, baby. I'll tell you after you guys get your strength back." Rio pulled her in for a kiss, arms fully wrapping around mother and child. "I've got a lot of catching up to do."

    Agatha felt the icy grip of panic. "Don't go," she blurted out.

    Hands stroked her face. "The sooner I get caught up, the sooner I can come home." The Green Witch pressed another kiss to her lips, fingers tracing along the sides of her face. "Te veo."

    The goddess lurched forward as her wife disappeared. She swallowed back a sob at the chilly hole Death's absence left.

    "I say we all do as Rio says, and get some rest," Jen told the other women. "We can rotate so the boys have someone to go to if the need something."

    "Food first," Alice told the potions witch. "Something small and light." "I'm craving applesauce," Wanda laughed, a hand pressing to her stomach. "And a glass of wine."

    Jen stepped over to Agatha, hands settling on the immortal's shoulders. "She'll be back," she whispered. "Best thing you can do is listen to her advice. You're not exactly looking put together, Harkness."

    The goddess fought off a grin as she hugged Nicky tighter. "Wine sounds great. Maybe some broth, too."

    "Broth? You sound like old people," Tommy said. He took Nicky from Agatha to toss him into the air. Giggles filled the house before he tucked the child under his arm. "Can we get some pizza?"

    "Pizza for the boys, broth and applesauce for the women," Wanda said. She waved her right hand over her left palm. Money appeared in a haze of red. The witch looked over at Agatha with a devious grin. "I had it removed from S.W.O.R.D.'s bank account." The immortal smirked. "Good girl," she purred. "It's the least they can do." She turned to Billy. "You two go get the pizza. Don't stay out too long. We're still going to have a chat about everything."

    He nodded and followed his twin out of the house.

    "What are we going to do about him?" Wanda asked. "That was grossly inconsiderate of him."

    Agatha shuffled past them and into the kitchen. "I don't know. I'd cap his magic, but that feels cruel and unfair. It's a part of him, and it didn't act on its own for this incident. He made a conscious decision to put us in there."

    Jen pulled out a bottle of beef bone broth while Alice found a pot to warm on the stove. Agatha grabbed a bottle of sangria and popped it open for the group. She let out an appreciative sigh, smiling down at her son. Agatha wiggled her fingers in his face before ushering him over to the table.

    "I doubt grounding him would get the message across," the Scarlet Witch mumbled. She lightly chewed on a nail, deep in thought.

    "How about a group lecture?" Jen suggested. "Explain why he was wrong for a lot of reasons. If he doesn't understand, then we'll consider capping his magic."

    "That's what my mom would do," Alice said. "Talk things out. Explain it. We just can't lose our heads."

    "Mama, can I have some juice too?" Nicky tugged at the hem of her shirt with imploring eyes.

    "We have apple juice for you," she told him. Agatha sent Wanda a look, jerking her head in their son's direction.

    The red head nodded before magicking a pack out of thin air. "Tada!"

    The child's eyes lit up. "It has a bendy straw!" He made grasping gestures as Wanda set a box up for him to drink. "Thank you kindly!"

    "You are so adorable," Alice cooed. "What were you up to while we were...away?" He took a sip before setting the juice box down on the kitchen table. "Mother left me with Mr. and Mrs. Kaplan so her and my brothers could do research."

    "Great," Agatha grumbled under her breath. Now, she was going to have to play nice with The Man and Rebecca. "Did you behave?"

    Nicky nodded, his hair flopping around. "I really missed you guys. Mother was really sad and scared, so I made sure to be very good."

    Agatha scooped him up, hugging him tightly. "We really missed you, too." She pressed a kiss to his forehead. "I'm sure your mother really appreciated you doing that for her. I know I do." "Hey, why don't we watch a movie?" Alice told the boy. "You can pick, and we'll all cuddle up on the couch."

    He gave the goth a toothy grin. "Can we watch one on birds?"

    "Oh, I've got just the documentary, little man," Jen told him. "I'll get it set up so we can watch it after Billy and Tommy get back."

    "Broth's done," Wanda announced. "I can pour it into mugs for us to sip on." "I think I'm going to take a quick shower," Agatha told the group. "I'm covered in snot." "You are really stinky, Mama."

    The goddess gasped dramatically. "Well, that's not very nice, mister." "You said not to lie," he told her. "I'm agreeing with you."

    The group shared a laugh as the goddess let out a sigh. "Still, not very nice." She pressed another kiss to his head before setting him down in a chair. "Behave for the others. I'll be right back." Agatha stifled a yawn before making her way towards her room.

    Billy turned the engine off and let out a sigh. "Tommy...Do you think I went too far?" His brother unbuckled himself before grabbing the pizza boxes. "I dunno, man. I thought it was a good idea. Then again, I don't really know them all that well. They'll get over it." The younger Maximoff frowned. "It was fine on the Road. They got closer, and it was nice. When Alice died, that's when things changed."

    Tommy took the pizza inside and dashed back; hands empty. "Look, bro, you're just gonna have to take the L. Some ideas are good in the moment, and some aren't. Fake it 'til ya make it, baby." He grabbed a bag of sodas from the floorboard. "Come on. Sooner you take your asswhooping, the sooner you can get over it."

    "I'm starting to get more worried about your responses to life," Billy said with a nervous chuckle. He grabbed a parcel behind his seat with a sigh. Hopefully, Agatha would appreciate the gift after everything.

    The brothers entered the house to the sound of a nature documentary playing on the t.v. The coven had all showered and changed into something comfortable. Billy looked around for his mentor, a spark of panicking making his stomach drop. He stepped into the living room and stopped by the sectional Wanda must have created. Agatha had her head in Jen's lap, snoring softly. Her legs were thrown over Wanda's lap. Wanda had an arm thrown over Alice, and Alice had Nicky nestled into her side. The group looked cozy and relaxed for the most part. "We're back," he told them.

    Jen pressed a finger to her lips. "Don't wake Agatha," she whispered to him. "She needs all the rest she can get. Lots of bad stuff kept her up."

    He nodded, swallowing around a lump. "Nicky, do you want cheese or pepperoni?" His brother turned to face him. "Can I have pepperoni and cheese?"

    "Sure." Billy went in search of the pizza to serve the child. Once he had plated the slices, he joined the group on the couch. "What're we watching?"

    "Animal Planet," the youngest coven member informed. "I wanted to see more toucans." Billy nodded, falling silent as he munched on his pizza. Wanda turned and offered him a small smile behind Alice's back. He returned the gesture, hunching his shoulders lightly. As the documentary continued, the women began to fall asleep. Even Nicky and Tommy crashed with them in a giant pile of blankets, pillow, and crazy hair. Billy got up and began to clean up. The last thing they needed was a messy house to clean. It was a good thing Rio had run a tight ship when she would check in on them. He gathered up the wine glasses and slunk off to the kitchen to wash them.

    "That was very nice of you," a raspy voice said from the doorway.

    Billy turned to find Agatha leaning against the doorframe, arms crossed. There were slight bags under her eyes, and her hair hung limply around her face. For the first time, she looked older. He wondered if she had always seemed that old, or if he had brought that out of her with his 'little stunt.' "Thought you guys might like that," he told her softly. He turned back to rinse his hands off. "How are you feeling?"

    The goddess watched him for a moment, mouth a firm line. "I've been better," she told him honestly. "Well....maybe not. There wasn't a whole lot of good to reflect on." Agatha looked away, eyes landing on the pile of mail stashed on the counter. "How'd you find a way in without a door?"

    The teen fidgeted with the hand towel. "It's sort of a long story...We were trying to figure out if we could bend time, but Rio said we'd shatter the Universe if we did that. Then magic started going on the fritz and crazy things were happening with the moon. Took us a few days to realize we could use the moon to connect with you. Rio took me to those ladies, and they helped me enter your mind that way."

    Agatha tapped her chin. "Guess the whole 'I'm the Moon' bit is literal, then." She made a face before dropping her hand to continue hugging herself. "Do you even understand what you did?"

    Billy pressed his lips together before shaking his head. "On the Road-" "What you did on the Road wasn't right either, Billy. You just weren't aware of what you were doing."

    He stared at her, mouth hanging open. The teen snapped his mouth shut, ears turning red. "But you said..."

    "I know what I said," Agatha began. She gestured with her head for him to sit. The goddess, however, remained in the doorway almost as if she were afraid to get too close to him. Billy swallowed thickly before taking a seat. "I guess I haven't understood for some time then."

    "That's partly on me, but we'll deal with that later. The matter at hand is your impulsive do- goodery." She took a breath as her lips twitched. "When you use magic to try and fix your problems, people get hurt. If anyone understands that it's me."

    He nodded, listening intently.

    "You can't do something like that again, Billy. Not without the proper guidance and knowledge needed for that level of magic. Your coven was nearly killed by your rash thinking." Her voice had begun to raise, but she quickly reined it back in. Agatha took another steadying breath. "Not only did you nearly kill them, but you also forced them to see some truly awful stuff. There was more than just murder in my life. You caught a glimpse of my mother. They had to watch everything that happened to me. There are things I've experienced that no one should have had to see." Agatha looked away, blinking back tears. "And there were things I'd purposely forgotten that you forced me to relive. That is what you did with your spell."

    Billy lowered his head. "I had no idea, Agatha. I just wanted everyone to get along. The last time we were all together, you were upset. I just...I don't know...I wanted us to feel like a family again."

    His mother sniffled. "I know I was being an ass to you over the movie. I was working through some painful emotions, and I took them out on you and Jen. I'm sorry, but that doesn't give you the right to force people to play house or get along." "But I didn't force anybody to get along," he reasoned. "They were just supposed to get a better understanding like I did."

    "Billy," she hissed. "Did you like it when Rio forced her way into your head? Did you enjoy reliving one of her worst moments?"

    He shook his head quickly. "No, I-"

    "You did that to all of us with that spell. You experienced one, one, bad memory on Rio's end. It left you sick and weak. But you gave them every terrible moment I have ever experienced over four-hundred-years!" Agatha turned away, fighting off her anger and taking in deep breaths. "No, I'm fine," she told someone in the living room.

    The teen wasn't surprised as the other women appeared. Alice pulled Agatha away to talk to her as Jen and Wanda took over. He shrunk in on himself. "I wasn't trying to hurt anybody," he told his other mother. "You guys were fighting. No one was happy. I just wanted us to be like a real coven again."

    Jen sat down and patted his hand. "Look, I kinda get why you're the way you are because you were raised in a sitcom world, and then turned into a teenager, but you actually did a really fucked up thing. You tricked us into a spell and then left us to figure it out." The teen clasped his hands, frowning deeply. "I didn't know about the runes. I'm sorry about that. But you guys are always fighting."

    "Billy, that's just how Agatha and I talk to each other. We've run into one another a few times, and that's just our banter. If there were a real issue, we would have let our magic settle the score."

    Wanda poured herself a fresh glass of wine. "It's the same for me. We all decided we'd make things work for the three of you. Agatha just needed a minute to adjust to so many people in the house. Things were...rough for her under my spell."

    Agatha reappeared, face red. "Rough doesn't even begin to describe the nightmare that was 'Agnes's life! Potlucks, Wanda! Fucking potlucks every week with men who got handsy," she growled.

    "Yes, I remember. I made sure to stay awake, so I knew exactly what I put you through. I'm very sorry." The red head handed her glass of wine over to the upset woman. "Let's just try to calm down, so we can have a real conversation with Billy about what happened and why it's wrong, okay?"

    "Don't baby me, Maximoff. I'm angry, not incompetent." Agatha added more wine to the glass as she grumbled to herself.

    "I would never assume nor imply such a thing. I know you're just tired and upset about everything, Aggie."

    Billy looked between the four women, ready to tell them he had to be right about what he did. But the more he looked at Agatha, the more he saw just how shaken she was. On the Road, Agatha would have just made a joke before leaving the conversation. She had yet to do so. Then, there was the fact that she was crying in front of other people. Something she would have run away to do. His mother seemed small. Agatha Harkness was not small, but, somehow, he'd done the impossible. No...Not impossible. Hurting his mother seemed to be a specialty of his by this point.

    "I am sorry. Really," he told the coven. "I thought what I was doing was a good thing." "Sometimes, the best intentions are the most harmful," Alice told him gently. "That's why it's better to talk things out. Assumptions often lead to misunderstandings." Billy fidgeted with a ring. "I'm sorry," he repeated. "I wish I hadn't done it. I'd take it back if I could."

    Agatha finished off the glass of wine before flipping her hair back. "Sorry won't undo the trauma you've inflicted on everyone," she explained with a thick tongue. (Though if it was from wine or emotion, Billy wasn't sure.) "I am well within reason to cap your magic, but I'm not going to. This is your one and only warning for intentional mishaps." She used her magic to ferry the glass to the sink. "I do not appreciate what happened to me. Not in the slightest. But I will survive. We just need you to understand that that was very wrong, and I don't want to talk about it further."

    He opened his mouth only for silence to fill the space. Was Agatha was trying to pull back again? He didn't want her to if she was. Billy took a breath. "But we need to talk about it. Ignoring this won't make you feel better. I hurt you. You have every right to be mad at me. I'm not a kid, but I acted like one. You...you can yell at me. Do whatever you need to do." The women shifted their gazes to Agatha, opening the floor to her. The immortal stared at him; lips lightly pursed. He could tell she wanted to run just like she had when Rio appeared on the Road. There was a look in her eye like she was facing a wild animal. I so fucked up, he groaned inwardly.

    Agatha straightened her back, a single mask slipping on as her features settled. "I will not be my mother and blow things out of proportion," she told him firmly. "I am not ignoring what happened; I'm simply taking a moment to cope with everything. That doesn't mean you don't get a say about your behavior, and now's the time for that."

    Billy swallowed thickly. "I don't think my overall idea was wrong, just my execution. You guys are closer, but I can see that I've really hurt you all." He dared to move from his spot to approach the goddess. Tears pricked his eyes as she flinched back ever so slightly. "I'm sorry I hurt you the most, Agatha." He wrapped his arms around her gently to keep from scaring her further. Slowly, she relaxed and returned the hug.

    "You're a good kid, Billy. You just make dumb decisions sometimes." She let out a shaky chuckle. "You get that from me, unfortunately." Agatha let him go, pulling back. "No more unsupervised magic from now on. And...And I'm going to need some time. You really rattled a few skeletons in my closet, and none of the fun kind."

    He nodded. "I understand. Can...Can I still come over?"

    Agatha reached out to cup his chin, a small smile appearing. "This is still your home. Come over whenever. There just might be a day or two where I step out for fresh air." She swallowed thickly. "I'm not mad at you, okay?"

    Billy went in for another hug. "I promise I'll do better. I'm sorry."

    She pulled him back into, arms tightening around him. "You are better," she told him quickly. "Don't...You don't have to promise that. Don't say that."

    He nodded into her shoulder. More arms closed in around him, a sense of peace easing over the group. Billy sighed into the group hug, eyes sliding shut.

    "Where is everybody?" Rio said, stepping up to her wife. "It's quiet," she added as she looked around the living room. Pillows and blankets were strewn everywhere. It was deliciously homey if she had any sense of the word. Agatha was in a different pair of pajamas and oversized t-shirt. Her hair was a tangled mess, but she seemed less frazzled than she had earlier.

    The goddess turned around before latching onto the woman. She rested her head against the taller woman's shoulder. "Out. They needed fresh air."

    Rio ran a hand through her wife's hair. "And you didn't?"

    Agatha shook her head. "I just need you."

    Death swallowed thickly. "I swear, I tried to get you out as quickly as possible. Without a door-"

    "I needed to be in there," the witch told her. Agatha looked up at her, a hand cupping her cheek. "I needed to see just how much you've done for me. For Nicky....But I have questions. If you're willing to answer them, that is. If you don't want to, I'm perfectly fine with snuggling up until the end of time."

    Rio chuckled. "How about we snuggle and you ask you questions?"

    Agatha tugged her over to the sectional. "Don't have to ask me twice." The Green Witch made herself comfortable, practically straddling her wife. "What did you want to ask me?" She raked her fingers through wavy tendrils, humming gently. The goddess sighed at the contact, eyes sliding shut. "In wherever we were, I saw from my birth up until the Road." She shifted as Rio continued to work out knots in her hair. "You said you'd met my father at one point, and I know you'd kept an eye on my mother. What was it about him that made her hate me so much?"

    Death stopped, her gaze flicking down to steel-grey eyes. "Agatha..." How did she tell her wife she was the product of assault? That nothing would have ever been good enough for Evanora Harkness.

    "Please, Rio..."

    How could she say no?

    The Green Witch nodded, resuming her ministrations. "Your father was a witch hunter who was enamored with your mother," she began slowly. "And, one day, he decided to act on his desire. Evanora killed him once the shock wore off." Rio watched her face, gauging her wife's reaction. "I don't know why she chose to give birth to you when she was likely never going to appreciate you for the gift you are."

    "I guess that's why she was hoping I'd die afterwards," Agatha said with a bitter chuckle. "I...I know what she said. I know what all she did in those early years..."

    Death swallowed thickly, eyes misting. "You were never supposed to know. She was awful, and I couldn't stop her." She stroked her wife's cheek. "But you survived, mi flor. And I have always been so proud of you for that."

    Agatha pulled her down for a kiss, a hand fisting the front of her work clothes. Rio cradled her face and moved to fully sit in her wife's lap. She moaned as a hand palmed a breast. The back porch doors opened as Alice walked in. She waved to the cosmic being. "Welcome home, Rio!"

    The Green Witch jerked her head back, waiting for the other woman to make a comment. She hissed as Agatha moved to attack her neck with nibbles and butterfly kisses. Meanwhile, the goth served herself some lemonade and walked right by them as if nothing were happening.

    "What's the matter?" Agatha asked her. She magicked her wife's top away and bit back a moan. "Fuck, I've missed you."

    Rio laughed. "Didn't realize Alice was cool like that," she said, licking the inside of her cheek. Her grin only grew as the goddess looked up at her with dark eyes. "Yeah, well...They got used to seeing us together pretty quickly," Agatha told her. She leaned forward to pull a nipple into her mouth.

    Death held the back of her head with a sigh. "I hadn't...thought of that," she huffed. The cosmic entity arched her back as a hand trailed down her spine.

    Agatha released her with an audible pop! She smirked. "I'm all for defiling Wanda's precious couch, but the twins could walk in at any minute." She picked the other witch up. "I'm gonna take you to my bed and fucking smother you with my love."

    Rio laughed, wrapping her arms around her wife's shoulders. "Agressive...Sounds fun." She tugged Agatha's hair, earning a moan. "I hope you'll wrap that hand of yours around my neck again."

    "I'll do more than just that with my hand," Agatha purred. She kicked the door to her bedroom open and tossed her wife down on the bed. She shut the door and soundproofed the room with a quick spell. "Now, where was I? Oh, right..."

    Rio sat up as Agatha dropped to her knees. "What're you doing?"

    The goddess smirked as she ran her nails lightly along her wife's thighs. "I told you already. I'm going to smother you with my love." Agatha gripped Rio's hips and shifted her closer to the edge of the bed.

    There were far too many emotions running through Rio for her to form a coherent sentence. Agatha had never gotten on her knees for anyone. Not since gaining her freedom from the Salemites. And Death knew Agatha had been working hard to prove she wanted to fix their relationship. She just never expected this.

    "Don't look so terrified, Hot Stuff. If you don't want me to, I won't," Agatha told her softly. She rested her head on a thigh, her right hand stroking taut skin.

    "I...You..."

    Blue eyes blinked up at her, slow and full of devotion. There wasn't an ounce of hate or loathing or fear in those brilliant orbs. "Yes?" her wife asked softly. She cupped the goddess' chin, tilting that beautiful face upwards. "Te quiero much, vida mia. Siempre te querré," Death told her. She bent down to kiss her wife, heart clenching from the rush of emotion.

    "I'll always love you, too," Agatha said against her lips. She kissed her way back down, gently massaging flesh with her cool hands. "I'll always want you. Always need you." Rio tipped her head back with a breathy moan as a tongue swiped at her, slow and deliberate. "Agatha..." Her heart stuttered as her wife moaned against her. Those piercing blue eyes were trained on her once again, drinking in her reaction. She combed back strands of auburn hair, panting. Her wife had always been a thorough woman. And when that talented tongue was involved...

    Agatha reached up with a hand to roll a nipple between her fingers, tugging lightly. She was taking her time. Building pressure for the grand finale. Coaxing and easing Death towards her first orgasm. Rio let herself be consumed as her wife seemed determined to reduce her to ashes. She could hear the woman's thoughts loud and clear.

    How many petit morts could the personification of Death handle? How long could the Divine Mother love her before it was too much? Would all the things she couldn't express with words be translated through her acts of devotion? What more would the Triple Goddess need to do to prove her love for Lady Death?

    Well, unfortunately for Agatha, her tired body was no match for the insatiability of Death, herself. It wasn't for lack of trying, though. Poor thing had done all she could with the energy she had. Death's beloved witch exhausted herself in a mere four hours. If she had had more rest and it were nighttime, the goddess might have given Rio a run for her money. Regardless of sexual stamina, the Green Witch had truly been smothered by the goddess' love. Was left warm and content as she pulled the sheets up and over them.

    Death dropped kisses to her snoring wife's face. Love drunk and limp limbed in all the best ways. She shuffled deeper into Agatha's embrace, inhaling her scent. Rio used a nail tip to trace flower symbols and runes along pale skin. If she could stop time permanently, she would. Rio was more than willingly to stay in their tiny world for as long as Agatha would have her. Thankfully, she didn't have anywhere to be any time soon.

    Chapter End Notes I swear, I want to write smut for them, but I can't find the groove. If any writers have tips for these two characters, please help a homie out lol Hold Your Hand in Mine Chapter Summary Okay, now the fluff with a lil something extra!

    Chapter Notes See the end of the chapter for notes Agatha hummed Nicky's Ballad as she prepped a basket for Coven Night. With school out for the day and the weather cooling, it was the perfect time to relax outside. Teddy and Billy would be arriving soon, and she still needed to find a blanket big enough for them to use. At least she managed to finish prepping the multitude of snacks for nine people. She packed a container of cut fruit with a satisfied grin. The witch popped a leftover strawberry in her mouth and turned as the air shifted.

    "Someone's in a good mood," Rio drawled. She stalked over, wrapping her arms around her wife's waist. "What's the occasion, amor?"

    "Picnic," Agatha answered simply. She cupped Death's face to bring her in for a kiss. "All of us."

    The Green Witch grinned. "And you're going out wearing this?" Rio bit her lip, eyes raking over her beloved. "We might have to take a long walk for a bit."

    Agatha winked at her. "Ah, so you're a fan of modern exercise wear?" She gave her wife a spin, showing off her outerwear. It wasn't much, but she was sure that was what had Rio drooling over her.

    The goddess pressed the older immortal against the kitchen counter, lips curling into a smirk. "I know that look, Hot Stuff. Can't be too hot and bothered before we head out."     Teeth nipped at her jaw line, stopping long enough for an, "I'd say ten...fifteen minutes out." Agatha bit her lip and tugged her wife along to the small room.

    Rio laughed as fingers tangled in her hair. Her laughter was cut off as lips met hers. She kicked the door shut just in time for her fellow immortal to shove her against it. "Gotta make it quick, sweetheart."

    "You should have gotten home sooner," the woman growled. She slipped a hand under Rio's waistband with a groan. "Why are these pants so fucking tight? You know I'm going to stare at you in any ridiculous get up you wear. This is just a bit much, don't you think?" "If you would give me a second, you can have your wicked way with me without them on," Death snarked playfully. "But you leave those tights on. I know my way around a tight squeeze."

    Agatha bit her lip as she was turned and pressed up against the door. Warm fingers snuck under the stretchy fabric of Agatha's tights before stopping. The goddess tipped her head back with a breathy moan. Her hips bucked forward as she gripped muscular forearms. Hazel eyes snapped up to her blue eyes, a smirk growing. "Oh dear...Is someone in the midst of a succubi's heat?" Rio licked the inside of her cheek as she pressed more firmly against her wife. "No wonder you're all flushed and needy."

"What if I grabbed Wanda and asked her to help me out?" the goddess growled. Death pressed down on her wife's clit, rubbing with intention. "Then I'd really leave you to suffer," she hissed. Rio attacked her neck, teeth scraping along sensitive flesh as she continued to rub circles around her wife's clit.
