    The younger immortal gasped as she met her wife thrust for thrust. Outside, a car door slammed. Agatha slapped a hand over her mouth as she began to see stars. The goddess felt her legs give out as she came.

    Death caught her, giving her a kiss. "We'll make more time once we get to the park," she promised.

    Agatha nodded as she caught her breath.

    Rio sat on an arm rest, legs crossed, as she watched Agatha and Billy. She leaned back, bouncing a foot. There was something about watching her wife teach a spell that made the cosmic entity giddy. Maybe it was the fact that Agatha had never had a real mentor aside from Rio and the handful of spells they worked on. Watching her take charge always gave her a thrill, too. Those firm eyes. Those soft lips. By Agatha Harkness, she loved every inch of her wife!

    "Fix that thumb. It's too far to the left. You want it right here," Agatha said as she adjusted her son's hand position. She carefully curved his thumb, careful to avoid touching his magic. Billy bunched his brows in concentration. A haze of blue misted around Wanda. Gradually, her appearance shifted. For Rio, it lasted a second before she could see through it. (Glamour spells never worked on her, unfortunately.)

    "Hey, not bad. Made her blonde, but kept her the same height. Her nose is a little wonky, but that might make people too uncomfortable to stare at her. Good job," Agatha told her son. "Now, let's do the same with Tommy."

    Rio licked the inside of her cheek, her eyes taking in her wife. She was still in her tights, but she had changed into a low-collared tank top that flashed an expanse of flesh that belonged to Death and Death alone. If Billy would hurry his ass up, she could take her wife for a romp in the bushes. Touching wasn't enough when she had a perfectly good tongue for tasting too. Agatha looked over at her and did a double-take. "...that's a good...uh...You've got..." She snapped her gaze away from her wife with a slight scowl. "You're doing good," Agatha said a bit more forcefully.

    The Green Witch chuckled, a smirk playing on her lips. She'd let a lot of souls suffer if it meant she got to tease her wife for much longer than a few minutes a day. Death would rather their time be spent in the safety of their bedroom, but she didn't mind watching a magic lesson. She knew how much it meant to Agatha to share the knowledge she'd acquired over the years. The way it let her connect with her coven.

    "How do I look?" Tommy asked the room. He spun in place, hands outstretched. "You look kind a funny," Nicky told him. He squinted up at the teen. "And your face has a lot of bumps."

    "A pimply teen? Bro, what the hell?"

    "You're undercover," Billy reminded. "Now, let's get going before the sun goes down." Agatha walked over to Rio, pulling her up until their lips were centimeters apart. "I'd take you right now if Nicky weren't within earshot," she growled.

    Rio leaned forward to press a kiss to the very tip of her wife's nose. She grinned wolfishly as Agatha's pupils dilated. "I bet the suspense is killing you."

    The goddess bit her lip. "I hate you," she hissed.

    "Sure you do," Rio said with a hum. She slipped off the couch, purposely pressing up close to the woman before sauntering off. "Hey, Nicky! Let's hold hands."

    The park was in the process of turning into shades of red, orange, and yellow. A chilly breeze moved through the trees until Rio diverted it for the evening. Agatha walked with her wife, hands clasped tightly. (Nicky had insisted on Jen holding his other hand.) The coven set up a blanket before sitting to have snacks. Containers were passed around, everyone picking at what they wanted.

    "How come you don't cook more often?" Tommy asked the goddess. "These muffins are fuckin' bussin'."

    Wanda shot the teen a look. "Come on now, there are children around. No foul language where someone might hear."

    "Sorry, Ma. They're just so godda-, uh...I like em!" The boy gave Agatha a grin. "Thanks, Ma Squared."

    The immortal toasted him with her own strawberry muffin. "Cooking requires a patience I normally lack," she told the speedster. "That, and I'm used to dining at places with unwilling hosts."

    "But you cooked all the time Salem," Wanda argued. She cocked her head to the side. Agatha laughed. "That was a few centuries ago, Wands. I don't know if you've noticed, but we don't use hearths and fireplaces to cook anymore."

    Rio batted her eyelashes at her. "It's a shame. All that bending over made for a good work out. Strong arms for carrying a cauldron. Toned calves and stomachs...." The goddess felt her succubus hunger flare. Why did her wife have to rile her up in the middle of her fucking muffin? She could syphon magic from Wanda again, but Rio was so willing and extremely beautiful. The Green Witch had that look in her eye, and she had promised to frisk her while the others were preoccupied. She just needed to survive until the boys ran off to play with their frisbee.

    "You're lucky I don't have back problems," she grumbled. "Or that I never burned myself." Death leaned forward from her perch, cleavage on display. "You know I would've healed you, sweetheart."

    "I have a question about that," Billy began. Because, of course, he did. The day he ran out of questions....Well, that would be a very sad day for Agatha.

    Rio shrugged. "What about?"

    "Well, when you two were fighting in the kitchen, you licked the cut on Agatha's hand. Do you have to lick a wound to heal it?"

    The mortal women began to blush furiously and busied themselves with food and drink. "No, a kiss can make it better," Death told him. "Or a wave of my hand. But I cannot interfere when someone is going to die for certain." She flicked her eyes over to Agatha. "Doesn't mean the licking isn't fun."

    Agatha licked her lips. She needed to segue the conversation before her fantasies and memories got the better of her. "Are you asking for healing lessons? I'm sure Rio would love that." She ignored the way her abs clenched when she saw Rio's dagger. How Death had carved her name over her heart just to lick the pain away.

    "Yeah. I can cut up Agatha real good and you can take a stab at healing her." The teen made a face, visibly disgusted. "I think I'm gonna be sick..." He got to his feet and ran for a nearby bush.

    Agatha and Wanda were on their feet in seconds. They rushed over to check on him, but found him laughing. Agatha wondered if there would ever be a sense of normalcy when the whole group got together.

    "Funny story," he said, wiping his chin. "I can see memories just as easily as I hear thoughts now."

    Agatha paled. "Billy, I'm so-"

    "No, no," he laughed. "Your mind is locked up tight again. But the others who saw what you two got up to..."

    The goddess nearly screamed in embarrassment. She cleared her throat, shooting Rio a look. "Just...go play frisbee. Yeah, that'll keep you preoccupied enough for you to avoid any more unpleasant memories."

    "You guys are freaks," Billy groaned out. "Mom, stop thinking about it!" He turned back to the bush with a gag.

    "Wanda, what the fuck!" Agatha smacked the woman's arm. "Everyone's getting telepathy lessons now. Five sets of my memories does not make for a safe environment with such a sensitive telepath."

    "I'm just gonna..." Billy walked away with a shiver.

    Wanda rounded on her. "Don't give me that. You started it. You and Rio have been eyeing each other all day."

    "I'm having a flare," Agatha bit out. "So unless you're gonna juice me up again, I'm going to take my wife to a spot far from here. You are going to keep everyone busy. Then, we'll regroup and I might even buy you an ice cream." She turned the Scarlet Witch around and began to push her back to the others. "Rio."

    Death pranced over, all teeth and reaching hands. "Is it my turn to play~?" Agatha took her hand and pulled the cosmic entity down a path and well away from the others.

    Billy watched the immortal pair leave before turning to the rest of the coven. "Where are they going?"

    Agatha looking down at Rio, a hand to her throat. Death pulled at the wrist with a grin. "Really?" he groaned. Billy pressed the heels of his palms to his eyes. "We're out in public!" Jen cleared her throat, looking away. "I don't know what you're talking about." Wanda shook her head. "He can read our thoughts and see any memories if you're remembering something...too loud." She gave him an apologetic look. "Sorry, Billy." "Just...just give me the frisbee so we can go play. I don't want to see those two doing anything but holding hands." The teen grabbed the bag they had brought and began to rummage around. He was hit with another memory, stopping him in his tracks. Billy whipped around to face the women. "Seriously, you guys. Stop! I don't wanna see my mother having sex."

    "You act like we can control what we had to see," Alice laughed. "Just be glad it's only snippets and not everything else." The goth shook her head with a grimace. Billy rolled his eyes. "Tommy, do you know what happened to the frisbee? Agatha said I needed to stay distracted." He eyed the group of women. "And to put some distance between us."

    His twin stuffed the last of his fifth muffin into his mouth. He shuffled over and pulled the bag to himself. "I don't know if we packed it, bro. Nicky wanted to toss the football around." "Football's fine with me. Anything that keeps me busy," he told the older Maximoff. Billy turned to Nicky. "Wanna go play catch with us?"

    The child nodded eagerly. "Come on, guys!" He ran from the blanket, his jacket flapping at his sides.

    Billy grinned. "Let's make a triangle that's close enough for him to toss the ball to us." "Hey, can I join you guys?" Alice asked. "I promise to go easy on you three." The twins grinned.

    "Hell yeah," Tommy laughed. "Let's get to it." He jogged at a normal speed until he reached Nicky. "We're gonna make square, 'kay? Billy's gonna toss it to you; you toss it to me." The child jumped with energy. "I'm ready! I'm ready!"

    Billy tossed the football to Tommy. "Show him how to hold it. I made it smaller so he can grip it better." He watched his twin crouch down and show him how to curl his fingers along the stitching of the ball. The teen wondered if this is what his life could have been if they had stayed in his mother's hex. Would his father have shown him and Tommy how to throw a ball? Before he had a chance to spiral, Alice bumped shoulders with him. He offered her a smile.

    "I bet you've never even tossed a football?" the goth playfully ribbed. "Theater kid," he confirmed. Billy nudged her back. "Doesn't mean I can't kick your ass." Alice smirked. "Oh yeah? Okay, tough guy. Let's see what you're made of." "I'm ready," Nicky announced. "Watch me, watch me!"

    "Go on. Give it a whorl," Alice told the child.

    Nicky gripped the football before tossing it towards the speedster. Tommy dashed forward to catch it before jumping up and flipping dramatically. Nicky whooped, doing a small dance. "Heads up," Tommy told Alice. He threw the ball over.

    Billy found himself relaxing as they tossed the football around and around. The sun began to set, the air chilling further. They would need to head back soon, but none of them wanted to leave yet. Nicky took the ball and began to run around them in tackle-less version of football. Alice scooped him up, tickling the kid until he was red in the face. Billy laughed as the world turned into a blur. Tommy sped them through the park, far too fast for anyone to notice them. "Kids! We're leaving," Agatha shouted. She waved to them, Rio nowhere to be seen. The twins met up with the group, all smiles and laughter.

    "Let's go get a treat, and then we'll head home, okay?" the goddess said. Agatha gave them a thumbs up before gesturing for them to follow her.

    Billy took the backpack from Jen and slung it over his shoulder. "Everything cooled down for you guys?"

    "Well, if you bring it back up, you're gonna see more," the potions witch laughed. "I'm surprised you're not on a team. You've got a pretty good arm."

    The teen waved her off. "Oh, no. I don't like contact sports. All those egotistical guys trying to prove something? Not for me."

    "Except for me, right?" Teddy asked.

    "How come you didn't play with the others?" Jen asked the other boy. "You could have taught them a thing or two."

    "That would have been too much of a distraction for Billy," Teddy teased. He sent his boyfriend a wink. "Besides, I had a lot of fun chatting with you guys. Where else am I gonna go to learn what's the difference between a sigil and a rune?"

    "Uh...me," Billy told him. "I know those things too."

    "Yeah, but I don't want to bother you about all of that." His boyfriend wrapped an arm around his shoulders. "You already have so much to focus on. I don't want to add to that." Billy looked away, a blush tinting his cheeks. Agatha, he loved his boyfriend! He looked back at Teddy to find him staring down at him with a soft expression. "What?" he asked, looking away again.

    "You're cute," Teddy whispered.

    Alice sent him a thumbs-up behind the taller teen's back. She took longer strides to catch up with the other women.

    Teddy took his hand, holding it tightly. "I love you, Billy...uh...What are all your last names again?"

    Billy laughed before pressing a kiss to his boyfriend's cheek. "I think I gained a few more parental figures since we met."

    "Well, regardless, I love you."

    "I love you too, Eddie Altman."

    The group sat around the ice cream shop with their own cartons to eat from. Nicky sat between his brothers as he told Agatha about his first time playing with a football. She fidgeted in place. The idea of him playing such a physically violent sport creeping up on her. One day, he'd be big enough to make such a demand, but she had no idea how she was going to tell him 'no.'

    "I'd rather you played the one with the hoops," she told him.

    Nicky's eyes lit up. "There are other games!"

    She laughed, her face breaking out into a grin. "There's so much to teach you," Agatha sighed. "Thank Myself that you have wonderful brothers to help me."

    Her son bobbed his head. "I want to learn it all, Mama. I want to go to school with my brothers."

    "They're too old, love. You wouldn't be at the same level as them in some things." She leaned in with a conspiratorial wink. "But we both know you're more intelligent than your brothers." "Hey now," Tommy laughed. "I have excellent grades when I want them."

    Agatha grinned at him. "You and Billy can't read an analog clock to save your lives." "I've never even seen one of those," Billy argued.

    "Kid, there are three in your parent's house," she told the boy.

    "Yeah, well...I'm surprised you could read the numbers on the clock," he shot back with a cocksure grin.

    The little... "Billy, stop telling people I don't know how to count!"

    "I'm just saying," her snarky child began, "we've never seen her in a room with numbers higher than 20."

    The group snickered as Agatha sent him a glare. "I'm going to bind you for a day, you dunce."

    Billy shrugged. "I'll still be able to count higher than you."

    Alice shook her head, leaning against an arm. "This has got to be my favorite inside joke you two have."

    The teen gave the goth a look. "Inside joke?"

    Jen wiped the corner of her mouth with a napkin. "Yeah. You're always ribbing her for her math skills, but she's the one who taught you to count."

    Agatha rubbed a temple. "He doesn't remember that bit," she reminded the others gently. Billy gave her a look as the information sank in. "When?"

    "You were two-days old, probably six," the goddess told him. "Tommy found a picture book, so I read it to you both. But you insisted we work on numbers for the rest of the day." Agatha laughed to herself. She could still see the twins making faces as they tried to trace her numbers on the white boards the hex had provided. There had been the briefest of moments where she considered leaving the hex up to play the part for longer than necessary. "At this point, what haven't you taught him?" Wanda laughed. "Don't think I forgot how you showed them how to unlock doors."

    The immortal chuckled darkly. "Watching you panic was highly entertaining." Billy tossed a wadded up wrapper at his mother. "I bet you stopped at ten, though," he teased. "But I appreciate it, even if I can't remember it."

    Tommy nodded. "Yeah. I bet we had a bunch of fun. You seem like a chill teacher." Agatha quirked a brow. "Thanks?"

    Nicky wiggled in his seat. "Can we go home? My fingers are cold."

    "That's just from the ice cream, but it's definitely time we get going." Agatha finished off her ice cream, sending her sons a grin.

    Once the coven reached Agatha's house, they bid Billy and Teddy a good night. Agatha waited outside on the porch as each Westview member went inside. She moved over to the car and pulled them both into a tight hug. "Go practice your maths," she told Billy. "Because your next lesson is going to require measurements and I don't want to hear your bitching when you can't convert."

    Teddy pulled her into another hug. "Take care of yourself," he told her. "We'll be back Saturday."

    She waved them off before entered her home. "Tommy, Nicky, time for bed!" Wanda popped her head out of the kitchen. "I think Tommy's already in the shower. Nicky's in here with me."

    Agatha entered the room, hands in her pockets. "What's going on in here? You two are always hanging out wherever there's food."

    "I just like all the shiny stuff," her son told her.

    "And someone has to do the dishes," Wanda added. She pointed to the sink. "Unless you're going to take over tonight..."

    The immortal hummed in thought. "Sure, what the hell! I've got a lot of energy. Maybe you guys can...keep me company..."

    "Rio still isn't back yet?"

    Agatha huffed. "No...She's still out."

    "Can I stay up, Mama?"

    "Nope," she said quickly. "You need to get lots of rest." Agatha brushed his hair back. "You're a growing boy, Nicholas Scratch."Nicky pouted. "Will you read me a bedtime story?" Agatha rubbed his back. "Only if you let me snuggle up in bed with you." He nodded, a hand extended. "Deal!"

    "Who taught you that?" she asked, a brow quirking.

    Nicky giggled. "Tommy."

    "Okay...Maybe his devil-may-care attitude is a bit much for you."

    Wanda laughed. "Now you mind the bad habits?"

    "The youth of today are concerning creatures," Agatha told her. "I'll be back to do the dishes. Consider it payment for keeping an eye on the kids while I took care of my...affliction." The mother and son traveled upstairs. She helped him wash up and change into warm pajamas. He looked so cute in stripped onsie and a stuffed rabbit tucked under his arm. Agatha crawled into his twin bed and had him snuggle up with her. The witch opened up her Grimm's Fairytales and let him pick out one of the short stories. Nicky chose The Little Red Riding Hood, pleasing his mother greatly.

    She read to him softly, changing the tone of her voice for the wolf. He giggled when the Wolf tricked the girl into leaving the path for flowers.

    As Agatha reached the end of the story, the huntsman bursting into Granny's Cottage, a loud snore interrupted her. She looked down at her son, a smile breaking out over her face. "Goodnight, my darling." She pressed a kiss to his forehead and slipped out of his bed. Agatha made sure to tuck him before turning to leave. She grinned impossibly wider as Rio stepped forward. "You're home," she whispered.

    Death pressed a kiss to her lips, eyes practically glowing in the dim light. "I missed you both." She stepped away to press a kiss to Nicky's cheek. "Wine?"

    The pair left the room, door cracked in case their son needed something. Agatha filled her wife in on the day's events and made sure to let her know about Billy bullying her. "Sweetheart, why don't you just drop him off a cliff or something?" Rio suggested, lips curling upwards. She hugged her wife from behind, chin resting on Agatha's shoulder. "And risk being put in another hex?" The goddess cackled. "I'll stick with the bullying." Agatha went over to the sink as Rio waved to the group of women hanging out around the island.

    "Congratulations on scarring Billy," Jen told the Green Witch. She toasted the woman with her glass of wine.

    Agatha rolled her eyes as she filled one side with soapy water. "He'll live. I'm more impressed with the fact none of you had succumbed to the pull of alcohol." "It was a thought, but we were in there too long to fully give in," Alice told her. She sipped at a beer.

    Rio stepped up to Agatha's side, rolling up sleeves to a turtleneck she didn't have on seconds ago. Death seemed to be making a show of helping her. Agatha felt her cheeks warm at the gesture. The voices around her faded softly as the couple moved together, hand over hand, to care for the home they'd built.

    Agatha bit her lip as she cupped the back of Rio's head. "I never said that. Who said that? I didn't say anything of the sort."

    The Divine Mother rolled her eyes despite her smirk. "I'm well aware how amusing you find me, my love. It's my greatest gift to you, and one I seldom have to think about." She found she couldn't really care as a thumb stroked gently across her cheek. Agatha Harkness. Her greatest strength, and her greatest weakness. Her Achille's Heel if ever she had one.     Rio eased her head back against the pillow as soft lips traveled south. What to do with the swelling of her heart and the tightening of her lungs? Death shed her worries, and simply basked in the praise her wife showered her in.

    Agatha yawned as the sun began to rise. She glared at the offending celestial body and its horrendously offensive rays. Sure, the sun had begun to decrease it's time during the day, but Agatha was starting to wish the damn thing would implode. The more she eased into her new role, the more annoying her body became. Nicky complained about her cold hands. She never had energy if the fucking sun was up. (Agatha had never hated the sun before, but it was really starting to get on her nerves. Like, seriously!)

    No one could thank the Divine Mother or the Goddess around her. Any variation of her title would force her coven and nearby witches to praise her by name now. (She had a sinking suspicion the Ancient Ones were behind the verbal jinx. Probably Dolly.) It had been funny at first, but now she could hear people faintly in the back of her mind. It itched something terrible.

    And then there was Rio.

    Rio leaned over her, face inches from hers. "Come on, little bird! You've got three little witches to train."

    "You're too cheery," Agatha told her wife. "Why?"

    The Green Witch shrugged. "Seeing you always makes me feel better."

    Agatha visibly sagged. "Sorry, my love. I guess I'm not much of a day person anymore." She took the hand closest to her and pressed a kiss to the warm fingers she found. (Funny how Death was warmer than she. Scholars would be kicking themselves if they knew. All that talk of Death's cold embrace. It was very warm and pulling and teeth and...) Rio leaned down, a hand stroking her brow. "Are you okay? Do yo feel sick?" "No, I'm just exhausted. Doesn't matter if I sleep at night, I just don't have the energy most days." The immortal groaned into her pillow.

    "If you're tired, you need to rest," her wife argued. "There's no point in pushing yourself. I'll tell Billy and Teddy to stay home today."

    Agatha pulled Death down by the hand. "No, don't do all of that. You know how much they look forward to coming over and seeing the rest of the family. Just..." She pursed her lips. "Teach them something. Force them to learn plant names. Anything! Just don't let them fall behind in their studies."

    Rio chuckled. "You want me to teach a class?"

    The Divine Mother pouted. "Please?"

    Death's eyes widened before she pressed a kiss to her head. "I'll see what I can do. If I have to leave, though..."

    "Don't worry about that. I shouldn't sleep too long. I just need an hour or two." Agatha forced herself to sit up. She must have done a piss-poor job of something because her wife's eyes narrowed. "What?"

    Rio eased her back down, a hand combing back some hair. "Rest, amor. I'll take care of today's lesson."

    Agatha swallowed thickly, suddenly a child who had failed to do her part. "I'm sorry. It'll only..."

    A finger was pressed to her lips. "Don't apologize. It's not your fault. Winter means longer nights. You're going to be more tired as you stay up more." Rio tucked her in with a warm grin. "Sleep."

    Agatha tried to keep her eyes open, but they were doing a damn good job at keeping her from her wife. She took one of Rio's hands and held it in hers. Sleep was quick to claim her, but peace was her true companion.

    Small fingers took blades of dry grass, braiding the strands with determined, practiced patience. The plant life here was nowhere near the same Nicholas had been used to when it was just him and Mama. There was an acrid smell to the air. Tainted. Pollutants that robbed the land of much-needed nutrients. It saddened him greatly. His mama had always taught him the importance of caring for the land they lay their head upon. Why couldn't the rest of the world do the same? He glanced over at the black tarmac that smothered the dirt below. What beautiful things were destroyed in the attempt to control the environment? "Nicky," his mother called from the back porch. She waved him over, a smile on her face. The child got up from his spot next to Mama's grave and ran over. He brushed hair out of his face, squinting up at her as the sun shone behind her head. "I missed you," he told her. He always made sure to tell her. Nicholas could still remember the way his mother's gaze would linger on his mama before she left for the night. He wanted his mother to know how much he loved her, so she never left with a frown.

    Death bent at the waist, cupping his chin. "Te extrañé también, querido mio." She tickled his sides with her free hand. "¿Desayuno?"

    Nicholas nodded eagerly. "Can we have waffles?"

    His mother took his hand as she led him inside. "You had waffles all last week. Don't you want to try something else for once? How about an omelet?"

    He wrinkled his nose. "I don't like eggs. They stink." That, and Mama had forced him to eat an egg everyday. "Witches need to stay big and strong," she would tell him. "What about cereal?" The witch walked over to a cabinet above his eye level. "These are healthy for boys your age."

    "Can I add a spoonful of sugar to it? Tommy does."

    Death eyed the box of Cheerios. "I'm pretty sure you're supposed to eat these without the added sugar."

    The child clasped his hands together. "Please," he begged, a deep pout forming. "Just a sprinkle of sugar. It's so yummy!"

    His mother sighed, head tilting to the side that told him he'd won her over. "Only one sprinkle, but I'll do it. You'll grab a handful," she said with a laugh. "Deal!" He shook her hand with a wide grin.

    "Just don't tell Mama," Death told him with a wink.

    Nicholas looked towards the living room. "Mama isn't up yet..." He frowned. She never slept in unless she wasn't feeling well. "I'm gonna go check on her."

    A hand stopped him before he could take more than a step. "Don't worry about her, mijo. Mama's taking a break today. Her new job makes her sleepy during the day." He looked up at her. "Does Mama like her new job?"

    Death shrugged. "Hard to say. She's not done it long enough." She poured milk into the bowl of grainy circles. "Here. Let's eat. I can hear your stomach." His mother set his bowl down on the kitchen table.

    Nicholas made himself comfortable and spooned some cereal into his mouth. He watched her watch him and smiled. Nothing made him happier than knowing his mothers weren't mad at each other anymore. Mama had always looked so sad and scared. Mother always had to hide. He had felt so torn between the two. Like he couldn't make one happy without hurting the other. Thankfully, he didn't feel that now.

    "Penny for your thoughts," Death whispered softly, lips twitching upwards. "I'm happy here," he told her honestly. "I like that you and Mama can be happy, too." Nicholas hoped his mother didn't take offense. He had a feeling his mama would have cried at the words. She didn't like remembering their days on the road. It always made a shadow pass over her face.

    His mother grinned, warming his chest. "I'm happy you're here, too." She chuckled, looking away briefly. "And I love that Mama and I can be happy. We just missed you so much, we forgot how to talk to each other."

    The child nodded, bangs falling into his field of vision. "That's okay. So long as it's all better now."

    "Good morning," Wanda greeted. She gave his mother's shoulder a squeeze before moving to pat his back. "You two are up extra early!"

    "Mama's taking a break today," Nicholas told her. He filed away the worried look on her face. Perhaps his Mama being tired wasn't a good thing. Then again, Mother had never lied to him before. Therefore, Wanda was just being worried because she cared. That thought made him feel fuzzy.

    "Well, we'll be sure to be extra quiet when Billy and Teddy get here," the witch told him. She made herself a bowl and sat next to his mother. "How was work, Rio?"

    Nicholas watched them talk, words drifting between the two with a slight charge. His mother looked tense, but Wanda looked at ease. In fact, the two were constantly at odds. He made a note to ask Mama about that later. His mind drifted back to the grass outside. The feel of the tips tickling his toes every time he would go for a walk in the back. He missed the river. The sound of water flowing. There was so much noise, now. And it rarely was pleasing to the ears. Especially when a car would honk loudly. No, this world was nothing like the one he and his mothers had shared when he was younger.

    "Why so quiet today?" Wanda asked him, her brows furrowing. It reminded him of his mama when he'd cough. She was concerned. He didn't like concern.

    "I miss my old home," he told her. It was his hope that honesty would alleviate the tension in her shoulders.

    "Oh...What was it like?"

    "Quiet. Peaceful. Trees forever and ever." Nicholas sighed heavily. He missed the woods more than he'd realized. Was that what it meant to grow up? To constantly yearn for the things you couldn't hold and protect in your hands?

    His mother slid out of her seat to hug him. "I know things are different now, querido. Trust me, I miss the quiet, too. But there are good things here. Mortals have safer homes and boats and all sorts of things!"

    He hugged her tightly, pressing his face into her shoulder. "I know," he told her. "I just miss it."

    Death curled around him the way Mama used to when he was smaller. She rocked him gently. "Mama and I will make you a garden to play in. One just for you with all the peace and quiet you could ever want."

    His ears perked at the idea. "With birds and butterflies and bees?"

    "Whatever you want," she promised. Mother always made good on her promises. "Okay," Nicholas told her. He pressed a kiss to her cheek. "Can I go back outside now? I wanna look for ladybugs."

    Death laughed. "If you must."

    "I must," he told her seriously, his hands balled into fists. "I want them to live on Mama's grave." The red would pop nicely with the creams of the mushrooms and other fungi. Nicholas waved to the women before rushing off in search of his insect friends.

    "He's very into the outdoors," Wanda told Rio. "I guess that's what happens when you're born in a time before the internet."

    The Green Witch shrugged. "Maybe." Now that her son was off doing whatever, she didn't need to pretend around the Scarlet Witch. "Don't wake Agatha up. You won't like the level of angry I can become if you do."

    "Rio, I'm not a homewrecker," the red head argued. "You don't have to worry about me trying to flirt with her or anything. I love Vision."

    She eyed the woman, not particularly convinced. After all, this was the same woman who had played with her wife's hair the night before. Wanda had also shared wine with Agatha. They had snuggled during a movie. The more Rio thought about it, the more her cosmic blood boiled.

    "I don't trust you," Death told the chaos witch. "You're too comfortable around her. You do anything to hurt her, and I'll reap you every chance I get."

    Wanda laughed. Laughed! The nerve. The audacity. The disrespect!

    Death stood to her full height. "I'm being entirely serious, Wanda Maximoff. You are on my shit list." She left the room in search of something else to do. Maybe Alice was up and would want to listen to some rock before the boys arrived. Or maybe Tommy would consider lighting a building on fire just to make something happen in the sleepy town of Westview. In the end, she ended up joining Nicky outside. He sifted through the yard for ladybugs. She didn't have the heart to tell them they'd all left or died with the colder weather. Rio followed behind him, holding the many sticks and rocks he stumbled upon in his search for the six- legged insects. She cleared her throat, catching his attention.

    "I'm going to give Billy and Wanda a lesson over green magic today. Do you want to join them?" She didn't miss the way his eyes lit up. It made her cheeks ache as a grin split them. "Yes, yes, yes," he cheered. Her son danced a small jig. He giggled as she picked him up to twirl him.

    Oh, her son! How she loved the small mortal with every fiber of her being. With every thread of cosmic matter she encompassed. His soul pulsed a brilliant white. So pure. So innocent. If only she could sequester him and Agatha away where nothing could ever hurt them again. A place of laughter and love.

    "Hey guys," Teddy greeted. He entered through the fence gate as Billy headed inside. "Aren't you guys cold?"

    When the hell did those two pull up? she wondered. Rio offered him a smile. "I can't feel the temperature difference," she told him.

    "We're having too much fun," Nicky added. Only...now she could see how flushed his cheeks and nose were.

    "Let's get you a jacket just in case," Death told her son. "Human bodies can't stay cold for too long." She ushered the two inside, probing them with her magic. Both were healthy. She let out a sigh.

    "They told me Agatha's resting for today," Billy said before stuffing a piece of buttered toast in his mouth. (Honestly, he had manners worse than Agatha some days.)

    "She is. So, bundle up. We're going to go over plants," the Green Witch told the group. Rio clapped her hands, shooing them off to get ready. There was a lot of botanical jargon they would need to get through, and so very little time. A major accident could occur at any moment, and then they'd be behind.

    Minutes later, the group stood in the back yard. Clouds had begun to gather as a cold front moved southeasterly over the state. Rio took her hood and wrapped it around Nicky. He stared up at her from under the dark cloth, eyes bright with excitement. She realized, with a grin, that this would be their first lesson together. Death pressed a kiss to her son's face before straightening her back. Billy and Teddy huddled together; hands clasped tightly between themselves. Frustratingly, Wanda seemed unaffected by the chill.

    "In nature, there are bunch of things that can tell you if something's gonna send you to me or not. Wasps are bright yellow. Rattlesnakes cause all that racket. Plants, however, are more subtle. They want you to foolishly grasp at them. Some give you a warning, like Stinging Nettle. Urtica dioica, when touched, will sting you with her acids. She's a beauty," Rio told them. She coaxed one to grow from the soil along Agatha's fence. Toothed leaves unfurled, waving as the plant shot up from the ground. "Young leaves are medicinal in property. Teas can be brewed for an assortment of ailments. Most common uses are for urinary issues and hay fever." The Green Witch grew another plant. "But some are relatively harmless unless consumed in large quantities. Achillea millefolium, or Yarrow, is safe to touch and eat in small quantities." Death grinned as a bunch of white flowers bloomed at the top of the stalk. "But can lead to a world of pain and loss if not careful. Women, beware." She continued on, growing more and more deadly plants. Soon, there was a full fence-line of plants ranging from floral to unassuming leaf bunches. They were beautiful, but always deadly. Just the way she like her flowers. And now here came her favorite one of them all. "Have we been taking notes?" Agatha asked as she walked over to them. She eyed her students as they shivered.

    "I th-think we've g-got it," Jen chattered. She buried her face back into her scarf. Rio grinned at her wife. "I think I ought to give them a pop quiz now. Which one of these four is the deadliest?" She gestured to the plants behind her.

    "Nicky!" Agatha threw herself forward to pull her son back from the plants. Her face paled as the whole plant came with them.

    Death waited for the tell-tale tug that came with a dying soul.

    "Uh...Maybe I have my plants wrong," she mumbled. Rio took the plant from her son and examined the leaves. Her stomach dropped. "No..."

    Agatha checked over their son, fingers prodding and poking. "He's...He's okay?" "I got it right, though," Nicky pouted. His eyes welled up with tears as he looked between his mothers. "Did I do something wrong?"

    Rio turned and buried the plant, kicking herself mentally. Why had she grown poisonous plants around her child? Her mortal child who was prone to touching things. "Conium maculatum is very dangerous," she bit out. "Our first rule was 'no touching.' You could have died."

    Agatha sucked in a shaky breath. "You don't feel funny? No upset stomach? No headaches?" Death turned around as the child shook his head. "I play with Hemlock all the time," he told them. "It's pretty."

    The women shared a look. What had he meant by that?

    "Querido, we're not mad at you. We were just scared. If Billy or Teddy or Tommy touched that plant, they would have died. Don't..." Death swallowed thickly. "Don't do that again unless Mama or I are with you."

    His eyes shifted between the two. "But I used to gather Hogweed for Mama all the time and she never said anything."

    Rio rounded on Agatha, ready to loose hell on her.

    "I didn't know plants all that well," she was quick to say. "We would just gather flowers around the river."

    The Green Witch glared at the duo. She could feel Agatha's panicked heartbeat. It was all too much. "Ambos me llevan a la pared. ¿Lo sabes? ¿Por qué no pueden mantener sus manos para sí mismos? ¡Dime por qué!" Death stomped away from the pair with a huff. She could feel the eyes of the coven boring into her back, but she refused to turn and face mother and son. Touching deadly plants as if they were made of paper! She had half a mind to light the backyard on fire.

    "Mamá no lo sabía. Los agarré por mi cuenta," Nicky argued. He furrowed his little brows as he put his hands on his hips. (Very Agatha. Very irritating.) "No puedes gritale." He was telling her not to yell! Death shook her finger at the wayward child. "Podrías haber sido herido. Podrías haber sido asesinado. Voy a gritarle a tu madre por eso." She'd just make sure she yelled at Agatha in private. Here wasn't the best place. Then again, she was currently arguing with a child. Not her best move.

    Nicky shook his head and stomped a foot. "¡No!"

    "Agatha, you better get your son before I lose what little sanity I have left," Rio told her wife. She took her dagger and sliced a hole in the fabric of space. If she didn't leave now, she was going to hurt someone's feelings. Out of the corner of her eye, Wanda pulled the two back. It did little to ease her irritation. She stepped through the portal and closed it up tight. (Later, she'd realize she didn't tell them goodbye....Uh oh!)

    The goddess rubbed her temples. "It's cold. I'm confused. Just...get your asses inside. We'll pick up on her lesson at another time." Agatha scooped Nicky up. "And you, mister. Even if you're defending me, don't yell at your mother. She's completely right. Just don't tell her I said that."

    He pouted, looking down.

    She pressed a kiss to his cheek. "Are you sure you're okay?"

    "Yes, Mama. I feel fine."

    "Don't cop an attitude with me. You're the one who sent us into a panic. Even if you can touch poisonous things, it doesn't mean you should. I just got you back, I can't..." Her voice gave out as her throat swelled with emotion. Agatha blinked back tears. "You scared us, Nicky. That's why your mother needed to step away. We'll talk about this more, later. Go wash up."

    Once he was set down, he hugged her tightly. "Sorry, Mama. I thought you knew." "It's okay. It was an accident. You've got a pretty amazing gift, my love. A heads up would have been nice, though." She ruffled his hair. "Go on. You know how to work the shower. I'll be there in just a second with a warm towel."

    Nicky stood on his tippy-toes and pressed a kiss to her cheek. " 'Kay! Tell Mother, I'm sorry." "You'll tell her yourself," she shouted after him. Agatha shook her head. Her son had inherited her stubbornness...great! She looked forward to his teen years. He might even try to smother her with a pillow if Rio's violent tendencies won out. Rio...

    It wasn't like she didn't understand where her wife was coming from. The immortal had been ready to lash out at Death for being so careless, but she had been the worst of the two. At least now they both knew Nicky wouldn't succumb to a plant. That put her at ease, for now. Agatha gathered a long-sleeve shirt and sweatpants with fuzzy socks for her son. She knocked on the door before entering the bathroom. Steam poured out as she set his clothes aside. And then she heard it.

    Agatha gripped the edge of the sink, praying with all she had that she'd just imagined it. But then it happened again. Twice, actually, in rapid succession.

    Nicholas Scratch had a cough.

    Chapter End Notes Question for you all....How fond are you guys of Nicky? (hehehehe)

    Also.......I love y'all!!!! I haven't told y'all in a while. Hope y'all have a great week before I crush your hopes and dreams!

    My Son Needs Me Home Chapter Summary Nicholas Scratch has a cough Chapter Notes As I write this, it's my lil sister's b-day. She doesn't read my stuff (for good reason), but I'm still going to dedicate this chapter to her. I can recall, vividly, what it was like to see someone you care about fall sick. It wasn't fun in the slightest. (Plus, she cried a lot. I never got any sleep.)

    Here's to you, my dearest baby sister! May the coming years be free of illness and pain. (I'm doubling everything meant for you and putting it on the coven hehe. Love ya, Agatha!)

    See the end of the chapter for more notes Agatha paced, eyes glued to her red-faced son. He sat on the couch with a blanket thrown over his legs and his stuffed rabbit in his lap. Nicky sipped on a cup of Pedialyte with the occasional slurp. The younger Harkness had his own eyes glued to the t.v. He'd insisted on watching Finding Nemo because, "Hey, look Mama. That's us!" (Agatha vowed to set the Disney-Pixar studios ablaze for the emotional pain she was being put through.) She hugged herself tightly, a hand tucked under her chin. At least his immune system was stronger than what it had been. Or was it?

    Cough, cough Her bottom lip trembled. Or was it her whole body this time? She couldn't tell anymore. Time, itself, had slipped beyond her grasp. Like wispy tendrils of smoke. Like a drop of rain into the raging, angry ocean of their volatile planet. The goddess dug her nails into her side. Anything to keep from crying out. The pain was good. Kept her mind sharp in between the soul-tearing, teeth-gnashing, heart-wrenching coughing fits. (How easy it was for children to get sick! What a cruel world they lived in.)

    Alice sneezed before sniffling. She looked at Agatha with bleary eyes and a bright red nose. "Yuh're mahking meh nuhvous," she told Agatha, tone nasally. Poor thing was the first to fully succumb to whatever horrid illness had infiltrated her coven. At least Lilia wasn't here to relive the nightmare. Fevers and incoherent ramblings. The woman would have had a meltdown by now. (Agatha was on her way to one, and quickly.)

    The Divine Mother went to the goth's side. She pressed a cool hand to the younger woman's forehead with a hiss. Her fever had worsened. "Where's that tea, Jen?" Why have a potions witch if she can't brew a damn thing?

    Something, a fist likely, pounded the countertop. "You try destemming these leaves with body aches," the woman grumbled from the kitchen.

    Agatha shot a look in Nicky's direction. Other than the cough, he seemed fine. He should be okay if she slipped out of the room for a moment. In fact, she needed to make a soup. Soup was good. Soup helped heal and nurture souls. Soup...soup was a hug. (The immortal was starting to spiral.) Agatha entered the kitchen, eyes narrowing. Jen swayed next to the counter, hands gripping the edges. The goddess eased her shoulders, anger falling away like the red and yellow leaves outside her house.

    "Come on, Kale. Nicky needs company," she told the robed witch. Agatha put an arm over her shoulders and led her towards the living room. Once Jen had settled next to her son, she helped move Alice over. "There. You three stay here. I'm going to go see if Wanda was able to break Tommy's fever."

    They thanked her with nods, sneezes, and coughs. Each sound was like another knife to her heart. Here was her coven, her students, her family, sick. And Agatha? Agatha was still as powerless to help them. She didn't have healing magic. Her magic took. Her magic killed. Agatha left the room before her tears could fall. She stopped on the stairs to collect herself. What was the point of having mastery over magic if she couldn't do a fucking thing with her knowledge? Her second chance at life was more like a cruel punishment. One she willingly accepted. A lamb to the slaughter. Agatha bit her hand to keep from screaming her frustrations. (Worthless. Worthless. Worthless. Agatha Harkness was worthless.) "Knock, knock," she croaked before pushing the door to Tommy's room open. Agatha found Tommy and Wanda huddled on the bed. The Scarlet Witch had looked better, but she wasn't anywhere near the level of sick Alice and Tommy were. From the looks of her coven, the flu had taken hold of her family. Agatha stepped forward. "How is he?"

    Wanda sniffed. "Still has a fever and upset stomach." (So that was that sickly acrid smell that permeated the air.)

    Agatha nodded. "I'm going to try and make a tea. Would...Would you be willing to try it before I give it to the others? You're just..." The witch licked her lips, eyes falling to the sweaty teen. "You're the only one who won't die permanently if I get something wrong." The red head gave her a weak thumbs up. "Gonna nap," she breathed. Those green eyes, so much like Neva's, were dulled by the fever Wanda was battling. (Worthless. Worthless. Worthlessworthlessworthlessworthless...)

    "I'll be back," she choked out. Agatha swiftly left the room.

    Once she made it back to the kitchen, she pulled out her new spell book. Agatha flipped until she found a slew of remedies. There were so many! How the hell was she supposed to know which one worked best? What if one of them was allergic to one of the plants? Agatha nearly threw the book at the wall. Nearly. She leaned against the counter with a heavy sigh. Cough, cough Agatha bit back a sob. Goddamnit, Rio. Where the fuck are you? She squared her shoulders. She was The mother-fuck-ing Divine Mother! Gods bent the world to their whims! The goddess could cry later. The goddess could rain fire on the world that dared take her family from her once they were better. Right now, she needed to focus.

    Agatha went into the back yard, the moon starting to rise as the sun set. Good. Now, her magic would be stronger. Her teas would be more potent. The immortal focused on her task and began to pick leaves from the list of plants in her book. At least Rio had grown the ones she needed most. Her basket of pouches were quickly filled, her breath misting around her face. For once, the chill began to settle in her bones, but she pressed onwards. Unlike Rio's botanical garden, these plants would die with the freeze. She needed to collect all of them. Her fingers turned red. Her sight began to blur, but Agatha Harkness persevered. She returned to the house, limbs trembling and teeth chattering. Agatha set the basket down and set upon gathering the ingredients she needed most. In one pot, she put in the exact number of leaves to sunflower, speedwell, black mustard, pearly everlasting, and common mullein. She measured out the water and set the pot to boil. In another, the Divine Mother prepped coltsfoot according to the recipe and set a deeper pot boil. Agatha determined a triple batch would be best given the number of coven members with respiratory issues. A third pot was filled with boneset, watercress, trembling aspen, and yarrow leaves. Soon, the kitchen was hot with all the steam she was producing. The witch began to sweat, but she didn't dare stop. Agatha pulled out a bundle of horseradish and separated the steams, roots, leaves, and petals. She set everything but the roots off to the side. Agatha didn't feel like using up all of her stores just in case she needed more. Hopefully, Rio would grant her more. If not...

    The goddess rifled through her cabinets and drawers until she found a mortar and pestle. She put moon water in the mortar before adding root after root. Agatha was blessed with a thick poultice that smelt medicine-y in the best of ways. (Had she known about this, Nicky could have slept soundly most nights.) She turned and pulled the coltsfoot off the burner. Agatha measured the sugar according to the recipe and added it to the strong-smelling liquid. She mixed the sugar in until a thick syrup was created. Everyone would finally be able to sleep without choking on their phlegm.

    Agatha sectioned her teas away, marking them for the symptoms to alleviate. The first pitcher for the congestion and other respiratory issues. The second, for the fever and aches. The coltsfoot syrup was poured into a jar and sealed up tight. Agatha labelled the jar and set it next to the teas. Lastly, she found another jar and put her horseradish poultice into it. Prepared for battle, the goddess sought out Wanda.

    "Have you been in the kitchen this whole time?" the woman asked her. She cleared her throat, a hand pressed to the column of skin with a wince. "Take a break."

    "Later." She poured a glass from her first pitcher. "This is for coughing, sore throats, and...uh..." Her mind blanked. Downstairs, Nicky had begun his first, worse coughing fit. Agatha swallowed thickly, her heart racing. "Uh...congestion," she managed to say. "I'll be right back."

    Nicky had settled by the time she reached him, but a fever had begun to creep up on him. He gripped at her weakly.

    A cold body in her arms and, "I want more time...I want more time!"

    "Mama's got you," she whispered, tears sliding down her cheeks. "I'm right here." Wanda appeared, the tray of herbal remedies shaking in her grip. "I tried everything. They seem to be safe."

    Agatha sighed in relief. "Wait right here. I'm gonna get you..." She swallowed back a sob. The immortal rushed over to the coffee table and began to pour a cup for her son. She would tend to the others once he was settled. Her hands shook as she carried the mug over. She pressed the rim to his lips, whispering encouraging words that likely sounded like broken sobs.

    Nicky pushed the cup away with a wrinkled nose. "That's yucky," he whined. Good. That's good. Her son still had some fight to him. Still had warmth to his skin. "That just means it's working," she told him, attempting to smile reassuringly. Her stomach twisted with worry as he leaned back, closing his eyes. "Nicky?"

    " 'm fine, Mama. Just tired," he sighed.

    She thanked Herself before pulling out the poultice. "I'm gonna put some of this on your chest okay. It'll help with the coughing." Agatha rubbed the cream over his sternum, feeling for his heartbeat. It was still steady. Still strong.

    Once he fell asleep, Agatha moved to Alice. The woman coughed before gagging. Her lungs sounded awful. The rattle not at all unfamiliar to the goddess. Agatha helped her to sit up, a trashcan at the ready. She rubbed the goth's back as she spit up phlegm. (Caring for the sick was a nasty business, and certainly not for the weak.) Alice mumbled a thanks before sipping at the offered tea. She winced as the warmth stung her raw throat.

    Another set of coughing wracked the young witch's body. Agatha pulled out her cough syrup and fed two tablespoons to Alice. "Might be a bit strong, but it's better than puke," she told the girl.

    "Th'nks, Ahg'tha," Alice wheezed. She sucked in a breath, eyes falling shut. (Worthless. Worthless. Worthless!)

    Next was Jen. She sipped at the second batch of tea with a sigh. "Not bad," the potions witch praised. "Sugar can be added to taste in case Nicky needs more. You're doing great." Agatha nodded, sniffling. "Sleep," she told the woman. "I'll still be up." (Like hell she was sleeping. Not when Rio was still missing.)

    "You need to rest, too," Jen argued. She took another sip.

    "Immortal, remember? At most, I'll just need a nap. Don't get all sentimental on me now, Jenny Kay." The goddess pressed the witch back against the pillows. "Your tea will be here on the table should you need it. I need to go make sure Tommy got some." A phone began to ring upstairs. Agatha's work was all but done.

    The call was for her. Rebecca was checking in on the coven. Billy, thank Herself, had managed to avoid being sick. (Who knew what would happen if he were to have a waking, fever-induced hallucination?) Agatha promised to keep the woman updated before promptly hanging up. There was still so much to be done. Tissues needed replenishing. Trashes needed to be thrown. More tea was needed. (So much was needed. So much...)

    Cough, cough Agatha took a moment to step into her room to scream into a pillow.

    What was this nightmare she was in? Why...How had things managed to get so bad in a mere twenty-four hours? What had she done wrong? Was she still doing things wrong? Agatha wanted to know. Wanted someone to step up to her and tell her why this was happening to her again. She threw the pillow at the wall and ran a hand down her face. Now wasn't the time to dissolve into tears. There were five sick witches in her home that needed her attention. Three of which needed as much assurance as they could possibly get. Agatha fixed her hair back into a bun and returned to her never-ending battle.

    Nicholas sat up as his lungs clenched. He felt his lip tremble at the sensation. It was the same one he had before he left Mama and went with Mother. And if that was the case, his Mama was going to be very sad again. The child felt around for one of his parents. All he found were his big sisters. Not exactly who he needed, and his body knew that. He sucked in a shaky breath before he burst into tears.

    "Mama..." It was weak, but it was heard.

    A lamp was switched on before cool hands were cradling him. His damp hair was brushed back as he sobbed into his mama's shoulder. She smelt of strongly of plants and a little bit of magic. "I'm right here," his mama told him. Her voice was soft like a feather. "Do you need some more tea? Jen said I could put some sugar in it."

    Nicholas nodded, rubbing at an eye. Another cough tickled his chest. Another shadow flitted over the goddess' face. He hated making her sat. Hated the way she clutched at him like he was slipping away. Maybe he was? "Where's Mother?" he whined. Now, he hated how small he felt. Even before, he had never felt this awful. His body felt icky and wrong. It made him cry harder, which made Mama cry harder, which made him cry harder, which made... "Don't go," his Mama pleaded. "I'll...I'll..." Mama never lied to him. That was their one rule. So, why couldn't she promise he'd feel better? Why was she shaking just as much as he was? "I'm not gonna go," he promised. "I won't go. I'm staying, Mama. I'm staying." Nicholas burrowed his face into her neck, holding on for dear life. He refused to make his mothers cry over him. "I'm staying."

    His mama rocked him until they both stopped crying. She began to sing to him, her voice broken and hoarse, but it soothed him the way it always had.

    "Down, down, down the road...I walk the windy road..."

    Nicholas relaxed in her hold, breathing in time with her as their voices mixed. He could almost hear phantom claps and cheers from years gone by. His audience of old cheering him on. There, in the distance, was the sound of a campfire cracking and popping. Birds chirping and hooting in the distance. The gentle sway of branches overhead. The world was safe here in his mama's arms. She had never let any harm befall him. Had always held him close and loved him with all her heart. Nicholas held onto that feeling as he drifted off to sleep.

    Rio docked her boat with a groan. Mortals really, really, really needed to stop setting fire to places if they weren't ready to murder hundreds of people and animals. If she could, she'd yell, "The sex of your baby isn't worth my forests and plains!" But no! She was a guide first, and Mother Nature second.

    There were still so many more souls to lead away, but enough had been ferried for her to take a short break. Especially since she'd left in such an unsavory way. Agatha was going to have her head! Then again, her wife's heart hadn't stopped racing since she left. She was probably with Wanda, the horrid woman. Rio could already see their smiling faces, those gentle touches. It made her fume and seethe and scowl. Maybe she'd catch them, and she could have an excuse to put the Scarlet Witch in the ground for a little bit.

    Death slipped through the veil and directly into Agatha's room. It was empty. She froze, her senses screaming at her. One soul was fighting for their life downstairs. The rest were close behind. Agatha's heart was still racing. Rio threw the door open and checked Nicky's room. It was empty and stale. Never a good sign. Next, she checked Tommy's room. The boy and his irritating mother were cuddled up on the bed.

    She wrinkled her nose at the stench of pestilence. A mixture of the flu and bronchitis ravaging the souls around her. Nothing too serious, thankfully. (For Tommy, not Wanda. Fuck Wanda. Stupid homewrecking, wife-stealing, shifty-eyed woman!) Death left the room and check Alice's bedroom. Empty. Jen's room? Empty as well.

    Cough, wheeze, cough The Green Witch descended the stairs quickly and moved towards the living room. She found the rest of the coven resting on the sectional. Well, most of them. Agatha was tending to Alice as she hacked up a lung. (So, that's who's soul was treading the fine line between realms.) The goth caught a glimpse of her and smiled weakly. Rio stared at her with wide eyes. She hadn't exactly fully stepped through the veil yet.

    "M'ning," she mumbled out. There was a glassy look to her eyes.

    Agatha looked up, a stricken expression slipping onto her face. Blue eyes flicked down to Nicky and then back to Rio. "No..."

    "I'm not here for anyone," the older immortal clarified. She raised her hands in self-defense as she took the state of the house in. It had become a den of desperation. Jen held a flushed Nicky. The witch, herself, seemed to be the strongest of the mortals. "What...?" Did she have the right to ask such a question?

    "Must have been all the cold air," her wife told her. There were bags under her eyes. Of course, there were. The sun had risen many hours ago, but there she was. Standing in the filth of her family like the survivor she was. Agatha eased Alice back before applying more of a white poultice.

    "Horseradish?" Death asked, a brow quirking.

    "For her congestion," Agatha informed.

    Rio knew that, but when had her wife learned that. She dared to move closer, eyes trained on the goddess should she see her as a threat. "Agatha...she's not doing well," she told her carefully. "Wake Jen up."

    The younger immortal glared at her. "Just help me," she snapped. "Let me take the consequences. Just help me!"

    The Green Witch swallowed thickly. The Ancient Ones wouldn't be kind to her wife if she started messing with the Natural Order again. "I am helping you. Wake Jen up." Agatha growled. "Why do you always...?" She covered Alice back up before shaking the potions witch awake. "I need your help. Alice is getting worse."

    Jen sat up quickly, eyes wide. "Okay...okay...What are her most prominent symptoms?" "It's mostly phlegm and fluid in her chest than anywhere else," Agatha told her covenmate. "The teas...and...the teas..."

    "Come on, Harkness! Get it in gear," Jen hissed. "What about the teas?" Rio glared at the witch but held her tongue as her wife stomped a foot. "Give me a fucking second, Jen! I'm not a damn healer. I don't know the first thing about healing," the goddess spat. Agatha wiped her brow as sweat began to bead. "The teas aren't working. I've tried both, the syrup, and the poultice. What the fuck am I missing?" Rio stepped towards her. The wild beating of their hearts urging her to hold her wife. The Divine Mother was going to work herself up into a panic attack if she wasn't careful. "Tell her what you used."

    Agatha magicked over her spell book before pointing out the recipes she'd followed. "There was horseradish, coltsfoot, uh..., colts..."

    Death couldn't stand it any longer. She pulled Agatha into her arms and pressed a kiss to her cheek. "Take a breath, amor. You're going to pass out."

    "You were supposed to be here," her wife hissed. "I needed you."

    "Agatha, the list," Jen urged. "Be mad later."

    The goddess gripped Rio tightly. "First tea was sunflower, speedwell, black mustard, pearly everlasting, and common mullein. Horseradish for the poultice. Coltsfoot for the syrup. Second tea...second tea was boneset, watercress, trembling aspen, and yarrow leaves." "Your first tea had too many different types. We need to narrow it down to a few and focus on her congestion. I'll take of the tea, you gather me some more moon water, Moon Goddess." Jen brushed past the couple to find the ingredients she needed.

    "Go," she told Agatha. "I'm not here for anyone," Rio reminded.

    Agatha gave her a look. It wasn't distrustful or pleading. It was tired. Her wife had pushed herself further than she had in a long time. Had wadded through the plumes of viral clouds and infected herself tenfold. And to think the goddess deemed herself unlovable and unfeeling.

    "If Nicky gets worse, I'll let you know. Same with the others."

    It was enough to spur Agatha into action. She squeezed her tightly before she slipped off to help Jen. Rio moved to the front yard and coaxed as many plants as she could from the cold dirt. Jen would want, if she was a good witch, more sunflower, black mustard, and common mullein leaves. Death pulled them from the ground and took them inside. She set the bundles on the island before plucking the leaves from the stems. Jen took them with a silent nod. Death wasn't directly healing the girl, so no one could claim she'd bent the rules again. Hazel eyes settled on her wife. The woman was moving slower and slower. It was apparent now, more than ever, that Agatha was not immune to the virus. She gave it another hour before the goddess collapsed under the weight of her exhaustion and failing strength. Rio vowed to be there to catch her. "Drink some of the tea, Agatha."

    "Go to hell," her wife spat.

    Rio didn't take offense. "You'll need it," she warned. Why was her wife so stubborn? Agatha set down a large bowl of water, a light glow to it. "Moon water," she told Jen. The potions witch boiled the leaves in it, Latin tumbling from her lips like gasoline on a flame. Their combined magic made a heartier concoction. As soon as the ten minutes of steeping had been completed, Rio sent a small gust of air to cool it to a safe temperature. Jen served a glass and rushed it over to Alice. The goth was weak but fought hard to sit up and drink the tea.

    Agatha paced.

    The goddess kept Rio in her line of sight at all times. She had sworn she wasn't there for anyone, but Agatha had a hard time forgetting how Nicky had been stolen from her. She worried her lip, then resumed biting her hand as the minutes ticked away. A warm hand took hers out of her mouth. Rio looked at her, a pained expression darkening those brilliant hazel eyes. Her wife pressed a kiss to the bruised skin. Agatha sniffled, her head pounding from the day's events. Even if Alice was saved right now, there was still Tommy, Nicky, and Wanda to worry about. It made her stomach twist.

    "If we keep giving her a tablespoon every two hours, she'll be better in no time," Jen informed the two. She pressed a hand to Alice's cheek. "She's a fighter. She'll be fine." Agatha refused to sleep just in case. She owed as much to Lorna for tricking her into thinking the Road was real. If she hadn't, the mother and daughter could have spent more time together.

    The goddess resumed her pacing. Occasionally, she went upstairs to check on Wanda and Tommy. The Scarlet Witch was starting to look better. Color had returned to her face. Tommy, on the other hand, seemed about the same. It wasn't great, but it was better than him slipping further towards her wife. The soup, thank Herself, helped his metabolism as a fever burned his body up.

    "You need to rest," Rio urged. She tugged Agatha towards her room, but the Divine Mother held firm.

    "My coven still needs me," she reminded the Green Witch. "I'll rest later." Death dragged her away from the sleeping coven. "Agatha, you're immortal not immune. You're already sick."

    "Oh, like you care!" She hadn't meant to spit venom. Agatha had been doing so well in keeping herself in check. But after Nicky's plant trick and then the whole coven falling sick, she had little patience left.

    Her nerves were fried. Her brain hurt. She wanted Rio to hold her and tell her for certain no one was going to die. The goddess couldn't bear to lose a single family member so soon. The cosmic entity pulled her in, hands finding her hair. "I do care," Death reaffirmed. "I..." She made a sour face, gaze shifting to the side. "I thought you and Wanda were fucking like crazy, not that everyone had fallen sick."

    Agatha scowled at the thought. She supposed an accelerated heartbeat was indiscernible when it came to emotions. Fear and arousal both made one's heart beat faster. But for her wife to think she would actually sleep with the Maximoff...

    She took Rio's hand and pressed it to her heart. "I have not, nor will I ever, leave your side," Agatha growled. "I married you. I gave you my heart. You gave me Nicky and time. Wanda has given me nothing." Agatha sucked in a breath as her wife dropped her head. "You've both been...fraternizing and touching and..."

    Do you never learn? she thought, mentally kicking herself. "She is nothing more to me than the Kaplan's are. Co-parents and, at times, a friend. My love, I do not want anyone else but you." Agatha tilted Rio's chin with two fingers. "Do you still not know how much I love you?"

    If her wife had to question it at this stage, then the goddess was still doing a piss-poor job. What more could she do? Did she need to follow the cosmic entity around? Rub her wife's feet more often? What? Why couldn't Death grasp the magnitude of her love? Maybe it was time to sink another ship? Bodies had always been her love language.

    Agatha pulled her wife to her, kissing her soundly. If she was sick, Rio would just have to get over the damn germs! Her marriage was at stake dammit! Fucking Wanda. Fucking stubborn ass Green Witch. She put what little energy she had into the kiss. Pulled and poured and burned Rio with everything she had. Thumbs brushed away tears she wasn't even aware she was crying. (At this point, she was dehydrated beyond a normal mortal's capacity.) "Lo siento, mi flor. He sido tonto. ¿Puedes perdonarme?" Death asked, butterfly kisses pressing to her face.

    "You're always forgiven no matter how silly you're being," Agatha laughed. She took a steadying breath as her vision swam. Her body wasn't going to hold out much longer, but she refused to fall asleep. Not again. Not after...

    "Let's get you back to the others," Rio told her. She wrapped an arm around her wife's waist and led her back to the living room. "If you insist on staying up, you should at least see if Wanda will give you a boost. You look like shit."

    Agatha rolled her eyes. "I'm fine." Like hell she was going to go near Wanda any time soon. Risk hurting her wife again? Not if she could help it. Then again... "You left without saying the Thing™," she huffed, crossing her arms. "I wasn't going to yell at you." Rio climbed over the back of the couch to run her fingers through the goddess' hair. "Well, someone was getting up close and personal with you again." Death separated the hair into two halves. "I didn't mean to take it out on you. I should have watched Nicky more closely." Agatha looked over at her dozing son. His cough had all but disappeared. The rouge in his cheeks had abated to a rosy pink. She guesstimated he'd be up and running around by the following day. Alice would need more time, but she hadn't woken up choking on her own phlegm again. "That was one time. I neglected his safety...well...a lot." She sunk into the couch cushions with a frown. That must have been why her son always kept a bundle of white flowers for himself and handed her the rest. He really had known for some time. "Rio...Do you think Nicky has green magic?"

    Death chuckled. "As if that wasn't extremely obvious by now, my love. But yes, it would seem so." She began to braid Agatha's hair, careful with her tugging. "He is, at the very least, immune to poisonous plants. But I've noticed that he has knowledge of plants I didn't teach him."

    "Well, don't look at me. I didn't learn my herbs until after he...y'know." Agatha shifted, clearing her throat. "Will you teach him?"

    Rio hummed in thought. "You're the mentor, Agatha."

    "Yeah and look how well that turned out. I can't even heal my own damn coven," she grit out. Panicking and crying when she should have been calm and collected. What kind of bullshit was that?

    "You did very good for your first time. Most skip steps and kill their patients. Don't beat yourself up, amor." Rio tied off the first braid with a vine and a lilac flower. She moved to the next section of hair, fingers checking for tangles. "Evanora would have never done this for you, so take solace in that. You'll always be better than that woman." Agatha smirked. "True. I hadn't thought of that. Hope that bitch is turning in her grave." Death laughed, waking Nicky. "What grave? We left her for the buzzards." "Mother, you came home," their son exclaimed. He scrambled across the couch to give her a hug. "I was looking for you."

    "See," Agatha told her, craning her neck to look at her wife.

    Rio smirked before leaning down to kiss her. "Nicky, your mama doesn't want to go mimis. Help me get her to take a nap."

    The boy jumped into her lap, Agatha's lungs emptying with a wheeze. "You need to sleep," he told her with a scowl. "Mother says so, so you gotta."

    "Excuse me? You're giving me orders?"

    Her son nodded. "If you don't go to sleep, I'm gonna go live with Billy." Nicky huffed. (Don't laugh. Don't laugh.) "By all means, move out. Just know that Billy snores and has stinky toes. You'll have to sleep in the closet with all his dirty socks and cahones." Nicky wrinkled his nose. "On second thought..."

    "Can you three go to another room?" Jen hissed. "Alice needs to rest." (Agatha made a note to look into those diuretic plants.)

    "Let's go lay in your bed, Mama. I wanna take a nap with you. Pleaseeeeeeeeeeeeeeeee." (Agatha, but her son had a pair of lungs on him now!)

    The goddess grumbled to herself as she struggled to sit up. She cleared her throat as it tickled with the effort. (Nope. Not sick. Agatha Harkness didn't get sick. Nope. Nope. Nope.) "Fine! But your mother has to come with us. She owes me a snuggle."

    "Yes!" Nicky jumped off the couch and ran towards the stairs.

    Rio helped her get up, brow creasing as Agatha cleared her throat a second time. (She was not fucking sick!) "If you want me to put Nicky in his own bed at any point..." Agatha gave her a look. "Much as I want to jump your actual bones and traumatize the fuck out of Jen and Wanda, I'm not going to pass up a chance for a group snuggle." Death nodded but sent a wink regardless. "You actually get some sleep, and I'll send the kids over to Rebecca's for the night. We can terrorize the coven as much as you want," she purred. The goddess fought a shiver. (From arousal! Stop! Don't look! Nooooooooo) "Behave," she chuckled. Agatha swallowed thickly (From. Arousal. Shut up! That's not a cold sweat.), "I call big spoon."

    "Any excuse to touch my ass," Rio laughed. "My offer still stands."

    "We'll see. Right now, we're gonna take a nap. Get on the bed."

    Rio flashed her a smirk. "Yes, ma'am!" She jumped onto the mattress, Nicky bouncing along the top with a giggle. "Querido, is it okay if I cuddle with you? Mama's gonna hug me." "Duh," he told her. "Mama missed you. She needs to hold you more."

    Agatha choked on her spit (from shock not...oh who the hell am I kidding at this point...). "Nicky," she laughed, cheeks warming. "I don't tell people when you're crying over a fish." "You were crying too, Mama. I know you like Nemo."

    Damn right, she did, but she didn't go around telling people that for good reason! "Close your eyes," she huffed. The huff triggered a cough. Agatha scowled at Rio's knowing look. "Don't," she warned. "I'm resting now. You can be smug later."

    Rio and Nicky got comfortable, their backs to Agatha. The goddess climbed onto the bed and snuck an arm under their heads. With her free hand, she pulled the blanket up and over them. Her throat began to itch in earnest.

    Chapter End Notes Y'all are a bunch of silly geese. I would never ever kill Nicky off.

    Teddy, on the other hand....

    We'll pick up with this sick fic tomorrow. Stay warm when you go outside. Drink teas. Don't touch giant hogweed. And most importantly!!!!
