    Chapter Summary A sick Agatha is a loopy Agatha. The coven isn't quite prepared for the things that come out of her mouth.

    Chapter Notes Will this be fluff? Will this be angst? Will this kill me because I refuse to get a healthy amount of sleep so I can post daily? Will this be comedic?

    Letssssss finnddddd ouhhhhttttttt!

    Normally, the chapter has a little nod to how I'm feeling/doing in the moment. Makes me wonder if my body knows I'm going to be sick soon. Hm....

    See the end of the chapter for more notes The Moon rose, ready to greet her beloved Earth once more. Only, this time, She felt hot. No, not hot. Hot was when the tap was turned up too high and you had to pull your hand away with a hiss. This was scorching. Like a raging wildfire eating everything in its path. Like the fucking Sun had been set in your hands and the flesh was sizzling away to a crisp. The Moon tried to move away, but the heat persisted. It chased her like a shadow. She couldn't reach her beloved. Couldn't scream. It was so hot. So hot. Sohotsohotsohotsohotsohotsohot "Get another towel," a voice said.

    The sound pierced her skull like a knitting needle to the frontal lobe. Agatha groaned, but the sound came out a strangled croak. Her throat felt like it had been stung by a million fire ants. Like she'd tried to swallow a cactus. When she opened her eyes, the world was too bright. (That fucking bitch named the Sun!!!) The goddess tried to roll over, but her body refused. Her joints ached and screamed and throbbed.

    "Cálmate, mi amor. Estoy aquí, vida mia." A hand brushed back sweat-soaked hair from her forehead. "Va a estar bien, mi corazón."

    Agatha couldn't get her eyes to open again. Couldn't lift her hand to find Rio's. A pitiful whine reached her muffled ears. She felt pathetic. Bedridden and helpless. Someone should have just drowned her in the bathtub already. Or pressed a pillow to her face and finished the job. Anything was better than this. Hell, the never-ending darkness and nothingness when she'd died the second time was nothing compared to the agony she was currently in. Agatha Harkness hadn't been sick since the Spanish Flu Pandemic of 1918. (It had been awful then, and it was awful now.) Those days, she had no coven to turn to. No healing witch to offer up even a single leaf or drop of tea. She would have died if a certain Green Witch had dropped her off on the curb near a hospital before disappearing again. (Rio had actually checked in on her regularly as a nurse, but Agatha had been too out of it to notice. Yes, yes. It was very sweet of Death.)

    She tried to sit up again as a coughing fit hit her. Her head swam as pressure built back up. The goddess felt her stomach roll as a dizzy spell took over. Hands helped turn her as she spit up bile on what she hoped was the floor. (The lack of splat said otherwise.) A cool cloth dabbed at the sides of her mouth, gentle and careful. Rio's handiwork if she knew anything about the cosmic entity. And given her position next to her, Agatha had likely covered her with her ick.

    "Ughhhhh," she croaked. "M'head."

    "I know, I know. Jen's making more tea for you," Death soothed. Fingers thumbed sweat and tears from the corners of her eyes. Always so gentle. Always so loving. "Would you like some soup? Nicky helped make it."

    The goddess wheezed before attempting to sit for a third time. Her son wasn't in bed with her!

    "Ah, ah," Rio chastised. She pushed the sickly witch back against the mountain of pillows. "He's fine. Everyone's fine."

    Agatha heard the sound of the towel be dipped into what had to be a bowl of water. The water trickled back down into the container as it was wrung out. She sighed as the cool fabric dabbed at her brow and cheeks. "Tir'd," she mumbled. It was an understatement, but the only word she could think of in the haze of her fever.

    "Go back to sleep, amor. I won't go anywhere."

    She pouted. "Truhhble..."

    "This is different. I can help you. You're not a mortal anymore," Rio chuckled. "Besides, I promised to burn the world for you. Think it's time I showed you just how much I meant it." Agatha coughed, her body tensing and relaxing rapidly. She groaned as the throbbing in her head increased. (The goddess vowed to find a cure for the flu, or whatever the hell it was she'd contracted, so she'd never have to feel like this again.) Her wife helped her to sip some water before pulling away to set the cup aside. Agatha licked her lips as sleep pulled her under once more.

    Nimble fingers picked at leaf after leaf. A row of stems sat on the counter to the boy's left. Nicholas sorted the green pads into useable and unusable for Jen. The witch was currently pouring over Mama's spell book as more tea was made. Her brows were furrowed as if she were confused.

    "What kind of remedies have you all used before?" he wondered aloud. Surely the potions witch didn't need a spell book to make a simple tea.

    Jen turned to face him, brows rising. "Uh...I usually go to the doctor's office. Since I'm a tad wanted, your mother...Agatha...didn't call one." She stirred a pot before facing him once more. "Are you feeling better?"

    The child nodded. "Mama worked really hard so I wouldn't cough anymore." The witch smiled sadly. "I know she did. It's very sweet of her." She wafted some steam towards her nose with a hum. "That should do it."

    Nicholas followed her movements, noting the color of the tea. It should have been a light goldenrod, but Jen's brew was more chartreuse. "It's too strong," he told her. "You need to make another batch."

    The woman blinked. "Are you sure?"

    He nodded. "There's too much yarrow. You'll make Mama's stomach upset." Jen dumped the tea out and moved back towards him in search of the right leaves. "If you knew all this green magic, why didn't you try a thing or two on yourself?" Nicholas pursed his lips lightly. (Mother always laughed and said he looked like Mama when he did.) "I always had a feeling it wouldn't help," he whispered. If his mothers heard, they'd be upset, and that was the last thing he wanted. "And I didn't want Mama to think Mother had taught me." The boy leaned closer. "Promise me you won't tell them. They'll get mad at each other again."

    "I'll do you one better. I'll make you a pinky promise," Jen told him. She extended her hand, pinky out. "I won't tell them if you don't tell them I almost made things worse." He giggled. "I'm gonna go check on them. Mama's never been sick before." "Put your mask on," she reminded him. "Or you Mother will have a field day torturing me." Nicholas tied the cloth around his face as he made his way upstairs. Already, he could hear his mama's coughing. It was odd, hearing that rattle in someone else's chest. For so long, she'd tried to soothe that sound. Now, she was the one needing soothing. It was weird. He stopped at her bedroom door and knocked. The boy waited for permission to enter; hands clasped behind his back as he rocked on his heels. (That was rule number one in the house. Always knock before entering any room his mothers might be in.)

    His mother opened the door with a smile. "Come to check on our sickly mother goose?" He nodded. "Is she feeling better?" Nicholas asked as he stepped into the room. His voice was muffled by the thick cloth. Modern concepts were still a bit hard for him to grasp. How were the layers of fabric supposed to keep the bad air out? He'd ask for clarification later. His mama, the tall, proud witch, had been reduced to a sweaty woman with a bright red complexion. Nicholas wouldn't have recognized her if it weren't for her hair. (He still didn't understand the white streak either, but that, too, could wait.) His mother held up a hand to stop him from getting any closer.

    "Let's not go through all of that again, okay? Your mama would beat me with a stick if you got sick again." Death returned to wiping the Divine Mother's face. (What was with his mama's coven and wanting to beat each other?)

    "How come you can't heal her?"

    His mother gave a tight smile. "I can heal her wounds, but not something like this. That's where green magic comes in. All those herbs and tinctures..." Death looked down at his mama before looking back over at him. "Would you...Do you want me to teach you what I know?"

    Nicholas grinned before remembering his mother couldn't see half of his face. "Yes, please!" The goddess shifted with a groan. She coughed weakly, eyes opening. "Nick...Nicky?" Mama reached out for him, her eyes squeezing shut.

    "He's here, amor," his mother soothed. Her voice was so soft. It reminded the boy of a steady river stream running over rocks.

    The bedroom door opened as a masked Wanda entered. "I've got tea for Agatha, and darker curtains for the room."

    Nicholas took the tea so the red head could put up the panels. At least the color was finally right. "Why am I so good at plants, Mother?"

    Death carefully poured droplets of tea into his mama's mouth. "I suppose you get that from me, querido. It certainly isn't from your mama," she said with a laugh. "Will I be able to grow things, too?"

    "Maybe. It's too soon. You're only starting to grow into your powers mijo." She set the mug aside as his mama mumbled something in her sleep.

    He twisted his small hands, standing on his tippy-toes to see over his mother's shoulder. The Divine Mother was still flushed and sweating profusely. "What if we tried a 'doctor's office'?" Death chuckled. "I'm not so sure that would be a good idea. Your mama is technically a wanted woman. That would put her in danger." She pressed the back of her hand to Mama's cheek. "You never can be a little sick, can you?"

    His mama jerked upwards, but never fully left the pillows. She coughed a terribly wet sounding cough. He jumped back, eyes widening. Mama's coughs sounded scarier than Alice's had. And now...now his mama was crying from the pain. Nicholas didn't like it. Wished he were still the sick one, so her body didn't hurt her.

    "Take him downstairs," his mother hissed. "He doesn't need to see this." The goddess wheezed in a breath, the sound sending a chill down his spine. "No. Let me help," he told Death. "I don't wanna go. She needs me."

    "Nicky, you can't get sick again," Wanda told him gently. She moved to take his hand, but he pulled away. "Nicky..."

    "I'm gonna stay," the child said, tears wetting his mask. "She asked me to stay. I have to, now."

    His mother let out a sigh. "Go downstairs, querido. I will take care of Mama. I won't let anything happen to her."

    Nicholas shook. He wanted to argue with the women, but in the end, his sickly mama terrified him. Nicholas couldn't get the sight out of his head. Couldn't get the sound of her pained whines out of his ears. He turned and bolted from the room.

    Rio looked out the window of Agatha's room with a sigh. The moon had risen, but it had dulled like there was a cloud blocking its brilliance. She rolled her shoulders before dabbing at her wife's face for the millionth time. Her beloved witch wheezed and snored in her sleep. The new sheets would need to be tossed. They reeked of sweat and sickness. "How is she?" Alice asked from the doorway. The goth had mostly recovered, but she retained her paleness. Jen had worked hard to finish what Agatha had started. They would all need to thank the goddess for her efforts.

    "Worse," she told the witch. "None of Jen's teas or the cough syrup are working. Might need to see if Billy can make a run for the other gunk."

    "I can give him a call. Anything in particular?"

    Death shrugged. "Tell him to go crazy. Wanda will pay him back. I'll try anything at this point."

    What the others didn't know was that Agatha's immune system had significantly weakened with her new position. She couldn't die like a mortal, so the virus continued to grow and grow and grow in her body. She could run a fever all she wanted, but viruses were known for their adaptability. And since she couldn't die and the virus continued to grow, Agatha was forced to endure the full extent of whatever virus she happened to catch.

    Rio had no doubt in her mind this was a ploy initiated by the Ancient Ones. A way to keep the sociopathic witch in check. They would continue to punish Agatha as long as she existed. It disgusted the cosmic entity, but there was little she could do. They had more power than her. Couldn't kill her, no, but they could easily revoke her wife's immortality. Could send Agatha back into that nowhere and nothingness to torture the witch that way. "Billy said he'll be here in an hour. Jeff made a soup for her. Also, his parents asked if you wanted to do dinner again," the goth relayed.

    Agatha's eyes shot open, glassy and unfocused. "No, I've never ridden a horse. The damn things are ugly," the woman croaked.

    "Okay..." Rio waved her hand in front of her wife's face. "Run that by me again." "You smell like shit."

    Alice laughed from the hall. "I'm...I'm gonna go see about a midnight snack." She closed the door behind her, her soft footsteps growing softer.

    "Amor, can you hear me?" She poked the goddess in the shoulder.

    Blue eyes swiveled around the room unsteadily. "There are so many snakes in my fingers." "I think those are veins and arteries, my love." Rio took a breath before projecting herself into her wife's mind.

    Once securely inside, there were a jumble of people and things just all over the place. "Ah...a fever dream," she purred. "An acid trip without the acid. Always fun until you walk off a building." Death walked around in search of Agatha's main core of consciousness. It wasn't hard to find her wife amidst the chaos. The Green Witch grinned, eyes raking over the figure. "Whoa! Watch out there, cowboy," she laughed.

    A version of Agatha whipped around; a gallon hat nestled on her head. (It was doing delicious, torturous things for the cosmic entity. She'd suggest a little roleplay once her wife was better.) "I reckon you must be Dead Eye Dixie. You're notorious 'round the parts, partner."

    Rio laughed to herself with a nod. "Okay. I'm game. Not like we haven't done this dance before." She changed her appearance to a bandit in white. (The true color of villains back in the day, just so you know!) "How ever did you come by such a gun?" she purred. "They said you'd hung up your holsters, Sheriff."

    The gun in question was actually an item phallic in nature. (Purple, of course.) Something Death hadn't had the pleasure of seeing since before Agatha found the Darkhold. Agatha had actually thrown it at her head a week before their final fight. It was somewhere in their cabin, tucked away for safekeeping. She liked the inside of her cheek as Agatha stroked the length with her left hand. Blue eyes burned into her.

    "Heard you were a-comin', Dixie. I didn't wanna let you down." (As if a strap-wielding Agatha could ever let her or anyone down.)

    A tumbleweed made of wriggling goldfish bounced wetly across the ground. Nicky, with a cartoonish mustached, stood between them. He held a banana in his hand and aimed it at the sky. He fired(?) the fruit into the air, syrup raining down on the two. Rio furrowed her brows. "I think we've lost the plot, Agatha. Let's change the scene already." "You forfeitin', old gal? I never thought I'd see the day," Sheriff Agatha laughed. "Tuckin' that tail 'tween your legs like the yellow-bellied dog that you are."

    "Now you're just being mean. I thought we were having fun," Death chuckled. "Don't you think a fight between lovers is more interesting?" Her eyes dropped back to the 'gun' with a salacious grin.

    The goddess' brain accepted the suggestion, grass sprouting. Soon, they found themselves standing in a field. Agatha was dressed like the nurse from Kill Bill with a comically large syringe in one hand. Rio was...what in the actual fuck!

    Death growled. "Why am I Bill? I'm better than Bill. Bill was a jealous...Oh, I get it now." She lowered into a fighting stance, her dagger now a long samurai blade. (It looked pretty damn good, if she was being honest. They both were learning some things today.) "Wait, why are you attacking me? Bill and Patchy never had a fight in the movies." "Time for your medicine," Agatha hissed.

    Rio, where are you? I've got Agatha's medicine, Billy sent her telepathically. "Gotta take a rain check on that penetration, sweetheart." Death slipped out before the needle could pierce her skin.

    Agatha mumbled incoherently, hands twitching at her sides. At least her mind was keeping her entertained.

    "Send him up, but stay in the hallway," she shouted to the rest of the coven. Billy made his way to her, a bundle of plastic bags in his hands. He gave her a grin with his eyes, the rest of his face covered with a mask. "Dad suggested giving her Robitussin since it sounds like bronchitis." The teen passed over the medicine. "If it keeps getting worse, you might need to take her to the hospital."

    Yeah, like that was going to happen! "Thanks, Billy. Wash your hands before touching your face. She's pretty sick. That virus is partying it up in her lungs."

    He laughed. "Time to kick those germs out."

    Death made a face. "You do know germs, viruses, and bacteria are all different, right?" The boy blinked at her.

    "Goodnight, Billy." She moved to close the door. A foot stopped it from closing. "Can I see her?"

    "You'd have to hose yourself down in disinfectant before you can go into your own home," she warned him. Rio sighed as he shrugged. "Make it quick. She's stewing in her own filth." "She looks terrible," he exclaimed. "You have to take her to the hospital!" "Hey! Cut that shit out before your magic fucks with her a third time." She removed the plastic sealing the bottle of thick syrup. Agatha was going to hate her for this. "She looks like she's dying, Rio!"

    "Technically, she is." Death hissed as the dosage cap fell to the floor. "Who designed this crap?"

    Agatha blinked, eyes settling on Billy. "You seen Dead Eye Dixie, Boy?" "Who?"

    "That's me," she explained. "She's having a fever dream. Looks real fun in her head. Don't go in there!"

    Billy raised his hands in self-defense. "I wasn't going to. Not after all those freaky things Jen and the others showed me from her memories."

    She had missed that bit. "Well, still, you have a habit of touching things." Agatha grabbed the bottle from her hands, the syrup sloshing. "Thought you could start without me, huh, Hot Stuff? I've never met a squid that could outdrink me." "No, don't-!"

    The goddess was already chugging the bottle. Billy grimaced. "That's the strongest kind..." "So?" Rio stole the bottle back, wrinkling her nose at the putrid stench of chemicals and pollutant plastic. "I'm sure she'll be fine."

    "You ever heard of 'robotripping?' Because she's about to be, and there's gonna be a lot of vomit," the teen informed. He dragged a trash can over. "I'm just...I'm just gonna bounce. Best of luck with all this. Bye!" Billy bolted from the room. "Guys, Agatha's about to be super crazy. Might want to put some plastic down," she heard him yell. Surely not. How bad could things get?

    Death narrowed her eyes as Agatha scrambled towards the fridge. She was...awake...but definitely not aware of her actions. The goddess was now chugging a half gallon of milk. She wore a robe, the purple and floral one Rio loved so much, but the damn thing wasn't tied shut. That would be fine if Wanda wasn't living under the same roof. If only she could get Agatha to keep the robe closed, everything would be okay. But she wouldn't because she was stubborn and insisted on irritating her.

    "Okay, Nicky and Tommy are hidden away in Nicky's room. And...Whoa! Girl, put that thing away," Jen shouted. She slapped a hand over her eyes as Agatha slipped her robe off to find something new to drink.

    "I'd laugh if this weren't so sad. She should be climbing me right now," Rio said, head tilting to the side. "When did we stock up on dark liquor?"

    "That's mine!" Wanda ran over before sliding to a stop in her socked feet. "Agatha, put my whiskey down!"

    "Oh crap..." Alice turned to face the others. "You said she took Robitussin, right?" Rio shrugged. "Yeah, why?"

    "Alcohol and Robitussin can't be mixed," the goth squeaked. "No, no, no, no, no!" Alice grabbed the sides of her head, likely remembering how Sharon had died. The Green Witch laughed. "Oh, we're about to have a lot of fun," she purred. Drunk Agatha was always a hoot. Especially once the clothes came off and her tongue loosened. Agatha hissed as Wanda tried to steal the bottle from her. "You don't even have a penguin; you damn dirty leprechaun!" The goddess hissed at her as if she were a cat. "I'm taking the kids to the movies," Jen sighed. "I don't want to be here for whatever this is." "Can I come?" Alice asked, eyes wide and hopeful. She yelped as the goddess brushed past her.

    "Hey~," Agatha breathed. She fluttered her lashes at Rio, cheeks bright red as she stumbled over. "Is that a grin on your face or are ya just happy to see me, sailor?" Rio grinned wider. "You should all go to the movies."

    Wanda huffed. "She's sick, Rio. The two of you can't do anything."

    Death wrinkled her nose at the insinuation. "My wife's agency is far more important to me than sex, Maximoff. I also happen to care about the things she might say or do around all of you. Those two wanted to torture her the last time she was in a similar situation," she said, pointing to Jen and Alice. "And you're the one who fucked her over the most." The red head threw her hands up. "I was doing what was best for the world. She was mad with power!"

    "Agatha was never insane," Rio argued. (After all, her wife was the only one who had owned the book for the longest outside of its creator.) She felt hands tickling her sides as Agatha moved to stand behind her and sniff her hair. "Feeling better, sweetheart?" Agatha moaned. "I want to sit on your face and fuck the shit out of you," the younger immortal hissed aggressively.

    "See, that's the shit I don't want to hear," Jen told the cosmic entity. She made a face as Agatha pawed at Death.

    Rio swatted the hands away. "You guys suck," she growled. "Alice threw up all over her five times. Five." Rio hugged her naked wife, a hand stroking a cheek. "And she did a lot for all of you just for you to abandon her in her time of need." (She didn't really need their help; she just wanted them to suffer for getting her wife sick.)

    Alice mumbled a sorry before picking Agatha's robe up from the floor. "Here you go, Ags." "You'll never take me alive!" The woman ran from the kitchen, hands waving in the air. Jen watched Agatha run out with a twitching eye. Finally, she groaned and stomped a foot. "I'm only helping you because no one ever thought to take care of her when she needed them."

    Rio hummed. That was the last thing she expected from the potions witch. But she'd never made an effort to talk to Jen before, so that was more on her than the mortal. Death made a mental note to look into the woman a bit. Agatha had left Jen alone, so there must have been something about the witch. She turned away to sift through the fridge. If she knew her wife (which, of course, she did) then the woman was going to want some soup. (Agatha always insisted on soup for cold weather.)

    "What do you want me to do?" Wanda asked. She hadn't chased after her wife like the other two had. "Do I need to help wrangle her back over here?"

    The Green Witch threw a glare over her shoulder. "Like hell you're touching my wife!" She kicked the fridge door shut as she pulled out a bowl of left-over soup. "You can take care of the kids, unless you're going to try and steal my son too."

    "Rio," the Scarlet Witch groaned. "I'm not trying to steal anybody from you! I didn't even want to kiss her, but we didn't have a choice."

    The bowl plopped to the floor, juice spraying everywhere. "WWWHHHAAATTT!!!" Wanda paled. "...Oh shit..." She bolted from the room.

    "Get back here!

    In the living room, Agatha jumped around on the couch, still as naked as the day she was born. Jen and Alice were trying to convince her to sit down and, "Please put some fucking pants on!"

    "I'm not gonna kill you," Rio cackled as she chased the red head down. "I'm just gonna torture you for a couple of decades. That's all."

    Agatha caught a glimpse of her wife and bounded over as if her lungs weren't completely fucked. The rattle-y wheeze underscored the mayhem in the house. "Murder? Let's go kill a bunch of Avengers," the woman laughed.

    Jen tackled the goddess to the ground, wrapping a comforter around Agatha. "Get the belts," she yelled to Alice.

    "You're not tying her up," Rio growled. She pulled out her dagger. "Wanna see how well that ends?"

    Jen glared up at her as Agatha wiggled violently. "Your son could come down here at any minute. Do you really want him to start asking questions about his mother's body?" Death scowled. Why did she have to make a good point? Why did the coven hate fun? But, unfortunately, her and Agatha weren't ready to talk about sex with the child. Limbs would be left untouched this woeful day. "Fine," she bit out. "But you're not tying her up. Just help me get her back to the room."

    Alice scoffed. "I'm sure you could convince her pretty easily if you just flashed her a tit or something."

    Agatha grumbled incoherently as she struggled to roll over in the blanket. "We're takin' tits out now?" She locked eyes with Rio, blue turning black. "Dead Eye Dixie, we meet again," the goddess said in an overdramatic southern drawl.

    Rio laughed, shaking her head. "Come on, Sheriff. Let's get you back in bed. You can handcuff me or whatever kinky thing you're into." She bent down and tugged her wife to her feet. "Keep that on, or I'm running."

    "Whatever you say, Hot Stuff," Agatha laughed, voice changing to a high-toned suburban housewife's. "Must have skipped supper 'cause this Mama's ready for dessert." "Where's Billy with his poisoned wine when you need it?" Jen groaned. "Go, already!" "Don't worry. I got that recorded in case she ever tries anything," Alice whispered. Rio shot the goth a look. "Don't abuse that power, or I'll bring that demon back." She tugged her wife along, sending a glare in Wanda's direction.

    Agatha stretched with a yawn. Her limbs were sore in all the wrong ways. Hair stuck out in all directions. She smacked her lips, mouth dry as a bone. Her room, once organized and pristine, was now the remains of a battlefield. Medicine bottles, tissues, clothes, pillows, blankets, books...everything, really, were strewn about. She sneered at the disaster. So much for having the favor returned.

    The witch pulled on her favorite robe before descending the stairs. The sun was out (damn annoying thing) and shining brightly. Agatha glared at the orange glow. The rest of her house, at least, was in much better shape. The tv was on, playing some cockamamie show about bimbos, broads, and baby-faced nobodies. Unsurprisingly, the viewers were none other than Jen and Alice. What was surprising was what the two were doing instead of watching the show. Agatha snuck forward, a smirk growing the closer she got.

    "Now, I know coven members love each other, but I don't think this is what they had in mind when they said 'sisterhood' of the craft," the goddess laughed.

    The goth and femme broke apart with shocked gasps. Their reaction only amused Agatha further.

    "Don't stop on my behalf," she told them. "You got to watch my wife and I. It's only fair I get to watch, too."

    Jen threw a pillow at her face. "You're supposed to be in bed dying," she grumbled. "Pretty sure I did at some point," Agatha said, shrugging. "I sorta blacked out at one point and don't know what happened."

    Alice chuckled. "You don't remember chasing Rio out of the room with a flogger in your hand?" She hid her face as she began to laugh harder. "You...you...haha...You screamed..." Jen started laughing with her girlfriend(?). "Oh, yeah!" She smirked at Agatha. "You screamed, and I quote, 'Mrs. Clause wants to feed you a carrot,' before throwing a book at her."

    Agatha stared at the two as she fought off a blush. Whelp! I'm setting the house on fire tonight. I wonder if Nicky and Tommy would like to move back to Massachusetts... She cleared her throat, shaking her hair back from her face. "Well...was my aim true?" The pair roared with laughter, holding each other.

    "Does the bump on my head answer your question?"

    Agatha rushed over to the kitchen where her wife was making..."Soup," she gasped. And not just any soup, no no. It was asopao de camarones! Agatha hadn't had the dish since the last time her and Rio had lived together. She didn't need to be told that the shrimp and cilantro were fresh. Her wife would never use frozen or freeze-dried. Agatha pulled her wife in for a kiss before remembering just how gross she was. "Eugh. I bet I smell awful," she groaned. Death bumped noses, chuckling lightly. "It'll take more than that to keep me from kissing you, sweetheart. Are you feeling better?"

    Agatha rolled her neck, popping a few cervical joints in the process. "Y'know, I'm not sure. It sounds, and looks, like I might have been possessed, not sick."

    Rio grinned. "I wondered the same thing for a moment. But apparently that's what happens when you mix alcohol and drugs, so..." She pulled away to put some of the stew into a bowl. "I'm just glad you're not hurting anymore."

    The goddess remembered the gentle touches, the soothing whispers, and looked away before her own heart could choke her. "Yeah, that shit was not fun. Where's Nicky?" "Wanda took him and Tommy out for to walk around a store for a bit. She won't let me stab her."

    Agatha rolled her eyes. "What happened this time?"

    Rio fixed her with a look. "I don't know, Agatha. You tell me."

    What the hell did I do, she wanted to scream. Instead, she held back her temper and moved to take her bowl from her wife. "I don't like that tone," Agatha said evenly. "Tell me what it is you're accusing me of, and we'll go from there."

    Death pressed her against the island, a hand gripping at her hip. "You. Kissed. Wanda." Oh.....fuck!

    I heard that! Rio pulled away in a huff. She began to throw dishes in the sink. You said you only loved me!

    Agatha ignored the rumbling of her stomach and walked over to her wife. Goddamnit, Rio. Don't start this shit again. I do love you. Only you. I kissed Wanda because I needed magic while we were stuck in my memories. We didn't know what would happen if I got too weak. So you kissed her!? There are other ways to take magic, Agatha.

    The goddess cupped Rio's face, staring her down. My love, Wanda couldn't use her magic in my head. It's a protected space, remember? You helped me set up protections for my mind. Wanda couldn't hit me with her magic, so I had to pull it out the least sexual way I could. Her wife stilled. Her little 'oh yeah' face would have been adorable if Death hadn't been two seconds from leaving her again. I forgot...

    Agatha laughed as she pulled Rio in a for a hug. "You do that a lot when I'm in danger. Should I get you a notepad and a pen?"

    Rio relaxed, fingers digging into her back. "So, you didn't enjoy kissing Wanda?" The goddess couldn't help herself. "I didn't say that," she teased.

    Death growled. "That's it!" She grabbed Agatha and threw her over a shoulder. "No, my stew!" The younger immortal magicked the bowl to follow them up the stairs. She caught a glimpse of her smirking coven before sending them a wink. "I bet you Wanda would have let me feed her my carrot."

    Rio threw her on the bed and slammed the door shut. She pulled out her dagger. "Okay, Agatha. I'll play."

    It was a good thing the sheets were already slated to be thrown.

    See the end of the chapter for more notes Rio leaned forward, eyes narrowing. She watched the body on the bed as it lay still as a corpse. "Why does he have alarms if he never wakes up on time?"

    Agatha shrugged, nose wrinkling. She wagged her fingers at a wall. "I want to know where he finds the money to buy all of these posters. I mean...what the hell are half these people wearing?"

    Death chuckled. "Those are my little friends," she purred. "They love to sing me songs and feed me their tears and teenage angst."

    The Divine Mother reached for a poster of a goth woman, a sneer twisting her lips. "This bitch ever comes near you, and I'll make sure she wishes she was imaginary." Billy groaned as he rolled over. He lifted his head with narrowed eyes. "Who...Rio? Agatha?" He rubbed an eye with a frown. "How did you get in my house?"

    Rio chuckled. "We're two beings not defined by this realm and you're asking how we got in?" (Why was he the Demiurge again?) She sent a small puff of air at his face, watching his curls dance.

    "I killed your parents on the way to work and used their keys to let us in," Agatha told the teen with a straight face.

    Rio licked the inside of her cheek, eyes darkening. She loved it when her wife talked dirty. "You're going to be late."

    Billy poorly threw a pillow at her face. "There's no school today," he grumbled. "It's Saturday."

    Agatha laughed. "Good to see the untimely demise of your mortal parents doesn't hinder your desire for five more minutes." She picked the pillow up and gripped it as if she were going to smother him. The goddess released it. She chuckled as it bounced off his head. "That, and it's not Saturday. I changed the dates on your phone," Death informed with a grin. The Maximoff was quick to Google the actual date. "What the hell, Rio? I could have been late."

    She snickered to herself as Agatha ripped the blankets off the bed. "Up and at 'em, Billy Boy. Big day ahead of you. School, Teddy, Coven Day tomorrow. Need to make sure your brain is big and strong for the lessons I have planned."

    The teen yelped. "What if I had been naked?"

    "Billy, I wiped the shit that crawled up your back and I was a ghost who haunted this very room daily," the Divine Mother reminded. "There's nothing about you that could surprise me."

    Rio took her knife out to carve more runes into the foot of the teen's bed. "Different body now, sweetheart. That's not the same tuchus."

    "You know Yiddish?" Billy asked.

    "I know every language," Death told him. She pointed her dagger at him. "You gonna get up, or do we need to go get Jeff and Rebecca?"

    "I'm up, I'm up!" The Demiurge rolled out of bed with a grumble.

    "Come on," she told her wife. "You can steal Billy's breakfast. He never has time to eat. Rebecca will appreciate not having to eat it all by herself."

    Agatha chuckled. "Made yourself pretty comfy with this lot, have we?" She pursed her lips. "You better not cozy up to another woman, Vidal."

    Rio shrugged. "They're not so bad once you get to know them. Jeff likes to garden. Rebecca has a good joke here and there."

    "Ah, that's why you're buddy buddy with them!" Agatha waited at the foot of the stairs for Rio to reach her. She offered an arm, lips curling upwards.

    Death hooked her arm around Agatha's before leading her to the kitchen. "Morning," she greeted the mortals simply.

    Rebecca looked up from her newspaper with a smile. It twitched downwards as she caught sight of Agatha. "Good...morning..."

    Rio watched the two women size each other up. This was the first time they'd seen each other since Agatha had gotten her body back. From the looks of things, the two were still at odds with one another. If only Death ate food for fun. She'd have a bag of popcorn for the show. Instead, she sat back with Jeff, a smirk on her lips.

    "Rebecca," Agatha said, an air of superiority surrounding her.

    "Agatha," Rebecca responded, not backing down. "You're looking well. Billy said you looked a like a drowned rat the other day."

    The goddess huffed. "Glad to know he was enjoying my suffering." She pulled a face before sighing. "I...appreciate you two helping while I was...indisposed. Unfortunately, I don't remember eating any soup, and Rio spilt the last of it in a jealous rage." Rio stuck her tongue out at her wife. "Be glad I didn't shove it down her throat." Or pour its boiling contents into another orifice. Oh, medieval torture methods...How Rio missed them so.

    Jeff chuckled. "Still having issues with Wanda?"

    Agatha gave her a look. Friends with a man and you're gossiping with one too? "Aggie dearest kissed her," Death said with a faux pout. "I was very shocked and deeply hurt."

    Rebecca's eyebrows shot up. "That's a very serious betrayal..."

    "You kissed my mother!?"

    Whoops! Billy wasn't supposed to know that bit. Death mentally kicked herself. Things were bound to get heated now. "It was for survival," Rio was quick to add. "Nobody cheated on anybody."

    The teen glared at Agatha. "How is kissing a survival tactic?"

    "Billy, you don't really want to have this conversation right now," the goddess sighed. "You've got school, and I'm not in the mood to explain how it's your fault." Rio nodded her head in the direction of the door. "Go on. You two can argue about the logistics later."

    "You never hold her accountable," she heard him grumble. The front door slammed shut. Death crossed her arms, a frown settling over her features. Why did he have to pick at the one insecurity she had? Had Rio been mad at Agatha? Yes. But at the end of the day, her wife had no other choice. They'd discussed what happened and why. They'd handled it and made up spectacularly. Rio held no ill will toward her wife. The last thing she wanted was for Billy to have another reason to distrust his other mother. Things were still tense after he sent her into her own head. (A part of her wondered if he'd accidentally magicked them all sick so he could have a reason not to visit.)

    "Earth to Rio," Agatha whispered in her ear. "They're asking you a question." "No, I didn't put that dead bird in his locker. That was another green witch," Rio sighed. "What? No," Jeff laughed. "We wanted to know if you wanted to do dinner again. It went so well last time. We just thought, if you both would like to, we could do it again." He wrapped an arm around Rebecca with a dopey grin.

    "I'll see what I can do. Agatha will certainly go regardless."

    The goddess shot her a look. "What if I'm busy that day?"

    Rio laughed. "Yeah. Sure. Busy." She eyed her wife. "There'll be wine~." Agatha pursed her lips. "...What kind?" she asked, shaking her head lightly in that way that always proved her interest.

    "Oh, whatever you want, sweetheart," Rio purred. "We've got a bottle from Versailles stashed at home home."

    Jeff's eyes bulged. "How do you have wine from France?"

    "Straight from the French Revolution," Agatha groaned, biting her lip. "We've been saving it for a special occasion, haven't we?"

    "Look, I'll put a dress on if that's what it takes to get a look at that bottle," Jeff told them, practically salivating. "We'll even kick Billy out of the house."

    Agatha laughed loudly, head tipping back. "Now, there's an idea!" She elbowed Rio. "I'll move my schedule around. You get the bottle. Who knows? It might be fun." Rio grinned. "We'll keep the boy. He's entertaining. What day were you two thinking?" Rebecca turned to face Death. (Funny how she found the cosmic entity more relatable than the formal mortal woman.) "What about tomorrow? After Coven Day? Billy can drive you two here."

    The Green Witch hummed, thinking. "Souds doable. But I'll have to be gone by the witching hour. So many bodies pop up around that time." Rio moaned at the thought. Alcohol and vehicles and mortals. The perfect triple threat.

    A paper dropped from the heavens in a pastel purple haze. It floated to the floor before snuffing itself out.

    Death sucked in a breath, pulling back from it. She knew a summons when she saw one. The fact they hadn't been yanked to that hellhole meant they were in deep shit. "What is that?" Rebecca asked. She moved to pick it up.

    "Don't touch it!" Rio used a gust of air to keep the mortals from the glittering paper. "Your flesh is weak."

    Agatha eyed her, mouth falling open. "What is it?" She bent down to pick it up. " 'Your presence is requested'...What does that mean?"

    "Who's it addressed to?" Rio asked. Please don't be Agatha. Please don't be Agatha. The goddess turned it over, lips pursing. Agatha looked up slowly. "Says it's for both of us." She passed the note over to Rio.

    Death sneered at the cursive. Agatha Harkness and Lady Death scrawled in that perfect, manicured way. They were pissed at them. "Send a message to Jen. We'll be gone for a while."

    Agatha watched her wife closely, a knot forming in her stomach. Rio was twitchy. Rio was tense. Rio was scared. It wasn't something she was used to seeing. Death was an unkillable, chaotic, and violent being. Death was feared. Death did not fear. Yet here they were, apprehensively waiting in the Ancient One's temple with Rio a ball of manic energy. Agatha tried to hold her hand, to offer some comfort, only for her wife to pull away. Not here. Not now, Rio told her telepathically. The Green Witch pulled her shroud up, features shifting, as five robed figures entered.

    The goddess chose her most comfortable mask. (If Rio felt she needed one, then Agatha would prepare accordingly.) She plastered on a grin as the Ancient Ones took their seats. "Well, hey guys! What's shakin'?"

    Stevie held up a hand, silencing her. "Agatha," she greeted. "Lady Death." Agatha curtsied, robe sleeves sweeping along the ground. "It's been a while. I haven't seen you since Coachella. You stole my jacket."

    Dolly drummed her acrylics along the tabletop. "Another day," she instructed. "You're supposed to be keeping Lady Death in check. Instead, you've got her running around even more than before. Not to mention the fact that you two have been interfering with mortals." The couple shared a look.

    "What mortals? Rio never directly helped me with a single person." It was a technicality, but it had to count for something. Rio had made sure not to touch a thing. Frida pulled out a list. It wasn't very long. The page was the size of a stencil notepad's. Still, the fact they had a list didn't bode well. "Lady Death, did you or did you not use your powers to slow time so the Demiurge could reach his school on time?"

    Agatha quirked a brow. "You want to pitch a fit over that? Come on, guys! That's a load of horseshit. It doesn't drastically change anything!"

    Death ignored her and nodded. "I did."

    "And you ignored your duties to tend to sick mortals, as well as Agatha?" "Frida, baby, that doesn't count," Agatha argued. "She didn't help me with anything. I should know. I was fucking there!" What were these women on about? No wonder Rio hated visiting them. They looked for any reason to shit on her. So a couple of souls had to wait. Who the fuck cares?

    Stevie leaned her chin on a fist. The rock legend didn't seem amused with her outburst. She looked between the couple before settling her gaze back on the cosmic entity. "You also abandoned your duties to help the Demiurge undo a faulty spell. Over 300,000 souls were put at risk of becoming Lost and Vengeful. Then, there's the matter of..." The woman faced Agatha. "...your son, Nicholas."

    The goddess bristled. "What about our son?"

    "There was a very good reason he wasn't meant to survive his birth," the head of the group told her. "We can't have two death magic wielders. Especially not in the hands of a child." Stevie sat up straight and clasped her hands together. It all felt very business-like. Agatha bared her teeth. "Oh, but it's fine to give god-like powers to a teenager who can't control his emotions? I think all those concerts have finally fried your brain. Are you even listening to yourself?"

    "The Demiurge is something of the Universe. He is not our prerogative. A mortal soul with abilities that belong solely to Lady Death is. You must bind his magic." Agatha felt a chill. "What did you just say?"

    "Come on, darling," Eartha purred. "We both know it's for the best. No child should have that power. She knows it, too." Eartha pointed to Rio.

    Death clenched her jaw. We'll talk later, she promised. Just tell them you will. Don't make things worse for him.

    Why the hell are you backing down? This is our son we're talking about! He deserves to have his magic, she threw back.

    "I don't know what you're telling our fair Lady, but it won't make a difference," Betty huffed. "It's just a miracle she's being so well-behaved this time. We were hoping for something more dramatic."

    Agatha snapped her face back in the panel's direction. "What do you mean 'this time?' What happened last time?"

    Dolly laughed sharply. She slapped the table as she sucked in a breath. "Oh, darlin', she must not have told you. That's sweet." She leaned forward to share a look with Betty. "I guess I owe you a few realms after all."

    Agatha stomped her foot, the ground shaking. "What. Happened. Last. Time!" Frida snapped her fingers. "Now, now, sweet thing. Let's not start all of that." The goddess found herself frozen in place. She tried to tell the group off, but her jaw remained shut. Agatha fought off the rising panic. It was like Wanda's spell all over again. Her lungs refused to draw another breath. Her heart stilled. She was suspended in time. "Leave her alone," Rio roared. "It's not her fault. She's still new."

    "Then you should have told her how things work around here," Eartha sneered. "You know how rash your plaything can be."

    "You're the ones who made her an immortal. You should have let her know what she was getting herself into," Death reasoned.

    Stevie quirked a brow, clearly bored. "Would it have mattered? You two never listen. You two never learn. You insisted on 'marrying' a mortal. You insisted on impregnating her. You insisted on granting her spawn time. Now, you're insisting we just let you two run around to do as you please? We have been lenient enough, Lady Death."

    Frida snapped again, returning Agatha's mobility. "Just bind the boy and all will be well. We're not asking much. lovely."

    Agatha fumed, face reddening. "Like hell I will!" She held her ground, not at all a coward in the moment. "And you're going to back the fuck off and leave my wife alone! She's followed all of your stupid fucking rules."

    "Followed?" Frida laughed. The others joined her as if they'd heard the funniest joke. No, like they were looking at a joke wrapped in purple. "Lady Death has broken nearly all cosmic rules for love of you, Agatha Harkness. Even at the expense of her own sanity, she has dared to challenge this court. Punishing her directly didn't seem to work, though. I suppose that's why she never told you about the boy."

    Rio stepped between her wife and superiors. "Punish me for my crimes, but don't you dare drag her into this." She turned around, hands cupping Agatha's cheeks. "Look, I'll just be a bit busier. It might be a while, but I'll come back once things have settled. We'll-" "Lady Death, you've shown your hand too soon again," Dolly laughed. "Was the boy not lesson enough? Shall we enlighten our third-party?"

    "I said I'll take your stupid fucking punishment," Rio growled. "Agatha will focus on training the Demiurge and Scarlet Witch. Nicky will have his powers bound. What more do you want?"

    "Respect," Stevie answered firmly. "We've not had it for some time." She looked towards the other ladies before nodding. "Agatha is still new, so her punishment will be light. And, knowing you, her punishment will hurt you just as much. We will discuss the boy further, but for now, his powers must be bound. Dolly, if you will."

    "With pleasure," the woman purred. "Hold still, darlin'. This'll only hurt a bit." Agatha gasped as her very being was yanked towards the group. Her mortal like bits burned. Her heart pounded in her ears.

    In the blink of an eye, Agatha found herself sitting behind the table. Now, only Rio stood before the panel. She looked around as far as her eyes would let her. The other Ancient Ones had pulled their hoods up, the room tense.

    "You must leave the mortal alone," Betty told her wife. "She would have died had you not interfered."

    "It was not my intention, Your Eminence," Rio reasoned. "She pulled at the magic around me. I never purposely healed her."

    "Maybe not, but you hang around her too much. The mortals will notice. Her mother has tried too many times to end her life, just for her to live." Stevie waved her away. "This is your only warning."

    Agatha felt lightheaded as the room spun. Once again, Rio stood before the panel, alone and quiet. She tried to reach towards her wife, but the goddess could do nothing outside of viewing the memories. Who's? She wasn't quite sure. Agatha was no longer sitting in the center of the table, so it was likely all of theirs over the course of time. "Lady Death," Frida began. "For what reason have you been training the mortal? For what reason did you reveal yourself to her mother?"

    Rio raised her head. Her hazel eyes never wavered, but there was a sharpness to them. "I have a duty of care, Your Eminence. Agatha Harkness is my soul to nurture." Eartha scoffed. "One mortal's promise does not make another your property. Disillusion yourself of this notion. She still belongs to the Mortal Realm. She will still die one day. You are not permitted to teach her further."

    "Reconsider, Your Eminence. Agatha could be a great leader. Her powers are unlike any other witch's. With her, witchkind can usher in a new era of magic."

    "Agatha Harkness is not destined to save witchkind," Betty told the entity. "Her magic and her soul are not meant for the light. Leave her be."

    Agatha had little time to react as Rio stepped forward. "There is good in her. She wishes to be good. Mortals are under my jurisdiction and I-"

    "Incorrect, Lady Death. Mortals belong to us. You are simply a ferryman for their souls," Stevie interrupted. "If you pursue the mortal, there will be consequences." Death glared at the woman. "I will not stop teaching her. She has a right to learn the craft. Why must she suffer?"

    "It makes for good entertainment," Frida laughed. "They can't all have wonder lives, Lady Death. Such is life."

    Agatha felt sick. She hadn't loved the women on the panel. She hadn't even thought of them as friends, but she never considered them her enemies. Her wife's distaste for the Ancient Ones was quickly becoming her own. If they saw her as insignificant, Agatha feared what punishments they would dish out.

    Eartha waved a hand, the floor opening up to reveal her younger self with Neva. "If you choose to follow the mortal, you will be forced to remove the only friend she has." Rio shrugged. "You don't scare me."

    Then what does? What did they do to you? Agatha bristled as Stevie gave the order. Her magic jumped at the command, killing Neva.

    "I'm sure we'll be seeing you again," Betty sighed. "Nothing's going to get her out of your head now."

    Agatha wanted to scream as Rio faced the group in her mortal form. There was a flower in her hair. One Agatha remembered putting there on their wedding night.

    "What is the meaning of this?" Stevie growled. "You are not permitted to marry a mortal." "We refuse to acknowledge such a taboo union," Eartha added.

    "You have gone too far," Frida hissed.

    Death hefted her chin, facing the women. She stood tall and proud as she declared, "I love Agatha Harkness. You will not keep me from her."

    Betty pounded a fist on the table. "This is unacceptable! You would upset the Sacred Balance for one measly mortal?"

    "I have said it once before. I shall say it again. I would destroy the world for my wife." The temple shook with a clap of thunder and shouts of protest.

    "You do this, and we will send a hoard of enemies after her. She will never know peace," Frida warned.

    "My wife will best them at every turn."

    Stevie growled. "You will refrain from such blasphemous expressions. You have no wife. You have a plaything." She rapped her knuckles on the tabletop, passing judgement. "Henceforth, you shall be barred from residing in your kingdom. Now, you will house yourself in the Ether where none shall ever be able to see you. You will, never again, touch the sands of the Afterlife."

    "Sounds peaceful," Rio bit out. "Are we done here?"

    Agatha's wife was dropped into the void below.

    "If you've come to beg, do so on your knees," Betty sneered. "You don't mind doing it for the mortal. Why are we any different?"

    Rio raised her head, eyes red and rimmed with tears. She grit her teeth before dropping to her knees. "Please...Please allow me to give her this one thing. I will accept any and all consequences. Just let her have a child."

    Agatha strained against the spell, looking for a weak spot. She needed to hold her wife. Needed to brush those tears away from the only person who had ever fought so hard for her. "And why would we do that?" Stevie asked calmly. "I thought your mortal was capable of anything."

    Death growled. "What is the point of torturing her? There are other mortals that could entertain you. My wife-"

    "You forget yourself," Stevie barked. "You have no wife. You have no right to create life. The consequences would be disastrous."

    "The child will die," Rio choked out. "As all mortals do. I ask only for a little time." Stevie hummed. "Very well then. That can be arranged."

    "No," Agatha shouted. "It's a trick." Her words fell on deaf ears.

    Nicky was never meant to live.

    "LADY DEATH!"

    Agatha jumped as Stevie's voice bounced throughout the universe. Below, the panel had her life pulled up once more. Like they were watching a movie. Like her suffering truly meant nothing more than a source of entertainment. Then again, they'd already said as much. Agatha had no reason to be shocked. She had thought her mother cruel, but now she knew the true meaning of the word.

    In the swirl of a time pool, Rio, as she stood before a pregnant and bleeding Agatha, closed her eyes. Death slowed time and slipped into the temple.

    "I have granted more time to my son," Rio admitted. She was no fool. None of them were. They knew what she'd done.

    "You are to reap that soul immediately," Frida hissed. "It would be an abomination." "And I will reap him, in time. But I will not reap him today. He will know his other mother." Eartha cackled. "You would let her get attached to it just to steal it away? And you call us callous, Lady Death."

    Rio glared at the woman. "She will understand and cherish her time with him." Agatha felt her stomach drop. Her wife had had so much faith in her just for Agatha to turn on her like the Ancient Ones had. Had Death ever known peace?

    "You have still broken the rules. And as much fun as it will be to watch the two toil like worms, you still require a fitting punishment," Dolly told Rio.

    "You don't know what it cost me," Rio had told her when they reconciled. Agatha had always thought it meant their love and how she'd pulled away from the Green Witch. Now, she shook with fear. What terrible thing had they done to her wife?

    "Not to worry," Stevie purred. "I know the perfect punishment. If the boy is to live, his body shall not be his own. And since Lady Death is so keen on experiencing mortal hardships, she shall know his pain as her own. Just as she has taken Agatha Harkness' heart as her own. Let her experience both ends of the spectrum. Let her feel her own child slip away. Let her feel Agatha's heart break and burn with hatred and grief."

    Rio roared, a wind blasting towards the panel.

    "This was all your doing," Eartha told her. "All you had to do was leave the mortal alone. Now, you have condemned them both to suffer for the rest of their lives." Death clutched at her chest as the group linked her being with Nicky's. She cried out and dropped to the floor. Agatha howled for her wife as she was pulled backwards forcefully.

    The goddess slid and tumbled until Rio reached her. Her wife helped her to stand, hands pressing against her as if she feared she were no longer real. Had they tortured her that way too? Did they ever make Rio see visions of her just to pull them away? "Well, darlin', what did you think?" Dolly teased cruelly. Her eyes twinkled with all the joy in the world. She had enjoyed the mental anguish she'd dished out.

    Agatha lifted her head to face the women. If they wanted a villain, she'd give them a villain. "I will bind his magic," she told them evenly, schooling her features. "Very good," Eartha praised. "I told you she was worth adding. Far more reasonable than Lady Death. Plus, none of us have to handle that hormonal boy."

    The goddess hummed. "If that's all. We have a dinner to prepare for."

    "Lady Death-"

    "Will be attending dinner with me," Agatha said, cutting Frida off. "It's part of the Demiurge's training."

    Dolly scoffed. "I fail to see-"

    "Yes, I've noticed," Agatha told her. "That's why I've survived as long as I have." She pulled Rio to her, giving her a small look. "We really must be going."

    "We're not finished," Stevie told her.

    "Oh, but you are," she threw over her shoulder. Agatha tightened her grip on Rio. "We'll chat later, dear. I'll be sure to make it worth your while."

    The panel murmured amongst themselves before releasing the couple.

    Rio pulled Agatha into the Ether the second they were out of the Ancient One's grasp. She probed the witch with her magic, checking for injuries. "What did they show you?" Cool hands cupped her face. Blue eyes softened and welled with tears. "They showed me just how much you love me," she breathed. "I am proud to call you my wife." Death's eyes widened as her wife kissed her. She pushed the goddess away, blinking. "I don't understand."

    Agatha laughed, pressing her forehead to Rio's. "I will make it up to you and Nicky, my love. I promise on all that I am, I will." She hugged Death tightly, cradling the cosmic entity. "You're really going to...?" Rio couldn't even bring herself to say the words. Her wife sniffled. "I am." But it won't be for long, she sent telepathically. Rio, I need to know where in the Universe the Ancient Ones can't see anything. We need somewhere to talk free of their oversight.

    Agatha...If you try anything, they'll take you from me again. They'll take Nicky. She gripped at her wife, heart clenching. Agatha knew what she meant. Agatha had seen what they'd done to her.

    Trust me, the goddess soothed. I won't do anything right now. But when the time is right, they'll burn for what they've done.

    Rio shivered at the heat in her wife's internal voice. The roll of rage and vitriol tied together with the promise of sweet revenge. There was a reason why she chose this witch to love and be loved by. If Agatha Harkness wanted to kill the Ancient Ones, who was she to stop her? Death dropped to her knees, eyes drinking in her wife for the righteous fury that she was. They cannot see into Wanda's or Billy's hexes, she relayed mentally as she worshipped a wrist.

    Agatha laughed darkly. "Perfect."
