    Chapter Notes I live!

    Let's get the ball a-rollin' folks. 🤠 Also, I know all the real celebs I put on the panel are wonderful women. I love them very much for the changes they've made irl, so I don't want anyone to think I hate them or something.

    Okie, let's go! (coat swish)

    See the end of the chapter for more notes Agatha sucked in a shaky breath as Rio and her returned to her Westview home. Things were going to be different now. Very different.

    "And you're sure there's a way to keep the two separate?" she asked Death. "Because if it affects both...I don't know if I can do it."

    "I'm sure. They're two very different kinds of magic." Rio squeezed her hand. "And if you want him to keep living, this is the only way."

    The goddess squeezed her eyes shut, preparing herself mentally for the task at hand. Agatha opened her eyes and stepped into Nicky's room.

    Her son was sleeping soundly. His hair would likely stick out at odd angles, but it would make him giggle. Would have made him giggle.

    Agatha swallowed thickly. "I can't...not while he's asleep. He deserves to know." "I'm right here," her wife told her. "Together, this time."

    Agatha bit back a sob, pressing a hand to her mouth. She nodded before wiping the tears from her face. It wouldn't do to show him how scary this would be. If she could convince him, it wouldn't hurt her as much. "Nicky," she said, shaking him. "Nicky, my love, wake up."

    Her son shifted with a groan. He rolled over to face his mothers with a squint. "Is it time for breakfast?"

    Rio laughed softly. "No, querido. We...There's something we have to do, but you deserve to know why it's being done."

    Agatha sat down on the edge of Nicky's bed and took his hand. "You know we love you, right? That we would never do anything to hurt you?"

    Nicky nodded slowly. "Am I in trouble?"

    "No," Agatha breathed. She swallowed the emotion that threatened to overcome her. "But...But there could be trouble. See, you've got magic like your mother, but that's not safe. Not right now," she began. "Mother and I's bosses are worried you might accidentally use that magic and hurt someone."

    "And we know you would never do anything like that," Rio added quickly. She sat down to run a hand through his hair. "But we still have to..."

    "We have to put that magic away. Like a toy for big boys. You can't have it just yet, but I promise you'll have it back some day," Agatha said before Rio sacrificed herself. "Nicky, Mama has to seal away some of your magic, okay?"

    His eyes widened. "But you said-!"

    "I know," she sighed. "Nicky, trust me, I know. But if we don't do this, you will be hurt. We don't want anything to happen to you," she whispered as tears threatened to fall. "I'm sorry, my love. I have to."

    Rio took his other hand. "She won't take away your green magic. You'll still have that with me. You've just got an extra kind that some not nice people think is too much for you right now. Your mama and I are going to fight for you, but this is our only option right now." He looked between them, tears forming. "Am I evil?" he asked in a small voice. Agatha nearly fell to pieces. "No. Never! You could never be evil." She pulled him into a hug, sniffling. "You're too good for this world, Nicholas Scratch. I'm sorry I can't protect you from it." But I will in time, she vowed. I'll do you proud.

    "Will it hurt?"

    The goddess didn't know how to answer. She'd never been bound before, and she never lied to her son. "I...I don't know, Nicky. But I promise to be as gentle as possible. Or you could go to sleep, so you won't feel a thing."

    He looked up at her with those wide, trusting eyes. Her son, doomed once again for being her child. "I wanna be awake, Mama. Can Mother hold me when it happens?"

    Nicky made it sound like she was going to kill him. But in the end, she practically was. She was forcing her son to be punished for something that wasn't his fault. For magic he never asked for. The cycle continued. The Ancient Ones would pay.

    "Whatever you want to do," she told him. Agatha prepared herself. Prepared her magic for the ultimate betrayal.

    Nicky crawled into his mother's lap and wrapped one of her arms around him. "Okay, Mama. I'm ready."

    "My brave boy," she praised as a tear slipped down her cheek. "I will make it up to you," Agatha promised. "I won't stop until I do."

    He simply nodded before holding still.

    Rio kissed his head and hugged him tightly. "Te quiero mucho, querido." Agatha unfurled her magic, guiding it towards her son. She moved slowly, careful not to scare him. The goddess tried to smile. Tried to make it seem like it wasn't as serious as it was, but that would be a lie. She would not lie.

    Her magic settled over him like a fine mist and sought out the source of his death magic. She blinked back tears as Nicky began to squirm. Agatha had bound so many witches before. Had killed so many witches. Had committed atrocities without ever batting an eye. But this? This turned her stomach. Watching her son be bound and subdued was the worse thing she'd ever experienced. But knowing she was the cause of his pain killed a part of her. The source was found and capped.

    Nicky yelped, flinching.

    Agatha pulled her magic back slowly, trying to reduce any more pain. She was crying in earnest. Nicky was too.

    "I wanna be alone," he told his mothers, hugging himself.

    Agatha tried to ignore the sound of Rio's breaking heart. "I understand." She tugged Rio away. "I'm sorry, Nicky."

    Her son looked away, tears shining in his eyes. He would forgive her. It's who he was. Agatha would never forgive herself, though. That's who she was.

    They pulled the door shut before the pair slipped into the Ether to mourn in peace.

    Billy pulled up to Agatha's house with a grin. Teddy unplugged his phone from the AUX cord and got out. The Maximoff-Kaplan-Harkness-Vidal killed the engine and followed his boyfriend. The second his foot touched the ground, his magic tensed.

    Something was wrong.

    "We're home," Teddy greeted as Billy stepped up behind him. "Guys?"

    Jen stood with a glare. She had Nicky behind her. Before her, Agatha stared forward with a stony, unreadable face.

    "How could you?" Wanda growled. "He's a child!"

    Agatha blinked.

    "What's going on?" Billy asked. He stepped past Teddy to get a better look at the coven. "What's wrong?"

    "Why don't you ask your mother?" Jen spat.

    Billy turned to face the Divine Mother. "Agatha?"

    The woman stared at him blankly. Her eyes were puffy and dull. She had been crying. "It's none of anybody's business what I do. Are you ready for your lesson?"

    The teen narrowed his eyes at her. "No. I won't be ready until someone tells me what's going on. Why do you look like shit? Why is everybody mad at you?"

    "Agatha's bound Nicky's magic," Jen told him. She shot another glare at the goddess. "Though she insists it's only part of it."

    "Because it is," the immortal hissed. Her eyes flashed purple, objects shaking. "By all means, make the situation worse, Kale!"

    "I don't see how I could, Harkness! You've bound your own child and won't even tell us why."

    Nicky began to cry. "Don't fight," he pleaded. "Mama-"

    "Quiet!"

    Slap!

    Agatha reached up to hold her cheek. She swallowed thickly. "Today's lesson will be over levitation," she said as if the blow had never occurred.

    "Sorry," Jen began with a sickly sweet tone. "I forgot you're used to that kind of thing." "That's too far," Alice whispered. "There's gotta be more to the story. Agatha would never-" "If you're all through gossiping, I'd like to make myself a cup of coffee for a long day of teaching." Agatha brushed past them, eyes flitting down to her son's. Her steps faltered. "I'm sorry, Nicky..."

    He looked up at her. "I know."

    Billy looked for Tommy. "What's happening?" he mouthed to his twin.

    Tommy sped over. "Little Dude got some of his magic sealed away or somethin'. Whole coven's furious."

    "Billy...Wanda...," Agatha yelled from the kitchen. "We don't have all day." The teen swallowed thickly. "Maybe see if Mom will take you, him, and Teddy for a walk or something. Give him a break from all of this."

    Tommy nodded. "You up for helping me with Lil Bro?" he asked the jock. "Yeah, I'm down," Teddy told him. The two left Billy's side to coax the boy away from the house.

    Billy stepped into the kitchen. Wanda had yet to heed Agatha's call. He moved to stand next to the witch, watching her closely. "Agatha, what really happened with Nicky?" "I did my job," she grumbled. "Stop harping on me already. We've got a lot to do today." He scowled. "Well, I don't want to be here if everyone's going to be so moody." "So, go then! What the hell do I care? Teach a bunch of snotty nosed brats how to wield chaos magic? Ha! You'll be lucky if you can lift a pen." Agatha tossed her mug in a huff. It fell to the ground and shattered. "Fucking fantastic!"

    Billy fought with his options. He could stay and figure out what was really happening....or he could go home. Home was a nice option. "If you're going to be..." He trailed off as a paper floated to the ground. "O-kay..."

    Agatha swiped it before he could even consider picking it up. "Yeah, yeah. Let's just get this over with, shall we?" She disappeared in a flash.

    The teen looked around, confused. "Uh...Agatha?" He left the kitchen. "Guys, I think Agatha's been kidnapped!"

    "Good," Jen spat. "Maybe someone's looking out for Nicky since she clearly isn't." "Stop!" Nicky stomped a foot. "Mama didn't want to," he huffed. "Can't you see how sad she is?"

    "I'm not going to feel bad for her after she did that to you," Jen reasoned. "It's wrong. You're supposed to have the magic you were born with. It's a piece of you. You have so much potential for green magic, and she just took that away!"

    Billy hugged his brother. "Are you okay? Do you need anything?"

    "I want my Mama," Nicky told him. "I was sad, but she's more sad. Mother and her didn't want to. They told me." He lowered his head. "I was just scared they didn't love me anymore because of my bad magic."

    "You don't have bad magic," Wanda told him. "Green magic is good. It's...Billy what is it?" "I have my green magic," Nicky pressed. "Mama had to seal away the other one. The one that comes from Mother."

    The room fell quiet. Billy only knew of two magics that Rio possessed. If Nicky had the other one, then it was no wonder it had to be sealed away.

    "Where'd my Mama go, Billy?"

    "I don't know," he told his brother. "She poofed away. Something took her." By the time he finished speaking, the goddess reappeared out of thin air. She dropped to the floor, landing in a pile of limbs and hair and clothes.

    "Mama!"

    Agatha flinched.

    "Whoa there," Billy said, holding his brother back. "Are you okay?"

    His Divine Mother swatted Alice's hands away. "I'm fine. Got my ass chewed out, but that's no biggie." She scrambled to her feet, fixing her hair. "I'm going to make myself another batch of coffee. Please try to not annoy me." Agatha moved towards Nicky and picked him up. "And you, mister, are not allowed to leave my sights." She gripped him tightly. "Ow," he winced.

    Agatha apologized and loosened her hold. "You wanna come with Mother and I to eat with the Kaplan's tonight?"

    Billy shared a look with the others. "You guys saw that, right?" he whispered. "Something's not right here."

    Stop talking, Agatha sent him telepathically. You're making things worse. I'll explain everything later. Right now, you and Wanda need to want a lesson asap. The teen turned to his mother. "I would really love it if you joined Agatha and I today. For the lesson, that is."

    She made a face. "I'm sorry?" Wanda laughed. "Now you're acting weird." Billy shook his head. "Don't be silly. Agatha's always cranky in the morning. She'll be fine after she eats something."

    His chaotic mother stepped towards him and pressed a hand to his forehead. "Are we about to have another round of the flu?"

    "Come on," he told her. Billy grabbed her arm and pulled her along. "You guys wanna join too? The more the merrier."

    Alice, Jen, Teddy, and Tommy shared a look.

    "We need to practice with some test dummies," he joked, nodding his head towards the kitchen. "It'll be fun."

    They followed him into the eerily quiet kitchen.

    "Why do you have a bruise, Mama?"

    "It's from the fall," Agatha told her son. "Eat your cereal."

    Billy eyed her. His Divine Mother looked...off. "Everyone's going to join us after all," he told her evenly. "For the lesson."

    Agatha rubbed a temple. "Yes, yes. The lesson in levitation. Tommy and Teddy can throw things at all of you to see how fast your reaction is."

    "Mama, why do you smell funny? Did Mother give you a bunch of marigolds?" "Nicky, please," the goddess sighed. "I don't want another lecture."

    "Who's giving you a lecture?" Wanda asked. She wafted a hand around Agatha's hair. "You do have an odd floral scent today."

    Which meant Nicky was telling the truth about his green magic if he could still identify a plant by smell alone. Billy narrowed his eyes at the goddess. What aren't you telling us? Not now, Billy. She cut him off from her mind.

    The lesson progressed with an uncomfortable silence. Billy paired with Teddy. Jen with Alice. Wanda with Tommy. Agatha walked around, changing hand positions and giving the non-magic wielders objects to toss. The goddess considered putting some music on, but the thought of all that noise made her migraine worse. Her eyes drifted to Nicky as he talked to a bug.

    "Oh, darling," Frida had whispered in her ear. Her fingers inched across Agatha's waist. "I knew you were a horse worth betting on." Lips pressed to Agatha's cheek before sliding towards her lips.

    Agatha shoved the Ancient One away purely on instinct. "I have a wife," she managed to get out. "You've already said you'd acknowledge it."

    Frida and Eartha had circled her like piranha. All toothy smiles and hungry eyes. They'd gotten a taste of her before. They certainly wanted it again.

    "Leave her be," Stevie ordered. "We brought her here for a lecture, not an orgy." The leader of the group waved the two back over. "You bound the boy. We're grateful to you for that. Now, we have the issue of your unwilling students."

    Agatha clenched her jaw. "They're attached to...Nicholas," she told them. Calling him her son would likely make things worse. She needed to gain their trust first. "They will be fine once they see he's fine. I wouldn't worry."

    "Good. If the boy becomes a problem, we'll remove him," Dolly laughed. Agatha jumped as a hand settled on her shoulder. "What!"

    Wanda pressed her lips into a firm line. "You were just standing there," she said softly. Her green eyes shone with concern.

    The goddess pulled her shoulder away gently. "Let's take a break. I'm tired. The sun is very draining." She walked towards the house, not bothering to look back.

    Rio eyed the setting sun before slipping into Agatha's house. She immediately sought out Nicky before pulling him into a hug. He pressed his face into her shoulder, gripping her tightly.

    "Mama's very sad," he whispered. "Everyone's mad at her."

    Death sighed. "It won't be for long, mijo. I promise."

    Nicky looked up at her. "Mama said I could go with you tonight to see the Kaplan's." "She did?" That was a bit odd for Agatha. "Well, we better get you ready." Rio took his hand and led him upstairs.

    Agatha happened to be stepping out of the bathroom when the pair reached the top of the stairs. She opened her mouth before snapping it shut. The goddess moved swiftly to press a kiss to Rio's lip. Fingers dug into the Green Witch's skin. "I missed you." Death blinked. "That's my line," she laughed. She didn't miss the slight panic in Agatha's eyes. Nor did she miss the way her wife pulled back ever so slightly. "I missed you, too," she added, bowing at the waist.

    She pressed a kiss to Agatha's knuckles before producing a flower. Her wife was in need of cheering up. A crocus vernus was bound to do the trick. Agatha smiled at the offering. "It's been a while since you grew me something," her wife sighed. Agatha sniffed the petals, suddenly a young maiden. "What's this one?"

    "It's a crocus," Nicky told her. He gave her a toothy grin. "They attract bees 'cause they smell so nice."

    Rio beamed. She'd been worried his green magic would have been affected by the binding. "He's correct," she told Agatha. "And I made sure this one was purple as well. You seem to only hold on to them when they are."

    Agatha scoffed, a bit of color returning to her face. "I can't help it if they're the superior flower colors."

    Nicky tugged at her hand. "Let's get ready, Mother. Billy's gonna get cranky if we're not on time."

    She laughed. "Why don't you pick your clothes out, mijo. You're a big boy. Let's see if you got your mama's fashion sense or not."

    The child accepted the challenge. "Be right back!"

    Rio turned back to her wife. "You showered without me," she lamented. "I was going to lather you up." She winked at the goddess.

    Her alarm bells began to ring as Agatha gave her a tight grin. "Ah, I was too sweaty. Had a long lesson today. I didn't wanna wrinkle that pretty nose of yours!" Agatha tapped Rio's nose with a finger.

    Death knew something was bothering her wife. The over-the-top accent had given the younger immortal away. But she didn't press for details. Agatha would tell her when she was ready. Right now, her wife needed her support.

    Rio pulled her into a sweeping dip before planting a big, dramatically heated kiss to the goddess' lips. She stood her wife back up, hands settling on Agatha's hips. "Consider that payment for showering without me. She pulled Agatha in for a hug. "Are you ready for tonight?"

    Agatha sunk into the hug with a sigh. "I'm not sure what to wear, to be honest. How did you go last time?"

    Rio pulled back with a smirk. "I went as Agent Vidal. Sans badge, of course." She smoothed a hand across Agatha's chest. "You should dress comfortably for once." "I don't know..." Agatha looked away, biting her lip. "Not exactly feeling comfortable with much lately," she mumbled.

    Death filed the comment away. Someone was going to lose a limb or two the second she found out what happened. "I'll go in short-shorts if you do~," she purred. Agatha chuckled. "What? So you can sit on my knee the entire evening?" Rio licked the inside of her cheek. "Well, there's a thought!"

    "No," Agatha laughed. "I'll wear something sensible. Go check on Nicky. He's..." A frown tugged at her lips. "...Coping."

    Rio pressed another kiss to her wife's knuckles. "It's not forever, remember? And with Billy and Tommy's streak of wreaking havoc with their powers, maybe we managed to keep Nicky from having a similar experience. He'll be the only in this family without a body count." Agatha hummed. "I hadn't thought of that.......He'll...He'll come to appreciate that when he's older and find out just how bad it was for the rest of us." She cupped Rio's face and pressed a chaste kiss to her lips. "What would I do without you?"

    "Smother yourself in dark magic and murder hundreds," Rio joked darkly. Agatha laughed before gently shoving her backwards. "Nicky. Go."

    She gave a dramatic bow. "Sí, mi amor." Rio turned on her heel and pranced over to the bedroom.

    Agatha stared out the window, a hand tucked under her chin. The trees whizzing past the car did little to distract her. She adjusted her lilac turtleneck sweater, careful to keep her thoughts hidden from Rio. If her wife knew, she'd lose her temper before Agatha was ready. So much was at stake.

    It was like she blinked, and they'd arrived. A hand shook her gently, so she must have dozed off. Not a good sign since the moon was up. Sure enough, Rio was watching her carefully. Hand settled on her dagger.

    "My magic is hungry," she lied. "Don't worry."

    Death tucked the ancient bottle of wine into her arm as Agatha opened the car door for her. "I'm sure a good frisking will solve that."

    Agatha moaned at the thought. "Better behave tonight, or I'll send you straight home." "Promises, promises," Rio tutted. She waited at Agatha's side before they moved to the front door. "No manners in that boy. He's already gone inside."

    "What's with the box he was carrying? Did we stop and get a cake?"

    "Not sure. I don't know what we'd be celebrating."

    Nicky waved his mothers inside. "Come on, come on," he whined. "The food smells so good."

    "We're comin'. Hold your horses," Agatha told him. She scoffed. "I guess none of our children have manners."

    "That's not surprising," Rio laughed. "You're just as impatient."

    Agatha rolled her eyes and pulled Rio along. She eyed Billy and Teddy as they chatted with Nicky. She made a note to thank them later. The two had been very gentle with her youngest since the binding. Agatha steeled herself as she stopped to greet the Kaplan's. "I hope Billy drove the speed limit," Man Kaplan Jeff teased. "We know how much he likes to speed."

    The goddess forced a laugh. "Oh yes. Speeding. We were fifty miles over the speed limit the whole way here."

    Rio gave her a look, smirking. "Agatha drove here."

    The Kaplan's balked.

    "She's kidding," Billy told his parents. "Agatha hates driving. It reminds her of when she was under Wanda's spell."

    She narrowed her eyes at the teen. "Rude. I don't tell people you don't walk around barefoot because it reminds you of being on the Road."

    Billy stuck his tongue out at her. "At least I'm not scared of 70s rock ballads." "Yeah...well...I didn't need a night light to sleep with after we got back." "You were a ghost, so that doesn't count," he told her. Billy cracked a smile. "I missed arguing with you."

    Agatha smiled back. "Yeah, yeah. Get over here and get your hug already." She waved him over before squeezing him tightly. "Sorry, I've been such an ass lately. Got a lot on my plate right now."

    "It's okay. Nicky explained it to us," he whispered in her ear.

    She fought the urge to flinch away. Agatha patted his back and released him. "So, what's for dinner? I hope it pairs with a vintage Chenin blanc."

    Rio held up the labeless bottle with a grin. "Straight from Château de Goulaine," she informed.

    Jeff made a strangled noise as he fainted.

    The grouped rushed to get him back up while Rio laughed. He thanked them and moved to sit down.

    "He just really loves his wine," Rebecca explained. She gestured for them to take a seat as well.

    Agatha sat across from Death so the two could look at one another. She was rarely given the chance most days. "We'll keep the batch number that came from a secret then." Agatha shot her wife a grin. "You might open it for them, my love. I'm sure the cork needs changing again."

    Rio pulled out her knife and skillfully used it to tug the cork out. "That was a good year," she moaned. "The guillotine remains my favorite execution method."

    "We'll build you one to chop vegetables with," Agatha laughed.

    Billy cleared his throat. "After dinner, I have something for you, Agatha. I meant to have you open it earlier, but then everyone got sick and someone tucked it away." She quirked a brow. "A gift for me?"

    Her older younger son nodded. "You'll love it. Trust me."

    Trust was a hard thing to give the boy. He'd done quite a number on her as of late. But if it meant gaining his trust to gain the Ancient Ones' trust, she'd suffer through it. Agatha gave him a nod before using her magic to serve the wine.

    "I suppose I should add there's a lesson in this dinner," she informed the teen. "Not entirely my idea, but necessary for...reasons. We practiced levitation earlier. Let's see you put it to use. Use your magic to serve the food for your mother."

    He furrowed his brows. "But you said not to use magic around them."

    "When I'm not around, yes. I'm here, and your parents have worked hard enough. Let's see how well you did today."

    "If he doesn't want to," Rebecca began.

    "He has to," Agatha grit out. "Not because I want him to. But sacrifices must be made for the sake of others." She calmed her ire. "You can do this. I know you can." It was probably the softest she'd ever spoken to him, but it did the trick. The casserole dish floated over with a spoon. Billy grew quiet as he mumbled incantations under his breath, fingers twitching.

    "You're doing great, but try to do so without your hands," she instructed. "You created the Road without saying a single spell, and without a single hand gesture. That takes real talent, kid."

    Billy took a deep breath as he put his hands away. The dish began to shake. "Imagine you have as many hands as you want holding the dish up," Agatha told him. "Feel the weight with your mind and distribute it evenly."

    "I'm trying," he grit out. Billy grunted as the casserole began to move from side to side more erratically. "I can't do it."

    "That's quitter talk," she laughed. "What if this was Tommy falling from a cliff but you were holding off an enemy? Are you just going to let him fall?"

    "No!"

    "So hold him up. Keep him safe." Agatha kept her eyes on the dish, waiting for it to stabilize. She bit back a sigh as it tried to flip completely over. Purple caught it before it had a chance to fall to the table and ruin the night. "We'll keep working on that," she told him. "You held out longer than I was expecting."

    He dropped his head into his hands and took deep breaths. "Don't make me do that again," Billy pleaded. "I'm tired."

    Agatha served the food, kicking herself mentally. "Rest for now."

    Rebecca shot her a look. "I can do the rest."

    "No, it's fine. You cooked," Agatha told her.

    "Jeff cooked," Rio and Rebecca said in unison.

    A man who cooked for his wife! Agatha was shocked. "Even more reason for me to do it." She finished plating the food and sent the dish back to the kitchen. Agatha took a sip from the wine and bit back a moan. Much better than poisoned wine, she told herself. "So, is that all you do with Billy and the others?" Jeff asked. "Make him use his magic for practical reasons?" He ate a forkful as he waited for her to respond.

    She tapped the side of her fork with the tip of her nail. How dangerous would it be to get the mortals involved? Very, she deicided. "He has to learn to control his emotions while using magic so he doesn't accidentally injure anyone. Levitation is a big one. A witch is more likely to hurt someone in a fit of rage by lobbing an object or two."

    "Like you do when you're really mad," Nicky said unhelpfully.

    She gave her son a tight grin. "Yes. Even Mama has to work on her control too, my love." Teddy leaned forward. "Hey, I get it. When Coach calls a bad play, we all wanna throw our helmets at him."

    I love this kid, Agatha told herself. She gave him a bigger smile. "You ever want him gone, let me know. Rio and I would happily find a way to convince him to do better." "He's fine, just old." Teddy nudged Billy. "Remember when you tried out for football?" The teen pulled a face. "Don't remind me. I hated all that yelling."

    Agatha hummed. "I don't imagine all those angry thoughts made it better." Billy shook his head. "I passed out."

    "You never told us," Rebecca said. "What if you had gotten hurt?"

    He gave them a tight grin. "I didn't want you to worry. I was still trying to figure myself out." Agatha let the group talk as she sat back to sip at her wine. Enough of her body was still susceptible to the alcohol as her cheeks began to warm. She stiffened at the scent of marigold. She had yet to make an excuse for Rio's participation.

    "Billy, I do have one more test for you," she blurted out. Agatha nearly slammed her head into the table. She didn't even have a test planned for the boy. "But it has to do with Rio." The table looked at her as if she'd grown an extra head. Billy nodded slowly, a brow quirked. Think. Think. Think! "Grow a flower. Whichever flower she tells you. Grow it." "There's no dirt in here," he laughed.

    "Use your chaos magic to turn something else into that flower." Agatha rubbed a temple and took a larger sip of her wine. "You need only make three."

    Rio gave her a look, mouthing a 'sorry'. "Make a rose," she told Billy. "Purple with thorns." She couldn't make it too easy for him. Not with the Ancient Ones watching them so closely. Agatha held her breath as Billy speared a small forkful and stared at it. "You can use an incantation," she told him. "It just needs to be a real rose."

    The teen began to mumble the incantation necessary as his parents watched on. Nicky continued to eat as if it were a daily occurrence for him. Billy hissed and looked away. "There's too many people watching me," he complained. "It's hard to concentrate." "People are always going to watch you," she told him. "You'll need to learn how to get over that. Focus."

    Billy glared at her. "Why are we doing this here? This is supposed to be a nice, normal dinner."

    Agatha clenched her jaw. "We are no longer afforded those. I promise this will be the last one. Just make the three flowers and we'll be done."

    "I don't want to make the flowers. I want you to tell me what's going on," the teen growled. "You've been acting weird all day."

    "There's nothing wrong," she told him.

    "You're lying!"

    Agatha gasped as she felt a sting along her cheek. She touched the area gently to find blood on her fingertips.

    Nicky jumped in his seat. "Mama!"

    "It's fine," she told the group. "I'm fine." Agatha held up a hand to keep the others seated. Rio, however, left her seat and walked around the table.

    "Let me see, sweetheart," Death cooed softly. Warm fingers turned Agatha's face gently to the left. Rio leaned in as if she were going to whisper something only for her to drag the tip of her tongue along the cut. She moaned, eyes sliding shut.

    Agatha shuddered. "Thank you, my love." She cleared her throat. "We should finish here. Enjoy it while we can."

    Rio nodded, squeezing her shoulder. "All good," she announced to the table. "Agatha, I'm so sorry," Billy told her.

    She gave him a small smile before using her magic to pull the fork out of the wall behind her. "This is why we have to have our lessons. Don't worry, though. Wanda's thrown a whole car at me and I was just fine. Immortal, remember." Agatha waved his concern away. "No more lessons. I promise." She swallowed thickly. "This will be our last dinner here tonight. If it's not magic related, we are not permitted to indulge in...frivolous endeavors." "Says who?" Rebecca asked. "You don't get to just waltz in here just to waltz right back out." Agatha finished off her wine with a sniff. "Our bosses say. And if Billy enjoys having a teacher, he'll get over it." She set her glass down, waiting for him to challenge her. Billy gave her a long look. "I do enjoy having you as a teacher, Agatha." He flicked his eyes over to Rio. "We'll do dinner at your place next time. So everyone can join in." The group settled, some of the tension ebbing away.

    "We'll see if that can be arranged." Agatha served herself another glass and hoped they'd given an entertaining enough show to the panel of bitches upstairs. "How's school for you and Teddy?"

    Gradually, they turned to small talk. Teddy told them about a project he was working on for physics. He was builting a paper rocket that the teacher would be launching with an air tank. Billy talked at length about an art piece he had in the works. He hoped to debut it soon. Time ticked down until Nicky's eyes began to droop. He yawned, covering his mouth. "I think that's our cue," Rio told the Kaplan's. "Dinner was delicious. I almost wished I needed to eat."

    "Thanks! That means a lot, Rio," Jeff said, beaming. "And thank you for sharing the wine. I can die happy now."

    Agatha and Rio shared a dark chuckle.

    "Wait! Your gift," Billy reminded. He reached under the table before popping back up. "It's the only thing I could think of getting you to show you how sorry I am about the whole memory thing." He slid the package over.

    Agatha pulled it to herself. "It's not a bunch of poisonous snakes, is it? Because I hate to inform you that they simply aren't enough to kill this tiger."

    Billy laughed, shaking his head. His curls bounced as he waited impatiently for her to open it. "The suspense is killing us," Rebecca told her. "Billy wouldn't let us sneak a peek." Agatha lifted the lid and pulled the lining away. She grinned from ear to ear. "Oh, kid....." Agatha pulled the coat to her nose and inhaled deeply. It smelt of the Road. Of nature. Of woodsmoke and magic. "All is forgiven," she laughed, hugging the material to her. Rio grinned. "You could get away with murder now, Billy. She's wanted her coat back since you tried to kill her."

    "Hell, I'll kill for him at this point. Forget the leather jacket. Stevie can shove it up her ass. This coat is everything to me." Agatha stood up to put it on, sighing at the weight. "Come here, kid."

    She didn't wait for him to get up. Agatha moved towards the teen, coat swishing deliciously. She pulled him into a tight hug. "You get on my nerves, but fuck if I don't love you!" Billy wheezed and gasped for air. He tapped her arm, eyes pleading. He gasped as she released him. "Love...love you, too," he croaked.

    Agatha scooped Nicky up and rested his head on her shoulder. "Hate to dine and dash, but the missus has to get back to work. I need to go play with my jacket."

    The group stood to exchange farewells. Agatha pulled Billy aside.

    I promise I'll tell you, Billy. But I can't right now. Too many moving pieces. Just...trust me, okay?

    He nodded. "Get home safely."

    She tussled his curls. "Be good, Billy. I'll see you Tuesday."

    Chapter End Notes This was long only because I was determined to write the coat gifting scene 😂 Let's see how Agatha fairs with The Ancient Ones really breathing down her neck now. I'm Not the Only One Who Wants to See You Dead Chapter Summary Billy has a new teacher. (At school guys. At school!)

    Chapter Notes This is the biggest disclaimer I can put up. I am not a Marvel girlie. I'm taking from the comics and using it to further my story. So, if you're a die-hard fan, you're probs not gonna have a good time with me cherry picking stuff. If that doesn't bother you, strap in. We're officially on the last leg of the tour. Next chapter might be the last one depending on how the writing process goes.

    See the end of the chapter for more notes The moon was high in the sky, but Agatha was anything but energized. Rio hadn't come home in several days. Her absence was beginning to weigh heavily on her and Nicky's shoulders. No doubt, the Ancient Ones were sitting on their shitty little thrones with their shitty little grins and enjoying their shitty little show. Agatha paced. She had an idea of what it would take to remove the five from their position. But that was all it was. An idea.

    The Ancient Ones, as she'd found through reading, were beings made in tandem with cosmic entities. Immortal, but not unkillable. They were nexus beings who had removed themselves from the mortal realm to safeguard the Universe. She would need to be as close to indestructible as possible if she was going to take them on. Agatha knew she had two very viable options...but they weren't even remotely ready to support her in any way. Especially not Billy.

    But if she could get the Demiurge entirely on her side, the five would tumble. But Billy didn't see her as indestructible. A goddess, maybe, but not one that could destroy worlds with a twitch of her finger. That was what she needed him to believe. Needed his chaos magic to finish reshaping her. Unfortunately, that would take time. And in that time, her and Rio would continue to be hounded. Nicky would continue to stand with five blades pointed at his precious head.

    Agatha turned to face her bedroom window. The soft glow of the moon beckoned her. She listened. Agatha stepped into the light and sunk into the gentle moonbeam. One of the great things about being The Moon Goddess was the ability to be, well, the moon. Agatha Harkness gazed down at the world, blue eyes scanning for something. Anything. A familiar Subaru drove down a highway towards Eastview.

    "What are we up to, mister?" Agatha followed the car along until it lined up perfectly with a moonbeam. She transported herself into the vehicle and turned to face Billy. "Did you sneak off to see Teddy?"

    The teen screamed and swerved the car dramatically. "What the hell, Agatha?!" He looked between her and the road several times as he got the vehicle under control. "How did you...How are you here?"

    "Neat trick, huh?" She wiggled her fingers at him. "Now, answer my question. What are you doing out so late?"

    Billy gripped the wheel. "I...may have snuck out. Nothing serious. I just...I wanted to see him."

    Agatha leaned back, crossing her arms. "Why?"

    The Maximoff pursed his lips lightly. "We were talking about...you," he said slowly. "I'm worried about you."

    The goddess sat in silence. She sighed heavily. "I'm fine, Billy. There's nothing for you to worry about. I'm just dealing with the repercussions of not reading the fine print." Agatha looked over at him. "Watch the road! Watch the road!"

    Billy swerved back into his lane with a mumbled apology. "Look, you said you were going to tell me whatever it is going on, but you haven't. And Rio hasn't stopped by in a week. It's hard not to worry when you both suddenly pull back. Even Mom's worried." "On a scale of one to ten, how confident are you in consciously creating a hex?" Billy frowned. "I haven't been able to make another since the Road, so probably a 'two' on that scale."

    Agatha pursed her lips, stewing in thought. "You're just gonna have to trust me until then," she finally told him. "Anything else you wanna share?"

    Billy pulled up to his Eastview home and killed the engine. "Not really." He unbuckled his seat belt. "Well, I did get a new art teacher. Mr. Vincent, from upstate New York. He really likes my art."

    The Divine Mother hummed. "Have you finished that piece you were working on back when I was dead?"

    The teen laughed as he levitated up to his bedroom window. "Not quite, but he really likes that one. He wants me to consider sending it to an art gallery. Might get me some scholarships."

    "Wanda can just steal more S.W.O.R.D. funds if she needs to. There's no point in dealing with shifty art dealers in nitty gritty alleys, kid." Agatha used the moonbeams to transport herself around. She sat on his bed, making herself comfortable.

    "Careful with Bobby," Billy told her. He pointed to a beautiful bonsai perched to her right. It had its own little space on his desk.

    "Rio give you this?" Agatha tapped a leaf gently, lips quirking upwards. "She can hear you through it. Make sure Bobby's out of the room or in a safe space should you ever sneak Teddy in."

    Billy groaned in disgust. "I'm not...I'm not discussing that with you." He pulled off his shoes and set them near his backpack. "Are you bored? Is that why you're here?" "Can't I just check up on you?" she huffed. "Most sons are happy to see their mothers." Billy shot her a look. "Yeah, during the day, Agatha. Not at the witching hour on their way back from cuddle session."

    She chuckled quietly. "Downside to being the moon is that I'm too tired during the day." Agatha hummed as she remembered something. "Say...tell me more about how you got me and the others out of my memories. We never did have a conversation about that." "I'm tired, Agatha."

    "It's pretty important, Billy. I probably won't see you again until Thursday." Agatha raised her brows and shrugged. "Just really quick."

    Billy sighed. "Fine...When the moon started doing weird things, Rio thought it might have to do with you. So, she reasoned we could reach you if we went to the actual moon. Since I'm not an astronaut, she had transport us to that cosmo temple with those robed people. They got into an argument with Rio before helping me go into your mind that way." "Argument? About what?" If they did anything...

    Billy shrugged. "I dunno. It didn't really make much sense to me. Something about realms and souls being ignored. They seemed pretty pissed. Rio couldn't enter the moon the way I could, though. They wouldn't let her."

    Agatha furrowed her brows, lips pursing. Her wife hadn't said anything. Then again, she hadn't said anything about her last summons either. They were both trying to protect each other, but only Agatha had the means to do something. "Those robed people...those are our bosses," she told him.

    It was extremely risky revealing that information, but she needed him to have a nugget of information. Especially if they were watching him so closely. She had to trust that he would stick to their side of things after seeing how Rio was treated. If not, she'd need to find another way to take the Ancient Ones down.

    "Really? They seemed nice for the most part. One of them kept calling me 'darling'." Agatha fought a snarl. "They didn't tell you anything? Do anything that might have been odd or out of the ordinary?"

    Billy shook his head. "They were just frustrated with Rio and the whole situation. Can't really blame them."

    "Well...let's not have you two mingle unnecessarily. They're busy people, and you need lots of training."

    The teen gave her a look. "Is that where you went the other day?"

    She felt pressure against her temple as he tried to read her mind. Agatha kept him out. "Don't worry about that. Get some rest, or you'll be late."

    "You're doing it again," he groaned. "Why can't you just give me straight answers for once?" "When the time is right, you'll know what you need to know. For now, enjoy being a kid. And no more magic when I'm not around. You could have been seen levitating, mister. Someone could have their phone out and send it off to those sickos in tights." Billy rolled his eyes. "It's almost 4am, Agatha. No one's up."

    "Wrong! We're up," she reminded. "Anyone else can be up too. No. Magic." Her son glared at her. "I'm not a child. I can do some things."

    "Yeah, like creating more problems," she huffed. Agatha regretted the words as soon as she registered what she said. And to add insult to injury, Billy pointed to his window in heated silence. "That's not what I meant," she said.

    "Go home, Agatha."

    She slipped off his bed. "Billy..." She reached out to pull him into a hug but thought better of it. "Have a good day at school," Agatha told him before slipping away through the moonbeam.

    Nicky sat inside his mama's house and waited. There wasn't much to do outside of waiting. Tommy was off doing who knows what. All Wanda ever did was clean. Now, Jen and Alice were hugging all the time. (They made a rule for him to knock before going into their rooms, too.)

    His mama, unfortunately, was still sleeping. Nicky supposed she wouldn't be too mad if he went to take a nap with her. At most, she'd grumble before pulling him closer. The thought made him giggle. His mama was a funny witch when she grumbled. It made her sound like a bear.

    He snuck into his mother's room and pulled up the edge of the covers. Slowly, he slid into the empty spot next to her. (His mother was still out doing her job. He missed her.) Nicky set his back against hers and closed his eyes.

    Mama rolled over and hugged him tightly. "Don't fall," she mumbled sleepily. "You'll get hurt."

    " 'Kay, Mama." He leaned back and pressed a kiss to her cheek. Nicky shifted closer and let himself fall asleep.

    He woke up a little later in the day as his mama stirred. She stretched with a groan before combing his hair out of his face.

    "Sorry, Nicky. It's hard to be up for breakfast now."

    He crawled out of bed and helped pull his mama off the mattress. "It's okay. Wanda made me eggs. They taste better now."

    Mama pressed a kiss to the top of his head. "That's because we have salt and pepper now," she told him with a laugh. "Come on. I'll make us lunch."

    Nicky toddled behind her, hands in his pockets. He pursed his lips before speaking. "Mama, when can I go to school?"

    Her steps faltered. "Probably not for a while longer. We need to do some things, so you don't stick out too much. You're much smarter than the other kids your age. You're also behind on the technology."

    He sighed. "Okay."

    She turned to face him with that look she was wearing more and more often. "I'm..." His mama's smile dropped. "Let's do something today. Just the two of us. What do you say?" He grinned at the idea. "Can we go to the, uh...What did Tommy call it? A...a museum!" The goddess bent at the waist to tap his nose. "An excellent idea. You go get ready, and we'll take off after lunch."

    Nicky beamed before turning on his heel. "Be back in a second!"

    Agatha finished turning over a waffle (Nicky's favorite) before turning to pour a glass of orange juice (also Nicky's favorite). She hummed to herself, letting herself relax momentarily. For one, single, solitary day, the two could pretend they were ordinary people. Not a resurrected child from the 1700s and an ancient witch now elevated to a god's status. Of course, that was too much to ask.

    "Agatha!" Jen shouted from the living room.

    The goddess felt her stomach drop. She hadn't heard the potions witch sound like that since Lilia had died. Agatha rushed into the room. "What is it? What's wrong?" Jen had her phone pressed to her ear, face pale. "Billy's been taken to the hospital." Agatha blinked several times as her brain tried to catch up with the news. "Get the car. I'll get ahold of Wanda and Tommy." She ran to the foot of the stairs. "Nicky, get in the car with Jen. We've got to make a run to see Billy." The immortal reached out with her magic, looking for the Scarlet Witch. Basement. Agatha rushed down the stairs. "Wanda, where the hell is Tommy? We've got to go."

    The red head turned away from the washer, pants in hand. "What? Why?"

    "No time. Get him over here and in the car." She ran back up the stairs and out the front door. Agatha could see that Jen was buckling Nicky in, so she made a detour to her fence line. She bent down towards a shrub. "Rio, something's happened to Billy. I'm headed to Eastview with the coven." She didn't need to worry about Rio not getting the message. Rio always got the message.

    The coven sat in the waiting room as Agatha stood near a window. The Kaplan's sat huddled together, hand in hand. All was quiet. All was tense.

    The door opened as a nurse stepped forward. "For William Kaplan." She glanced up from her clipboard to see who she was speaking to.

    The entire coven, Kaplan's included stepped forward.

    The poor nurse laughed nervously. "Uhm, just the parents."

    Jeff and Rebecca stepped forward. The young woman ushered the couple past the doors. Agatha clenched her jaw, hugging herself. Wanda sent her a look, just as wounded. A glass door swung open.

    "Rio..." Agatha flew to her. She gripped at her wife, hugging her tightly. "What happened?" Death whispered.

    "I don't know. Rebecca only told Jen an accident happened at school." Agatha tugged her along. "Come on. If we use the Ether, we can get some actual news."

    Rio followed her faithfully. Once in the Ether, they slipped through the doors and down the hall. It took a moment, but eventually Death caught a whiff of Billy's magic. She took the lead and pulled Agatha along until they reached his room. "He seems fine. I don't know what everyone's freaking out over."

    Agatha laughed. "Fucking dramatic kids," she huffed. The goddess settled next to her son's bed. "Look at him. A bump on his head and they're acting like he broke something." Her wife chuckled. "You were so panicking," she teased. "You had the whole coven come." "How did you get in? The sun's up," Billy told them.

    The couple froze.

    "You have annoying abilities," Rio grumbled. "I'm not even going to bother asking this time." The teen rubbed an eye. "I tried to tell Mom it wasn't that serious, but she just had to go and cause a panic."

    "Billy, who are you talking to?" Jeff said. "Are you...Do you have a concussion?" "Oh, Agatha and Rio are here," Billy told them. He gestured to his right-hand side. "They snuck in."

    "Right..." Rebecca nodded. "I didn't know they could do that."

    "Not much was going to keep us out," Agatha told Rio. "I would've killed the nurse if we weren't trying to keep Jen and Wanda under wraps."

    Rio gave her a look. "You can't kill a mortal," she laughed. "You'll get in trouble, sweetheart." "Now, they're being gross," Billy told his parents. "I think they're about to kiss." Agatha shot him a look. "Billy, shut the hell up! Stop talking." She stuck her tongue out at her son. "Tell me what the hell happened so I can go tell Wanda. You've got everyone worried out there."

    Billy reached up to stroke the bump on his head. "We were in gym, and I got...distracted." A blush tinted his cheeks as he looked away.

    Agatha leaned down, a smirk growing. "Was this distraction in the form of a certain jock with curly hair and plump cheeks?"

    Billy dropped his head into his hands as his blush grew. "He was lifting weights, okay! We were running bleachers, and I missed a step."

    The immortal couple fell into a fit of laughter. The sound echoed in the In-Between. Rio leaned on her wife as she tried to catch her breath. "You're really head over heels, aren't you, Billy?"

    "No, no." Agatha wheezed. "He...He can't help falling in love with him," she sang. "This is why I didn't want you to tell them," Billy whined. "Now they're laughing at me." "Okay, okay. We're leaving now." Agatha pulled at Rio. "Ice that head of yours, Billy. Don't let it get any bigger that what you were born with."

    The teen shot them a look as they slipped away.

    Agatha reappeared in the waiting room, only somewhat caring if they were seen. "He's fine. Just a bump to his noggin," she informed the coven. "Why don't you all get something to eat? I need to catch up with my wife." She smoothed a hand over Rio's chest, eyes twinkling with mischief. "I need a boost."

    Death growled, hands digging into her wife's hips. "I think I can spare a few minutes," she laughed. "Unless you want to test their patience."

    The goddess pulled Rio roughly to her. "I'm sure I can find a reason. You need discipline, right?" She bit her lip as Rio clawed at her shoulders.

    "You two know we can still see and hear you, right?" Alice told them.

    "We're going." Agatha leaned over and swiped the goth's phone. "In case we're needed. I need to make a new calling card."

    Alice opened and closed her mouth several times. "Stay out of my messages!" Agatha smirked. "Alice," she purred. "Didn't know you had it in you...I'll leave it alone unless you call it or whatever."

    The goth swallowed thickly. "Okay...Just...be careful with it. I still have old business contacts."

    "Let's go," Rio whined, tugging at her. "Need you."

    "Have fun you freaks," Jen told them. She stole her girlfriend away.

    Agatha cupped her wife's face, "Shall we?"

    Rio pulled them back into the Ether with a chuckle.

    Billy thanked the nurse for the hundredth time as his parents filled out the release papers. His stomach growled. "Can we go get a bite of something? I missed lunch."

    His father gave him a smile and nod. "Jen sent a text. They're headed to a small restaurant in town. Do you want to meet up with them?"

    "Yeah!" The teen stuffed his hand into his pocket to find his phone. "Maybe Teddy can meet us."

    "Won't he still be in class?"

    Billy sighed. "I forgot school's still in." He put his phone away. "We'll need to get my stuff from school. And I need to turn in my art project to Mr. Vincent. It's due today." "We'll stop by on the way to the restaurant," his mother told him. "I'll text her your order." The trio left the hospital, Billy's parents chatting away about being more careful. His mother talked at length about how she walked into a glass door because she'd been too busy checking his father out. They laughed as they got into the car. It was a short drive to the school, thankfully. Billy got out and jogged over to his locker. He pulled out his portfolio and made his way over to Mr. Vincent's room. The man was sitting at his desk, classroom empty. "Mr. Kaplan," the bearded man said. He gave Billy a small smile. "I figured you'd be at home resting."

    The teen laughed with reddening ears. "I'm headed that way. I just wanted to give you my final project." He handed over the large sheet.

    Mr. Vincent opened it, eyes scanning the charcoal sketch with a hum. "It's very detailed." Billy nodded. "My family's pretty important to me. I figured they should be the subject." He clapped his hands together, leaning slightly forward. "If that's all, I'm going to head out. I need to ice this bump and get some rest."

    The art teacher snapped the portfolio shut and gave him a wide grin. "Well, you have a lovely family, Mr. Kaplan. I bet it's a crowded house, though. There are so many people listed." Billy waved him off. "Oh, no. I go between places. Most of them stay in Westview." "Oh, Westview!" Mr. Vincent nodded. "I've been there before. It was a little after the Maximoff Anomaly. Such a quaint little town."

    The teen twitched at the use of his other last name. "Right...I should get going. I'm meeting with my family. We're getting a bite so they can see I'm not too banged up. Have a great weekend, Mr. Vincent."

    "You too, Mr. Kaplan," Mr. Vincent told him. He drummed his fingers on the top of the portfolio. "Enjoy your meal."

    Billy nodded before rushing out to get back to his parents. His stomach was really causing a racket now. He slid into the car, panting slightly. "All good to go," he told his mother.

    Nicholas swung his legs as they waited for their food to be served. He grinned widely as a plate of dinosaur nuggets and crinkle-cut french-fries were set down in front of him. "Thanks again," he told the coven. "Should we order for Mama and Mother?"

    Wanda made a face. "I think they'll be just fine, Nicky. They don't need to eat as much as we do."

    He nodded. "Well, I'll save Mama a few nuggies. She likes to steal some of mine whenever we have them at home."

    The group laughed.

    "Oh, hey! Billy and his parents are here," Alice announced. She stood to pull another table to theirs. Jen got up to help her with the chairs.

    "What are we gonna do after this?" Nicholas asked Wanda. "Can we go to the park?" She giggled. "What's with you and parks? Do you want to live in one when you grow up?" Nicholas shrugged. "I like all the trees and grass. It reminds me of living with Mama and when Mother would visit us."

    The red head furrowed her brows. "When did Rio visit you? We never saw that." The child dipped a fry in some mustard. "Usually when Mama was asleep. Mother told me Mama would get scared if she tried to see me in the daytime." He popped the fry into his mouth with a wiggle. He loved the tang of the yellow sauce mixed with the saltiness of the fry.

    Wanda leaned in with a small smile. "Did you know your Mama was only scared because she loved you so much?"

    He nodded. "Mother told me all the time." Nicholas waved as Billy and the Kaplan's sat down. "We used to look for stones to skip across the river. Or Mother would tell me what Mama was like when she was my age."

    "That's sweet," Mrs. Kaplan told him. "When was this?"

    "When I was little, and Mama and I still lived in the woods."

    "That's a bit irresponsible of her," the woman mumbled. She must have thought he wouldn't hear it, but Nicholas had always had excellent hearing.

    He looked up from his plate of food and fixed her with a look he'd seen his Mama use a thousand times. "My mama always took good care of me," Nicholas told her firmly. "My mother wouldn't like that if she heard you."

    Mrs. Kaplan's smile dropped from her face.

    "Okay," Wanda said with a laugh. "Rebecca doesn't know so-"

    "So, she shouldn't say mean things," Nicholas huffed. "Mama never says anything about them when we're home. That's not nice." He pushed his plate of food away and crossed his arms. "Hey," Billy soothed. "It's okay. We won't talk about Agatha anymore. Why don't you tell us about...uh...Tell me about your favorite plant."

    Nicholas eyed his brother. "I don't wanna."

    Tommy snickered. "You pissed off Lil Bro," he told his twin. "I'll take you to the park now, Little Man. We can go chase the geese and ducks."

    He perked his head up at the suggestions. "I like ducks!" Nicholas stuffed the nuggets into his pockets. "Let's go, let's go!" He pulled at his favorite brother's arm. "Maybe we can catch one so I can take it home as a pet."

    "You can't go off on your own," Wanda sighed. "Jen, I'll be right back. Tommy and Nicky are ready to go to the park. Could you get us to-go boxes?"

    "Yeah. Sure thing. We'll be there in a moment." The pink witch flashed the young Harkness a grin. "Collect me some pine needles, please."

    " 'Kay!" He rushed to the front door, hoping from foot to foot as Tommy and Wanda walked over to join him.

    They stepped out into the evening air with a laugh. Tommy scooped Nicholas up and set him on his shoulders.

    "Careful, Tommy. We don't want Nicky to fall off," the Scarlet Witch warned. "Are you okay Nicky? I don't think Rebecca meant it in a mean way. Mamas are just really careful with their children."

    He held onto his brother's hands as they walked down the street. "I'm okay. I just don't like the way some people look at my mothers." He let out a soft sigh. "Everyone's scared of Mother because she's Death, and everyone hates Mama because she killed to survive. But even though they have to do scary things, they were never scary to me." Wanda hummed. "Well, your mama and Rebecca have had a rough go of things. Let's not start fights, okay? The adults should handle their own issues."

    "Like how you trapped my mama in a mean spell?"

    Tommy snickered. "He's got a point, Ma. You put Ma Squared in a nasty spell for what? Three years?"

    The woman huffed. "I'm not explaining myself to you two. There was a lot going on." She chuckled as Tommy shot her a look. "What now?"

    "Billy told me you two kissed. You two gonna go on dates now or what?" Nicholas wrinkled his nose. "You kissed my mama? I'm surprised Mother didn't kill you." He was pretty sure a lot of bad luck had fallen on the women that dared flirt with his mama. The child was very much like his mothers, after all. He learned how to use a search engine very quickly. Death didn't have much information, but the Moon Goddess did. His findings were supported by the notebook full of notes Billy had written on his mama. She'd gone on to kill a lot of witches and became very powerful. He was proud to be the son of such powerful witches, even if he wished murder wasn't something his mama was known for. "We've already got that sorted out," Wanda told them. "I'm not in love with Agatha. It was purely for magic boosting purposes. In fact, Agatha has been very clear on her boundaries as of late. So, put that silly idea out of your head, boys."

    They entered the park. Tommy put Nicholas down. Wanda helped the child fix his jacket hood to keep his ears warm.

    "We're not staying out for very long, okay? I don't want to see anyone else get sick for a long time." Wanda zipped his jacket up tightly. "Don't go too far, okay?"

    Nicholas nodded. "Are you gonna come play with the ducks too?"

    She smiled sweetly at him, cupping his cheek the way mothers were known to do with their children. "Only if you want me to."

    He grinned at her. "You're not trying to break my mothers up, so I do." This time Tommy and Wanda laughed. They took his hands to walk him over towards the pond's edge.

    A man stepped away from a tree and removed his glasses. "Wanda Maximoff," he greeted. "Well, isn't this a surprise."

    The woman pushed Nicholas and Tommy behind her. "How did you find me?" "You might tell Billy not to draw your faces on a piece of paper next time." The man eyed the witch. "I'm going to need you to come with me, Wanda. Nothing serious." Tommy picked Nicholas up, eyeing the man. "Who are you? What do you want with my mother?"

    The man narrowed his eyes. "Mother?"

    Wanda summoned up her magic, eyes glowing red. "I don't want to fight you, but I will if I have to."

    The stranger summoned up his own magic. Nicholas knew this wasn't any ordinary threat. He wiggled out of Tommy's hold and ran for a tree. His actions spooked the man who immediately froze Tommy in place. Wanda shot a spell at him, shouting for Nicky to get as far as he could. The child placed his hands against the bark of a large tree. "Mother, help! Someone's coming for-"

    Nicholas screamed and kicked as he was pulled back by a stream of magic. Him and Tommy were sent through a swirling mass of magic before landing in a strange room with shiny floors. It wasn't long before Wanda came flying through the portal. She dropped to the ground with a grunt.

    "Runes," she growled, eyes roaming the walls.

    The child ran to her side and hugged her. They were stuck with the strange man. No one would know where to find them now.

    "Okay, Wanda. Let's start from the beginning..."
